member of the commission. − mr president, thank you for bringing forward this important question. the protection and promotion of children’s rights is a priority for the commission, especially since the launch of the communication entitled ‘towards an eu strategy on the rights of the child’ in 2006. the strategy on the rights of the child focuses on the fundamental rights of children, including the protection of the best interests of the child as enshrined in the european charter of fundamental rights. the commission is determined to ensure that all fundamental rights encompassed in the charter are duly respected by all eu actions, both legislative and non-legislative. this practice will be upheld and further developed in the forthcoming communication on the rights of the child that the commission will be publishing this year. as of this year, 2011, the commission will also be reporting annually on progress made on the application of the eu charter of fundamental rights. we have to remember that the provisions of the charter are addressed to the institutions and bodies of the union, with due regard for the principle of subsidiarity, and to the member states only when they are implementing union law. we therefore have to remember that, currently, no european union legislation on international adoption exists. the subject is regulated by the hague convention of 29 may 1993 on protection of children and cooperation in respect of inter-country adoption, as well as by national laws. all the member states are party to that convention, but the eu is not. its aim is to implement article 21 of the un convention on the rights of the child by establishing safeguards to ensure that inter-country adoptions take place in the best interests of the child and that the child’s fundamental rights are respected. internationally, the commission supports the accession of third countries to the 1993 hague convention on inter-country adoption and its correct implementation by participating in relevant meetings of the contracting parties. the commission does not consider specific european rules on intra-eu adoptions to be necessary, as all 27 eu member states are parties to the hague convention. that being said, the commission is closely following the issue of international adoption within the european union, given the link between adoption and children’s rights. the commission has taken steps to see how countries are implementing the convention on adoption, and, in november 2009, provided a forum for an exchange of views on the issue. the commission’s green paper on the free circulation of public documents, published on 14 december 2010, addresses the lack of mutual recognition of adoption decisions as civil status acts between member states and its impact on the freedom of movement of eu citizens. this is a specific step which addresses the question raised today.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, food security and food security for the people remain the central challenges of agriculture, not only in europe but also in the world. i am very pleased with the content of this report, especially since food security is recognized as a fundamental human right. the objective of food security can only be achieved if two important issues are seriously addressed: market and price volatility and the depletion of food resources. europe must be able to intervene with common and effective measures for food security, to avoid the still existing strong asymmetries in safety standards between eu and non-eu products.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in these weeks the various parliamentary committees dealing with the subject of the community's agricultural policy have been dealing with this subject, the subject of the reform we will have after 2013. in the basic elements of agriculture it is always clear that food safety is an integral part of it. this is why this consideration must be evaluated in the light of the measure we are voting on today, where safety is defined as a fundamental right and therefore as such must be protected in every possible way. this attention, mr president, must be exercised both in times of emergency, such as the one linked to the dioxin scandal we are experiencing these days, dioxin discovered in animal feed, but also, and above all, in ensuring a normal production process which respects the entire production chain, the quality of the farmers' work, the quality of the environment and also of marketing and, therefore, of consumers. this is a measure which this parliament has taken as part of a series of measures to improve agriculture and i am pleased about that.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, after having voted with conviction in favour of this important report, i would like to draw particular attention to paragraph 35 of the opinion of the committee on the environment, which, in view of the importance of the european food safety authority in assessing all the risks associated with the food chain in the context of measures to protect the public and health, calls for all member states to set up equivalent national bodies to cooperate with the european agency. as the recent serious incidents in germany show, it is necessary that each state establishes a national food safety body. it is surprising that the italian government, after having set up the agency, has changed its mind for budgetary reasons. i believe that food security should not be limited by budgetary constraints.

in writing. - in italy, just yesterday, a study was presented which showed that the firms which have best withstood the crisis at the moment have been those which have strengthened their assets. in particular, according to this study prepared by a well-known italian university on behalf of the most vibrant business association, mergers have been the main instrument of strengthening. it is no coincidence that special financing operations, including mergers, accompany restructuring and the search for efficiency in all production sectors. it is therefore the task of the european institutions, in a single market context, to define rules which guarantee all the actors involved and allow the most virtuous companies to compete at their best, free from regulatory uncertainties, bureaucratic constraints and obligations arising from mere misunderstandings. a modern, liberal and efficient economy, such as i believe we must have, needs specific legislation for mergers, provided that, like the proposed directive, it is light and non-intrusive and protects the freedoms and rights of those who may be harmed by these operations.
in writing. - in assessing the draft legislative resolution on mergers of public limited liability companies, i have taken account of the following legislative acts: the commission proposal to the european parliament and the council, the common position defined at first reading on 17 june 2008, articles 294 and 50 tfeu, pursuant to which the commission submitted the proposal to parliament, the interinstitutional agreement of 20 december 1994 on an accelerated working method for the official codification of legislative texts, articles 86 and 55 of its rules of procedure and, finally, the report of the committee on legal affairs. on this basis i have wished to be consistent with parliament's position at first reading as adapted to the recommendations of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, especially in view of the fact that it represents a mere codification of existing texts, without any substantial changes.

in writing. the community has exclusive competence in external air transport policy, which is traditionally governed by bilateral air service agreements concluded between member states and third countries. in june 2003, the commission opened negotiations with third countries with a view to replacing certain provisions in existing bilateral agreements with community agreements. among these, one agreement stands out, replacing the 47 existing bilateral air services agreements concluded between eu member states and the west african economic and monetary union. the main points of the agreement are: the designation clause replacing the bilateral agreement which avoids discrimination between european union air carriers; the taxation of aviation fuel in general in the eu; the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the application of the competition rules to commercial agreements between airlines. the agreement negotiated by the commission was provisionally approved on 30 november 2009. i am also very much in favour of renegotiating these agreements, given the court of justice's case law, which is based on the exclusive competence of the community, both because they are geared towards the increasingly indispensable community sovereignty and because this draft decision is in line with the eu's competition and budgetary rules.

in writing. the construction sector is one of the key european sectors for both employment and the development of our small and mediumsized enterprises. it is therefore essential to support a regulation setting harmonised conditions for the marketing of construction products to ensure the safety of the materials used and the health of workers. physical and health damage also continues to be reported for citizens living in daily contact with hazardous substances, such as asbestos, used in the construction of urban buildings. i therefore support the sthiler regulation, which was voted on today at second reading, because it underlines the importance, in a globalised world, of the need to introduce common rules for the labelling of substances and products used, which can thus guarantee safety and reliability and at the same time reduce costs for producers, especially smes.
in writing. the proposal for a parliament and council regulation laying down harmonised conditions for the marketing of construction products is designed to ensure the free movement of construction products within the internal market. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation precisely because ensuring accurate and reliable information (through the ce marking of products on the market) on construction products is a further step towards a competitive free market and capable of protecting small and mediumsized enterprises. as construction products are intermediate products of a final work, the harmonization of new european rules guarantees the safety and quality of the work, puts all construction companies on the same level, improves the control of materials already on the market and ultimately achieves better transparency of the trade in construction products.
in writing. − there are still too many barriers to trade in the construction sector in the eu, with which states justify the technical rules they have put in place to restrict the free movement of goods and services. the fast-growing sector generates 10% of gdp, 50.5% of gross fixed capital formation, employs 12 million eu citizens and is 92% made up of smes, the backbone of our economy. i therefore believe that it is necessary to introduce measures to harmonize the market in these products and to guarantee a high level of safety and health for workers. in the light of the recession which has caused serious problems in the sector, such as the bankruptcy of companies, liberalization measures are necessary to ensure the economic survival of enterprises and to preserve jobs. the proposal for a regulation is designed to simplify, update and replace the construction products directive in the light of changed circumstances, for example as regards market surveillance. it also wants to give greater protection in the areas of ce marking, dangerous substances, national product contact points, independence and transparency, health and safety, electronic communication.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that there are still too many 'restrictions' on trade in the building sector in europe. the revision of this directive should help to remove trade barriers, while protecting the jobs of companies in the sector which remain exposed to the global economic crisis. new specific measures are envisaged to verify the recycling of these products, promoting their use in order to meet eu climate change objectives. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. finally, the demand for the gradual digitisation of documentation in place of paper copies is intended to make the construction products market even more 'unique'.
in writing. - although the introduction to the regulation contains general statements which cannot be accepted, in particular on the free and full movement of services in the building sector, because until the cost of labour is harmonized between the various member states there will be risks of unfair competition, our vote will be in favour. the reason is that the substance of the measure deals exclusively with the regulation of the marketing of products for the construction sector, which in this period of economic recession has had very serious repercussions with the bankruptcy of many companies and the loss of jobs. the proposal provides for the harmonisation and labelling of goods containing dangerous substances, simplifies, updates and replaces existing rules in order to remove some regulatory obstacles to the benefit of operators and small and medium-sized enterprises.

in writing. the rapporteur stresses the importance of agriculture in relation to the new food challenges. the fao has stated that food production will have to increase by at least 70 percent, as the world's population will exceed 9 billion by 2050. so food security continues to require a strong cap. the main objectives of the cap were: increase agricultural productivity, help farmers achieve a fair standard of living, stabilise markets and ensure a secure supply of affordable food. however, its success has led to unintentional overproduction and surpluses that have distorted the market and raised environmental concerns. the new cap will therefore have to improve the food system by increasing productivity while encouraging environmentally sustainable food production. the report stresses that it is essential that cap financing reflects its ambitious vision and policy objectives. the cap must be maintained at its present level by ensuring sustainable food prices and, above all, a decent income for farmers with the aim of ensuring food security. improving and strengthening food safety controls in the union and in third countries is essential and that is why i am expressing my favourable opinion of the resolution.

in writing. − food security is a fundamental right that is hampered by limited natural resources, high energy prices and climate change. according to fao, production will have to increase by 70 percent by 2050, with some 900 million people worldwide suffering from hunger and 16 percent of the population living below the poverty line in europe alone. a strong common agricultural policy is essential and the cap has been geared towards this, but reform of the cap is needed to create a 'sustainable cap' on the one hand and to improve food security on the other. this can only be achieved by addressing the problem of price volatility (caused by speculation) and the depletion of food resources. the text also calls for the revision of existing financial instruments legislation and the creation of a global food security system to help the global market in the event of price surges and protectionism. the new cap after 2013 will have to be ready for all this and that is why i support the text in favour of competitiveness, traditional agriculture, access to land and credit for young people, greater integration of food and energy.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioners, it is true that haiti is a special case, different, because when we remember the anniversary of a disaster, we always do so to remember the victims, to learn the lessons better, but in haiti it is different, because there is nothing to remember, nothing is yet past. instead of saying a year since the earthquake, we should say a year of earthquake, seismic earthquake, then earthquake of the aid disorder, health earthquake with cholera, political earthquake with elections that are not very transparent and probably at the most inopportune time and earthquake in some respects also historic, now, with the return of the former dictator as a billionaire tourist. the commission is doing a good job, very good job, i was in haiti last june with the development committee and saw the excellent work and we thank them, but we also need greater political protection with an increased role for the international community to set objectives, deadlines and to manage directly part of the reconstruction. this must be balanced by greater involvement of the local population and ngos, which are often excluded. so less role for national politics and national government institutions in haiti, and more for a so far weak partnership between citizens and the international community.
member of the commission. − madam president, i sincerely thank members of parliament for all their comments this evening. in closing, i would like to make five points. firstly, i agree very much with all speakers who emphasised the governance failure as the most significant factor underlying the problems haiti faces today. that was my first impression after the earthquake and it still stands today: that bad as the earthquake was, it is not haiti’s biggest problem. its biggest problem is the many decades of bad governance that have practically left no social structures and government structures in place to help the haitian people, and that creates a big deficit of trust of the haitian people in their government. i remember very vividly how, when i was there, universally all the haitians i talked to had one message for me consistently, which was ‘do not give money to the government’. now, on the humanitarian side we do not give money; we provide direct assistance. but it does give us pause for thought on the question of how long it will take to rebuild haiti: it will take a very long time because it will not happen without this institutional infrastructure in place. this being said, my second point is that there is actually a positive side to haitian society which has helped the haitian people survive: their own resilience and the resilience of their communities. i met people who lived together: they lost their houses together, they moved to camps together and they have organised in the camps a support system for each other, with some taking responsibility to oversee the kids and to improvise some schooling for them; others taking responsibility to find work; others, actually the women, taking on responsibility for cooking for everybody. that resilience is what gives us some hope today for the future of haiti. this leads on to my third point, which is that our support programmes for haiti have to take into account what the country has and does not have. for that reason, we have on the humanitarian side emphasised cash for work, vouchers programmes, innovations like getting seeds and tools at the community level so that people can actually increase their reliance on themselves. fourthly, i am grateful for the points that were made on what lessons we have learnt from haiti. i would not agree that we were slow to respond: help from the european union was flowing within 24 hours. but i would agree that coordination left room for improvement and that our ability to organise ourselves before a disaster strikes is absolutely essential. in this sense, i am grateful for the point that was made that, based on lessons from haiti, we have indeed moved in the direction of creating a european response capacity and stronger coordination through the european disaster response centre. let me then move to a last point, looking forward on the humanitarian side. what is it that we are very worried about? it is actually the question of protection, especially for women, and of increasing our support for dealing with the tragedy of primarily women-led households stuck in the camps. i can assure you that this year as well as with the funding next year, we will put the emphasis on making sure that this question of protection is addressed and that the eu is there for people. let me in closing just thank everyone once again for their comments and especially those of you who have recognised the sacrifice of the humanitarian workers for the benefit of the people of haiti.
member of the commission. − madam president, first i would like to thank members of this house for their solidarity and support. i will start with the political dimension. the situation is certainly not easy in haiti, but the high representative is following it very closely and giving all the necessary diplomatic support to ensure that there is stability. the second round of presidential elections will help rebuild credibility if there is no violence around it, so we are also making all the necessary diplomatic efforts; but diplomatic efforts sometimes give immediate results and sometimes need time to produce results. some of you mentioned baby doc’s visit. we can say that whilst anybody can move freely, this was definitely not the best sign of the whole political process. but we should not be somehow misled by this. i think there is a healthy political core in haiti and we should believe in it. our hope is that the people who are elected in the legislative elections and the president will have the necessary capacities to lead the reconstruction of the country. the second point i would like to emphasise is that development cooperation is about hard choices. one choice is do something with high visibility that does not entail a structural change. it would be no problem to finance thousands of doctors from the eu or to build a new university in the name of the eu; it would be visible and everybody would say fine. but what about the insecurity in the streets? we finance security in quite difficult conditions through the government. so if security is provided partially, it is financed by the european union. is it visible? not very much so, because there is no eu label, but i believe it is definite that we have provided for the stability of the country. another point is where to invest money. again, rebuilding the houses would be the easiest political choice, but what help is that if the country is not reconnected, if there is no infrastructure? and infrastructure requires massive investment. roughly speaking, one kilometre of road costs usd 1 million and in haiti even more, because there must be maintenance and also we need to help the local communities through which the road passes. so the costs are very substantial. haiti will not have such funds to invest. strangely enough, in haiti we are the only ones involved in the road infrastructure. normally many other countries participate in road infrastructure, but in haiti we are alone in giving grants for this. it is a difficult choice, but i believe it will help the country to have structural change. a last point which was not raised very much today is the speed of commitment and disbursement of funds. the funds should not be misused and it takes time for budget support. it is not just that the government gives us an account and we just transfer the money. no. we check the account, we know where the disbursements go, so it is quite a procedure. you cannot just immediately send eur 1.2 billion to an account and expect that everything will be sorted out. we also have a responsibility to our taxpayers. the same considerations apply with the roads: we need to launch a tender, we need to be transparent about this and that takes a bit of time. but i believe this time is rightly taken, because it needs only one case of a misuse of funds for the support for haiti’s reconstruction to be damaged in the eyes of european citizens. i can assure you that we will take all the necessary steps in this regard, too. again, i thank you for your support. it was a very helpful and encouraging debate and i believe that we will try to deliver on the issues that you have mentioned today.

author of the book. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the situation in campania, and in particular in the city of naples, has been known throughout the world for years, and the european union has had to deal with it on several occasions. in view of this paradoxical situation in the third world, i would therefore ask the commission what consequences italy will face from the point of view of community law and what economic sanctions italy may be subject to if the waste crisis in campania is not resolved in the near future. i would also like to know whether the commission can provide details of the european funds which have so far been managed by the campania region for the creation of the integrated waste collection and disposal system. you see, commissioner, when we talk about emergencies we usually talk about dramatic, extreme situations which nevertheless find a solution within a reasonable time. when a so-called "emergency" has lasted for more than 15 years, something is clearly wrong. the italian government has tried in recent years to do everything possible to solve the age-old problem of the waste collection and disposal cycle, but obviously if today the streets of naples are flooded with tons and tons of garbage, the blame is mainly to be laid on the local authorities and their total inability or lack of will to make efforts to find a solution. it is clear, beyond all doubt, that the conditions in which naples and campania are found are due to the latitude that has characterized the municipality, the province and the region for so many years in the management of the waste cycle. if separate collection, the first essential element of a successful waste management plan, is not properly carried out, it cannot be the fault of the central government. if the italian government had to send the army - member of the commission. − madam president, first of all i would like to thank all members of parliament who drew my attention and the attention of my services to this important question. i am pleased that the european parliament has taken an active role in monitoring the waste management situation in campania, as shown, for example, by the report adopted by the committee on petitions following the visit to campania which it carried out in april last year. parliament has truly an important role here and has assumed it fully. immediately after the european court ruling, on 4 march 2010, the commission wrote to the italian authorities asking what measures they had planned or taken in order to comply with it. after that, the commission has had several contacts and meetings with the italian authorities, most recently during the mission to naples carried out on 22 and 23 november 2010 by a delegation from the environment directorate-general. our view is that the italian authorities still have a long way to go in order to execute the ruling. in particular they need, firstly, to expand and upgrade waste management facilities throughout the whole of campania and, secondly, to develop an effective management plan for urban waste in campania, taking into account, amongst other things, the eu waste management hierarchy. the commission is not satisfied with the measures that the italian authorities have communicated since the court’s ruling because they do not include a detailed calendar indicating milestones for the construction works of the foreseen installations. we think that the waste management plan for campania must be fully compliant with eu environmental law and must give priority to waste reduction, re-use and recycling; ensure implementation of separate collection in the whole region; provide campania with the necessary composting capacity; and establish measures for the safe disposal in a reasonable timeframe of more than seven million tonnes of baled waste stored in several cities in campania, which also means that the italian authorities will have to carry out an analysis of the baled waste, the so-called ‘ecoballe’, before deciding which is the safest way to dispose of them. if there is no adequate and effective waste management plan, the commission will return to the court and propose the imposition of fines. therefore we must closely assess the draft waste management plan that the campania authorities have just submitted to the commission – and ‘just’ really means ‘just’ – and monitor carefully that they actually adopt and implement the plan. the decision on whether and when to open article 260 proceedings against italy will depend mainly on the content of the waste management plan and the timing of the measures used to immediately address the problem in a convincing way. with regard to the existing landfills, the commission has started an investigation and asked the italian authorities to report on the functioning of the terziano and cicciano landfills. the italian reply is still pending and once it is received, the commission will assess it. at this stage, the commission does not have evidence of a breach of european union environmental law. the fact that the landfill is situated in a nature protected area is not in itself a breach of eu legislation, provided of course that other rules are applied and that the competent national authorities carry out an appropriate environment assessment and implement the necessary mitigation and also compensation measures. as concerns the co-financing of waste management measures in campania, in the 1994-1999 programming period eur 88.1 million were devoted to waste management projects, almost 49% co-financed by the erdf. however, only 90% of the total allocation was used because of difficulties also linked to the waste management crisis and the institution by the italian authorities of the extraordinary management in 1994. in the 2002-2006 programming period, a total financing allocation of eur 140 million, 50% co-financed again by the erdf, was concentrated on waste management projects. however, following the waste management crisis, the commission decided to take specific measures in order to ensure that erdf funds allocated to campania were used properly. firstly, as from 1 january 2005, expenditure management was considered ineligible for co-financing. secondly, after the official notification to italy of the opening of the infringement procedure for waste management on 29 june 2007, the commission informed the italian authorities that no further co-financing would be acceptable for waste management. the 2007-2013 regional operational programme in campania foresees a total investment of eur 270 million, again 50% co-financed by the erdf, for the management of waste. however, the disbursement of ec financing for projects in the waste sector is subject, in particular, to the condition that the italian authorities adopt a regional waste management plan, to be validated of course by the commission. tomorrow we will publish in the commission the report on the implementation of a thematic strategy on prevention and recycling of waste. this report shows significant differences between member states in terms of waste management performance. it clearly demonstrates that with an appropriate waste management strategy, landfilling can be reduced close to zero and that incineration could be dramatically reduced by increasing waste composting and recycling. in addition to transforming waste into resources, this creates jobs and economic activity while reducing the environmental impact of waste management. so i really hope that this crisis will eventually be transformed into an opportunity by the competent authorities through the launch of serious separate collection and recycling schemes in campania. in brief, the commission is hoping that the waste management plan for campania is convincing. until we are certain of an effective plan setting up a system with the necessary infrastructure and have robust guarantees that projects will be implemented effectively, commission funding of relevant waste management projects in campania is interrupted. i will address some of your questions which you have already raised in my closing remarks.

member of the commission. − madam president, i should like to thank the members very much for all their views. there are three or four issues which i would like to address. first is the issue which has been quite passionately addressed by many of you. the situation is critical; there is no quick fix. there have been some positive developments but it is obvious that we still need a systemic answer to the question. it is not easy but it is more than needed. in that respect our partner in finding a solution is, of course, italy, but cooperation with regional authorities in this respect is undoubtedly necessary. so i am very much looking forward to the evaluation of the new draft waste management plan which we sincerely hope is what we all believe it should be. it will be evaluated by my services, by the experts, and i can assure you that it will be done in such a way that there will be the same treatment for italy as for any other member state, because it is of fundamental importance that we keep that trust between member states on the table. so when we talk about dealing with these problems, my approach could actually be put into four words. i want to be helpfully strict and strictly helpful. the idea is certainly not to impose fines. as was mentioned by some of you, the idea is to solve problems, but by imposing fines if there is no other way to solve the problems, because that is my duty. so i am truly doing everything in cooperation with the italian authorities so that we find proper solutions. that is my sincere hope. at the end of the day we are talking about the health of italian citizens and the italian environment. the second thing i want to mention is connected with the waste framework directive. it is a new directive which was recently adopted. in that directive it is pretty clear that each of the countries, as a matter of law, has to introduce a waste hierarchy. that means the best waste is no waste; there is re-use, recycling, energy regeneration and, if there is no other possibility, landfilling. that is the picture which is taken from the report that will be published tomorrow on how efficient the member states in the european union are. it is about the trends in landfilling municipal waste because our best available data are on municipal waste. believe it or not, there are five member states where landfilling is below 5% of municipal waste, but there are also seven member states where landfilling is over 80%, so we have really very different situations in europe when we deal with these programmes, and this is an issue which we certainly want to address. this picture is of the situation between 1995 and 2007 and, if it shows anything, it shows that if countries want they can change. if they organise themselves in a proper way, they can really change. fundamentally, you can today divide europe into two parts: one part which sees waste as a problem and one part which sees waste as a major opportunity for resources and also for the new financial profits because that is the reality. i have heard many stories of the need for the question of who will take the waste to be decided by public procurement, because there are more than the necessary number of users who would like to have it in order to use it. however, for this purpose the waste has to be selected at the very beginning. that is the fundamental and most important need. the last thing which i would like to mention is the honourable member who said that we should be more careful about waste management problems elsewhere in the european union. in the infringement cases by sector in 2009, waste accounts for 19%, water 20%, nature 19%, air 16%, and the rest less. we are looking horizontally at all implementation problems and we are bound to do that. i can assure you that we will do it also in the future. to conclude, we should truly do our best, you as members of parliament and i as commissioner for the environment, to spread across europe the message of waste as an opportunity for the future. we desperately need that message in the context of the limited resources which we are increasingly facing from day to day. resource efficiency is the name of the problem and resource efficiency is at the core of our future competitiveness in europe. if you do not believe me, ask me in 10 years’ time. i can guarantee that this will be the case.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president of the european council, i see two major problems with the proposed amendment to article 136, one institutional and one political. the institutional one: article 3 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) defines the monetary policy of countries whose currency is the euro as an exclusive competence of the union, but article 2 provides that an exclusive competence may be exercised by the member states if authorised by the union. it is difficult to understand why the application of a rule clearly defined by the treaty requires a reform of the treaty. there is a political problem, though: the choice of the treaty reform procedure, instead of using article 2 or articles 352 plus 136, puts the esm, and thus the future of the euro, in the hands of 27 ratification processes. is there any awareness that if just one of these 27 ratification processes goes wrong, it would be difficult at this point to come up with a plan b for the euro? is the european council aware that the choice of this procedure places the future of the euro at great risk?

in writing. − this recommendation to the council was essential to ensure that patients have the highest possible level of legal certainty to exercise their rights in concrete terms, as indicated by the european court of justice. this approach, however, does not interfere with the exclusive competences of the member states in the management of their internal health systems and in the choice of national health policy as provided for in the treaty. the main issues were rare diseases, quality standards and safety standards, reimbursement and prior authorisation procedures and advance payments, and the need to ensure that the european union's financial instruments are used effectively. the role of contact points as a 'one-stop shop'; the exclusive competence of member states in the field of 'baskets of health services' and ethical choices in the field of health; e-health and cooperation between member states. in addition, the rights of patients as enunciated by the european court of justice have been clarified and the overall legal certainty in cross-border healthcare has been improved, access to cross-border healthcare and its reimbursement, according to safe and quality criteria, has been facilitated, cooperation in healthcare between member states has been promoted.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of the directive introducing new rules on crossborder healthcare. with the new legislation, europe is taking a major step forward, not only in terms of facilitating healthcare, especially in border regions, and expanding care opportunities for eu citizens, but also in terms of advancing healthcare in general, thanks to the incentives for research from cooperation between states. in particular, i support the introduction of rules to strengthen cooperation on rare diseases, so that those who suffer from them can benefit from the benefits of closer health cooperation between member states. moreover, the rule that reimbursement is subject to the condition that treatment and costs are covered by the respective health systems and the provision for prior authorisation for treatment involving hospitalization constitute safeguard clauses designed to ensure the stability of national health systems. the directive thus makes it possible to make significant progress towards improving health services by striking the right balance between the needs of the states which are responsible for the provision of these services and those of the citizens who are the main beneficiaries.
in writing. − i welcome the new legislation regulating patients' right to medical care in another eu country. the work of the epp, in close cooperation with the other political groups, was once again crucial: the adoption of the report by mrs grossetête, the french member, comes after lengthy negotiations with the council and makes it possible to take a significant step forward in an area where the existing rules were not sufficient. the new rules, which only apply to those who choose to seek treatment abroad, provide that eu citizens can be reimbursed for medical care they receive in another member state, provided that the treatment and related costs were covered in their home country. this is particularly important when considering that seeking healthcare abroad could particularly benefit patients on long waiting lists or those unable to find specialist care.

in writing. − during the previous discussions in committee, it was repeatedly stated that this directive does not seek to encourage 'health tourism', but only to establish clear rules on crossborder healthcare. it is important that access to medical care in a member state other than the member state of origin be subject to a proven and objective need in such a way as to avoid overburdening national health systems with excessive financial burdens which would necessarily undermine their efficiency. a step forward has been made with regard to rare diseases: patients will have easier access to highly specialised care and the possibility of seeking specialist advice in another member state. i think it is important in this respect that national contact points are set up to provide patients with comprehensive information on the treatment available in other countries and on how to access and reimburse cross-border care. finally, i would like to emphasise that the exclusive competence of the states in the field of 'baskets of care' and ethical choices in the field of health should in no way be called into question.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the initiative approved by this parliament today has created an agreement which will certainly boost trade between the european union and certain pacific states. in particular, the interim partnership agreement was concluded with papua new guinea and the republic of the fiji islands, which are seeking to achieve the objective of protecting their sugar and tuna industries. i believe that this is a step forward in terms of development and prosperity, and that it can bring real added value - also thanks to the rules of origin - to the fishing industry and to the exports of these regions. i would also like to stress that the agreement could have important implications for relations with other states in the pacific region, including australia and new zealand.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the interim partnership agreement between the eu and the pacific states because i believe it is important that europe has trade partnership agreements with third countries that can export products that are difficult for european countries to access. the development of international trade is followed logically by agreements which facilitate trade and make the trade network increasingly accessible. negotiations for new economic partnership agreements (epas) were launched in 2002 with the aim of establishing and strengthening regional integration processes within the acp states. the agreement in question concerns rules of origin in the fisheries, textiles and agriculture sectors, providing opportunities for investment and employment, and market access, with a duty-free tariff that would provide investment and employment opportunities. the interim agreement also reduced the policy room for manoeuvre of governments in terms of regulatory powers.
in writing. − in 2002, negotiations were launched for new acp-eu economic partnership agreements (epas) to replace the previous unilateral trade preferences regime for the acp. given that the issues of specific interest were the subject of individual national negotiations and that it was not possible to conclude partnership agreements immediately, it was agreed to conclude interim agreements focusing on trade in goods by the end of 2007 (they aim to avoid the disruption of trade and may not necessarily be a prelude to a full epa). in the pacific, only fiji and papua new guinea have signed such agreements. the agreement covers rules of origin in the fisheries, textile and agricultural sectors and provides for investment and employment opportunities. the european commission hopes to conclude a comprehensive economic partnership agreement with the pacific regional group, so much so that negotiations are under way. i thought it appropriate to stick to the council's position in favour of the interim partnership agreement, because i consider it a priority to secure the supply of resources, especially in view of their scarcity and the deterioration of the environment. it is also essential to keep alive, albeit in a different form, the agreements with the acp countries which have been in force for ten years.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint resolution on intercountry adoption because i firmly believe that european coordination of adoption strategies and instruments would not only improve the procedure itself but would also ensure greater protection for orphaned and abandoned children and their right to have a family. the synergy between international bodies, community institutions and member states would create a virtuous circle in which the needs of the child would be at the centre, alongside the provision of information, preparation and support services for adoptive families. i believe that greater coordination can give the adopted child greater certainty about the correctness of the procedures for obtaining and mutual recognition of documents, and prevent the phenomenon of child trafficking.
in writing. - adoption is always a sensitive issue and deserves special attention, since it is the children and their future who are being decided. adoption often proves to be a useful tool in rescuing abandoned or orphaned children from an unhappy childhood, spent in orphanages, without the affection and care that every child should enjoy. to deny an innocent child the chance to be loved and guided in his or her journey by loving and present parents would be a cruel and unjust act, which is why i voted in favour of the resolution, as i firmly believe in the power of adoption as a means to give a better life to children who will become the future of the world. at european level, a coordinated strategy is needed, backed up by transparent and effective post-adoption support procedures and a monitoring mechanism to monitor the activities of each member state. adopting a child means giving them a better, safer and more hopeful future, and i believe that practical legislation on this matter is essential to overcome the international differences.
in writing. - with the new migrations, the problem of abandoned children, which was gradually being solved, is becoming more and more serious and important. it is essential to find a regulatory framework which takes account of the protection of minors, parental responsibility and the bureaucratization of practices, which harmonises the laws of the member states in compliance with the 1993 convention on the protection of minors and cooperation in respect of intercountry adoption and the treaty of lisbon. i would like to mention as a negative example the way in which germany handles adoption practices and, in particular, childcare, when couples with one german partner and the other from a different country in the union are involved. it is clear that the ultimate aim of the legislator must be to guarantee children the right to the protection and care necessary for their well-being by avoiding their being forced to live in orphanages.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on 1 february 2010 the stabilisation and association agreement between the european union and the republic of serbia entered into force. although 11 months have passed, not all eu member states have yet ratified the agreement. with this motion for a resolution, the european parliament wanted, on the one hand, to reaffirm the importance of serbia's role within the union and, on the other hand, to approve the political and social improvements that the serbian government has made in recent years and to recall the steps that the country still has to take in order to meet the demands for democratization, freedom and the adoption of sustainable and clean policies demanded by the european union. i believe that serbia's accession to the eu is a significant step forward for both the union and the republic of serbia, and i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution, believing that serbia will soon be able to overcome all the barriers that have for so long created a wide gap between the two.
in writing. − this report reduces trade barriers between the european union and serbia and represents a step forward towards a prospect of accession for the balkan country. this stabilisation and association agreement was signed in 2008, but has since been ratified by only 12 member states, including italy. the important objective achieved today must, however, be a new starting point for serbia, which submitted its candidature in december 2009. it will have to continue to cooperate fully with the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia, which has always been an essential precondition for accession.
in writing. - i welcome the stabilisation agreement between the eu and serbia: the stabilisation and association agreement (saa) reduces trade barriers between the eu and serbia and represents a step towards the possible accession of the balkan country to the union. it was signed in 2008, but since then only 12 member states, including italy, have ratified it: today's vote expresses parliament's consent to the agreement, thus sending a signal to the remaining 15 member states to also proceed with ratification. despite being severely tested by events in its recent past, serbia has slowly managed to recover and consolidate its democratic structure. the country, because of its geographical location and its strategic role, is undoubtedly at the heart of the process of integration of the balkans into the eu; serbia is also an important trading partner, with a key role in sectors such as iron and steel. today's vote follows another important step, which took place in december 2009: the abolition of visas throughout the schengen area has allowed serbian citizens to feel more european.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the context of the enlargement process, the situation in the western balkans requires special attention. a country like serbia certainly has its problems, but belgrade's situation seems to be much better than other countries in the same area. i therefore support the text, hoping that it will be interpreted as a stimulus by the serbian people and the serbian authorities, and i hope that the process of cooperation with the tribunal for the crimes of the former yugoslavia will be accelerated.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the european integration process of serbia and the stabilisation and association agreement with the eu because i believe that constructive approaches to regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations are essential elements of the stabilisation and association process, which play a decisive role in the process of transforming the western balkans into an area of long-term stability and sustainable development. serbia also plays an important role in the security, stability and reconciliation of the peoples of the region. the eu condemns all the war crimes that destroyed the former yugoslavia, and supports the work of the icty (the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia) by reiterating that serbia's future lies in the european union and encourages the country to continue its efforts to achieve this goal.
in writing. - in view of the draft council and commission decision, the stabilisation and association agreement between the european community and serbia, the request for approval by the council under articles 217 and 218 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, articles 81 and 90 of the ep's rules of procedure and the recommendation of the committee on foreign affairs, i consider it extremely logical and necessary to follow parliament's line. i therefore approve the draft council and commission decision in question, with the aim of encouraging, first of all, ever closer cooperation with serbia and, more generally, stabilization and cooperation within the european community.
in writing. − alzheimer's disease affects more and more people in europe and worldwide, with a trend in recent decades towards a decline in the average age of patients. a disease that was once a health and social problem has now become an urgent issue on the agenda of national health policies. the eu's commitment over the next few years to coordinate policies at community level on research and the exchange of good practice in alzheimer's disease, early diagnosis and support for families of the sick, who are currently in many member states psychologically and economically burdened by the care of people in need of ongoing care and therapy, is therefore positive. i am voting in favour of mrs matias' report, in the hope that much, and more than has been done so far, will be done to combat a disease which is becoming more and more widespread but whose serious social implications are not as well known.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, by voting today on the matias report, the european parliament has wanted to underline that the fight against alzheimer's disease is a health priority for the union. according to the 2009 world alzheimer's report, approximately 28% of european citizens suffer from this type of dementia, and this figure is set to increase as the european population ages. i therefore believe that the institutions should not underestimate this disease and should take concrete action to support patients and their families. in this context, the european parliament's task must be to promote a policy of raising public awareness of this issue and to call on the council and the commission to take due account of this disease when preparing future actions in the field of preventive health policy. among these, as suggested in the text of the report, i would like to mention the development of guidelines for the implementation of early diagnosis services and the identification of instruments to facilitate access to funding.
in writing. − the 2009 alzheimer's report is alarming: approximately 35.6 million people worldwide are affected by all forms of dementia. this estimate is constantly increasing, especially in europe where the average age of the population is increasing rapidly. it is therefore important to activate a network for the sharing of statistical data and a platform for the coordination of research activities on the causes, prevention and treatment of alzheimer's disease among the member states. given that early diagnosis can help to reduce healthcare costs across europe, it is also essential to share the level of financial investment and to provide for policies at european level to encourage targeted prevention. i would also like to stress that the specific needs of women, who represent twice as many patients and a disproportionate share of the care staff, must be taken into account in the areas of medical research, health and social policy. alzheimer's disease is a major challenge for european societies, and only through a joint effort can we address the social and health consequences of dementia and provide services and support to people with neurodegenerative diseases as well as their families.
in writing. - i am in favour of mr matias' report because in europe there is a need to ensure close cooperation and coordination between the member states capable of providing an effective response, geared to the prevention and treatment of alzheimer's disease which today affects 6 million european citizens. without european support for national efforts not only in the field of prevention and treatment but also in the coordination of research funding, the dissemination of best practice and appropriate funding for the pharmaceutical industry working to discover effective medicines, we will not be able to give autonomy and dignity to people suffering from diseases that severely disable them, also in terms of emotional and social relationships.
in writing. - my decision to vote in favour of the alzheimer's report is based on the objective of improving the current european strategy to combat this disease. the progressive ageing of the european population is accompanied by a considerable increase in the number of people suffering from neurodegenerative diseases, 50% of whom are alzheimer's patients. this report is therefore a step forward in the fight against this serious disease. i believe that prevention is key here, both in early diagnosis and in collecting epidemiological data. it would also be necessary to address some gaps both in the training of professionals in the field and in supporting families by raising public awareness of living with dementia.
in writing. − alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia present very worrying data, such as the fact that 1.4 million eu citizens are affected every year and a new case is diagnosed every 24 seconds. one in 20 people over the age of 65 are affected, and more than 8 million europeans are thought to be affected. in the light of this, coordination between the various national policies is necessary at european level. the fragmentation of interventions, the divergences in responses across europe and the disparity in access and treatment conditions related to the disease are reasons more than enough to justify the initiative on the basis of four main objectives: promoting early diagnosis; improving epidemiological knowledge of the disease; fostering solidarity between member states and respecting the rights of people living with the different forms of dementia. at present, there is no cure for alzheimer's disease, so it is crucial to enhance non-pharmacological treatments by promoting those that contribute to improving the well-being of those affected. in the light of the above, i am absolutely in favour of better coordination between the member states and a more effective response to prevent dementia.
in writing. − the average age of the european population is continuously increasing, and this phenomenon is making the problems of ageing, particularly dementia, more and more relevant. it is estimated that over 35 million people worldwide have dementia and that this number is expected to double every 20 years. in europe, the number of people with dementia is 9.9 million, with a large number of people affected by alzheimer's disease. a study by alzheimer's disease international shows that the annual cost to eu countries for each alzheimer's patient is €24,000, with a total of around €161 billion. dementia is expected to be one of the major challenges to the sustainability of our national health systems in the coming decades. the data on the number of people affected indicate that services and support should be provided to people with dementia, in particular their families, which are the main sources of support for care, such as the alzheimer and related disease plan, already implemented in several member states. the common objective should be to promote greater public awareness of the diseases of ageing and to accompany world alzheimer's day, celebrated on 21 september, with information campaigns on the prevention of these diseases and the treatment of cerebrovascular accidents.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, my vote in favour of the motion for a resolution is based on the need to affirm that europe, and in particular the european parliament as a democratically elected body, is always on the side of its citizens. the resolution adopted today is based on petition 0473/2008 by christoph klein, a german citizen, on the commission's failure to intervene in competition matters in relation to the withdrawal of an asthma device. in such cases, what we have to ensure as european citizens first, and as members of the european parliament later, is the practical possibility of being able to activate protection mechanisms in the event of non-compliance with the rules of the treaties by one of the european institutions. in short, that is the reason for my vote, and i hope that the commission will correct its behaviour or at least provide timely answers to the problem of the withdrawal of the asthma device, which will shed light on what has happened.
in writing. − asthma attacks cause sudden breathing difficulties that may last for hours. in germany, first in 1997 and then in 2005, sales bans were introduced for particular asthma inhalers. the european commission, called upon to answer for the legality of the bans introduced, never made a statement on the subject, in breach of the 'obligation to safeguard' enshrined in directive 93/42/eec which should have obliged it to do so. the seriousness of this behaviour is further underlined by the fact that, according to reliable estimates, withdrawn inhalers could have improved the quality of life of some 30 million people suffering from asthma. the question put by mr mazzoni asks the european commission to respond to the non-compliance with the 'safeguard clause' in article 8 of directive 93/42/eec. this article states that the commission, when it is called upon to assess a national legislative measure in the field of health, must consult the parties concerned as soon as possible and inform them of the legality - or otherwise - of the national measure. at this point in the matter, as the court of justice has also ruled, it is necessary to set up a committee of inquiry to ascertain the real responsibilities of the commission.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the earthquake that struck haiti on 12 january 2010 caused some 222 750 deaths and almost 2 million displaced persons. ten months after this tragedy, the same island was struck by a cholera epidemic that has, to date, caused the death of 3,333 people. the situation, as these tragic figures show, is not simple. in addition, despite the fact that the political elections in november were marred by fraud, the country is still without a government. today's vote calls on the european union to work with the institutions of haiti to enable the country to produce rules and regulations that will help it to make better use of all the financial aid it has received over the past year, and above all to do so on the basis of the principles of democracy and the rule of law. the emphasis on the relationship between emergency aid, rehabilitation and development and the promotion of a policy of close cooperation with local government are, in summary, the results that are hoped to be achieved from this resolution.
in writing. - one year after the terrible earthquake in haiti, one of the most devastating natural disasters in human history, the signs of the disaster are still deep. incredibly, a few months after the tragic earthquake, the arrival of a hurricane brought cholera epidemics, further exacerbating the already complicated political crisis. my decision to vote in favour of the resolution is firstly about the need to mobilise interventions and actions to ensure that the country receives full assistance which can bring it back to a situation that is at least viable. the current civil and political tensions only add to the concern, as they create obstacles to the delivery of humanitarian aid from the eu, thus slowing down the pace of reconstruction. i therefore believe that the full availability of the european institutions is a duty and a must, at least to guarantee these deprived populations housing, medical care, food and the provision of basic social services. only with our help can those people slowly return to a normal life.
in writing. - of all the disasters that have struck our planet in 2010, the earthquake in haiti left the most difficult wound to heal. today, one year after the second most devastating earthquake in human history, the signs of the disaster are still painfully evident. more than 1 million people, half of them children, still live in slums and tent cities, and a cholera epidemic last october killed more than 4,000 people. there is still a lack of food, access to clean water, health services and education. of the $500 billion promised by governments and private individuals, very little has come to fruition, only $6 billion, the rest has never materialized! the adoption today of this joint resolution is an important step towards meeting the challenges of the future together. if nature destroys, man has to rebuild. these words should be the stimulus to increase our commitment even more.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the motto of the european parliament is: 'unity in diversity' is the guiding principle which must guide all our activities inside and outside the european union. it is in accordance with this principle that i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, because i believe that, while not wishing to interfere in the internal affairs of another state, the european parliament must always be able to express its views, acting as a sounding board for the expression of demands common to all european citizens. the resolution adopted today is a statement of parliament's common position with the lithuanian legislature, which calls for amendments to the draft law amending the code of administrative offences to punish 'public promotion of homosexual relations', with the real risk, as the text clearly states, of criminalising any public expression, representation or information about homosexuality. i therefore believe that it is our duty today, as members of parliament, but even earlier as citizens, to ask the lithuanian parliament to reject the new legislation, in the name of the indispensable principle of the protection of fundamental human rights.
in writing. − in 2010, the lithuanian parliament voted an amendment to the administrative code implementing the law on the protection of minors from harmful effects of public information, adopted in 2009. this amendment would prevent the mass media from promoting sexual relations or other homosexual behaviour, which is not already provided for by the constitution or the civil code, also in view of the influence that the mass media have on the formation and education processes of minors. article 10 of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms states that everyone has the right to freedom of expression. the exercise of this freedom, however, carries with it duties and responsibilities and may be subject to sanctions provided for by law, as measures necessary to better protect public morals. too often the mass media, driven by market dynamics, do not seem to be interested in children, as they are particularly susceptible to emotional influence. the common objective must be to develop a greater focus on childhood and adolescence issues and this requires cooperation with all the professionals involved in the information world, in order to develop a solid collective responsibility.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i supported this agreement because climate change and pollution, which originated in the industrialized regions, have unfortunately long since reached the arctic region. this area, often portrayed as pristine, has unfortunately not been so for many years. unlike the antarctic, this region is inhabited and its natural resources have traditionally been exploited to the detriment of the environment. in 1996, in an attempt to stem the tide, the arctic council for the protection of the environment in this region was created, which also includes 3 eu member states - sweden, denmark and finland. the economies of the emerging countries will increasingly need the resources that this area is rich in. energy, minerals, fish, gas, oil, wind and wave energy are all resources of which the arctic is very rich, and which therefore expose it to new speculation.

in writing. - the objective of diversifying transit is set out in paragraph 39 of this report. the strategic importance of the nabucco project is explicitly mentioned. while recognising the importance of this project, i would like to stress the need to give equal status to other southern corridor projects (itgi, tap and white stream) and also to recall the key role of south stream in helping to achieve the objective of diversification. moreover, as regards the oil pipelines, in addition to the constanta-trieste pipeline already mentioned, the key role of the samsun-ceyhan pipeline, already recognised by commissioner oettinger, is essential to reduce traffic in the bosphorus strait and thus also to reduce the risk of environmental accidents in the black sea (odessa conference, 27 july 2010). only by considering all the possible paths, not just some, can the objective of diversifying energy sources be finally achieved and thus guarantee energy independence for europe.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, given its strategic position as a bridge between europe, central asia and the middle east, the black sea region is of great importance to the european union. if we add to these purely geographical considerations the fact that many countries in the region are also member states of the union, we can better understand why europe has been working for several years now to strengthen its relations with the countries of this area. the ungureanu report aims to achieve a strategy by both the commission and the european external action service to define an ever closer cooperation relationship between the eu and the black sea region. however, this relationship will have to be subject to strict controls in order to maintain effective coordination of activities and division of tasks. i believe that the success of such an important partnership is in some way dependent on the achievement of a peaceful settlement of the conflicts that are currently taking place. finally, i would like to emphasize the part of the report which calls on the union to promote strategies to strengthen the institutions of the black sea countries, because i believe that respect for democracy must be at the heart of such relations.
in writing. − the strategic importance of the black sea region has been recognised since 2007; in the context of the accession of romania and bulgaria to the eu, the black sea has begun to have a direct impact on the union's internal affairs, which is why its greater involvement in the area would be necessary. in my view, the implementation of a strategy aimed at developing greater cooperation between the eu and the region is an objective which the community should set itself as soon as possible. this initiative, called synergy, could become an area of stability, security, democracy and prosperity. in line with the european parliament, i voted in favour of supporting the creation and launch of the black sea synergy. i believe that, while respecting human rights and fundamental freedoms in the region, it is possible to promote the economic, social and cultural development of the region by further liberalizing trade and intensifying intra-regional trade. in the interests of development and greater integration between the member states, i am encouraging, by my consent, the growth and development of the black sea through an action plan with clear objectives and initiatives of excellence.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in 2007, with the accession of romania and bulgaria to the eu, parts of the black sea coast became european. in the same year, a new european policy was created, the black sea synergy, which is committed to promoting stability, security, democracy and prosperity in the region. the european parliament already expressed its support for the creation of such synergy in 2008 and, in parallel, called for the development of a concrete action plan for the area with a view to achieving a number of tangible objectives; unfortunately, it is now clear that the project has been partially unsuccessful, partly due to the lack of transparency of the funds made available. a specific budget line should therefore be provided for as soon as possible, with clear rules for the disbursement of funds, so that the needs and specific features of the territory are taken into account. the local authorities, business communities and ngos in the area need to be more involved. the potential for economic and social growth in the black sea region must be developed by starting from areas such as lifelong learning, adapting teaching to the needs of the labour market and planning an interregional trade strategy that is able to increase international trade.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, parliament is called upon to give its opinion on two agreements signed with the united states and 11 latin american countries, which are involved in a long and troubled affair. the european union has been called into question in the world trade organisation and, above all, has failed. the subject is very sensitive because the disputes concern the principle of non-discrimination in international trade relations, which europe allegedly violated in the organization of banana imports within the union. this is due to a double track, a double system applied to the acp countries, different from that applied to other countries. a system which allowed these countries to introduce this product onto the european market without paying any duty, unlike the other countries which were required to pay duties of eur 176 per tonne. this agreement thus restores balance to the situation and, above all, preserves the right of the acp countries, which are fragile developing countries, to import their products into the union without paying import duties. at the same time, the other countries that have signed the agreements will be able to export bananas within the union with the payment of duties, which will however be progressively reduced, over a period of time from 2011 to 2017, from the current eur 176 per tonne to a final level of eur 114. but what is more important is that these agreements, in addition to finally making the union compliant with the commitments it has made as a member of the world trade organisation, and thus restoring some institutional credibility as well, have a particular focus on these acp countries in delicate development conditions, because they also provide for new financial support instruments in their favour. these instruments will enable these countries to invest to diversify their production and thus, hopefully, to strengthen their economies. these measures, which have a weight of eur 190 million, are for the time being planned until 2013. i believe that these agreements are positive, not only because they define disputes which undermine the union with economic consequences, sanctions and, as i said earlier, institutional credibility, but also because they allow for a balanced solution which respects those acp countries and european producers - i am thinking of the outermost regions - who certainly cannot be left to unbridled competition. i therefore propose that parliament give its assent to these agreements, but ask the council and the commission to commit themselves first of all to providing as soon as possible an assessment of the impact that the agreements will have between now and 2020, with a broad time horizon, on the acp countries and on the producers in europe - i am thinking of the outermost regions - whose economies are closely linked to this fruit, but also to commit themselves firmly to giving an assessment of the operation of the financial accompanying measures specifically dedicated to the acp countries a year and a half before their expiry, so that action may be taken with another instrument of aid and support in relation to these countries, so that they are not left alone and are supported to combat, counter and mitigate in some way the possible negative consequences of the entry into force of these agreements, with a correlation of the prices and therefore the competitiveness of products coming from other countries within the union. i therefore believe that the agreement, by resolving an age-old question, certainly allows at this moment to see a way out which also respects these weaker countries, which, i repeat, have always been the main concern we have had in mind, also during the long debate in the committee on international trade, and which i hope will find strong support and a good solution in these accompanying measures and above all in the monitoring and commitment that we as a parliament ask the commission and the council to make on the impact of the agreement, on the functioning of the aid measures and possibly on their prolongation or strengthening for the future.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, bilateral trade agreements are often concluded to the detriment of european producers, who suffer from the liberalization of imports. the agreements to be voted on tomorrow include a reduction in import duties on bananas from latin america. these agreements have helped to resolve a ten-year conflict but they risk putting european banana producers in serious difficulty. it is clear that the tariff reductions negotiated with the latin american countries, together with the acp support programme and the accompanying measures programme in the banana sector, are likely to seriously undermine the competitiveness of european producers. so far, the financial support, the support for our banana producers, has been provided through the posei programme, but the last reform of the posei programme, which dates from 2006, does not take any account of the conclusion of these agreements. i therefore think it is appropriate to invite the council to consider the need to identify appropriate instruments and resources to cover the financial needs of european producers, improving their status and at the same time seeking to compensate for any damage resulting from the conclusion of agreements and the reduction of duties. i do not think it is possible to proceed with the annual search for resources to meet the needs of european banana producers, but i believe that a stable and lasting solution must be found to compensate for the damage caused by enlargement and the opening up of markets.
