in writing. − the waiver of the immunity of a member of the european parliament is always a sensitive issue to deal with, but in some cases requests for waiver must be analysed within the remit of a member of the european parliament. i do not think that a request for the waiver of parliamentary immunity on the basis of a simple complaint alleging public statements which are considered defamatory can be a valid reason. it is also clear from the immunity regulation that the charges against mr deutsch relate to opinions expressed in the course of his duties as a member of the european parliament; mr deutsch was therefore exercising his duties as a member of parliament by expressing his opinion on a matter of public interest to his constituents. we cannot try to prevent a member from expressing his views on matters of legitimate public interest and that is why i voted in favour of mr speroni's text against the waiver of mr deutsch's immunity.

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i fully agree with the decision to re-propose the same amendments which were adopted at first reading and rejected by the council. the proposal, which is part of the wider context of the interinstitutional negotiations on the use of delegated acts in the instruments for financing external action, aims to safeguard the prerogatives of parliament as provided for in the lisbon treaty and, at the same time, to ensure effective control over the implementation of eu legislation. the council's objections to the applicability of the procedure under article 290 tfeu to the instruments in question not only show an unjustified refusal by the council to recognise the role of parliament as co-legislator in the adoption of strategic decisions on the management of financial instruments, but also end up by legitimising an unacceptable democratic deficit in the implementation of community legislation. the council's refusal is contrary to the letter and spirit of the lisbon treaty. i therefore believe that it is necessary, for reasons of legal as well as political expediency, to insist on the adoption of the proposed amendments, so as to strengthen the role of parliament and to ensure that it is placed on an equal footing with the council, while respecting the respective competences and the legislative changes introduced by the treaty.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, bananas are the fourth most important crop in the world, after rice, wheat and maize, and they make a decisive contribution to food security. in december 2009, the european union, a group of latin american countries and the united states reached an agreement on the tariff regime applicable to imports of bananas into the union. the signing of this agreement put an end to one of the longest-running disputes in the recent history of the multilateral trading system. in fact, in the recent past, banana import policies have been the subject of a decade-long dispute within the wto between the eu and several latin american banana-producing countries and the united states. we cannot, however, ignore the possibility that the change in tariff rates resulting from the application of the agreement will have a negative impact on the livelihood of the union's banana producers. i therefore urge the commission to carry out a serious and independent impact study in the coming months to assess the possible negative effects and consequences of the entry into force of the agreement for european banana producers and, if necessary, to revise the aid measures provided for under the posei programme.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that an essential aspect of a globalised economy is the efficient and innovative use of energy, materials and resources. with reference to the report under discussion, i would remind you that waste electrical and electronic equipment (weee) is the fastest growing waste stream in the european union. the current weee directive requires member states to separate the collection of electrical and electronic equipment and sets recovery and recycling targets. the analysis carried out in the context of the revision process of this directive has revealed a number of problems in its application. in particular, the problem of extending the scope of the directive arises. experience shows that the scope of the directive has been interpreted and applied in a highly heterogeneous way by the member states and that it is not advisable to establish a definitive list of products, since the electrical and electronic products sector is a rapidly changing market which would require a continuous revision of the directive, without it ever being able to be truly updated. i therefore believe that it is essential to work towards better harmonisation of the weee directive and to reduce the administrative costs borne by small and mediumsized enterprises in the sector, without compromising the level of environmental protection.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i fully share the aim of this directive and i am convinced of the need to separate waste in order to reduce the environmental impact and increase recycling. two steps are required for this: used household appliances must be disposed of properly and their management optimised. the directive addresses both points, with absolutely identical aims. however, i must point out some criticisms. firstly, the objectives set are too ambitious and could be counterproductive. i also think that the cost of disposal should be included in a wider scheme of incentives and penalties, and that it should be transparent to those who will have to bear it. nevertheless, some points of considerable interest also emerge. i believe, for example, that information should be given to consumers in the most effective way possible, to avoid bad manners due to misinformation. in view of the objectives and general scheme of the directive, i am in favour of approval. i am sure, however, that there is room for improvement in the details, and i am referring in particular to the additional charges for traders in connection with the collection of small equipment for disposal. with these interventions we are playing with the health of the environment and the sustainability of our lifestyle.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for a directive to be voted on today concerns the amendment of the weee directive, which requires member states to separate the collection of electrical and electronic equipment and sets recovery and recycling targets, including the fixing of a collection rate of 65% of weee, to be achieved by 2016. as is well known, the efficient and innovative use of energy, materials and resources is a fundamental aspect of a globalised economy. it is a responsibility which concerns all those involved in the market, from public authorities to consumers and producers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the current crisis. i also believe that it is essential, in addition to the commitment to comply with the commission's instructions, to avoid burdensome administrative obligations and the imposition of excessively burdensome requirements on producers, distributors and retailers.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on the revision of the directive on waste electrical and electronic equipment was intended to encourage the separate collection, recovery and recycling of this type of waste. theoretically, therefore, this line should have been supported. however, some amendments have been made to the report, which are very burdensome, especially for small traders who are obliged to bear new bureaucratic costs and obligations which are difficult to sustain, and for this reason i have decided to vote against the proposal.
in writing. - electrical and electronic equipment is now a huge category of consumer goods and therefore also a huge amount of waste with risks, considering the type of waste, of serious damage to the environment and the health of citizens. the report on the proposal for a directive on waste electrical and electronic equipment aims to regulate at european level the collection of waste electrical and electronic equipment and its treatment and recycling, by setting out the quantities and percentages. i therefore supported the report by mr florenz, which requires member states to separate the collection of electrical waste by at least 4 kg per inhabitant per year, to reach a quorum of 65% for separate collection by 2016 and to recycle at least 5% of materials, also in order to avoid the waste of raw materials.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this vote updates the 2003 waste electrical and electronic equipment directive by addressing issues such as the consistent application of the relevant provisions, the simplification of the rules and the reduction of administrative costs. the final objective, as already envisaged by the envi committee, is to collect 85% of weee waste electrical and electronic equipment by 2016, recycling between 50% and 75% of it depending on the category. the aim of the text approved is not only to recover valuable raw materials but also to stem the illegal flow of e-waste outside the eu, which poses risks to health and the environment when treated below minimum standards. it will now be essential to reach an agreement with the council, which has promised to reconsider its position after today's vote.

president-in-office of the council. − mr president, it is a privilege and an honour for me to address this distinguished audience today. as mr lehne has just mentioned, the presence of the presidency on a monday bears witness to the importance of the issue. first of all, i would like to thank the european parliament for its constructive approach with regard to the council’s efforts to improve conditions for obtaining patent protection in the european union. i also wish to extend our gratitude to the former belgian presidency for its relentless efforts to further the cause of the creation of a unitary patent protection. second, i would like to report that this morning the council decided, by an overwhelming majority, to request your consent for the authorisation of enhanced cooperation in this field. subject to your consent, the competiveness council on 10 march is expected to give its authorisation. the hungarian presidency attaches particular importance to improving the eu’s competitiveness and to supporting small- and medium-sized enterprises operating in the eu. it is our joint responsibility to help them with innovation, which is one of the driving forces of competitiveness of smes both at european level and globally. it has been clear from the outset that one of the key elements in fulfilling this objective would be the creation of an eu patent, which has been delayed for more than 30 years. maintaining the status quo is not an option. millions of euros are spent every year on translations and on administrative paperwork to obtain patent protection in the 27 different legal systems in the eu, while in the us an inventor can acquire a patent for the entire us territory for an amount equivalent to 1 850 euros. in the eu it costs 20 000 euros for only 13 member states. according to calculations, european enterprises suffer a loss of seven to eight hundred million euros because of the lack of an eu patent. needless to say, this amount could be put to much better use if channelled, for example, into technological research. there is currently no internal market in terms of patent protection. the applicant is obliged to work with 27 separate national legal systems. as a result, in practice, protection is often sought only in a certain part of the eu territory, thus creating serious problems in terms of the free circulation of goods, which are protected by a patent in some jurisdictions but can be freely produced in others. our clear preference has always been the creation of a truly eu-wide patent that would cover the territory of all 27 member states. we profoundly regret that negotiations relating to the linguistic regime have resulted in a stalemate, with no prospect of reaching the necessary consensus in the foreseeable future. i also need to stress that eu decision-makers are under pressure to make rapid progress in this field. the freshly-released innovation union scoreboard confirms that there is already a yawning gap between the innovation performance of the us and japan and that of the eu, and the major emerging economies are rapidly catching up. although patenting rules are not the only factor determining innovation activity, their importance is obvious to all. each year we keep on working with the current set of rules, our fragmented system becomes less attractive and competitive. under these circumstances the overwhelming majority of the member states consider that the creation of unitary patent protection within the framework of enhanced cooperation is the only way forward for the time being. 27 member states have submitted official requests with a view to establishing enhanced cooperation. their clear expectation is that visible results be achieved within a reasonable time. as the presidency-in-office we will do our utmost to make substantial progress in the field. on the other hand, the presidency has to pay attention to the objections and reservations voiced by spain and italy too. let me turn now to address the distinguished spanish and italian members of this house in their mother tongue. en primer lugar, a los distinguidos diputados de nuestro socio españa. tenemos la confianza de que, mediante la cooperación reforzada, con la creación del sistema de protección unitaria de patentes, damos un paso importante hacia una situación ideal, en la que el sistema de protección unitaria de patentes abarca a todos los países miembros y a todo el territorio de la unión europea. mi rivolgo adesso ai nostri amici italiani. tengo a sottolineare, per evitare ogni sorta di equivoco, che nessuna impresa e nessun individuo, indipendentemente dallo stato di origine, saranno esclusi dai benefici del futuro brevetto unitario. mr president, thank you for your patience. i very much look forward to working with parliament in the future on this subject.
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the approval which president lehne is proposing you give to this enhanced cooperation will, if you will, represent a decisive step towards making life easier for european companies and inventors by finally uniting patent protection in europe. it is an incredible weakness and, i believe, unacceptable for the competitiveness of our continent in this extremely tough global competition, that we are not able to protect inventions or creations better and at a reasonable cost, especially in the industrial field. that is why, from the time i was heard before you on 13 january 2010, and on several occasions, i had pledged to take this matter forward so that i could be - it was a kind of wish i had expressed - the last european commissioner to raise this issue. we made a proposal. thanks to the willingness and intelligence of the belgian presidency, it has been completed, strengthened and improved, and we have not - as you know - met the unanimity i had hoped for on this matter. this is why and how the idea of enhanced cooperation was born in the new lisbon treaty. the commission has responded swiftly to the request for enhanced cooperation which was initially addressed to it, as president lehne said, by a dozen member states. as i speak, 25 member states have agreed to this enhanced cooperation. the hungarian presidency, after the belgian presidency, has also shown a great deal of willingness, and i thank it for that. it wants this cooperation to start in march and i am very grateful to parliament, and in particular to you, mr president, klaus-heiner lehne, and to the members of your committee, for the leading role you are playing, together with the committee on legal affairs, in moving this work forward and reaching a rapid conclusion on this matter. the commission wishes to see enhanced cooperation extended to as many countries as possible, and i hope that all the member states will finally support this proposal, which is, i repeat, politically acceptable to all countries and economically necessary for all businesses. it is by being as broad as possible, and if possible unanimous, that this advance will bring the greatest number of benefits to european enterprises and inventors. as commissioner for the internal market, i will ensure that enhanced cooperation remains compatible with the treaties, in particular with the rules governing the functioning of the internal market. this means, ladies and gentlemen, that unitary patent protection - as mrs győri has very well said in italian and spanish - will be available to all companies in the union, regardless of their member state of establishment. there will be no discrimination. in addition, the benefits of unitary protection will be the same for all inventors and innovative enterprises in the union, both in terms of simplified procedures and reduced translation costs. an overall impact analysis of this project has already been carried out and we are currently working on a thorough assessment of its economic impacts. in conclusion, the commission, which regrets that an agreement at 27 has not yet been possible, will do everything possible to implement this enhanced cooperation quickly, as soon as the council of ministers in march has taken a decision by presenting the draft regulations which are necessary for the implementation of this enhanced cooperation, so that we can very quickly bring this real added value to european businesses. i thank you in advance for your attention and support of this proposal.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the transition to a low-carbon economy and the achievement of the objectives set out in the climate package require the definition of rules to regulate co2 emissions in various sectors, including the automotive sector. i am very pleased with the negotiations which led to the agreement with the council on the emission limit of 147 grams of co2/km by 2020. this is a feasible limit and a good balance between environmental, social and industrial standards. i hope that i too have made a contribution as a shadow rapporteur in the itre committee. the agreement reached takes account not only of the economic crisis in the sector but also reasonably takes account of the difference between the car sector and that of light commercial vehicles. as with the cars regulation, the european car industry will be able to develop green, competitive and environmentally friendly technology for light commercial vehicles. i hope that it will also take up the environmental challenge and invest even more in innovation and research.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal initially set a long-term emission limit for light commercial vehicles of 135 grams of co2/km by 2020. in the unanimous opinion of the manufacturers, it was technically impossible to comply with this limit. if the text were to be adopted as it stands, the co2 reduction would be 0.00014 per cent worldwide, with a very high economic impact of over eur 45 billion for europe alone, which would inevitably lead to an increase in prices of about eur 3800 on average per vehicle. despite the criticisms, an agreement was reached at first reading with the council setting the emission limit by 2020 at 147 gr/km co2, subject to feasibility which the commission will have to verify by january 2013. however, this decision is purely political and does not take into account actual industrial, market or consumer conditions. we will vote against this because we believe that the economic impact is excessive compared to the insignificant reduction in co2 emissions worldwide.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the negotiations which i conducted the first year alone and then, in the conciliation phase - i would like to recall that this was the first conciliation after lisbon - with the leadership of vice-president kratsa-tsagaropoulou and the support of the chairman of the tran committee, mr brian simpson, were more arduous and difficult than expected. the 70 million european bus passengers will also benefit from a whole range of rights which have been very limited or almost nonexistent compared to other modes of transport. the objectives we set ourselves in the negotiations with the three presidencies that have taken turns on this important dossier were the following: a regulation protecting non-discriminatory access to bus transport; a regulation which took account of the specific characteristics of the sector, which employs small and medium-sized enterprises on which it was not possible to impose additional and excessive economic burdens; a regulation to cover a regulatory gap which placed the bus transport sector in an anomalous position compared with other modes of transport and thus ensured minimum guarantees for all passengers; a regulation to protect the rights of persons with reduced mobility as best as possible, given the rigid conditions prevailing in the council; a regulation that takes account of the needs of an ageing population for which public transport will be an indispensable resource in the coming decades. the text put to the vote today is the result of a compromise which has been very difficult, but which we are satisfied with in view of the direction taken by the debate and the negotiations themselves. the main problems were mainly in defining the scope of application. the regulation applies to all regular services, whether regional, national or crossborder, covering distances of more than 250 km. however, a list of fundamental rights is provided for which cannot be derogated from, irrespective of this distance. these rights mainly focus on the right to transport, training, information and liability. as regards the 250 km distance, the regulation essentially provides for compensation and assistance in the event of an accident, the rights of passengers in the event of cancellation or delay, and the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility. in addition, as regards complaints, carriers shall establish and implement a complaint handling mechanism for the rights and obligations set out in this regulation. the time needed to provide a final response may not exceed three months from receipt of the complaint. finally, each member state must designate a new body - preferably one that already exists - to be responsible for the application of this regulation. member states may derogate from the application for a period of four years, renewable once, after notifying the european commission of the reasons. the member states are also urged and invited to develop in future a single ticket for each mode of transport and a single national body responsible for passenger rights for all modes of transport. the final text can be considered a satisfactory and balanced compromise. the outcome of the conciliation procedure must be considered a success for parliament.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i too thank mr cancian for his commitment to this difficult compromise. this regulation also allows bus passengers to enjoy rights similar to those of passengers on other means of transport, such as trains or ships. the regulation, which applies to all national or crossborder services where the distance to be covered is equal to or greater than 250 kilometres, also protects passengers using regular services over shorter distances. i am referring in particular to disabled persons or persons with reduced mobility, who have been granted non-discriminatory access to transport and have been provided with the right to compensation in the event of loss or damage to wheelchairs and disability training for bus staff. i am also pleased that an agreement has also been reached on compensation in the event of death, including a reasonable sum for funeral expenses and personal injury, loss of or damage to luggage due to accidents. i also regard it as a positive factor that the passenger can choose between continuing the journey without paying any additional charges and being reimbursed for the ticket price in the event of cancelled departure, delay of more than two hours or overbooking. as regards passenger information, i think it would have been useful to provide passengers with information on coincidences with other means of transport, thus also ensuring a dialogue between passenger transport services by bus and those by rail. finally, i am pleased that the negotiations have succeeded in finding and guaranteeing the best possible assistance for disabled people and persons with reduced mobility, by giving them the opportunity to choose an accompanying person without incurring any additional costs.
member of the commission. − madam president, i should like to thank the honourable members for their mostly positive comments. we now face the challenge of implementation. we face this challenge with all passenger rights legislation. fine-tuning the legislation will of course be a long process for us, but i still think that the compromise we have achieved will probably be adopted in a future document and is a great opening. it is also a matter of principle that we have introduced certain principles of passenger rights into bus and coach transport, which is such a large area. modest compromises will probably be needed; everything must be fine-tuned and must be implemented, but it is a very important opening and i hope that you will vote in favour of this regulation.

madam president, the aim of the services directive, which came into force in december 2006, is to open up the market to service providers in the european union by eliminating all protectionist barriers, arbitrary obstacles and any discriminatory rules. the european parliament has always insisted, however, that this directive must not be used as a pretext for dangerous deregulation and liberalization of the sector, thus undermining the rights of workers. the country of origin principle, which has been criticised as a precursor to social dumping, has been abolished and replaced by the country of destination principle. i voted in favour of this report because, as regards the transposition of the directive by the member states, it has the merit of pointing out unjustified delays and shortcomings, as well as some disputes concerning its interpretation and application. i shall end here, madam president, because it is rather difficult to speak in these circumstances.
madam president, i voted against the adoption and application of the services directive, the so-called bolkenstein directive, with all my heart. the aim of the directive was to produce greater competition in europe by providing aid for the development of small and mediumsized enterprises. unfortunately, however, the real objective has been to take over and attack our companies, which are small and mediumsized enterprises. in italy we have sectors which are of excellence, such as the bathing areas, where the owners have invested all their assets and for which they have made enormous sacrifices. now, thanks to this directive, they've lost everything. this is not the system to be implemented in a europe of bureaucrats and large industrial groups, of multinationals that want to penetrate italian territory and overwhelm our companies. we cannot afford that and i will stand by these small and mediumsized enterprises and defend them, because we are committed to our traditions and to italian excellence.
mr president, the commission proposal for a regulation presented in 2008 was intended to introduce new rights at european level to protect bus passengers comparable to those applied in other modes of transport, thus ensuring a level playing field between carriers and between the different modes of transport in the various member states. it took a long and difficult negotiation with the council, including the conciliation procedure, to reach the text voted on today. the final text can be considered a very satisfactory and well-balanced compromise, since it succeeds in guaranteeing the rights of passengers without at the same time imposing a heavy burden on the carriers, which - we must not forget - are mostly small and mediumsized enterprises. the outcome of the conciliation procedure can rightly be considered a success for the european parliament in that some of our main demands have been met, namely the scope, the fundamental rights of passengers regardless of distance, derogations and, finally, the cases of accidents, cancellations and delays through the provision of appropriate forms of reimbursement, assistance and compensation for passengers.
mr president, we are entering a new era of rights, rights which could have been more widely spread. we must be aware that, below 250 kilometres, the rights of the weakest, the disabled, the elderly and those with reduced mobility are not addressed in this measure. while it is true that uniform quality standards are established, it is also true that the exclusion of local transport greatly limits the number of travellers involved. the implementation over the next four years will allow the sector to prepare itself better, but it will be necessary to keep an eye on the establishment of the implementing bodies. the outcome of this work is a success for parliament and a positive sign of attention to the needs of citizens. but compromise is always a mediation - in this case, a downward mediation - of the will of this house. we have shown that we are good interpreters of needs, unlike the council, which has shown itself to be the sole bearer of interests.
mr president, i would like to congratulate mr cancian on the excellent work he has done in bringing this measure to fruition. mr mastella will allow me to disagree with him in that i think this is a great achievement for our citizens. it cannot be denied that citizens are protected only when they travel more than 250 kilometres by tram or bus. where is the protection of the rights of the citizens of europe, which - as mrs gesine meissner has already said - includes whole states such as cyprus, luxembourg and malta, which are excluded from this protection? that is why our group voted in abstention. we did not vote against because certain positive rights are protected, such as those of the disabled and of people with reduced mobility. that is why we abstained. but for the rest, we ask that the matter be brought back as soon as possible so that the rights of citizens can be protected in a real way.
mr president, i congratulate mr cancian on the excellent work he has done and in particular on the good result achieved in the conciliation procedure with the council. the compromise reached, both in terms of the scope of the directive and the inclusion of 12 fundamental rights in the proposal, represents an important step forward in the protection of passenger rights. the rights and needs of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility have been duly taken into account in the proposal, in particular as regards non-discriminatory access to transport, the right to compensation in the event of loss of or damage to mobility equipment, the lodging and handling of complaints, disability training for bus staff, information to be provided during the journey. the final text also succeeded in guaranteeing passenger rights without at the same time burdening the industry's carriers, which, being largely small and medium-sized enterprises, could not have borne heavy burdens on their own.
madam president, the path that led to the vote on this report today was a long one and i therefore join my colleagues in congratulating mr cancian, who has made this path in a very stubborn way. all modes of transport now finally have their own regulations on passenger rights. i think the next step is to draw up a single text, which will bring together all these different regulations. the scope is reasonable, although we would have dealt with it on other grounds, but the fact that we have succeeded in including almost all european countries except two is certainly a positive thing, as is the fact that many articles have been made compulsory even below 250 kilometres, and this without any other compensation. in the debate this morning some colleagues made claims which have fortunately been refuted by the present speeches, namely that there was no adequate protection for passengers with reduced mobility. the commission has already taken a number of steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
madam president, the council has submitted a proposal for a decision authorizing an enhanced cooperation procedure in the area of the establishment of unitary patent protection, because some member states, including italy and spain, have repeatedly expressed their opposition to the adoption of the proposed translation system, i.e. a trilingual system, which would end up being truly discriminatory, since it clearly violates the principle of linguistic equality of all the official languages of the union. despite the many negotiations that have taken place so far and the vote this morning, it seems impossible to adopt the regulation unanimously. however, legal and institutional reasons would suggest, or would have suggested, that we await the opinion of the court of justice, due in the next few days, which could not only clarify a number of technical aspects of the unified patent system but also highlight all the legal consequences arising from it. it is not the path she has chosen and that is why i voted against it.
mr president, we live in a market where our companies are operating in global competition. the spirit of the reform of the language regime for patents, as announced by the commission, is to reduce the costs of translation in order to be competitive on the markets, especially the asian market, where we are in competition with the united states. i wonder, therefore, whether it would not have been more efficient to patent only one language. this would really help our businesses to compete in the global market. as is well known, there are two legal systems in europe at present, with different characteristics and rules. i think it would have been more appropriate to harmonize them. finally, the establishment of enhanced cooperation is not only contrary to the spirit of the european union but also damages the internal market, which is subject to geographical segmentation and distortion of competition between member states, which means that some states will certainly be in less favourable situations than others.
mr president, while i welcome the fact that europe has achieved its objective of acquiring, after many years, an important instrument such as patents, which will finally enable the european union to compete on an equal footing with other territorial entities, i express my deep regret at having to note that this has been achieved at the expense of other entities, such as italy, which have always advocated the strengthening of the union's role. the decision to issue the patent in only one of the three working languages of the patent office will create a disparity between italian companies and those of the countries which are part of the proposed language scheme. i remember that i put a question to the commission a few months ago to defend the use of the italian language. in the meantime, 25 out of 27 countries have complied, which is why i abstained.
mr president, when meucci's patent was not recognized by the american telephone industry a century ago, it was not because of the lack of english or the use of italian, but because of the lack of a requirement: he didn't have the money to register his patent for another annuity. in this sense, we are today faced with a paradoxical situation and, beyond the vote, i believe that the adoption of a patent with trilingualism, which excludes the italian language, is essentially a sign of the weakness of our government, of its inability to influence european policy and of the weakness of our policy, which is reflected above all in research and innovation. in this connection, it is enough to recall the study on competitiveness published last december, which reveals how italy has, in recent years, kindly given away 4 billion euros to other countries that have welcomed our researchers. the italian language is no longer needed by these researchers, because they have learned english, french and german and have all the tools to apply for these same patents, in defiance of italian products.
mr president, i would like to explain the reasons for my vote against today. the creation of the patent will certainly bring benefits to the patent system in europe but the result would have been vastly better if we had conducted the procedure differently. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the current procedure is just a new stage in the long history of patent adoption in the european union, which dates back to 1990, and has been applied for by only 12 member states. i voted against this resolution because it is incompatible with the requirement of last resort laid down in article 20 (2) of the treaty. the commission proposal does not create a uniform title throughout the union as required by article 118, and enhanced cooperation has a negative impact on the establishment of companies and the free movement of capital. it would also have been much more politically elegant and at least appropriate to wait for the decisions of the court of justice scheduled for 8 march. we are probably going to have to reconsider our position as a result of this ruling.
mr president, once again we have seen the inability of the italian government to protect italy's pro-european profile, the interests of business on a crucial issue such as the adoption of the european patent. 25 out of 27 countries and the overwhelming majority of the parliament support a proposal which regulates the subject of patents and which affects the most innovative and most international-oriented companies. the italian self-exclusion from this decision will expose our companies to the risk of not being adequately protected in europe and in the world. it is astonishing that a government which does nothing to spread italian culture throughout the world, cutting funding to cultural institutions and failing to value the language of the country which holds the greatest cultural heritage of humanity, should be using the language issue in a chauvinistic way, when our companies have always demanded that patents be drawn up only in english, which is now the language of use in the global economy. however, one result has been achieved by allowing patent applicants to do so in their own language. mr president, nothing, however, obliged commissioner barnier to force a vote by asking for it in such haste before the opinion of the court of justice, which will be delivered, as we know, in the first week of march and which will deal mainly with two qualifying points, such as the use of the national language to defend oneself before the european union patent court, and the very legitimacy of the establishment of the patent court itself. these are essential questions, as we know, to be resolved before any decision is taken. hence the decision of the italian delegation of the democratic party to abstain.

in writing. - mr president, the potential benefits of implementing the services directive are undeniable. the activities covered by the directive contribute 40% to gdp and jobs in the eu and if properly implemented we could unlock enormous economic potential, creating jobs and contributing to economic recovery. the quality of the implementation of the directive by the member states is as essential as the respect of the deadlines set for this purpose. the european parliament has already shown that it can play a crucial role in the negotiations leading up to the adoption of the directive, and i therefore believe that it must ensure effective monitoring of the implementation of the directive by the member states. european service providers must be able to offer their services anywhere in the european union without being hampered by bureaucratic barriers. however, during the implementation phase we must also pay attention to other aspects, in particular the administrative costs which are currently borne by the states. i agree with the rapporteur that the mutual evaluation procedure introduced by the council imposes unnecessary bureaucratic burdens on member states' administrations at national, regional and local level. i hope that the potential benefits of these procedures will be appreciated as soon as possible, otherwise the high bureaucratic costs will continue to exist.
in writing. − the european services directive came into force in december 2006 with the ambitious aim of opening up the market to service providers in the european union, removing protectionist barriers to the provision of services in the member states and implementing the principle of the free movement of goods and services in the union. the directive requires that european service providers be able to offer their services without any bureaucratic barriers within the european union. the commission's own-initiative report, which parliament is preparing to monitor closely the transposition of the directive into national law, assesses the work done so far by the member states. in particular, it is noted that, in the course of the transposition process, there are delays in the implementation of the directive and significant problems of interpretation relating to its scope. therefore, in order to protect market operators, i urge an urgent and unequivocal delimitation of the services covered by this directive. finally, i believe that the effective implementation of the internal market information system, the extension of functions and the increased computerisation of the single points of sale in the territory would undoubtedly represent a huge advantage for service providers and would make it easier for smes to access information.
in writing. − the aim of this directive, which entered into force in december 2006, is to open up the market to service providers in the european union by eliminating all protectionist barriers, arbitrary obstacles and any discriminatory rules. the european parliament has always insisted that this directive should not be used as a pretext for dangerous deregulation of the sector. i voted in favour of this report which has the merit of pointing out the often unjustified delays and disputes in the transposition of the services directive, which also contribute 40% to gdp and jobs in the eu. it also has the advantage of enabling european companies, especially smes, to provide citizens with better services at competitive prices. a correct and transparent application of the services directive would have the merit of unlocking the enormous economic and job creation potential of the internal market, estimated at between 0.6 and 1.5% of european gdp. and the european union is in dire need of it. the full application of the directive throughout the eu will therefore introduce elements of competition in the internal market which will bring benefits to citizens and businesses.
in writing. − the transposition process of the services directive is based on a delicate process which aims to create transparency and consistency in the member states' systems about the results of the implementation of the services directive and to verify the results in the internal market following transposition. this is the aim of the report, which i have supported, given the need to check the work of the member states. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to the marketing of products for human consumption, which is to be adopted by the end of the year, is designed to ensure that the rules on the marketing of products for human consumption are applied in a uniform manner throughout the community. i just want to remind you that our economy is 75% services and that in a global market these must be our strength. i think that in the future we should see more liberalization, which does not mean no rules, but only more competition.
in writing. the report on the implementation of the services directive was voted on in the house today. the aim of the directive is to open up the market to service providers in the european union, to remove protectionist barriers to the provision of services in the member states and to implement the principle of free movement, which is the basis of the single market: in short, european service providers must be able to offer their services anywhere in the european union without any bureaucratic barriers. mr gebhardt's own-initiative report provides an assessment of the implementation of the services directive, which expired on 28 december 2009 after a three-year period for the implementation of this very important directive, which entered into force on 28 december 2006. the report by the rapporteur shows that some member states have not yet adopted all the horizontal legislation required for the proper application of the directive, which is why there is still work to be done to try to make all the mechanisms provided for in the services directive operational.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the full implementation of a dynamic services market is one of the fundamental priorities of the european union. today, despite the significant progress made by the single market, services account for only one fifth of total trade within europe, and only 8% of european smes operate in other member states. the figures in the single market communication adopted by the commission last october are clear: the commission has already proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the services provided by the public sector. this can only be achieved by the development and implementation of common rules. in the current crisis, we need to harness the growth potential that exists by helping businesses to grow, innovate and create more jobs. only then will we be able to offer better and more competitive services to both consumers and businesses. the single market in services must be a tool for boosting economic growth, regaining consumer confidence and ensuring reliable products for all.
in writing. - i can only support mr chancian's report on the text in question, where the institutional debate is centred not only on the creation of a common basis for guaranteeing the protection of the rights of bus passengers, but also on the mobility needs of the handicapped and disabled. in this connection, bus companies are required to equip and train themselves to provide minimal assistance to disabled persons or persons with reduced mobility, without prejudice to the burden on the passenger of informing the company in advance of his needs, not less than 36 hours before departure. the compromise seems to set common minimum standards which are very favourable to passengers, without imposing excessive burdens on carriers, most of which are small and mediumsized enterprises.
in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur, mr cancian, on the excellent work he has done, which has enabled a satisfactory and well-balanced compromise to be reached. the report also guarantees the rights of passengers on buses and coaches, the only ones not specifically protected at european level. i therefore voted in favour of this document, which i also appreciate the attention it has paid to the motor vehicle companies active in this sector. the agreements reached have avoided placing an undue burden on the carriers, which are very often family-run and small. at the same time, i think it is important that the european union should put in place precise regulations, so that a charter of passenger rights can be drawn up soon, with particular attention to the needs of disabled people and people with reduced mobility.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, after a difficult diplomatic process between the council and parliament, it is only today that we can finally launch the report drawn up by mr cancian. my vote was in favour because this report will enable the eu to require individual member states to legislate on this subject in accordance with the guidelines provided in the report which focus on greater respect for bus passengers. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of public transport services, including the introduction of a european public transport service. the report is a good compromise and what i would like to stress most is that the right attention has been paid to the rights of disabled people by calling for greater assistance from bus companies for all disabled people or those with reduced mobility. with the entry into force of this legislation, citizens will be entitled to clear and common rules on what is also covered by compensation for any damage or reimbursement in the event of delay in respect of scheduled times.
in writing. - the conciliation work carried out by mr cancian on the passenger rights regulation has led to the adoption of a european regulatory framework for the protection of bus and coach passengers which goes hand in hand with the creation of a single transport market. the legislative vacuum has so far left regulation to national legislation, to the detriment of competition, given the various disparities, and to the detriment of disabled and/or reduced-mobility citizens whose rights will now be guaranteed by the union. i voted in favour of the text because i consider it to be a great piece of work which, through a good compromise, takes european transport policies a good step forward, succeeding not only in guaranteeing the rights of passengers but also in not putting too much pressure on the transport companies that sell the service.
in writing. the report on passenger rights in bus and coach transport was voted on in the house today. in december 2008, the commission presented a proposal for a regulation on passenger rights in bus transport. the commission's proposal aims to introduce eu-wide rights to protect passengers comparable to those applied in other modes of transport and to ensure equal conditions of competition between carriers in the various member states and between the different modes of transport. the main points agreed at the conciliation committee were: scope; time-limited derogations; compensation and assistance in the event of an accident; passengers' rights in the event of cancellation or delay; and the rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility. the final text can be considered very satisfactory and well balanced, since it succeeds in guaranteeing the rights of passengers without at the same time imposing a heavy burden on carriers, most of which are small and mediumsized enterprises. in particular, the outcome of the conciliation procedure can be considered a success for parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution which finally recognises and protects the rights of passengers in all modes of transport, thus putting users at the centre of transport policy. better protection of passenger rights helps to encourage the use of public transport and encourages healthier competition between operators, encouraging them to develop more competitive services. it is important to emphasise that the new regulation will be applied in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity. two important new features are the provision for financial compensation in the event of accidents to persons and damage to or loss of luggage and the guarantee of assistance in the event of delays or interruptions to travel on model trains and aircraft. the final text recognises and protects travellers, with particular attention to passengers with reduced mobility and disabled persons, and ensures appropriate information and services. it is also important to stress that there will be no new costs for the companies in the sector, which have been shielded from the risk of unsustainable adaptation costs, thus ensuring a fair balance between passenger rights and guarantees for small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. - finally, this regulation lays down the rights of passengers in bus transport. although the commission proposed such a regulation in 2008, it is only now that a good compromise has been found, so that the only mode of transport that did not yet have rules to protect passengers has them. particular attention has been paid to disabled people and persons with reduced mobility. the only criticism of the measure concerned the scope of the rules, which applied only to routes longer than 250 km. assistance in the event of delays will include the provision of meals, drinks and alternative transport. if a service is suspended, not only must the traveller be reimbursed but, if necessary, an overnight service must also be provided for a maximum of two nights. the maximum amount of compensation for loss of or damage to baggage shall be eur 1200.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr antonio cancian's report because it will finally lay down the basic principles for guaranteeing the rights of the 70 million european citizens who travel by bus or coach in europe every year and who have been waiting for a long time to see their rights regulated. whatever the means of transport chosen, european citizens will be protected and protected by the european commission's commitment to review the existing regulations and to harmonize them into a single legislation, which provides for common standards for each type of journey and specific features depending on the means of transport chosen.

in writing. − within the european strategy to combat pollution and climate change, co2 emissions reduction targets for vehicles are an important aspect. the light commercial vehicles pollute only a small part of the whole transport category, but in each specific sector limits must be defined to achieve the objectives set, which is why i voted in favour of the report. the community's objective is to reduce co2 emissions by up to 120 gco2/km, so to progressively reduce the average emissions i agree with the implementation of the regulation which requires, from january 2014, the registration and production of new light commercial vehicles that do not exceed 175 gco2/km of emissions and 147 gco2/km in the long term (2020) also to meet the design needs of the vehicles.
in writing. - i congratulate mr callanan on his excellent work. we have today approved the agreement reached with national governments on new co2 emission limits for european commercial vehicles, including incentives for industry to produce trucks with improved energy efficiency and penalties for those who do not comply with the new rules. the legislation adopted strikes a delicate balance and sets a series of ambitious but feasible environmental objectives for producers. the new legislation will complete the community regulatory framework by adding to the passenger vehicle emission standards of two years ago. manufacturing a van with a lower emission of 50g co2/km will give the manufacturer a 'super credit', valid for a limited period of time. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the number of vehicles that were sold in the period 2014-2015 to the creditors of the company. on the other hand, newly produced vehicles consuming more than the limits imposed will be subject to a penalty of up to eur 95/gram from 2019.

in writing. − the internal market and competition policy are two pillars of the european unification process, aimed not only at economically strengthening the eu and businesses, but above all at reversing the union's fundamental freedoms. this objective must be pursued for the benefit of all community citizens and businesses, both by offering them equal opportunities and substantial equality and by avoiding difficulties, over-cost and over-structuring which might differentiate, discriminate or reduce their possibilities of access or protection of their rights. recognising that all eu citizens have the right to express themselves in their own language when addressing the eu institutions is a fundamental right of equality, equal opportunities and non-discrimination. the use of some official languages has a technical rationale only within the activities of the eu institutions and not in relations with citizens, businesses and institutions of the member countries. enhanced cooperation is useful when it increases the opportunities of those who join it, without prejudice to others. i therefore voted against the recommendation because i consider that enhanced cooperation in such a sensitive area as political equality of languages is unacceptable, creating discrimination against the right to equal opportunities and access to the fundamental freedoms of the eu.
in writing. - i am opposed to parliament's free hand in using the enhanced cooperation procedure to create a unitary patent system because i consider the issue of the language regime to be of fundamental importance to italian interests, italy being the fourth largest country in europe in terms of the number of patents filed. i believe that the enhanced cooperation procedure, which was created to give a greater impetus to the process of european union integration by giving a limited number of member states the opportunity to make progress on matters on which it is not possible to reach unanimous agreement, has been used as a tool. this may set a dangerous precedent, because it is detrimental to a member state and circumvents the unanimity provided for in the treaty of lisbon on the single market and the principle of non-distortion of competition within it. we would also have preferred to wait for the court of justice's judgment, which is due on 8 march.

in writing. - italy and europe are not doing well in the choice of enhanced cooperation in the creation of unitary patent protection. the implementation of enhanced cooperation in this area is deeply wrong because it renders futile the efforts to establish a community patent valid for all eu countries. we also contest the decision to force this vote in the house without taking account of the consequences of the court of justice's ruling on the compatibility of the unified patent court with the treaty. italy, like spain, rightly opposed the recognition of only three languages (english, french and german) for the filing of european patents, instead of respecting the principle of equal dignity of languages enshrined in the treaty. it is clear that this is not only discrimination but also a real economic damage to companies from countries with different languages.

will it help to strengthen the economic governance of the european union or will it be a step in the direction of a new, inevitably discretionary 'intergovernmentalism', a direction in which the unfortunate formulation of the franco-german competitiveness pact has also been placed? i mean, what tracks are we putting the train on? who's the foreman? on the one hand, the proposed amendment to article 136 outlines an intergovernmental mechanism which is entirely independent of the union and its institutions. on the other hand, we read in the commission's opinion that the mechanism will necessarily have to be based on the economic governance of the union and that the commission will take all the initiatives to ensure consistency between the stability mechanism and this economic governance. we appreciate the intentions but, as there is no trace of this in the proposed reform of rule 136, we feel that this is the time to clearly define how the mechanism will operate. what procedure will be adopted to establish the mechanism? member of the commission. − madam president, i am very pleased to have this opportunity to address parliament on this important issue of falsified medicines. the proposal before us today for an amending directive on falsified medicines will, subject to parliament’s approval, take us into new territory. a successful conclusion of this file will mark the first time that the european union has tackled, with legislation, the specific threat of falsified pharmaceuticals. this text is going to make our regulatory system fit for the future; making a major contribution to protecting patients from the many dangers of fake medicines. as members will know, falsified medicines are different from counterfeit products. falsified medicines are about public health. i was very pleased that an early agreement on the substance of the proposal was reached between the co-legislators just before christmas. let me thank all those who worked so hard to make this agreement possible, especially the rapporteur of the lead committee, ms matias, as well as the rapporteurs of the committees giving opinions, ms sartori and ms bastos. i would also like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs. the commission stands fully behind the substance of this well-balanced agreement, which introduces rigid and effective measures whilst being risk proportionate and flexible. this is crucial as not all medicines are the same: the likeliness of falsification varies, as does the risk of public health. turning to some of the specific issues, i would like to highlight the following. on safety features: we saw the risk that member states might in future take divergent approaches on the packaging. this would have led to different levels of protection in the european union. it would have led to a fragmentation of the european union market for medicines. i am sure members will share my satisfaction that we have paved the way towards a european safety feature to identify and thus authenticate a medicine. the commission has always supported a european approach in this regard. on active pharmaceutical ingredients: the agreed text strengthens inspections and international cooperation in this field. the commission and the network of european agencies will work more closely with international partners. only through such cooperation can we achieve a truly effective system of inspection and enforcement. the legislation, once adopted, will increase the transparency of actors involved in the distribution of medicines. finally, parliament insisted on rules concerning online sales of medicines. i consider that parliament found a strong, pragmatic solution by focusing on issues of transparency. the argument acknowledges that the rules for pharmacies in the eu vary but, in future, it will be easier for patients throughout the eu to distinguish legal operators from illegal online pharmacies. president, members, i trust i can count on your full support as regards the next step in in writing. protecting the pharmaceutical supply chain from the introduction of falsified medicines is a duty owed to citizens and companies that conduct their business in a correct and responsible manner. the directive before parliament must therefore be strongly supported, since it introduces procedures and obligations which i hope will produce concrete and effective results. in particular, i would like to stress the importance of certain obligations on persons other than wholesale distributors who are involved in the distribution chain and, even more so, the provision of 'safety features' for prescription medicines, with the aim of providing consumers with assurances about the integrity of the production and distribution chain. stricter rules on inspection, on the traceability of substances in medicinal products and on online sales seem to me to be just as important as those to curb the trade in counterfeit medicines. it should be noted, however, that the compromise provides for regular inspections at the production sites of third countries but that these are carried out by the authorities of the same third country. it would have been better if they had been carried out by the competent authorities of the countries to which the medicinal products were destined, since the greatest danger of falsification arises precisely from third countries.
