in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because i believe it represents a positive step forward in an economic sector as crucial to europe as fisheries. i believe that any action by the european union in this area must always start with an analysis of the needs of the local communities that depend on this activity, which is often characterized by the presence of small and mediumsized enterprises, which are essential to the economy and society. in the mediterranean, many areas have these characteristics, so it is very important that the legislative proposals which are intended to deal with fisheries in this area are clearly inspired by respect for the principle of subsidiarity, so as not to risk compromising the whole system. i am also firmly convinced that it is essential to protect, above all, the small and mediumsized enterprises operating in this sector, involving them in the decision-making process and providing them with the greatest possible support, because they are very difficult to re-skill. rules which do not take account of these peculiarities could irreparably damage smaller markets, forcing them to convert to another area which appears very complex to achieve.
in writing. − the european union's membership of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) is reaching a major turning point with this proposal for a regulation. it is of particular interest in that it provides for the transposition of certain recommendations adopted by the cgpm into a single community legislative act. this is a much more stable legal instrument than the current one and it is only possible to add further recommendations by amending the legislative act itself. it is a key step in improving legal certainty and also contributes to regulatory simplification. beyond the importance of provisions on a minimum mesh size for fishing nets, article 28 of this proposal for a regulation calls into question the prerogatives of parliament. it provides that the provisions of the regulation may be amended by the 'comitology procedure', whereby the commission is assisted by management committees, chaired by a representative of the commission and composed of representatives of the member states. this would effectively deprive parliament of its powers, which is why it seems desirable for the commission to act by means of delegated acts, with the possibility of the parliament or the council revoking the delegation of powers.
in writing. - i share the rapporteur's view that the fisheries regulation should be simplified to a regulation which can incorporate the recommendations adopted by the general fisheries commission in the mediterranean into a single instrument. i also share the objectives and principles of the common fisheries policy, but i believe that in all coastal member states a fair balance must be struck between socioeconomic value and the protection of ecosystems, that is to say, i believe that the protection of the particular interests of local communities must also be claimed, in accordance with a general principle. regulation no 1967/2006 sets out in detail the gear permitted for fishing in the waters of the gfcm area, in our particular case, the mediterranean. i would like to point out, ladies and gentlemen, that the objective of protecting our natural habitats sometimes has serious repercussions for certain fishing communities, as is provided for in the current regulations. italy is awaiting a commission derogation from the de facto ban on fishing for two species, which are the main product of a large marine industry. i would therefore like to call on all the representatives of the 27 member states and, through them, on the commission to consider whether it is appropriate to make these instruments less rigid in the face of the survival needs of a local fisheries sector.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr rivellini's report because i fully agree with the importance of achieving a regulatory simplification of the union's regulations. the report offers the possibility of bringing together all the recommendations of the committee on fisheries in the mediterranean into a single european legislative text, making it easier for the citizen to access the documentation and making it easier for the competent bodies to make any future changes. i believe that the task of simplifying legislation for citizens and operators in the sector is a duty, which we as legislators must carry out quickly and carefully in order to enable them to understand the opportunities that the european union offers, but above all to eliminate the bureaucratic burden that so many additional costs present.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the regulatory work of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean has been essential in order to achieve a sustainable level of fishing in the mare nostrum. the latest statistics on mediterranean fish stocks show that over 54% of the stocks analysed are overexploited. this is why it is a priority to take legislative action to protect the marine environment by bringing the use of fish stocks back to sustainable levels. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied in a uniform manner.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because i share the need for the european union to look for new innovative financing instruments. they enable the eu to meet the challenges of today, because they play both a regulatory and a revenue-generating role. it has often been pointed out in this house that the economic crisis has highlighted the shortcomings in the regulation and supervision of the global financial system. it is also well known that today it is the taxpayers who are bearing the cost of the crisis in the first place, not only through direct contributions but also in terms of rising unemployment, ever lower incomes, reduced access to social services and increasing inequalities. new instruments are therefore needed to formulate an organic and integrated response to the crisis. i therefore agree with the introduction, which has been under discussion for some time, of 'eurobonds', which could lead to joint debt management by aggregating part of the sovereign debt. the rapporteur then proposes other financing instruments to curb speculation: the commission will continue to support the efforts of the member states to achieve the objectives of the treaty, including, for example, consistent and effective taxation of the energy sector and the development of proposals for taxation for development that will increase the resources to be allocated to achieving the millennium development goals.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is a positive step towards the future innovative financing instruments which will be the basis for the revival of the european economy. i believe it is essential for europe to also find resources on the market to finance the crucial sectors of our economy, in line with the europe 2020 objectives, in particular the transeuropean infrastructure in the transport, energy and telecommunications sectors needed to overcome the crisis. it is essential to keep the european economy moving. the eu's responsibility is not to impose and/or raise taxes, but to have the courage to face the market. the solution is to find new forms of financing which can guarantee the full realisation of projects in the shortest possible time, by creating ad hoc funds based on the issue on the capital market of securities directly linked to the realisation and economic exploitation of the project, the so-called project bonds. as regards a possible tax on financial transactions, it should only be proposed in europe if it is introduced at global level: i think that the commission should consider the possibility of introducing this tax at eu level, trying to assess whether this could have negative consequences for the competitiveness of the eu system.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the economic and financial crisis has shown the complete lack of ethics in this area. the new welfare economy paradigm that the pursuit of individual welfare is the key to collective welfare, which is the summation of it, shows in all its inadequacy. in fact, in this logic, the individual interest is not limited by the collective and even less by the general interest. since the government of the public interest must first of all set the general interest as the horizon within which to operate, and within it give free rein to individual freedoms and rights, it must be supported by a fair and progressive tax system. in line with this approach, which must be supported at global level, starting with the eu and all the g8 and g20 countries, financial transaction revenues must be made comparable to other income through a specific taxation that, together with other rules and new paradigms, encourages greater responsibility of operators. finally, the introduction of eurobonds for the crisis fund and infrastructure projects could strengthen the eu's capacity to act, if in addition to the community budget. the report we have approved seems to me to be moving, albeit slowly, in that direction.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the resolution on innovative financial instruments, which is parliament's contribution to the debate on how to generate new revenue, ensure a fair tax policy and maximise the capacity to recover the levy. i am in favour of the introduction of a financial transaction tax (ftt): the recent crisis - in which a certain type of speculative finance is largely to blame - shows that it is the states and citizens who pay for the damage caused by others. a financial transaction tax would bring about €200 billion into the eu's public coffers each year and would help to reduce speculative activities, making them more costly and therefore less profitable. however, i believe that this tax should be introduced at a global level and not just at a european level, in order to avoid creating a competitive disadvantage for europe itself, which, let us not forget, has a very high attractiveness as the world's largest market. finally, parliament's support for eurobonds and project bonds to support the recovery by stimulating the real economy and promoting the construction of vital infrastructure for the european economy is to be welcomed.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, if the financial system, the author of reckless transactions and speculation, is identified as one of the main culprits of the financial crisis, then it is right that the architects should contribute by making the most significant economic contribution. however, i believe that the form of this report is likely to undermine the precarious balance of competition, and to undermine the basis of it, since its application would be on a global scale. for this reason, and in order not to set a dangerous precedent for the european tax system, i do not think i can support the report by voting against it.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report which parliament is voting on today concerns the introduction of innovative financial instruments. i voted in favour of this resolution because the economic crisis of recent years has shown the lack of regulation and the need to create new financial instruments to deal with the large-scale financial speculation. in this way, european action will be able to re-establish unequivocally the need to respond to the needs of the real economy, supporting long-term investment and creating new additional resources, in order to address and overcome the main global and european challenges, achieving the growth and development objectives under the 2020 strategy. the dramatic increase in financial transactions has revealed the growing gap between finance and the real economy. the introduction of a financial transaction tax, the issue of common european bonds and the envisaged carbon tax are some of the proposals aimed at creating the new pathways needed for our economy, but without in any way prejudicing the most vulnerable groups of consumers.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i wanted to express my negative opinion of this report because, while the idea of a contribution from the financial system, which has many faults in the crisis of the last two years, would seem to be right, the way in which it is being applied leaves me very puzzled. i must say that i am very much in favour of the proposal to create eurobonds, which i believe can be a useful instrument, but it is the preponderant part on the introduction of a financial transaction tax that is creating the greatest problems. i think it is too risky to apply it at a single european union level, because it would risk taking away the competitiveness of the whole community financial system and operators could easily circumvent it by focusing on other places. i would also not like this tax to open the way to the creation of a potential centralised treasury at eu level, which i would strongly oppose.
in writing. − the recent economic crisis has exposed the weaknesses of the global financial regulatory and supervisory system. all too often, in fact, the volume of these transactions has far exceeded the needs of the real world, causing speculation that over time has made the capital involved extremely volatile and at risk of insolvency. this is weighing heavily on taxpayers, including in terms of high unemployment rates, ever-lower incomes, reduced access to social services and rising inequalities. to prevent future crises, the european union must now promote concrete changes in regulation and supervision, shaping a healthier and more robust financial environment. the idea of a levy on financial transactions has important advantages, especially in the aftermath of a crisis such as the present one: stabilise markets, encourage long-term investment and ensure traceability for the purpose of auditing individual transactions. curb speculation, support long-term investment and achieve higher long-term growth under the eu 2020 strategy: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there are considerable health inequalities in the european union and the measures taken to combat these inequalities vary widely within the member states. as i believe that these health differences can produce a significant influence on individuals throughout their lives, they are a problem that must be tackled with determination and with innovative policy vision. the report under discussion contains points of considerable interest concerning the recognition of the practical right to health of citizens, in particular by focusing on both the education of the population and the widespread availability of health services. the social consequences of the recent economic and financial crisis are obvious: since the start of the crisis, the number of unemployed has increased by 5 million, many households have been hit by the recession and are now more at risk of poverty or over-indebtedness. in my view, it is crucial that reducing these inequalities is considered a priority at all levels of decision-making. i also call on the commission to give them greater recognition in the europe 2020 strategy and to ensure that the objective of reducing health inequalities is fully taken into account in future community initiatives.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it must be admitted that this report contains a number of points of considerable interest concerning the recognition of the right to health in the concrete sense (access to health care, training of the population, the widespread availability of services, etc.). we cannot, however, fail to raise certain reservations which stem from the contradictions inherent in the document itself and which have given rise to a wide-ranging debate. equality should be understood in a concrete sense and not by isolating individuals (particularly women) from their relationships with their partner, with their children and from the social context in which sexuality and reproductive capacity are practically exercised. furthermore, the proclamation of "new rights" such as the "right to safe abortion" is a matter of concern because such a statement constrains or sometimes cancels out the rights of others (the expectations of the father or the life expectancy of the conceived child). we can also point out some shortcomings, such as the complete omission of the document on professional operators: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the health and well-being of european citizens is a priority which this parliament must guarantee and protect. but even more importantly, it is essential for us to promote the uniform guarantee of this right for all european countries. socioeconomic, cultural and structural inequalities often create a diverse landscape in which not everyone has equal access to care and healthcare facilities. it is therefore the weaker groups, migrants, the elderly, children and the disabled who pay, even with their lives, the high price of a right to health that is denied to them. this must not happen, ladies and gentlemen, at european, national or regional level. the victims of an unfortunately widespread disease are as blameless as those who lack equal access to health care. i voted in favour of the resolution which encourages the reduction of inequalities between the member states in health standards and promotes more efficient health policies that are available to all, not only to users but also to those who, as health workers, can find better working conditions to work better for the health of all.
in writing. − health inequalities are a problem that must also be addressed at european level. the reasons often stem from differences in opportunities, access to services and material resources, as well as from different lifestyle choices made by individuals. an innovative policy approach is needed to address them. the economic and financial crisis of recent years has led to a reduction in the level of funding for health and long-term care services, as a result of budget cuts and tax revenue reductions, while demand for health and long-term care services has increased. many member states have included in their recovery plans measures such as investments in health infrastructure, restructuring and additional financing of the health system. however, interventions to address health inequalities vary widely from country to country. the collection and sharing of data on effective strategies, policies and interventions will help to win support from governments. it is essential that reducing health inequalities is considered a key priority, thus pursuing a 'health in all policies' approach and ensuring effective impact assessments that take into account the achievements in terms of health equity.
in writing. - the attempt to reduce health inequalities in the european union, for cohesive social and economic development, is certainly to be assessed positively, which is why i voted in favour of the estrela report. the suggestions for improving health in europe through health education, access to care, data literacy and the use of mechanisms to measure, monitor, evaluate and disseminate information offer an important contribution to developing policies for effectively reducing health inequalities. but i think it is equally important to respect the principle of subsidiarity and to defend and safeguard certain national characteristics and peculiarities.
in writing. the 2010 eurostat data are clear: there are still large disparities between the 27 member states in the quality of healthcare provided. parameters such as life expectancy in different member states still vary widely from region to region, showing that quality standards of healthcare are still too heterogeneous within the eu. access to primary and secondary education, stable and satisfactory employment, gender, cultural background and access to quality health care are the factors that contribute more than others to raising the quality of life of citizens. the report must therefore take account in particular of the rights of the most vulnerable groups, especially women, and their specific needs.
in writing. - while starting from a shared principle, that the average level of health in the european union has continued to improve, despite the fact that there are still important differences in the health field due to the different systems of the member states, the report is lost in the rights of migrants. these are placed among the most vulnerable groups, such as the disabled, the elderly and children, without taking into account that many of them are illegal immigrants and therefore in europe illegally. we cannot therefore treat migrants in the same way as disabled people, who are a vulnerable group requiring special attention and assistance adapted to their needs. the report divides society into classes rich, poor, ethnic minorities, men, women, children with outdated methodology instead of talking about citizens with rights and claims to measure, through specific legislation, these alleged health inequalities. the amendments adopted have even made the text worse, including various issues such as climate change, violence against women, assisted reproduction, and equal access to the health system for illegal immigrants.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report, in agreement with the commission, emphasizes the need to strengthen the synergies between fiscal and development policies. the commission has published two studies on this subject and a resolution on the same subject was adopted in this house a year ago. i voted in favour because i share the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs) and the management of the tax system, the commitment to supporting the tax systems of developing countries, and international dialogue and cooperation in the field of taxation. however, it is necessary to stress the shortcomings still in place in the management of customs revenue, the current gaps in the oecd, the erosion of tax revenue. i think it is appropriate for the european union to work to combat inefficiencies such as the fight against tax havens, the manipulation of trade prices, the weakness of the international structure. it is time to reduce the manipulation of commercial prices, the so-called 'curse of natural resources', the widening of the tax base, greater coordination between donors.
in writing. − the commission is doing a good job of promoting principles and criteria for developing good tax management practices in cooperation with developing countries. the criteria of transparency, exchange of information and fair tax competition are fundamental. it is a process which the commission aims to implement by strengthening the synergies between fiscal and development policies, with the aim of identifying the difficulties encountered by these countries in mobilising revenue through taxation. on the other hand, however, the commission is still omitting several issues which require a prompt response. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. to this end, it is desirable that most international organisations have a specific mandate to combat tax havens. finally, an extension of the tax base, by means of adjusting the tax reform to the development of direct taxation, is essential to resolve the collection difficulties arising from the regressive vat system.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mrs joly's report on taxation and development, cooperation with developing countries to promote good tax management practices, because - in line with the europe 2020 strategy - i believe it is essential to have a global governance that supports international tax dialogue and cooperation. i agree with the report when it says that it wants to expand the synergies between tax and development policies through the exchange of information on tax matters and through multilateral mechanisms that refer to the model of the eu directive on taxation of savings income in order to combat tax evasion and avoidance. tax cooperation with developing countries is precisely intended to prevent these countries from becoming 'tax havens' for multinational companies and from distorting competitiveness, which is a negative factor in the development of economic processes, given the global interconnectedness of the economic system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text of this report because i share the view that greater synergy between fiscal and development policies can help the developing countries. the commission's latest reports on taxation and development also show that taxation, if specifically designed, can be a source of financing for development policies. it is no coincidence that many developing countries do not even reach the minimum level of tax revenue needed to finance basic public services. cooperation to strengthen their tax systems and the fight against tax havens, which facilitate illicit capital flight, must be at the heart of these processes, which can facilitate the introduction of country-by-country financial reporting obligations, to the benefit of the fight against poverty.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr papastamkos. international trade plays a decisive role within the eu, especially in view of the fact that european farmers are disadvantaged by imports from third countries and the non-application of the principle of reciprocity, which gives foreign farmers an undue advantage when they are often not required to comply with the same stringent and costly regulations that european farmers must comply with in order to operate in the internal market - especially from the point of view of health and plant health. i will continue to fight for a strong coherence in europe between the cap and the eu's external trade policy, which must guarantee the european agricultural model a level playing field for producers in the member states on the world market.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, agriculture is a strategic sector for the european union. although it is not of average importance in terms of employment and gross domestic product, or at least in terms of the characteristics of our territories and our food traditions, it is of greater importance, since it ensures self-sufficiency in many of the ingredients essential to our traditional and non-traditional agri-food products. it is also a sector which is fundamental to the preservation and protection of the environment and to the sustainable development of our territories. it is clear that trade agreements, especially in the world trade organisation round, must be reached. but to do this, the european union must pay greater attention to the protection of quality, traditional and certified products, so that they can be safeguarded at international level to avoid fraud on foreign markets of products falsely traced back to our territories. the main thrust of the report as adopted seems to be in the right direction

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today's vote sends a strong signal to the commission: the european union cannot continue to grant concessions to gain access to third country markets at the expense of the agricultural sector! at a time when the european union is considering the new common agricultural policy, finding mechanisms to ensure coherence between the cap and external trade policy is becoming a primary objective. the european agricultural sector guarantees the achievement of many public goods, such as food safety and quality. the protection of the interests of european farmers must therefore be given priority and i welcome the inclusion in the document of some paragraphs which provide for the guarantee of reciprocity for european producers by requiring that meat exporters to europe be subject to the same restrictions as european producers in order to ensure consumer safety and fair commercial competition. at this stage of the negotiations on the mercosur and morocco agreements, i think it is essential to make clear to the commission our concern and our firm position in defence of the interests of european and italian farmers.
in writing. - mr president, there is a close link between the future of the cap and the union's external trade policy. these two realities cannot be separated from each other and require special attention from the union. we cannot ignore the trade talks and their impact on the agricultural production of the member states. i am therefore in favour of a liberalised market which also takes account of the needs of the union's economic and trade partners, but at the same time i think it is appropriate for agricultural policy to be involved in the negotiation of agreements to control the quality of products exported or imported on our markets and to protect community producers and our food supplies. i therefore support the papastamkos report, even though there has been an imbalance on some trade issues, due to the division of powers between the agriculture and trade committees of this parliament, which should work in synergy to define a negotiating balance applicable to the different agricultural trade treaties of the union.
in writing. the report on agriculture and international trade covers trade agreements between the eu and third countries in respect of agricultural products. the european commission, which has been criticized on several occasions in the field of agricultural policy, is condemned in this text by the european parliament, which too often comes to conclusions which are not acceptable to european agricultural policy. i voted in favour of the text because i believe that the political role of parliament is essential, which the commission avoids consulting when it comes to trade relations with third countries. i agree with the request to the commission to suspend the agreement with mercosur until a new agreement is drawn up with the states concerned in order to guarantee european consumers quality and safety of products and affordability on foreign markets.
in writing. the report on agriculture and international trade was voted on today in plenary. the report by mr georgios papastamkos stresses that international trade policy must not have the effect of undermining the union's ability to ensure food security in a context of volatile markets and the maintenance of a strong european agricultural sector. the report condemns the commission's approach of granting concessions on agriculture to obtain better access to third markets for industrial products and services. the report covers a number of issues, including impact assessment, financial compensation, the wto/doha, but above all the problematic bilateral trade agreements, such as those with morocco, pakistan, ukraine and in particular mercosur, and considers it unacceptable that the european commission should resume negotiations without making the impact assessment public and without initiating a real political debate with the council and the european parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it strengthens the position of the agricultural policy, a cornerstone of european economic and social cohesion, also in view of the challenges posed by the europe 2020 strategy. the european union is now the world's largest importer of agricultural products, particularly from developing countries. in the last ten years the value of its imports has almost doubled, accounting for 20 percent of the world's industry. against this background, it is necessary to build a strong european trade policy that implements article 208 tfeu, which states that europe is committed to cooperating in the implementation of growth policies in developing countries. the priority now is to ensure that european trade and agricultural policy act together in a global perspective, facilitating access to the markets of developing countries and enabling them to promote economic development through these practices at the same time.
in writing. − the dependence of some european sectors on non-eu markets is a problem not only for raw materials but also for the feed sector. in particular, mr häusling's report shows that over 40 million tonnes of protein plants are imported into europe every year, mainly soybeans and maize gluten feed, representing 80% of the eu's consumption of protein plants. in view of this, i can only support the requests of my colleague, who hopes that in the future cap europe will promote agricultural policies aimed at breaking this dependence on imports with a clear beneficial effect on the quality and sustainability of the supply chain.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the import of proteins from third countries is a major problem, since the equivalent requirements for imported legumes are not ensured. these protein plants are mainly used for the animal sector and this puts the price system at risk as the volatility of the latter on international markets has increased exponentially. that is why i support the rapporteur's call for an ever-increasing reduction in dependence on imports from the eu.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, to say that protein crops currently occupy only 3% of the cultivated land in the eu and only 30% of the vegetable protein needed in the form of animal feed describes a reality that is difficult for most people to understand. the decline in the supply of plant protein is a paradox at a time when plant protein production gives rise to a number of positive externalities which are necessary for the agricultural ecosystem, beneficial to the quality of the final livestock products and important for market price balances. the comparison, which has already begun in committee, has proved to be fundamental in redefining the role of plant protein cultivation in the context of the future challenges of european agriculture. i am referring to the fight against climate change and the proper use of natural resources, which are the subject of due attention at this stage of the elaboration of the framework for the future cap. i have supported this report, which i regard as emblematic of a new phase which must be opened up to reduce the deficit of vegetable protein. i consider it a priority to create a specific framework programme for decentralised agricultural research to strengthen cooperation, share best practice and accelerate the process of improving the cultivation of protein plants adapted to local needs, innovating the supply chain in the various member states.
in writing. − the production of protein plants in the european union is declining significantly, making the situation alarming. the protein deficit causes imbalances not only in agricultural production but also in the field of research and development of agricultural techniques. farmers have gradually lost interest in protein crops, leading to a loss of practical experience at european level. the report stresses the urgency of formulating a genuine integrated european strategy. only a more balanced supply and consumption of protein crops produced within the eu will be able to respond to new challenges such as climate change or the loss of agricultural biodiversity. the european commission is therefore expected to examine the possibilities of overcoming the current emergency of protein deficiency by means of a radical reform of the cap, which is capable of meeting the new challenges. it would also be appropriate to introduce a complementary payment with a mandatory rotation of at least four different crops, at least one of which is protein. finally, a unit for agricultural research should be set up within the commission's agriculture and rural development dg to encourage consumers and catering services to make more environmentally friendly food choices.
in writing. the report by martin häusling on the 'protein deficit in the eu' was voted on in plenary today. the eu is very dependent on imports of protein crops, which are mainly used for animal feed, which poses important risks, particularly for the european livestock sector. a number of compromise amendments have considerably improved the original report. the report adopted calls on the commission to adopt a medium- and long-term vision of protein policy and calls for the reform of the cap to introduce new provisions, supporting farmers in improving crop rotation systems, to reduce the deficit in plant proteins and price volatility. the report also calls for research on seeds and their contribution to disease control. the report calls on the commission to ensure unhindered supply of soya to the european market by providing a technical solution on the low level of gmos for food and feed imported into the eu.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the latest estimates concerning the protein crops sector show a worrying trend in the decline of protein crop production in the european union over the last decade. each year in europe, the production of legumes is reduced by 30%, and that of soya beans by 12%, resulting in an import of 40 million tonnes of protein plants. the text of this report shows that the european livestock sector, which is vulnerable to price volatility, is too dependent on the availability of imported plant protein. this dependence is undermining the economic viability of domestic meat production, which is increasingly weakened by the additional costs of importing feed, not to mention the economic problem that, in view of climate objectives, the production of protein crops would substantially contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
in writing. - the production of pulses has declined in recent years, leading to a heavy dependence on imports from third countries, as they are used for both human and animal feed. these crops, in addition to reducing the european union's protein deficit, are, once the product is harvested, an excellent soil additive, which therefore requires less use of chemical fertiliser. good agricultural management should provide for crop rotation, thereby reducing fertilisation and safeguarding the diversity of species in wild and cultivated varieties. the request, which we share, is that the future cap should include measures to overcome the union's protein deficit by increasingly reducing imports.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we are celebrating the centenary of the international women's day, a symbol of the struggle for social equality and freedom from the discriminatory and harassing behaviour which women have suffered and still suffer. in every single country in the world there is a different perception of the female figure, there is a lot of talk about islamic countries and the way women are judged and treated, further influenced by religion. fortunately, even though we in the west have an equal vision of men and women, the data describes a disconcerting situation. in europe, many disparities persist to the disadvantage of girls and women in terms of employment, privacy, health and the right to access education and vocational training and to occupy jobs in non-traditional sectors and with a high level of responsibility. but that is not all, women face not only multiple forms of discrimination, but they are also victims of all kinds of violence, psychological and physical. it is therefore necessary to protect women and to enable them to lead a life of equal quality to that of men. gender equality is not just a matter of social justice, but is one of the prerequisites for achieving the objectives of sustainable growth, employment, competitiveness and social cohesion set out in the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in its 2010 annual report, the european commission has highlighted the challenges facing europe in the wake of the recent economic and financial crisis in the field of equality between men and women. one important consequence of this crisis for women is employment: they were affected later than men because of their greater presence in the sectors that withstood the effects of the crisis longer (health, education, etc.), but now these sectors are also at risk of being affected, leading to a long-term precariousness of working women compared to men. i believe that this is another reason why equality between men and women in employment should no longer be just a goal to be pursued, but should become a reality. the member states and the commission must therefore commit themselves not only to maintaining policies for equality between men and women but, above all, to not reducing the budgetary expenditure allocated to them. finally, since i believe that the promotion of equality must be achieved through the education and training of citizens, and in particular of young people, i would draw the commission's attention to the need to renew awareness-raising campaigns on this subject over time.

to participate in joint action, with an industrial policy governance, without wanting to impose choices on the part of the community on individual member states, but trying to coordinate their policy. this seems to me to be a choice which goes in the direction of your request, but which confirms that europe needs its own industry to face the immediate challenges of getting out of the crisis. we cannot expect to overcome the present difficult situation, aggravated by the crisis in the mediterranean area, without a firm action in favour of industrial policy, of enterprise policy, because these are the only ways of allowing us to develop and create new jobs. the report you have prepared, mr president, rightly emphasizes the economic, environmental and social challenges, in short the sustainability of our industrial policy, and puts sustainability on the same level as competitiveness, because these two dimensions are closely linked, and i am convinced that in today's world these two aspects cannot exist without each other. to do this we must also have a modern and competitive industry which finally ends the old way of conducting industrial policy. what does it mean to have a modern industry? it means having an industry that is efficient in the use of resources, in the consumption of energy, in the emission of greenhouse gases, and therefore an economy that has the green economy as its objective, going through the path of the greener economy, but it must also be a responsible industry, which faces the difficulties on the basis of a constant and fruitful dialogue with the social partners. i think we should also send a strong signal, reminding ourselves that the industrial model of 2010 cannot be an industrial model based on state aid, just as european industry cannot fail to rely on innovation and research to be competitive in an era of global challenge. that is why the european commission has presented, before the document on industrial policy, the document on innovation policy, which i believe is absolutely essential for the development of a serious industrial policy, which also goes in the direction of identifying paths in the field of research and innovation as regards raw materials. it is no coincidence that one of the innovation partnerships indicated by the commission is specifically about raw materials, to find actions through research for recycling and substitution of raw materials. so it is clear that - also because we will be talking about rare earths in the next debate - it is clear that innovation, raw materials and industrial policy are part of a single strategy, as is the revision of the small business act, in my view. so by the european commission's implementation of this series of political and legislative interventions we are demonstrating that there is a desire to implement political action in favour of industry and business. as far as governance and industrial policy are concerned, the process seems to me to be well under way - as we said earlier - both within the commission and in the member states. as you know, president barroso entrusted me with the chairmanship of the commissioners' group on industrial policy at the beginning of my term of office. i have already met the group twice, once before the adoption of the communication to discuss the political priorities, and a second time to discuss the practical implementation of the communication with particular regard to the competitiveness test and the standardisation strategy. i consider the commissioners' group to be a privileged instrument for guiding the political process and ensuring the coherence of industrial policy initiatives. as far as the member states are concerned, i think the reaction has been positive. as i said, on 10 december we launched the first cooperation exercises with the hungarian presidency on access to credit for small and mediumsized enterprises, which will be followed by other similar exercises in close cooperation with the member states. we will continue to provide you with the necessary elements for continued cooperation between parliament and the commission. before concluding, mr president, let me make a point of emphasizing the importance of supporting women entrepreneurs. it is no coincidence that today is 8 march, and i have always said that we need more women entrepreneurs, but once business act. the network of female entrepreneurial ambassadors that we have already launched will continue to exist, but we want to go beyond awareness raising, we want women entrepreneurs to be able to get good advice from experts, and that's why we are going to launch a very short-term consultation to support some initiatives to provide mentors to new women entrepreneurs who want to do so. this person will be able to give them practical advice on starting up and then running the business. the aim is to implement this initiative in at least 10 member states and then extend it to all the other vice-president of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank parliament because this debate gives strength to the action which the european commission - and especially the barroso ii commission - is taking to solve the delicate problem of rare materials. as mr scholz has rightly pointed out, the european commission has taken decisive action since the madrid meeting, and not just announcements, but concrete actions. when i speak of concrete action, i mean the drawing up of a list of 14 rare commodities on which we must act, a list which i fear will have to be extended. in addition, the first agreement with the african union involved several months of work and was concluded with an agreement within the african union-european union action plan, which sees africa directly involved in joint action with our union and the commission, which concerns both what we can do within the union for an analysis of our needs, and an analysis of the real possibilities of extractive activity in africa, the possible realization of a geological service and the project to create the infrastructure of the trans-african networks alongside the mines from which the extractive industry can multiply. the agreement with the russian federation to put agreements on raw materials on the agenda is another concrete result, it is not just an announcement, two meetings have been held. the european commission's document on raw materials is not an announcement, it is a text approved by the commission which sets out a clear and precise strategy, as i have said, based on three concrete pillars on which we intend to continue to work. the decision to set up an innovation partnership linked to an action involving private individuals - and i hope parliament and the other institutions will also do so - on innovation and research to identify strong actions on recycling with concrete results and on substitution is not an announcement, but it is concrete action by the european commission, it is a request that has been approved by the college and is therefore part of the commission's strategy with regard to innovation. as far as the wto is concerned, we will of course continue to work towards a diplomatic solution. the latin american trip is another concrete action, not another announcement, because trips on such sensitive subjects require dedicated preparation which must then lead to concrete results. of course, we shall not miss the opportunity to inform parliament of what has been done. as regards certain areas of europe where it is possible to check whether the raw materials are underground, i am thinking of greenland, the barents sea, and other areas in northern europe, it is necessary to check whether extractive activity is possible, whether it is economically viable. however, we are ready to support any initiative to test any research. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as far as the wto is concerned, i am responsible for the raw materials issue for the industrial part. the trade side is the responsibility of commissioner de gucht, who has already made it very clear that he intends to defend the interests of the eu, as is the case in the commission document on raw materials, paragraph 5.2. as regards the wto proceedings for which commissioner de gucht is responsible, we have, as i said in the course of the debate, initiated a procedure with mexico and the united states for nine raw materials, which do not include rare earths. the study is already at an advanced stage of completion, so the conclusions will also be decisive in helping the commission to decide what initiatives to take on the subject of rare earths. we are evaluating the situation in order to identify the most appropriate instruments in this area. as regards the recycling of rare earths and the question raised by mr rinaldi in his speech, i can tell you what we intend to do as the european commission on recycling. the current legislation covers 40% of the waste produced in the union. the commission has proposed to significantly increase the recycling targets for electrical and electronic waste containing rare earths, as proposed by commissioner potočnik, which is not my own proposal. other actions are planned to improve the treatment of products and to facilitate their recycling at the end of their life. there is already legislation in place and commissioner potočnik intends to continue to work in this direction. as regards industrial policy action in relation to rare earths and raw materials, i intend to go on, not making promises, because i am not used to making promises, i am used to keeping the commitments i make, especially those i make before parliament, as i have done since i won the confidence of the committees to which i have presented myself, and i intend to go on, i intend to keep all the commitments i have made without making announcements, but trying to give concrete answers to the needs of european companies and citizens, also in this delicate sector of industrial supply.

said about the issues of refugees. we have worked hard with member states to try and support getting people home. for a lot of refugees who arrived at the tunisian border, their home was egypt, and there is much more to do. my belief is that, if we can make the country more stable, people can stay at home – which is where they want to be. so one of the challenges for the eu – and i am very open about this – is that by providing stability in our southern neighbourhood, we enable people to stay where they wish to stay, with economic prosperity and democracy, rather than feeling that they have to flee because of violence, lack of opportunity or other issues. then there is this whole question of a no-fly zone and the role of military options. i indicated the work on what we described as prudent planning that has been going on with the political and security committee (cops) and which continued last night. those discussions are referred to in our discussions with the united nations, which i have also indicated are ongoing, and nato, where i will attend a meeting tomorrow. of course they are done in conjunction with our partners. the arab league will discuss a no-fly zone on saturday. but what i am also very mindful of is something that the secretary-general of the arab league said to my delegation visiting him yesterday: we have to define what we need, because a no-fly zone by definition means different things to different people. ensuring that whatever is done can be done properly is something i think this house would be very keen to see. we have to be sure that whatever options are taken, they are taken with the full knowledge of what we are doing and with the support of the people who are going to be affected by that. in that context i refer again to the need for our continued discussions and dialogues with the african union and with the arab league. we could have a big debate – and perhaps we should – about a subject that i started to write about in the press, which is isolationism versus engagement. it is a real challenge, and what i would say to the gentleman who held up the photos is, of course if you are the president of the european council and you go as president to the african summit which is held in libya, you will find that there is a picture of the president with gaddafi. of course. there are pictures of many people. there was a picture shown in the same group of our esteemed alde group leader. there are pictures that you can take on many occasions where those of us who are given positions of responsibility have to engage with people who we probably would not wish to. so i think it is unfair to show a picture of herman van rompuy performing his responsibilities as president of the european council on behalf of all of us in the host country with the person who was hosting the event. whether we would prefer the african union to have held its summit somewhere else is another question; whether, indeed, we would have made some remarks to them on many occasions that perhaps they should. but in the end, we go to meet the african union largely where the african union suggests. we may not like that, and it is a genuine debate. i think we have to engage in that at some point, because my general principle is that engagement is better than isolation. isolation is effective in some circumstances, but engagement is better. having said that, as i have also made clear, we may have brought gaddafi out of the cold. it is now time to send him back into the cold, fully and properly. this is also very important: to have an assessment of what we engage and how we engage and be prepared to review that and stand up and say: we have done this for a set of reasons we think are right, whichever country it is; that we believe engagement in these circumstances is better, but there are circumstances when that is not appropriate and circumstances where, even if that is what we did, it is not appropriate now. but let us be honest, let us not throw down challenges with photographs or other things, where people did this and people did that. people mainly do their very best in circumstances that are very difficult, and i think we should take pride in the president of the council trying to be the representative of the member states. i want to just also say something about labels. we hear a lot about a marshall plan: somebody even called it an ashton plan. no, let us have a libyan plan or an egyptian plan or a tunisian plan, owned by the people of those countries in which we engage and offer our support. i do not want to make a plan that we arrive at and about which we say: guess what, we have come to bring you our plan for your country. no, let us not do that. let us actually be the people who offer the support to ensure that their plan is able to be everything that we would want it to be to support democracy. there are people in this house who have years of experience, who have come through revolution and change and who have a huge amount to offer. i firmly hope – and i have said this in these countries – that they will call upon (if they feel it would be valuable) those people who have lived it and who not only know what worked but also can tell them what did not work. perhaps the things to avoid can be just as important as the things to do. i agree that we need to review what the eu does, what tools we have available to us, whether we have enough, whether we need to think again about what we are able to do. because you are right, i operate within a mandate that i am given, and i can only operate in that mandate. that mandate allows me to do some things, but it mainly requires me to gather together the institutions and the 27 countries in a concerted and joint effort. one final thing about publicity and listening. i have done more press, i think, than anybody else in the world on all of this. i have been wall to wall on the airwaves. we were the first out on the resignation of mubarak, and i have done a huge amount of press. but i have also done far more without the press in the room. again, that is what i think is important, because more than anything, we need to listen. we are all visiting these countries, and they have so many visitors from across the world, and that is great – though i think sometimes we need to give them space and time to be able to work together to plan and then have an even more informed conversation with us. but we also need to listen, and if there is anything i urge upon all of us it is to take the time to really listen – i will say this to member states as well – to what people on the ground are saying, to go to tahrir square as i did, to talk to the young people in egypt, to talk to civil society in tunisia and to engage with the people of libya wherever we can: to discuss what they want for their future and do everything we possibly can to back them.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is not rhetorical to say that we are at a historic moment in the process of european integration. the economic crisis has made it clear that the single currency needs a real european economic government and for the first time important and innovative steps are being taken in this direction. at the same time, there is a dangerous tendency to give this new governance an intergovernmental character, with the risk not only of jeopardising the institutional set-up of the european union, but also of rendering the new mechanisms ineffective. in this sense, the issue of the permanent stability mechanism is emblematic and central. on the one hand, the establishment of a permanent stability mechanism is a decisive and important step forward. parliament supports this choice, although it is important to emphasize this, this must not preclude the possibility of using extraordinary solidarity mechanisms, those based on article 122 which are currently in operation. on the other hand, while the establishment of a permanent mechanism is a good thing, the european council has chosen to build a purely intergovernmental mechanism, depriving the european institutions of any role, including in the procedure leading to its establishment. this, among other things, could raise questions in the course of the ratification process about the appropriateness of a simplified procedure, since it is hardly disputed that a reduction in the powers of the european union would require an ordinary revision procedure and since the treaty says two very clear things, that the monetary policy of the member states whose currency is the euro is an exclusive competence of the union and that the member states must coordinate their economic policies within the framework of the union, since the treaty says this, a mechanism operating entirely outside the institutional set-up of the european union would hardly be compatible with these principles and would therefore constitute a reduction in the powers of the european union which would not be compatible with a simplified revision procedure, and this problem could be raised by some national parliament in the course of the ratification procedure, which we know will not be a simple and risky path. for this reason too, the european parliament would have preferred a different procedure, more appropriate institutionally and less politically risky, article 352, alone or in combination with article 136; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the substance is that the permanent stability fund will be set up by the member states because they have decided so, but that it may be the foundation stone of a new building outside the institutions of the european union, or it may be an intergovernmental carriage placed, however, inside a convoy of the european union travelling on the tracks of european law. the european parliament wants to make its contribution to ensuring that this is the second road we are taking. in our report we therefore asked for two conditions to be met: either a rewording of the amendment proposal, which would somehow place the establishment of the mechanism's distribution within a union procedure, or substantial involvement of the community institutions in the actual implementation of the mechanism and also, above all, in the definition of the conditionalities. what principles and rules for giving aid? by whom and how will they be established? this requires a regulation under the ordinary legislative procedure and we look forward to discussing these points with the european council and the member states.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the peculiarity of the council's proposal is that, once adopted, it gives the go-ahead for the creation of a permanent stability mechanism through an instrument of international law and therefore without a direct link with the institutional system of the union. this has been a matter of great concern to the committee i chair, whose task it is to ensure the consistency of the union's institutional framework. the proposal for a simplified amendment has therefore given rise to a lively debate, in which arguments based on the sound principles of the european integration process have been compared with those based on pragmatism and political realism. in summary, the committee on constitutional affairs considers that the european parliament, in order to decide on the proposal to amend the treaty, must assess the economic governance context in which the proposal is placed. we need to know better how the future mechanism will interact with existing institutional structures. it would be wrong to create double structures which in the long run would risk a fracture of the union. the proposals and suggestions in the brok and gualtieri report are intended to build appropriate bridges between the union's institutional system and the new mechanism. i would also stress that these points must be considered by the council as essential to harmonious cooperation between the european institutions. i therefore strongly urge the european council to take note of the need and the consideration it must give us before our vote on 24 march. we are waiting for a useful signal and i warmly thank the rapporteurs brok and gualtieri for the great work they have done.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the amendment of a treaty is always a complex and delicate matter, and the first amendment is even more so because it can set a precedent to which subsequent speeches will refer. for this reason too, i believe that the work of elmar brok and roberto gualtieri was very careful, balanced and entirely shareable. there are three points i would like to stress in the text they have presented to us. the first point is that the permanent mechanism cannot and must not be outside the institutional framework of europe. for this reason, the commission's presence on the board will be the key to giving this community dimension to the relationship between the current institutional framework and the mechanism that will be modified. the second issue is the full continuity with the existing situation of temporary measures, and woe to us if this were to fail. finally, and decisive for the future development of economic governance, the relationship with economic institutions. we must avoid creating dual models that would bring harm instead of benefit.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, as has been said several times, sometimes for the commission to be heard it must speak up. i will try to do this now. firstly, i would like to thank the rapporteurs for their excellent cooperation and the members for a very important debate. i think that we can definitely agree with many points which have been made in this discussion, especially that we need strong action at european level and that a future mechanism should be as close as possible to the community spirit and the method. to react to the comments on our assistance to greece and ireland: i think our experience clearly demonstrates that we should be constantly searching for a delicate balance between preserving the sustainability of the debt and avoiding moral hazards. the
