the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this was an important debate which seems to me to have clearly demonstrated the existence of a broad consensus among the political groups on the analysis and the line set out in the report. parliament is really speaking with one voice, with a few exceptions, and that is important. we are saying yes to the permanent stability mechanism, we are not hiding our doubts and concerns, which we have heard from the commission, and we are also sharing them, although we would have liked to have read them in the commission's opinion on the procedure chosen. we are prepared to show realism and a sense of responsibility in acknowledging that the political conditions do not exist for defining a community mechanism today, and yet we have shown, we are showing determination in our willingness to help place the mechanism within the framework of the union's law and procedures, in compliance with the treaties. the proposals we have made are clear, but the crucial point seems to me to be different now. is the european council prepared to open a real debate with parliament on its proposals and is the commission prepared to play an active role in this debate? i would point out that parliament has taken what i would call a ritual decision to postpone the vote until the 24th. i think this is an important signal, we are a responsible parliament, but i think it is necessary that the european council should also show the same sense of responsibility in considering the european parliament's proposals.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as we all know, turkey is a strategic partner for the european union and its position is central to the economic and political interests of the union itself and it attributes to it an important role in promoting european action in the black sea area, as well as in promoting peaceful relations in the middle east. the 2010 report on the state of play of turkey's accession negotiations with the european union, however, highlights the slow pace of the process and the resistance of turkish political forces to some of the key provisions of the association agreement. i believe, mr president, that the turkish authorities have not made any significant progress on justice, fundamental rights, freedom of information, freedom of religion, immigration, despite the pressure from the citizens. economic interests in the region cannot make us indulgent on fundamental rights and freedoms. the resolution also calls on the commission and the council to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu and the member states are able to meet the challenges of the 21st century. my concern is that this partnership hypothesis may jeopardise the acceleration of the accession process, which must remain our main objective.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the framework in which we should frame the debate on this resolution is that set out in directive 2008/56, the so-called framework directive on the marine environment strategy. as the honourable member who spoke earlier said, the framework is that of the protection of the marine environment, because the directive lays down common principles on the basis of which the member states must draw up their own strategies, also in collaboration with third countries, for the achievement of good ecological status in the marine waters for which they are responsible. this is the framework within which the strategy for the atlantic region should have been set, also on the basis of the indications given by the council of the european union on 14 june, as the commissioner also mentioned in his speech in the house. the resolution put to the vote by parliament goes beyond this perimeter, proposing, far beyond what emerges from the consultations carried out by the commission itself, a strategy for a macro-region that addresses territorial as well as maritime issues. this guideline anticipates a different decision. i hope that the commission's communication, in line with what has been anticipated in this house, will bring the initiative within the scope of the directive on the integrated maritime strategy, which i support as such. that is why i am voting against.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the resolution on turkey because the constitutional reform which took place on 12 september was unanimously recognised as an important step towards europe by turkey. of course, there are still many steps to be taken and i am concerned about the many arrests of journalists. i would like to stress that turkey is the seventh largest trading partner of the european union, that the european union is turkey's main trading partner and that trade, properly interpreted for centuries, has fostered people's peaceful understanding and understanding. i therefore welcome the considerable progress made in boosting links between the european union and turkey, in particular those via the motorways of the sea crossing the northern adriatic and the northern tyrrhenian sea, on which there is now a flow of over 250 000 tirs per year in both directions, in connection with a major tir lorry-wagon rail link from the port to an internal european destination. this has eliminated a considerable amount of the remaining truck traffic on the road and i hope that this will continue.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there is still a lot to be done in the fight against discrimination in europe. i agree with our rapporteur that, although discrimination on ethnic grounds may be considered to have been eliminated, the social and economic exclusion of the majority of the roma population still exists and remains one of the major challenges we will have to face in the coming years. this is due to a whole range of specific factors such as geographical disadvantages, low levels of education or the collapse of planned economies which attract a multitude of low-skilled labour. a strategy to promote their socioeconomic inclusion will not undermine anti-discrimination laws but complement them. a significant proportion of europe's roma face such precarious and unfavourable conditions that measures to promote their social inclusion must be seen as addressing one of the biggest gaps in respect for constitutional and human rights in europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, by approving today's own-initiative report, parliament has taken a concrete step towards the genuine inclusion of roma in the communities that host them. the marginalisation of roma communities must be overcome through the full recognition of fundamental rights such as health care, education and protection for vulnerable groups. we also welcome better coordination with local and regional authorities, as well as the improvement in the text in the part where there are concrete checks on the consistency and effectiveness of funding in relation to the expected result and in the part where premium criteria are introduced for the benefit of the member states, which ensure the appropriate use of the resources allocated. however, more could probably be done in terms of the recognition of mutual rights and duties, because it is necessary to consider the concurrent responsibility of the roma communities to make their inclusion effective.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we all share the need for a european strategy for the integration of the roma and we certainly must not underestimate the possible discrimination against them, but there can be no rights without duties, no integration without legality. unauthorized shantytowns in appalling sanitary conditions, high school dropout rates, illegal activities such as theft, hospitality, induction to female and child prostitution, harassing solicitation, refusal of any integration and work accompaniment path proposed by the local authorities: this is the reality of many roma communities in my country and in other european countries. and it is a bit hypocritical to say that the responsibility is always and only with the institutions and never with those who have chosen to place this conduct on the shoulders of the community. finally, i regret that this text has not sought to refer to the correct application of directive 2004/38/ec, which provides for strict requirements for the stay of community citizens in another member state and for removal on grounds of public security. for these reasons i voted against in my group.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mrs járóka's report is particularly important at the moment and will, together with the communication which the commission is about to adopt, form the basis for the subsequent discussions at the meeting of the european roma platform in budapest, scheduled for 7 and 8 april. i share the call for the introduction of binding minimum standards at european union level in the fields of education, employment, housing and health care. in particular, i believe that more attention should be paid to primary education, which is crucial for the full integration of the roma minority. the firm invitation addressed to the european commission by france, romania, bulgaria and finland is certainly to be welcomed. however, the commission needs to play a more active role in providing guidance and direction in the development of an effective roma inclusion strategy. it is clear that there is a need to identify the specific duties which the nomadic communities will have to assume.
mr president, my group supports this report because it is a move in the right direction, calling for an eu strategy and a road map for roma inclusion. the report is inspired by a keen perception of the extremely heterogeneous cultural aspects between different roma communities in europe. at the same time, it advocates the introduction of binding and minimum standards at eu level for starting a real policy of integration. the eu strategy addresses all forms of violation of the fundamental rights of the roma people and calls for effective access for the roma to the labour market by making micro-credit available for self-employment and entrepreneurship. my group particularly appreciates the stress on the education of roma children, namely the abolition of classroom segregation through the employment of roma mediators and an increase in the number of roma teachers.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this important own-initiative report strongly affirms the need to develop a european strategy for the social inclusion of the roma. the economic and social discrimination against roma communities in europe, which has increased as a result of the current economic crisis, must be combated. the european union must develop a new legal framework and avoid continuing to tackle this problem through legislation of a non-binding nature, because it is insufficient and not suitable to achieve the objective. it is equally important to keep the roma task force as a permanent body and to start thinking about a mechanism similar to that used for the internal market assessment also for this issue. finally, europe must make every effort to ensure that its citizens, especially those who are most vulnerable, are protected in all the human rights linked to human dignity. the overall inclusion of roma is essentially a matter of fundamental rights, even if we must ask the roma community to want to integrate and not to close themselves in their own reality where they do not respect european and national standards.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, by voting today we have given a further impetus to the, shall we say, definitive solution of this problem, but we have not voted for the best possible solution. i would remind you that the more than 300 amendments to the report have been converted into 38 compromise amendments, all of which have been adopted, which aim to define better the priority areas of the strategy, that is, the objectives of this strategy. the commission, with the standing task force, will have to ensure the collection and dissemination of statistical data and good practice, and the member states should appoint a government official, hopefully at a high level, to act as a point of contact for the implementation of the strategy. but we could have been even more incisive and less hypocritical if we had focused in the report on the obligations and duties which the roma community should in any case respect in the host countries. i hope that solutions will soon be found to enable this community to live together better in all the member states.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, no more children who are not in school, no more children who are forced to beg or are exploited. these are some of the aims of the járóka report, which is an important political response. beyond the declarations of principle, we await the european commission's proposal, due in april, for clearer and more shared responsibility and coordination between member states and european institutions on roma policies. the aim must be to make the best use of available resources, starting with community funds, and to avoid leaving the burden of all problems and continuing emergencies to local authorities. i hope that a debate on directive 38 will be opened. the directive provides for specific conditions employment, sufficient economic resources, health insurance for the maintenance of the right of residence but, at the same time, it presents gaps in relation to the eventuality that these requirements are not met. it's a shortcoming that needs to be addressed as soon as possible.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report and i would like to congratulate mrs járóka on her work, which has been able to summarise the various positions by clearly defining the objectives and priorities of the strategy, such as the provision of specific measures against nomadism and guarantees relating to basic health care, as well as equal access to primary, secondary and higher education and the right to housing. the strategy is aimed at inclusion, not mere integration, and it is clear that the role of the commission and local authorities will be crucial, especially with regard to the control and management of community funds. the only limitation of this report is the lack of instruments to verify the actual willingness of some roma communities to integrate and the consequences that should result from an unavailability in terms of staying on the territory of a member country, such as continuing treatment and assistance and welfare programmes that certainly cannot be extended indefinitely without results.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the recent and deep economic crisis which has hit european industry has also highlighted its importance for the economy of the european union. it has often focused on the idea that markets should self-regulate and this has so far been achieved mainly through individual measures with virtually no coordination between member states. the europe 2020 strategy, for the first time, recognises the need for a new approach by introducing a flagship initiative. it is time for the european union to make full use of the common opportunities for sustainable renewal and further development of the industrial base with quality jobs. european industry should maintain its leadership in key sectors, not be left behind. it is time for the union to choose its own path for the industry of the future. we must ensure that the added value is created within our european market. to this end, a distinctive macroeconomic coordination of economic, fiscal and budgetary policies for growth and employment, for example through the tax harmonisation of corporate taxes, is essential.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the lange report deals with a very topical problem, the problem of how to respond to the economic and financial crisis which has seriously affected our productive system. i think that the answer contained in this resolution is an extremely positive one, because it manages to bring together all the variables necessary to build a good economic recovery plan. the idea of focusing on innovation and research, taking into account the size of our entrepreneurial fabric, is very important and i think it suggests a valid stimulus to the commission's perhaps a little more conservative position. i would like to express my appreciation for the work of the rapporteur, who has succeeded in summarizing the more than 500 amendments and has put down a resolution which, taken as a whole, makes a major contribution to the work ahead. the picture that emerges is that of an industrial policy centred on european policy, cross-sectoral and above all participatory through the use of bottom-up and top-up monitoring models. there is only one remaining point of contention, and that is the european patent. i am totally opposed to this, but that did not prevent me from voting in favour of a very positive report.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report highlights many positive aspects and reflects the views and demands expressed by the various national industrial associations. i cannot therefore fail to agree with the general outline of mr lange's report. however, some critical issues have emerged which have not been addressed and resolved, such as the demand for new legislative measures on resource efficiency and, above all, the issue of enhanced cooperation on patents. it is important now to address the question of the european rules of origin mark, which i believe is an indispensable instrument for strengthening and improving european industry and its competitiveness. i voted in favour of the lange report because i hope that the adoption of this report will encourage all the institutions to work towards the ambitious programme outlined and to translate it into concrete political action.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it would be inconceivable that a sector which represents 57 million people in the union, three quarters of european exports of industrial goods and about a third of the gross value added of the european union, should not be supported by adequate sectoral policies aimed at growth and development. there can be no competitive trade policy without innovative and quality industrial activity. i agree with the suggestions made by the committee on international trade, particularly those which stress the importance of an effective trade defence system, using the instruments provided for, where appropriate. defending the union's interest in the future negotiations, in order to protect industry and employment, is an essential necessity to help overcome the crisis and to ensure that, with the manufacturing sector, the real economy is given priority over the financial one, avoiding those speculative bubbles which have led to so much disaster.

in writing. − the 2012 budget, like the 2013 budget, will be consolidation budgets, designed to reflect member states' expenditure containment and to provide a benchmark for the amounts to be set under the next financial framework. the objective for this budget must be excellence, which means pursuing the objectives of economy, efficiency and effectiveness with the minimum of available resources. what parliament must aim at in this consolidation phase is an increase in the budget which is not above the rate of inflation. this threshold represents an exercise of high responsibility. the increased expenditure resulting from the enlargement of croatia and the 18 new members provided for by the lisbon treaty will be supplemented by an amending budget. in order to respect the expenditure-containment approach, i would like all the institutions to forward in advance the information needed to draw up a general picture of administrative expenditure, so that the budgetary authority can take decisions on the use of resources in accordance with a multiannual, sustainable approach, aimed at the comparability over time and between the institutions of the data provided.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution by mr fernandes on the guidelines for the 2012 budgetary procedure provides an overview of the european parliament's budgetary management with a view to optimising the future management of the resources available to the european institutions, which is why i voted in favour. parliament will have to adopt its budget in such a way as to consolidate the future financial framework and the additional human resources to meet the requirements of the lisbon treaty, improve and complete the buildings available, the computer and interpreting services. the main objective remains to find a good method of managing resources in order to be able to contain expenditure while still improving services.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on the guidelines for the 2012 budgetary procedure because i considered that the current economic crisis, which is having repercussions at the present stage, especially in terms of employment, requires a joint effort to contain it not only by the member states but also by the european institutions. i therefore agree that in the present context the general principle of european financing should be based on budgetary austerity. however, i would like to stress that, even in the face of the economic situation, the budget of the union, and in particular the budget of parliament, as the only community institution directly elected by the citizens, should be particularly attentive to promoting and bringing citizens closer to the institutions of the union, especially in times of uncertainty about the future such as these. in particular, i think it would be particularly useful to be able to think about a better distribution of parliament's information and liaison offices in the member states and a more strategic location of these offices, also in the light of the recent upheavals in neighbouring countries.
in writing. − the motion for a resolution on the european union strategy in the atlantic region follows the european council's call on the commission to develop an integrated strategy addressing maritime and territorial issues in the atlantic. i voted in favour of the resolution to urge the european commission to prepare and report on the negotiations for the strategy by june. the aim is to implement better coordination in the region on issues such as the integrated maritime policy, trans-european transport networks, fisheries, climate and environment projects, research and development, increase the movement of people, goods and services in the regions, in order to achieve the goal of cohesion policy, ensuring that all this coincides with the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy and with the policies of the european union for the period after 2013.

member of the commission. − mr president, let me first of all thank the honourable members for a very responsible debate on next week’s european council. on behalf of the commission, i would like to comment on several speeches concerning libya and japan before commenting on economic issues. as you know, the commission has no competence on the security and defence front but we have been coordinating the european response to the escalating humanitarian crisis on the libyan borders. the no-fly-zone military action implemented according to un security council resolution 1973 brought new circumstances which need to be taken into account when delivering humanitarian assistance in a secure and efficient way to those in need, either at the borders or inside libya. it brought new hope as well that innocent civilian lives would be spared. although the events in japan have no immediate health consequences for citizens in the european union, it is important to take stock of eu nuclear safety policies, as well as contingency plans and safety measures in place. the commission uses all instruments available to monitor the impact, including on future safety. to my mind, japan teaches us that risks can become reality; what was thought to be impossible must now be included in our planning. a european approach for a comprehensive safety and risk assessment of nuclear facilities would maximise the effects at the european level. before drawing final conclusions, a full analysis of the accident in japan is essential; the assessment should cover the most important issues, such as safety requirements for earthquakes, as well as emergency power supply assistance for reactor cooling. on economic policy too, your debate reflected the magnitude of what is at stake at tomorrow’s european council and i trust that the messages sent from here will be heard and listened to in all capitals of europe. it is fair to say that the european union will have profoundly evolved after this march. the financial crisis which turned into an economic recession and then into a sovereign debt and banking crisis has forced europe to seek new ways forward, to consider all possible options and to take decisions with long-lasting consequences. as president barroso said in his opening remarks, we will respond to the challenge with a comprehensive strategy which builds on the strengths, values and institutions of the european union. it is exactly the kind of challenges which are facing us today that the european union was created for: to be able to withstand storms together and to be able by joint efforts to come out of a crisis stronger than before. as a result of very long talks for several months, the elements of a comprehensive response in economic policy are now finally there for the leaders of the union to agree and commit to in the european council tomorrow. the member states, and especially the euro area member states, are all pursuing intensified fiscal consolidation and growth-enhancing structural reforms with very strong determination. this is now the first and foremost cornerstone of making progress on this strategy. secondly, both the council and the parliament are delivering on your commitment to conclude the commission’s legislative package on economic governance by this summer. reinforced economic governance is indeed the cornerstone of our comprehensive response. thirdly, the permanent european stability mechanism will be made functional as of june 2013, with the effective lending capacity of eur 500 billion. by this decision we will have in place a financial backstop with a sufficient containment effect to clear away even the slightest doubt about our capacity to act even in the most stressed scenarios. the role of the commission in the running of the operations of the esm will be central, and the link of the esm to the eu institutions, of course including the european parliament, will be very clearly and firmly established. we shall in due course propose a regulation based on article 136 of the treaty clarifying the steps to define policy conditionality and to ensure consistency with the eu framework for country surveillance. last but not least, the banking sector repair must be completed, to safeguard the provision of credit to the real economy, to enterprises and to households. the next round of bank stress tests will be conducted in the coming months; the results will guide the necessary restructuring and possible recapitalisation of the eu banking sector. before the publication of results, all the member states will need to decide and present their strategies, if needed, for the possible restructuring and recapitalisation of their vulnerable institutions. it is indeed essential that we see that these two problems have to be resolved in parallel; financial repair must be accelerated, banks restructured and, if need be, recapitalised as soon as possible. this is a precondition for restoring and reinforcing confidence in the european economy, improving banks’ robustness, and ensuring that we safeguard economic growth through credit supply. to conclude, once the european council confirms its full commitment to all of these elements of our comprehensive economic strategy to overcome the crisis, the european union will be well on track for turning the economic tide this year, 2011. this does not mean all is fine, even less that we can sit back. but, yes, it does mean that we are prepared to face the current and emerging challenges and to prevent crises in the future.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the document we are considering today is not only a document on the priorities of the next european budget, but it is also, and above all, a strategic document on the new role that the european budget must play in the context of stronger economic governance. this year is the first year of the european semester, a semester designed to create the greatest possible coordination between the union's budget and the member states' budgets, to create the greatest possible synergy, the greatest possible complementarity, and all this basically means one thing: the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. today, these objectives, the european objectives, can only be those of the 2020 strategy, a large, ambitious strategy with five very important targets and seven major flagship initiatives. they're important, big goals, but they're also very specific. the first target is very important: it is a question of building a more and better employed europe through the right investments. we therefore have a high priority for the 2012 budget: we must not waste time in making the 2020 strategy a reality, starting with the very first of the targets, more jobs in europe. it is therefore essential and urgent that we start defining the dimension of the 2020 strategy in our budget now. to do this, two basic things are needed: we need to plan, we need to look ahead. design means excluding mathematical approaches to budgeting, it makes no sense! a mathematical increase, a dry and indiscriminate increase is not useful! we need to look at exactly what programmes and actions are useful to our 2020 strategy. looking to the future means one thing: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. there is also a very important issue, which is that of flexibility. we are at the end of the programming period and therefore the budget is particularly tight. i therefore believe that it is really important to consider from the outset all the available flexibility instruments as fundamental, indispensable for this budget we are about to draw up, if we want it to be not only possible, not only fundamental for taking the first step towards the 2020 strategy which cannot be a failure at all, as we have seen in the past, but also if we want it to be a useful and effective budget. i am convinced that all these great objectives will be possible only if we patiently build together, from the outset, a renewed climate of institutional cooperation. institutional cooperation is one of the great challenges of the lisbon treaty, which we always talk about with little attention. institutional cooperation really means finding a climate of renewed parity to work together on this delicate issue, the budget, which is one of the most not only strategic but also the most real and most real instruments for building our future.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report seeks to put an end to the fragmentation of the regulatory framework which has hitherto hindered the completion of the internal market by revising the four existing directives: the aim is to improve the functioning of the market for consumers and businesses, increasing the confidence of the former in the market and reducing the reluctance of businesses to operate across borders. the proposal is complex and has many specific aspects which have been examined and debated since the last french presidency. with the new barroso commission, led by commissioner reding, total harmonisation was no longer considered a dogma and we have rightly embarked on the road towards more targeted harmonisation. although i am not entirely satisfied with the result achieved, which i consider to be modest and the result of a compromise downwards, i believe and hope that this proposal can serve as a starting point for further developments. that is why i have supported this report.

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the united nations conference on trade and development in 1968 recommended the creation of a 'generalized system of preferences' (gsp) under which the industrialized countries would grant trade preferences to all developing countries on a non-reciprocal basis. the european community was the first to implement a gsp scheme, and since its inception, the gsp has been one of the main instruments of the eu's trade and development policy to help developing countries reduce poverty by generating revenue through international trade. although this is the most widely used system among those implemented by the industrialized countries, i agree with the need to review the regulation in question in order to simplify the application of the system. i also believe that the general review should be addressed in the proposal for a new regulation, which i hope will be presented in good time. the new proposal should aim at greater clarity and transparency of the gsp system. i also call the commission's attention to the need to verify compliance with the commitments by regularly launching investigations involving the european parliament and representatives of civil society in the country concerned.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the draft resolution voted today in parliament on the introduction of a single application procedure for the issuing of a permit permit enabling third-country nationals to reside and work in the territory of the union represents a further step towards the harmonization of the national legislation of the member states. the establishment of legal immigration measures that are uniform across the union, by defining common application procedures for those seeking admission to the territory of a member state for employment purposes, will enable the eu to respond to the labour needs of the internal labour market by providing, through the granting of equal rights, a tool to combat exploitation and discrimination. i think, however, that it is necessary to allow the states, under certain conditions, to set limits on the capacity to take in nationals from non-eu countries and offer them employment in their territory. the proposal has the obvious aim of combating irregular immigration and illegal work, but it can and should also be seen as a useful contribution to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, also allowing for easier border controls.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report, which is returning to the house for the second time, because i believe that it responds well to the considerable demographic challenges facing the european union in the coming years by establishing a single application procedure for third-country nationals wishing to be admitted to the territory of a member state for employment purposes and by offering them a secure legal status. economic immigration is a reality that needs to be organised, but it is also a necessity in view of the democratic and economic challenges that the european union will face in the near future. immigration policy must therefore be conceived as a means of adjusting our labour needs, thus contributing to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. from a technical point of view, the exclusion of seasonal workers and workers posted within their undertaking is justified by the presentation by the commission of proposals for directives specific to these categories of workers. as regards the exclusion of asylum seekers and persons enjoying international protection, it is important to stress that the existing instruments in these areas provide greater protection than the present proposal for a directive.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mrs mathieu's proposal for a directive on a single procedure for applying for residence and work permits for thirdcountry nationals because i believe it is important that europe should have community rules on the entry of non-community workers, both economic and social. labour immigration can increase the competitiveness and vitality of the economy and make europe better able to face the demographic challenge of the future. the proposal for a directive calls on member states to adopt flexible immigration policies in order to support the union's long-term development, and will simplify the often complex administrative practices of welcoming migrants for employment purposes, while also offering a tool to combat exploitation and discrimination against certain categories of workers.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the stockholm programme adopted by the european council on 10 and 11 december 2009 calls on the member states to adopt flexible immigration policies in order to support the development and economic performance of the union. the aim of this proposal for a directive is to contribute to the implementation of the programme. in particular, a single application procedure is introduced for third-country nationals wishing to be admitted to the territory of a member state for the purpose of employment, by: (i) simplify the often complex administrative practices of the reception of migrants; (ii) to define a means of combating exploitation and discrimination against workers; (iii) to ensure that the labour markets of the member states are able to meet current and future labour requirements. the directive applies to all citizens admitted to the territory for work purposes and to those who were initially admitted for other reasons and who subsequently obtained a work permit in accordance with the provisions of national or union law. the proposal for a directive thus contributes to fostering a common approach to economic immigration for the 27 member states. i therefore reiterate my vote in favour.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today's vote is a step forward towards the adoption of a single application procedure for thirdcountry nationals wishing to enter european territory and work. europe is aiming to simplify the administrative procedure and to issue both residence and work permits in the form of a single document. i would like to stress that today's vote is not about attracting new workers to our territory indiscriminately, nor is it about countering illegal immigration. any non-community worker who wants to settle in europe will always have to obtain a residence permit first. the proposal adopted today also ensures full respect for the principle of subsidiarity, setting minimum requirements in terms of rights and obligations but leaving member states flexibility and freedom as regards the introduction of the procedure into national legislation and its practical application. the european union cannot limit the power of the member states to organise social security schemes and each state must be able to set its own rules in this area.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission's proposal for a directive on consumer rights combines four previous directives into a single legislative instrument. it is the result of the review of the consumer acquis launched in 2004 with the aim of simplifying and complementing the existing regulatory framework for consumer protection. the current regulatory framework causes significant compliance costs for european businesses wishing to operate cross-border and having to comply with fragmented legislation. i believe that the fragmentation of legal rules is a deterrent both for businesses from buying or selling across borders and for consumers. the report under discussion seeks to strike the necessary balance between a high level of consumer protection and the competitiveness of firms on the market, while ensuring respect for the principle of subsidiarity. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's proposals which are converging towards a type of targeted harmonisation, i.e. harmonisation limited to specific aspects of certain contracts such as, in particular, information requirements, the right of withdrawal with distance and off-premises contracts, while managing to maintain a high level of protection for european consumers.
in writing. - i congratulate mr schwab on the work he has done so far. i voted in favour of the schwab report because it has the merit of protecting consumers in crossborder purchases. the text voted today is intended to ensure a high level of consumer protection in the 27 member states. at the same time, it aims to protect and support businesses, which, regardless of their size, can supply their goods and services to european consumers without encountering unnecessary legal obstacles. the aim of bringing together four directives on this subject is therefore to bring the existing rules more closely into line, avoiding the legal fragmentation which is so often an obstacle for both consumers and businesses. in this sense, this document can contribute to a better functioning of the internal market by increasing consumer confidence.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the objective is very ambitious: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a breach of the directive. about a year ago, professor monti said in his report to president barroso: '... the legislator should reach agreement as soon as possible on the draft consumer rights directive, in order to ensure a high level of consumer protection in an integrated retail market.' i agree with professor monti. the absence of common rules in the various member states has led to a fragmentation of the regulatory framework which is harmful both to consumers and to businesses and which in fact prevents the completion of the common market. at a time of crisis such as the one we are experiencing worldwide, europe certainly cannot afford to have its businesses left behind and its consumers not adequately protected. it is therefore urgent to identify the right common denominator as soon as possible, so that the rules can be harmonised at european level. we must all make an effort to reach an agreement with the council as soon as possible, perhaps at first reading.

member of the commission. − mr president, in these times of austerity the commission is rationalising as well. mr simpson, as rapporteur you said that this is a technical report and it is indeed, but nevertheless it is an important one. the purpose of the proposal from the commission was to update and optimise the existing legal framework for european statistics on tourism. both producers and users of tourism statistics have requested this adjustment. so the ultimate aim is to provide monthly and annual european statistics on tourism supply and demand using a common framework. the proposal is very well balanced in terms of data needs and the burden put on respondents and administrators. to achieve this, permission has been included to collect some parts of the data on an optional basis or every third year, to defer the entry into force of certain provisions to a later stage and to exclude the smallest enterprises. following an informal trilogue held on 12 january 2011 and further discussions, as you mentioned, rapporteur, a compromise text was agreed between parliament and the council. in particular, the council agreed to an additional demand from parliament of having the variable concerning the accessibility of tourist accommodation for persons with reduced mobility included in the regulation. all amendments in the report and the compromise text are acceptable to the commission. therefore i would like to thank you, mr simpson, and the shadow rapporteurs and the members of the committee on transport and tourism for your constructive work on the proposal. following fruitful cooperation between all three institutions, i believe that we have now reached our objective, which is the establishment of a common framework for the systematic development, production and dissemination of european statistics on tourism.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam commissioner, allow me first of all to thank the rapporteur for his commitment and for his ability to summarize the political situation. the european people's party group will strongly support the compromise reached with the council. this regulation replaces the text in force since 1995, which no longer reflects the current reality in relation to some key aspects, such as new needs and habits of users, the need for more timely data and an improvement in the comparability and completeness of the statistical framework. the final text incorporates all the political priorities supported by the epp during the negotiations, in particular a better definition of the parts of the regulations that can be amended by delegated acts, the introduction of the definition of 'day visits', which is essential to include in the data collection also all those who do not stay overnight, thus also including the phenomenon of conference tourism, a better definition of the data to be collected, including the expenditure of tourists during the journey for food and drinks in bars and restaurants, which represents a substantial part of our tourism industry, accepted albeit only on a voluntary basis by the council, and data on accessibility for people with reduced mobility. the rapporteur has already pointed out that this was a key point for the parliament's delegation. in conclusion, this regulation is an important part of the new european tourism strategy on which all the european institutions are debating. it will provide an updated legal framework to keep pace with market developments, more clarity and consistency in the collection of tourism data, and also ensure more effective monitoring of the sector to better understand consumer needs. i would like to thank mr simpson, the commission for the initiative and the council for the excellent mediation.

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, tourism is an important economic activity in the union, with a high potential in terms of contributing to job creation and economic growth. with some 1.8 million smes, the estimated contribution of the european tourism industry to eu gdp is over 5%. the system of tourism statistics is currently regulated by directive 95/57/ec on the collection of statistical data in this field. i believe that statistics are not only useful for monitoring specific tourism policies, but can also be useful in the wider context of regional policy and sustainable development. in recent decades, the sector has faced major challenges such as increased global competition, demographic trends, environmental constraints, the seasonal distribution of tourist movements and the increasing use of new information and communication technologies by customers. in recognising the key role of statistics in the development of more effective tourism policies at european, national, regional and local level, i believe that the overall objective should be to strengthen the eu tourism sector through coordinated action at union level integrating the initiatives of individual member states.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs svensson. we know that violence against women and children is on the rise throughout europe. we therefore urge the commission to present a proposal, as it has already promised, for a comprehensive strategy on violence against women by 2011, which includes domestic violence and genital mutilation, but also some more subtle forms. i am thinking of the serious discrimination and harassment in the workplace against pregnant women or those who intend to marry with demands for their early resignation, as is the case in my country, and which is no longer a crime as it was in the past. i am also thinking of the actual incitement of violence perpetrated through the media and advertising. after the directive on trafficking in human beings and the one we are waiting for on victims of violence, announced by commissioner malmström, i believe that the lisbon treaty provides the basis for further harmonisation of the rules in the member states' recognition of the importance of the crime of violence against women and children as specific forms of violence, also by defining essential standards for counselling, legal assistance and protection services for women and children, also in collaboration with ngos, as well as constant and comparable statistics with impact analyses of the forms of prevention and response by member states on the reduction of violence. i think that there is a common will in parliament - i too have signed the written declaration - to define a year of reflection for the whole of europe on the subject of violence, and i think that parliament can give a very strong and very authoritative voice in this.
in writing. my commitment to the protection of the most vulnerable and of women who are offended by violence requires me to vote in favour of legislation to guarantee the rights of victims of violence. women, like children, are in some contexts particularly vulnerable members of our society. i therefore believe that it is important to ensure greater protection for women who report that they have been subjected to violence. i am therefore in favour of free legal aid for women who are victims of violence. i know that there is a risk of inequality when men wrongly accused of violence have to pay the legal costs while the accusers benefit from free legal aid, and i have thought this through carefully. however, i believe that the numbers of cases of violence, including domestic violence, require that we stand up for those who are most affected by the lack of support: women victims of violence are statistically a highly predominant proportion compared to the few malefactors who can take advantage of the system to infer on innocent men. it is difficult for abused women to report abuse, and free legal aid would encourage victims and help reduce the number of cases that go unpunished.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this tragically timely own-initiative report was produced over a year ago in order to give a pragmatic and balanced assessment of the phenomenon of immigration and its structural causes, regardless of political or ideological prejudices. we wanted to explore the role of foreign policy and its possibilities for intervening in the root causes of immigration, beyond the humanitarian or emergency aspects. wars, ethnic tensions, persistent climate change, violation of human rights, lack of civil and economic freedoms, endemic corruption, absence of institutional representatives of the needs of citizens, such as trade unions, associations, political parties: the european union has a long history of being a major player in the world economy, and it is in this context that the european union is making its contribution to the development of the world economy. no development cooperation policy can be fully effective without addressing the causes of instability in the countries of origin of migrants. this implies regional cooperation with both the countries of origin and transit, including through bilateral agreements. the millennium development goals are already very ambitious, but they will certainly not be achieved without political stability and without effective mechanisms to prevent conflict and maintain peace. the global scope of this policy and its all-inclusive approach require clear ideas and substantial financial resources, which are hard to come by at this time of crisis. the union's initiatives should therefore be coordinated with those of other major powers, such as the united states, in order to avoid overlapping of interventions in the same areas or dispersion of financial resources, as has often happened in the past. a global phenomenon must be met with a global policy. we must help the countries of origin of immigrants to move towards democracy and good governance by making available our values and our experience. the european neighbourhood policy should offer an economic agenda capable of raising employment levels and trade agreements capable of generating real economic development consistent with market laws. commissioner füle and high representative ashton, using the phrase 'more for more', recalled the concept of conditionality in aid, which is intended to reward countries which are most active in democratic reform and respect for human rights. this is consistent with our european values, effective for development and - excuse me - morally just towards the european taxpayer. in conclusion, i would like to stress that a european policy for managing large migratory flows must be matched by the acceptance of the concept of burden sharing, in line with the duty of solidarity of the states under article 80 of the treaty, because no country can cope with an emergency of such enormous dimensions on its own. finally, i thank commissioner malmström for his support of some or many of the points in this report and i hope that europe can work concretely together with italy to deal with a phenomenon which is of international dimension and which affects us all.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, before i come to the report i must give an answer to mr tavares and mr meyer. i have great respect for everyone's opinions, but i think their judgment on lampedusa and what has been done in lampedusa is not very generous. i wanted to inform them that in three nights 12,000 people have arrived in lampedusa. lampedusa is a small island, with 6,000 inhabitants, and in three nights 12,000 people suddenly arrived, and the number of people grew to 20,000. i think it's very difficult for any country to accommodate such a large number of people arriving in such a short time, on a small island that has no facilities for such a large number of arrivals. at present, there are 1,400 migrants on lampedusa. much has been done and as soon as sea conditions permitted, migrants were moved to other reception centres, mainly in the south of the country. that brings us to the report. i would like to thank the shadow rapporteurs from the different therefore in the council. if you put that kind of enthusiasm into it, i think the results will come. i conclude by saying that it is very difficult to summarize. however, if a summary is possible, it is that as long as there are enormous differences in the levels of development between the north and the south of the world, as long as there are enormous differences in the quality of democratic institutions, as long as there are enormous differences in respect for human rights, any policy of reception will be ineffective and partial. we must take action in a major strategic policy of cooperation and aid which will address the structural causes of these enormous inequalities between the north and the south of the world. if we solve those structural causes, everything else will follow, and we'll probably all live in a better world.

the agenda includes the report by elisabeth jeggle, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on the role of women in agriculture and rural areas (2010/2054(ini) (a7-0016/2011).
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i would first like to thank the rapporteur and the members of the committee on agriculture and rural development, as it was important to put this topic on the table. the commission is very conscious of the essential role women play in agriculture and in rural areas. it can see that this is a task for the rural development policy. the rural development regulation provides for support in a number of areas which are important for women in rural areas. the setting-up and development of micro-enterprises, adding value to agricultural projects and seeking sales outlets for them are only a few examples. the rural development policy also foresees possibilities to help men and women to balance family and professional life. for example, under the basic services measure, social facilities like day care centres for children or elderly people can be supported. in addition, local transport services and small-scale infrastructure are eligible for support. the situation in rural areas is very diverse across member states, including as regards possibilities and requirements for women. member states and regions have to carefully analyse the situation and design tailor-made measures linked to local conditions, taking account of the specific problems women face. for example, member states can give preference to women with regard to certain measures. in addition, member states can use financial engineering to set up guarantee funds in order to help women to get access to credit. women should also play an important role in the leader programme, where they should bring in their specific interests and their specific potential in order to mobilise the development potential of an area. the commission agrees that it would be useful to have more data on the situation of women. however, especially in the light of member states’ call for simplification, it would prove difficult to convince them of additional reporting burdens. but for those data for which it is possible, statistics should be presented and analysed, broken down by gender. the commission will include, where available, data on women in its progress report on the implementation of the strategic guidelines for rural development. one very important factor in taking women forward in agriculture and rural areas is the exchange of experience. in this context, i would like to draw your attention to the european network for rural development and its constituent national networks. they can be used to learn from each other’s best practices and it would be desirable if more women’s associations made use of these existing networks in order to connect women in different rural areas with each other.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 5 april 2011. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by marian-jean marinescu, on behalf of the committee on budgetary control, on the efficiency and effectiveness of eu funding for decommissioning of nuclear power stations in the new member states (2010/2104 ((ini)) (a7-0054/2011).
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, the commission very much welcomes parliament’s own-initiative report on the efficient and effective eu funding of decommissioning of nuclear power plants in the new member states. nuclear safety is, and will remain, an absolute priority for the eu, and this is why the commission attaches great importance to efforts that facilitate the safe decommissioning of nuclear reactor units that have been deemed not to be upgradable to the necessary safety standards. let me first say that we share with parliament many of the views expressed in its report. we agree with the need for member states to provide detailed decommissioning plans, as well as sound long-term financial planning. we also deem it essential for the funds for the most part to be allocated to decommissioning activities and for the commission to have an important role to play in ensuring strict monitoring of the use of the funds. the commission believes in a strict application of the ‘polluter pays’ principle, so we share the opinion of parliament that it is up to the operators of the nuclear plant to ensure that financial resources for decommissioning are already allocated during the operational life of the plants. decommissioning must be made as safe as possible, and sound, transparent and supervised management of decommissioning funds is crucial for this. it can also be noted, however, that the report focuses on the efficiency and effectiveness of eu funding in the area of decommissioning. the commission was glad to see, in various parts of the report, that there is full recognition that the main objective of the eu funding was, first and foremost, to ensure that the reactor units were closed and remained so for nuclear safety reasons. we believe that having met this objective is an essential element to be taken into account when assessing the efficiency and effectiveness of eu funding. the commission considers it important to clarify that eu support was never intended to cover the full cost of decommissioning, nor to compensate for all the economic consequences. eu support was aimed merely at contributing to compensation for the early stages of closure. the commission also underlines that it is the member state that bear full responsibility for the decommissioning of its nuclear installations. providing detailed long-term planning is the responsibility of the member states, which are equally responsible for establishing precise timetables and cost estimates for the completion of decommissioning. i would like to thank the rapporteur and parliament for this timely debate on an issue which, in the context of fukushima, has become more pertinent. safe and complete decommissioning is a key element of nuclear safety, for which we aim at the highest standards. parliament’s report constitutes a valuable contribution to the discussion that the commission will have with the three member states concerned in view of assessing possible financial eu support beyond 2013.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 5 april 2011. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by mr kader arif, on behalf of the committee on international trade, on the future of european policy on international investment (2010/2203 ((ini)) - (a7-0070/2011).
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, the commission welcomes parliament’s report on the future european international investment policy. it is an important step that paves the way for the implementation of the new eu exclusive competence on investment. as you know, investment is a new frontier for the common commercial policy. we should seize the opportunity – we are in absolute agreement with parliament on this – to build together an integrated and coherent investment policy that promotes investments and makes a positive contribution both to economic growth and sustainable development. the commission also fully shares parliament’s statement that investor protection should remain the first priority of the european investment policy. we believe that the new policy should serve the purpose of assuring all european investors that they are able to operate in an open and properly and fairly regulated business environment, not only within the internal market, but also when operating in third countries. i also take note of parliament’s recommendation that the eu should draw on member states’ best practices found in their bilateral investment treaties. indeed, the thrust of the union’s action in this area should be to deliver better results than those obtained by member states individually. while aiming at high levels of protection for our investors, we should not compromise other objectives, such as the public capacity to regulate or coherence with other eu policies. the right of states and of the eu to take the measures necessary to achieve legitimate public policy objectives is a standing rule of the common commercial policy. it will equally apply to our investment policy. the dispute settlement regime and the related financial responsibility are also very important issues and we need to further reflect on them. our objective, as mentioned in the communication, is to ensure transparency, consistency of rulings and make the system as productive as possible. we also need to address a number of issues which arise because of the eu’s status under international law. we will take into account parliament’s views, as expressed in the report, when we analyse possible options and further ideas for a comprehensive approach to these issues. we will carefully consider all recommendations put forward in parliament’s report, while progressively developing and implementing our investment policy. the commission has already tabled proposals for investment negotiating directives for canada, india and singapore. we want to seize opportunities for ongoing wider trade negotiations and to engage in comprehensive investment negotiations with those countries. parliament’s opinion is therefore very timely, to guide the commission and the council when we define final respective negotiation directives. last but not least, i would like to assure you that, as the development of a comprehensive european investment policy is now a joint responsibility of all the institutions, the commission will stand ready to cooperate with parliament and the council while respecting the division of competences among all the institutions involved.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on wednesday 6 april 2011. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this council has dealt with three very important subjects: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. on the first point, although we are close to the people so badly affected, we cannot accept a revision of the trade agreements to the detriment of our companies. we are in favour of humanitarian intervention with means, men and money. to think that the financial crisis is over is pure utopia. it is essential to have a package of measures to help the member states to get out of the current situation, ensuring stability for the whole euro area. we are also in favour of reducing the regulatory burden and bureaucracy and promoting trade with third countries, provided that it is mutually beneficial. on the maghreb, we think the european union has made a bad impression, because each member country has acted independently and the high representative, baroness ashton, has not been able to manage the crisis. in particular, the european union has abandoned italy to an uncontrolled invasion of illegal immigrants.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, there is no doubt that the establishment of a permanent stability mechanism is an important achievement, which provides the basis for the political commitment to defend the common currency at all costs. the european parliament therefore supported this approach, despite its reservations about the intergovernmental nature and method of the fund, and focused on the objective of ensuring a strong link between the esm and the union institutions. in this sense, the reference in the european council conclusions to a regulation to establish the procedures for defining cross compliance is important and we now expect the commission to draw up an appropriate proposal. however, this positive result is difficult to consider adequate. the problem is the underlying direction of european economic governance. the emphasis is on treating the symptoms of the disease rather than the causes. the deficits are the effect and not the cause of the crisis and to think that we can solve the disease by simply cutting deficits with one hand and refinancing the banks with the other is illusory and risks aggravating the crisis and rendering the very task of the permanent stability mechanism unsustainable. if you want to treat the disease and not just the symptoms, you have to attack some of the underlying nodes. we are talking about strengthening europe's competitiveness. that is true, but what model of competitiveness are we pursuing? we cannot pursue the model of a recovery driven solely by exports outside europe, because that model will accentuate imbalances. to be more competitive with the outside world, we must also create a domestic demand for quality. we must therefore tackle the banking and credit system's link to the economy in order to channel european savings towards long-term investment. we must have instruments such as eurobonds, the financial transaction tax and a budget worthy of the name for large public investments at european level, which act as a steering wheel for private investments. finally, we must regard the european social model not as a burden but as a resource.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report because it represents a first step towards an eu policy on migration flows arising from instability. in this regard it is important that this parliament speaks out against this hysterical vision of a looming invasion of migrants and asylum seekers coming from the south. we are not going to be overwhelmed by millions of people escaping political deprivation and tyrannies. many people are afraid that asylum seekers are arriving in greater numbers, straining our buckling welfare systems. this claim is good to gain votes and build support for harsh immigration policies, but it is not backed by the facts. the overall number of people claiming asylum in the west dropped by more than 40% over the past decade according to data just released by the united nations.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the european debate on migration, we often hear the following: "what problem can a country of almost 60 million inhabitants like italy have in welcoming a few tens of thousands of immigrants?" in this question two data are often ignored. first, many of these immigrants want to go to other countries in the european union. secondly, in the last two years, less than 4,000 people have landed on italian shores, thanks to bilateral agreements with libya and tunisia. in the last two months, after the political crisis, we've already reached 22,000 people. italy is a pressure cooker today. on the one hand, the flow from north africa, particularly the flow of economic migrants from tunisia, is not stopping. on the other hand, france, in ventimiglia, rejects migrants because they have no residence permit. if european solidarity exists, it is time to demonstrate it by jointly deciding at community level how to deal with these flows, both in emergency and in the long term, what instruments to implement in relation to those arriving in europe and what measures to adopt in the countries of origin. this text is a first step in that direction and that is why i voted in favour.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the measure we voted for today provides some clarity on the phenomenon of migration flows and enhances the work of frontex. i think that this should be seen positively and, in that sense, the vote should be seen positively. i believe, however, that this position must be accompanied by equal clarity on the part of the member states, because this is a challenge which concerns the european institutions but also the policy of the member states. i must say, however, that this clarity has not been implemented and practised by all the member states so far, starting with the policy of the italian government, which has dealt with the situation in lampedusa in a very critical and questionable way, where thousands of migrants have been basically left to fend for themselves, whereas solidarity - more than legal, human - would have required immediate and certainly greater attention than has been given, except for the fact that we then had to deal, as we have done here, with the legal problem.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, if it is true that many migratory flows are caused by instability, it is with a certain modesty that we use this term inappropriately, because instability is in fact war, genocide, uncontrolled violence, insurrections, the misery to which these peoples have been condemned, even with the silence of the european union. then there is the desire for freedom. the resolution we voted for calls for a policy towards the east of the union and its most appropriate instruments to deal with the various aspects that cause this instability. i wonder what credibility this foreign policy will have, given that events in libya and north africa have shown that there is no such thing as a foreign policy for the union. the governments of the states have gone their separate ways, offering a bleak spectacle to the world and to the people we are supposed to be helping. the union has been unable to offer a policy of reception for refugees except to a limited extent in relation to needs. the island of lampedusa and italy have not been given an answer. we therefore certainly vote in favour of this measure, but we call on the union to finally develop a foreign policy worthy of the name.
