in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr provera's report in respect of one of the founding principles of the union, the principle of solidarity between peoples. the current situation, given the political crises in north africa and the slow or no response of european policy to the migratory flows, is so serious and problematic that i believe it must be addressed in a timely manner. the request to the council, by adopting this text, to give full effect to the solidarity clause with a concrete action plan and burden sharing among the member states cannot and must not be ignored. the text specifically calls for minimum standards for granting temporary protection to immigrants and for measures to share responsibility and effort between member states which, like italy, take in immigrants responsibly and unilaterally bear the consequences.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the migratory flows caused by instability are the indirect consequence of human rights violations, environmental disasters and the lack of economic and social structures capable of ensuring the well-being of large sections of society. they represent a challenge for the eu, both in terms of development cooperation and in terms of preventing social tensions, which often arise not only between the countries of origin and destination but also between the countries of origin and transit. this challenge requires concrete eu responses, addressing not only the development cooperation dimension but also the foreign policy dimension, by implementing preventive measures at both regional and global levels in the fields of security, regional cooperation, bilateral agreements with countries of origin and transit, the protection of human rights and democratisation, making use of all available foreign policy instruments. i am firmly convinced of the importance for the eu of addressing directly the causes of instability, and of doing so by making better use of the instruments at its disposal, and i can only express my vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − managing migration flows caused by political instability is a key challenge for the eu. wars and armed conflicts, ethnic tensions, systematic violations of human rights, natural disasters and the absence of sound economic and democratic structures are the main causes of these flows. i believe that we must now implement a policy of prevention, by putting in place the most appropriate instruments to deal with the causes of instability. european foreign policy should focus on the sources of instability and structural difficulties in the countries of origin. i believe that this text represents an additional tool for the eu to devise a coherent and effective policy on the phenomenon of migration flows, directing the choices towards the most appropriate way of restoring conditions of political, economic and social stability.
in writing. - i am strongly opposed to this report. the motto 'united in diversity' means that everyone is the master of his own home and it cannot and should not be the eu that forces us to accept unwelcome guests. the fact that we are denied the right to send illegal immigrants back to their country of origin is contrary to common sense. if the law is not respected, millions of desperate refugees will be forced to flee. we must help those who are suffering but in their own homes, preventing human trafficking. i strongly reject the accusation of racism and xenophobia against europe because i am tired of witnessing the strikes of illegal tunisians because they are not given money to buy cigarettes, the refusal to eat tuna-based food because it tastes like fish, the claim to receive, once they land in italy, housing and work, of course free of charge, in the face of the unemployed and the poor who have lived in our country for all their lives. the high representative, baroness ashton, is to be congratulated on her failure to deal with the current crisis in the maghreb. the icing on the cake is that they are persecuted or have few rights, and therefore deserve special attention, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transsexual and transgender people.
in writing. - mr president, i am happy to support mrs jeggle's report, as it focuses on the 42% of women living in rural areas who play an indispensable role in the development of these areas, as well as in their stabilisation and modernisation by developing new forms of entrepreneurship. through their efforts, these women have shown that they can contribute to the evolution of traditional ways of living and producing in the countryside, creating economic activities that can provide employment and that allow family obligations to be reconciled with work. in order to ensure equivalent living conditions in all regions and to avoid the unilateral development of urban centres, it is necessary to equip all rural areas with the most modern it infrastructure, with adequate broadband access, and to develop electronic enterprises such as e-business that allow economic activity to be managed regardless of the distance from urban centres. the training of women and easier access to credit to support female entrepreneurship will also need to be improved. the social protection policies to be undertaken will also have to take account of the living conditions of migrant women employed as seasonal workers on agricultural holdings, with particular reference to the need to ensure adequate housing, medical insurance and health services.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report under discussion today is of particular importance because it focuses on the main points to be worked on in order to ensure that women make an effective contribution to the development of rural areas, while at the same time aiming to promote employment prospects in the context of the new common agricultural policy. i believe that the role of women in agricultural enterprises and rural areas is an important factor in territorial development policies. one of the main objectives of european rural policy is to ensure equal living conditions in all regions so that women and men can also take advantage of opportunities in the countryside. at the present stage of the cap's development, it is crucial to take account of the needs of women living in rural areas and, at the same time, to use their potential. i believe that, in the light of a future vision, more efforts will have to be made to ensure that the sustainable use of rural areas is efficient in terms of both energy and quality. moreover, a stronger commitment will be needed from all actors involved in the process of reforming the agricultural policy.
in writing. - given that the risk of social exclusion in rural areas is higher for women than for men and given the importance of the subject, i support this resolution with enthusiasm and a favourable vote, which, focusing on the role of women in agriculture, calls not only for greater consideration of women's occupational, agricultural and non-agricultural skills in the context of business and regional development strategies, but also for incentives to promote their involvement in the market, eliminating all forms of discrimination and improving their training and access to postgraduate and specialist courses.
in writing. - i congratulate my colleague, rapporteur jeggle, on her work, which has made it possible to publicly appreciate in this house the 'multifunctional' role of women in agriculture. this role is still not adequately recognised, despite the fact that 42% of the 27 million or so workers employed in the sector are women and almost 29% of farms are run by a woman. i voted in favour of this document because i share the need to recognise the specific role that women play in agriculture. i also believe that it is important to identify the specific needs of women in rural areas and to adapt future strategies to them, starting with the next reform of the cap. the european union cannot ignore the professional, family and social aspirations of women living in rural areas. to enable this, however, the european institutions should ensure adequate support services and an innovative offer that is not exclusively market-oriented. finally, i agree with the rapporteur's proposals, particularly on the question of better representation of women in the political, economic and social bodies of the agricultural world.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i strongly supported mrs jeggle's report because i find in it important principles which need to be emphasized and supported in the future. of the total of some 27 million people regularly employed in agriculture in the eu, some 42% are women, and according to official statistics, one in five farms (around 29%) is directly managed by a woman. i invite you to reflect on the great contribution made by women to the development of many local communities, often accompanied by their disproportionate participation in decision-making processes. this is a limit to be overcome by a service policy which, through the new common agricultural policy (cap), can facilitate the processes of development and animation in the rural fabric of many areas. i am thinking in particular of training, counselling and business creation initiatives which, under the second pillar of the cap, could still be strengthened and could be the cornerstone of a significant improvement in the living conditions of women and men in rural areas. i think this is quite strategic, also in view of the achievement of the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy, with particular reference to initiatives focusing on innovation, research and development.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i strongly believe that the central role of women must be restored where their work is essential to the development or recovery of the local economy which contributes to the overall growth of our countries. the role of women in agriculture has changed dramatically in recent decades, becoming increasingly multifunctional. for this reason, action by the european institutions is needed to prevent women leaving the countryside or to encourage them to return to rural life. support for women and their projects would make it possible to make progress in the development of rural communities as a whole. women in agriculture must be given the opportunity to realise their life plans and become economically independent, including in the face of family responsibilities. agricultural jobs must remain attractive to women so that they can fit in to carry out their multiple occupational skills. in this period of financial and economic crisis, it is essential to provide equivalent working conditions in both rural and urban areas, so as to repopulate territories that can be a driving force for the economic recovery of a given european region.
in writing. the new community agricultural policy (cap) also focuses its work on social issues such as the role of women in rural areas. the common objective is to avoid development exclusively in towns and cities and, consequently, to avoid discrimination on grounds of sex and/or geographical origin of citizens living in rural areas. i agree with these proposals and voted in favour of the report which stresses the importance of the role of women in farms and rural areas and how important this role is for territorial development policies. the report indicates the areas to be worked on for the better integration of women, to make the most of their employment potential and to improve their life prospects through greater ecological and energy efficiency in rural areas.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, women are the backbone of the agricultural sector in rural areas. it is therefore important to emphasise the role of the latter on farms and in rural areas. in this respect, their needs must be taken into account and their potential exploited, since aspects such as quality of life and economic power are linked, especially in rural regions, to the presence and involvement of women on several fronts. it is therefore essential that their needs and conditions are reflected more strongly than ever in european support policies, so as to avoid the exodus of women of all generations from the countryside or at least to encourage the return of the latter to rural life. in this respect, eu aid can help to improve the quality of life in rural areas, both for women who run businesses or provide services and for women who consume goods and services. as women play an indispensable role in the sustainable development of rural areas, i am voting in favour of this so as to ensure that women are given practical support in this area.
in writing. − in europe, sustainable rural development has always been considered a priority, in order to ensure optimal living conditions for men and women who decide to undertake this specific activity. at present, 26.7 million people in the european union are employed in agriculture. of these, 42% are women and at least one in five farms is run by a woman. these simple data reveal a radically different reality for rural women than in previous decades, where women have played a leading role in these changes, with very different social and economic situations between the states. i therefore agree with the text of this report, which stresses the need to plan european support strategies for rural areas 'tailored to women' in order to contribute in the medium term to an improvement in their social and working conditions.
in writing. - the report on the role of women in agriculture and rural areas is only to be welcomed because we still believe in the professional farmer who lives on the income from his farm. women, because of their typical nature as mothers and their routine role as carers of other family members, are undoubtedly disadvantaged in the agricultural sector. the time of farming is not fixed but must take account of seasonal requirements, growing seasons and the possible presence of livestock. there are periods when the working days will be 12-13 hours including holidays and others when they are quieter. it is clear that a woman who is a farmer, for example on maternity leave, cannot give up working the land if that period requires it, because otherwise she would not have an income for the whole year. the needs of a female farmer are therefore different from those of another worker, and it is therefore essential that they are provided with appropriate and dedicated services, taking into account the fact that farms are almost always located far from public services, whether transport, care or social services.
in writing. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the catastrophic accident in japan a few weeks ago shows, for those who have not yet understood it, that nuclear energy is no joke: the commission has therefore a duty to check how the programmes for the dismantling of the old power stations in the three former communist countries have been implemented.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr marinescu's report, which focuses on a very topical issue today. in the light of what has happened in japan, questions are now being raised about the safety of existing and operating nuclear power stations in europe. the commitment made by lithuania, bulgaria and slovakia in the eu accession negotiations to dismantle old nuclear reactors for which it was not possible to meet the minimum safety standards required must be a sustained and consistent commitment to which the european union has long established and ensured support and financing programmes. i hope that the dismantling work will proceed swiftly and ensure maximum safety for citizens and the environment. i also hope that the delays which have been partly accumulated will be made up and that the operations will be completed within the deadlines set. finally, i would like to stress, beyond specific cases, the need to provide for verification checks also for other reactors in europe, by making the institutions responsible for the safety management of both existing plants and new ones, should they be built in the future.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the question of the efficiency and effectiveness of eu funding for the decommissioning of nuclear power stations in the new member states is more topical than ever. the recent events in japan have made the need for security more urgent than ever. the report by mr marinescu deals more specifically with the issue of providing adequate financial resources to ensure the decommissioning of nuclear power stations in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria. since their entry into the european family, these states have assumed certain obligations relating to the decommissioning of nuclear installations on their territory. in response to these obligations, the eu has committed to providing adequate financial support. i believe that the european union must propose decisive action on certain issues close to the citizen, such as the safety of nuclear installations.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the text on eu funding for the decommissioning of nuclear power stations in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria because, in view of the recent events following the earthquake and the nuclear crisis in japan, i believe that a policy of nuclear reactor safety control that leaves no margin for risk is fundamental and indispensable for the european union. the countries concerned had old soviet-designed nuclear reactors in operation whose renewal was deemed technically impossible in order to bring them into line with the international safety standards now required. the union funding is consequential to the economic burden borne by countries for the closure of nuclear installations.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the efficiency and effectiveness of eu funding for decommissioning of nuclear power stations in the new member states, tabled on 14 march 2011, aims to assess the results achieved in the field of decommissioning of obsolete nuclear power stations on the basis of the experiences of lithuania, bulgaria and slovakia, which have received eu financial assistance for this purpose since 1999. security of energy supply is one of the key priorities of the eu's energy strategy. according to current forecasts, the delays in the programmes will not prevent the start of decommissioning and waste management activities and the execution of the works by the plant staff by 2013. however, there remains a strong concern that decommissioning plans have not yet been finalised and that efforts are needed to improve the management of financial resources and coordination with the national authorities of the member states concerned. for these reasons, i shall vote in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is of paramount importance to keep the focus on the decommissioning of the nuclear power stations in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria, where, at the time of their accession to the european union, old soviet-designed nuclear reactors were still in operation and could not be upgraded to the latest safety standards at sustainable costs. after the recent disaster in japan, it is no longer possible to delay such procedures for the safety of all european citizens and beyond, and the exceptional financial burden to be borne in this connection can no longer be an excuse for any delays. the european union has therefore committed itself to providing adequate financial assistance for the decommissioning of these reactors until the end of 2013. any further delay cannot be tolerated in the interests of the european community as a whole and must be immediately reported to all appropriate authorities.
in writing. - following the nuclear disaster at the japanese power station, which was also due to the failure to adapt to current safety standards, we can say that we made a good choice when, during the accession negotiations, we set binding closure dates for three old soviet-designed nuclear power stations in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria. the final closure and safekeeping date was set for 2013, with an estimated cost to the european union of almost eur 3 billion. the report calls on the commission, following delays and increased costs in securing the three plants, to monitor more closely and to verify the current situation and the forecasts for the implementation of the different phases of the decommissioning process according to the initial timetable.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the european globalisation adjustment funds are funds set aside by the union to provide economic support to certain sectors in difficulty in the member states or sectors which are expanding towards the average standards of the union, which is why i voted in favour of mrs matera's report. the union budget line for 2011 for the allocation of such funds has been increased by eur 50 million, thus making it easier to grant funds for the most diverse sectors, in particular the first calls for funds for 2011 for the machinery manufacturing sector from the czech republic and poland. the fund (almost €1 million) will support skilled workers in trade and machinery manufacturing.
in writing. - on 15 february, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in the czech republic to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. the application concerns 634 redundancies, all of which were eligible for assistance from the fund, in the unilever company operating in the retail sector in the nuts ii region of střední čechy during the four-month reference period from 16 september 2009 to 16 january 2010. my vote in favour of today's resolution reiterates the favourable opinion already expressed in the committee on employment and social affairs.
in writing. - the control of exports of dual-use goods, i.e. goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes, has been the subject of action at union level for some 15 years. this control has a significant impact on european trade policy, as it can affect more than 10% of all eu exports. in my view, the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and the related clarification of the eu's competences in the field of international trade provide a valuable opportunity to reaffirm the role of the union and the responsibility of the european parliament within the eu institutional framework for decision-making. the main export control instrument is regulation (ec) no 428/2009 which has made a number of significant changes to the scope of controls on exports of dual-use items in the european union. in particular, i believe that the eu dual use regime should be organised in a more transparent way. to this end, i agree with the rapporteur that it would be decisive for the european parliament to be fully involved in implementing the obligations of the lisbon treaty and in adopting a joint interpretation of it by parliament and the commission in the context of the new framework agreement.
in writing. the report by the honourable member deals positively with the important subject of eu export controls on dual-use goods, i.e. goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes. the control of such exports, which account for more than 10% of total eu exports, is of particular importance for the purposes of arms non-proliferation. i am voting in favour of the report because it seeks to introduce more transparent control procedures for these exports.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the new eu powers in the field of international trade now introduced by the lisbon treaty provide a good opportunity to make the dual-use market more transparent. the amendments to this regulation, which covers products for both military and civilian use, will bring about closer control of these products. this is essential for the purposes of non-proliferation. the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection has also been consulted on this matter.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1334/2000 establishing a community regime for the control of exports of dual-use goods and technology, presented on 7 february 2011, aims to provide the union with an effective system of preventive measures to counter the proliferation of weapons, including weapons of mass destruction. the regulation currently in force in this area (ec no 428/2009) sets up a control system that enables the union to fully comply with the commitments under the four international export control regimes of which the eu is a member. however, the clarification of the eu's competences in the area of international trade introduced by the treaty of lisbon provides a good opportunity to increase the prominence and strengthen the union's image in such international contexts and the role, power and responsibility of the european parliament in the eu institutional framework with regard to decision-making in the field of international trade. for these reasons i think it appropriate to make the necessary amendments to the rules of procedure to enable these objectives to be achieved and i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the control of exports of dual-use goods, i.e. goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes, has been the subject of action at european level for some fifteen years. such control is essential to prevent the proliferation of weapons, including weapons of mass destruction. given the high volume of trade across the borders of the european union, the implementation of controls on eu exports of dual-use items should be based on preventive measures such as the imposition of export authorisation requirements and customs registration procedures. the adoption of this resolution is a further step in that direction. i voted in favour of this report because the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon provides a good opportunity to reaffirm europe's role and the european parliament's power and responsibilities in the eu institutional framework in taking such decisions. the system must be reorganised in a more transparent way, by implementing the obligations laid down in the treaty and by adopting a joint interpretation of it by parliament and the commission in the context of the new framework agreement.
in writing. the purpose of the measure proposed by the european commission is to introduce the oecd-negotiated 'agreement on publicly supported export credits' into european legislation to ensure common rules and transparency in the operations of national export credit agencies. this is a good measure in itself, because it combats corruption and the lack of transparency which results in a great deal of time and expense, but it is improved by mr jadot's report, which is aimed at further increasing transparency and fairness in the introduction into community legislation of the agreement negotiated within the oecd.
in writing. - trade with the outside world is one of the most important policy levers we have in relation to third countries. at least until it was decided otherwise, the eu chose not to have its own army and to adopt trade policy as a negotiating tool in international relations, with considerable satisfaction. the foreign direct investment of our companies is also a source of development for the third countries where it creates jobs and it certainly makes sense to stimulate it through export credit agencies. what we can no longer allow in an internal market with a single customs tariff is that these investments can be directed by individual member states. this is not the path the eu has set out on and is trying to propose to the rest of the world. the transfer of all competence in international trade from the level of the states to that of the union is a further step in the construction of a unified industrial policy, with a view to a common economic policy and, in the future, to further synergies between our states.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, export credit agencies (eca) are the world's main source of official financing for private sector projects. however, they can also create a huge distortion of trade if their financing operations are not governed by common rules. therefore, a review of the oecd agreement (agreement on officially supported export credits) is necessary to better monitor the fairness of the financial transactions of european ecas and to ensure their consistency with eu policies and objectives. furthermore, clarity should be provided on the transparency requirements in relation to the calculation of risks and the publication of off-balance sheet instruments. in essence, it is essential to establish an obligation for eu member states to report on an annual basis to the commission on the activities of their aces in the above areas. in the light of the foregoing, and considering that aces can be effective tools to contribute to the union's external objectives (in particular climate change and the fight against poverty), i express my favourable opinion on the adoption of this resolution as i consider export credits to be an important instrument to support trade and investment by european businesses.
in writing. most industrialized countries have an export credit agency. these agencies are, taken together, the world's main source of official funding for private sector projects. the financial support of large industrial and infrastructure projects in developing countries by export credit agencies is considerably higher than the combined annual financing of all multilateral development banks. agencies facilitate legal trade where the private capital market is lacking. since they are not taxed and do not make a profit, they have a much higher risk-absorbing capacity than private players and therefore enjoy a greater margin of manoeuvre than private banks, even on large loans. however, for the same reason, they can create a huge distortion of trade if their financing operations are not governed by common rules. i voted in favour of this report because export credits must be subject to conditions of repayment within a certain period and to the charging of a minimum premium rate to cover the risk of non-repayment of export credits.
in writing. − in europe, one in four women will experience at least some form of violence in her lifetime. the annual cost of violence is around 33 billion euros, a figure that should not be underestimated. respect for the principle of gender equality is a value that is constantly neglected in the face of a wide range of human rights violations affecting women, penalising them in their physical and mental health, their rights and their position within society. the limited data available does not give us a global picture of the phenomenon, but it is enough to look at one's own family or work environment to see how women are still not protected from violence. i appreciate the commission's commitment to present in 2011-2012 the 'communication on a strategy to combat violence against women, domestic violence and female genital mutilation', which will be followed by an eu action plan, but i also hope that a comprehensive political approach will be adopted, including legal, judicial, executive and health actions that can effectively reduce this type of violence and its consequences, unfortunately also for the 26% of children and young people who reported having suffered physical violence in their childhood.
in writing. − gender equality is a fundamental principle of the european union. despite decades of talk about violence against women, the international community has still not succeeded in putting an end to this serious form of crime. gender-based violence causes serious damage to the psychophysical health of the individual, and this results in high costs for society because, as a social problem, it involves legal and health costs. the social costs of gender-based violence, in the form of expenditure on health, justice and social services, are estimated to be €2 million per hour in all eu member states. in my view, a major area where strong legal protection of the psychophysical integrity of women is required is that of genital mutilation. i believe that acts which seriously damage women's health cannot be justified on cultural grounds. it is also essential to increase awareness of the scale of gender-based violence in europe, so that the public is more aware of this issue. i therefore welcome the action to encourage member states to develop national action plans to combat gender-based violence.
in writing. - i expect a report on violence against women today to highlight as an absolute emergency the growing violence against women within muslim communities in europe. the phenomenon is growing, and this is according to the associations in europe dealing with women's rights and gender-based violence. the matter is plain to see, but there seems to be a certain retrogradeness in admitting the problem in the correct terms. the report mentions, for example, forced marriages and female genital mutilation, but these phenomena, which are increasing exponentially in our cities, are treated as problems of a cultural matrix. the truth is that they are linked to the mass presence of immigrants who bring to europe a fundamentalist conception of religion, the islamic one, which today is paid for by the women who belong to those communities, but which tomorrow could affect our women and western society at its heart. it is on this, and not on the meaningless 'cultural' violence, that the eu must put in place adequate and targeted policies to combat a phenomenon which is rapidly expanding today and which will become impossible to manage tomorrow at this rate.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, violence against women is an evil in our society which we must combat at all costs. but i cannot support this resolution because i think that too much attention is being paid to migrant women. this attention, especially at this time, should be really visible from the eu and its governments and should not be limited to nice words of support in european projects.
in writing. − a european regulatory framework to combat violence against women is a necessary step forward in a global strategy. only a combination of legal, social, economic and preventive measures can help to solve a problem that is not so far from our reality, since more than a quarter of women in the european union have suffered violence in their lifetime. violence against women does not discriminate on grounds of age, ethnic origin or culture, and it remains an invisible problem that nevertheless has very high human, social and economic costs. the european union must assert its active role in combating discrimination against women and that is why the svensson report supports the european commission in its efforts to develop a clear and homogeneous regulatory framework in the context of the stockholm programme. i therefore welcome the call for a criminal law instrument to define violence against women as a real crime, through the development of a directive against gender violence, to be combined with the many initiatives of training, prevention and awareness raising to combat all forms of abuse against women.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament has adopted the motion for a resolution on the definition of a new eu policy framework to combat violence against women. i strongly and convincingly supported the resolution because i believe that the european union must respond to this social scourge in a united manner, by providing for joint and effective political action. violence against women, whether physical, psychological or sexual, is an expression of incivility which europe must repudiate, a plague which produces traumas which inexorably affect the social life of women. the statistics we have paint a sad and bleak picture. one in four european women has been a victim of violence at least once in her life. i therefore believe that the identification of uniform legal instruments, the possibility of free legal aid, the creation of reception centres capable of providing psychological and moral support and the activation of a single emergency number throughout europe are the priorities which the eu must pursue with its action.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, violence against women is an international and european problem. gender-based violence includes violations in the form of violence in family relationships, sexual abuse, human trafficking and prostitution, forced marriage, genital mutilation and other forms of violation of personal integrity that particularly affect women and girls. in this connection, a series of political, social and legal measures must be adopted in order to guarantee european women a decent life. in its own-initiative report, the european parliament stresses that this violence can be eliminated by ensuring comprehensive and consistent legal protection of their integrity. it is also necessary to record the extent of this type of crime; to raise awareness of the implications of sexual abuse in the courts; identify this type of violence early, through active and preventive work; ensuring legal certainty of the investigation and trial; establish new reception centres and a victim hotline; support research in this field. on the basis of the foregoing, i am voting in favour of the practical implementation of all the measures necessary to combat this type of violence and the drawing up of effective action plans to combat it.

vice-president of the commission. - i thank mr harkin for also highlighting the work being done by the commission, but also for calling for a greater commitment from the executive. at this stage we are waiting for the policy recommendations of the expert group before we can indicate a complete strategy from the commission. in the medium-term working document the expert group proposed a three-pillar bridge to bridge this innovation gap. each of the pillars represents a condition that must necessarily be met in order to spread kets in the european union. the first concerns technological research. europe must develop more competitive technologies up to the prototype stage which are protected by patents. this requires that the union's research programmes be more focused on technological research. the second is the demonstration of products. we must be able to convert technological achievements into competitive products, and this requires rebalancing the union's research programmes by means of demonstration projects. the third pillar is global industrial competitiveness. europe must maintain its current advanced production capacity or create new ones in order to compete on a world scale with innovative products in terms of price and size. to this end, the framework conditions for investors should be improved to encourage them to invest in the european union. so we must not only attract investment but also do a better job in all the community programmes which can help this important sector, and try to bridge the gap between research and application which is characteristic of many sectors of the european union's productive activity. this transition from research to application is a problem for the whole industrial sector. that is why i am in favour of and have supported the cluster policy - we have about 2000 - which makes it possible to link research and industry, universities, research and industry, universities, research and industry and innovation, to make our industrial system more competitive. mr harkin, this is the state of the art. we shall continue to work and i shall examine all the proposals and suggestions that come from the european parliament with great care and i shall take advantage of all the information that this house will give me.
member of the commission. − when my services started to prepare the reform package for the common fisheries policy, they carried out a thorough impact assessment of a number of possible reform options. one of these options was to continue the current policy beyond 2013. this status quo has been used as a benchmark for comparing the impact of other possible options. this status quo scenario takes into account new long-term management plans, the control regulation and the regulation on illegal, unreported fisheries. the results of the status quo scenario option are clear: if we do not change our policy then, by 2020, sustainability of stocks will in general be out of the question. regarding environmental sustainability, only 6% of the stocks analysed would reach maximum sustainable yield by 2020. this should be compared with our obligation to achieve maximum sustainable yield by 2015. so if we continue under the status quo situation there is no way we will fulfil our obligation to achieve maximum sustainable yield by 2015 with reference to the economic performance of our fishing fleets, under the status quo scenario only some fleets will be economically viable. the catching sector as a whole will have profits close to zero or even worse. finally, the picture for social sustainability is the same. employment in the catching sector would continue to decline at the same pace as is the case now; wages would remain low, which would make the profession of fisherman increasingly unattractive to the younger generation. so the status quo is really not an option for the commission. we need the reform and we are working for it.

integration. in particular they contribute to ensuring that political issues are presented and discussed from the european perspective in time, before the elections to the european parliament, thus avoiding situations where these elections are dominated by purely national issues, which, as we well know, is very often liable to be the case. i therefore welcome the forward-looking tone of the report and look forward to discussing its content tonight and in the future as well. article 12 of regulation (ec) 2004/2003 stipulates that the european parliament shall publish by 15 february 2011 a report on the application of this regulation and the activities funded. the report shall indicate, where appropriate, possible amendments to be made to the funding system. we welcome, as i said, mrs giannakou’s own-initiative report and the accompanying resolution as a positive step, but it must be underlined that information on the actual implementation of the current regulation and the activities funded could be more precise and improved. in this context and in the light of the vote by parliament tomorrow, the commission could be called upon to act through a further revision of regulation (ec) 2004/2003 and the financial regulation, or through new legislation. should parliament come to the conclusion that the relevant existing legislation requires modifications, or that new legislation is required, the commission will seriously examine these conclusions and, if it agrees, will take the necessary initiatives. the commission will also reflect on how regulation (ec) 2004/2003 could be further improved in the longer term in order to support the development of stronger and genuinely transnational political parties and foundations at european level, with a view to developing a truly political european public space. on the specific issue of a legal statute for european political parties, i am aware that this is not the first time that parliament has called for such a statute. this issue is addressed in some detail in a study that was commissioned by the committee on constitutional affairs (afco) and i believe that the study itself clearly demonstrates that a range of complicated constitutional, political and practical issues are at stake with regard to establishing such a statute. the matter therefore requires a very careful and detailed analysis indeed. the same can be said about some of the other issues brought up in the report. for the proposals that would require amendments to the financial regulation, the commission also sees the need for a wider reflection on legislative solutions and the timing of the possible changes. in conclusion, mrs giannakou’s report and the accompanying draft resolution raise issues that are at the heart of european integration and its democratic nature, and which therefore need our full attention. i look forward to the debate on those issues tonight and in the future as well.
