in writing. - i welcome the approval today of the mobilisation of the european solidarity fund for poland, slovakia, the czech republic, hungary, romania and croatia in response to the floods that occurred last year. the european parliament and the council have disagreed on the technical procedure for obtaining the eur 182.4 million needed to compensate the member states for the damage suffered, but europe is once again showing its solidarity with its citizens. i am confident that the surplus from the 2010 budget will be used to cover the 'negative reserve' used to raise the necessary funds. the reserve is a 'book' instrument which must be used in case of emergencies which may arise during the current financial year.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is necessary to mobilise the european union solidarity fund in support of the countries that suffered damage as a result of the floods that occurred in 2010 in a large part of central and eastern europe. countries such as poland, slovakia, hungary, the czech republic, croatia and romania have had to bear enormous costs as a result of the heavy rains during this period, which caused extensive damage to their infrastructure. poland alone, for example, suffered two consecutive floods of its main rivers in may and june 2010, causing severe damage to the agricultural sector, transport networks and cultural heritage sites, totalling almost eur 3 billion in damage. the priority now is to get the regions most affected by the tragic events of last year back on their feet, enabling them to get their production systems back on track without further delay.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership with the union of the comoros is intended to highlight the role to be played by the european parliament in the procedure for the revision of the agreement. europe has always pursued the conclusion of fisheries partnership agreements and partnership relations have been in force with the union of the comoros in this field since 1988. the new protocol aims to define the fishing opportunities to be offered to union vessels, to provide for a sustainable policy and responsible exploitation of fisheries resources, to increase investment in small-scale fisheries and to optimise their activity. the draft council decision ensures that both partners, europe and the union of the comoros, benefit from the re-proposal of the agreement, but since parliament has acquired a specific role in the implementation of the agreements following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, it seems inevitable to identify measures involving parliament at every stage, up to the final approval of the agreement.
in writing. − the conclusion of bilateral fisheries agreements between the european community and third countries has always been a common practice of the common fisheries policy and therefore a central element of its external dimension. agreements with african and pacific countries provide that a substantial share of the eu's financial contribution is earmarked for supporting national fisheries policies based on the principles of sustainability and good management of fisheries resources. bilateral fisheries relations between the european community and the union of the comoros date back to 1988. the resolution adopted today stresses that greater information and control by the european parliament during all stages of the negotiation process would strengthen the partnership elements and have a positive impact on the development of the fisheries sector. the european parliament and the council should be on an equal footing, both as regards the right to be fully and immediately informed and as regards monitoring and evaluating the implementation of international fisheries agreements and negotiating the revision thereof.
in writing. − the liberalisation agreement between the eu and morocco must be a signal for the development, stability and economic recovery of the entire north african region. the union cannot and must not lose the opportunity to play a leading role in a renewed trade policy, capable of helping those countries which have been overwhelmed by political and social crises with dramatic consequences for their national economies and, as a result, for our investments in those territories. with today's vote on the creation of a standard, applicable and effective dispute settlement mechanism, we have therefore an additional guarantee to support european investment in morocco, investment which is fundamental to the economic well-being of the entire region and which covers almost all sectors. today's vote also underlines the union's will to avoid negative economic effects on final consumers on both sides of the mediterranean through protectionist policy choices which continue to take account of particular interests, by postponing the ratification of agreements which are essential to rebalance and balance the economic choices of an area which is beginning to be of interest to our commercial competitors such as china and the countries of the middle east.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the dispute settlement mechanism proposed by mr susta. i agree that the proper application of a standard dispute settlement mechanism could be a further step towards the establishment and proper functioning of the euro-mediterranean free trade agreement. to date, disputes arising from euro-mediterranean agreements have been resolved, where possible, only through diplomatic relations. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's trade policy is not distorted by the excessive use of the euro. in the light of what is happening in some countries in north africa, there is no doubt that the path towards economic and political stability in those territories also passes through the proper functioning of free trade agreements in the mediterranean.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this resolution because i believe it is essential that the european union should provide for an appropriate mechanism for settling disputes arising from the implementation of the euro-mediterranean agreements. in 2006, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with the mediterranean partners and it was not until 2009 that the agreement was signed. the creation of a pre-defined dispute resolution mechanism should finally introduce simplified and effective appeal procedures within precise time limits. i share the rapporteur's view that updating the euromed free trade agreements is essential in order to contribute to economic and political stability in this region and to consolidate a single area of peace and development. the proposed mechanism is modelled on the dispute settlement mechanisms of the most recent partnership agreements concluded by the european union and the wto dispute settlement framework. at a time when foreign direct investment is crucial to the economic well-being of european member states, i hope that an effective and functioning dispute settlement mechanism will also serve to resolve disputes in this area.
in writing. − in 2010, the commission presented to the council a proposal on the rules for importing fishery products into the eu, using article 203 tfeu as the legal basis for its work. i agree with the interpretation that this legislative activity should be regulated on the basis of article 43 in conjunction with article 204, thus allowing amendments to the regulation to be made through the ordinary legislative procedure. in 2007 alone, almost 87% of fishery products exported from greenland were destined for the eu. the commission and the council cannot therefore be the only ones to lay down general rules for trade and imports of fishery products from greenland, because this is contrary to the provisions of the lisbon treaty itself. i therefore believe that the european parliament must make its voice heard in such an important area.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the trade relations between the eu and greenland have been of considerable consistency for many years. in fact, as early as 2007, greenland exported 82% of its fishery products, of which 87% went to the european market. we can therefore say that this represents an important resource for greenland, to be added to what europe provides in terms of financial support in exchange for maintaining its fishing rights in greenland waters. on 26 april 2010, the european parliament requested the legal affairs committee to deliver an opinion on the legal basis on which the greenland agreements could be implemented. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights has recently expressed its support for parliament and confirmed that the legal basis for the agreements is, as claimed, to be found in articles 43 (2) and 204 tfeu.
in writing. − a special agreement is currently in force between the european union and greenland, whereby the european union maintains its fishing rights in greenland's waters, in exchange for financial support. greenland, a former danish colony, achieved full independence in 1985, and continues to be associated with the european union as one of the overseas countries and territories. it is sufficient to consider that in 2007 alone, fishery products exported by greenland accounted for 82% of its total exports, of which approximately 87% was destined for the eu. on 26 april 2010, the committee on fisheries and the legal service of the european parliament expressed serious doubts about the legal basis chosen by the commission for the conclusion of the agreement. i hope that the agreement voted on will result in the extension of the application of the internal european rules on trade in fishery products to those from greenland. at the same time, european standards on animal health and food safety in the fisheries sector must be respected at all times.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for a directive submitted to parliament for its opinion on the possible introduction of a uniform procedure for the 27 member states of the union in the recognition of the right of asylum is an important step forward, but the sensitivity of the subject requires careful and thorough reflection. finally, to ensure that the member states approximate their legislation in accordance with the commitments they have made under the stockholm treaty, by simplifying and speeding up the procedural mechanisms. the commission also intends to provide a high degree of protection for asylum seekers, ensuring a rapid first instance verdict, free legal aid and the possibility of residing in the country until a final judgment is rendered. i am not opposed to this proposal for a directive, although i have good intentions, because it is not very precise in terms of certain technical and procedural aspects and because it is ambiguous in terms of certain definitions. the directive, when worded in this way, would be open to abuse by applicants. for these reasons i have decided not to support this version of the text which i do not think is entirely acceptable.
in writing. - after years of heated debate and following the lisbon treaty, the legal affairs committee has submitted to the european parliament the first draft of a common asylum procedure between member states. the aim is to establish by 2012 a common area of protection and solidarity based on harmonisation between member states on asylum, despite the persistent divergences between national provisions. in fact, such national disparities are incompatible with a common european asylum system and constitute an obstacle to its implementation. in particular, the new legislation provides that asylum seekers should be treated equally throughout europe, regardless of the member state in which the application is lodged. progressive improvement and effective harmonisation of asylum procedures and guarantees should be pursued with a view to establishing a common european system. i hope that in this review context an accessible, fair and effective procedure will be ensured, in the interests of both asylum seekers and the member states' guarantee systems.
in writing. - we have strongly opposed parliament's directive on the single asylum procedure because, if implemented, it would effectively take away the sovereignty of the member states. we believe it is unacceptable to prevent the member states from rejecting people they do not want, and even to guarantee asylum seekers a high level of treatment that is equivalent throughout the european union to that of european families who do not even have the right to a home. asylum seekers are also entitled to free procedural and legal advice, legal assistance and representation. it is specified that ngos may also be active in providing services for access to information on procedures for obtaining protection, and provide guidance and legal advice to asylum seekers, which should also be provided at border crossing points or in reception centres. it should be noted that all these benefits from european taxpayers will not be granted only to refugees but to all asylum seekers and therefore to any illegal or irregular immigrant who applies for them.
in writing. - the simpson report and the regulation to which it refers propose to establish a common framework for the collection and dissemination of european statistics on tourism by means of the collection and compilation by the individual member states of harmonised statistics on tourism demand and supply in the form of aggregated tables which will then be transmitted to the european commission (eurostat) by computer. although the rapporteur's work is commendable, i cannot vote for the report because it does not change the amount of work and data collection required by the regulation. the tables proposed by the rules of procedure are rather complex and the collection of so much information is, in my view, an excessive burden. i cannot therefore support the interference and bureaucratic burden that such a regulation would create.
in writing. - we cannot deny that tourism has changed radically in the last decade, thanks in part to technological progress. the legislation on the collection of data and statistics therefore needs to be updated. in this respect, i agree with the commission's proposal to introduce a new regulation which would repeal certain articles which are now obsolete. at the same time, however, i am in favour of the amendments made to the regulation by parliament, particularly as regards the need to introduce harmonised statistics which also take account of the purely social aspects of tourism and the opposition to the adoption of delegated acts by the commission on essential matters for an indefinite period. i also think it is a serious mistake that the commission has not considered the introduction of satellite accounts of tourism (sta), as this type of data would allow a more complete picture of the impact of tourism on the labour market and the economy. finally, i find the proposal to introduce on a voluntary basis the collection of statistics on the tourist habits of disabled people and the consequent implementation of pilot projects to improve the participation of disabled people in tourism extremely interesting.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think that the proposal for a regulation on european statistics on tourism, which has been put to the vote in this house, is of particular interest and great utility. the tourism industry is a major industry in europe and of great importance in the community, as it plays an important role in the economy of the individual member states. the tourism industry still has significant potential in terms of employment and it is therefore useful to implement measures aimed at promoting better organization, which will allow its full potential to be expressed. the establishment of a common framework for the collection and compilation of comparable and comprehensive european tourism statistics can only help to improve the situation. knowing consumer demand will enable businesses and public bodies to respond to the needs of the sector, improving their capacity and competitiveness. i supported the proposal for a regulation because i am convinced that uniform, transparent, reliable and objective statistics at european level are an effective way of supporting this large sector, which is of considerable importance also for my own country.
in writing. - the simpson report on european statistics on tourism is a text which will replace the directive on tourism which is now 15 years old. the european system has the right to adapt to the times and to reform its own regulations, especially in view of the importance and the continuing evolution of the tourism sector in europe over the last decade, which is why i voted in favour of the report. the new needs in the sector, which require increasingly detailed, up-to-date and comparable data, make updating the basic tourism statistics necessary. access to facilities, disability services and costs for basic necessities are the main data for which an up-to-date database is needed, which can be consulted by users.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, tourism is an important economic activity in the eu. in this context, statistics are useful for monitoring specific tourism policies and are useful in the context of regional policy and sustainable development. within the eu, the system of tourism statistics is governed by directive 95/57/ec. however, following the entry into force of the above-mentioned directive, the tourism industry and tourist demand have changed considerably. the commission has therefore drawn up a new proposal for a regulation which aims to define a policy framework for tourism by making use of the powers introduced by the lisbon treaty. the aim is to update and optimise the regulatory framework for european tourism statistics to take account of the latest trends in this field. in this regard, it is necessary to strengthen the tourism sector through coordinated action at union level and to establish a common framework for the systematic production of statistics by the collection, compilation, processing and transmission by the member states of harmonised european statistics on supply and demand in the sector. on the basis of the foregoing considerations, i shall vote in favour of the adoption of the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because tourism is an important economic activity for the eu, with a high potential in terms of contributing to job creation and growth. tourism plays a key role in the socioeconomic integration of rural areas, which are often peripheral and underdeveloped. in this context, statistics are not only useful for monitoring specific tourism policies, but also in the broader context of regional policy and sustainable development. the document also addresses the main challenges facing the sector, such as increased global competition, demographic trends, climate change and environmental constraints, the seasonal distribution of tourist movements and the increasing use of new information and communication technologies by customers.
in writing. - i voted against the report because the regulation proposed by the commission would require monthly data collection to measure the seasonal influences and the economic and social aspects of the sector, which is run mainly by small and mediumsized enterprises. this strategy is aimed at a thorough knowledge of the dynamics, characteristics and volume of tourism, but it seems to us to be too demanding, bureaucratic and costly. the commission also requests delegated powers and therefore the possibility of amending essential elements of the proposal. the monthly tables proposed by this regulation are complex and require the collection of an excessive amount of information.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report amending regulation (ec) no 861/2006. in may 2006, the council approved this important instrument for financing fisheries. however, a review of that regulation is now necessary in order to ensure consistency between all elements of the legislative framework. keeping up with the times also means using new technologies that can provide a better service with less expenditure of economic resources. in order to better respond to real needs, it was therefore considered appropriate to clarify certain articles of the regulation and to specify the scope of certain measures financed. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that fisheries management must be based on up-to-date and rigorous scientific knowledge of the state of resources and that greater controls must be introduced to make fishing more sustainable.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal to amend council regulation (ec) no 861/2006 establishing a financial instrument for the implementation of the common fisheries policy and in the field of the law of the sea is an important financial instrument which protects fishing activities. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that the current version of the regulation needs to be amended to bring the rules contained in it into line with the treaty of lisbon. the revision has made it possible to improve the text, so that it can respond more adequately and effectively to the needs of the sector. the increasing importance of aquaculture justifies the introduction of provisions on the collection, management and use of environmental, socioeconomic and health data to contribute to its sustainability. the individual states also have a key role to play in ensuring compliance with the rules and monitoring of water by using new technologies in the light of scientific developments.
in writing. the union's financial action for the implementation of the common fisheries policy and the law of the sea offers the economic possibility for the implementation of the common fisheries policy through targeted funding for those areas which need development and coordination in the field of the law of the sea, which is why i voted in favour of mr ferreira's report. the amendment of the regulation will help to make the common policy effective and will mobilise funds for fisheries in relation to data collection, international relations, technical and scientific fields.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 861/2006, establishing a community financial action for the implementation of the common fisheries policy and in the field of the law of the sea, is an important eu funding instrument for fisheries activities. the document is also one of the two main instruments used to put the common fisheries policy into practice. it provides for financing in the following areas: the commission shall be assisted by the european parliament and the council. the resolution adopted today recognises the importance of fisheries management based on up-to-date and rigorous scientific knowledge of the state of the stocks. the document recognises the growing importance of aquaculture, which generates sound prospects for the development of this and related activities, and which justifies the introduction of the possibility of applying to this sector also the provisions on the collection, management and use of environmental data, as well as socioeconomic data, thus allowing environmental and health control and monitoring of the sector which will contribute to its sustainability.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr ferreira's report on improving the management of financial instruments for fisheries, which regulate the financing of a whole range of activities, including those typically concerned with monitoring fishing activities. i therefore believe that the general agreement between the council and the european parliament on the text represents a good compromise on the common fisheries policy and the law of the sea.
in writing. − the failure to agree on the draft legislation to simplify and clarify community rules on the conservation of fishery resources in 2008 led to the adoption of a regulation establishing a set of transitional measures initially planned for the period from 1 january 2010 to 30 june 2011. the legislative proposal voted today aims to extend the transitional arrangements for a further 18 months, i.e. until 1 january 2013, with the aim of defining a new set of technical measures in the context of the ongoing reform of the common fisheries policy, on which the commission will present a proposal in the course of 2011. the european parliament also adopted resolution a6-0206/2009 on the proposal for a council regulation on the conservation of fishery resources through technical measures in the atlantic ocean and the north sea, which stresses the importance of an appropriate division of competences between the council, parliament and the commission. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the community's financial interests against fraud and other irregularities is a very important one.
in writing. the report adopted today aims to promote sound management of resources with a view to reducing public expenditure. in the context of the well-known difficulties facing the public finances of the member states, it is necessary to reduce costs by keeping their increase below the current rate of inflation. the reduction in the overall amount should therefore be welcomed. the additional resources needed to meet the needs of the lisbon treaty and future enlargement should be identified through the budgetary adjustment instruments at a later stage.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr fernandes' own-initiative report on the forecast of revenue and expenditure for 2012. i fully agree with the objectives set out in the text adopted, namely strict management of human resources before new recruitment, greater security within the european parliament, a digital strategy for social networks and the implementation of a wi-fi service, and a building strategy to manage expenditure on parliament's buildings more prudently.
in writing. - mr president, i support the motion for a resolution on health claims on foodstuffs for children. the health of the youngest needs to be better protected from all those sometimes misleading food claims which are put on products and which lead people to buy them simply because they claim to have a beneficial nutritional or physiological effect. it is necessary to ensure that the consumer is assured of the veracity of the claims and that the products placed on the market are safe and adequately labelled, in order to give consumers the information they need to make informed choices and to create a level playing field in the food industry. currently, in some member states, there is a wide range of claims used in food labelling and advertising which refer to substances for which the beneficial effect has not yet been demonstrated or for which there is insufficient scientific consensus at national level. therefore, it is necessary to ensure that substances for which a claim of benefit is provided are subject to scientific testing and studies by the european food safety authority (efsa).
in writing. - unfortunately, we have missed an important opportunity today to reiterate that breastfeeding should not be discouraged in any way, let alone with a nutritional profile that should give certain information. there is no consensus scientific evidence to support any benefits for the development of vision from the addition of dha to infant formulae. i supported the resolution as it was perfectly in line with the spirit of the international code on the marketing of milk substitutes drawn up by the world health organisation. the purpose of the code is, inter alia, to ensure that there is no advertising or other form of promotion to the public of breast milk substitutes. breast-feeding is recognized as having positive effects on the health of both the child and the mother by reducing the risk of breast cancer. moreover, recent research reported by unicef, as well as by the italian society of prenatal medicine, points out that newborn deaths could be reduced by 22 percent if babies were breast-fed. i would have preferred to see all the energy put into promoting artificial milk in support of mothers who would gladly breast-feed their children if they received the necessary support.
in writing. - public health and food safety seem to me to be the solid cornerstones on which human society develops. when these requirements are met and guaranteed, health risks are reduced and population growth is controlled to a safe level. these were the criteria that allowed the union to benefit from the regulation of 20 december 2006 on nutrition and health claims made on foods. it is the principles laid down in that regulation which still guarantee a close link between scientific data evaluated and tested and authorizations for the use of certain foodstuffs. the commission's draft regulation we are discussing today does not, however, offer all the guarantees required, and the normal precautionary principle, in the absence of the necessary scientific requirements and to avoid misleading nutrition and health claims, leads us to refuse to adopt it. the dha acid contained in breast milk fulfils the function that science has demonstrated, whereas the synthetic dha acid is not compatible with the objective and content of that regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 at present. health is not to be trifled with, and children's health even less so. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's view.
in writing. - mr president, i voted against the resolution on the refusal to indicate the presence of dha in infant formula because i think it is right to point out the reasons why dha is added. i would like to remind you that dha is an omega-3 fatty acid found in breast milk and that it has positive effects on improving the visual abilities of the baby. i would remind you that the european food safety authority (efsa) has given a favourable opinion on the need to give a broad indication of the presence of this substance. i didn't appreciate the many emails we received, which made it seem like we wanted to favor breastfeeding over breastfeeding. adequate information on substances added to food is always necessary, especially if intended for children.
in writing. − docosahexaenoic acid, known as dha, is a component of breast milk and numerous scientific studies show that it plays a positive role in the development of the visual system of newborns. i believe that a specific indication on products enriched with this ingredient, such as artificial milk, will enable the consumer to make a more informed choice when buying. i therefore do not believe that the fears of those who claim that such a claim would encourage mothers to give up breastfeeding and to prefer this type of product are well founded. breast milk contains essential and irreplaceable substances and active ingredients for newborns, but unfortunately not all women have access to them. i therefore voted against this resolution because to prevent correct information is to deprive mothers of an additional tool which, since they cannot breastfeed their children directly, they are forced to resort to the use of these products.
in writing. − according to the treaty on the functioning of the european union, foreign direct investment is an area of the union's exclusive competence. this is a challenge that must be met at all costs, especially in terms of defining a european investment policy that meets the needs of investors and beneficiary states and is able, at the same time, to respect the objectives of the eu's external action. the eu's many investment agreements, whether bilateral or multilateral, must ensure investor protection in all appropriate venues. future eu policy will need to promote sustainable and environmentally friendly investments that promote good working conditions in enterprises affected by foreign investment. each investment agreement will have to be accompanied by a set of appropriate social and environmental standards as a form of additional guarantee.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, article 325 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union imposes on the european commission and the member states the obligation to protect the eu's financial interests and to combat fraud in areas where the responsibility is shared between the union and the member states. i believe that, in general, the european commission's report on 'protection of the european union's financial interests fight against fraud annual report 2009' does not provide information on the estimated level of fraud and irregularities in individual member states, but rather focuses on the level of reporting. the results, in my view, cannot be regarded as empirical evidence of the level of fraud and irregularity, precisely because it is not possible to have a global picture of the actual situation of fraud and irregularity in the member states. i therefore share the rapporteur's view that the most appropriate approach is to base the conclusions on the situation of the protection of the eu's financial interests and the fight against fraud on the annual report of the court of auditors on the implementation of the budget, which is the most reliable source of information, whereas the commission's report and olaf's report mainly provide information on specific cases.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate my colleague on his work. the work reveals, also through an olaf overview, fraud irregularities within the european union. the commission's work is not exhaustive, however, in that it does not report the fraud data of individual member states, as the honourable member has pointed out. that is why i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report on the fight against fraud in the community is going in the right direction, emphasizing the need for greater clarity on this subject and stressing the absolute need to remain vigilant. italy is unfortunately among the countries most affected. the vast majority of these incidents occur in the regions of southern italy and concern the misappropriation or misuse of funds intended for the development of these areas. the purpose of these community funds is to promote the growth and development of the most disadvantaged areas. if, however, these fraudulent incidents occur precisely where investment is most needed, then one can well understand how the damage is twofold. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used effectively. the report under consideration emphasizes these aspects and that is why i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on the protection of the european union's financial interests and the fight against fraud because it is an issue of interest to all the member states, on which all must confront each other in order to coordinate in the best possible way against speculation or misuse of national and/or community resources. the text lists a number of statistics on fraud, irregularities and various inconsistencies found in the member states and in the european institutions themselves. the data serve as a warning to those who protect the financial interests of the union and seek to provide reliable and detailed information to exhaustively show the international situation on irregularities and fraud in order to protect the public interest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because there is too often a lack of reliable information on irregularities and fraud in eu spending in the member states. in addition, there is too often no real control over the collection of customs duties and the recovery of funds wrongly spent. it is important now to take concrete measures to distinguish clearly between irregularity and fraud, as fraud is a criminal offence, whereas irregularity is the failure to comply with a rule and can even be unintentional. it is necessary to have a breakdown of these for each individual member state so that disciplinary action can be taken against individual countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr ivan on the protection of the european union's financial interests and the fight against fraud in areas where the responsibility is shared between the union and the member states. i believe that, especially in the light of recent events, it is important to draw attention to this problem and to ensure that there is a constant effort to ensure that anti-fraud activities are homogeneous and uniform throughout the eu.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 'political parties at european level help to form a european political consciousness and to express the will of the citizens of the union'. in these words, article 10 (4) of the treaty on european union defines the role of political parties at european level. despite the role assigned to it by the lisbon treaty, they do not always interpret it in the best possible way. i believe that european political parties can and must make a more significant contribution to the political and social life of europe by arousing public interest in the internal affairs of the union. in the light of these considerations, it is essential that political parties at european level be granted a single and uniform legal, political and fiscal status which also allows for genuine organisational convergence. i believe that the statute on political parties at european level can open the way not only to the involvement of the population but also to the creation of a genuine transnational party system, which is essential to guarantee greater democracy in europe.
in writing. − the democratic system on which the european union is based places the citizen at the centre as the reference point around which all decisions revolve. the citizens are represented by the political parties, which, in order to guarantee the will of their voters, must have common rules on transparency and uniformity, which is why i voted in favour of the application of the regulation on the statute and funding of political parties at european level. a community regulation of this scale provides a means of obtaining in-depth information on european political parties, protects against internal economic corruption and stimulates the interest of citizens by facilitating their participation in the political life of the european union.
in writing. − the development of a reform package for political parties at european level as a tool to mobilise the democratic energies of individuals and citizens' organisations is not a simple task. the creation of a secure and transparent environment for the functioning and financing of political parties at european level is, however, a profoundly democratic act. it is necessary to support the creation of a european space for the action of political parties that puts citizens at the centre of the european union and helps them in their daily lives. the adoption of specific standards makes it possible to achieve this objective and brings a double benefit. on the one hand, it provides timely, rapid and public information on the formation of political parties at european level and on their common european status. in this way, citizens know that participation in a political party at european level means being covered by european union law and that political parties have not only rights but also duties. on the other hand, the european statute of political parties at european level paves the way for the creation of a transnational party system. the adoption of this resolution is a first and indispensable step towards greater participation by citizens in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. governance and partnership are two essential aspects of reviving the single market. in particular, the role of the european parliament in the development of single market legislation can be further strengthened. the lisbon treaty has already made a major contribution to this, but it is not enough. i am thinking in particular of those cases in which parliament expresses a strong and clear position, but which diverges from that of the council and the governments of the member states. i am thinking, for example, of the longstanding question of the indication of the origin of products, the so-called 'made in', particularly in the textile regulation which i am personally following. the fact that parliament has the power to block the adoption of an act if it does not agree with the council is sometimes not enough. they must change the mindset and attitude of all the actors involved. we must all work together to make europe more democratic.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report i have supported contains many of the principles which i personally regard as fundamental to the european union. i am referring in general terms to the kind of dialogue that will necessarily have to be established as soon as possible between citizens and the institutions at various levels. this aspect has particular and varied connotations in relation to the lives of all of us european citizens, but it is much more important when we consider the creation of a single market aimed at revitalizing the entire european economy and improving communication between the legislative bodies and the direct beneficiaries. i believe that this is a priority on the road to common growth. we must move in this direction by looking at new forms of governance, by monitoring various types of procedures, but at the same time simplifying the citizen's approach to public administration.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, if you will allow me, i will start with some figures because they were referred to by several speakers in their statements. i will use the comext data for this. eu imports of tomatoes from morocco grew from 185 000 tonnes in the 1999-2000 season to 295 000 tonnes in 2009-2010, following the normal trend of fresh fruit and vegetable imports from all over the world. at the same time, total additional eu imports of tomatoes increased from 242 000 tonnes to 493 000 tonnes. i have to underline that morocco’s share of total eu imports actually decreased from 76% to 59%. eu tomato production varies between 16 and 18 million tonnes per year, of which 6.5 to 7.5 million tonnes are destined for the fresh market. i think that it is very good to bear these figures in mind so that we can keep this discussion and the size of the problem in proportion. regarding the new agreement with morocco, we in the commission believe that it is modest and balanced. if it is adopted the commission will of course ensure that all its conditions and rules are fully respected. additional quantities under the tariff rate quota will be kept below the traditional average of supplies to the eu. the current average annual level is 300 000 tonnes. with an additional 52 000 tonnes there will be 285 000 tonnes within the tariff rate quota, so there will still be scope for 15 000 tonnes of imports under the usual erga omnes regime. turning to another problem raised, namely the claim that we failed to act, i really cannot accept that because we did not chairman of the agri committee. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to make a brief comment just to underline the importance of the wojciechowski report on bluetongue for an institutional issue which concerns us all. there is no conflict between the commission, parliament and the council as regards the content. the question of the inclusion of correlation tables in the text remains very sensitive. despite the council's strong opposition, the committee on agriculture voted in favour of a text which includes the tables of correspondence obliging the member states to report on the implementation of the directive. the council will now have to choose between accepting the correspondence tables and concluding the agreement at first reading, or accepting the responsibility before the european farmers to cancel the vaccination campaign against bluetongue this year in order not to give in on this point. i believe that this dossier can serve as an example for future negotiations with the council and we must be united and decisive in demanding the utmost transparency from the member states and in advocating full compliance with community legislation.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this is an important measure for the whole of the agricultural and pastoral world. but this measure must be followed swiftly by a commitment from the council, and therefore from the national governments, to adopt it immediately, before the end of the season, in such a way as to solve this problem which concerns not only the southern part of europe but also - and today's vote is a testimony to this - the whole of europe. the bluetongue disease affects the sheep and cattle herds on our farms. so, moving towards total eradication is a health policy objective to which national governments can contribute more by being more resilient. it is also a matter of adopting it immediately by transposing the directive.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr janusz wojciechowski, which, through a series of interesting amendments to the commission's text, aims to bring an outdated and outdated legislation up to date and flexible, helping the member states to increase the efficiency of the use of vaccination against bluetongue by reducing its incidence in the agricultural sector.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, bluetongue is a disease affecting ruminants and has already caused a number of losses of animals affected by the disease since the early 2000s. europe has intervened with directive (ec) no 75/2000 to tackle the problem by regulating the use of so-called 'live modified' or 'attenuated' vaccines in order to effectively combat the consequences of the phenomenon. however, the vaccines used so far, the use of which was provided for in that directive, posed a risk of the virus being transmitted to unvaccinated animals, which is why it was provided that the vaccine could only be administered in well-defined areas. the newly available vaccines, so-called 'inactive vaccines', do not present such hazards as those on the market at the time of the introduction of directive (ec) no 75/2000. i voted in favour of this report because the new rules will enable the member states to control the phenomenon, reducing the burden of this disease on many european farmers. i hope that this will help to ensure that the emergency measures are adopted in due time, starting in the coming months.
in writing. − to ensure better control of bluetongue and reduce its burden on the agricultural sector, it is necessary to update the current rules on vaccination. the report voted today aims to make the current legislation more flexible, given that inactive vaccines are now available, which can be successfully used outside areas where restrictions have been imposed on the movement of livestock. the proposal is in line with the new eu animal health strategy (2007-2013) 'prevention is better than cure', as it provides both for a more flexible approach to vaccination and for an improvement of the measures currently in place to fight major animal diseases.
in writing. - madam president, the fukushima nuclear disaster has had a number of repercussions on european political life. the first lesson the eu learned from the japanese disaster was to act quickly to intensify safety checks at nuclear plants through stress tests. every nuclear plant, whether in europe or outside its borders, can be a potential weapon of destruction, and i believe that none of us wants to relive the chernobyl disaster of 26 april 1986. the second lesson is that science and technology can make giant strides in all areas, but always keeping in mind one great limitation, namely nature and its unpredictability. it is precisely because of events beyond human control that we should diversify our energy supply, including by making use of the renewable resources at our disposal. but if nuclear power is chosen as a source of energy support, it would be important first of all to inform the citizens about the costs, benefits and consequences of such a choice, without forgetting that this technological choice must necessarily be legitimized by the popular will which must be heard and respected.
in writing. − i voted against this report because of its several flaws, starting with its approach to the nuclear issue. after the japanese tragedy it is no longer possible to deal with the nuclear argument solely in terms of safety. the title of the report is ‘on the lessons to be drawn for nuclear safety in europe following the nuclear accident in japan’, but there is no special lesson to be drawn except that confirming the practical impossibility of controlling both the risks and consequences of a major nuclear accident. a resolution on this subject cannot be centred around the issue of nuclear safety without addressing the most important nuclear safeguard, which is an exit strategy from nuclear energy itself.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on nuclear safety because after the recent events in japan we cannot fail to approach the problem with responsibility and objective criteria. i think it is important that europe should review the safety regulations for nuclear power stations to ensure absolute safety levels that can be identified by stress tests that will show any risks and limits of the use of nuclear energy. the resolution itself is intended to show how, despite everything, we can always learn from disasters and react in a clear and effective way to make sure that they do not happen again. it also stresses the need to focus on alternative energy sources such as renewable energy, although nuclear remains indispensable as a low-carbon energy source.
in writing. the very serious nuclear accident at the fukushima daiichi nuclear power station on 11 march caused the death of thousands of people and unimaginable material damage to the entire economy of the rising sun. this catastrophe is causing all the countries of the world to reconsider their positions on the use of nuclear energy technologies. unfortunately, in many cases these decisions are being accelerated in the wake of the recent tragic events and there are calls from many quarters for the total and immediate dismantling of nuclear installations. the eu as a whole has been reviewing its approach to nuclear safety for some time now, but it must take into account that this technology will continue to be part of the energy mix of several member states for many years to come. in the future it may be possible to meet our energy needs from renewable sources, but this is not yet possible and will not be for a long time. i am in favour of stricter safety standards for nuclear power stations, as is already the case for the next generation. however, i consider the option of stopping nuclear power production overnight to be a short-sighted and unnecessary choice, driven more by sentiment than by real motives, capable of bringing the economies of the world's major industrialized countries to their knees.
in writing. - after the nuclear disaster in japan, we must review the european energy plan. particular attention should be paid to both existing and planned nuclear power stations. the european union has already planned to carry out stress tests on all plants, including those in neighbouring countries but which have current relations with the union. this resolution also provides for a moratorium on the construction of new plants to allow for appropriate risk assessments. we must be aware that in any case many countries will continue to be dependent on nuclear energy in the coming decades, but at the same time we cannot allow that there should be plants in europe which put the population at risk. the plants before 1980 must be dismantled. in some countries, such as italy, there are assessments under way on whether or not to abandon nuclear energy, and it is essential that shared choices at european level also be implemented. the fact is that the european parliament has not been able to express itself on an important subject which is of interest to the citizens, such as the one under discussion today. in fact, all the resolutions were rejected, including the joint resolution on which we voted in favour.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i think that we all agree and are in agreement that this programme of harmonising frequencies and coordinating the use of spectrum can serve two purposes. i think this is a point which must always be borne in mind, namely to develop the great economic potential of this sector for telecommunications, audiovisual and new services, while giving an impetus to economic development and other sectors linked to telecommunications, and developing the potential for cultural and social development which this dual function affirms and requires. i believe that this programme must also be an opportunity for our choices to respect and affirm certain fundamental principles. the first: the issue of media pluralism. the revision of the system for managing radio and television frequencies at european level is very important and, in my view, it is clearly necessary to avoid the accumulation of rights relating to frequencies and the formation of monopolies or oligopolies which unfortunately exist in some european countries and are being stabilized and strengthened in the field of radio and television. the second: the principle of a balance between liberalisation and opening up the market to new entrants and, at the same time, an equity that also allows the market to promote, support and maintain the commitments made to those operators who have made significant investments. finally, transparency and the guarantee of good governance and good administration in the allocation of frequencies. we are talking about auctions not only to give priority to a market aspect which must be balanced with all the social use of spectrum, but also to say that there must be no discretion and no allocation of improper advantages in radio frequencies. this too is a point that deserves great attention. finally, i regret that i do not have time to dwell on the social aspects, which have, however, been widely discussed by all the members of my group.

madam president, the treaty of lisbon lists foreign direct investment among the issues relating to the common commercial policy and, on the basis of article 3 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the union has exclusive competence in this area. following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, member states have maintained in force a number of agreements with third countries on foreign direct investment. if we want to avoid these agreements interfering with the rules laid down in the treaty, we cannot but adopt the rules and measures contained in mr schlyter's report. the adoption of measures replacing existing agreements is the only way to ensure a high level of protection for investors and to ensure that their rights are recognised and guaranteed through the legal certainty of such agreements. the project is certainly going in that direction and that is why i voted in favour.
madam president, i voted in favour of this report because i am absolutely convinced of the need to control european investment abroad at a time of great economic crisis and uncertainty. with the entry into force of the new treaty, competence for investment protection is transferred from the member states to the union. i hope, however, that the commission will present a report in september setting out the strategic lines in this area. the transition phase needs to be regulated and it is essential that, through an authorisation process, bilateral investment agreements concluded by member states are maintained and that member states are allowed, under certain conditions, to renegotiate existing agreements or to complete those in the process of adoption and to enter into negotiations for the conclusion of further agreements. however, legal certainty will remain relative as long as the transition of the investment protection regime is not completed and deadlines for bilateral investment agreements already concluded by member states are not set. a transitional period is therefore necessary to manage this transition and, in order to avoid legal loopholes, this regulation leaves the management of the treaties to the member states. in view of the above, i would like to reiterate my hope that the commission will shortly define the appropriate strategic lines.

in writing. − i am in favour of the european union's accession to the agreement on the protection and sustainable development of the prespa park area, signed by greece, macedonia and albania, as this park is a natural area of international interest for its geomorphology, ecology, biodiversity and cultural importance. i also share the objectives and principles of the agreement, which are based on the sustainable use of natural resources, attention to the conservation of ecosystems and biodiversity, and the prevention, monitoring and reduction of pollution of the waters of the prespa lakes.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the prespa river basin, which straddles the borders between greece, macedonia and albania, is an important natural site. the agreement the eu will sign will help achieve important objectives for the protection of this area, by protecting the ecosystem and introducing the sustainable use of renewable energy. that is why i shall be voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the european union has well-established legislation on water protection, the most important of which is the water framework directive. under this legislation, where river basins extend beyond european territory, member states are to seek to establish coordination with the third countries concerned which share the river basin district. where coordination takes the form of an international agreement, the participation of the european union as a party is necessary in so far as the agreement concerns matters falling within the union's competence. prespa park is a natural area of international interest because of its geomorphology, ecology, biodiversity and cultural importance. the document adopted today aims to establish cooperation to ensure the integrated protection of the ecosystem and the sustainable development of the prespa park area, including the preparation of integrated basin management projects based on international and eu standards. the agreement will contribute to the proper implementation of the water framework directive, to environmental protection, to improving the living standards of the inhabitants of the area and to strengthening good neighbourly relations in a particularly sensitive area of the balkans.
in writing. - i supported the report because the european union must send a strong signal against illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing. the european union is an important international player in fisheries management issues and as such must support all that concerns compliance with international infringement rules. mrs fraga welcomed the european commission's efforts to adopt resolutions on the basis of the fao recommendations on the agreement on port state control measures. we in the committee have strongly supported the idea of continuing to push for these proposals. illegal fishing is defined as fishing by a registered vessel for undersized species, but also by unauthorised vessels fishing in protected areas or too close to the coast. unfortunately, it also represents 60% of the products that reach our markets and this leads to uncertainties about the quality of the products that reach our markets with difficulties in tracing them. we therefore believe that europe should be an example for all the other countries involved in this sector, which often, by not having to respect certain limits imposed on our fishermen, end up gaining an advantage on the international markets.
in writing. - the lack of available fish resources on a global scale, not just in our seas, is a problem that is becoming more and more pressing. we know that marine life is not only a major source of human food, but also a key factor in the health of the entire ecosystem. it is therefore important that all levels of government, from the regions to the central government, and even the european union itself, use all the means at their disposal to promote regulatory measures and legislative instruments that are geared to the protection of fish stocks, the only guarantee for the long-term sustainability of fishing activities. i voted in favour of this recommendation from parliament to the council to approve on behalf of the european union the agreement on measures of national competence for the prevention and elimination of illegal fishing. this international agreement, if properly implemented by national actors, will be an important tool for the long-term protection of marine fauna and the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text presented by mrs estévez, to whom i extend my thanks for the work she has done. i believe that the european union must have all the instruments at its disposal to prevent and combat illegal trade while preserving the fish market, which has always been a solid pillar of the common fisheries policy. it is therefore time to adopt and above all to respect strict rules, to ban the entry of vessels which do not comply with european and international fisheries rules and to ensure that more information is provided on all vessels requesting to enter ports. we must not forget that europe, the third largest fishing power in the world, has been fighting for years to ensure that member states and third countries comply with the rules, in order to guarantee a sustainable fisheries market and to protect the fisheries environment from possible damage.
in writing. − illegal fishing is one of the most serious threats to the sustainable exploitation of living aquatic resources worldwide. the fight against this form of exploitation is an essential component of the common fisheries policy; the eu must be able to promote international cooperation in this area by participating actively and constructively in the adoption of an international instrument on port state measures. in 2001, fao developed an international action plan to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. this action plan, following a holistic approach, provides for a series of actions to be undertaken by flag, coastal and port states. the document adopted today aims to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal fishing by applying effective measures under the responsibility of the port state, thus ensuring the long-term conservation and sustainable exploitation of marine biological resources and marine ecosystems.
in writing. - mr president, the internal market is without doubt the most important instrument available to the european union to promote growth in the wake of the recent financial crisis. the millions of citizens and businesses who benefit from the internal market must be able to exercise their rights and to travel, work and live freely throughout europe. for this reason they must also have effective remedies if they intend to take action against another citizen or undertaking which jeopardises these rights. to date, there are a number of instruments in the european union which allow for the recovery of cross-border claims and the mutual recognition of judgments of national courts; however, an effective right to enforcement of judgments is still lacking. the establishment of an effective regime for the freezing and transparency of the debtor's assets, together with increased cooperation between enforcement authorities in different member states, are the appropriate tools to address these shortcomings. that is why i voted in favour of mrs mccarthy's report.
in writing. − a key component of effective enforcement of judgments is the possibility for judges, as a transitional measure, to act swiftly to freeze and make the assets of debtors transparent. in the absence of such measures, unscrupulous traders and other debtors may escape their liability simply by transferring their assets to another jurisdiction, thereby depriving the creditor of the effective enforcement of the judgment within the single market. this is why it is necessary to create a genuine 28th system, i.e. an autonomous european remedy additional to those available in national courts. this preventive measure will also act as a further deterrent to late payment and will have the effect of making assets transparent in cross-border litigation.
in writing. − millions of businesses operate within the european market and millions of citizens exercise their right to live, work and travel in all member states. it is therefore essential that in the internal market citizens who wish to take action against an undertaking or against another citizen should have the necessary and effective means of redress. within the european union, there are rules allowing for crossborder debt recovery and mutual recognition of judgments of national courts, but often obtaining a judgment is only part of the process. the over 500 million european citizens and businesses must have the right to effective enforcement of judgments. a key component of effective enforcement is the possibility for courts, as a transitional measure, to act immediately to freeze and make the assets of debtors transparent. the report we are adopting today is intended to invite the commission to submit rapidly proposals on interim measures for the freezing and transparency of debtor assets in crossborder litigation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of authorising the 2009 discharge for the european commission section, because, despite the difficulty of managing these funds, the result obtained by the court of auditors shows objective improvements. the increased transparency in the audit and the improved performance of all those involved in the management of european funds are the two main reasons which motivate me to support this discharge.

the rapporteur. - madam president, mr minister, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i shall make a single statement on both questions, which concern the same subject. this debate, and the vote that will follow, marks the end of the work and negotiation period of the working party chaired by mr wallis and composed of colleagues from all the political groups with the european commission delegation, led by mr šefčovič, which resulted in the drafting of a text of agreement for the establishment of a common transparency register. the afco committee drew up this report in a few months, and also rejected a text of amendments to internal regulations. i was personally very surprised by the attention paid by the public to this transparency agreement. i fear that the effects attributed to it are greater than those actually pursued. transparency is the advanced defense of the correctness of political action but it is not the tool that strikes at the heart of corruption. recent incidents of journalists attempting to bribe some mps may also occur in venues other than parliament buildings. on the other hand, those who want to bribe know how to hide their identity, and the records are not an absolute limit. the appropriate instrument is criminal law, and if the member states' criminal law is not sufficient, then we will have to go back to reading articles 82 to 86 of the treaty of lisbon, consider whether it is possible to attribute to the corruption of european parliamentarians the character of a transnational crime or in any case offensive to the financial interests of the union, and consider whether it is appropriate to build a european public prosecutor's office, which would also be an important step on the road to unity. the transparency register has a more modest task. in some countries the term lobbyist has a negative connotation, while in others lobbying is considered almost a semi-public activity because it informs decision-makers about problems they might otherwise not know about. this is particularly important for the european parliament, because the issues which parliamentarians deal with are often very complex and technical, and a balance must almost always be struck between companies and between states with divergent interests. so lobbyists become very useful. we shall no longer call them lobbyists but interest groups. of course, interests can be conflicting and it is good that they are. i have been a judge and i can say that the contradiction between opposing parties is considered a condition for discovering truth and justice. so, whether there are lobbyists or stakeholders with opposing interests is not bad: the important thing is that the judge - and therefore the parliamentarian - retain his freedom of thought, his independence, his honest pursuit of the common good. the transparency register was set up by common agreement between parliament and the commission, and it is hoped that the council will soon join the agreement. the representatives of the interests may freely enter the offices, but must be entered in the register, which contains all the information necessary to identify their legal and financial structure. the register is public. there are also bodies which do not pursue selfish interests but seek to collaborate in european policies in the name of general values, such as churches, parties, regions. the following shall not be entered as such in the register: however, if there are independent offices which are solely responsible for contact with the european institutions, they must be entered in the register, even if they are subject to a different legal regime from that of the stakeholders. as already stated, the new register also involves a change in the regulation, so there are two reports, but it is still a first step towards more complete transparency. some hypotheses are already under consideration and may be converted into rules after more mature reflection, and therefore in particular point 9 of the act approving the agreement indicates the possibility that the reports may include the indication of the stakeholders encountered by members during the preparatory work of the report itself. this wide openness to possible revision makes me express an opinion against amendments which would place constraints on this future reflection. i hope, however, that in addition to the council's support for the short-term agreement, there will be a broad consensus in this parliament immediately, a strong indication of the duty of transparency and also a guide for action. i hope the vote will be almost unanimous.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i think mr weber rightly said that the transparency register being jointly managed is something to be proud of because, with the exception of the united states or canada, i do not know of any other place outside the european union where such a lobbies’ register with such parameters as we are going to establish is functioning. here i am also referring to member state capitals. the question that was raised by several speakers, the first being mr groote and then mr häfner, concerned the mandatory register. we, in the working group, are discussing this issue at great length. the problem is that currently we do not see the legal basis that allows us to oblige companies, citizens or interest representatives to register in order to exercise their profession. we, as an eu administration, cannot refuse to deal with such an entity or entities on this basis. therefore we have been looking for ways in which we can turn to the positive motivation of companies, organisations and lobbies to register. i think we achieved a lot because, with the agreement of parliament, we are actually turning this system into a mandatory one. with our joint actions, together with the council, we will increase the reputation and pressure so much that we will see in the next two years how this is to work and it will give us additional experience to have a high-quality review and we will see how we can improve the working of the system further. the calls for appropriate verification as regards financing the activities of those who register: here i can assure you that the commission is already performing random checks on all the registrants that are already in the register and i am sure that these activities will even increase once we manage the register jointly. all those who are in the register should be sure that if there is something inappropriate we will find it, we will criticise it, try to correct it and we will not be afraid to shame those responsible. i was very glad – i am coming back to this because several speakers referred to the importance it – that all three institutions are progressing in this work. i am sure that after this very important opening by the hungarian presidency, we will not waste a minute and we will try to start the interinstitutional talks with the council as soon as possible so we can find, i am sure, a very accommodating manner in which to manage the register together, the three institutions working on this issue with the same goal of increased transparency of european union legislation. the last point that was raised by several speakers and described by mr casini: the transparency register is definitely not a silver bullet or a magical solution to fight corruption. we know very well that high moral standards, ethics, dignity and clear rules are key. but it would certainly serve as a very good instrument and good indicator that those who register are prepared to respect the rules and be transparent, that they have nothing to hide and – this should be the key indicator for all of us – that they should be real partners to work with us and exchange information with us and that they have trust in our future communication.
the president of the council. - mr president, mr commissioner, distinguished members of the house, ladies and gentlemen. allow me to welcome today's debate as a representative of a member state which has had a lobbying law since 2006 and which sees parliament and the commission agreeing on the transparency register. transparency has always been a very important issue for that council. i am very pleased that while we failed to show results in 2008 and 2009, we have now, under the hungarian presidency, really achieved a breakthrough in that the council is ready to monitor the processes and, at some level, as you know, we are still in negotiations, and will be able to link up with this activity. we are therefore ready to discuss how we can contribute, and as i indicated in my opening speech, we are thinking of confirming this readiness in a political declaration in the course of june. so it's not about joining the interinstitutional agreement. and why this formula is being adopted by the member states at this moment, which is - i repeat, a major advance compared to previous years - is that the council, as an eu institution, is not being approached by lobby groups, so there is hardly any precedent for this. these activities are targeted more at member states, member state governments, government bodies. so the council as an institution is not exposed to the same lobbying as the commission or the european parliament. i trust, mr president and mr commissioner, and honourable members, that we will work well together and that after these negotiations we will be able to make this political statement.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to make a few points. i would also like to emphasize very strongly that this agreement was concluded long before the british journalists incident. unfortunately, this is a way of spreading false news through the media. for example, one of the biggest italian newspapers, corriere della sera, today mocks europe by saying that we would have moved late and only after these news events. which is false. this is an unfair way of spreading mistrust of europe. the agreement was reached long before that. the reason why this debate is taking place with some delay is precisely because, once the scandal broke, we asked ourselves whether we could make an attempt to enrich the agreement further; but the text is the same. that's the first clarification. the second concerns the question of compulsory nature. the register is already compulsory. anyone who wants to lobby has to register. i don't know what "required" means. it cannot mean that all companies, enterprises or citizens have to be registered in this register. it's not possible. it is the duty of individual members, if they are approached by someone who wants to put pressure on them, to ask them to register before they address them. the third point concerns possible future changes. there is a working party on this subject, and i think that it should be given the widest possible scope. i agree that it is appropriate to mention the lobbyists we have met during the course of our work, but i do not know whether this is a task for the rapporteur alone or whether the president should also be involved. we are giving the working party the freedom to make any necessary suggestions. finally, i should like to thank both the commissioner, who has made a great contribution to the implementation of this agreement, and the representative of the hungarian government, also for the assurances given about the forthcoming accession of the council, which certainly has its own specificity, because the council certainly represents the second chamber. thus, to provide the council with the register also means to emphasize better that the scheme of europe is constituted by a government the commission a legislative body, made up of both the representatives of the citizens and the representatives of the states. i am aware, however, that there is a specific feature, since the council of ministers represents the member states. i'm sure we'll come to a positive conclusion.
