vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr manders, for the work he has done, together with all the other shadow rapporteurs and the committee, to reach an agreement after difficult negotiations. i think it is absolutely important that this agreement be reached at second reading, because it will enable citizens and businesses to benefit more quickly from the new fibres and the new innovative products that will result from them and enable national administrations to reduce costs. i would like to thank parliament once again for its contribution to the interinstitutional debate through the amendments which have been tabled, some of which have particularly highlighted the political dimension and the interest of consumers in the matter. in fact, at the first reading, adopted by a large majority in parliament, the need to relaunch a broad debate on the labelling of textile products, including the question of the mark of origin, was underlined and it was proposed to extend the scope of the regulation to certain sectors. as you all know, the negotiations with the council in the months that followed required flexibility on the part of all in order to find workable solutions for the institutions. i believe that the agreed text is a balanced compromise which complements many of the amendments tabled by parliament and leaves room - this is a very important factor, as mr győri emphasized in his speech - for further developments in the near future. in the short term, as soon as the new regulation enters into force, consumers will have more information on the presence of animal parts in textiles and will also be able to use information on the complete composition of textile products. another immediate result of the new regulation is simplification, as the commission will replace a detailed technical annex of over 50 pages with european standards. but, more importantly, the immediate results of this regulation are not the final stage of the procedure. on the contrary, they are a starting point for further analysis and improvement of the legislation. in the short term, the text of the new regulation establishes a global review clause which calls on the commission to provide, if necessary, for further labelling obligations in this area. the commission will therefore present appropriate legislative proposals in the areas where further harmonisation is needed. it is my intention - and i am now making a commitment to the european parliament - to tackle this review immediately and thoroughly. we are already preparing the work to consult consumers on some fundamental questions, namely: the type of information that is important and how it is to be made available; how technological developments, such as e-commerce, affect the way textiles are purchased; how the growing requirements for traceability, sustainability and corporate social responsibility are affecting the textile fibre market; how we can best use the technologies available in the digital age; how can we, as the institutions of the european union, adapt our legislation to the growing ethical, social and environmental needs of citizens? mr president, these are just some of the issues on which work has already begun. as you can imagine, the trademark will certainly be one of the main priorities and central elements of our work. the review will therefore be an opportunity to reaffirm my support for the trademark of origin and to clarify once and for all the question of 'made in', a necessary tool for the competitiveness of european businesses and the health of the citizens of the union. we will look at this in depth in order to provide clear rules to avoid misleading information and to facilitate responsible consumer choices when purchasing the product. as rapporteur manders has said, the commission will also assess the link between allergies and chemicals used in textiles. a specific analysis carried out in this area can indicate how best to use existing legislation, for example reach. let me explain briefly: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the textile industry is not affected by the new rules. the review clause - and i thank the council again for stressing its importance and for its willingness to work with the commission immediately to complete the regulation - provides that the commission will present a report, followed by a legislative proposal if necessary, by 30 september 2013. it is my firm intention to try to get ahead of time and for that reason i have already instructed my services to start working.

mr president, i voted in favour of the textile labelling report because i think europe can and must do more to support the companies in the sector. the commission's proposal was purely technical and aimed at simplifying the existing labelling provisions. but this parliament has achieved two important things. the first: textile products derived also from products of animal origin fur and leather will have to include this information on the labels so that consumers can make an informed choice. the second: the european commission will have to present an impact study on the introduction of labelling by 2013, which will clearly indicate which garments have been produced in europe and which ones have a non-european origin. the latter is a decisive milestone for the competitiveness of european textiles in europe and the world.
mr president, the proposal for a regulation on which we are called upon to vote certainly has the merit of bringing together all existing legislation on textiles into a single text. this regulation will simplify and improve the existing legislative framework for the development and use of new fibres, support the development of innovative products and promote innovation in the textile and clothing sector. i appreciate that mr manders has also taken into account other aspects, such as the reduction of the administrative burden for the member states in transposing the national legislation on the technical adaptations required by the inclusion of the names of new textile fibres in the so-called 'harmonised list'. although i noted that we could have done more by introducing a specific article regulating the indication of the origin of textile products, i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation.
mr president, this regulation is vital for the european textile industry because it guarantees a free market with rules that prevent the irregularities and illegalities of the past. we welcome the decision of the institutions to accept the proposal and to look into the problem of traceability and origin of products, in order to ensure that european consumers are properly informed even if the time limits are too long. the aim is ultimately consumer protection. i would remind you that last october parliament voted by a very large majority in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the indication of the country of origin of certain products imported from third countries, including textiles, but to date the council has not opened negotiations or discussions with parliament, even informally. i thank the hungarian presidency for making this a priority, but i ask that the comparison be speeded up, otherwise there is a risk that european consumers will be protected in the food sector but not in the manufactured sector.
mr president, the report on the labelling of textile products which we have supported today is an important step towards legislative simplification for the benefit of consumers and all european producers in this sector. this regulation establishes new rules for labelling in the textile sector, with increasing attention to innovation in the sector and to an accelerated integration of union legislation, so that innovative products can be safely used. the text proposes to unify the three composition labelling directives into a single regulation, simplifying the existing regulatory framework and improving the transparency of the procedures. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. at the same time, however, the question of the indication of the country of origin cannot be ignored. we hope that a further step forward can be made soon by adopting rules governing the indication of origin in this sector too.
mr president, quality, labelling and traceability: these are the consumer protection instruments that guarantee excellent products. until now, europe has been the only market in the world without legislation on this matter, which has put it at a disadvantage vis-à-vis its main trading partners. today the european parliament is making its voice heard by voting a regulation to protect the excellence of european textiles. our products and manufacturing must be defended, especially in a time of economic crisis such as the one we are going through. so far, we have been able to make our mark through research and innovation, which has enabled the production of innovative textile fibres. consumers will no longer be at risk of purchasing textile products that are potentially hazardous to health because they may have been treated with chemical agents. the adoption of this regulation finally guarantees the right protection of the rights of over 500 million european citizens, who will no longer be able to be deceived by false information.
mr president, making the way in which decisions are taken easily verifiable for the citizens, as well as the processes, elements and resources that have influenced them, helps to ensure a high degree of transparency and to bridge the gap between the european institutions and the citizens, which is often mentioned in connection with the legitimacy and the so-called democratic deficit of the european union. a great deal of progress has already been made in recent years. just think of the register of interest representatives, adopted by the european parliament in 1996, or the commission's proposal to the european parliament in 2006 for a single register for lobbyists. the adoption of the stubb-friedrich report by this house has led to the creation of a joint working party. we can say that the results achieved by this group, in relation to the objectives set by parliament, are more than satisfactory. i fully agree with mr casini's report, because the transparency of political institutions is an essential condition for legitimacy. that is why i supported the proposal.
mr president, there is no doubt that this regulation is an important step in the process of putting the european institutions at the centre of attention. more transparency, more publicity, more transparency in behaviour and accessibility of information and, finally, the formation of a common transparency register. if we consider that the lobbying discipline in the united states of america was established as far back as 1948, we realize that they certainly play a role and, although they are mainly the bearers of mainly selfish interests, they must be taken into account. this is a draft report which looks to the future and, while not a starting point, is certainly a way of defending the correctness of the activities and decisions of the european institutions. that is why i voted in favour, convinced of the absolute importance of this path.
mr president, as the shadow rapporteur for the alde group, i am fully satisfied with the result achieved by today's vote. the arsenis dossier on forest protection is a flagship report, a basis for how the european parliament intends to tackle the protection of our forest heritage and the adaptation of forests to climate change. the european parliament has clearly expressed its views today, and we await the commission's proposals in the light of these, so that we can define the sectoral policies in greater detail. i would like to thank mr kriton arsenis in particular for his expertise and serious work, which has been developed through a long and not easy discussion because, as we know, the situation of forests is not the same in all the member states. nevertheless, we have found common ground and have also achieved particular objectives, such as the removal of certain areas from the speculation of building or the greater protection of forests of great value for biodiversity, such as those in the northern boreal and mediterranean regions, and a ban on building on land affected by intentional damage. mr president, as i have said, this is of great importance for many mediterranean countries, including your own greece.
mr president, i should like to say at the outset - and i hope that my time will not be taken away - that, as far as hypocrisy is concerned, there are very few of us left who believe in certain things. each of us intervenes with statements of vote after the votes: we'll be about five or six, we'll listen to each other and maybe we'll be picked up by the tv. but it's all really quite sad. i would therefore like to suggest - and i will certainly do so at the next meeting of the epp group - that the explanations of vote should be made before the vote, so that perhaps by talking and listening to each other we can also convince each other how to vote, rather than submitting to some kind of pre-defined team play. that said, i announced in my statement that i had voted in favour. i still believe in this europe, just as i still believe in the effectiveness of the presence of a high commissioner. i still think, however, that the member states believe in it much less than we do. it is perhaps appropriate to note, as i said to mrs ashton this morning and on other occasions, that if europe does not stop being partly economic and instead becomes more political, our role will probably not be as effective as it should be.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report for its moderate approach to the most pressing issues in the common foreign and security policy. thanks to the socialist group’s amendments, a more constructive language for the dialogue on russia and iran has been achieved. the amendments on the eu strategy on afghanistan also contributed to improving the structure of the report. the albertini report is a step forward towards a better eu security policy. while i support the efforts and the commitment of the rapporteur, i should also stress that the eu is still far from having a coherent long-term strategy in this area. the eu contribution to global peace and stability is still quite small and still depends too much on the usa’s vision of international security and on the ‘needle approach’ to the same issue. let us work for a more autonomous, eu-centred foreign and security strategy, because that is what european citizens expect from us and that is what we should deliver to them.
mr president, the most significant document on the eu security strategy was delivered by xavier solana. it is entitled ‘a secure europe in a better world’ and was adopted by the european council on 12 december 2003. since then, little progress has been made in this field. the union still lacks an effective strategy for its foreign security and on most relevant issues still follows the lead of the united states. this report tries to introduce some positive changes on tactical topics like crisis management, the fragmentation of the eu defence technological industrial base, and the ineffectiveness of the 24 eu security and defence missions around the world. i voted in favour of it, and i hope this parliament will continue to make a contribution towards the goal of enhancing eu strategic autonomy in security affairs. in particular, what we need is a redefinition of the major threats to our security after the collapse of the so-called islamic terrorist threat and the emergence of new dangers like the financial crisis.
the eu is still a very limited global actor; its role in the un system and in all multilateral organisations does not match its democratic, economic and cultural weight. this report addressed this deficit and calls for removing some obstacles to the full participation of our union to the global context. this is the reason why i voted in favour of it. the eu can make a powerful contribution to the peace and prosperity of our planet. let us allow its civilian power to expand its influence everywhere.
in writing. - this directive on labelling or marking to identify the lot to which a foodstuff belongs cannot but be welcomed, also because too often the criminal world falsifies codes for illicit purposes. the grouping and simplification of all the existing regulations on terms or marks can only facilitate controls and the detection of any abuses.
in writing. - this directive on the protection of wheeled agricultural or forestry tractors in narrow gauge tracks when they are overturned is to be welcomed. the grouping and simplification of all the existing regulations on this subject is an important step which will help to protect those who use agricultural equipment on a daily basis.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report because it aims to protect the operator who uses the agricultural machinery, since the controls must be easily accessible and not present a danger. they must be designed and arranged, or protected, in such a way as to preclude any involuntary movement or other manoeuvre dangerous to the operator.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report as it aims to regulate and simplify the legislation on the braking of wheeled agricultural or forestry tractors. in order to protect and safeguard the operator of agricultural or forestry tractors, machinery should be type-approved in accordance with ec provisions.
in writing. - it is essential to codify in a way that is comprehensible and accessible to the public the rules on the manoeuvring space, the driver's seat and the dimensions of the doors and windows of agricultural tractors in order to ensure safety. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - the report also promotes the simplification and clarity of community legislation, not least because, as in the case of excise duties, there are innumerable scattered provisions which have been amended on several occasions. unifying and making them comprehensible can only be useful for operators and users alike. our vote is in favour.
in writing. - the resolution adopted today fully endorses the position expressed by the commission as adapted to the recommendations of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission. the advisory group considered that the proposal in question was merely a codification of the existing texts without any substantial changes.
in writing. − in january 2009, the commission adopted the proposal for a new regulation on textile names and labelling of textile products. the proposal, which aims to simplify and improve the existing regulatory framework for the labelling of textile products, is intended to promote the development and use of new fibres. by replacing the three existing directives with a single regulation, it simplifies the legislative process to adapt legislation to technical progress and allows fibre consumers to benefit more quickly from innovative products on the market. i welcome this proposal and i think it is particularly significant that the new regulation contains an explicit reference to 'made in'. it is essential to continue to provide the european union with the tools to compete and compete in the globalised market with its main trading partners, such as the united states, canada, china and japan. i would also like to stress here what i consider to be the most important aspect of the agreement reached with the council, namely the commitment of the european commission to present, by 30 september 2013, after an appropriate impact assessment, a report accompanied by legislative proposals on origin labelling, traceability and the use of new technologies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, which has the merit of simplifying the existing system for labelling textile products, promoting the development and use of new fibres and reducing the time between the submission of an application and the adoption of a new fibre. with these new rules, consumers would benefit more quickly from innovative products. the document we have adopted today also encourages the use of the 'marque d'origine', which would make it easier for consumers to choose and help reduce fraudulent or misleading indications. in this respect, i support the amendment which introduces an obligation for the manufacturer to indicate on the labelling the presence of non-textile parts of animal origin, thus protecting end-users from the risk of inadvertently purchasing products, for example, with genuine fur and better safeguarding the health of allergy sufferers.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr manders' proposal has reached a crucial stage in its passage through the imco committee, where it was decided that the composition of 100% of the product, and not just of certain parts, should be introduced. but then our group came out in favour of defending textiles and 'made in' textiles, which were not addressed in the mediation with the council. there are, however, elements that can be shared, such as the process of de-scaling in the materials registers. i shall not be able to vote in favour of this resolution, as the defence of the 'made in' is a priority, and i shall therefore abstain.
in writing. - mr president, the text under discussion today is unfortunately very different from the one which was approved at first reading by this house. the main difference is that this report does not make any reference to the mark of origin to be used on the labels of textile products. the council has strongly opposed this hypothesis, and the reason for this is not clear: is it not right that consumers should know where the clothes they wear come from? the presence of a mark of origin would certainly serve as a guarantee of quality and protection of the product. i am very puzzled that only two member states, italy and lithuania, have insisted in the council that the recognition mark be inserted: i wonder what interest other european countries have in not protecting their own companies in this way, which are thus more exposed to unfair competition and counterfeiting. the european parliament has unfortunately bowed to the council's shortsighted will in not protecting a necessary trademark, and for this reason i felt i had to vote against today's report.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr manders' report. the text adopted not only proposes to unify the three directives on composition labelling into a single european regulation directly applicable to all member states, but also aims to simplify the procedure for the recognition of new fibres. the introduction of a rule on mandatory origin labelling for products originating in third countries would probably have made mr manders' report more complete, but given the difficulties encountered in dealing with certain subjects, i believe that a good compromise has finally been reached in the final text voted on.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the purpose of these measures is to help countries in the process of stabilising their economies, such as those in the western balkans, with preferential trade procedures with the eu compared with third countries. in view of the right will to extend until 2015, with particular attention to bosnia and serbia, i confirm my vote in favour.
in writing. - i congratulate mr hökmark on the preparation of such a timely report on the radio spectrum policy programme. i voted in favour of this because i strongly support all the measures to support and implement the single market. europe needs advanced and accessible systems for broadband and internet use that can reach rural and peripheral areas as set out in the digital agenda. at the same time, the safety of individuals, producers, users and public administrations must be guaranteed. in addition, high fibre costs and the growing demand from users for high-speed connections require a review of the technological framework, both from a regulatory and operational point of view. this requires the establishment of multiannual legislative programmes on radio spectrum to establish strategic planning and to meet the growing demand for broadband access, especially as official estimates suggest that data traffic is set to double every year until 2013.
in writing. - by adopting the hökmark report, the european parliament is making an innovative choice: the broadband and mobile telephony sectors are not only of great interest to european citizens, but also open up new perspectives in research and innovation, areas in which the eu can and must aspire to play a leading role. in this regard, it is important that the first european radio spectrum programme is in line with the objectives already outlined in the eu 2020 strategy and the 'digital agenda', and is part of the priority actions of the single market act. the eu needs to work to overcome the digital divide that causes great disparities within europe, especially between urban and rural areas, to ensure that all citizens have equal access to services, especially those related to new technologies. i therefore welcome the proposal for ambitious targets to provide broadband access to all european territories by 2020, with particular emphasis on wireless networks.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i believe that all those measures to promote and extend the transparency of parliamentary work are to be welcomed. the ratification of the treaty of lisbon has strengthened parliament's powers, making it a co-legislator in many areas of the ordinary legislative procedure. as a result of this process, parliament's work has become increasingly attractive to a wider range of stakeholders, which is an essential source of information for members of parliament. i therefore welcome the establishment and compilation of a common register for the control of organisations and individuals involved in the formulation and implementation of european union policies.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to congratulate the honourable member on his excellent work. i will support your proposal for the establishment of a lobbyist register to increase transparency in the european institutions. but we want the representations, such as the regions, to be given due recognition.
in writing. − relations between the european institutions and political actors on the one hand, and civil society, citizens and representative associations on the other, are recognised and encouraged by the treaty on european union. the institutions shall give citizens and representative associations the opportunity to make known and publicly exchange their views in all areas of union action. in particular, the institutions shall maintain an open, transparent and regular dialogue with representative associations and civil society. the adoption of the treaty of lisbon has strengthened the powers of the european parliament, which has become a co-legislator in almost all areas under the ordinary legislative procedure. in the light of these developments, the european parliament and the commission decided to establish a common register for the registration of the control of organisations and persons involved in the formulation and implementation of the policies of the european union. in order to take account of the changes to existing rights and duties and the creation of new rights and duties relating to the procedure for members, the resolution adopted today supports the need to amend parliament's rules of procedure.
in writing. - the report, which initially did not see us favourably as it applied the same rules on 'lobbyists' to public bodies including the representations of the regions to the eu, was amended following our requests. we think it is right to provide for a code of conduct for those who attend the european parliament on behalf of private associations or companies, just as we think it is right not to apply the same rules to churches, political parties, trade unions and public bodies. we therefore vote in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr casini's text. the transparency of the activities of the european institutions, which have also recently come under attack, is a precondition for legitimacy and a fundamental component in the establishment of a fair and open relationship with representative associations. i therefore believe that the creation of a joint register of parliament and the commission, with the aim of bringing together all the information relating to the actors who are in contact with the institutions, as well as reducing bureaucracy by allowing a single entry, represents a clear improvement in the way of an increasingly open and transparent dialogue with the so-called 'lobbyists'.
in writing. − the creation of a common register by the european parliament and the european commission to bring together all information on actors in contact with the institutions in a single access point is a step towards greater transparency. the transparency of political institutions is, in my view, the fundamental component of an open dialogue with civil society. ensuring that opinions and information in the various fields of union action can be publicly communicated and exchanged, while ensuring the control of organisations and individuals actively involved in the formulation and implementation of eu policies, is an important element of the democratic life of the institutions. i would like to make a few reservations, however: the exclusion of a number of actors from the scope of the register, including the social partners, local, regional and municipal authorities, is not shared. the exclusion is unjustified because these actors are stakeholders and actively participate in decision-making processes to the same extent as many other representative associations. i also think that the information required should be better defined so that it does not lend itself to different interpretations, as is the case in the present situation.
in writing. − the adoption of the common register on transparency - following the overwhelming majority vote in the committee on constitutional affairs - is a further step towards greater clarity in parliamentary activity. a common register between the european parliament and the commission, which will be public and accessible online, will make it easier for citizens to check the different stakeholders with whom members interact. however, this agreement still needs to be improved, as registration for stakeholders is still on a voluntary basis, although it is necessary to gain access to the institutions. the next objective will therefore be to achieve a mandatory registration for all interest representatives. we also expect the council, like the other european institutions, to follow the lead of parliament and the commission and join this register.
in writing. − transparency in the work of political institutions is a precondition for legitimacy. at all times and in all situations it must be possible to easily verify the manner in which each decision is taken, what factors have influenced it and, above all, how resources, i.e. taxpayers' money, have been used. parliament was the first european institution to establish a register of interest representatives in 1996. the resolution adopted today stresses that the creation of a common register ensures the widest possible participation of the various categories of operators, while respecting their differences and specificities. this mechanism provides important information, including the number of natural and legal persons involved in the various activities related to the register and the amount of eu resources benefitting the members.
in writing. - we have supported this resolution and put a question to the commission because we believe it is essential at this time, when the price of oil has been at its highest for some months. it has become unsustainable for many fishing vessels, especially small-scale fleets, to increase their expenditure capitals constantly because of the increase in crude oil, often failing to benefit from the various fishing campaigns. by calling for the de minimis ceiling to be increased from eur 30 000 to eur 60 000 over the next three years, we want to send a strong signal to the sector that in recent years, especially as a result of the entry into force of the cfp and the new restrictive measures, some medium and small-scale fishing models have been reduced or even abolished. it should also be remembered that measures have already been taken in other sectors, such as agriculture, to help it cope with this increase. so this aid, which we remember is at national rather than european level, and is therefore linked to the individual economic resources of the member states, could represent for many an imbalance in terms of competition, but in reality it would bring some breathing space to a sector that is increasingly on its knees.
in writing. mr president, i think this resolution on the free trade agreement with india should be rejected. it does not in any way denounce the problems which this agreement will bring to the textile sector in europe, and in northern italy in particular; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the resolution stresses, in order to show the validity of the agreement, how the two economies, indian and european, are complementary: the fact is that there are several sectors, including textiles, in which there is no complementarity at all, but rather unfair competition from the asian counterpart. for these reasons i have decided to vote against the resolution.
in writing. - we are strongly opposed to the eu-india free trade agreements because, while we consider that country to be making progress in protecting workers' health and safety and in fighting counterfeiting, we must still consider it to be an unfair competitor to our companies. for example, india, which as a state has been called back by the wto on the 500% duties it applied to european wines, has unfairly turned the corner by having the same duties imposed by individual member states. we also have to consider the negative economic impact of further liberalisation of trade with india, as the eu exports 1.9% of its services to india and india exports 11.6%. it is clear that this means making it 10 times easier for india than for europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on eu-japan trade relations. in 2009, the european union and japan accounted for around 20% of the world economy and in 2010 the value of bilateral trade reached eur 120 billion. in the light of these figures, i believe it is urgent and necessary to start negotiations on free trade agreements to encourage closer cooperation between the two trading partners and to offer the possibility of jointly addressing common challenges, such as the world economic crisis and the relentless political and economic rise of china. the precondition for the opening of negotiations and for the strengthening of trade relations remains the removal of non-tariff barriers and obstacles to access to japanese public procurement. at this preliminary stage, the commission should also focus on removing the barriers which hinder european smes.
in writing. the text on eu-japan trade relations sees us favourably as japan, despite being a third country, guarantees protection and respect for workers and the global economy. reducing and simplifying the rules, making it easier to trade openly and fairly, can only improve relations with europe. mutual investment between the two economies is worth €200 billion a year: the eu is japan's third largest trading partner and japan is the eu's sixth largest trading partner. the report also asks to assess the possible negative impact of these choices, but it certainly considers that the removal of barriers to trade and investment can only be positive. we therefore vote in favour of the text of the report.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 42% of the total area of the european union is covered by forests and woodlands. the forestry industry, with a turnover of over eur 300 billion, employs some 2 million people. these are the facts we need to bear in mind to understand the importance of a european strategy for sustainable forest management and a more effective protection of this considerable european heritage. we must remember both the important role of forests in providing socio-economic services and their fundamental contribution to the fight against climate change. it is therefore urgent to improve our capacity to prevent forest fires which continue to destroy more than 400,000 hectares of forest each year. to this end, it would be appropriate to improve the collection of information on forests, to increase research and, above all, to encourage the exchange of knowledge and experience between member states, starting from the cross-border area. i would like to stress the value of the work done by the european forest fire information system (effis) and, above all, the importance of the gmes programme, which makes it possible to monitor and map forest areas.
in writing. − the development of a european strategy for the protection of forests is part of the eu's overall commitment to combating climate change. the proposal for a specific regulation on the prohibition of building on land destroyed by arson fires and the request for adequate funding for forestry strategies, which is currently lacking, are particularly positive in their implementation. finally, it is relevant to require appropriate sustainability criteria in the production of biomass for energy purposes. we therefore urge the european commission to continue along this path by presenting a white paper on forest protection which addresses these issues.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report because forests, which cover more than 42% of the surface of the european union, provide a livelihood for many workers and businesses in the forestry sector. a framework of commission guidelines should be established, binding sustainability criteria should be introduced, including the mandatory nature of national forestry programmes, payments for ecosystem services should be formalised, and forest protection policies should be strengthened by reintroducing the fire prevention regulation. of particular value and impact was the approval of the amendment which prevents speculation on land resulting from intentional forest fires. in italy there is already such a rule which prohibits building destroyed by arson.
in writing. - the albertini report contains some ideas which are acceptable, but there is a fundamental problem. the basic approach is that the eu should gradually gain a pre-eminent position in the field of foreign and defence policy vis-à-vis individual national governments. this means that the member states would have to cede further substantial sovereign shares in foreign policy to the community bodies, which would be responsible for reaching a common position to be represented in the international community and in all multilateral forums. i cannot agree with this perspective: the member states could no longer base their foreign policy on national interests which they considered to be of paramount importance. we agree that the eu must strive to speak with one voice in certain areas in order to be stronger globally and to represent the interests common to all member states; but this cannot be done at the expense of the autonomy of the states in formulating their foreign policy. the report also calls on the eu to take a firm stand on turkey's accession to europe, a point on which i have traditionally been very much opposed. turkey must remain outside our organization, it is not and will never be europe. my vote is against the report.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i cannot vote in favour of mr albertini's proposal because there are too many points on which we cannot agree. one of these is the one which provides for the coherence of the european union's foreign policy. a flawless concept, but one that, given the crisis in north africa this year and the ongoing crisis in libya, shows how this is not possible. too many distinctions made by different eu countries. another point on which we cannot agree is the call to increase efforts to bring turkey into europe. that is why i shall be voting against.
in writing. − the albertini report on the 2009 annual report from the council to the european parliament on the main aspects and basic choices of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) is an important milestone for the future of the union's foreign policy. it is indeed necessary for parliament to speak out unanimously in calling on the council not to limit the scope of the annual cfsp report to a mere description of the activities of the cfsp but, as the report rightly states, 'to make it a policy instrument geared to the development of solutions'. we should also stress that 'the report should provide more than a simple list of events and developments by country and should also address the question of the effectiveness of eu foreign policy and the means needed to pursue the objectives of the union's external action'.
in writing. the report emphasises the eu's leading role as an effective global actor on the international stage. to do this requires more strategic external action and a single foreign policy uniting all states. it seems to me to be a utopia in the face of the continuing events in the middle east and the mediterranean countries. i voted against because the report seeks to limit national power by creating new agencies and new military operations, which would mean an increase in expenditure, and it also seeks to give greater impetus to the accession negotiations with turkey.
in writing. - defence policy is one of the most closely guarded areas of member states' policy. the impression that one gets from analysing this report, as indeed from other reports on the same subject or on foreign policy, is that the eu is being pushed to ensure that it gradually takes over the states in the formulation of foreign and defence policy. apart from the objections of principle which can be raised against this approach, it is difficult to see how the eu can be expected to speak with one voice on such sensitive issues, where the interests of individual states are often different, if not openly contradictory. just look at what happened in the case of libya and the humanitarian intervention. it is almost impossible for states to reach agreement and a single, agreed position on events of this magnitude, and even if they did, this would inevitably be to the detriment of the decision-making autonomy of governments and the interests considered to be the priority by national diplomacies. my vote is against the report.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty should represent a new political model in europe, both in terms of the need to pool the resources of the states to achieve the maximum results and in terms of working on common strategies and operations that make europe the political union that its founding fathers dreamed of. we are celebrating this week the europe day, which commemorates the schuman declaration, which speaks of a europe which will "rise from concrete achievements which first create a de facto solidarity". but it is precisely this solidarity that is lacking at the moment, above all in the expression of a strong political will common to all the states which would serve not only to protect our borders better but also to make our economy more credible. the gualtieri report clearly underlines the inadequacy of the european armed forces both in building a common european defence and in achieving the objectives of the lisbon treaty concerning the internal and external security of the union. without a credible military capability, the european common security and defence policy will remain only on paper and in the words of those who do not have the necessary tools to implement it effectively.
in writing. - the libyan crisis has highlighted the limits of eu external action, both diplomatically and militarily. at the moment, the much-talked-about unity of purpose seems to be undermined by what are the rightful aspirations of the member states to maintain their prerogatives in matters of security policy. i do not agree with the call for a more adequate budget for this policy, without a real sharing of responsibility by national governments for the use of these funds. i think that this kind of policy should be a matter for national competence, and i therefore vote against this report.
in writing. - my vote on the report on the development of the common security and defence policy following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon is in favour. our role in the mediterranean, in the middle east and therefore in the whole world will become increasingly important. the current upheavals, which will increase after the death of osama bin laden, must be dealt with in full compliance with the provisions of the treaty of lisbon. the key to the future will be to strengthen our political capacity to define common strategies and objectives in an increasingly coordinated and timely manner.
in writing. - mr president, the report under consideration today contains both positive and negative aspects, and it represents at best (or at worst) the typical contradictions which the european union displays in its external action. for example, greater integration and joint management in crisis situations is desired: the recent events in libya have shown how europe is acting in a dispersed manner, with some member states directly involved, others having withdrawn and practically only one country, italy, managing the direct consequences of the libyan crisis and the north african crisis in general, namely a massive flow of migrants. we must therefore decide how europe should behave: the european union must be able to take the necessary steps to ensure that the union is always united, with the consequences that follow. i am puzzled by the emphasis on the need to increase the power and resources of joint actions and the european defence agency: i would not like, given the circumstances, to see this too become a useless, self-serving cart, and actions totally ineffective. for these reasons i decided to abstain, until i had understood what the european union really wants to do 'when it is big'.
in writing. − the report outlines the need for the european union to play a stabilizing role in the world, working to maintain peace, strengthen international security and manage crises. i voted in favour of this report to join the chorus of parliament's disappointment at the lack of a genuine, comprehensive and uniform post-lisbon approach to the common security policy by the european union. credible and reliable military systems and expertise are an essential condition for the development of an autonomous security and defence policy. i believe, however, that to strengthen the european union's capacity to respond to crises, while ensuring its strategic autonomy, it is necessary to adopt a common political will in the long term.
in writing. the report sets out the developments in european defence policy since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. i voted against because it is clear that the european union has not acted in a coherent and shared manner following the recent events in libya. there has been a lack of solidarity in the management of the migration crisis, making it clear that when national interests are at stake, the eu forgets noble concepts and disregards them.
in writing. - this report is completely unbalanced on positions favourable to a perspective where, in the future, in the framework of global and regional multilateral organisations, the eu is in a position at least equivalent to that of the member states. this would mean the end, in essence, of the autonomy of diplomatic action by the member states - the member states should adjust their positions so as not to be in clear contrast with those of any community representation - and the consequent inability of national governments to assert their interests adequately in international forums. while it is acceptable that in certain areas, such as monetary policy, the eu should be the dominant position in the relevant multilateral bodies, it is also difficult to accept the idea that the external action service should take it upon itself to represent a position shared by the member states in the world, when the interests of european countries are often so different that it is impossible to reach a common position. i therefore intend to vote against a report which proposes a future scenario in which national diplomacy would be substantially superseded by community diplomacy, to the detriment of the diplomatic autonomy of the member states.
in writing. the effects of the lisbon treaty necessarily imply a review of the role played by the eu in international organisations. however, as we have seen too often in recent times, the so-called single voice with which europe should approach multilateral issues is often detrimental to the prerogatives and decision-making autonomy of the member states. i therefore think i should abstain, because there are positive aspects to the report, but these are being undermined by the comments made a few moments ago.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because i want the eu's role in multilateralism to be further strengthened in the years to come. this is also in line with the treaty of lisbon, which, by giving the union legal personality, enhances its capacity to join not only the various international organisations but also regional organisations and the relevant groups of states. these relations will be able to resolve economic and commercial issues as well as environmental ones. the european union's contribution must also be an added value in multilateral organisations or summits where not all its members are represented. unfortunately, recent but also ongoing political and humanitarian crises around the world have called for swift and decisive action by the eu. it is often not easy, but countries affected by such crises look to the eu for rapid intervention not only through foreign policy instruments but also first aid in emergencies.
in writing. − the external dimension of the eu needs to be strengthened as article 21 of the eu treaty promotes an international system based on enhanced multilateral cooperation in which member states ensure that the union can assert its interests and values on the international stage. the lisbon treaty has created new permanent structures for the eu's external representation, but this new dimension does not yet allow the union to participate fully and unilaterally in the work of many international bodies. this risks undermining the union's commitment to effective multilateralism, limiting its decision-making capacity and undermining its credibility. it is precisely because of the increase in political and humanitarian crises in the world that the eu should make the best use of its foreign policy instruments, so as to ensure better use of its leverage within multilateral organisations and its capacity to take the lead in dealing with current and future international crises. the promotion of democracy and human rights, in particular the rights of women and children, freedom of expression and the rule of law should be at the heart of all eu external action.
in writing. the final text of this report strengthens the eu's strategic role in international organisations. to do this, we must first of all promote active and practical participation, which will allow for the strengthening of both internal and external cooperation. this must be the key to strengthening the legitimacy of decisions taken, while ensuring full responsibility sharing. finally, the member states must coordinate within the human rights council in order to establish clear and rigorous access criteria, especially for countries where human rights violations are on the agenda.

the agenda includes the debate on the oral question to the commission on antibiotic resistance, by mr paolo de castro, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development (o-000048/2011 - b7-0304/2011).
author of the book. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, today is an important opportunity to take a serious and responsible approach to the growing problem of antibiotic resistance in animals, a strategic issue for the agricultural sector and, in particular, for the future of the european livestock system. in europe, data indicate that about half of all antibiotics used are prescribed for animal use. antibiotics, when used correctly, are a useful tool to help farmers keep their animals healthy and productive and to ensure their well-being. we are not here to demonize the use of antibiotics in animal husbandry, but we want to ask the commission for a concrete response to the more efficient and effective use of antimicrobials in order to reduce resistance in animals. this parliament, in its resolution of 5 may 2010 on the european union action programme on animal welfare, had already stressed the link between animal welfare, animal health and public health, and called on the commission and the member states to address responsibly the sensitive issue of antibiotic resistance in animals. in particular, we had asked the commission to collect and analyse data on the use of all animal health products, including antibiotics, in order to ensure the effective use of these products. one year later, the committee on agriculture, which i have the honour of chairing, is here to ask the european commission to take all the necessary steps to reduce this longstanding problem, which can also have consequences for human health. what is needed, mr president and commissioner, is a concrete commitment by the commission to put the results achieved into practice, starting from the data collected, not only by encouraging research and monitoring activities but also by ensuring greater effectiveness in the use of antibiotics as an important tool in the fight against animal diseases. on this front, i would like to point out that some studies show that a low-energy animal diet could lead to an increased incidence of disease and therefore to an increased use of antibiotics. it would therefore be desirable, in full respect of the highest food safety, to be able to review the prohibition on the use of animal meal for monogastric animals, in accordance with the opinion of the european veterinary scientific committee. these are the demands of the resolution adopted by the committee on agriculture on 12 april and which we shall be voting on in this house tomorrow. it has been a lot of work in the last few months, and i would like to personally thank mr paulsen, the shadow rapporteurs and all the groups in this parliament for their valuable contribution to the definition of a common text on a subject on which the competitive future of european livestock farming could depend and whose cross-cutting nature requires efforts and responsibility, through a coordinated approach and a common will.
member of the commission. − madam president, the commission strategy on antimicrobial resistance (amr), which we plan to present in november, will provide further ideas on how the commission, together with the member states and stakeholders, could tackle amr in all sectors involved. some of these actions may require changes in legislation. others may not. the key is to select the right tools for the task in hand. i fully agree with you that this is not only, or chiefly, an animal farming issue. this is why our aim is to reduce the development of antimicrobial resistance attributed to the use of antimicrobials in animals. there are various tools here: education, awareness-raising campaigns and so on. by the same token, we believe that data has to be collected to promote better understanding of the problem. the member states do actually show interest in providing data, which is encouraging. and yes, we do have a timetable for action. preparatory work is on-going, including impact assessment, the revision of rules on veterinary medical products and so on. legislative proposals, as i already mentioned, will follow in 2012. the commission very much welcomes the valuable input of parliament and looks forward to continued collaboration with parliament, member states and stakeholders from all sectors, with the common aim of protecting the health of citizens throughout the european union.

in writing. - mr president, the commission pays great attention to smes. 23 million smes, which form the fabric of the community economy, are a source of innovation and creativity and enable europe to continue to stand out on world markets. the bureaucratic and legislative obstacles which until recently stifled the creation of small innovative companies are gradually disappearing, and young people are also seeing a window of opportunity for a stable future, and we hope that it will also be full of opportunities. entrepreneurship, training, flexibility, smart regulation and access to credit are the key words in the small business act, a framework that sets out the union's policy for smes through targeted support and training activities for young people. now that a number of initiatives have been defined, it is up to the member states and the european union as a whole to give them due implementation, by giving smes greater freedom in their actions, allowing them to participate in public procurement tenders, adopting the single european patent in the future and rapidly implementing the directive on late payment. we must not forget that if we are not to frustrate the efforts made so far, we need investment, because only this will act on the basis of the proper functioning of the mechanism and european competitiveness itself.

in writing. - the request for the introduction of the single european patent put forward by the report, as well as the satisfaction it expresses over the adoption of forced cooperation in relation to the introduction of the patent, prevents me from voting in favour. the introduction of an anglo-french-german european patent is unacceptable for at least two reasons. firstly, trilingualism would have a negative impact on the competitiveness of firms in member states not represented in the system. these companies, including italian ones, would have to wait for the translation processes to be completed before they could have access to documents, at the expense of timeliness, which is of primary importance in the commercial sector. they should also bear additional translation costs. on the other hand, anglo-french-german companies would not face any of these obstacles, which would give rise to discrimination on the basis of language. furthermore, the introduction of the trilingual system does not seem to meet administrative requirements, and does not even seem to reflect the demographic weight of the member states, because then italy would also have to be represented. it is rather an attempt to impose german prestige at the expense of the principles of parity and equality between the member states on which the eu is founded. i therefore decide not to support the report.
in writing. - innovation is in many ways the key to economic growth. as early as the second half of the 20th century, the most authoritative growth economists had understood that innovation is one of the main variables to leverage on declining marginal returns. in this way, we have moved from the growth models of the 1950s, according to which the economy is destined to stabilize and lose its propulsive momentum sooner or later, to the endogenous growth models of the 1980s, where, thanks to technology and the design of ever-changing and innovative products, the economy manages to maintain a positive growth rate over the long term. to activate these levers, which will be used from now until 2020 to achieve research objectives, energy efficiency and internationalisation processes, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, we need a strong political will to set in motion the incentive and guidance mechanisms currently in the hands of the member states, for which the european funding instruments provide valuable support. resources are limited because of the crisis and the europe 2020 directives will have to be accompanied by strong fiscal and industrial policies by european governments.
in writing. - europe, which is emerging from an unprecedented crisis in recent months, is facing very strong competition at world level. in this context, innovation is a necessity but above all a priority. if we fail to turn europe into an innovation union, the economies of the 27 member states will be doomed to decline, with the consequent loss of talent and ideas. innovation is the key to achieving sustainable growth and contributing to a fairer and greener society. innovation is essential to creating a modern economy and is the main tool for creating new jobs. a common commitment is needed to bring about a profound change in europe's capacity for innovation. only then will we be able to create stable employment and well-paid jobs that can withstand the pressure and competition of globalisation. the union is innovating. it is not a mere play on words but a real wish that must be fulfilled.

in writing. - mr president, regulations (ec) no 1541/98 and (eec) no 3030/93, which were originally adopted with the aim of applying trade policy measures to the textile sector, have now become two outdated texts which place limits on the free market and are ill-suited to the evolution of the new regulatory environment. until recently, there were quantitative restrictions on imports from wto member countries and special safeguard measures for those textile products from the prc. as the wto agreement expired in 2005, these restrictions were removed, also for the prc in 2008, therefore the only effective tool to prevent market distortions and at the same time continue to control imports of textile products remains the subordination of textile products to verification procedures requiring the indication of the country of origin. this is also stated in the proposal for a regulation on made in, voted on in this house on 21 october 2010, which introduces a control mechanism and aims to simplify the legislation in force, with a view to creating a better and clearer legislative framework for businesses and consumer protection.
in writing. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's textile industry is not left to the mercy of the market. the rapporteur's arguments that future legislation on made-in and new agreements within the world trade organisation will soon be a good solution to defend our industry do not seem to hold water: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it certainly seems wiser to wait until a clear regulatory framework is defined to regulate the import of certain textile products from the east in the future before proceeding to repeal the old regulations. i therefore vote against.
in writing. − we strongly supported this report in view of the eu's political commitment to simplify existing legislation: we want to create a better and clearer regulatory environment for business. european trade policy measures in the textile sector can be managed without imposing an excessive burden of proof of origin for all imports. to continue to control imports of textile products subject to quantitative restrictions still in force and originating in countries not yet members of the wto, the eu will rely on import authorisations; while for product categories falling within section xi of the combined nomenclature, not subject to quantitative restrictions on imports and released for free circulation in the eu, an ex post statistical surveillance system will be applied to monitor their impact on the european market. it should be recalled that, since 2010, in order to better inform consumers about the origin of various products, the indication of the country of origin of certain third-country products has been mandatory in addition to the abovementioned import control mechanisms. we will now have to work on improving the uniformity of import rules by aligning those for textiles with those for other industrial products, thus improving the overall consistency of the legislative framework in this area.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted against this report because it is based on unfounded assumptions and vague assumptions about the future. on the one hand, it is argued that the proof of origin is useless, since it is claimed that the european union can protect itself by relying on an ex post customs statistical surveillance system: however, it is not mentioned, for example, that the 'updated community customs code' is far from being fully operational and that it still has obvious shortcomings, especially in terms of the complete and necessary computerization of the system. at the same time, it is expressly stated that the implementation of the muscardini report on made in, which we have strongly supported, is planned to support the protection of the trademark of origin; i am glad that the rapporteur is so confident, but at the moment there is no regulation on the made-in system, and we do not know whether, when or how it will be adopted. in essence, therefore, this report seems to me to be a dangerous leap into the void, with heavy effects as usual on the textile sector, which the european union continues to torment in the conscious general indifference.
in writing. the adoption of mr zahradil's proposal reopens the debate on the importance of a designation of origin for products from third countries as a means of implementing a trade policy capable of avoiding market disturbances due to an increase in foreign imports and of resolving the complicated legislative situation which today hinders the development of small and mediumsized enterprises. i am therefore in favour of a regulation which would harmonise the rules for european textile imports, currently in force, and bring them into line with those for other industrial sectors, but i think it is worth recalling that despite the efforts made to assess, through ex ante and ex post control mechanisms, the impact on the european market of imports from third countries, the european union has not yet been able to establish a control mechanism based on fair and important information for consumers such as origin labelling. i hope that the council will also be able to assess positively, and in a timely manner, the decisive steps taken by this parliament towards traceability and adequate information on products, measures which can both ensure appropriate and reliable knowledge of goods on the market and enhance the specificity of european manufacturing.
in writing. the commission's proposal to repeal council regulation (ec) no 1541/98 on the attestation of origin for certain textile products and to amend council regulation (ec) no 3030/93 on common rules for imports of certain textile products originating in third countries aims to simplify the legislation in force with a view to creating a better and clearer legislative environment for businesses, especially as regards the simplification of administrative formalities carried out by importers of certain textile products put into free circulation in the community. the requirements for attesting the proof of origin of textile products were introduced in order to ensure the correct application of the import restriction measures, in order to avoid market distortions due to imports from the people's republic of china. the impact and number of measures applied by the eu to imports of these products has gradually decreased in recent years, as special safeguard provisions have been created for imports of textile and clothing products originating in the people's republic of china and quantitative restrictions on imports originating in countries that are members of the wto have been removed. for the reasons i have given, i shall vote in favour.

in writing. - the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has increased the number of cases in which the european parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of an international agreement. airline agreements now fall into this category. the new powers of parliament established by the treaty imply new responsibilities to ensure that parliament and the committee responsible are adequately informed about the preparation of agreements on which parliament will be asked to give its consent. in the light of this change, i welcome the corresponding new responsibility of parliament to monitor more closely the conduct of the negotiations. i take this opportunity to emphasize that in order to be in the best position to assess whether or not to give approval at the end of the negotiations, it is essential that parliament follows the process from its initial stage rather than after the conclusion of the negotiations themselves. finally, i renew my call on the commission to encourage a constant exchange of information with the european parliament by regularly submitting reports analysing the strengths and weaknesses of existing agreements. i believe that this instrument will enable parliament to evaluate future agreements more effectively.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, at today's sitting i voted in favour of mr simpson's report on international air transport agreements under the treaty of lisbon. following the entry into force of the treaty on 1 december 2009, the european parliament acquired the right to give its consent to agreements in areas covered by the ordinary legislative procedure. this is a major step forward, especially in relation to the so-called democratic deficit in the eu, if we remember that previously parliament, a body democratically elected by european citizens, was only consulted on the conclusion of such agreements. we therefore expect the commission to respond to our call to maintain the flow of information and to provide the committee responsible with all the information concerning its intention to propose negotiations with a view to concluding and amending international air agreements, in such a way as to enable the whole of parliament to express its opinion in full knowledge of the facts.
