in writing. the report under discussion today is of particular importance because it provides for the amendment of directive 1999/62/ec on the taxation of heavy goods vehicles. i believe that the formulation of the proposal for a new directive, which is the result of a compromise between the hungarian presidency, the commission and parliament, is very damaging to the italian economy, which carries around a third, or about eur 200 billion a year, of all trade on european roads. as a result of the implementation of the directive in the european countries of transit, goods imported and exported from italy would be most likely to be subject to additional charges. i share the strongly critical view of the italian government that, in a period of great economic difficulty such as the present one, the political choice to hit a major economic category in our market is certainly not far-sighted. in my view, the small openings which were closed during the compromise do not have a decisive impact on a system which is highly negative both for the italian system and for the road transport sector. in addition, the effectiveness of the measure is not demonstrated: road transport, and its costs in terms of pollution production, will continue to rise until an intermodal infrastructure network is established.
in writing. the house voted in favour of the road toll directive, which represents a step forward in protecting the health of european citizens and a commitment to reducing the harmful effects of road freight pollution. by introducing the 'polluter pays' principle for the first time in this sector, the aim is to encourage more sustainable and safer transport, thus favouring alternatives such as rail transport. the compromise reached, however, also calls for consideration to be given to the protection of road transport, without penalising the sector excessively. it is therefore necessary that member states commit themselves to making effective use of the revenues generated by the eurovignette, for example by investing in improving the infrastructure network and encouraging the use of less polluting road transport vehicles, to ensure that the benefits of the directive are shared by all sectors concerned.
in writing. - mr president, i voted against the compromise text proposed, which appears to be in line with the position of the italian government, which had already expressed its opposition to this assumption in the council of the eu. the introduction of an additional taxation system for road hauliers is a very serious blow to a sector which in italy is a pillar of our commercial system. increasing the costs for these categories means increasing the burden on the community and penalizing our goods which are therefore less attractive on the demand side. i do not think that this compromise is the right solution, especially for a territory such as italy, which is the starting point of transport flows which are a source of wealth for our country system and which must be safeguarded by identifying appropriate instruments to combat air and noise pollution, but which take into account its structural and logistical peculiarities.
in writing. − directive 1999/62/ec on the charging of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures allows member states, if they so wish, to charge road users for certain external costs, thus giving them further opportunities to increase the efficiency of their national toll systems and thus providing them with a better tool for managing transport demand. we believe that in a period of great economic difficulty, the choice to hit a major economic sector in our market for the sole purpose of making money is not a particularly far-sighted political choice. the instrument thus identified, moreover, places an unacceptable burden on the geographically peripheral states, the countries of origin, departure or arrival of goods, to the advantage of the 'central' and transit countries. finally, the impact of this measure on traffic flows and thus on existing concessions, with the consequent risk of shifting these traffic elsewhere, is not taken into account in the development of the principle. the effectiveness of the measure is not demonstrated: road transport and its pollution costs will continue to rise: that is why we, the italian delegation of the epp, are opposed to this.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i wanted to express my negative vote on this proposal because it would have a very negative impact, especially on the smaller road haulage companies. it is certainly right to fight pollution and try to reduce traffic congestion, but the introduction of a further tax burden does not seem to me to be the best solution. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european road haulage industry is not left behind. many small firms, especially in italy, risk having to leave the market because the burden would become excessive, and this would certainly have a heavy impact also from the employment point of view. i hope that other european countries will follow the italian government's line, which has already confirmed that it will not apply this measure: the crisis has hit the road transport sector hard and i do not think this new tax will help it much to recover.
in writing. the new eurovignette directive, which aims to encourage the implementation of harmonised charging systems between member states to improve the efficiency and environmental performance of road freight transport, ends up penalizing some peripheral states, such as italy, which are destinations of departure or arrival of goods. i therefore voted against the report amending the 1999 directive. instead of increasing competition and establishing common rules for the internal market, the new directive distorts competition to the advantage of certain states, which are at the centre of road transport in europe. under the pretext of reducing co2 emissions, a tax is being introduced which is intended to discourage road transport in favour of rail and intermodality. the directive, as conceived, represents a major blow to the whole road transport system at a time of economic stagnation when measures to revive the sector would be necessary.
in writing. - mr president, with the amendment of directive 1999/62/ec, member states will be able to charge road users for certain external (content) costs, thus definitively introducing the 'polluter pays' principle in road transport; these states will have further opportunities to increase the efficiency of their national toll systems, thus having a better tool for managing transport demand. this is why road tolls for the transport sector will reflect the cost of noise and air pollution as well as infrastructure costs. these costs will always take account of certain exceptions, provided that the requesting state has a good justification. there will be incentives to promote the renewal of the heavy vehicle fleet, derogations for heavy vehicles with less polluting engines and finally the toll price may vary according to the time of transit. this is to ensure that heavy vehicles can avoid certain road sections during rush hours. the money raised from this toll increase will have to be reinvested in transport infrastructure with at least 15% initially going to transeuropean transport projects. for these reasons and in the interests of a better european viability, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the recommendation is the last step in the process of amending directive 1999/62/ec on the charging of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures (eurovignette). it is the result of long consultations and compromises, including with the various political groups. charging users for some of the associated external costs allows member states to increase the efficiency of their national toll systems, thus improving their capacity to manage transport demand. the 'polluter pays' principle also helps to empower users of the sector. finally, a transparent and effective allocation of revenues from infrastructure and external costs raises public support and accelerates the reduction of external costs of road transport.
in writing. - i voted against the text tabled by the rapporteur, mr saïd el khadraoui, which allows for a surcharge to be charged for air and noise pollution from heavy vehicles. although i agree with the so-called 'polluter pays' principle, it is rather questionable in a situation of economic crisis to impose additional taxes on tir motorway tolls, especially without the obligation to use the proceeds for investments to improve infrastructure. the text adopted does not help those member states, including italy, which suffer from geographical barriers which make the movement of goods for import/export more costly.
in writing. - i have welcomed the proposal of my colleague, for whom i voted in favour. european environmental policy is becoming increasingly crucial in the light of the economic crisis and the eu 2020 strategy, and only through reliable data can european environmental policy be monitored in depth. environmental data are the only tool for evaluating environmental policy and should be supplemented in the medium term with additional reliable information. in addition, data could be monitored more easily if reliable information on the interactions between environmental and economic factors were available: environmental economic accounts could contribute to policy evaluation by providing data on the environmental impact of economic policies and will be instrumental in economic-environmental decision-making. the member states will have to have common methodologies, classifications and rules to be compiled within a framework binding on them, and it is hoped that these new measures will not entail additional costs or bureaucracy. the rapporteur believes that the proposal for a regulation under consideration is a first step towards the drawing up of a more comprehensive environmental accounting system.
in writing. − measuring the air quality of our cities and analysing this measurement in depth would be a step towards greater transparency of policy-making. this indicator, although it refers to chemical and physical quantities which are not immediately available for communication between elected officials and voters, is the result of a number of economic decisions: it indicates, among other things, the concentration of polluting economic activities, the composition of the energy mix used for production activities and for heating homes and offices, the use of motor vehicles and the management of road and traffic infrastructure, the insulation of buildings and the quality of materials used, the presence or absence of green areas, to name just a few. on the other hand, air quality has important consequences for health expenditure, particularly for the pulmonary and oncology departments. it is therefore clear that an environmental indicator can be transformed into an economic and political indicator. it can also point to new mechanisms to discourage vicious behaviour and to fund virtuous projects. these links help politicians to make better decisions in the interests of citizens. the first step is to establish the correct methodologies, and it is good that this is done.
in writing. - the treaty of amsterdam has placed great emphasis on the interrelationship between economic and environmental policy. this is why factors such as sustainable transport and energy resources have become key issues in other policy areas as well. in fact, as early as 2006, the european council called on member states to extend national accounts to the core aspects of sustainable development, in order to provide fully consistent data. i am voting in favour of this proposal for a regulation because i believe that it will facilitate the work of the national statistical institutes by allowing the production of harmonised and timely data on environmental accounting. in this respect, the adoption of a european legal basis for the collection of data on environmental economic accounts will provide estimates at european level of the existing interaction between the economy and the environment. finally, i hope that this instrument can be seen as a further confirmation of the leading role played by the european union in environmental accounts worldwide.
in writing. − only with reliable data can european environmental policy be assessed in depth, which is why data collection by member states should be compulsory. we refer in particular to data on atmospheric emissions, environmental taxes for various economic activities and accounting for material flows at the macroeconomic level. in our view, environmental economic accounts should contribute to policy evaluation, in particular by providing data on the environmental impact of economic activities, which could prove particularly useful for decision-making in economic-environmental matters. we support the need for a review clause and for the european commission to submit periodic reports on the practical implementation of the regulation. we believe it is important to check the reliability and comparability of the data in order to make some improvements and to ensure a high level of quality in economic and environmental accounting. due account should also be taken of the development of new modules and of the experience gained in the course of the pilot studies. the verification report should provide an opportunity to adapt the regulation in the light of the latest developments and experience gained.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for a regulation on european environmental economic accounts is intended to provide useful tools for achieving some important objectives such as a european environmental accounting strategy and a deepening of the work of the statistical institutes which provide data on the subject to the administrative bodies. i voted in favour of the text because i believe that it is important for sustainable development to integrate environmental issues into the policies of the union and to have national accounts and a european programme with integrated economic and environmental accounting on transport, recycling and waste prevention, atmospheric emissions, climate change, sustainable production and consumption.
in writing. − the european council in 2006 called on the european union and its member states to extend statistical data for sustainable development and existing national accounts data. the commission itself in 2009 in its communication 'more than gdp: measuring progress in a changing world' proposed several measures to be taken in the short and medium term on the definition of broad indicators that create a more reliable cognitive basis for better public debate and more appropriate policy action. but the issues concerning the european environmental economic accounts were also discussed in particular. the in-depth assessment of european environmental economic accounts can only be done in the presence of reliable data, for this reason member states should be equipped with common methodology and accounting standards, definitions, classifications and rules to be developed in a framework binding on all states. in order to clarify the objectives pursued and the future orientations with regard to environmental economic accounts and so that they may constitute an indispensable element for decisions on economic and environmental matters, i am voting in favour of the proposal in question.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr jo leinen's text. in recent years, environmental policy and sustainability policy have become increasingly important, with increased attention to the integration of economic and environmental policy. climate change, sustainable transport, nature, biodiversity, the use and exploitation of raw materials and natural resources, and waste management have seen their importance in member states' policies increase exponentially. this is why evaluations of european environmental policy and eu thematic strategies can only be carried out in a serious and rigorous way if reliable data are provided.

member of the commission. − mr president, when the european system of protected designations of origin (pdos), protected geographical indications (pgis) and traditional specialities guaranteed (tsgs) was set up, equivalent systems already existed in some member states. the concept of geographical indications was thus familiar and names had already been registered at national level. this explains why there are many registered names in certain member states. nevertheless, growing interest in the system has been observed in many member states. the procedure for registering a name generally takes several years. this is because the applicant group has to draw up specifications and have them approved at national level and then by the commission. the single document summary of the specifications for geographical indications or the specifications themselves for traditional specialties are then published in the official journal of the european union in order to allow objections to be made. the objection period lasts six months. if there are no objections, the name may be registered. if an objection is lodged, the interested parties have six months to reach agreement. if no agreement is reached, the commission issues a decision that is voted on by the standing committee. this procedure explains the time required for registration to take place. on the other hand, once a name has been registered, it enjoys strong protection and international recognition and benefits from communication tools, particularly use of the logo. the commission is aware of the need to speed up the registration procedures. proposals to this end have been made in the context of the quality package, including reducing the time for the commission to scrutinise applications received to six months and reducing the objection period to two months. awareness of the system varies greatly from country to country, often depending on the number of registered names in a country. the commission makes funds for promoting quality products available to operators in order to raise consumer awareness of the system.

mr president, the document on the mid-term review of the seventh framework programme is particularly important. i voted in favour of this report for four reasons, which i consider to be of the highest priority: 1) simplification and streamlining of procedures to facilitate access to finance; 2) participation of small and mediumsized enterprises, a decisive instrument for development and employment; (3) innovation for a competitive production system that meets the challenges of the market; 4) risk financing mechanism, which has so far produced very positive results. finally, i would like to point out that only a concrete commitment to research policies can consolidate the knowledge-education-research triangle in europe, on which the future of cohesion policy is based.
mr president, research and innovation play a central role in the development and competitiveness of the european union and are crucial to achieving the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. the seventh framework programme is the main instrument for financing research in europe, as the report voted today shows, but there are still many difficulties due to the excessive administrative burden on small and mediumsized enterprises. the european parliament, in its resolution of 11 november 2010, requested the european commission to introduce measures to simplify the procedures, administration and finances in the current management of the seventh framework programme, which have not yet been implemented. i would ask the commission to take parliament's comments into account and to identify solutions which will facilitate access for smes to the seventh and eighth research programmes.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is undeniable that the rating agencies have now acquired enormous and uncontrollable power. their initial function was to provide valuable information to investors, but they have evolved over time into supreme and uncontrollable judges of the international financial markets. i do not think it is acceptable that companies, and even european states, should be judged by three large american companies, whose valuations have not always been correct but have sometimes led to glaring errors, as in the case of lehman brothers. i hope that the new european authority will be able to act in the best possible way and that it will be given real powers of intervention, including sanctions, if necessary. i also think it is appropriate to introduce the principle of civil liability in cases of gross negligence. we need more competition in this sector and we must break the historical oligopoly and try to bring in new, independent and possibly european players, who are aware of the economic situation and reality of our continent, which is completely different from the us logic. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
mr president, the external dimension of social policy covers all the activities and initiatives of the european union aimed at promoting social and labour standards in third countries. although both the lisbon treaty and the european union 2020 strategy place unprecedented importance on social policy, competitiveness issues and economic factors continue to override social issues. but it is becoming increasingly clear that we must no longer focus strictly on markets but on people in general, that is to say, on their protection and on workers' rights and labour law. the european union must have as its long-term objective the ability to guarantee men and women the opportunity to obtain decent and productive work, in conditions of freedom, equality, security and dignity! it is therefore necessary that in future the european parliament and the international and european trade unions should join forces to incorporate their positive and urgent recommendations into the initiative voted on here today.
mr president, 2011 is a strategic moment to build on the experience gained during the four years of application of the regulation establishing a financing and development cooperation instrument. since its entry into force, the main problem that has emerged seems to be the difficulty of understanding or accepting the specific role played by development cooperation in the context of the european union's external action. it must therefore be made clear that development cooperation is the political dimension of the european union's external action, together with humanitarian aid, which was not designed to meet european interests but to defend the interests of the most vulnerable and marginalized people on the planet! with today's vote we are going to stress the need for a separate financing instrument for cooperation and development, intended exclusively for developing countries and specifically aimed at achieving the objectives set out in article 208 of the treaty. in particular, we ask - and i conclude, mr president - that decisions on the general objectives, the priority areas, the expected results and the allocation of funds in accordance with article 290 of the treaty be taken by means of the delegated act procedure.
mr president, in a highly globalised economy such as the present one, the opportunity and ability to study and work in an international environment is an essential condition for professional success. the key factors identified in the european strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth require, as regards vocational education and training, to be translated into concrete measures at the level of the european union and the member states. the forecasts suggest that the growth in skills needs will continue to increase: industrial and technological developments are creating a greater need for workers with medium and high skills, but at the expense of less skilled people. rapid action is therefore needed, particularly in the case of young people: the continuing rise in youth unemployment is one of the most important challenges facing europe! to achieve these objectives, we believe it is essential that vocational education and training should remain a strong, long-term, political and common priority, the implementation of which will require the participation and commitment of all the actors concerned, the european institutions, but also local and regional actors.
mr president, it is very significant that with this resolution the european parliament is sending a strong signal to both the member states and the younger generations, calling for greater commitment to european cooperation in education, vocational training and higher education, in support of the europe 2020 strategy. we know that early unemployment has long-lasting effects on poverty and social exclusion, such as the prolonged precariousness in which 40% of young europeans live. a mix of training policies and a new wave of incentives for enterprises that employ young people and women on a permanent basis must be given a strong impetus. the adaptation of training skills to the skills needed also to those of citizenship to the new sustainable and intelligent development goals, as well as to the policies for the transition from training to work, is fundamental, including by accelerating the recognition of professional qualifications, qualifications and training credits. the member states which, like my own, cut resources to the education and research systems in times of crisis must know that they are working against young people and against the future of europe.
mr president, the report by mr garriga polledo is a very important piece of legislation which will help to define a new financial framework for a competitive, sustainable and inclusive europe. we need a budget adapted to the new challenges and a strong and innovative response to meet the new needs, with research and innovation for small and mediumsized enterprises, development and employment as the first objective; the second objective is the reform of the cap to promote and support the competitiveness of agriculture in europe. but the future of cohesion policy deserves special attention, as i consider it a very important instrument of financial support for investment in economic growth and, above all, in the creation of new jobs. i would like to stress one point which is particularly important to me in this connection: the establishment of a new intermediate category. i believe that the creation of this new category cannot be achieved by taking resources away from the existing categories, which are a necessary condition for promoting a balanced, harmonious and sustainable development of our communities.
mr president, my vote in favour of the garriga report on the next financial perspective of the union is based on the conviction that, at a time of the greatest crisis in the so-called european spirit, it is crucial to insist and win over the need to give the union credible instruments, starting with an adequate financial allocation. the request for an additional 5% for the next budget is therefore a right and necessary request, perhaps not sufficient, but indispensable in order to answer the big questions before us: the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the programme to include the following areas: without adequate resources, none of these problems will be sufficiently addressed, starting with the introduction of the intermediate category in cohesion policy, which makes sense only if it does not cause damage to the other existing categories. that is why i voted in favour of it and i hope that the commission and the council will follow the report's recommendations.
mr president, i am speaking to express my satisfaction but also to give reasons for voting in favour of the garriga report, which in some ways outlines serious and effective prospects for strengthening cohesion policy. we have expressed our concern by voting for the amendment to the directive on the introduction of an intermediate category in cohesion policies for those european areas which account for less than 90% to 75% of gross domestic product. we are very concerned, not because we do not think that attention should be directed towards cohesion policy, but because we believe that if there are no additional resources, this extension risks depriving, reducing resources for those areas included in objective 1, the 'convergence' objective, which are in great need of the attention and support of the european union. so, satisfaction with the report, satisfaction with the work done, some concern with a focus we would have had on a policy that could have confirmed the so-called 'facing out' as we are used to seeing it.
in writing. - i voted against the full application of the schengen provisions to romania and bulgaria. despite the overall positive assessment of the progress made by the two states in the field of security, the report itself admits that numerous technical and administrative deficiencies have been identified within the bodies responsible for ensuring the security of the borders of these two states, and in particular in the bodies responsible for the control and surveillance of maritime and land borders. secondly, the report admits that if the two states were included in the schengen area, their geographical location close to the turkish border would offer two new routes to illegal migration flows currently directed only to greece, which for now remains the only schengen state on the balkan peninsula. the accession of romania and bulgaria would thus considerably widen the eu's south-eastern 'achilles heel', tripling the pressure it is still under. the draft resolution is therefore in direct contradiction with the security needs of the citizen, which the lega nord has always placed at the heart of its political line, and i cannot support it.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr coelho's report on the application of the provisions of the schengen acquis in bulgaria and romania. romania and bulgaria adopted the schengen acquis in 2007 through their accession to the european union. article 4 (2) of the act of accession provides that verification of compliance by the new member states with the conditions necessary for the application of the schengen acquis is an essential requirement for the council to decide to abolish internal border controls with those states. the evaluations carried out show that both romania and bulgaria have demonstrated that they are sufficiently prepared to implement all the provisions of the schengen acquis in a satisfactory manner. i therefore share the rapporteur's call. i think, however, that we must not forget that the area in question is one of the most sensitive of the eu's external borders in terms of illegal migration. this makes it necessary to adopt some additional measures because, as is well known, the abolition of internal border controls requires a high level of mutual trust between member states and the existence of effective external border controls, as the security of the schengen area depends on the rigour and efficiency with which each member state carries out controls at its external borders.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i consider the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen acquis to be a very good step forward in the area of free movement of european citizens within the union, which is why i voted in favour of the application of the provisions in this area. i also believe that although both countries have committed themselves to the free movement of their citizens in europe, they must still continue to bring their controls and regulations up to european standards, given the sensitivity of europe's external borders in the balkan area.
in writing. − the balkan area is one of the most sensitive areas of the eu's external borders in terms of illegal migration. this is a far-reaching phenomenon which affects the daily lives of many of our citizens and increases their insecurity. before any entry into the schengen area of bulgaria and romania can be considered, special and detailed plans to contain migratory pressures must be prepared. the improvement of external border controls must also be accompanied by a fight against corruption in local authorities. for these reasons and to protect our citizens better against illegal immigration, i voted against this measure.
in writing. - article 4 (2) of the act of accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen acquis states that the essential condition for abolishing internal border controls with these countries is verification of compliance with the schengen requirements themselves. since both romania and bulgaria have demonstrated that they are sufficiently prepared to implement all the provisions of the acquis in a satisfactory manner, both member states should be fully integrated into the area. i would stress, however, the importance for internal security of strict controls at the external borders. as bulgaria is in a sensitive area in terms of illegal migration, it needs to take additional measures to respond to any increase in migratory pressure at its borders.
in writing. − the bulgaria-turkey-greece area is one of the most sensitive areas of the eu's external borders in terms of illegal migration. i disagree with the rapporteur because the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area cannot be achieved in the short term, as there are shortcomings in the areas of instruments, the implementation of border controls, staff training and the obligation to exchange data.
in writing. - while expressing some doubts about the excessive length of the text (which falls within the europe 2020 strategy), i consider the objectives of the resolution broadly compatible and therefore voted in favour of mr coelho's text on verifying compliance with the conditions for the application of the schengen acquis as an essential requirement for the abolition of internal border controls with bulgaria and romania.
in writing. - we are witnessing radical changes in the international order in recent months, changes which can no longer see the european union as a mere spectator. i believe that the european union should take inspiration from this and take a really active role in dealing with both the existing and the emerging world powers, and once and for all shed the label of 'political dwarf' in international politics. in this sense i support the need, expressed in mr lambsdorff's proposal, for the member states to make an effort to secure a permanent seat for the european union in the discussions on the reform of the security council. strengthening the role of the european union in the united nations will ensure that the eu plays a leading role as a regional and global actor, otherwise we will continue to face the continuing lack of coordination of member states' interests on the international stage.
in writing. − i strongly supported the main thrust of this report. it calls for an enhanced role for the eu in the un system taking into account the institutional changes brought by the lisbon treaty. today’s vote comes after a relevant success for the eu in the un: the adoption of a set of modalities granting the eu delegation in the un general assembly the right to make interventions, as well as the right of reply and the ability to present oral proposals and amendments. these improvement reflect a clear reality: the eu and its member states are the biggest financial contributors to the un system, with eu funds amounting to 38% of the un regular budget, more than two fifths of un peacekeeping operations and close to half of the contributions to the un funds and programmes. moreover, the eu, in spite of all its limitations, is a major global actor whose weight must be properly recognised at every level.
in writing. - i support this proposal for a parliament recommendation to the council on the forthcoming session of the united nations general assembly. the proposal underlines that the european union and the united nations share a common commitment to promoting democracy, respect for human rights and peace in the international community. the proposal argues that further enlargement of the un security council to include the eu is a key factor in the effective pursuit of the above objectives. the proposal rejects germany's request to occupy the eu's new potential seat at the un permanently, and welcomes italy's proposal to allow all member states to rotate the seat in order to protect the principle of equal dignity between member states. the german request was seen as an attempt to impose the political authority of germany and the anglo-french-german axis inside and outside the eu, but the adoption of the italian position by the present proposal confirms that the eventual enlargement of the security council would also ensure that italy would have the opportunity to make its voice heard on crucial issues of the international order outside the eu. my vote is therefore in favour.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this document sets out the european union's priorities to be presented to the united nations general assembly. the key point that has been under discussion for some time is the discussion on the reform of the security council. the proposal for a seat for the european union and perhaps a rotating one between the member states seems to be a very good one. the report is therefore supported.
in writing. − the current shift in the international order is spurring the eu to engage more actively with world and emerging powers in order to play a proactive role in building a un that can actually contribute to global solutions: the european union is committed to peace, security, democracy and an international order based on the rule of law. an essential starting point for tackling climate change and environmental degradation, the universality and indivisibility of human rights, poverty reduction and development for all, the consequences of demographic change, migration, international organised crime. thanks to the treaty of lisbon, we now have new permanent structures for external representation. this allows us to assume an international role commensurate with our pre-eminent economic status, acting as a global actor, able to share responsibility for world security. it is up to us to identify clearly our interests and strategic objectives in order to be able to act effectively. the eu is the world's largest provider of development aid, and is an important partner of the un in crisis and post-crisis situations; we therefore believe that effective multilateralism must be pursued as the union's main strategic interest in order to strengthen its coherence and visibility on the international scene.
in writing. - with regard to the 66th session of the united nations general assembly, i support the position that the european parliament should urge the council to play a leading role in promoting the millennium development goals. a debate needs to be launched on how to support the international community's commitment to sustainable development and poverty eradication, and this effort needs to continue beyond 2015. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. − despite a number of negative factors, such as the economic crisis, the persistent gap with the us and increasing competition from emerging economies, fp7 has proved capable of adding value to european research and development. fp7 offers the european union the opportunity to match its research policy with its economic and social ambitions, in particular by consolidating the european research area. i share the objectives of the mid-term review in mr audy's report, in particular the simplification of administrative procedures, the participation of smes through the cooperation programme, innovation and the intensification of the risk-sharing financing mechanism. these measures will allow the europeanisation of research in the context of the negotiation of the financial perspective from 2014 onwards.
in writing. − in march 2000, the european council set the union an ambitious target of: to become, in 2010, 'the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world'. the central role of research has been recognised in this strategy. i believe that examining the review of the 7th framework programme for research and technological development is an opportunity to strengthen the valuable link between knowledge, education and research. over the years, fp7 has become one of the world's leading research support programmes, the main instrument of eu research policy and an opportunity for the union to match its research policy with its economic and social ambitions by consolidating the european research area. in particular, i believe that there are two main aspects on which this review should focus: overcome the difficulties associated with the burden and complexity of administrative procedures, which result in researchers giving up european funding in favour of national funding. moreover, despite the progress made in recent years, the participation of small and medium-sized enterprises in the framework programme should be further strengthened in order to develop the knowledge that will enable them to improve their competitiveness.
in writing. - the report by mr audy on the mid-term report on the eu's seventh framework programme for research, technological development and demonstration activities certainly has some points of agreement, such as the view that the programme has had a low success rate, especially in relation to smes, or the request for a reduction in grant grant delivery times. however, i abstained because the own-initiative report contained a point which i considered particularly weak and which prevented me from voting in favour. in particular, i do not support the rapporteur's call for increased funding for the erc, including by making it an independent legal entity with decision-making powers directly responsible for its scientific strategy and administrative management.
in writing. - the unanimous vote in committee on this important report and today's vote once again demonstrate that parliament can take a strong and clear position on vital issues for citizens and businesses. i think that the report clearly highlights the critical points of the seventh framework programme and makes some good proposals to ensure that the funds that remain to be allocated can really be used to increase competitiveness and excellence in the european market. in my view, simplifying administrative procedures and bureaucratic burdens remains the most important challenge if we are to make it possible for our enterprises, especially small and mediumsized enterprises, to access finance. through these funds, we need to improve system capacity, by improving public-private partnerships, by rewarding clusters between regions and by providing for strong coordination between cohesion funds and those directed at research and innovation.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the seventh framework programme of the european community for research, technological development and demonstration activities (fp7) is the largest instrument of support for research worldwide and is the main instrument of eu research policy. the measures taken so far to develop knowledge in a wide variety of fields demonstrate the ever-greater need to move towards the dissemination of innovations and their implementation in the daily lives of each of us. it is precisely the proximity of this tool to everyday human activities that has made me favourable to the report by my colleague audy, with the hope that future innovation policies will make the best use of synergies across the entire r & d value chain. at present, the 7th framework programme, which is mainly focused on research and technological development, is the only instrument to achieve the objectives set out in the 'innovation union' and to accelerate europe's transformation into a knowledge-based society. thinking about the future of innovation means creating jobs, harnessing the capital of research and translating it into practical applications in real life and exploiting the potential of human resources, all of which are factors that must be included in the next framework programme.
in writing. − the 7th framework programme for research and technological development has become over the years one of the most important support programmes in the world and is the main instrument of the european union's research policy. following the failure of the so-called 'lisbon strategy' which envisaged the eu as the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world by 2010, it was decided to examine whether the revision of fp7 is an opportunity to consolidate the golden triangle: the european union is a global player in the field of education. we believe that fp7 is an opportunity for the eu to match its research policy with its economic and social ambitions, in particular by consolidating the european research area (era). it is also necessary to territorialise research and development policies and for the union to adopt an ambitious european defence technology research plan, strengthening the industrial and technological base of the sector and improving the effectiveness of public military spending. finally, we agree with the committee on budgets that the design and implementation of all the fpis must be based on the principles of simplicity, stability, legal certainty, consistency, excellence and trust, strengthening the links between european research institutes and industry.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr audy's report because in order to achieve and align with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, the seventh framework programme needs a complete overhaul. the need for a review of priorities was given by a negative mid-term evaluation; i therefore agree with the reformulation of the main objectives, stressing the need for a more effective research policy which eliminates the burdens of administrative procedures and provides for greater participation of smes, innovation and integration of funding. these changes are intended to ensure the success of projects under the second phase of the seventh framework programme.
in writing. − a review of fp7 is needed to further align the fp7 programme with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. to make european research policy more competitive and to meet its economic and social ambitions, fp7 needs to be adapted to four major objectives: promote the simplification of the research framework programmes by removing the burden of administrative procedures; improving the participation of smes; reinforce the innovation dimension; pursue and strengthen the risk-sharing financing mechanism. the importance of collaboration between academia, public research bodies and the 'industrial sector' should also be emphasised. we need to pay more attention to proposals for research collaborations between the public and industrial sectors, facilitate collaboration between networks of smes, universities and public research bodies, and include among the main parameters in the selection of fp7 projects the assessment of possible market impact, technology transfer and commercial exploitation of research results. for these reasons, and in order to make the eu more competitive in research, without having to wait for fp8, i am voting in favour of a revision of fp7.
in writing. − research is an essential element of the world of knowledge and an activity designed to strengthen the growth and employment of the european union in a globalised economy. the seventh framework programme for research is a good opportunity for the european union to develop research policy while consolidating the european research area (era). through this programme, europe aims to meet the research and knowledge needs of industry and more generally of european policies. the european parliament, by adopting today's report, underlines the results achieved by the research programme in its first four years. to achieve more and better results in the future, administrative simplification, encouraging sme participation, supporting innovation and adopting risk-sharing financing mechanisms will be necessary. the eu and its member states are also invited to adopt an ambitious research plan with the aim of consolidating the european defence industry.
in writing. - relations with canada have long been mutually beneficial, and from a commercial point of view they are a relationship of mutual interest and good cooperation. despite being an advanced country, where there is little doubt that social rights and the most advanced environmental standards are being respected, the commission, even before parliament, has laid the basis for negotiations with its canadian counterpart on many specific points and issues which we must be satisfied with. my vote is in favour of a resolution on a chapter of the european trade policy agenda which should be taken as a model when dealing with countries such as india, china and pakistan, which certainly do not guarantee fair competition like canada, let alone respect for social rights and environmental standards. when we go to negotiate with these countries, we should remember how precise and punctual we have been with very civilised realities like canada and adopt the same linear and open conduct in defence of our interests.
in writing. − trade relations between the european union and canada can go well beyond the commitments made in the world trade organization, provided that they are based on a balanced agreement, the guarantee of genuine reciprocal market access and improved protection of trademarks, patents and geographical indications. we believe that new investments are needed which respect the environment and promote good working conditions. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. finally, we believe that the council must obtain parliament's consent before signing any new international trade agreement and that our institution must be informed at all stages of the procedure in order to ensure greater democratic control of the procedure. only then can there be greater growth in trade and investment between the european union and canada.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr klinz's draft report on credit rating agencies because i believe that the text contains many positive elements and points. in particular, i agree with the desire to improve the transparency, integrity, accountability, independence and reliability of these agencies. i also share the rapporteur's view that a european credit rating agency should be set up, independent of the governments and institutions, and that oligopoly is a problem for the sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it clearly and objectively expresses the situation regarding credit rating agencies. i too believe that they play a necessary and very useful role in summarizing and simplifying the flow of information on financial markets, both in terms of the solvency and reliability of debt issuers and in terms of individual financial instruments. however, as the rapporteur rightly pointed out, the business model risks diverting attention from investor protection to that of the debt issuer, if appropriate corrective measures are not taken. i do not think that the competitive situation can improve, as the proliferation of agencies could undermine the credibility of the rating; i think that greater responsibility can be translated into greater objectivity and more rigorous work, not to protect the interests of a few, but to reduce information asymmetries, that is to say, the functioning of the markets and therefore the general interest.
in writing. the european parliament takes a further step towards greater transparency in financial markets by endorsing the klinz report, which calls for effective regulation of credit rating agencies. it is important to overcome the current problems in the sector: the lack of competition, the excessive regulatory reliance on ratings, and the unreliability of ratings. in this connection, the european parliament's request to the commission to consider the establishment of an independent european agency which could also be responsible for the valuation of sovereign debts is significant. in the reform work currently under way, which will be completed in the autumn, it will be of great importance to review the role of the agencies in the valuation of sovereign debts, since often the irresponsible behaviour of the latter has been the first cause of speculation, ultimately harming european taxpayers above all.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the resolution adopted today contains a number of measures to reduce the current dependence on very few rating agencies. these measures include increased and timely use of the internal credit rating, in particular by large financial institutions with the capacity to carry out their own risk assessments, but also increased competition. it is certainly a theme which has seen us, in the preparatory stages, somewhat disaggregated but which in the final positions gathers a lot of agreement. this sharing also goes into the transparency issue as i am in favour of all registered credit rating agencies conducting an annual review to assess their own credit rating performance and then passing this information on to the supervisory authorities.
in writing. the recent financial crisis has highlighted three main problems affecting credit rating agencies: lack of competition, due to the lack of relevance of credit rating agencies in global capital markets and the inability to compete, especially in regulatory standards; the commission is also proposing to support the establishment of a european network of credit rating agencies. the commission is also proposing to support the establishment of a european network of credit rating agencies. in this connection, we support the importance of better information to investors and of allowing market participants to invest in derivative financial instruments only if they can demonstrate that they are able to understand and assess the credit risk involved in the product. finally, we agree on the possibility of establishing a fully independent and non-public european credit rating foundation (ecraf).
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the work of credit rating agencies is important as a guarantee of reliability and stability, so it is necessary to establish rules and criteria for their ratings and their impartiality. i voted in favour of mr klinz's text because i believe it is essential that the european union should have adequate rules to manage the impact of ratings on the whole financial and economic system. despite the regulatory vacuum in this area and the possibility for these agencies to influence the economies of the member states to the point of causing them to collapse, this report is nevertheless the first step towards new regulation of credit rating agencies, in view of the recent approval by the commission of the new cra regulation.
in writing. − this measure is a final expression of support for improving the activities of rating agencies by increasing their transparency, integrity, accountability, independence and reliability. while recognising the role of agencies in providing information and stimulating liquidity in markets, it is now clear that financial operators have relied too much on their judgment and that their actions have contributed to the financial crisis. there is an excessive reliance on external credit rating agencies and an oligopoly in the sector. i therefore support the establishment of an independent european credit rating foundation responsible for rating in the public, corporate and structured finance sectors.
in writing. - i congratulate mr klinz on his excellent work. i would urge the rating agencies to be more clear about how they calibrate their sovereign ratings, asking the industry to explain their methodologies and why their ratings differ from the forecasts of the major international financial institutions. another controversial point concerns the structure to be proposed to counterbalance at european level the three major rating agencies, which are considered to be too dominant on the european scene. i therefore call on the commission to undertake a detailed assessment for a fully independent credit rating agency with initial funding to cover at most the first five years of operation. finally, it is essential to examine how credit rating agencies can be held liable for the information they provide, and i ask the commission to identify ways in which credit rating agencies can be held liable under the civil law of the member states.
in writing. the main objective of the resolution adopted today is to eliminate the dependence on external credit assessments from the whole system as far as possible and within a realistic timeframe. the role of external evaluations as a determining criterion is particularly relevant when it comes to downgrading an investment category to a lower one. in a well-functioning and competitive market, the reputation of an agency should be sufficient to guarantee the quality of the ratings issued. however, since credit rating agencies operate in an oligopoly during this period, they benefit from a market which is 'guaranteed' by its very nature.
in writing. − the financial crisis of recent years has highlighted the three main problems affecting the sector: lack of competition, over-reliance on the regulatory framework for external ratings and lack of agency accountability for the credit ratings they issue. i voted in favour of mr klinz's report because i think it is a valid and interesting idea to set up a completely independent and non-public european credit rating agency.
in writing. − the report on the external dimension of social policy relates to a priority for the eu social policies. it calls for the strengthening of the core labour standards embedded in the ilo conventions, including freedom of association and collective bargaining, elimination of forced and compulsory labour, elimination of discrimination in respect of employment and occupation, and the abolition of child labour. i voted in favour of this report because it also calls for a change in governance, globally and in the eu, in order to better implement workers’ rights and working conditions.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the external dimension of social policy includes the union's initiatives aimed at promoting social and labour standards in third countries. the european union, by adopting labour standards, promotes the possibility for citizens to obtain work in conditions of freedom, equality, safety and dignity. in the current phase of globalisation of the world economy, international labour standards represent the basis on which to build a country's social and economic growth. china, india and other emerging economies are increasingly important players in the foreign investment landscape. however, this phenomenon is associated with the risk that these countries and, in particular, their enterprises, export labour standards that are less stringent than those within the union. i therefore believe that the european union must take a cautious approach to third countries which wish to conclude trade agreements with it. european smes are the main actors in the implementation of social standards. i believe it is of the utmost importance to have a clear and unambiguous definition of corporate social responsibility which prevents the current diversity of interpretation while at the same time laying down the procedures for ensuring that it is respected.
in writing. - i would like to support the report by mr falbr, which recognises the strategic importance of corporate social responsibility as a motivating tool for stimulating growth and stresses that the approach to this subject should be voluntary. i also fully share the rapporteur's critical approach, which disapproves of the european union's hypocritical behaviour in promoting a social model that is sensitive to social rights on the one hand and concluding trade agreements with countries that do not respect or provide for protection for workers on the other.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, one of the fundamental objectives of the eu is to combine human and social development with economic development. their balanced relationship allows people to do their jobs with adequate remuneration that respects human dignity and professional quality, and allows entrepreneurs to pursue the development of their businesses in accordance with market logic, tempered by the human dimension in which they must develop. this perspective, which some also call the social market economy, is actually a new paradigm that goes beyond the welfare economy and reorients itself to the centrality of the human person. this reorientation must include consistent support for social policy, including the promotion of social standards and the associated responsibility of enterprises. this approach and vision cannot and must not only be applied to the internal eu environment, but also to external action, at all times, in particular when agreements are being negotiated. respect for the rules of the ilo, the principles of the european social charter and the social dialogue are just some of the issues that can be developed on such occasions. i think the report we have adopted is a good support for these objectives.
in writing. - the desire for new things, which has been shaking the states for some time, would eventually result in the desire for change moving from the political order to the adjacent sector of the economy. i quote the beloved pope john paul ii, who, taking up the themes dealt with by his predecessor leo xiii in the encyclical rerum novarum, in the encyclical centesimus annus, analyses and intervenes on the social 'question', which in 1991 as today must find a solution in christian doctrine, that is, in the recognition of the dignity of the human being, of the worker, without any distinction. i voted in favour of mr falbr's report because it stresses the importance of safeguarding human rights and the fact that the european social model is an important starting point for the union's external relations. social responsibility must work in this direction and the european union, through its parliament, must recover and strengthen these principles in all its actions and especially towards third countries whose citizens do not enjoy fundamental rights. as vice-president of the femm commission, i cannot fail to stress the importance for all of us to cooperate also externally to eliminate gender discrimination and gender-based violence, so as to recover the social dignity of women and their active contribution to the growth of the local economy as a supranational.
in writing. − the external dimension of eu social policy aims to promote social standards in third countries, but competitiveness issues and economic factors continue to override social and labour issues. we have eight ilo conventions so far, ratified by all the eu member states. these lead to the production of a common base of international standards for all member states. it is still necessary to focus on people in general as human beings, and this is possible with the protection of workers' rights and the right to work. the ilo plays a key role at international level in the construction, promotion and effective implementation of these standards. companies must also contribute to sustainable development in order to promote quality conditions for workers, but the difference between developed and developing countries persists in their social protection systems. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the social dimension. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this.
in writing. - a company can be socially responsible if it adopts a solid model that takes into account not only the economic, but also the social and environmental impacts of its actions. today, people are not only asking how companies achieve their economic results, but also who they hire and how they treat their staff. a responsible company is an active and aware of the social reality in which it operates and which makes the relationship with all the parties involved in its activity the source of greatest wealth. the report adopted today commits the european union to playing a leading role in social policy worldwide by promoting global objectives, and underlines the importance of the role of the european parliament under the lisbon treaty.
in writing. - i am in favour of the own-initiative report as it deals with the promotion of corporate social responsibility as a voluntary motivational tool to stimulate company growth. european enterprises are the engine of the eu economy: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. i am also in favour of the creation of socially responsible enterprises in which the key principles are the social protection of workers, consumer protection and compliance with transparency laws.
