in writing. - i am voting against a report which, by proposing an optional legal instrument on contract law, is in fact laying the foundations for a future european civil law, which will take precedence over national civil law. this would mean the end of national legal traditions and of the rules which each state has established for itself in such sensitive matters as civil law and contract law. however, if the objective of introducing an optional instrument is to facilitate trade while taking due account of the needs of consumers and businesses, it is sufficient to recall that the existing regulations at european level can already meet the requirements of the various stakeholders. the real aim of the report, therefore, seems to be the more ambitious one of creating a european civil code, which i cannot agree with.
in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur on her work, for which i gave her a positive vote. this report responds to the needs of consumers and smes, who, unlike other players representing larger economies, have obvious problems accessing the internal market because they face enormous costs. as a direct consequence, both smes and consumers tend to carry out their transactions within the domestic market, which is often much less competitive and therefore does not have access to the cross-border market, which often offers a product at a cost up to 10% lower than the national offer. differences in the law of contracts must be eliminated and the creation of an optional instrument for european contract law by means of a regulation, which would not replace but would be alongside the contract law of the individual states, is an excellent solution which would allow the parties to choose freely the legal instrument most suited to their needs.
in writing. − differences in european contract law end up discouraging businesses from engaging in cross-border trade and preventing them from benefiting from the opportunities and benefits of the internal market. as a result, consumers are also disadvantaged by the limited product range, higher prices and lower quality due to low cross-border competition. in this connection we are proposing to introduce some new features, such as: contracts between undertakings and those between undertakings and consumers governed by an optional instrument that will broaden their choices; the introduction of a monitoring and review mechanism to ensure that the optional instrument responds to market needs and legal and economic developments. the key objectives will be simplicity and immediate use; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. finally, the introduction of a trust mark system would ensure greater protection for consumers themselves. choosing the right prospects for the future in the field of contract law can make an important contribution to improving the functioning of the internal market itself and its full potential not only for businesses but also for consumers.
in writing. − the diversity of contractual rights in the member states creates structural problems which discourage businesses and consumers. the motion for a resolution tabled by mrs wallis is in favour of the creation of an optional instrument for european consumer and business contract law through a generic regulation, which is why i voted in favour of the text. moreover, this would not replace the contract law of the member states but would only support better choice of the contract model between the parties through examples based on general principles, definitions and model rules for both commercial and consumer contracts, without going against the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr wallis. the problems arising from the diversity of contract rights in the member states very often discourage businesses, especially smes, from engaging in cross-border trade, effectively preventing them from taking advantage of the opportunities offered by the internal market. the text voted today aims to create an optional instrument for european contract law by means of a regulation: the commission has also proposed that the court of justice should rule on the question of the interpretation of the treaty by the court of justice.
in writing. - mr president, gdp, which was devised in the 1930s, is the best-known measure of macroeconomic activity, used by policy-makers in debates as an indicator of their country's growth. at present, in the light of the increasing interdependence between economic, social and environmental issues, gdp is beginning to show many weaknesses as it does not record important social factors such as welfare, social inclusion, climate change or resource efficiency. therefore, in a context where the correlation between a range of non-market activities and gdp is no longer automatic, it is necessary to develop clear and measurable additional indicators in the medium and long term, which ensure comparability between countries and regions and which can be used to develop projections on future developments and to define targeted policies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it stresses the importance of agreeing on a systemic approach to setting up a coherent ‘beyond gdp system’ to contribute to improved policy analysis. gdp is an indicator of economic activity that has become a standard benchmark used by policy-makers throughout the world. but gdp is only a measure of production. it does not measure environmental sustainability, resource efficiency, social inclusion and social progress in general. therefore it can be misleading. we need to measure quality of life in societies; we need to consider that achieving and sustaining quality of life involves important, consensual factors such as health, education, culture, employment, housing, environmental conditions, etc. for these reasons this report deserves to be given the highest consideration. it takes the view that indicators which measure such factors should be assigned a greater role.
in writing. - the gross domestic product, devised in the 1930s and known as the most established unit of measurement of macroeconomic activity, is considered a global indicator of overall social development and progress in general. a number of international initiatives have highlighted the broad consensus among policy makers, economic and environmental experts and civil society on the development of indicators to complement gdp in order to support decision-making with more complete information. gdp is not a reliable basis for policy debate: it measures neither environmental sustainability nor social inclusion. in the political and scientific debate which has been going on for years, the problem, in my view, is rather how to achieve this approach through clearly defined and quantifiable indicators. a number of initiatives have been launched at eu and member state level to address gaps in these areas, but it remains difficult to identify a coherent approach. therefore, while recognising the importance of adopting a clearly defined unit of gdp, i would urge the commission to first present a phased strategy outlining how to apply the new 'not just gdp' approach in the day-to-day work of policy makers.
in writing. the report by mrs rosbach provides a critical analysis of the commission communication 'not just gdp - measuring progress in a changing world'. the commission's objective - to adopt a unit of measurement that goes beyond gdp to take a more comprehensive view of a country's development and progress, including for example environmental sustainability and social inclusion - is important and not controversial, but the rapporteur questions the commission's proposed strategy for achieving it. the suggested initiatives are not integrated into a gradual and pragmatic strategy that indicates how the new 'not just gdp' approach should be used. it's a perspective i share: i therefore voted in favour of mrs rosbach's report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that only with the right tools can we get a realistic view of the situation and then do our best to be able to change it if necessary. gdp, or gross domestic product, is a measure designed to indicate the aggregate value added of all economic activities, which are based on money. it is easy to see how a wealth indicator based on outdated parameters, today, in 2011, is anachronistic. i think it is appropriate to introduce new measures of gdp assessment, such as environmental sustainability or social inclusion, in order to obtain from the set of data constituting gdp a more authentic picture of the country or region to which it relates. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council at the next meeting of the european council in brussels. i believe that by introducing clear and definite indicators the work can be done in the best possible way.
in writing. - the economic literature has for years been debating whether or not to continue to use the gdp growth rate as a measure of the progress made by a geographical area over a given period of time. i do not think there is any indicator at present that is as concise and complete. we cannot present to our citizens, who are immersed in their daily problems, a medical record to describe the state of the economy. at the same time, it is not possible to insist on strictly economic measures which are not always able to take account of social phenomena. i therefore agree with the general aim of the report: let's join our efforts with those of the international academic community and try to surpass gdp. there are dozens of examples around the world, from the united nations development programme's human development index, to the gross national happiness of the kingdom of bhutan. priority objectives must be identified and their achievement measured in a rigorous, timely manner and not subject to bias based on vested interests. let us remember that it is not how many watches we have that matters, but how we spend our time.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, indicators are a way of reading a given phenomenon in a synthetic way. simple phenomena can be read through simple indicators, while complex phenomena require complex indicators to read. gdp is a simple indicator, while development is a complex phenomenon. in fact, the economic development of a territory has several profiles that are not contained in gdp, which also photographs a given moment, while other elements of reading are totally omitted, such as investments in intangible infrastructure, including knowledge (people, processes, products, just to name a few), or investments in tangible infrastructure, including communication and transport networks (ict networks, road and rail networks, to name a few). moreover, gdp is not adequate for the identification of the regions assisted by the eu's regional cohesion policy either. it is for these reasons that the european commission's effort to go beyond gdp and create a set of data and indicators that improve the ability to read phenomena and help to better define policies and financial allocations is to be welcomed. the report we have approved seems to me to be moving in that direction.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission's aim of going beyond gdp, that is to say of finding another unit of measurement (which, however, would be integrated into it), is rightly criticised in the report by parliament, which stresses that if the commission has not yet defined precisely the transition and the precise indicators, the debate will have to be postponed. the position is therefore in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - gdp, or gross domestic product, is the most widely known macroeconomic unit used in policy analysis and debate around the world to indicate social development. unfortunately, despite its widespread use, there is a growing awareness that the economic and social fabric of europe has changed profoundly. now, in addition to income and wealth information, other environmental indicators affect a country's standard of living and cannot be ignored any further. that is why i support mrs rosbach's report, which sets out new indicators which take account of the broad lines of environmental policy such as energy use, biodiversity, water use and waste generation. the challenge is to complement existing indices with other politically relevant and empirically measurable elements that provide reliable statistics on future developments in countries. in this sense, i believe that by eliminating subjective factors such as personal happiness, which cannot be regarded as indicators, the new text has reached a valid compromise. finally, i hope that both eurostat and the eurobarometer will play a key role in this innovative process. thank you for your attention.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the analysis of the rapporteur in the report voted on today. the gross domestic product no longer seems to be able to meet the growing economic and political needs. i believe that we must identify a possible complementary instrument which can help to improve policy analysis and debate by using clear additional indicators capable of detecting and measuring economic and social progress in the medium and long term. this is certainly not an easy task, given the sensitivity of the matter and the impact that decisions taken in this context can have. the challenge we are about to face is therefore to find reliable indicators that are both theoretically consistent, politically relevant and empirically measurable.
in writing. - gross domestic product is no longer a sufficient and appropriate indicator to measure progress and there is therefore a need to develop more comprehensive indicators that provide a more reliable knowledge base in an increasingly changing world. clearly defined information, data and indicators are often lacking. a number of initiatives have been taken at eu and member state level to address the gaps identified. although it is difficult to identify a method which is at the same time coherent, we believe that a global approach is necessary which takes account of existing measures and which can be applied in political practice. a new tool needs to be developed that can complement gdp, that can be used in practice and that is based on clearly defined indicators and high-quality data. we agree with the rapporteur that a step-by-step strategy is needed, which shows how to apply the new approach in a pragmatic way in day-to-day political work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr rosbach on 'not just gdp - measuring progress in a changing world' because i believe that gdp is no longer sufficient and appropriate to measure progress in a changing world and that more comprehensive indicators are needed, which provide a more reliable knowledge base. it should be remembered that gdp is a measure of production and does not measure, for example, environmental sustainability. other indicators need to be developed to give an idea of the factors affecting a country's standard of living. i am therefore in favour of the creation of new indicators to measure social and economic progress in the medium and long term, for example indicators that take account of climate change, biodiversity, resource efficiency and social inclusion. the development of these new indicators also helps to understand and measure the quality of life in societies. the development of a member state or a given region cannot therefore be measured merely by an economic indicator such as gdp, but also by the quality of life, which is determined by factors such as health, education, culture, employment, housing and climatic and environmental conditions.
in writing. − "not just gdp measuring progress in a changing world". a report which attempts to assess the level of progress of the union through that global indicator of social and economic development which is the gross domestic product. unfortunately, gdp is no longer a reliable basis for policy debate because it cannot measure environmental sustainability or social inclusion on its own. the need for improved data and indicators to complement the criteria for assessing progress is becoming increasingly evident, which is why i voted in favour of a text which seeks to integrate the development of the european union with new social indicators, which seeks a definite unit of measurement that goes beyond gdp and complements it in the context of the decision-making process.
in writing. - mr president, gdp is the most widely used unit of measurement in the world. this is considered a global indicator of overall social development and progress in general, but it does not take into account either the calculation of environmental sustainability or social inclusion. we must try to improve the data and indicators to complement gdp, or it will fail to provide a reliable basis for policy debate. this topic has already been discussed in the past years and in particular in 2007 the european parliament and the commission, together with institutions and associations, organised a conference entitled 'more than gdp'. at that meeting, the commission argued that gdp is not an adequate long-term measurement system, and that economic and social progress are not sufficient to assess issues such as climate change, resource efficiency or personal well-being, and subsequently proposed new indicators to assess progress in achieving social, economic and environmental objectives. for the reasons stated above and in order to develop a set of indicators which are clear and comprehensive but also coherent, relevant and objectively measurable, i am voting in favour of the proposal under consideration.
in writing. - this report proposes the adoption of a clearly defined unit of measurement to complement gdp as an indicator of overall social development. the complementary tool should have a practical use and be based on clearly defined indicators and reliable data. only then can gdp provide a sufficient contribution to the political debate and decision-making process. the commission is therefore invited to present a comprehensive and phased strategy which will illustrate the new approach in a pragmatic way in day-to-day political work.
in writing. − the report on the commission communication of 20 august 2009 'more than gdp - measuring progress in a changing world' highlights the importance of gdp as a global indicator of social development and economic growth. the aim is to adopt a new unit of measurement that is clearly defined and quantifiable on the basis of reliable and truthful data, but the communication to the commission does not indicate the step-by-step strategy for achieving this. i am in favour of the report because i believe it is important to make socioeconomic analyses with appropriate instruments to complement gdp.
in writing. - today i spoke in favour of identifying new parameters which are more representative of a country's progress, and not just its consumption, although i believe more should be done. the report in question has had a long and contentious process, after which it arrived at the plenary with nothing of substance. parliament should have put forward a proposal which took account of factors such as education, health, personal activities and others, but instead it merely stressed the need to set new standards, and asked the commission to set them. gdp is an outdated indicator, based on economic principles which, reducing quality to quantity, do not take into account the meaning of things, individual and collective well-being, underestimate work itself in relation to the object of production and do not consider maintenance, but only the production of new objects.
in writing. the project to implement a european satellite navigation programme is a major challenge and certainly useful for the future of technology in europe, but at present the estimates of expenditure and investment by the community bodies for this project are still unclear and not very transparent. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question. i therefore abstain on the final vote on the own-initiative report.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mrs ţicău's report because the project in question meets many of the expectations of those who are optimistic about the development of research and technology. egnos and galileo are projects that will produce around eur 60 billion in positive externalities for the eu economy and society, in terms of improved road and air safety, reduced air pollution and pesticide consumption, new job creation and improved public safety, generating very high value for money. it therefore requires the commission to present a clear assessment of all possible technical options and possible costs and benefits in the ante phase, i.e. before a decision is taken on further financial commitments from the eu budget in the next multiannual financial framework.
in writing. − we believe that the global navigation satellite system (gnss) developed by the european union, consisting of galileo and egnos, is an important step for europe as it guarantees autonomy and independence from other global navigation systems and, secondly, the possibility to participate in the fast-growing high-tech market worldwide. it is very important, however, to ensure continuity of service, as a (temporary) limitation or degradation of gps signals can have enormous effects on the economy and society, without other independent gnss systems. however, to fully exploit the benefits of galileo, full operational capacity needs to be achieved and further investment will be required to do so. the financial picture is far from positive at present. at this point we believe that a broad and comprehensive political debate is needed on the level of ambition desired and the financial resources available. finally, we support the importance of launching a comprehensive analysis aimed at defining more precisely the possible scenarios and means for operation and exploitation after 2013, which includes all the commercial aspects as well as the legal, contractual and financial structures of the different models capable of implementing a stable governance model.
in writing. − the galileo system will improve the accuracy and reliability of the us global positioning system (gps) information. this new system will be important in giving the eu autonomy and independence from other global navigation systems and in allowing it to participate in the fast-growing high-tech market worldwide. as you know, the programme is fully funded by the union budget with an allocation of eur 3.4 billion until 2014. it is known that the indirect benefits of the programme are estimated at around €60 billion per year, but the commission has admitted that further investment will be needed to make the system operational. since it is not clear how much the galileo system will cost the taxpayer, i have abstained on this measure, also to reiterate the request to the commission to clarify the future costs of the project.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i share the importance of the galileo project as part of a comprehensive european satellite navigation system. it ensures the union's autonomy and independence from other global navigation systems and allows it to participate in the high-technology market, which is growing rapidly worldwide. given that competitors are growing stronger and advancing dynamically, and that full operational capacity is needed to take full advantage of galileo, the project requires further investment, to the extent indicated by the rapporteur.
in writing. - mr president, after almost a year of work by the special committee on political challenges and budgetary resources, the future decisions on spending priorities for an effective and efficient use of community appropriations for the implementation of results-oriented policies have finally been presented. bearing in mind that the eu budget is primarily an investment budget, capable of generating additional investment from public and private sources, it is necessary that it can be appropriately aligned with changing circumstances and priorities. the decision to increase the resources of the new multiannual financial framework by 5% will ensure the stability of the existing programming cycles and the launching of new investments in areas such as the european energy and transport networks, which will in turn enable europe to defend its competitiveness and prepare the ground for long-term economic growth. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new eu-us partnership agreement on the environment, which is expected to be signed in the near future.
in writing. − mr president, the report on a new multiannual financial framework (mff) for a competitive, sustainable and inclusive europe is a valuable piece of collective analysis on the future configurations of the eu budget. it estimates the financial resources needed for the union to attain its objectives and carry out its policies for the period starting 1 january 2014. its essential point is a request for an increase of at least 5% in the total eu budget for 2013, and the request for the introduction of an autonomous source of funding. the report stresses very clearly that without sufficient additional resources in the post-2013 mff, the union will not be able to fulfil the existing policy priorities, linked in particular to the europe 2020 strategy, or the new tasks provided for by the treaty of lisbon, let alone respond to unforeseen events. i voted in favour of this report also because it calls for a more transparent, simpler and fairer financing system for the european union.
in writing. - i vote against mr polledo's report on certain points which i consider to be critical in the proposal put to the vote. although some paragraphs are shared, such as the one on the reduction of the european parliament to a single seat, the report calls for the introduction of a genuine european tax to finance the activities of the eu. there is talk of funding for roma communities, a subject which my political training has always opposed, there is talk of substantial spending forecasts for further eu enlargement in the western balkans area, another point on which i disagree. finally, european funding would be directed to developing countries in relation to climate change, an issue which, beyond the environmental propaganda, will certainly not change the fate of the ecosystem.
in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur on the work he has done, for which i gave him a positive vote. europe, through the next multiannual financial framework, must provide certain answers to the citizens who have suffered from the economic crisis for too long and must ensure solid growth in the long term. so far the european union has fallen far short of the expectations and ambitions it should have. we will have to face very complex challenges in addition to the economic crisis, demographic decline and energy shortages, and the response to these challenges will have to be sought in the eu 2020 strategy, which will have to be the political reference of the next mff. we need to identify a number of key priorities for the next mff, such as growth and jobs, sustainable development, cohesion for growth and jobs, citizenship and a global europe. the next mff should therefore be designed in a flexible way to overcome the shortcomings of the current mff. in this respect, provision should be made for an interim review which would provide the possibility of revising the ceilings. finally, the current system of extra-budgetary flexibility instruments needs to be improved, simplified and adequately funded. the next mff will have to embody the principles of a fair balance between stability, medium-term predictability and flexibility.
in writing. - the european parliament has made its voice heard on the future of the european budget by voting for the garriga report and has put forward an ambitious proposal for the next multiannual financial framework. the call for a 5% increase in the eu budget post-2013 - and thus a shift from 1.06% to 1.11% of total eu gni - reflects the will to maintain commitments to support growth and development, first and foremost the eu2020 strategy, for which adequate resources are needed. it is important to remember the added value of the european budget, which can act as a driving force for economic growth, research and development and employment, especially for young people, in addition to national budgets. the report also reinforces parliament's support for new financial instruments, such as the financial transaction tax and eurobonds, which represent an opportunity for the european economy. it is now up to the commission to match the european parliament's ambition by presenting its own proposals for the next european financial framework and not becoming a hostage to the restrictive budgetary policies of the member states.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate mr garriga polledo on the excellent work he has done on the important subject of the future financial perspective. the honourable member has in fact presented to the house an effective summary of the positions of the various national delegations and political groups. i strongly support the decision to request an increase in resources for the next multiannual financial framework of at least 5%. i would also like to emphasize the part of the report on the common agricultural policy, considering my role as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on agriculture and rural development. i therefore express my full support for the choice to keep the agricultural budget at least unchanged, recalling that the cap is the only true european policy, capable of playing an important role in a strategic sector, capable of providing public goods and of generating genuine european added value. finally, i would like to highlight the vote on cohesion policy, where a safeguard clause was inserted in the event of the introduction of the so-called intermediate categories, to avoid the withdrawal of resources from the regions covered by the convergence, competitiveness and cooperation objective. this means that additional resources will be needed to finance a new objective.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am very disappointed by the instrumental tone of this debate. i would also like to refer to the recent statements by mr lunacek, for example on the subject of discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation: the italian constitution does not contain any reference to this, so when will there be a debate in the european parliament on the italian constitution? it is also quite extraordinary because in my country the only party which would like to change the constitution is the centre-right party of mr berlusconi, to which the left has been replying for 15 years that we must not change the constitution because otherwise democracy will fall. so, be careful, because when we open a debate about what is or is not in a constitutional text maybe we should clear the field of a misunderstanding: do we really think it is a risk to modernity that this constitution mentions the rights of the unborn? do we really think that the mention of the christian roots of a country in this constitution could pose a threat to identity? i think we should all get used to the text of the european constitution, which has not yet become one, which had the motto 'united in diversity', and try to be a little more tolerant of the diversity of each one of us. we must understand that at this moment a huge consensus in hungary has brought to the fore the need of a people and that this need must be accompanied by a strong europe which recognizes the rights of all and the duties of each.
the new hungarian constitution, madam president, reduces the power of control bodies such as the constitutional court and increases the powers of the executive, thus calling into question the normal balance of power. social rights are exhausted, the state provides subsidies to the needy only if they agree to perform public works. finally, the right to self-defense is enshrined, allowing people to possess weapons in the home even without a license. the right to abortion is banned and rules are introduced which are highly discriminatory against homosexuals. this is contrary to directive 78/2000, which establishes a general framework for combating discrimination. i would therefore ask the commissioner what action she intends to take, given that the fundamental rights of the new hungarian constitution are hardly compatible with those of the european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union.

diverging opinions, which in itself shows how complex this matter is. so let me underline once more that the commission respects the lisbon treaty and does not intervene in the sovereignty of nation member state makes. the adoption of a new constitution in a member state is a matter for its people and for its institutions. as i have already underlined, we could become competent when the charter was violated or if union law was not respected. turning to ms guillaume’s question on union law: when union law is at stake i have never shied away from action. the question raised by ms with the words ‘let me live’, with the commission’s logo. i made it very clear: this campaign is not in line with the progress programme and it is not in line with the project proposal submitted to this is not done, we will start procedures to terminate the ground agreement and draw necessary consequences, including financial ones. that is how we answer when european law is at stake. the agenda includes oral questions to the council and the commission on the european arrest warrant.
mr president, the european arrest warrant is certainly a fundamental instrument in the fight against terrorism and organised crime. i think there is agreement and agreement on this from all those who have spoken, including the presidency and the commission. at the same time, it is a certification of how judicial and police cooperation in a transnational dimension of crime can achieve important goals. the waiting times have been resolved and the costs are currently to be verified and this needs to be investigated. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right to vote in the european parliament. it would be useful - i am addressing myself to mrs reding - to involve the european public prosecutor in this structure, which, once it is in place, will be able to have a kind of review and evaluation of these statements by the judicial authorities of the member states, for which further training is absolutely necessary. it is true that prison conditions are not the same in all the member states, but we hope that next week the commission will amend the communication and the green paper on essential prison conditions, which will then have to shape further behaviour. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
mr president, commissioner, the european arrest warrant is the first instrument to be used in the european union to implement the principle of mutual recognition of criminal decisions. this instrument is and must be of fundamental importance, especially in the fight against the mafia and organized crime! in the report on organised crime, for which i am rapporteur in the libe committee, we are proposing a number of considerations and requests relating specifically to the european arrest warrant: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the eam to include the fight against organised crime. i therefore ask the commission what it intends to do and whether it intends to put forward a proposal to overcome the discretion of the member states in transposing articles 3 and 4 of the framework decision as regards the grounds for mandatory and optional non-enforcement. as regards the grounds for non-execution, i would also like to know whether they should not be restricted to offences typically linked to organised crime, including the crime of mafia association, for which there should in any case be no double criminalization.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, there is general agreement in this house that the european arrest warrant is a positive tool and has served the european union well and acted as a security. the negative elements are in the implementation. those negative elements have to be eliminated. the proposals which the commission has put on the table for this purpose are the proportionality test, where we have to look at the seriousness of the offence, the length of the sentence which this offence would carry, and the cost/benefit of executing such an arrest warrant. in order to make this proportionality test easier, the commission will present an amended handbook as a guideline for the application of the proportionality test. training, which is very high on the agenda for the coming weeks, months and years, will be very important because we have to train judges, prosecutors and lawyers in the application of our european rules. the minimum standards for suspects and accused persons, which are under implementation, are very important because they also apply to the european arrest warrant. i agree with all those parliamentarians who have underlined the problem of prison conditions in europe. i would like to tell them that next week the commission will adopt a green paper on detention. national governments are responsible for detention issues and prison management, but the commission’s role is to make sure that judicial cooperation works and fundamental rights of all citizens are upheld. that is why the green paper will kick off a public consultation, which will run until 30 november and will help to explore more closely the links between detention issues and mutual trust in europe’s area of justice. everybody in this house knows that detention conditions have a direct impact on the smooth functioning of the mutual recognition of judicial decisions and are the basis for cooperation between judges in the eu. but the system is impeded if judges refuse – sometimes rightly so – to extradite accused persons because the detention conditions in the requesting country are substandard. we all know about prison overcrowding and the allegations of poor treatment of detainees. these factors undermine the trust that is necessary for judicial cooperation. the time that a person can spend in detention before being tried in court and during court proceedings varies a lot between member states. we have a lot of work ahead of us, and i know i can count on parliament. i hope i can also count on the member states.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, thank you very much for this debate. it is clear that an overwhelming majority says that it is good that we have a cooperation system for our judiciaries, the european arrest warrant. the system works. it is not perfect. it should be improved further. we are, of course, open to more efficient use and better implementation. i agree that mistakes, arrests of innocent people, etc., should be avoided. better implementation is, i think, in the interests of us all. i would be more specific on two outstanding issues which were raised several times during the debate. first, on proportionality: just to make it clear, a european arrest warrant can be issued to prosecute offences which are punishable by at least 12 months’ imprisonment, or to execute a sentence to at least 4 months’ imprisonment. this has been standard extradition practice for at least 50 years. it is enough to mention the 1957 council of europe convention on extradition. in the fourth round of mutual evaluations on the practical implementation of the european arrest warrant in all member states, it was found that only in a few countries were there examples of issuing european arrest warrants for relatively minor offences. it seems that, in those few countries, the practice was to issue a european arrest warrant every time a national arrest order was issued. in general terms, i believe that we should only use the costly system of the european arrest warrant for more serious offences. i think that those who mentioned this were right. concerning prison conditions: the member states are under a general obligation to ensure that prison conditions are in accordance with the basic tenets of human dignity and do not violate the prohibition of inhuman and degrading treatment laid down in article 3 of the european convention on human rights. if people are detained in violation of their basic human rights, they can take action before domestic courts and, later, before the european court of human rights. it is doubtful whether article 85 of the treaty provides a legal basis for legislative action at eu level on prison conditions as such. however, we are, of course, awaiting the green paper which the commissioner has just mentioned with great interest.
in writing. mr president, seven years after the entry into force (1 january 2004) of the council framework decision of 13 june 2002 on the european arrest warrant (eaw) and procedures between member states, the commission has released some statistical data collected between 2005 and 2009 within the member states. before the mandate was introduced, the average time for extradition of wanted persons was one year, whereas in these four years of the eia it was found that about 50% of wanted persons consented to their surrender after about 15 days. the need to take stock of the implementation and functioning of the emn is crucial at a time when the proper functioning of the schengen system and the possibility of its suspension are being called into question. let us not forget that the effectiveness of the emn in the fight against transnational crime, organised crime and terrorism depends on the principle of mutual recognition between member states, which is the basis of a genuine european judicial area, and also on the proper functioning of the schengen area. to compromise this context would be to take a step backwards rather than to concentrate on improving the transposition of the framework decision, especially in terms of the protection of fundamental rights.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the common agricultural policy is the european policy which has had to be renewed more than any other over the years in order to cope with the continuing changes in the economic landscape, including the international one. this was done without ever losing sight of two main objectives: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the cap. the cap reform we are voting on tomorrow is essential to continue to support the income of our farmers, as my colleagues have already said. the aim is not to reduce direct subsidies but to strike a balance between direct subsidies and rural development, so that the system becomes ever simpler and fairer, without jeopardizing the rules of competition. as regards the objectives of the cap under the europe 2020 strategy, the cap can contribute to the growth of a sustainable economy by responding adequately to new challenges and taking into account the diversity and richness of agriculture and the specificities of the 27 european states.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the importance of the common agricultural policy and the role it has played in the development of the european union and in food security is well known. environmental challenges and the fight against climate change give the cap a new role after 2013, and i believe that a stronger and more sustainable cap is needed, with a budget that is able to meet the objectives to be pursued, with particular attention to the development of quality food products and the needs of the small farmer. speculation on agricultural raw materials and extreme price volatility put food security at risk and require flexible measures. any market fluctuations must be countered by countercyclical measures, to be provided for in the first pillar, capable of reacting in a timely and automatic manner.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we shall be voting in favour of this own-initiative report because the cap is the fundamental instrument for european agriculture and for the protection of producers and products in the union as compared with those outside the union. the report's main points, which are based on the maintenance of the current financial resources, include new sharing criteria, as the historical criterion is abandoned as a parameter for the redistribution of direct payments, premiums are provided for farms, labour and production costs are taken into account and payment is simplified. it is called for direct payments to be made only to active farmers with ceilings, precisely because the recipients are those who actually cultivate the land and not the speculators. another point which we consider important is rural development, the development of all natural and human potential through quality agricultural production and the protection of the mountains. the new cap will have to target the integration of new farmers, especially young farmers, with targeted funding lines and reduce burdens and red tape.
the commission has already made a number of proposals. the report is an important step towards reform of the common agricultural policy. it will be fundamental and important to find and provide an efficient justification for the distribution of agricultural resources. this means that the distribution of the first pillar must also be more equitable. i think it's finally time to abandon the historical approach. we have a lot of discussion about the distribution between member states, but we also have to discuss the distribution within member states. there are also great imbalances. special attention must be paid to less-favoured areas, especially mountain areas and small farms. the commission has already submitted a report on the redefinition of the lessfavoured areas a year ago. we were very critical back then. we have not heard anything more about it, and i would be very interested to know what the commission thinks about it.
in writing. i would like to express my satisfaction at this first text on the future of the cap, which is already intended to send a positive message to our farmers to the commission, pending the legislative text. i think that many of the paragraphs contain the information that i and other colleagues have inserted. and i refer to the important quotations in favour of our southern agriculture. direct aid, for example, will no longer be based solely on a premium per hectare, but will finally take into account the size of the holding, the type of employment, the productivity of labour and the legal form of the undertaking. i am also enthusiastic about the award of these prizes only to farmers who are really active in the sector, so that the aid goes to those who really need it and use it for agriculture. the commission is also proposing a more equitable distribution of aid, given that the structure of agricultural holdings in the european union is very variable for historical reasons. i welcome the point that the new cap must be equipped with the necessary instruments to limit price volatility. i would like to conclude by mentioning the most widespread agricultural product in my region, olive oil, and the measures we are waiting for from the commission, an updated system of private stocks and the activation of private storage.

in writing. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i take this opportunity to express my opposition to a unilateral increase in the european target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by more than 20% by 2020 in the absence of a global climate agreement involving all the major emitters. it should be borne in mind that the european union is still the only area in the world to have adopted legally binding emission reduction targets. the immediate consequence is that european industry is exposed to strong competition from global competitors who are not subject to the same constraints. therefore, in my view, the priority for the union must first be to achieve the already very ambitious 20-20-20 targets set out in the climate and energy package. only then will we be able to define a community environmental policy which will enable european companies to remain globally competitive in order to support economic growth and, above all, job creation. i would like to conclude by sharing the concerns expressed by the representatives of the italian industrial system, which is not currently in a position to sign up to more ambitious commitments than those already agreed by the european council and reaffirmed by the european commission in the european emissions trading directive.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for belgium because i believe that this instrument represents a valuable resource for supporting workers in difficulty because of the economic crisis. as has been repeatedly stated, since 2006 the egf has provided concrete assistance to european workers made redundant as a result of the relocation of their businesses or, following the derogation introduced in 2009, also as a result of the economic crisis, in order to reintegrate them into the labour market. today's vote concerned a request for support for 2834 redundancies, all of which were eligible for assistance from the fund, at general motors belgium and four of its suppliers, operating in the motor vehicle sector in the nuts ii region of antwerp, during the four-month reference period from 14 june to 14 october 2010, for a total amount of eur 9 593 931 financed.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows. in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, which particularly affected general motors belgium, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of belgium. in this connection, particular reference was made to the unforeseen nature of redundancies and their impact on local, regional or national employment. we recall that the egf was created as a specific and distinct instrument with its own objectives and deadlines, and that it is therefore justified to allocate a specific amount to avoid carrying out transfers from other budget lines, which could be detrimental to the achievement of the objectives of the various policies. we consider that the application fulfils the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation and recommend that it be approved with our favourable opinion. however, a revision of the egf regulation is still essential to deal with the problem of multinational companies whose restructuring or transfer causes redundancies and, consequently, the intervention of the adjustment fund.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide additional support for workers who are suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows. on 14 april 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in belgium to support the reintegration into the labour market of 2,834 redundant workers in the main establishment of general motors belgium and four of its suppliers in the automotive sector in antwerp. the commission's assessment was based on the following elements: the link between the redundancies and major structural changes in world trade flows; the financial crisis; the unforeseen nature of the redundancies in question; the proof of the number of redundancies; an explanation of the unforeseen nature of such redundancies; the identification of firms which have made redundancies and of workers eligible for assistance; the territory concerned with the respective authorities and stakeholders; the impact of redundancies on local, regional or national employment; the coordinated package of personalised services to be financed. in order to ensure that these people are reintegrated into the labour market, i shall vote in favour of the proposal in question.

in writing. - mr casini's report addresses and contributes positively to the resolution of the problems connected with the interpretation and application of rule 51 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament. i fully share mr casini's view that it was not enough to refer to the interpretation and the guidelines intended to facilitate its implementation. the conditions for the application of the procedure with joint committee meetings and joint voting, in particular the criteria of 'competence and high relevance' of the subject under discussion, are clear and are suitable for eliminating the legal uncertainties which have existed up to now. i congratulate you on the good work you have done and i hope that this report will facilitate the work of parliament by making greater use of this procedure.
in writing. - the report proposes to amend rule 51, after the conference of presidents had raised the question of the rules of procedure for joint meetings between committees. the report proposes that the rules of procedure be amended so that the conditions for the application of article 51 are also examined more closely and according to stricter criteria by the conference of presidents. the fact that joint meetings are held only on matters of major importance will ensure that there is no unfairly extensive application of a procedure which is by its nature extraordinary. i shall vote in favour of the casini report.
in writing. - we support this amendment to the rules of procedure of the european parliament which provides that the conference of presidents, in the case of a legislative question of major importance, may decide to apply a procedure with joint meetings of parliamentary committees and a joint vote. this is only the case, however, if the matter falls within the remit of several committees and if it is a matter of major importance. the amendment is intended to emphasise the exceptional nature of the procedure and is justified, inter alia, by the administrative and technical burden involved. we believe that this could facilitate, at an early stage, an exchange of views between the committees concerned and that it could also be useful in preparing the ground for votes in plenary in cases of greater importance.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr casini's report on the amendment of rule 51 of parliament's rules of procedure because that amendment is the result of a work of synthesis of the legislation which makes clearer the scope of article 51. the new text lightened one article by removing references to other articles and by regulating the practice whereby two committees can meet in joint session only on important issues which reflect common interests. the purpose of the amendment is therefore to create the possibility for the committees concerned to exchange arguments in order to prepare the ground for a debate. the joint committees thus become competent for this procedure on the merits within the meaning of the regulation.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, to create the possibility for the committees concerned to exchange views at an early stage and to 'prepare the ground' in cases of major importance to the plenary. article 51 needs to be amended in order to: make the provision more legible and therefore more suitable for use; the commission has therefore decided to review the conditions for the application of the standard and to determine its legislative substance. to achieve these aims, the two conditions must be presented in a clear and immediately understandable manner. the matter must be dealt with by several committees and the practical consequences of its application must be determined in the light of the legislative procedure. the joint committees thus become 'committees responsible for the subject-matter' under the regulation. in order to amend rule 51 of parliament's rules of procedure, which concerns the procedures for joint meetings of committees, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. the report supports the proposal to amend rule 51 of the rules of procedure with regard to the procedure with joint committee meetings. the textual conflicts in the article cannot be resolved by mere interpretation, given the importance of the procedural issue. the new wording sets out in a clear and immediately understandable way the conditions for holding joint meetings, and eliminates references to other rules of the rules of procedure. furthermore, the redefinition of those conditions is justified by the technical and administrative burden involved in such a procedure. finally, the commonly recognised objective of joint meetings of exchanging arguments and opinions in advance in order to 'prepare the ground' in plenary for matters of major importance can only be achieved if the committees remain jointly competent on the merits at all stages of the procedure until the adoption of the act.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this document. the previous fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles, which expired in january 2011 and was renewed by the commission for a period of three years, has brought mutual benefits in terms of their respective interests in the tuna fisheries. the agreement has created 230 jobs on board vessels for the people of seychelles, 2900 jobs in seychelles and 760 jobs in europe in the supply chains of the sector. the extension of this agreement, which stabilizes the european canned tuna market, is useful, since it guarantees the presence of 60 vessels of the european tuna fleet on the spot with the possibility of creating jobs. it is also effective because it has given seychelles the tools to develop responsible fishing, increasing their capacity to manage stocks and monitor fisheries. i therefore believe that it is appropriate to continue the path of partnership agreements in this vital sector for the european economy.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in today's vote we approved the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of seychelles. the first bilateral fisheries agreement was signed between the european union and the seychelles in 1987, while the partnership agreement has been in force since 2006. as is well known, the economy of seychelles is essentially based on tourism and fishing, with the fishing industry accounting for 15% of gdp and employing 17% of the local working population. i believe that the negotiations conducted by the european commission, which led to the renewal of the protocol to the partnership agreement, have resulted in the drafting of a mutually beneficial document, capable of improving the level of cooperation between the eu and seychelles and of promoting a partnership which will enable seychelles to implement a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible use of fishery resources in its fishing zone.
in writing. the new fisheries agreement between the european community and the republic of seychelles will be valid for a period of three years and will facilitate job creation, sustainable exploitation of marine resources and responsible fishing, based on the principle of non-discrimination between the different fleets of fishing vessels operating in the area. at the same time, it will promote a political dialogue on the necessary reforms in order to strengthen cooperation between the parties, supporting a partnership that allows the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible use of fisheries resources in the seychelles' fishing zone. but fisheries partnership agreements must not only be a legal way for european vessels to access the resources of third countries, they must also be a tool for promoting the sustainable exploitation of all marine resources. we believe it is of paramount importance to take account of the improvement of the procedures for the accounting of total catches and to ensure the integrity of the mechanisms with regard to the problem of corruption, by strengthening the responsibility of local government. the european union will receive regular reports on the implementation of the agreement to facilitate monitoring and promote transparency and consistency in development policies.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, on 17 january the protocol governing fisheries and the associated economic partnership between the eu and the seychelles expired. in order to allow european fishing vessels to continue fishing activities in the indian ocean area of the republic of seychelles, the european union has negotiated the renewal of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendations to the council for the conclusion of the new partnership agreement with the seychelles.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the conclusion of a new protocol to the eu-seychelles partnership agreement is important for the economy and the development of the european fishing fleet. the new protocol is in line with the objectives of the fisheries partnership agreement which seek to strengthen cooperation between the eu and seychelles and to promote a partnership framework to facilitate the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the seychelles' fishing zone, in the interests of both parties. the new protocol provides for a financial contribution for a period of three years, providing for annual fishing authorizations in seychelles' waters for 48 purse seiners and 12 longliners. these opportunities can be increased. the new protocol covers a period of three years from the adoption of the council decision on the signing of the protocol and its provisional application and after the expiry of the protocol in force on 17 january 2011. for these reasons and in order to strengthen cooperation between the european union and the republic of seychelles for the development and responsible exploitation of sustainable fisheries, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i believe that this partnership agreement is mutually beneficial for the fisheries sectors between the european union and seychelles. the old agreement has already created many jobs for the people of seychelles and in europe, as reflected in the supply chains in the sector. the agreement also provides for specific suspension clauses in the event of a violation of human rights by either party. much remains to be done, particularly with regard to piracy in the indian ocean, which is increasingly damaging tuna fishing in particular. but today's decision strengthens cooperation between the parties and promotes a partnership capable of developing sustainable fisheries and of using seychelles' resources in a balanced way.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, this proposal concerns the conclusion of a new protocol to a partnership agreement between the eu and são tomé and príncipe. the main objective is to define the fishing opportunities available to eu vessels on the basis of the available surplus, as well as the financial contribution due separately for access rights and sectoral support. the commission will be able to use 28 tuna seiners and 12 surface longliners. in the light of the annual assessments of the situation of fish stocks, fishing opportunities may be adjusted more or less, resulting in a proportionate review of the financial contribution. the annual financial contribution shall be equal to eur 682 500. the total amount of the annual financial contribution will be increased by eur 65 for each additional tonne caught where the total quantity of catches by eu vessels exceeds 7 000 tonnes per year. the agreement is for a period of three years. for these reasons and in order to consolidate the sustainability of the eu tuna sector, the commission has decided to extend the current fishing season to the following year.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this measure to extend the existing agreement between the european union and the principality of andorra to customs security measures. the need for this measure has grown over the last few years, as the principality of andorra has become a hub for the illicit trafficking of products, especially cigarettes, which are then introduced into the trade network of the member states of the union. it is essential that the union and the principality itself define a framework for cooperation in the field of customs security. taking into account that the protection of border security has always been a key aspect of the political ideology of the northern league, i can only approve the measure in question.
in writing. − we believe that the conclusion of this protocol between the european union and the principality of andorra, extending customs security measures, will ensure the smooth flow of trade between the two parties, while respecting a high level of customs security, and will provide for a set of rules to ensure that the agreement and the eu acquis remain aligned. we therefore gave our favourable opinion that parliament should give its consent. we do, however, believe that the commission should inform parliament of the conclusions of the meetings and the work of the joint committee and of the results of the periodic evaluations, and should also undertake to report on the implementation of the agreement. given the extensive but fragmented relations between the european union and the principality of andorra, we recommend that an analysis be made as soon as possible of the possibilities and modalities of its possible gradual integration into the internal market. this will be necessary to ensure that trade between the two parties is carried out smoothly, while maintaining a high level of security. finally, we are proposing to abolish the obligation to declare goods in advance, provided that the european union and andorra guarantee an equivalent level of security in their respective territories as provided for in the respective acquis.

in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this recommendation concerns the agreement on aviation safety of 6 may 2009. in view of the climate of cooperation which has emerged in the agreement, i shall vote in favour.
in writing. − the 2009 civil aviation safety agreement is a first step towards the creation of a borderless airspace between the european union and canada. the agreement provides for joint inspections, exchange of safety data, enhanced regulatory cooperation and technical consultations to resolve issues before they become 'disputes' in order to maintain mutual trust in the systems. in addition, the creation of a joint committee and of various sectoral committees will save european and canadian companies millions of euros a year by mutually accepting certification results. the importing authorities will be able to issue their own certificates for products, parts or aircraft parts without having to repeat all the checks carried out by the exporting authority. the agreement will also benefit airlines, as it provides for the possibility of using the repair and maintenance services of the other party. not only will the competitiveness of the canadian and european markets be increased, but also global security will be improved. finally, we believe that this agreement is important for the establishment of international standards in the field of civil aviation safety and should serve as a starting point for future negotiations with other major aircraft manufacturers.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the conclusion of the ec-canada agreement on civil aviation safety because i believe that it represents a clear advantage for the european union in that it provides for the mutual recognition of documentation provided in all areas relating to aviation for all member states. the agreement provides for joint inspections, investigations, exchange of safety data, enhanced cooperation and technical consultations. mutual reliance on the certification systems of the other party means improving the security of the system, avoiding time wasted in repeating all the checks carried out by the exporting authority and ensuring benefits for airlines by the possibility to use the repair and maintenance services of the other party. this will increase the competitiveness and safety of the air transport markets.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the key objectives are to enable the eu and canada to rely on each other's certification systems. this will be achieved through a progressive alignment of the two sets of requirements and regulatory processes, systematic consultations between the parties to verify the continued suitability and capacity of the regulatory bodies concerned by the application of the agreement and the establishment of a joint committee to propose solutions to problems that may arise from its application. the agreement broadly follows the implementation of the bilateral basa agreements on aviation safety between the member states and canada. it is based on the confidence of each party in the system in force in the other party and on the comparison of regulatory differences. the agreement therefore lays down obligations and cooperation arrangements which enable the importing authority to issue its own certificate for aeronautical products, parts or appliances without having to repeat all the controls carried out by the exporting authority. in order to increase the competitiveness and security of the canadian and european markets and to have shorter and simpler product approval procedures, i am voting in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - cohesion policy has a great potential today, more than ever, which should not be underestimated, to give new impetus to less developed regions which are characterised by permanent geographical or natural handicaps. it would be a grave sin to waste or leave unused the resources available, and then it is good to adopt as a matter of urgency a results-oriented approach by setting clear and measurable objectives and result indicators. the first step, which should apply to all community resources, is to simplify procedures and improve the flexibility of the allocation of funds by reducing bureaucratic barriers, excessive administrative costs and other obstacles to the achievement of policy objectives in the field of employment and the fight against poverty. let us not forget that cohesion policy is a long-term mechanism, so starting work on a solid basis, setting clear objectives and assigning specific competences to each level of governance are progress factors that will only give visibility to the results in the second part of the programming period.
in writing. − member states, as evidenced by data published in the national reports, are making progress towards the objectives of cohesion policy, despite a degree of heterogeneity between states and regions. i would also point out that cohesion policy is a long-term mechanism and that most of the results will only be visible at a later stage of the programming period. in my view, sound financial discipline and, above all, transparency in the allocation of funds are the fundamental preconditions for achieving the overall objectives of cohesion policy. the future architecture of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020 will be at the heart of the political debate in the coming years. in the context of the negotiations for the future programming period, i believe that a strong european regional policy, adequately financed, is an essential condition for achieving the social, economic and territorial cohesion of the european union. therefore, the funds allocated to cohesion policy should not be subject to any reduction in the next programming period. in addition, simplification of the management and implementation of cohesion policy is essential to avoid funds being left unused due to overly complex rules and procedures.

in writing. − the report on the european urban agenda and its future in cohesion policy stresses the fact that, further to the significant contribution of cohesion policy interventions to the development of urban areas, a range of other eu policies (such as environment, transport and energy) have a strong impact on urban development. for this reason the commission should proceed with a territorial impact assessment of sectoral policies to enhance an effective eu urban agenda. the report also underlines that one of the weaknesses of the lisbon strategy was the lack of well-functioning multi-level governance and the insufficient involvement of regional, local authorities and civil society in the design, implementation, communication and evaluation stages of the strategy. taking this lack into account, it is imperative to improve the governance system for the eu2020 strategy, with greater integration of stakeholders at all stages.
in writing. − cities are the hub of social and economic life and have a fundamental capacity for social integration, as they ensure the preservation of cultural diversity on the one hand and maintain a permanent link between the centre and the peripheries on the other. that is why i am in favour of the proposal to extend the funds for urban areas. i also agree with the idea that new investment should not be confined to the economic sphere and specific sectors, but that projects should also be implemented with a greater focus on social cohesion and integration of the parties. to this end, it is essential to pursue projects that are sustainable in terms of cost and resources and flexible, as each city is different and deserves solutions that best suit its needs. the development objectives of a european agenda must therefore be aimed at improving social cohesion in urban areas, including through economic progress but not only; implement a well-coordinated policy at both european and local levels, involving local elected bodies in the strategic decision-making process; to raise funds and incentivise investment to implement new projects instead of creating projects to obtain funding.
in writing. − urban areas, home to 73% of europe's population and generating around 80% of gdp, are the union's major centres of innovation, culture and growth. however, the urban dimension has not been sufficiently recognised. this is why it is important that parliament proposes to strengthen the european urban agenda within the framework of eu policies, by strengthening the contribution of cohesion policy to urban development and by involving local political actors more. the urban dimension of cohesion policy should be geared towards supporting the development of basic physical infrastructure, the modernisation of the economic, social and environmental characteristics of cities, urban redevelopment and the promotion of social innovation in disadvantaged neighbourhoods. this requires direct participation of local authorities and civil society, involving city politicians in strategic planning and in the definition and negotiation of partnership contracts. in this context, the call on the commission to promote the training of city administrators and to set up an erasmus programme for local and regional elected officials is significant. we will be watching closely to see how the commission is able to take up the important proposals in the report, in the belief that a full recognition of the centrality of the urban dimension in eu policies is an indispensable condition for their success.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the general regulation on the structural funds and the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon have considerably increased the importance of territorial cooperation over the last five years. the 2007-13 financial framework has made the territorial cooperation objective one of the three pillars of the european union's cohesion policy, succeeding the interreg community initiative. subsequently, 'territorial cohesion' became one of the three components of cohesion policy in article 174 of the treaty, alongside the economic and social components, as it is one of the eu's main priorities. it aims to remove physical, administrative and regulatory obstacles and to mitigate the 'border effect' between territories and regions, so as to enable them to respond jointly to common challenges, whether territorial, global, economic or societal. objective 3 allows for complex and multidimensional cooperation involving partners from different member states. this requires simplification of the rules on auditing and control. in order to make territorial cooperation the symbolic personification of the eu for all citizens and to familiarize policy-makers and officials with the practical aspects of territorial cooperation relevant to their work, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
