in writing. the european parliament has concluded the long legislative process on the consumer rights directive by adopting, with the schwab report, a satisfactory compromise with the council and the commission. two important steps are thus taken: the commission has also adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a breach of the consumer protection rules. the new directive lays down aspects that go towards greater protection of the european consumer, such as the information to be included in sales contracts, delivery times, the right to withdraw or to have a defective product repaired or replaced, and cases where risk is transferred from the seller to the consumer. although even more detailed rules may be established in the future, the text adopted represents a positive compromise in the harmonisation of existing rules, ensuring security in purchases and putting an end once and for all to the typical fraud behind electronic purchases.
in writing. − the aim of the consumer rights directive is to simplify contractual relations between consumers and businesses, contributing to a better functioning of the internal market and increasing their confidence in cross-border purchases. it should ensure a high level of protection for consumers and the possibility for businesses to provide their goods and services without encountering legal obstacles. the european commission has proposed the application of the principle of 'complete harmonisation', as the current existence of divergent national legislation has contributed to the fragmentation of the market and the regulatory framework. we consider this proposal to be impractical at the moment and propose instead a minimum standard of harmonisation at a high level of consumer protection, stressing the need for convergence of national legislation on the exercise and effects of the right of withdrawal. this will help to strengthen consumer confidence and to combat business reluctance to engage in cross-border trade. persons and organisations with an interest in consumer protection will have to submit a report to the commission on the results of the application of this directive. on this basis, the commission will draw up a report, accompanied by any proposals for adjustment.
in writing. − i am pleased to see that after years of negotiations the agreement between the different political parties has finally been reached and that the new consumer rights directive is finally adopted today. the new rules will considerably strengthen the rights of consumers, who will be better informed about the terms of contracts and the conditions of sale, as well as about delivery times and the possibility of cancelling contracts. i am thinking, for example, of the time taken for the refund of a returned product, which will be considerably shortened, thus guaranteeing the consumer financial security. or the right of reconsideration, which will extend to 14 days. small but important steps which will be appreciated not only by consumers, because the directive, as amended, will also benefit small and mediumsized enterprises, allowing them to extend their business even to cross-border territories, where many, especially smaller entrepreneurs, still find it difficult to operate because of the distrust that consumers maintain towards new technologies, online transactions, guarantees of recovery of money and legal satisfaction in the event of reconsideration.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, this proposal for a directive is the result of the review of the consumer acquis, which was launched in 2004 with the aim of simplifying and complementing the existing regulatory framework for consumer protection. the proposal aims to ensure that consumers in the 27 member states enjoy a high level of protection and that businesses, regardless of their size, can supply their goods and services to consumers in the 27 member states of the union without unnecessary legal obstacles. in order to avoid the increasing fragmentation of existing rules in this area, a targeted comprehensive harmonisation was sought, i.e. harmonisation limited to specific aspects of certain contracts while maintaining a high level of consumer protection. this is why the scope of the directive needs to be adjusted, since, in addition to a number of sectoral exemptions in a wide range of areas, it is limited to contracts negotiated outside commercial premises, which are increasingly a very significant part of crossborder contracts. in order to enable eu citizens to benefit fully from their internal market, particularly in relation to electronic commerce, i am voting in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − in a large single market such as the european one, it is necessary to ensure the protection of consumer rights. mr schwab's report aims to merge four different directives: the commission has already adopted a number of directives on the subject, including the door-to-door directive, the distance selling directive, the guarantee directive and the contractual clauses directive. it is difficult to reconcile 27 different legal traditions on these issues. this is probably not the most appropriate time in history to bring about legislation of this complexity. i think it would have been more appropriate to focus on specific aspects and areas rather than trying to create a new competence shared between the eu and the member states. the directive will be an excessive and unnecessary step forward for some member states, while others will have to make concessions in the name of european harmonization. for this reason, while i acknowledge the great effort made by mr schwab, i cannot vote in favour of this report.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the proposal to amend directive 2000/25/ec on emissions from agricultural tractors is only quantitative, but it does not affect or alter the environmental protection objectives, nor does it affect the operational and expiry dates. this directive addresses exhaust gas emissions from diesel engines installed in tractors by setting the maximum level of emissions, depending on the power of the engine used, and organises in successive time steps the pathway to gradual emission reductions. phase a ended on 31 december 2010 and phase b started on 1 january 2011. the limits imposed in the newly launched phase are much stricter than in the previous ones. it was precisely to facilitate these stages that a 'flexibility scheme' was introduced in the directive, allowing manufacturers to place on the market a limited number of tractors with engines rated at the emission limits permitted in the previous stage. the amendment is to increase the proportion of these tractors from 20 to 50%. for these reasons, and because the technological backlog and the world financial crisis have not allowed these factors to be adjusted, i am voting in favour.

in writing. - 40 000 m3 of radioactive waste are produced in the european union each year, of which 80% is low-level short-lived waste, 5% is low-level long-lived waste and less than 10% is high-level waste. in view of these facts, i believe it is important to establish a community regulatory framework which, with the help of national programmes, will regulate the production and disposal of spent fuel and radioactive waste. the objective of achieving sustainable disposal of certain substances requires continuous monitoring and the progressive development of long-term technological solutions. that is why i agree with the rapporteur that we must focus on reversibility, and hope that research will soon lead to the final transmutation of spent fuel and radioactive waste for other uses. in fact, research and technological development are the key to the breakthrough in this sector, which will allow the safe use of nuclear energy, capable of meeting the energy demand of the food, medical, industrial, agricultural, research and education sectors. finally, i hope that the adoption of this report will be an important step towards the achievement of a european energy plan.
in writing. − the tragedy of the earthquake in japan is forcing europe to reflect more deeply on the consequences of the use of nuclear technology and its impact on the safety of european citizens; the european parliament, in approving the report on the proposal for a directive on the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste, shows its particular concern for this issue by expressing a clear desire to find definitive and common solutions to the storage of nuclear waste in europe. the demand for minimum standards common to all member states is encouraging governments to invest in new technologies with a view to achieving concrete and rapid results in the disposal of these highly harmful wastes. i therefore welcome two amendments tabled by the s&d group, which call for parliament to be involved in the co-decision procedure with the council on matters relating to the use of nuclear energy and which establish the fundamental ban on the export of waste to third countries, a ban which shows parliament's determination to take its responsibilities seriously. the vote by parliament is therefore a further step towards a gradual move away from nuclear power towards sustainable energy solutions that are safe for citizens.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the commission's proposal for a directive establishing an eu regulatory framework for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste. establishing requirements for member states to establish a national organisational and regulatory framework, so that they can develop appropriate national programmes for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste, from generation to disposal. the proposal is based on the euratom treaty and, in particular, on the guidelines set out in the report entitled 'evaluation of euratom - 50 years of european nuclear energy policy'. the rapporteur identifies four main priorities among the amendments proposed in the draft report for consideration by the committee members. the first is the planning of projects and technical solutions for final disposal, in particular deep geological disposal. the second is to ensure that financial resources are set aside to meet the requirements for decommissioning nuclear installations and waste disposal. the third concerns the development of regional waste disposal facilities. the last one is about transparency and public participation. for these reasons i am voting in favour of the proposal for a directive.
in writing. − this directive aims to ensure that member states establish a national regulatory and organisational framework and draw up appropriate national programmes for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste, irrespective of the prospects for nuclear energy and non-energy applications. the commission's position that member states are responsible for the safe management, including disposal, of spent fuel and radioactive waste produced by them, by developing their own programmes, is to be supported. many of the amendments incorporated in the text are questionable. in a sensitive subject such as this, the utmost transparency and information of the citizens is essential, but it is not possible to restrict such choices to public participation in decision-making processes. without definite rules, we risk not taking the decisions necessary for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste. that is why i cannot support this report.

mr president, i would like to congratulate mrs corinne lepage on her determination to ensure that this dossier was successful. i have strongly supported this report in all the forums because it seems to me to be a report which at the same time gives legal force to the text we have adopted and also fills a legal vacuum which has given rise to a serious legal dispute between companies, public bodies and citizens. it is a measure to prevent the colonization of territories; it therefore leaves the choice to the nations to ban or restrict the cultivation of gmos. the amendments made by this text will therefore allow individual states to ban the cultivation of gmos because of the impact they may have on the agricultural system, taking into account biodiversity in particular, but also the resistance to pesticides, the invasiveness of certain crops and therefore the protection of our territories.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report because i have always expressed many concerns about gmo crops in europe, especially because european agricultural production has always focused on the uniqueness, high quality and excellence of its products and aims to protect the health of citizens through numerous quality controls and transparent traceability processes. furthermore, as stated in the opinion of the legal affairs committee, gmos cannot be considered in the same way as any other product, being living organisms that are capable of reproducing and multiplying themselves and, secondly, they have an impact on production systems and ecosystems, which are extremely diverse in the union. that is why each member state must have the right to decide on gmos.
mr president, i have always taken a very cautious view of genetically modified organisms. i believe that in the absence of scientific evidence to prove that it is absolutely safe for health and in the face of serious economic problems, particularly in countries which are strongly committed to quality and uniqueness, the precautionary principle should be used. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i would also have liked the commission to be more courageous in its approach to prudence, but there are positive aspects to be taken into account, in particular the fact that it introduces a new element, namely the possibility for member states to ban gmo cultivation on agri-environmental grounds, which strengthens their legal position in the face of possible appeals to the wto. for these reasons i voted in favour of the legislative proposal.
mr president, a very difficult and controversial issue was voted on today, namely gmos. leaving it to the member states to ban or restrict the cultivation of gmos on their territory means that the european union is giving up its leading role on such a sensitive issue. there are still many questions. do we know what the long-term effects will be on the ecosystem? are we reasonably certain that the use of gmos does not pose serious health risks? are we sure that consumers whose state has banned the cultivation of these crops in their own territory are not consuming them anyway? we are far from certain, the only certainty i have is that both the commission and the member states should ensure that the necessary resources are made available for independent research and that gmos are not just a shortcut to profit.
mr president, the pieper report on cohesion policy after 2013 reduces the effects of a two-speed europe. only uniform growth can ensure real cohesion between our territories and, even in our diversity, overall unity. i voted for the text because it introduces an intermediate category, which allows many european regions to continue to benefit from the structural funds to the same extent as they have done so far. the lack of effective programming for the use of european funds has unfortunately meant that many regions have not been able to make the most of the resources made available by the european union, risking losing a large part of the funding. but there is a positive signal from brussels. we hope that our regions will be able to interpret and use the funds to the best of their ability.
mr president, there is great anticipation for the legislative proposals for the future post-2013 cohesion policy which will be presented next september. the commission has already announced that the reform will introduce an intermediate category which should replace the current system of phasing in and phasing out. i am perplexed about the implications of this new category, since it will also include, at least apparently, regions which are currently neither in the convergence nor in the competitiveness regime. i would remind you that the priority of cohesion policy is to help the regions whose development is lagging behind, and i would therefore not want the reform to harm the poorest regions of europe which are struggling to set in motion development policies. we hope, however, that the new programming will give a boost to europe's growth.
mr president, the pieper report is certainly a good report, and i believe that many countries like italy, which are in a position to be both major contributors and major beneficiaries of cohesion policy, attach great importance to this report and to this work. the revision is mainly aimed at strengthening the evaluation of results, controls and cross-compliance. it is certainly a shared and important path, provided that the budgetary structure remains unchanged and above all that the gross domestic product remains the main criterion. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the programme is implemented in the member states, and i would like to ask the commissioner to take this into account. the fifth paragraph, which i tried to amend by means of an oral amendment, introduces the obligation to submit programmes and projects not only in the language of the member state but also in english, french and german, and that is unacceptable. second question about the intermediate categories: i do not think that they are a useful introduction to helping the countries in greatest difficulty, which should be the main objective of cohesion policy.
mr president, this is a good report, a very important report for the balanced, harmonious and sustainable development of our communities. strong solidarity between member states makes our regions more attractive, more innovative and more competitive. simplification of access to aid, more effective controls and quality of expenditure are the objectives for a better functioning of this instrument. more investment in research, knowledge, innovation, growth, the development of small and mediumsized enterprises and jobs. one final thought: the creation of a new intermediate category must not take resources away from existing categories, but must bring and focus only on additional resources.
mr president, i voted in favour of the wagner report because it effectively highlights the strengths and weaknesses of the european commission's approach to the relaunch of energy infrastructure: the commission's proposal for a regulation on the financing of the common agricultural policy, which is the subject of a proposal from the commission, is based on the following three criteria: the need to determine the necessary infrastructure; the criteria for the selection of projects of european interest in the context of financing that attracts and stimulates private investment; the urgency of addressing the dangers of dependence on a single source in eastern europe, which, as has been demonstrated in recent years, can cause serious supply problems; and the opportunity to invest part of the one trillion euro over ten years envisaged by the european commission in reducing pollution, combating climate change and improving the quality of supply, for clean and secure energy.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument designed to support the reintegration of workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the ongoing process of globalisation of world markets. this fund is in favour of the workers and does not want to act in any way for the benefit of the company which made the redundancies. as regards the mobilisation of the funds for the case in question, i abstained because i believe that there were criticisms and that the admissibility of the request was not so obvious. in fact, although the commission approved the request, certain factors made me inclined to abstain: the non-sudden dismissal of workers, given that almost a year had passed from the announcement of the closure of the yard to the request for mobilisation of the fund; in addition, 750 of the 950 workers who should be eligible for assistance from the fund had already been applied for by a norwegian company for offshore activities.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on 6 may 2011 the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of denmark to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. this application relates to the mobilisation of the egf for a total amount of eur 14 181 901 for denmark. the commission has decided to initiate proceedings under article 93 (2) of the eec treaty in respect of a complaint lodged by a german undertaking concerning the failure of the commission to comply with the requirements of the directive. the commission has assessed that the application fulfils the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation and therefore recommends that the budgetary authority approve it. the egf was set up in 2006 with the objective of 'providing additional support to redundant workers affected by the consequences of large structural changes in world trade patterns, to assist them in their reintegration into the labour market'. following a revision of this regulation in 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the global financial and economic crisis. for these reasons i shall vote in favour of the proposal.

in writing. - we support the decision to mobilise the european union solidarity fund, up to a maximum of eur 1 billion per year, for croatia, slovenia and the czech republic following the heavy rainfall and flooding that affected these three countries last year. the disaster caused extensive damage to infrastructure, agriculture, businesses and private property, forcing people to flee their homes. we believe that, as the disaster is of natural origin, the request should be examined under the criterion of the so-called 'extraordinary regional disaster', which provides that a region affected by an extraordinary disaster, mainly of natural origin, which has affected the majority of the population, with profound and lasting repercussions on living conditions and economic stability of the region, may exceptionally benefit from the fund's assistance.

in writing. − the report on the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund for slovenia, croatia and the czech republic aims to provide funding for these countries following the flood damage caused by the heavy rainfall from 17 to 20 september 2010. as the overall damage is below the normal threshold for mobilising the solidarity fund, the request was examined under the criterion of 'extraordinary regional disaster', which defines the conditions for mobilising the solidarity fund 'in exceptional circumstances'. according to those criteria, a region affected by an extraordinary disaster, mainly of natural origin, which has affected the majority of the population and had a profound and lasting impact on living conditions and economic stability in that region, may exceptionally benefit from the assistance of the fund. i therefore voted in favour of the report because i believe that funding should be provided to deal with the damage suffered by slovenia, croatia and the czech republic.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have supported the report by mrs sidonia jędrzejewska on draft amending budget no 2/2011 which will make it possible to finance slovenia, croatia and the czech republic to provide aid following the severe floods in 2010. the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 on budgetary discipline and sound financial management allows the european union solidarity fund to be mobilised up to a maximum of eur 1 billion per year. however, under article 37 (1) of the financial regulation, 'in the event of unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances', the commission is allowed to present draft amending budgets. that is what the rapporteur has proposed in the report we are voting on today. the direct damage suffered by slovenia, the czech republic and croatia was estimated at eur 19 546 647 in total, which was the amount requested in the draft amending budget approved today.
in writing. − we believe that in the event of unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances, draft amending budgets should be presented. the activation of the eu solidarity fund (eusf) allows the fund to be used for up to eur 1 billion per year and its purpose is the restoration of infrastructure. as a refinancing instrument, it cannot therefore be used to compensate private individuals for the damage they have suffered. in slovenia, direct damage exceeds the normal threshold of 0.6% of gni required to benefit from the solidarity fund and can be described as a 'serious natural disaster'. however, as regards the czech republic and croatia, whose direct damage does not exceed the normal threshold, article 2 (2) of council regulation (ec) no 2012/2002 has been applied, according to which, exceptionally, a neighbouring country that has been affected by the same disaster may also benefit from eusf assistance. as an eu candidate country, croatia will therefore be eligible for the fund. finally, we believe that the unused appropriations of the economic recovery plan should be reallocated, i.e. to finance the need to mobilise the eusf, to create a negative reserve and to increase the payment appropriations for the egf.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the event of unavoidable, exceptional or unforeseen circumstances, the commission may present draft amending budgets. on 25 march the commission presented draft amending budget no 2/2011 to the 2011 general budget which aims to mobilise eu solidarity in order to mitigate the effects of heavy rainfall in slovenia, the czech republic and croatia during the summer of 2010. the conditions for eligibility for the fund are laid down in council regulation (ec) no 2012/2002 establishing the european union solidarity fund. it should also be recalled that the purpose of the fund is the restoration of infrastructure and that as a refinancing instrument it cannot be used to compensate for damage suffered by private individuals. the authorities of slovenia, the czech republic and croatia estimated the total direct damage at eur 19 546 647. as regards slovenia, the direct damage is above the normal threshold for recourse to the solidarity fund and can be described as a 'serious natural disaster'. the czech republic and croatia, on the other hand, have direct losses below the normal threshold. in order to ensure that these countries benefit from the solidarity of the eu, i am voting in favour of the proposal.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the aim of the proposal is to establish an agency responsible for various systems in the field of information technology. i agree with the rapporteur on the single location of the facility, the staff and the data protection officer. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − we agree with the establishment of a new agency for the management of new large-scale information technology systems in the area of freedom, security and justice, whose tasks will be exclusively technical and operational management. the agency will not have the power to take policy decisions on, for example, the creation of new systems or the interoperability between different systems. we therefore believe that it is necessary to establish rules to avoid the de facto extension of its powers through the proliferation of pilot projects, without control or transparency. the agency will therefore be responsible for the supervision and security of the communication infrastructure and will ensure a comprehensive network for the exchange of information. it will therefore be essential to protect the network from any threat and to ensure the security of personal data. the legal framework of the various systems to be managed by that agency applies to a diverse set of member states with different levels of participation and to several associated third states. finally, we believe that the role of the european parliament must be clearly defined and strengthened to ensure adequate democratic control.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the council proposal for the granting of special treatment to certain products in the french overseas departments. the reasons which led the french authorities to request a separate scheme, accompanied by partial or total exemptions from duties depending on the product, are shared. these are the so-called outermost regions, where social and geographical difficulties are combined with production which is usually concentrated in certain categories of goods. i therefore agree with the granting of a special tariff regime, since in similar cases it is right to use these means to ensure the economic and social stability of these regions.
in writing. - we agree with the european council that specific measures should be introduced to assist the outermost regions, in view of their particular economic and social situation. the existence of permanent disadvantages such as insularity, remoteness of large markets, small size, mountainousness, difficult climatic conditions and economic dependence on a limited number of products seriously hampers the development of these regions and fully justifies the implementation of appropriate measures. this is the basis for the 'maritime duties' scheme, which authorises france to provide for the application, until 1 july 2014, in its four overseas departments, of a differentiated taxation scheme for 'maritime duties' in favour of certain local products. we believe that the 'sea duty' is an important instrument for the stability of the economy of the outermost regions, as it allows local production and employment to be maintained and is a valuable support for investment policies for local development. we also support the definitive implementation of these measures so that the outermost regions concerned do not find themselves in economic insecurity every ten years. we therefore call for the exemptions or reductions in the imposition of 'maritime duties' granted to the french overseas departments to be maintained beyond 2014.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the existence of permanent handicaps such as insularity, the remoteness of the large markets, the small size, the mountainousness and the difficult climatic conditions, as well as economic dependence on a limited number of products, seriously hampers the development of these regions and fully justifies the implementation of appropriate measures. this requires the introduction of specific measures for the outermost regions, taking into account the economic and social situation of these regions. this is the basis for the 'maritime duties' scheme, which authorises france to provide for the application in the four french overseas departments, until 1 july 2014, of a differentiated taxation scheme for 'maritime duties' in favour of certain local products of those departments. the 'sea duty' is of fundamental importance for the stability of the economy of the outermost regions concerned: the commission has also proposed that the 'sea duties' be increased to cover the costs of the transport of goods and services by sea, in order to maintain local production and employment. the revenue from the 'sea duties' accounts for almost half of the budget of local communities in the overseas departments and is intended to provide a key support for investment policies for local development, and this should continue to be the case. i am voting in favour of the development of these regions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it can help to support the development of certain maritime regions which suffer from permanent handicaps such as insularity, remoteness of the major markets, small surface area, mountainousness and difficult climatic conditions. the 'maritime duties' scheme allows france to provide for the application in the four french overseas departments of a differentiated 'maritime duties' taxation scheme until 1 july 2014 in favour of certain local products of those departments. the report adopted today suggests that guyana may extend the list of products eligible for differentiated taxation to some 50 products. the commission should consider the instruments for the final implementation of these measures beyond 2014 in order to avoid the outermost regions concerned being left in a situation of economic insecurity every 10 years.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the '112 universal service and emergency number' because i believe it has wide-ranging implications for various aspects of citizens' lives. in particular, the report provides a broad assessment of developments in the so-called universal services, of which the european emergency number 112 is the most important. i think it is extremely important to have a single emergency number to call in all the countries of the union, also in view of the approach of the summer period during which many europeans travel to a different country for tourism and holidays. in addition, the rapti report analyses developments in several other areas related to public health and services to citizens, among which i would like to highlight the facilitation of access to broadband, which takes into account the needs of the most vulnerable and disabled, favouring them in terms of the provision of services, materials and reduced rates.
in writing. - i welcome the report by mrs rapti which aims to improve accessibility to the european emergency number 112. in a european union where people are increasingly travelling for business or pleasure, millions of people could be in an emergency situation; and the fact that we have a single number at european level is certainly a great help. among the aspects which the report intends to assess, i consider very important the coordination of approaches and its financing, taking into account the specific needs of vulnerable people and consumers with disabilities. in addition, the 112 number does not replace the national emergency numbers, but provides a parallel service.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report by mrs sylvana rapti on the development of universal service also takes account of the specific needs of vulnerable people and consumers with disabilities. in view of the importance of the subject and the sensitivity with which it has been dealt with, the vote in favour is confirmed.
in writing. - how many europeans know that 112 is the european emergency number which can be called free of charge from landlines and mobile phones anywhere in the union? according to a very recent eurobarometer survey, only 26 percent; 58% feel that their fellow citizens do not have adequate information about it. in today's vote parliament urges the commission to strengthen the '112' service so as to ensure its smooth operation in all member states. it is also essential that this number is really accessible to the most vulnerable categories: who have hearing or speech or other disabilities. member states must also engage in information and communication campaigns using the most appropriate places for dissemination such as schools, universities, pharmacies, clinics, stations, airports, etc. the establishment of the 'european 112 day', to be held on 11 february each year, will also help to promote this emergency number, which, once established, will be a real lifesaver.
in writing. − the single european emergency number 112 is a service that aims to ensure quick and free access to emergency services for all citizens in europe, thus greatly simplifying the availability of the service, especially for those abroad. the adoption of the rapti report is the european parliament's response to the lack of awareness and knowledge of the potential of this service among european citizens, a misinformation that is undoubtedly a cause for concern. the ep resolution aims to create an effective information and awareness campaign in key locations such as doctors' offices, pharmacies, schools, airports and railway stations, and calls for the single service to be improved in quality, efficiency and accessibility, ensuring easy access for disabled and vulnerable people too. by providing clear guidelines to the commission on how to improve the use of the universal service, we have taken a step forward in protecting citizens living and travelling in the union, with a particular focus on social geographical inclusion.
in writing. - since 1991, 112 has been the european emergency number, enabling many citizens to receive help in situations of extreme need. voting today in favour of mrs rapti's report means ensuring that this aid instrument, which has helped to save many lives, is strengthened to the point where it is known and used in all eu countries as the single number to call to contact the emergency services anywhere in the union. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the european schools in the member states and the european schools in the union. the promotion of broadband investment can also be of great importance for the full use of the number '112' in a uniform manner in all countries and in all areas that are often difficult to reach (mountain, rural and island) in order to protect citizens by providing them with the right to prompt and appropriate assistance.
in writing. − we believe that the spread and affordable access to basic telecommunications services is important in order to promote social inclusion and competitiveness in the eu. our aim is to make broadband available to all european citizens by 2013, while being careful not to impose any additional burden on them. we believe that the following are necessary: the commission will continue to support the development of the digital single market, enhanced interoperability, confidence and security on the internet, much faster access to the network, increased investment in research and development, improved digital literacy, skills and inclusion, and the application of information and communication technologies to address societal challenges. in 1991, the creation of the single european emergency number 112 gave european citizens access to all telecommunications services allowing voice calls to national emergency numbers. we still believe that a better campaign of information and awareness-raising is needed to inform citizens about the functionalities of the 112 number, because of the poor quality of service that this number has offered them so far. finally, we support the commission's decision to carry out an in-depth study on the provision of internet services.
in writing. - dear colleagues, every three years the european commission reviews the scope of the universal service directive to adapt it to new needs and to the technological contribution that is increasingly essential for supporting citizens. the purpose of the universal service and the single european emergency number (112 - a single number for all eu countries) is to improve the safety net where basic social services are not guaranteed, to prevent social exclusion by ensuring access to essential services for people in rural areas and low-income groups, and to improve access to emergency services for the disabled. i have spoken in favour of this because i also believe that 112 and the emergency services in general should be given the importance and publicity they deserve for the role they can play in everyday life.

in writing. − i am in favour of this own-initiative report as it aims to assess recent developments in the universal service, including access to broadband, the coordination of approaches and its financing, taking into account the needs of people with disabilities. the report also addresses the issue of the single european emergency number '112', which aims to make the service accessible to disabled users and to improve its management through new technological platforms. promoting social inclusion and competitiveness are some of the areas towards which europe is moving in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. - my vote for this report on a more efficient and fairer retail market was in favour. the document expresses and defends many of the principles that the lega nord has always put at the heart of its policy, in particular with regard to the defence of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and small businesses. among the various points made in the report, i particularly welcomed the points expressing the concern of smes about the growth of shopping centres and the decline of local shops and markets. similarly, i particularly appreciated the intention of the report to stress that smes are the backbone of the european economy and that they play a unique role in job creation and i appreciated the intention of the rapporteur to denounce those unfair practices which affect small traders and, in many cases, consumers themselves. for the reasons stated above, my vote was decidedly in favour.
in writing. - i appreciate the spirit of this report, which seeks to support the removal of obstacles to the free movement of goods and services. i voted in favour of this document, which also has the merit of wanting to relax the current legislation and to suppress the national restrictive measures, which are often harmful and burdensome for smes. the eu must take decisive action to remove protectionist barriers that restrict access for businesses to the single market; at the same time, all initiatives that reduce the dominant position of a few players in the market, thus guaranteeing contractual freedom and protecting consumers, should be encouraged. i agree with the line suggested by the rapporteur in creating a self-regulatory system that sees retailers and the supply chain as parties, while the eu will have to engage in public-private partnership actions. finally, there is a need to increase the spread of electronic commerce, which can reduce the distance between consumers and products, and to introduce policies aimed at restoring confidence in the economic system through the harmonisation of payments within the eu, ensuring that businesses no longer have a fragmented and burdensome system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr corazza bildt because it represents a significant step forward in the modernisation of the retail and distribution sector. i particularly welcome the 'non-regulatory' approach proposed by the rapporteur, which emphasizes the exploration of other means before resorting to new legislation. the report shows that the appropriate rules exist, but that the free movement of goods is hampered by their inadequate application. at the same time, the interests of european traders and entrepreneurs must be protected by a fully functioning single market, removing the barriers that hinder its proper functioning. in this connection, two important documents are worth mentioning which help to stimulate the growth of operators in the sector: the single market act and the small business act, which aim to 'make life easier for small and medium-sized enterprises' by reducing the administrative burden on them. all this must be seen in the context of the principle of subsidiarity. finally, particular importance should be given to the section on improving efficiency and sustainability, encouraging the retail sector to invest in innovative solutions for logistics and transport, energy efficiency, and packaging and waste disposal.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the retail trade sector is a growth engine for the european internal market and at the same time a means of ensuring greater transparency and easy comparability of final prices for consumers. in view of this multifaceted and strategic role, i gave my full support to the report by mrs corazza bildt, since it is necessary to take legislative action as soon as possible on a sector which, i recall, allows access to goods and services in difficult areas (rural, mountainous, sparsely populated areas, etc.) where the presence of small retailers and local markets is a service to the community. i hope that the process under way in the member states to implement the directives (delayed payments, e-commerce, services, etc.) which this parliament has already considered to be important for the european market will be completed. finally, by voting in favour, i believe i have made an important contribution to that process of simplification and reduction of administrative burdens for european retailers as well, thus removing obstacles and constraints that could slow down growth and job creation in the eu.
in writing. − we believe that the time has come to concentrate all our efforts on free movement and free establishment throughout europe, fair, balanced and transparent trade relations, in order to promote more sustainable consumption. we believe that to bring greater efficiency and fairness to the retail chain, so that consumers can benefit from a more integrated market, we need: overcoming obstacles to the free movement of goods and services; increasing trust in online commerce; facilitate access to justice systems and apply alternative means of dispute resolution. the sector should also invest further in innovative solutions for logistics and transport, energy efficiency, as well as packaging and waste disposal. finally, we believe that a european action plan is needed, capable of developing a policy framework with specific proposals, with a more pragmatic approach, a more constructive dialogue between all the parties concerned and a careful monitoring of voluntary initiatives by the eu institutions. a firm commitment is needed against all trade barriers, restrictions of any kind at national level and all direct and indirect infringements of the internal market rules, through sanctions and infringement procedures.

in writing. - i voted in favour of draft amending budget no 3/2011, which proposes to account for and enter in the budget the surplus resulting from the implementation of the financial year 2010 and, consequently, to reduce the overall contribution of the member states to the budget of the european union for the next financial year. the commission is proposing to redistribute a positive balance of over eur 4.5 billion between the member states in the form of a reduction in the contribution planned for next year. i think it is worth pointing out that, while it is true that a reduction in the national contribution is helpful, especially in a period of economic crisis, we must not think that this is a prerequisite for a reduction in the overall budget in the future. the surpluses which have allowed a reduction in the contribution for the next financial year are the result of the implementation of the competition policy and the result of fines and interest on late payments, so that these revenues could be entered in the union budget without affecting the revenue from national payments. it is necessary to create a legal basis enabling the eu to treat these surpluses as its own resources so that they can be used in the public-private partnership system to build the infrastructure considered as a priority in the telecommunications, transport and energy sectors.
in writing. − i support the council's position by voting in favour of draft amending budget no 3/2011. i hope that in future the surplus from fines and interest will be reinvested in the union budget. this possibility has no legal basis yet, but i think it is important to bring this forward in future negotiations with the council on the multiannual budget.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the european union's 2010 budget closed with a positive balance of €4.5 billion. the budget surplus requires corrective action to return the excess money to the member states through the reduction of the contributions planned for 2012. i voted in favour of the report on the draft amending budget precisely because the union's accounts, which have been in surplus for several years and show an overestimation of the forecasts, must be brought back into line. some member states think that the budget should be reduced, while the idea of withholding these funds emerges from the parliamentary debate.

in writing. − we agree with this regulation, which aims to remove obstacles to crossborder cooperation between public authorities responsible for enforcing legislation designed to detect, investigate, bring to an end or prohibit intra-community infringements of consumer protection legislation. this will increase their confidence in crossborder offers, preventing traders and suppliers from evading the application of the rules, of course at the expense of the competitiveness of law-abiding traders and suppliers. we believe that the current sectoral approach to consumer policy initiatives does not facilitate consistent application. the commission should therefore be given a greater role in coordinating the implementation of pan-european activities. we also believe that in order to promote greater consumer protection in europe, the scope of this regulation should be extended to take account of the existing body of eu legislation on the subject, but in a more global and horizontal way. finally, the cross-border enforcement of consumer interests should be one of the political priorities of the union. enhanced cooperation between national enforcement authorities should become a more effective tool for european consumers to increase their confidence in the functioning of the internal market.

in writing. − the g20 concluded that, with regard to the resilience and transparency of the otc derivatives market, all standardised otc derivative contracts should be traded on exchanges or, where appropriate, on electronic trading platforms and cleared through central counterparties by the end of 2012 at the latest. in addition, otc derivative contracts will have to be notified to trade repositories. i therefore voted in favour of the report because the regulation in question, which promotes the resilience and transparency of the derivatives market, must also maintain the efficiency of these markets for investment by users, whether financial or non-financial. the maintenance of the international nature of this market promotes both objectives if it is based on cooperation between supervisory authorities and on convergent international criteria.
in writing. - we support the need to improve the supplementary supervision of financial undertakings belonging to a conglomerate. the supervisory authorities must be able to exercise their supervision of financial holding companies in a manner similar to that used for financial holding companies (banking sector) and insurance holding companies. it is also necessary to ensure that the european supervisory authorities issue general guidelines for the supervision of financial conglomerates through the joint committee; the transparency of the supervision of financial conglomerates should be improved, including through the publication of the list and structure of financial conglomerates; define mixed financial holding companies and include them in supplementary supervision; introduce stress tests at the level of each financial conglomerate and extend the scope to alternative investment fund managers. we believe that coordination at european level is necessary to make this adjustment binding.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the supervisory authorities must be able to exercise their supervision of financial holding companies in a manner similar to that used for insurance holding companies. in the future, the commission intends to undertake a more in-depth review of this framework in the light of developments in supplementary supervision. although this directive does not seem to prohibit member states from adapting their legislation in order to exercise this prerogative over such mixed financial holding companies, coordination at european level is useful in order to make such adaptation binding.

in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, reading the newspapers in recent months, terms such as short selling or credit default swaps have unfortunately entered the common language and not for good reasons. they have been the instruments through which this harmful speculation has been and is being carried on, to the detriment of our states and our citizens. that is why it is important that regulations are put in place, but they must be careful and not be the result of an emergency. i therefore agree that the trilogue should be continued in order to try to achieve a balanced and shared text which does not demonize these practices. the original text of the proposal was rather restrictive and was, in fact, intended to block this type of activity. the text voted on in the econ committee is much more balanced, thanks to a number of amendments. the only point of concern at the moment is article 12, which provides for restrictions on naked or uncovered short selling, including cds. i really hope that the trilogue will reach a shared and balanced agreement.
