in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on short selling and credit default swaps, since it aims to harmonise the member states' short selling rules in order to eliminate the differences which currently exist and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. it also introduces common transparency obligations at eu level and harmonises the powers that regulators can use in exceptional situations, i.e. in the event of a serious threat to financial stability or market confidence.
in writing. - the report under discussion today is of particular importance as it provides for the amendment of directive 97/9/ec of the european parliament and of the council on investor-compensation schemes. i welcome the amendment of the directive currently in force, provided that the new union rules are aimed at increasing the harmonisation and integration of the european single market, strengthening consumer protection and improving financial stability within the union. i agree with the rapporteur that stricter common rules are needed not only to ensure higher levels of cover to protect investors and faster and more efficient repayments but, above all, to finance the systems at national level: those who make crossborder investments should enjoy the same level of protection in all member states. in my view, in a globalised market such as the present one, we cannot ignore the need to improve the harmonisation of investor compensation systems at eu level. i believe that only by achieving this objective can the level of protection of european investors be improved, helping to ensure a level playing field for them in the internal market for financial services and at the same time strengthening the european single market.
in writing. − the new eu rules should increase the harmonisation and integration of the single market in investment. in order to strengthen consumer protection, generate greater investor confidence and improve overall financial stability, higher levels of coverage are necessary and it is necessary to harmonise investor financing and compensation systems across the union in the long term. as regards the latter, we believe that the coverage of investor compensation schemes should be extended to firms authorized to make investments of any kind and in any form. we are in favour of total harmonization rather than a minimum one, in order to strengthen the protection of those involved and avoid the risk of arbitration between member states. we also believe that a principle of 'risk-sharing' should be included in this directive, whereby contributions for each member are determined on the basis of the degree of risk taken by the undertaking. in order to avoid that some member states reduce the size of their funds, the loan facility should only be launched when the funds of all systems have sufficient financial resources and should only be started after all systems have reached the target level of funding.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that we must restore confidence in investment and i believe that this report is a step in the right direction. an investor shall be protected to the maximum extent against the possible risks of bankruptcy of the holders of its deposits: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the compensation guarantee threshold is increased, with adequate and risk-adjusted financing. harmonisation at european level is also necessary to prevent and avoid market distortions; the commission has also proposed that crossborder investments be allowed the same protections as national investments. the security and stability of markets are essential to restoring consumer confidence, and the work of the new european authority, esma, can and must contribute to this. i hope that this package of measures will be useful in getting investment going again and with it the whole european economy.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr schmidt's report. the proposal for a directive, which follows the one on deposit guarantee schemes (dgs) for banks, amends the system of compensation for investors in the event of the insolvency of intermediaries (investment firms, but also credit institutions) by laying down a series of rules on the amount guaranteed and the system of contributions. i regret that, given the distance between our positions, we were unable to reach agreement at first reading and that we will now have to proceed to a difficult second reading. i believe that this sector too must be regulated as quickly as possible in a way that is appropriate and harmonized throughout europe.
in writing. the report on 'investor compensation schemes' was voted on today at the strasbourg plenary session. the three main objectives of the report are: improve consumer protection through higher levels of coverage, improve the single european market for financial services and harmonise investor compensation schemes across the union, and set sound long-term principles for the financing of investor compensation schemes. the new eu rules should lead to greater harmonisation and integration of the european single market, strengthen consumer protection, generate greater trust between consumers and depositors and thus improve financial stability.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the amendments to the directive on investor compensation schemes should be geared to improving consumer protection, with a view to further harmonising the european single market. total harmonisation of the amount of compensation is preferable to harmonisation of the minimum level, as it ensures greater protection for consumers, strengthens investor protection and avoids the risk of arbitration between member states. the harmonization of the financing of compensation schemes is also desirable, provided that the target level of financing is not too high. the funds should cover cases of mismanagement and fraud in relation to depositary receipts.
in writing. - as regards the directive amending the previous one on investor compensation schemes, i voted in favour, as i believe it is essential to improve consumer protection through greater coverage, faster reimbursement and more efficient protection systems. in addition, the functioning of the single european market for financial services needs to be improved and investor compensation schemes across the union need to be harmonised, as well as sound long-term principles for the financing of investor compensation schemes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr schmidt, which aims to achieve further convergence of european compensation systems, in particular by improving consumer protection through higher levels of cover, implementing the harmonisation of investor compensation systems within the union and laying down principles for the financing of investor compensation systems. the text voted on would, in essence, reduce the margin of discretion of the member states, thus protecting european consumers more effectively and more securely. this harmonisation would not only improve the level of guarantee but also affect the methods of financing the systems and the calculation of the contributions to be paid by operators.
in writing. - the discussion was wide-ranging and articulated, with different positions often difficult to reconcile. i voted in favour of the work done by my colleague because she has taken due account of the concerns raised by the member states with regard to the cultivation of gmos. in particular, i think it is important that the possibility of prohibiting or restricting the cultivation of the plant within one's own territory remains: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. the need for more coherent and balanced legislation between the system of authorization of gmos on a european basis and the urges of the states to decide autonomously how to implement the standard has created some difficulties in reaching a common position. the principle of subsidiarity remains intact when a state decides to apply legislation that is more stringent than european standards. it is absolutely essential that research on gmos should not be stopped. the sine qua non is that the maximum transparency in consumer knowledge is guaranteed by the traceability of gmo products.
in writing. the european parliament voted today to allow member states to decide for themselves whether to allow or ban gm crops on their territory, based on an examination of the social and environmental impacts that could result. it is well known that there is a deep-rooted mistrust of gm products among european citizens. according to eurobarometer surveys in 2010, around 61% of europeans are uncomfortable with such products and over 53% think they are harmful to their health. this lack of public confidence in these agricultural products cannot be ignored, and at the same time the local agricultural tradition rooted in each member state cannot be forgotten. in fact, it is precisely in the light of these elements that the resolution should not be understood as accepting gmo products, but only as recognizing greater national autonomy to structure an agricultural policy that is better adapted to the territory, to the tradition linked to it and to the sensibilities of the citizens who inhabit it. i hope that this vote will be the beginning of a debate at all levels on the cultivation of gmos in the union.
in writing. − the current european regulations on genetically modified food and feed set a very strict framework which, if properly applied, should allow for a high level of protection of human life and health, animal welfare, the environment and consumer interests, while ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market. the directive's requirements for risk assessment are not being met and these shortcomings are the reason why several states oppose the cultivation of gmos on their territory. we believe that environmental assessment and monitoring should be strengthened and that the powers of states should be strengthened in the absence of relevant elements concerning the impact on their national territory. the high level of protection of health and the environment can only be achieved to the extent that member states can effectively have all the necessary studies both on the recipient environment and on the conditions of the surveillance plans. the measures taken by member states should apply to a given gmo or, if necessary, to a group of gmos with similar characteristics rather than to all gmos. such measures must always be justified by the so-called 'scientific criterion' and by any cross-border contamination.
in writing. - i wanted to express my vote in favour of this report, since it fully reflects our position on the cultivation of gmos. i think it is essential that the member states should be free to decide whether or not to cultivate these organisms in the way they consider most appropriate. there may be legitimate environmental, socioeconomic and geographical-territorial reasons which can (and should) allow states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos. i do not want the freedom to grow gmos granted by the european union in this area to be translated into a coercive obligation and thus not to allow for proper distinctions: i want our lands and our tradition, with its world-renowned agricultural excellence, not to be destroyed by the reckless use of artificially modified substances and organisms, which have nothing to do with everything that nature already offers us in abundance.
in writing. - i appreciate the work done by mrs lepage and i believe it is essential that member states increase controls on gm products and the environmental impact that such production may have on the various national ecosystems. the commission must, however, be obliged to follow up these checks, which cannot be left to the national authorities alone: we cannot have gmo products imported or authorised in only a few member states, such as mon 810 maize, and then have them in our diets. i therefore call for greater coordination between the european and national institutions to identify the long-term environmental impacts of genetically modified crops, adjacent crops or on neighbouring land and, above all, the impact on human health through direct consumption and on animal health through the use of feed from products of these crops. we therefore call for a greater commitment from all the institutions to ensure that there is a certain and thorough verification before any type of genetically modified production can be authorized.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the lepage report on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmo products on their territory because i believe that every country in line with european principles should have the possibility of self-regulation in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity. many people consider gmos to be dangerous, the general public does not like genetically modified products, but the report in question does not create any problems for the public as it protects and guarantees their health. consumers risk nothing from the product point of view as much as traders from the market point of view. on the contrary, member states are free to introduce specific prohibitions in this way, depending on the case.
in writing. - i share the approach of the rapporteur, mrs lepage, who wants to give member states the power to ban the cultivation of gmos for reasons other than health and environmental reasons, which are the responsibility of efsa. the decision to introduce certain foods or crops cannot be left solely to efsa, as only national authorities can properly assess the environmental and socio-economic impact of certain crops.
in writing. - i congratulate mrs lepage on her excellent work. the european parliament voted today, by an overwhelming majority, in favour of the right of member states (and their regions) to ban the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) on their territory, even if they are authorised at community level. this is a clear signal from the european parliament to the council and the commission: the eu authorisation system must be maintained, but it must be recognised that the agricultural and environmental impact, as well as the socioeconomic impact, may justify bans or restrictions by individual states. if this regulation becomes law, it would mean that eu member states could ban or restrict gm crops from their territory on agro-environmental grounds, such as resistance to pesticides, invasiveness of certain crops, or threat to biodiversity. i believe that all member states should take measures to prevent conventional or organic farming from being contaminated by gmos, and also ensure that those responsible for each incident are financially punished. it is now up to eu governments to speak out.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i believe that it is appropriate to allow member states, in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity, to prohibit or restrict the cultivation of gmos on their territory, including for reasons other than adverse effects on health or the environment. the final text gives member states greater discretion as to whether to introduce specific bans, while still ensuring a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, and at the same time ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market. the guarantee of full protection of european consumers, who are often opposed to gmos and their use in agriculture for reasons that go beyond food safety, is nevertheless ensured. the text does not change the situation for countries which, like italy, already do not allow gm crops.
in writing. - on the report on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory, i voted in favour because i believe that it is necessary to leave individual member states the opportunity to prohibit the cultivation of gmos for reasons such as environmental protection. i also thought it right that the authorization procedure at european level should not be changed but should rather be supplementary to the decisions taken by individual states, since authorization remains the sole responsibility of the european commission, following the opinion of the eu food safety agency.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the actual draft of the new hungarian constitution is not acceptable. the hungarian authorities should consider amending the new constitution, particularly its preamble, so that it guarantees equal protection of the rights of every citizen, no matter which religious, sexual, ethnic or other societal group they belong to, and to include in it an explicit declaration on the separation of church and state. with this resolution we recommend the hungarian authorities to explicitly include all fundamental civic and social rights and to ban the death penalty. the primary source of law must provide sufficient guarantees concerning the protection of fundamental rights and discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation. the hungarian authorities should also ensure the existing guarantees on protection of national minorities, personal data and the transparency of publicly relevant information.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it calls on the commission to come forward, as soon as possible and before the end of 2011, with a proposals to achieve a 25% internal greenhouse gas reduction by 2020. one of the key points of the text is its emphasis in calling for more investments in renewable energy and energy infrastructures. the report also stresses the need for the eu to use the appropriate diplomatic means in order to dynamise the international climate negotiations while maintaining the pressure on third countries to deliver their share of global ghg reductions in the future.
in writing. − the report proposes to adopt a new commission proposal that the eu could be able to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 30% by 2020 instead of the 20% originally proposed. however, it does not seem advisable to forcefully accelerate the current action plan. the latter has proved effective and well calibrated, so that the eu is already making a substantial contribution to reducing gas emissions. the international actors who should be asked to be more committed and sincere in the fight against emissions are others, in particular the emerging countries of asia. the eu's increased commitment, as called for in this report, would only be effective if it was accompanied by a similar effort by the other industrial powers of the world. the eu and its citizens cannot bear the burdens of the other parties to the conflict. in the light of the foregoing considerations, i have decided to vote against the report.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the eickhout report after the vote on the amendments because i thought it was a good compromise text in the face of certain positions which are extremely ideologically biased and lacking any sense of realism. there are no adequate grounds for a drastic increase in the eu's 2020 emission reduction target, which should be based on careful verification and a detailed analysis of the cost implications. this is all the more so at a historic stage of the crisis when too many european companies are closing down and too many others are struggling under the strain of credit constraints and competition from emerging countries. to impose further environmental constraints on them would be to place them in further difficulty. the rejection of the final text will inevitably open up a new season of difficult negotiations which we can only overcome successfully if we can combine achievable environmental objectives with support for business productivity.
in writing. - parliament today rejected the increase in the emission reduction target to 30% by 2020. the report referred at various points to the alleged health, environmental and economic benefits of moving to a unilateral 30% reduction target, without sufficiently assessing the consequences of such a move for eu-wide development in the absence of an international agreement. we must bear in mind that while the environmental effects of a 30% changeover would be insignificant overall, given that the european union produces only 10% of emissions from human activities, the effects of such a changeover on the competitiveness of the industrial system would be significant, with heavy economic impacts and significant employment spillovers. i would remind you that the conclusions of the environment council of 21 june also stressed the importance of achieving the 20% energy efficiency target by 2020, while blocking any change in the commitments made to reduce greenhouse gases. without comparable commitments from industrialised countries such as china and the united states, it would be premature to change the targets already set without first carrying out a thorough cost-benefit analysis also at member state level.
in writing. − the threat of climate change to humanity shows no sign of abating; the frequency and intensity of extreme environmental events have increased. the failure of the international community to conclude a comprehensive and binding international climate treaty in copenhagen does not mean that countries are not taking action. the cancun meeting shows that countries are taking action and that negotiations have gained new impetus. we believe that moving towards a domestic greenhouse gas reduction target that is compatible with the eu's climate goals can go hand in hand with a healthier economy, more green jobs and innovation, and would also bring greater benefits for european citizens through improved air quality. we believe that there should be constant verification of the achievement of the ceilings set up so far: the european emissions trading system will be able to stimulate investment in green technologies and innovation. we believe, however, that the commission's proposal for a 30% reduction in greenhouse gases by 2020 is too ambitious, too difficult to achieve and, above all, too costly for european smes.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, mr eickhout's report on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions has sparked debate in parliament because of the strategic importance of this request. changing the greenhouse gas reduction rate from 20% to 30% changes the europe 2020 forecast. this is certainly important for the fight against pollution and for the protection of the health of citizens, but to reduce emissions further in such a short time is also to put european companies at risk on the international market. not only would industries have practical difficulties in adapting to the new emission levels, but they would lose competitiveness outside europe where the parameters to be met are far less rigid.
in writing. − outside of a legally binding global international agreement, involving comparable commitments by other industrialised states and adequate efforts by emerging countries, there is no adequate justification for a unilateral increase in the eu's 2020 emission reduction target. it is premature to accept the commission's assessment of a possible 25% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions compared with 1990 levels if the eu's target of increasing energy efficiency (20% increase by 2020) is reached. before doing so, a thorough check is necessary, as well as a thorough examination of the implications in terms of costs. in the context of international climate negotiations, recognition of this result at this stage does not seem appropriate because it undermines the unilateral commitment already made by the eu (-20% by 2020) in the eyes of the other parties. it is also premature to recognise the 'milestones' identified in the roadmap before the completion of the necessary in-depth assessments of their implications at member state level. i have therefore voted against the report.
in writing. - i am very pleased that this report on the european commission's communication 'analysis of the intervention hypotheses for a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions of more than 20% and assessment of the risk of carbon leakage' has been rejected. we could only say the opposite, because at a time when companies are enduring a global crisis and, in europe in particular, unfair competition from third countries, it is not possible to ask for an additional effort than what has already been agreed. outside of a binding global international agreement involving comparable commitments by other industrialised states and adequate efforts by emerging countries, there is no adequate justification for a unilateral increase in the eu's 2020 emission reduction target. the commission's communication also points out that many of the co2 reductions at present are linked to the economic crisis which has led to the closure or relocation of plants to third countries. i understand but i do not share the view of the rapporteur who would like to live in a bucolic world of forests, green pastures and small animals and no industry. the reality is very different and i'm sorry to say it. people need to work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the analysis of the assumptions for intervention for a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions of more than 20% and the assessment of the risk of carbon leakage, as i consider it essential that a global agreement on this matter be encouraged. the eu is one of the leading international actors in the field of the environment, and unilateral action to reduce co2 emissions would only risk weakening the competitiveness of european industries in the international market. moreover, it is not certain that unilateral action can lead to a level playing field with the other major players on the global stage. in any case, a desire to achieve a higher emission reduction target than the eu2020 target is present in the assembly, even if there was no concrete follow-up to the vote.
in writing. − despite agreeing with many of the points included in this report on cohesion and the strategy for cohesion policy after 2013, i was forced to abstain. the support which the document expresses for small and mediumsized enterprises and local economies, whose interests have always been defended by the political line of the northern league, is certainly to be shared. however, the rapporteur's intention to promote the establishment of programmes for roma minorities is not entirely to be shared. the lega nord does not consider the roma to be a 'disadvantaged minority', but rather a minority that rejects any form of integration and positive interaction with our society. i do not intend to support the promotion of programmes in favour of this group, so i could not vote in favour.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the policy of economic, social and territorial cohesion remains one of the eu's fundamental pillars for reducing the development gaps between geographical areas and sectors of society and the economy. it is a good way of promoting integrated and systemic growth, stimulating initiative and civic sense and enhancing the development of responsibility and the common good. the experience of the current 2007-2013 programming period shows that in the next programming period, the key is to give greater responsibility to actors, beneficiaries and recipients for strategic and operational programming, implementation, monitoring and control of the achievement of the objectives, through incentive and disincentive systems for achieving the targets, which make it possible to make the processes and active participation in them more transparent. the whole governance and management architecture must also be made more flexible and simplified, enhancing the integration capacity of the different territorial realities in the cross-border, inter- and intraregional spheres. finally, it requires that the resources and objectives of cohesion policy for the next programming period are adapted to the challenges facing the eu, including the 2020 strategy. i believe that the report i helped to adopt points the right way.
in writing. - i welcome the report by mr pieper, because i believe that cohesion policy - as also stated in the treaty of lisbon - is one of the foundations for the future development of europe, particularly by addressing the regions whose development is lagging behind. it seems to me important - as pointed out in paragraph 84 - that there should be more controls and stricter rules in the use of the structural funds in order to avoid irregularities and fraud. i would have preferred to have accepted the attempt to table an oral amendment to delete the reference to the three working languages (english, french and german) in addition to the national language in which the documentation must be submitted: i think that the national language and english would be sufficient to avoid additional costs and complications for those concerned.
in writing. − we believe that the eu must do more to rapidly expand renewable energy, to increase its storage capacity and to ensure the supply of sources and the security of raw materials. structural and cohesion policy must play a key role in issues related to future competitiveness and bring more smes closer to growing international markets. however, a policy geared to growth and innovation can only work in the presence of a barrier-free, highly harmonised internal market. such a policy can only be sustainable if a link is established between regional policy objectives and european-level objectives in the field of innovation and research. a strong cohesion policy is only justified if the original promoters of the projects are european programmes which add value; in this respect, a more precise and aggressive 'european added value' needs to be defined. we believe that compensatory measures are needed at regional and social level: the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (emah) is a step in the right direction.
in writing. - colleagues, the european union's cohesion policy needs well-defined strategies for the future and, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, projects must be formulated to take account of the socioeconomic integration of the member states. the report for which i voted in favour underlines the importance for the union of adopting an effective cohesion policy which will enable europe to play a leading role on the international scene in the near future. the role of the regions and small local authorities in each state will therefore be fundamental, since, although they are already well integrated into international trade, they will have to face the risks of a loss of economic weight and thus of general welfare. the emergence of states such as china, india, brazil, etc., and the predictions of the demographic future of europe, with a shrinking and ageing population, will take away space and influence from the old continent.
in writing. - i voted against the amendments which were intended to introduce a limitation of the eligibility periods for those regions which have not proved capable of achieving significant improvements in their economic, social and ecological situation, not because i believe in european-based assistance, but rather because the role of cohesion policy is that of a development policy aimed at improving the living conditions of the population and developing a balanced and sustainable growth of the communities. it would therefore be absurd to think that delays, sometimes due to causes not attributable to the population, would deprive us of the financial instruments which are essential to the development of our citizens.

in writing. − on the motion for a resolution on the commission's fifth report on cohesion and the strategy for cohesion policy after 2013, i voted in favour as i believe that structural and cohesion policy has a key role to play in issues related to future competitiveness. the regions and cities of europe, and their businesses, are already deeply embedded in the global economy, which is a fact that depends on the european history of the individual nation states. the economic fabric of europe is therefore considerably more complex than the structures of asia or north america. more than half of the global links between multinational enterprises and their subsidiaries have their roots in the union. cohesion policy must make more use of this still-present advantage of the international network by bringing more small and medium-sized enterprises closer to growing international markets.

in writing. − financial support means the transfer of financial resources from an external funding agency to the public treasury of a partner country, provided that the latter respects the agreed payment conditions. the eu grants financial assistance only to countries that meet certain eligibility criteria, such as: a clearly defined national development policy and strategy, a stability-focused macroeconomic environment, a credible programme to improve public financial management, which is to enter into force or is being implemented. aid should be given only to countries that meet minimum standards of governance and respect for human rights. the partner country must also demonstrate sufficient transparency, reliability and efficiency in the management of public expenditure. it is important to establish a systematic involvement of parliaments and civil society in the dialogue on anti-poverty policies and on annual reviews of financial support. we believe that this system should also allow information to circulate between civil society and the general public, so that citizens, universities and private organisations can provide their views in the context of the consultations of the thematic groups, set up specifically to monitor financial support for the
in writing. - the european union allocates funds to developing countries in accordance with a set of strict criteria, such as well-defined economic development policies and strategies, sound projects guaranteeing macroeconomic stability and a credible programme to improve the management of public finances. many of these countries are trading partners of europe and so providing financial support for their development also means encouraging investment by our companies, expanding trade and creating jobs. in addition, this is an attempt to give greater stability to the governments of these countries and, consequently, better prospects for stability and better living conditions for the entire socio-political structure.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr goerens because i strongly believe in the future of financial support for developing countries, provided that the criteria for granting financial support are analysed and implemented objectively with a view to improving its effectiveness. of course, we must avoid the many mistakes and waste of money that have occurred in recent years - i would stress this, at the expense of the european taxpayers - and which have for the most part gone unpunished. if we are to really help the people most in need, the eu's foreign and security policy must focus on promoting democracy and human rights and peace, which are fundamental requirements for sustainable development: all the necessary measures must therefore be taken to combat corruption in the countries receiving aid, including appropriate sanctions such as, for example, a proportional reduction in the allocation of future quotas.
in writing. - the report by mr wagner makes it clear that an integrated european energy network is essential to ensure both security of supply and diversification of sources. i believe that in order to achieve these objectives, which are also recognised by the recent treaty of lisbon, it is right to give priority to energy infrastructure, which is also considered by the commission to be obsolete and poorly connected. we must tackle this infrastructure deficit, and the measures in mr wagner's report are aimed precisely at that. the difficult and crisis situation in bilateral relations between the energy-consuming and the energy-producing countries is further proof that it is necessary to think about tomorrow, about a genuine community energy policy. the wagner report is a first step in that direction and that is why i have given my support to the honourable member.
in writing. − this year, as we celebrate the 60th anniversary of the european coal and steel community, i share the opportunity to launch a reflection on the european integrated energy network. this objective is even more ambitious than in the past because it concerns the energy sector as a whole. in my view, the climate and energy package is the effective synthesis of europe's energy priorities, on the basis of which to orient the european union's strategic measures. the green paper 'a european strategy for sustainable, competitive and secure energy' is recognised as the most ambitious document on european energy policy to date, but it is only with the lisbon treaty that the primary objective of promoting the interconnection of energy networks is enshrined. such infrastructure is essential to achieve ambitious objectives such as ensuring security of energy supply, security of energy production, price stability for consumers and the creation of a single energy market ensuring access to affordable energy sources for european businesses. finally, i would draw the commission's attention to the need for strict commitments in the field of energy policy, since, because of the many national interests involved, there are tensions between the member states and an excessive fragmentation of the energy market.
in writing. − the sudden power cuts that have hit italy and many other member states in recent years demonstrate the need for the eu to clarify the coordinates of its energy policy and develop a coherent strategy, both within the union and with supplier and transit countries, to prevent further power cuts. that is why i voted in favour of this report. however, i would like to make it clear that the promotion of an efficient energy strategy must not lead to indiscriminate support for authoritarian regimes in central asia, nor must it weaken the eu's position vis-à-vis turkey, which, thanks to its role as a transit country, is acquiring increasingly strong conditional power vis-à-vis the eu itself. i therefore vote in favour, but only if the points i have just mentioned are respected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is a positive own-initiative text from parliament in response to the commission's communication 'energy infrastructure priorities for 2020 and beyond'. i welcome the strategic approach of the document, which calls for systemic change, putting a proper, integrated and reliable energy network at the heart of the european political strategy, coordinating and optimising networks at continental level. i agree with the rapporteur that a new method should be used, leading to the identification of the infrastructure map which will enable the creation of a new european super-network interconnecting networks at continental level, focusing on a limited number of priorities to be implemented by 2020. finally, i believe it is crucial to set up innovative infrastructure financing instruments, optimising the leverage of the european union on public and private funds (public-private partnerships) and strengthening collaboration with international financial institutions, combining innovative and existing financial instruments, so that they become flexible and are built according to the different risks and financial needs that each project faces at different stages of development. in addition to the traditional support instruments (grants), equity participations, project bonds, rsffs, loans and guarantees for ppps may be offered.
in writing. − the modernisation of europe's energy infrastructure and the consequent development of an integrated network is one of europe's priorities. the european union currently imports more than 50% of its energy from non-eu countries, which have seen an average price increase of 15% in the past year. this situation highlights the importance of diversifying energy supply routes and building an interconnected and flexible network, which overcomes the various national bottlenecks and allows efficient supply capacity in the different areas of europe. in this respect i agree with the rapporteur on the importance of selecting infrastructure projects on the basis of the clear objective of the european overriding interest and balanced development between the regions. finally, the financing procedures need to be simplified in order to attract more private investment, which has declined slightly in recent years and which is essential for open and transparent energy development.
in writing. - it is now necessary to reflect on the need to create an integrated energy network at european level, i.e. common to all its member states. it is essential to act on demand and on the renewed objectives of european energy policy, such as: sustainability and promotion of renewable energy, competitiveness and opening of markets, security of supply and diversification of sources. the latter must become a decisive element in a policy to safeguard the necessary supplies. the famous '20-20-20' is the effective summary of european priorities; the european council has also adopted a compass to guide europe's strategic measures. we believe that the necessary infrastructure must be identified, criteria must be established for selecting worthy projects and financing must be ensured to attract and stimulate private investment. if we are to make any real progress, we must also make very firm political commitments and invest heavily. finally, we believe that once a project has been declared to be of european interest, a single contact authority should be designated in the member state ('one-stop shop') which should act as an interface, ensuring understanding and communication between the promoters, authorities and citizens concerned and also coordinating between the 'one-stop shops' and the commission's dg energy.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr wagner's report because it is important that the european institutions, and in particular the european parliament, should define the objectives to be achieved in greater detail in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. the priorities in particular are, as also highlighted among the main objectives of the lisbon treaty, energy-related. in the energy field, europe is making a major step forward in reducing greenhouse gases, achieving full energy efficiency and switching to renewable energy. as a result, investment in energy policy has increased dramatically, so much so that energy is now a key issue for the future of all of us, which must be managed within the community.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe that the objective of achieving a genuine internal energy market requires the resolute participation of the european institutions, together with all possible efforts by the companies in the sector. energy infrastructure is often outdated and poorly connected, whereas it would be indispensable to achieve long-held objectives such as reducing carbon levels, ensuring security of supply and creating a single energy market that ensures affordable access to energy sources for businesses and citizens. this requires projects of european interest which involve citizens from the outset and which provide for the establishment of a 'one-stop shop' which acts as an interface between promoters, authorities and citizens concerned.
in writing. − i am in favour of the report on energy infrastructure priorities for 2020 and beyond, as it is essential to create an integrated and competitive internal market. in addition, the ten-year network development plan should identify electricity and gas infrastructure projects, selecting those of european interest which should contribute to the completion of the internal market, promoting energy efficiency and renewable energy and improving security of supply. smart grids should be one of the energy infrastructure priorities for achieving the eu's energy and climate objectives. investing in research and innovation remains one of the eu's objectives in the context of economic, social and employment growth.
in writing. − the report on the priorities for energy infrastructure for 2020 welcomes the priority corridors identified by the commission agreeing on the need to optimise limited resources. i voted in favour of the report because it reiterates that while the responsibility for the design and development of infrastructure projects lies primarily within the market, the eu has a role in promoting some projects, granting them the status of 'project of european interest' and providing public funding to some of them, but it requires a clear and transparent methodology to determine the selection of priority projects that can meet pressing european needs. the report concludes that the following criteria should be taken into account in order to justify projects receiving priority: the project must have a european dimension, i.e. a clear eu public interest, its necessity must be demonstrated on the basis of the infrastructure hierarchy, it must also be in line with energy efficiency, climate and environmental objectives, it must be consistent with the eu's long-term energy policy (allowing for flexible and multifunctional application and avoiding bottleneck effects), it must offer good value for money and cost efficiency, and it must be technically sound.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as i value its proposal on the establishment of a high-level multi-stakeholder working group, co-chaired by the ep and the commissioner on social affairs. i strongly support its final aims to identify and find solutions to the problems faced by users and providers of social services of general interest. we need to prevent the current financial and economic crisis from putting the development of social services of general interest at risk. in the long term this would harm the growth of employment, the increase in fiscal contributions and the aggregate consumption. it seems also urgent, as stressed by the report, to conduct an assessment of the social consequences and impact on people’s lives of liberalisation measures in sectors that are essential to social progress (transport, energy, water, postal services, telecommunications, etc.). the commission should prevent any further liberalisation measures from being taken until this assessment has been submitted.
in writing. − i agree with many passages in the report on the future of social services of general interest, which has many points in common. the commitment to the social integration of women, and of women in need or victims of violence, is essential. it is essential to maintain the national competences of the member states in the field of social services, giving them priority over the imposition of a uniform and uniform european model. however, i decided to abstain because of certain clauses in the report which stress the urgency of promoting policies for the benefit of immigrants and the need to create employment for them. the lega nord believes that the first beneficiaries of such policies should be the citizens of the union, especially at a time of crisis such as the one we are going through.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the internal market, competition policy and fundamental freedoms have accompanied the growth of an open and integrated european union. the economic vision which originally fostered its constitution is not the only dimension of a political reality which intends to participate in the governance of globalisation. it is in fact a community of other dimensions from which common visions and policies are born, which must put the individual at the centre of their horizon. this change in approach makes it all the more important to foster the creation of an economic and social environment in which the needs of the development of one's identity and the response to the basic needs of daily living and the outlook on life are the driving force of public action. in this perspective, social services of general interest take on a greater and different importance. the economic aspect, which is important in terms of budgetary compatibility and medium- and long-term sustainability, plays an important role, but it is still subordinated to the main objective of the development of the human person and the quality of life, including in its family, social, work and institutional dimensions. i think the report we have adopted supports this view.
in writing. − high-quality universal services such as health, education and childcare and essential network services such as transport, energy and telecommunications can ensure a healthy, active, cohesive and inclusive society. this is why social services of general interest (ssigs), as economic and social pillars essential to our societies, should be adequately funded by the eu. together they make a very significant contribution in terms of jobs, economic activity and purchasing power. in view of the current economic crisis and unemployment, we believe that citizens need access to high quality social services of general interest more than ever, and our economies and society need the benefits that such services could offer. we therefore believe that a substantially strengthened eu budget, a greater role for the eib, the establishment of a high-level multi-stakeholder task force and the recommendations of the third biennial igss forum are all necessary. the reforms should address, inter alia, the role of enterprises, social economy actors and voluntary organisations in the provision of ssigs, as well as the mandatory compliance with national and local social and quality criteria in procurement.
in writing. − services of general interest cover a wide range of activities, ranging from large network enterprises such as energy, telecommunications, transport, audiovisual and postal services, to education, water supply, waste management, social and health services. these are services which are essential to the daily lives of citizens and businesses and which reflect the european model of society. the adoption of this resolution today serves to underline the important role these services play in the pursuit of social, economic and territorial cohesion throughout the union. they are key to the eu's sustainable development in terms of higher levels of employment, social inclusion, economic growth and environmental quality. eu action, in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity, is aimed at promoting social cohesion, while ensuring democratic choices regarding the level of service quality offered.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it highlights the role played by local and regional authorities and their networks in increasing the impact of the european development policy. the rapporteur reiterates that the quest for a strong impact policy should not only be focused on a purely quantitative and short-term assessment of the results. the text calls on the commission to formulate a comprehensive assessment policy based on clear-cut criteria and indicators. in addition to this it urges the eu institutions and member states to monitor and report on governance practices in developing countries (including fighting corruption, improving public financial management, enhancing transparency and upholding human rights). it is extremely important to focus on poverty eradication as the crucial criterion for the allocation of eu development aid.
in writing. - i have spoken negatively about this report on the impact of eu development policy. the report, which focuses on the promotion of human rights, contains some points that are certainly shared, especially those on support for women, the elderly and other vulnerable sections of society. however, the report does call for the promotion of pro-immigration policies in several places, which are not clearly defined and are not convincingly justified by the rapporteur himself. because of these immigration clauses, i could not therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the kaczmarek report. the maintenance of a modern eu development policy must be supported, especially at a time of crisis, as investments in poverty reduction and suppression can generate strong benefits for the union in terms of investment and new jobs. it is therefore necessary to implement and increase the impact of development policies aimed at the ambitious objective of poverty reduction, a focal point of eu external action. in this respect, efforts should focus on the concept of 'democratic ownership', a key approach involving direct investment in good governance, greater democracy and human rights, and the fight against corruption. the private sector, and in particular smes, should be more actively involved in the development support process, as they are key players in sustainable development and in achieving the objectives set. finally, the focus should be on industrial development that provides greater potential for transforming national economies and, in comparison with agricultural exports and the extraction of natural resources, offers the possibility of ensuring even more productivity growth in the long term.
in writing. − the european union has made significant progress in developing and implementing development policies over the past decades. projects, actions and development funds have been mobilised to create a reality that involves many aspects of the lives of all european citizens. supporting this report today, at a time like the present, when the debate on the next mff is taking place, means emphatically reiterating the need for a common strategy which guarantees, in financial terms, territorial, environmental and human development. i share the need for high impact aid, the inevitable goal of inclusive development, as also recalled by the eu2020 strategy, and the involvement of the private sector in the development process. i believe that the latter is a vital factor in the sustainable development of the many smes in europe.
in writing. − the main objective of eu aid must be the reduction and eradication of poverty. an approach to governance that emphasises human rights, democracy and the rule of law, the fight against corruption and the role of parliaments and civil society in holding governments to account and assessing development performance is important for this policy. growth is an important driver of development. it should be environmentally sustainable, respect biodiversity and prevent the worrying degradation of fertile land. the eu should therefore promote agro-ecological and low-input practices. we also support the importance of the development of social security systems and fair tax systems, as well as the promotion of the ilo's decent work agenda. finally, we believe it is particularly important that access to basic social services, in particular health and education, should remain a cornerstone of community aid. a modern european development policy therefore needs the understanding and participation of european citizens: further efforts will therefore be needed in development education and awareness-raising, based on the values of human rights, democracy, tolerance, social responsibility and gender equality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is the right way to achieve the main objective of the european union's development policy: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the future of the european union. to enhance the impact of european development policy, better coordination and harmonisation based on the principle of ownership, as well as a governance approach based on the key concept of 'democratic ownership' are needed. access to basic social services, especially health and education, is crucial to facilitating sustainable growth, and these should account for at least 20% of total eu assistance.
in writing. − i am opposed to the report on strengthening the impact of eu development policy, as it presents some problematic aspects: the request to introduce a financial transaction tax; the european union is also calling for an increase in the funds allocated to development aid and finally for the establishment of a new body within the eeas to deal with the coherence of the union's external policies. since the creation of new bodies and the imposition of new taxes would require additional efforts on the part of the eu countries and their citizens, i am voting against this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text presented by mr kaczmarek on the impact of the european union's development policy. the report is geared to an analysis which, on issues of particular importance (such as high impact aid, the concept of inclusive development and the involvement of the private sector in eu development policies), pays due attention to and assesses the possibility of a change of direction from what has been established in the past.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the report on consumer information is a new and important step for europe towards achieving its specific objective of protecting consumer rights. i thank the rapporteur, mrs sommer, and all the shadow rapporteurs, and in particular the shadow rapporteur for my group, mrs glenis willmott. but if it is true that europe can now look to the future with greater confidence, having strengthened the effectiveness of the instruments for food protection and transparency, it is equally true that the agreement at second reading reduces, albeit in part, what was approved by this house at first reading. we would have expected more, mr president, for example, on the origin labelling of agri-food products. the obligation to indicate the origin of all meat, which the new article 25 gives us, is a very important innovation that meets the expectations of large parts of european consumers. at the same time, it cannot fail to stress its less ambitious nature than the introduction of mandatory labelling for all fresh and processed agricultural products containing only one ingredient, which this house had just approved. and the very labelling of meat in annex xi excludes some important productions which require as much protection, such as rabbit meat, for which the reasons for the exclusion are not understood. however, the road to food transparency has been paved and now we must pursue it with the same commitment and responsibility that has brought us here.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the key word in this report is 'consumer'. we often forget who we're looking to when we make decisions. in order to give the consumer more accurate information, important decisions were taken in the report under discussion, such as the indication of particular nutritional values or the indication of origin. it's a step forward, but it's not the end. the indication of origin for agri-food products, the origin of the main foodstuffs constituting a product, should be the first information available to the consumer. there are several cases where traceability is crucial, the last in chronological order the bacterium that unfortunately has caused several victims. by identifying the origin of the product, it is possible to take timely action or to protect the product from misinformation. the competitiveness factor is equally important: the indication of origin is often synonymous with guarantee and quality. the various excellences of each country have won the trust of the consumer. we support the indication of origin because the consumer has a right to know what he is eating.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, fifteen years after the bse emergency, it is time to take stock of the implementation and prospects of the european legislative framework and the related controls on feed and food. as the rapporteur said, the data indicate that the number of positive cases in the european union has fallen from over 2 100 cases in 2001 to just over 65 cases in 2009 and that in the light of this epidemiological downward trend, the legislation applied can be considered to have contributed to the eradication of bse. the report we are about to vote on therefore represents an important opportunity to begin the process of adapting the legislative provisions to the real risk situation with commitment and responsibility. a good sign of this is the review of the ban on animal meal in animal feed. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the animal health standards are respected. this is an important new element and, while fully respecting maximum food safety, it is of particular strategic importance, especially in the light of the current protein deficit in the european union. at the same time, of course, we should not lower our guard on control and surveillance. this is something that must be avoided if europe's extraordinary progress in consumer protection and animal health is not to be undermined.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, gender equality is a fundamental right and it is one of the fundamental principles of the eu. gender equality is also a condition for economic growth, social inclusion and well-being in our societies. the under-exploited pool of well educated women represents real untapped potential for the eu economy, especially at a time when human capital is a key factor in terms of our competitiveness and when, as a society, we are ageing. eu member states might be very different, as the rapporteur has said, but they face a common challenge: the under-representation of women in high-level decision making, in particular in the corporate sector, is a reality almost everywhere. i know that there are fierce debates about voluntary agreements versus binding quotas. i know too that there are five eu member states which have followed the norwegian example and have introduced binding measures to increase the number of women in business leadership. no later than last week, two member states, belgium and italy, adopted legislation to impose gender quotas in business leadership. irrespective of the solution found in individual member states – and we know that there are other member states that have binding quotas for state-owned companies, or general voluntary agreements – one thing that is clear is the business case for gender equality. this evening and tomorrow at voting time, parliament will, i hope, take a strong position on this important issue. i thank vice-president rodi kratsa-tsagaropoulo for her efforts to bring the european parliament into this debate and for her bold report, and i would also like to thank the members of the committee on women’s rights and gender equality, who backed her almost unanimously. why, in the european union, do women constitute 60% of university graduates but only 12% on the boards of the largest publicly listed companies, and only 3% among the presidents of those boards? the question is: can europe afford this? the answer is no, and it is not simply my answer. it is the answer from studies commissioned by businesses such as mckinsey and deutsche bank, indicating that there is a positive correlation between the presence of women in senior positions and company performance. so gender-diverse boards improve corporate governance and, from a micro-economic perspective, companies that have introduced gender diversity on their boards can also mirror the diversity of their employees and customers. by the way, 80% of purchasing decisions are made by women so it is an advantage to have women on the board, and there is a business case for increasing their involvement in management and corporate decision making. the commission is determined to advance gender equality further. you know about our strategy and you also know i have made it very clear that ‘women on the board’ should be one of the aims we pursue. that is why, in march this year, i brought together the ceos and board chairs of big publicly listed companies to discuss possible ways forward. i wanted to give self-regulation a last chance, and i have encouraged companies to develop credible self-regulatory initiatives to make significant progress. i have called on the eu’s publicly listed companies to sign the ‘women on the board’ pledge for europe and voluntarily to increase women’s presence on corporate boards to 30% by 2015 and 40% by 2020. after one year – i.e. in march next year – i will see which and how many companies have signed up to the pledge. i will assess the situation to see if there has been significant progress and if we have credible commitments. i hope the answer will be yes. should it be no – should there be insufficient progress with self-regulation – then the commission will explore policy options for targeted measures to enhance female participation in decision making. for me what counts is the end result, and the direction that parliament takes tomorrow with this vote will undoubtedly be a very strong source of inspiration: not only for the commission but also, i hope, for the corporate world.
the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very good one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. in this report i am thanking mr kratsa-tsagaropoulou for the great effort he has made in accepting many of the proposals and objectives which i, as shadow rapporteur and s&d group, have put forward together with other colleagues. in the european union, women are underrepresented, already in senior management roles, with just 12% of the cdas of listed companies. in this context, we ask the european commission - and we are pleased to have heard commissioner reding's serious commitment - to propose by 2012 legislative acts providing for binding quotas, reaching the percentages of 30% by 2015 and 40% by 2020, in case of insufficient measures taken in the member states or by companies. in this respect, it is already a very encouraging sign that six countries, including italy, have recently passed legislation to this effect by a bipartisan vote. i would like to make it clear that this is not just about quantitative quotas, but also about improving the performance of the business system by sharing management, not only in large companies but also in small and mediumsized ones. we therefore propose that more instruments be used in the field of corporate social responsibility, from family-friendly services to flexible working time arrangements and training for women in management. it is also important to understand the link between the presence of skills and the role of women at the governance levels of a company with a different approach in the management of processes, the enhancement of human resources, anti-discrimination rules and sustainable productivity that they often ensure. i would also like to raise another point in reply to what mr bauer rightly said earlier, namely that we have not just provided for quotas for women, but we have provided for an important mechanism which was one of our proposals, namely that the participation of women and men be linked to a mechanism of greater transparency in appointments, in the selection of men and women, so that it is a benefit for all and not just a reserve for women.

package is fundamental to our response to the crisis: to strengthening and giving teeth to our economic policy coordination, in terms of both prevention and correction; to achieving sound public finances; and to avoiding harmful macroeconomic imbalances. i firmly believe that 99% of this package has been agreed. the council and parliament have both made important improvements to our original proposals. parliament has, for instance, codified the european semester and set up a structured economic dialogue, providing for a prominent role for parliament throughout the european semester. it has created the opportunity for detailed discussion of country-specific situations at every stage of decision-making, and it has obtained a commitment from the commission to carry out a study on eurosecurities within six months of the entry into force of the legislation. the commission will also commit itself, in the declaration accompanying the study, to reviewing the intergovernmental nature of the european stabilisation mechanism by mid-2014. honourable members, you have won an equal role for parliament in determining the scoreboard for detecting possible macroeconomic imbalances. you have inserted firm guarantees on social dialogue, respect for national traditions in relation to collective agreements, wage formation and the role of social partners. yet it seems that this is not sufficient, and therefore it is not possible to conclude the legislative process before the summer break. that is very disappointing. i hope that the council and parliament will pull out all the stops to reach an acceptable compromise on the issues that still divide them, so that this package can enter into force as soon as possible. looking beyond the vote, i welcome the ambition and scope of the vision outlined in the report. i share the view that we must look further ahead and focus on the long-term implications of the crisis for the european project. i assume that a clear majority of all of us here agree that deeper economic integration will have to be part of the answer, despite current trends that appear to go in the opposite direction. regarding your call for the commission to present a report on eurobonds, in the context of the economic governance package, the commission has agreed to table such a report on the feasibility of eurosecurities towards the end of the year. these eurosecurities would aim to strengthen fiscal discipline and increase stability, as well as ensuring, by taking advantage of the increase in liquidity, that member states enjoying the highest credit standards would not suffer from higher interest rates. this issue really has to be seen as part of the overall governance reform that will materialise through the adoption of the package. i appreciate your support for improving the european union’s role as a global player in the context of the g20, the imf and other elements of global governance. i am also glad that you have paid particular attention in your report to the issues of competitiveness and convergence, and sustainable growth and jobs. the paramount importance of growth policies cannot be overstated in relation to tackling the crisis. to conclude, i trust the commission and parliament share the view that a convincing response to this crisis and the effective prevention of future crises will require stronger, broader and earlier coordination at european level. this is at the heart of the economic governance package. in my view, the first concrete reaction to the final report of the special committee on the financial, economic and social crisis, as prepared by ms berès, must be the speediest possible adoption of the package. it does not yet mean completion of the economic and monetary union but it is certainly a very big step in that direction – and it is essential to restore confidence in the european project of deeper integration and an ever-closer union.
the decision taken by this parliament two years ago to set up a committee on the financial, economic and social crisis has proved to be a courageous and far-sighted one, in the light of the results which were set out in the mid-term report and in the final report which will be adopted today. it was not easy to make that choice and above all to keep the issues of the financial crisis together with the economic and social effects which have proved to be very dangerous in much of the world and, for us, especially in europe. so we've done important work, and it comes to an even more important conclusion. each of the hypotheses set out in the report foreshadows a strengthening of europe's institutional, political and economic structures in order to emerge from the crisis in a lasting way. this was far from a given and i think it should be appreciated, especially at a time of great difficulty such as the one europe is going through. the information contained in the document concerns: the creation of a minister of the treasury; own resources for the budget of the union; eurobonds and the financial transaction tax; the tax coordination assumptions, which are indicated there; the recognition that knowledge is fundamental to the creation of quality employment in the future for young europeans; the european union is a major player in the world economy. there are, however, some new developments which foreshadow a strengthening of the european union, a union which has become a little stagnant and is even suffering the most severe blows of the crisis itself. there are difficulties today which we cannot underestimate or ignore, but which can be overcome by applying correctly and consistently the guidelines contained in the report.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the sommer report because i believe that european citizens should be able to make a free and informed choice about their food. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take action to combat fraud. these are rules of common sense which have the merit of giving citizens the freedom of choice in order to ensure a healthy, balanced and conscious diet. this regulation is the instrument through which citizens will be able to assert their specific needs in the choice of foodstuffs.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, thanks to the compromise reached between parliament and the european council, european consumers will now be able to know where the meat they eat comes from. the amendment i tabled, which is part of the institutional compromise, was certainly more ambitious and called for greater labelling of the origin and provenance of other products, not only meat but also milk, dairy products in general and meat used as an ingredient in food. it is, however, gratifying to know that a step-by-step approach has been identified which will lead the commission to present a specific report on the subject within two years and within three years, which will then lead to proposals which will shortly enable european citizens as a whole to have greater and more complete protection.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the sommer report is certainly a milestone, but i would say it is only a milestone, not a final milestone, as mr uggias said. there are two- and three-year deadlines, which the commission has committed itself to respecting, deadlines in which it will certainly be possible to finalize the rules adopted, albeit laboriously, with laborious and appreciable negotiations lasting many years, because something may have escaped us. i take this opportunity to say that i think this report is generally positive and therefore i voted in favour, but i think the commission should make an effort to reassess some of the shortcomings, such as the lack of inclusion of rabbit meat, which is recognised as one of the best white meat in terms of nutrition and diet and which could be included in the evaluation that the commission has committed itself to do over the next three years, with a compatibility assessment that i hope i can develop as soon as possible.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, today's vote marks the end of an incredible cycle of work which has seen over 3 000 amendments tabled in three years. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a dispute between the commission and the member states. i welcome the new specific indications on the content of allergens, for example, the presence of which will be highlighted in a timely and recognizable way at a glance. finally, as an italian, i can only welcome the final abandonment of the so-called traffic lights. no food can ever again be labelled as harmful if it is not, forcing consumers to exclude it completely from their diet. this will make it possible to integrate it consciously into a varied and balanced diet, which i hope will follow the guidelines of our beloved and enviable mediterranean diet.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, my country, italy, receives a steadily increasing flow of tourists every year and, as the holiday season approaches, what happens every year is about to repeat itself: foreigners' offenses will go largely unpunished, except for those who are stopped at the scent of crime. but not for long, because we welcome this measure which aims at last to standardize the procedure for identifying the data of the owner of the vehicle with which the infringement has been committed. some facts: as many as 15% of speeding offences in the member states are committed by foreigners and the percentage of those who visited italy by car last year is 67%. you can see that this directive represents an important prerogative for my country in the identification and recovery of many claims on the state, which still weigh on the accounts of local authorities. i also welcome the fact that, in addition to the usual speed limit, the offences also include failure to wear a seat belt, driving at red lights, the high alcohol content of the driver, the effects of drugs, to name just a few of the most frequent. i therefore share the approach of the directive which does not seek to affect national regimes concerning the criminal or administrative nature of infringements and for which i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. − in order to cross the external borders between the eu member states, certain travel documents were required at the time of the intergovernmental cooperation on schengen. the list of travel documents enabled the border control authorities to verify whether a particular travel document was recognised by the schengen code and consular staff to verify whether the member states considered it necessary to affix the visa sticker. in the present institutional and legal framework, we believe that the list of travel documents should be kept up to date and that the member states should communicate their position on whether or not to recognise such documents, in the interests of simplification and efficiency, thus ensuring the fullest possible information in this respect. we are also of the opinion that the list of travel documents should be legally binding. the proposed wording duly respects the competence of the member states to recognise or not to recognise travel documents and, at the same time, guarantees legal certainty after the given period, which could indeed be longer than the commission's proposal.
