in writing. - i am firmly convinced that the right to privacy is one of the cornerstones of democracy. the continuing technological development can jeopardize this right and i therefore believe that the old rules, although still substantially current, must be adapted to new requirements. the report by mr voss, which i supported by voting in favour, highlights the changes that must be made so that every european citizen can be guaranteed, even when he has relations with third country nationals, the privacy that must be protected as a guarantee of our freedom. i also agree with what is stated in the document, namely the adoption of rules with a high level of protection of sensitive data, which ensure the right balance between the right to privacy and the right to information and expression, and finally rules which do not unnecessarily hinder the daily processing of such data. this means that, in general, sensitive data must remain secret, except where the data subject himself expressly wishes to derogate from this rule.
in writing. − the new threats to the protection of personal data caused by technological developments must be adequately addressed by the european union. i am referring, for example, to the widespread use of social networks such as facebook and twitter, which involve the creation of real digital profiles containing personal information that needs protection, which has not been adequately guaranteed to date. i therefore fully support mr voss' report, as it seeks to ensure a uniform level of protection for individuals and to strengthen principles such as transparency, purpose limitation and prior, informed and explicit consent. the data subject must be able to have the data deleted, corrected or blocked and must be informed of any misuse, without however underestimating aspects of great importance such as the need to specifically protect minors. for these reasons, actions such as the introduction of the principle of accountability through the mandatory appointment of data protection officers and the application of severe and dissuasive sanctions, including criminal sanctions, for the misuse and abuse of personal data have my full support, in the belief that the european parliament has taken the right direction to ensure an adequate level of protection for citizens.
in writing. − the rapid pace of technological development in the global information society requires comprehensive and consistent data protection legislation. the current lack of harmonisation between the national laws of the member states makes the adoption of a comprehensive legal instrument at european level necessary. every citizen must have the right not only to be fully informed about the processing of data concerning him, including the sources and recipients, but also to obtain comprehensible information on the logic underlying any automated processing of such data. we therefore support the need to introduce a general principle of transparency for the processing of personal data, to provide for specific forms of protection for vulnerable persons, to maintain the derogations allowed for certain journalistic purposes in order to protect the freedom of the press. finally, we call on the european commission to study the modalities for introducing a general obligation to notify personal data breaches (currently limited to the telecommunications sector only), to set up a system for notifying personal data breaches on the model of that introduced by the eprivacy directive and to provide for a special restrictive regime for 'sensitive data', which will therefore require a clear definition of the latter.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia (- > point 1.6.10). the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat the situation in the former yugoslavia. the report endorses the measures on the protection of personal data in the european union envisaged in the commission communication, and draws attention to the principles set out in the 1995 data protection directive which have not been fully implemented in the member states, such as the principle of transparency, the principle of purpose limitation, and the other provisions on consent. the new data protection regime should reduce bureaucratic and financial burdens and carefully assess the application of certain rules by small enterprises.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is important to commit fully to a comprehensive approach to the protection of personal data in europe. this protection must be provided by a set of coordinated legislation which is balanced, that is to say capable of protecting the citizen without placing an undue burden on the bureaucratic duties of the companies. in particular, such rules should not affect the right to freedom of expression and information by unnecessarily hindering the normal and harmless processing of personal data on a daily basis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr voss on the protection of personal data within the eu. i consider it important that the text adopted refers to the measures set out in the 1995 data protection directive, which, for various reasons, have not yet been fully implemented in the member states: i refer in particular to the principle of transparency and the principle of limitation of purpose. the text voted today should mean that the new data protection regime will not only reduce bureaucratic and financial burdens but also involve a more careful assessment of the application of certain rules relating to small businesses.
in writing. - the proposal for a regulation under discussion today on consumer information in foodstuffs is one of the most important topics currently under discussion at community level in the food sector and, in my view, to the extent that it can ensure uniformity of rules at union level, it can make a decisive contribution to the revival of the competitiveness of european agri-food businesses. in particular, i believe that the compromise reached and resulting from the interinstitutional trilogues responds both to the need for correct consumer information and to the protection of the key role played by the food industry in the processing of raw materials to produce the 'made in italy' that is recognised and affirmed throughout the world. although i believe that a fair compromise has been reached in the regulation of allergenic substances, by providing for their inclusion in the list of ingredients without the need for repetition elsewhere on the label, i express reservations about the possibility for member states to introduce, at national level, mandatory information in addition to the system of common rules. in my view, there is a risk that we will have to deal with 27 different systems of rules and that we will have to bear the increased costs of periodically updating the advice in each country and reviewing the labels.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs sommer's report because i think it is very important to have adopted this regulation which lays the foundations for ensuring a high level of consumer protection in the field of food information, defining in a general way the principles, requirements and responsibilities governing food information, and at the same time reducing trade distortions, burdens and red tape. i appreciate the choice of the ppe group to mediate with the other groups to get the report voted on: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the improvement of the comprehensibility of food packaging will make it possible to distinguish original products from so-called 'like products': this is even more important for italy, which has always been a home of excellent products and is often the target of agri-food piracy.
in writing. - the european parliament's approval of the sommer report shows that it is concerned about the transparency of information on the nutritional value and origin of food, in line with the european consumer's demand for greater safety in the products purchased. parliament adopted a resolution on the commission communication entitled 'the european union's role in the fight against drugs: a strategy for the future' (com (90) 050 final). the s&d group played a leading role in the negotiations, convincing the council and the commission to consider further adoption of rules of origin for meat used in packaged foods, as well as the effects of the use of hydrogenated fats, which are now covered by the legislation. the text approved today marks a recognition of the italian approach, which has already shown in the past how to protect and promote italian and european excellence, and is therefore a source of satisfaction for both italy and the operators in the sector. however, while this is an important step forward, our efforts to ensure that european citizens can make increasingly informed choices about the products they bring to their tables will continue.
in writing. − after almost three years of debate on the right to full and comprehensive consumer information, in which the various players took different positions, we have finally reached a good result that reflects most of the expectations of consumers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies. we wanted to bring the public's attention to the important role that a label plays in the final stage of product purchase. the aim is to ensure that consumers can recognise the product and to provide them with the nutritional information necessary for an informed choice. i would also add a healthy choice, considering that an agri-food label is a valuable tool in the prevention of cardiovascular disease and in the fight against obesity. the fight against land piracy is now being intensified and the protection of agricultural and food production is now gaining momentum.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, food labelling protects and informs consumers, allows for a detailed classification of the product and makes the purchaser's choice conscious and safe. finally, at european level, mrs sommer's report has defined a harmonized regulatory framework which will also facilitate those companies which will no longer have to comply with the rules of the member states to which they export their products but which will be able to rely on a single regulation which, although not perfect, is nevertheless a huge development for the european food market. in particular, in the light of recent developments concerning viruses and bacteria transmitted from infected animal meat, i believe that the mandatory origin labelling of fresh meat is important.
in writing. − consumers are at the heart of eu information policy and as such must be best protected. i voted in favour of the report on the provision of food information to consumers, because i believe that the new regulation, as drafted, allows consumers to check directly the composition of the products they buy. the energy content and the percentages of the various ingredients must now be indicated, and the country of origin labelling has been extended to include more products than under the previous directive. the new law not only ensures better consumer protection but also reduces red tape, thereby helping smes, which account for more than 80% of the european food sector.
in writing. - i am convinced that this recommendation will help to boost the competitiveness of agri-food businesses, insofar as it ensures complete uniformity of rules. i regret that the text provides for the possibility for member states to introduce additional compulsory information at national level in addition to the system of common rules. however, the compromise seems to respond both to consumer information needs and to the protection of the important role played by the food industry in processing raw materials for the benefit of the 'made in' concept. with regard to nutrition labelling, i welcome the forecast of the average daily requirement (adr) expressed on the label as a percentage, also with reference to the portion of the food. i believe that clear information to the public on recommended daily intakes can prevent and significantly reduce the pressing problem of obesity, and help consumers to make more informed and healthy choices when buying food. i would also like to support the requirement that a certain font size be used to ensure that the label is clearly legible. finally, i am pleased that the commission has chosen to proceed with caution in introducing the mandatory indication of trans fatty acids, which can be found in food not only as a result of a production process but also as naturally occurring.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr sommer because it will provide a better guarantee for european citizens by significantly improving the rules on the traceability of foodstuffs. it is important to emphasise that the new label will increase transparency in the supply chain, allowing the origin of the product to be understood with certainty at all stages. this is a clear sign of what the community institutions are doing to ensure greater consumer protection and safety, not only in the food sector but also in others, with the principle of traceability increasingly present in various production sectors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the ayala sender recommendation on the cross-border exchange of information on traffic offences because i firmly believe in the objective which guided it: road safety. more than two years after parliament adopted the proposal, the agreement reached after the trilogue of 20 june also saw the council accept certain key elements for the extension of road safety legislation at international level. although the council has maintained a rather rigid position throughout the negotiations, i am satisfied with the message that has come out of this parliament, namely that international recognition of serious traffic offences such as speeding, drunk driving and failure to wear seat belts is a fundamental objective to be achieved. the implementation of the legislation we voted on today is of two kinds: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment.
in writing. the new directive is an important step forward in identifying and punishing foreign offenders guilty of serious offences such as speeding, driving under the influence of drugs or not respecting red lights, which claim the lives of many people every year. a new procedure for exchanging vehicle registration information between member states will make it easier to trace foreign offenders, who often enjoy unjustified impunity because of the inability to trigger effective sanctioning procedures. transport commissioner siim kallas also pointed out that foreign drivers are three times more likely to commit offences than residents and that many seem to feel that the rules do not apply to them when they are abroad. with this directive we want to put a stop to this dangerous situation. it is worth recalling that in 2010 there were 30 926 road deaths in the european union and that the economic costs to society are estimated at €130 billion per year. although there has been a decrease in road fatalities of 11% compared to the previous year, much remains to be done to ensure that our citizens are safer on the roads throughout the eu.
in writing. − in europe, the proportion of non-residents involved in road accidents, particularly those caused by speeding, is extremely high. the adoption of the council's position at first reading is a first step towards a common transport and road safety policy. among the substantive changes indicated, many provisions originally proposed and strengthened have been removed entirely from the text. as a result, the new text now limits itself to an exchange of information between member states through an electronic data exchange network to identify the vehicle which committed the infringement. three member states will not participate in the directive, as the new legal basis chosen by the council has allowed an opt-in option for ireland and the united kingdom and an opt-out option for denmark. this decision will have a negative impact on the fair and equal treatment of european citizens, maintaining a general feeling of impunity. we therefore propose that member states should be required to communicate more effectively and more strictly, and that these obligations should be strengthened in terms of timing and content. we are in favour of a review of the enforcement procedures and the harmonization of road rules and inspection procedures.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, ensuring safety on the european road network is the primary objective of this recommendation on the council's position, a text which after two years of work seems to have reached a real conclusion with a good agreement on road traffic in europe. that is why i voted in favour of the directive which will allow the exchange of information between european countries on traffic offences, in particular to combat drunk driving, speeding and the failure to wear seat belts. states will also be able to recognise the infringement at international level and to apply appropriate sanctions accordingly.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is extremely important to continue on the road to harmonizing the road codes of the various countries of the european union. in particular, it is necessary to allow for an adequate exchange of information at cross-border level to ensure the prosecution of road traffic offences even if they are committed in countries other than the country of residence. the proportion of non-residents involved in road accidents, particularly those caused by speeding, is unfortunately still extremely high. as if that were not enough, the penalties imposed for infringements committed by a driver in the territory of a member state other than that of residence still remain unpunished in most cases. this undermines the eu's road safety objectives, and weakens the legitimacy of these checks in the eyes of european citizens. we must now continue along this path so that closer cooperation between member states can ensure ever more complete road safety throughout the european network.
in writing. - i am in favour of the parliament and council directive to facilitate the crossborder exchange of information on road safety infringements. the proposal arises from the fact that penalties imposed for infringements committed by a driver in the territory of a member state other than that of residence are in most cases unpunished, in particular for automatically registered infringements. the text allows for the exchange of data and leaves greater autonomy to the states in road safety matters. in addition, there is no harmonisation of national road codes, as the aim remains to punish irresponsible drivers when they commit offences in a member state other than their own.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr ayala sender because i consider it to be a step forward towards a common transport policy in the field of road safety. the establishment of a procedure for identifying the data of the owner of the vehicle with which a cross-border infringement has been committed is of considerable importance. until now, despite the existence of numerous bilateral agreements between member states on the identification and transfer of data, the offenders have enjoyed unjustified impunity due to bureaucratic obstacles. the adoption of this text - which has the disadvantage of not introducing a standard european model for the notification of infringements - will undoubtedly raise safety standards on european roads and motorways, allowing the identification and possible punishment of offenders.
in writing. − as laid down in article 312 tfeu, the regulation on the multiannual financial framework is adopted by the council after obtaining the consent of the european parliament. article 312 (5) provides for the three institutions to work together to find a solution 'in the course of the procedure for adopting the financial framework': this implies the need for preliminary negotiations. as mr böge has pointed out in his report, these negotiations have not taken place. the council has asked parliament for a mere approval, without any attempt to reach a common solution. the council has also failed to respond to parliament's request for greater flexibility. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that parliament cannot give its approval to the draft council regulation establishing the financial framework for 2007-13. i hope that the voice of this institution will be heard in all future proposals, as article 312 of the tfeu requires.
in writing. − this recommendation on the draft council regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2007-13 underlines that the council adopted the draft without consulting parliament, thus breaching article 312 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which was intended to strengthen the role of parliament itself. as this recommendation concerns a purely procedural matter, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. - with regard to the multiannual financial framework, we believe that, in view of the increase in needs and the reduction of margins, as well as the increasing use of the flexibility instruments provided for by the iia (adjustment and revision of ceilings and mobilisation of the flexibility instrument, the european globalisation adjustment fund, the european union solidarity fund and the emergency aid reserve), greater flexibility is needed. we believe that the present interinstitutional agreement should be considered operational until the new regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework enters into force, with the exception of the points in the annexes which are now considered obsolete following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia on the basis of the conclusions of the european council in strasbourg on the situation in the former yugoslavia. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, a new council regulation is necessary for the multiannual financial framework 2007-2013. the council adopted the proposal. the report by mr böge highlights the disagreement. the main reason is that the proposal does not provide for flexibility in the event of a revision of the mff below 0.03% gross. parliament stressed the need to maintain the current flexibility and in this case the unanimity of the council was not necessary to decide on a revision. after seeking legal advice, parliament considered that the existing rules, which are still part of the interinstitutional agreement, should remain in force until the new regulation providing for the entry into force of the mff. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (emah) was adopted unanimously.
in writing. - the report on the commission's work programme for next year contains points which i strongly disagree with. the call for the eu to establish new forms of own resources and the renewed desire to continue the process of enlargement in the balkans area mean that my vote cannot be in favour of the joint resolution. it also contains points which i share, particularly on the work programme on agriculture, the economy and sme policy. i therefore abstain.
in writing. - in recent years, the agri-food industry has been affected by a number of epidemics, the most representative of which is certainly the disease of transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (tses), commonly known as mad cow syndrome. in the mid-1990s, the spread of this disease in the union was more than 2 200 cases and has so far resulted in 207 deaths. i would like to point out that this epidemic has radically changed not only the european framework for the management of food crises but also the public's perception of these issues. even today, more than a decade later, a eurobarometer survey shows that 62 percent of europeans feel that they are unable to protect themselves against diseases such as mad cow disease. it is therefore important for citizens to know that there is constant monitoring of spongiform diseases in europe, which can prevent and ensure, if necessary, early detection. i agree with the rapporteur on the validity of the commission's proposals on the 'tes plan 2nd edition'. finally, i hope that the member states, together with the european union, will ensure that the european legislation on feed and food is strictly applied.
in writing. - we all remember the very serious consequences of the "mad cow" syndrome, a striking example of how the desire to get rich as quickly as possible often overpowers everything, in this case leading to very serious consequences both from the point of view of health and economic. we remember the many cases of deaths and the crisis in the beef sector. changing the habits of herbivorous animals is an example of how human nature is much more willing to recognize itself in unlimited enrichment. it is true that the number of tse/bse cases in the european union has decreased sharply in recent years, and this is an important evidence of the effective prevention measures taken in recent years. however, i fully agree with the rapporteur that, given the seriousness of the phenomenon, control and surveillance measures must be strengthened. i also fully agree with the need to encourage research in this area where knowledge is not yet complete. only in this way will it be possible to adopt and justify future policy decisions and protect the health of citizens in the global system.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, my support for mrs roth-behrendt's report is a tribute to the success achieved in recent years through constant monitoring action which has led to the almost total eradication of the bse problem on the basis of the number of positive cases in europe which has fallen from 2167 in 2001 to around 65 in 2009. the difficult time europe experienced during the bse epidemic is still alive among european citizens who for the first time faced a food emergency, but also a production collapse that devastated the economy of many rural areas. we therefore welcome the second edition of the strategy paper on transmissible spongiform encephalopathies, so that monitoring can be effectively continued alongside the development of rapid ante- and post-mortem tests for the diagnosis of bse and research into this animal health problem, which has become a bad chapter in european agriculture.
in writing. − consumer protection, animal health and the eradication of transmissible spongiform encephalopathies are our main objectives and must therefore be of the utmost importance in the evaluation of changes to the current rules. for this reason, we call on the commission and the member states to continue to monitor their development closely, with particular attention to the spread of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (bse). we believe that the primary objective of any measure in this area should always be to achieve the highest level of consumer protection and food safety. the precautionary principle should therefore always prevail where scientific knowledge is not sufficiently advanced or in-depth. the commission will be required to inform parliament of any new findings in this area; the proposed changes to the feed ban will only be supported under certain conditions; processed animal protein derived from animal parts fit for human consumption will have to undergo further sterilisation processes and any changes to the list of specified risk materials will need to be carefully evaluated. finally, we believe that research should be encouraged in areas where knowledge is not yet complete. only in this way will it be possible to adopt and justify all new political decisions in the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i believe that we must not let our guard down over the threat posed by transmissible spongiform encephalopathies, which have already threatened european citizens in the past, causing considerable damage to our cattle production. it is now more necessary than ever to clarify the existing legislative framework, updating it on the basis of the latest scientific evidence, in order to make it increasingly useful for consumer protection and animal health.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr roth-behrendt on legislation on transmissible spongiform encephalopathies and related controls of feedingstuffs and foodstuffs. fourteen years after the summer of 1997, when the outbreak of the so-called 'mad cow disease' broke out, i believe it is essential to insist on the strict monitoring of bovine spongiform encephalopathy and on the monitoring mechanisms, the prohibitions on the use of animal meal in animal feed, the list of specified risk material, the culling of cohorts and mechanically separated meat. only by taking such control measures can we prevent the spread of new, feared epidemics in the member states, which put the health of european citizens at risk.
in writing. the european union, together with all the democratic institutions of the member states, has an undeniable obligation to guarantee the security of its citizens against a global phenomenon such as terrorism. this obligation often involves the difficult task of mediating between restrictions on the exercise of certain freedoms and the guarantee of security. the civil aviation sector is the most concerned. mr pascual's report contributes to the debate and joint reflection of the three institutions with a view to adopting new measures and making further progress in the fulfilment of this duty. i share the call for harmonised eu-wide standards to be put in place, setting out the operating conditions and a set of common standards for the detection efficiency of scanners, and i therefore give my full support to the work done by my colleague.
in writing. − this report proposes the introduction of body scanners at airports, in order to further reduce the risk that potential attackers will be able to carry dangerous materials on board aircraft. the danger of new attacks has not diminished, but has been confirmed by the recent attacks in the united states and sweden, and by the persistence of the al-qaeda group, despite the killing of osama bin laden, and more stringent security measures seem more than necessary. since the report stresses the health risks that could arise from the introduction of the new body scanners and therefore specifies that they can only be introduced after thorough medical investigations have confirmed that they are not harmful to the human body, the report can be adopted and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which also has the merit of reviving the debate on aviation safety. following the 2001 attacks and subsequent terrorist alarms, europe adopted restrictive but necessary measures to ensure the safety of its citizens. in recent years, the alarm has not yet been raised, so the eu now needs to implement harmonised standards on scanners, with particular attention to the use of body scanners, and at the same time common standards on the operation and effectiveness of detection. the use of body scanners must therefore be subject to strict rules to protect the health and privacy of passengers, who must be given the right not to be scanned but to be screened with other equipment. finally, i agree with the decision, set for 29 april 2013, to gradually lift the ban on the transport of liquids, gels and aerosols: by that date, all airports must be equipped with new and reliable equipment capable of carrying out checks on liquids, aerosols and gels. i believe, however, that member states should be given the possibility of reintroducing such controls if situations arise which may jeopardise safety.
in writing. − the new generation of body scanners appears to be able to increase the safety of european union air transport. these are instruments which add value to the effectiveness of security controls at union airports and which also appear appropriate in relation to the risks they prevent. we support their inclusion in the list of screening and control methods and technologies which european citizens can choose from, as we believe it is essential to take all the necessary measures to ensure their safety, without prejudice to their fundamental rights. we are also in favour of the implementation of harmonised standards throughout the european union, setting out the conditions for their use and a set of common standards for detection efficiency. it should not be forgotten that controls, intelligence and surveillance services, the exchange of police information and the analysis of the human factor are fundamental elements that form part of the definition of aviation safety. finally, we believe that the use of body scanners provides an optimal level of protection for european citizens. it is therefore essentially a matter of safeguarding democratic values while at the same time fighting terrorism which threatens them.
in writing. - i congratulate mr luis de grandes pascual on his excellent work. the report on aviation safety, with particular reference to body scanners, was voted on today at the plenary session of the european parliament in strasbourg. the eu aviation security legal framework provides member states and/or airports with a list of screening and control methods and technologies to choose from; it is therefore necessary to amend the current legislation to include body scanners in that list, without prejudice to the possibility of installing scanners on an experimental basis or as a more restrictive security measure. i fully share the rapporteur's view that the commission's communication in response to the european parliament's 2008 resolution is positive and i believe that it is essential to evaluate all the different technologies available from next generation body scanners in order to minimise the possible negative health consequences of the radiation emitted by these devices, even if they are low.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i believe that a new global approach to aviation security is needed, one which is able to cope with new terrorist threats and new terror strategies. the screening systems currently in use at european airports for the detection of prohibited non-metallic objects have shown their limitations, while the testing of body scanners has so far produced satisfactory results. it is now necessary to go further on the road to prevention by adopting increasingly effective screening technologies which, through the use of the latest technologies, are able to not interfere with the privacy of citizens and the technical time of control.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr de grandes pascual, which would add body scanners to the list of methods used for checks, provided that the health and rights of passengers are guaranteed by specific rules. after the tragedy of 11 september and the subsequent terrorist acts in various parts of europe (see london, madrid, istanbul), the need for security of european citizens preparing to travel has increased. i therefore fully support the text voted today, which in any case protects the privacy of passengers by providing for a restricted use of scanner images and, in particular cases, allows the right to refuse the use of the scanner and to be checked in a different way.
in writing. - despite the emphasis in mrs kratsa-tsagaropoulou's report on the importance of women's presence in decision-making bodies in enterprises, a position which i share, i am not convinced that it is through legislation or quota imposition that we can achieve really positive results in this respect. i also voted against the report because an amendment was adopted. i do not share the intention expressed in this amendment, which has been adopted, to increase the participation of women from ethnic minorities or immigrants in the management of companies.
in writing. - i am voting in favour, as the gender gap in company management bodies needs to be reduced. i support a strong signal from europe on the integration of women at the top of companies, in order to prevent a loss of talent and skills of human potential and to contribute to the performance of companies. the gender diversity factor has a strong impact on the performance of a company. we must act quickly and with quota systems, because the data available to us in the european union are worrying: on average, only 12 percent of the board members of the largest publicly traded companies are women, and only 3 percent are their ceos. in this sense, more space must be given to competent and qualified women and they must be helped through the quota system not to be marginalised from the decision-making process of companies. finally, it is important to address the root of the problem by supporting actions to direct more young women to science and technology faculties, enabling them to reach top positions in sectors with less female representation.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i have voted in favour of mrs kratsa-tsagaropoulou's report and i now hope that the commission will present a proposal which will become the basis for future and careful discussions on this subject. i am a strong believer in equality between men and women and i believe that women can add value in running businesses. i am not a natural leader, but i think that in some areas it is appropriate to set a good example and introduce through legislation quotas and rules which cannot be achieved by leaving open access. however, precisely because of this 'educational' and exemplary role, i believe that these rules should apply only to public companies, while i believe that private companies should be free to choose and run their business in the way they see fit. and because of that, i abstained on paragraph 16.
in writing. the draft report on women and business management has some positive aspects: implement women's participation in the labour market, at all levels, based on the skills and abilities of individuals. despite their knowledge, women often find themselves hampered by the so-called "glass ceiling" that prevents them from occupying top positions. the report, while agreeable on some points, is less so when it highlights the intention to increase the participation of women from ethnic minorities or immigrants in the management of enterprises. that is why i am voting against the text of the report.
in writing. − in 2009, the european parliament established a special parliamentary committee on the financial, economic and social crisis (cris). the financial, economic and social crisis of 2007-2009 put the current governance system of the economic and monetary union to the test and posed a real threat to the stability of the euro. therefore, about a year ago, i supported the need for an extension of the mandate of the cris special committee, which was then crucial for the development of recommendations for a sustainable eu growth model. in my view, these recommendations should be taken into account by the special committee on the political challenges and budgetary resources for a sustainable european union after 2013. furthermore, i believe that further work is needed to develop a functioning crisis management mechanism at union level and to define a political strategy for the future that is linked to the reform of european economic governance and the eu 2020 strategy. finally, i stress the need to develop mechanisms to develop coordinated policies to overcome the public debt crisis in the member states while promoting employment and close cooperation with national parliaments.
in writing. - the report contains points of agreement, such as the need to focus on the real economy, the only sector that produces secure wealth and can protect the economy from speculation. i am also convinced that the measures for smes, which alone account for 99% of the european production, are in line with this. however, the general tone of the report is marked by a eurocentric view of reality; i cannot, for example, share the rapporteur's repeated calls for the establishment of a new system for the collection of the eu's own resources, an expression which conceals the creation, more or less surreptitiously, of a european tax to finance the union's activities and its intervention programmes in the economy and society of our countries. too much emphasis and too high expectations are placed on the eu2020 strategy, which is a de facto replica of the previous lisbon strategy, which produced nothing but a lost decade in pursuit of phantom community economic and social development programmes. i therefore abstain.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the financial, economic and social crisis. almost two years after the start of the work of the special committee, the report is intended as a document summarising the measures to be taken in various policy areas to define the future political strategy for reforming european economic governance. the report aims to provide the necessary guidelines to respond to the current crisis, but also to prevent future economic and financial imbalances, through 'more europe'. this must be done by combining a strong regulatory package of economic governance with an increase in the budget available. this increase must be achieved through the eu's own resources, made available by financial income support, fines, vat, but above all by the acquisition of new capital on the market, through instruments such as project bonds, which will play an important role in the implementation of strategic infrastructure in the transport, energy and telecommunications sectors.
in writing. - we believe that the work undertaken so far within the special committee on the financial, economic and social crisis (cris) has enabled us to take a thorough and holistic view of the crisis, draw conclusions and make important recommendations, especially in the field of public investment and fiscal policy. in particular, the extension of the mandate of the special committee has been necessary to develop new recommendations for a european model of sustainable growth, which complement its previous calls already adopted by the european parliament; to develop mechanisms and coordinated policies to exit the sovereign debt crisis in the member states and prevent its recurrence, addressing its root causes while promoting strong and sustainable growth and employment, and to develop close cooperation with national parliaments. we also believe that further work is needed to improve a functioning crisis management mechanism at eu level and to define a political strategy for the future of supervision, including and linked to the reform of european economic governance, the eu 2020 strategy, fiscal policy, financial impact, financial regulation, as well as the reform of global governance and the representation of the european union on the world stage.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i am convinced that i shall vote in favour of mrs berès' report, which is the result of the joint work carried out over the last 18 months by us members of the cris committee. i would like to stress in particular that unity and solidarity are essential if europe is to succeed in meeting the global challenge, and in this respect i welcome the reference in the report to eurobonds. the current european national bond market is extremely fragmented, and the joint issue of euro bonds can overcome this fragmentation by creating a new european market with a worldwide dimension. the lack of a strong european title with a strong presence on world markets is a problem for the union as a whole, even for those countries with sound public finances. but any solution must avoid that countries with responsible fiscal policies are forced to bail out, in one way or another, 'unruly' states. the concept of eurobonds is based on solidarity, but they must not become a tool to reward unsound policies and weaken the incentives for greater fiscal prudence by states in the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it will help to move in the right direction to combat the economic crisis whose consequences we are still suffering. financial markets have not yet stabilised and citizens and businesses are still facing serious socioeconomic threats. the financial, economic and social crisis of 2007-2009 put the current system of governance of the economic and monetary union to the test and, at its worst, the very existence of the eu, its single market and its social base seemed to be in jeopardy. the challenge now is to continue along the path already traced, focusing on public investment and appropriate fiscal policies, developing a new proposal for sustainable growth and developing coordinated mechanisms to exit the public debt crisis in the member states, preventing it from recurring in the future.
in writing. - we are not satisfied with the results of the crisis committee. greece, but also other eu countries, are facing bankruptcy and the percentage of the population in employment is falling steadily. crises are not solved by european taxes, oppressive rules for industry and business, by reducing tariffs to the exclusive benefit of third countries. the objectives which the special committee believes the union should pursue are, in our view, the opposite of the interests of our citizens. the aim of a balanced and fair global trade agreement, which aims to reduce the differences between the emerging and developed economies by removing trade barriers, is to liberalise unfair competition between producers in third countries and those in europe. the commission even considers that the absence of a world trade agreement is a major disadvantage, since developed economies block agricultural export projects of emerging economies. as if that were not enough, the commission is also concerned with creating job opportunities for roma. it is incredible how far the commission's proposals are from the real needs of european citizens and businesses. that is why we shall vote against it.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow we shall be voting on an important and demanding resolution which shows the willingness of the european parliament, despite a thousand difficulties, to express a clear position on the events affecting countries such as syria, bahrain and yemen, with all the problems they entail. it is true that what is happening in other countries, such as tunisia and morocco, shows that the road to democracy is possible, it can take different paths, but it is possible. this finding does not, however, eliminate the perception that public opinion has of the policies pursued by the international community and europe itself in these events involving the mediterranean region. and this perception calls into question the idea that a foreign policy can be a double standard in its own way. in essence, one wonders why in libya it is done one way and in syria another. it is not unknown that there are different balances in foreign policy: the european union is not only a political union, but also a political union of the peoples of europe. in any case, this is a contradiction which continues to haunt us and which we must know how to deal with. what do you mean, "what"? in two ways: the european union must be able to play a more active role in the world, and to play a more consistent role in order to give credibility to its presence throughout the region. the european union is not only a political body, but also a political body, and it is also a political body, and it is a political body. and this work must be done now with the necessary strength and determination.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the situation with regard to the so-called arab spring is in many ways in danger of turning into a cold winter, and the concern expressed by many colleagues speaks to that effect. in a very good speech this morning, president tusk also mentioned the possible development of the neighbourhood policy. he also referred to the crisis in the southern mediterranean and spoke of measured and reasoned interventions. i would urge you to go beyond this reasonable caution for one simple reason: when we intervened in the crisis theatre of the soviet bloc countries, we probably did so quickly and well, and the consequences were obvious. when we intervened in the balkans crisis theatre, we waited too long, we delayed too long, and the consequences were tragic. if we do not give coherence, strength and resources to action that shows that the axis of the crisis has shifted in recent years from the east to the south, we shall not be able to interpret fully the desire for justice, development and peace of the peoples of the southern mediterranean area. i believe that you can do a great deal to achieve this and that you can also appeal to the polish presidency to make the efforts we have made in these months effective.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam high representative, commissioner, the impression is that we are struggling to bring all the instruments together and to give even small but tangible signals. we have political dialogue, trade policy, development cooperation, immigration policies, humanitarian aid with separate officials, procedures and budget lines, and sometimes europe plays the three card game by using the policy that pleases us, but we must help those who deserve it the most with all the possibilities and update all the instruments. for example, trade with egypt and tunisia cannot continue under the same agreements for the other countries in the region. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's financial instruments are used effectively. the osce, the council of europe, are reaching the caucasus and central asia, while an organization for mediterranean cooperation for integration is missing. what steps are we going to take in this direction? the european parliament is currently calling for a specific erasmus for the mediterranean and why is the commission not immediately taking up this initiative? an arab employee of a multinational can get a visa to europe, but a tunisian small businessman who wants to sign a contract cannot. it is your role, madam high representative, not to disperse any initiative and to make a coherent composition of all our actions among the many rooms of the european union, otherwise the change will sweep and inspire the mediterranean, but it will not have inspired us.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam high representative, commissioner füle, we have understood that there are countries in the arab world and in north africa that are asking us to do something. public opinion demands that europe be close to that wind of freedom, that yearning for dignity, and it is a demand that is made of us and when i say 'we' i mean europe. it is right that europe should ensure that the international community is present, but that question, the question of those countries, is addressed directly to 'us'. we can rightly engage in all diplomatic efforts to get the international community to intervene, but it cannot intervene unless europe has a policy for the mediterranean. we must strengthen this will to have a mediterranean policy. it is said, and it was said very well, during the debate on the syrian issue: "let's meet her in turkey". but, high representative ashton, we must have a clear idea of our relationship with turkey, it cannot be an intermittent relationship. one day we want her close to us, and the next day we don't want her close to us, it's not possible. europe must speak out clearly about its relations with turkey, and today we realise how important it would have been in the past to bet on turkey.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, political and intercultural dialogue remains the winning approach to restoring peace to the citizens of the arab world, which is currently suffering from upheaval and turmoil. short-sighted tyrants and sometimes religious fundamentalism have caused violence and disorder, but also the revolutions that are liberating some territories from these cruel and violent tyrants, often unable to hear the voices of their people. the syrian dissident summit in recent days is a possible turning point towards a national dialogue that is hoped to lead to a new and more fruitful relationship between the opposition and president assad. the unresolved middle east issue does not diminish the complexity of a time when there are other conflicts between syria and turkey and a difficult regulating of irregular migration flows to the west. the climate in lebanon has also deteriorated considerably, and this is affecting the stability of the area. we don't talk about libya because others have. but there are some surprising signs: in morocco, the referendum just held scored 98.5 percent "yes" to constitutional reform, and a very high percentage, 72 percent of the population voted. this is the way forward, together with a more renewed, more effective and more incisive neighbourhood policy.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the syrian poet adonis has written an open letter to president assad, in which he says: "mr president, no one believes that democracy can be achieved in syria immediately after the fall of the current regime, but in comparison it is incredible and unrealistic that systematic violence continues in syria to restore order. and that's the problem. the foundations of democracy must be laid from the beginning, now and not tomorrow. on the other hand, without democracy, there will be nothing but backsliding to the brink. vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − madam president, can i first of all thank everyone who has contributed to what has been a long but truly important debate. when we began, i think it was mr salafranca sánchez-neyra who said that we had to make sure we met people’s expectations – those of our people and those of the people of the region we are seeking to support. in a sense, that idea frames all of the contributions that honourable members have made in the course of the debate this afternoon. i have been struck by many of the different elements of those contributions. i was particularly struck that the word ‘dignity’ – one i did not use in my initial contribution – was used by so many honourable members as a way of describing what we are seeking to develop as we support the people of the region in their future quest for democracy and human rights. i think dignity is exactly the right word. not surprisingly, many contributions have focused on syria. of all the countries and all the issues we are dealing with, syria perhaps provides the greatest challenge. honourable members have come up with important new ways in which we could support the people of syria and extend our action. extending sanctions is something we have done twice already, and we will continue to look at that option. mr verhofstadt described the idea of some 200 families being included in this respect, and we will certainly take that idea forward. i know that the desire to see safety provided for the people on the ground leads us to safe zone. however, it is important to understand that providing some kind of safe zone for people on the ground would require a security council resolution: otherwise it would be illegal under international law. many of the roles and ideas that honourable members have suggested are already being worked on, in one way or another, in our work in new york. it is interesting too that next week there will be a debate at the un on the whole question of responsibility to protect, and it will be interesting to see what emerges there as a result of these issues, not least in syria. honourable members asked too whether we can do more with diplomats. we keep a delegation on the ground because their job is to continue talking to the people of syria, and that is what they do. we have a head of delegation. we have removed people whom we have been able to move out of the country to safety, but we have a head of delegation and a very small team, and i really do pay tribute to the people who remain through all this turmoil and continue to support the work of the european union. the work of the head of delegation is very much about day-to-day contacts with civil society and groups of intellectuals, talking to people about what is happening, and also continuing to make approaches to, and put pressure on, the government on our behalf. i hear what people say about asking member states to remove ambassadors, and that is a tool we could look at. i could recommend it, though i cannot enforce it, but i am also very keen to do as we have done in the case of libya, which is to keep talking to ambassadors about what they believe is happening in their respective countries. you will know that many ambassadors to libya have ended up deciding that their future does not lie there. however, this is an issue we will continue to consider. i think the message about the children who are in prison is a significant one and i absolutely agree with it. it is essential that we continue the pressure to have all children taken out of prison. we will do all that we can within the operational framework we have, and we will continue to work with our partners, not least with turkey, which many have mentioned as a key partner here. i have already indicated that we are in touch with turkey, that i am in touch with foreign minister davutoglu, and that we are supporting turkish efforts not only in relation to the work with refugees – and we have met refugees in turkey – but also as turkey continues to make its own representations in syria. there was a concern, which fully and properly recognised. in addition, we discussed a number of what i would call rather more internal issues, so let me deal with those briefly. when we decide to have an eu special representative, we look for the person whom we believe can best do the job in hand. stefan füle and i and the 27 foreign ministers and other commissioners spend a lot of our time in our neighbourhood and our region. we are your political eyes and ears. we are the people who perform that political function. sometimes a special representative who has ministerial experience is incredibly valuable, response to those who say ‘you need to engage the international financial institutions and countries that wish to support the neighbourhood but to do it collaboratively with the eu’. at that level it would be ministerial, and stefan and i would be there, but the question is about how we bring in extra resources, through the eu special representatives, to do particular jobs. i know that bernardino león – whose reputation goes before him, not just in europe – will do a superb job on behalf of us all. i do not rule out involving ministers. i know miguel moratinos well. to the brazilians who were importance to having the sort of communities that are sustainable and can be developed for the future. ms lunacek, specifically in response to your point about money: the figures are eur 750 million programmes are now being reviewed to make sure that they fit, and all of the instruments will be revised in order to make sure that they fit with the new strategy and, just as importantly, that they are tailored to be able to respond to the needs of each country. we are doing this as swiftly as we can because one of the challenges, as honourable members have rightly pointed out, is to ensure we respond in good time to needs which are already very obvious. similar considerations apply in relation to mobility. we have proposed working with each country to establish mobility partnerships, visa the agenda includes the statement by the vice-president of the commission / high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation in nagorno-karabakh [2011/2688 (rsp) ].
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam high representative, the nagorno-karabakh issue is little known and often only through one-sided information, but one clear, indisputable and i would say fundamental point is the principle of the territorial integrity of a sovereign state. the inviolability of frontiers must be respected: the european union is not a party to the treaty of rome, but it is a party to the treaty of rome. there have been numerous statements on the nagorno-karabakh conflict and the following were mentioned: the european union has also taken steps to ensure that the eu is able to meet its obligations under the helsinki declaration of 2008, four un security council resolutions and our parliament has also spoken on the matter. the territorial integrity of a sovereign state is guaranteed by international law and to question this principle is to encourage future military aggression and attempts to change the international status quo, with destabilising consequences throughout the world. europe has a particular interest in the settlement of the nagorno-karabakh issue, because armenia and azerbaijan are part of the eastern partnership project, which expressly provides for stability and cooperation between partner countries. so we have to work for it. i would also remind you that the passage of time is actually consolidating armenia's position in the occupied territories, and this makes it more difficult to reach an agreement and the situation in the area more dangerous.
on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this debate comes at a very opportune time, following an emergency which it would be neither right nor wise to underestimate if we are to think about what is happening and will unfortunately perhaps continue to happen in libya. with these scenarios in north africa, do we want to dismiss the possibility that there could be an emergency maybe twice, ten times, god forbid, a hundred times bigger? it was foreseen by a great french writer, jean raspail, many decades ago, and today we are very close to this situation. so let us think carefully before we criminalise a small liberal country like denmark that decides to defend its borders. i am prepared to make a eulogy of borders, not that we should criminalize the existence of borders. when there are checks to be made and when a country feels that it is giving priority to the safety of its citizens, this decision must be respected and this should be democracy according to rules shared by all european countries. so we are very careful and we think with great concern about the danger of a biblical exodus from africa. this danger exists and it is very close, very close, surely... (the president cut off the speaker)
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it is more than 20 years since the schengen agreements were signed. no one doubts the benefits of free movement, but it must be recognized that the current system is no longer adequate for present and future needs. that is why the member states and the eu as a whole must work to review the mechanisms of schengen's operation, so that freedom of movement does not come at the expense of the legitimate need for security on the part of our citizens. as far as we know so far, the commission's guidelines may also be partially acceptable, especially as regards the introduction of a mechanism allowing states to temporarily reintroduce border controls in the event of an emergency. but it remains to be seen how this will be achieved and whether the declarations will be followed by the facts, and above all by concrete results. it is also clear that a general reform of the european border protection system will have to be undertaken, especially the external border protection system, where frontex must be transformed as soon as possible into an agency with real powers of intervention and support for the national authorities. we must protect our external borders if we are to continue with this schengen.
the resolution we are about to vote on is important and timely, because it sets out and clarifies in an unequivocal way the principles which must guide the action of the european parliament and its representatives in continuing this difficult negotiation with the national parliaments. these principles stem primarily from the treaties, which, by overcoming the pillar structure on the one hand and by giving the european parliament the function of directly representing citizens at union level on the other, make the european parliament a vital source of democratic legitimacy for the cfsp and csdp as union policies. this double innovation is, as is well known, reflected in increased functions and responsibilities, from the vote of approval by the high representative, to the powers of direction defined in article 36, to the budgetary powers which, it should be remembered, make the european parliament the budgetary authority of the vast majority of csdp missions which, as is well known, are civilian missions. however, the reasons for pursuing with firmness and readiness for dialogue the path of a real agreement with the national parliaments are also political and pragmatic. interparliamentary cooperation is useful and necessary to strengthen support for the cfsp and csdp and to increase coherence between them and the choices made by member states at national level. for this very reason, this cooperation must represent in a balanced way the institutions which express the democratic legitimacy of europe at different levels, and an imbalance which would excessively compress the weight of the european parliament would be contrary to the very mission of europeanising the debate on foreign policy, security and defence in europe, which is the very idea behind the establishment of a conference. it is therefore good that tomorrow's vote makes it clear that the willingness to discuss is accompanied by the utmost firmness on certain principles, starting with the fact that, as article 9 of the first protocol clearly states, no regular form of interparliamentary cooperation can be established without the consent of the european parliament.
