member of the commission. − madam president, let me start with a quote: ‘looking ahead, the commission confirms that the union would greatly benefit if a number of members of the european parliament were elected from european lists submitted to the whole of the european electorate.’ this is an extract, not from the report presented to you today by your rapporteur, andrew duff, but actually from a communication forwarded by the commission to the convention in 2002. so the commission remains convinced that european lists could help to enhance the transnational dimension of european elections. so let me say a few words about mr duff’s report. first, i note the tremendous personal efforts of the rapporteur – and i would like to thank him – to seek wide support in the parliament on such a complex and sensitive issue. the core of the report concerns the creation of a pan-european constituency to which 25 meps would be elected. i know some members of this assembly are against such lists, but i think it is an idea worth pursuing. it will, however, not be easy to implement and here begin the concerns of the commission. first, i am not sure our fellow citizens will understand the need to increase the number of seats. this was the conclusion of the convention: above 750 members an assembly may find it difficult to function. second, increasing the total number of meps requires a treaty change, unless the 25 meps elected on transnational lists would be part of the existing number. in the commission’s opinion, this procedural difference is very significant. i understand your rapporteur has already tabled amendments to leave the door open. third, it was so difficult to reach a compromise on the allocation of seats between the member states that it hardly seems conceivable to reopen such a debate right now. but such a discussion would be essential, should the 25 meps be part of the whole number here. fourth, the principal elements of the proposed reform would need to be ratified in all member states. in some countries this could even mean a referendum. are we ready to run the risk of a ‘no’ vote now? in the present climate of both institutional fatigue and economic austerity, any referendum would be risky, and the national parliamentary ratification processes cannot be taken for granted either. in any case, the treaty requires the european council to adopt by unanimity a decision on a proposal from this parliament so your assembly – this is a clear message – has the right of initiative on this matter. there is no formal role for the commission. i trust you will present your proposal in time for the european council to decide early enough before the spring-2014 elections. moreover, the report brings forward the idea of creating an electoral authority to conduct and to verify the results of this election. it also provides for the creation of an electoral role to prevent double voting. both instruments would indeed seem necessary and would be put in place after the revised electoral act has been ratified. the commission will need some time to draft a proposal on this. it will also likely take considerable time for member states to agree so this would be only possible for the 2019 elections at the earliest. this brings me to a specific request addressed to the commission to present a new proposal for the revision of the current information exchange system to encourage participation of eu citizens in european elections in the member state where they reside. the commission has already made such a commitment but the proposal has been blocked in the council since 2006 because member states cannot find the unanimity required to adopt this proposal. another demand addressed to the commission concerns statistics and your wish to improve the consistency and comparability of population data provided by member states. on this point, i can announce that commission services are currently working on a draft proposal which should be coming soon. there are many other points in the report. be sure that the commission can only subscribe to principles such as the better representation of women and minority candidates or the respect of democratic rules in the selection of candidates. the commission also supports the idea of having the elections in may rather than in june. so this report concerns constitutional issues rather than simply legislation. the commission is already ready to make some amendments in the procedure for the 2014 elections. i mentioned earlier the way forward with directive 93/109/ec, taking into account the outcome of our debate today, to encourage people to stand and to prevent double voting based on the current ex-ante checks. as regards statistics, the commission is already preparing the proposal to improve the consistency and comparability of population data. finally, three months ago, vice-president šefčovič promised you that he would examine your request to establish a specific european legal status for political parties at european level. the commission is presently looking into the key elements in the giannakou report with an open mind, and it may indeed come back to you in the near future.
the socialist and democratic group believes that the building of a genuine european political area is a decisive condition for continuing on the road to a political europe capable of facing with strength and determination, in an appropriate way, the colossal challenges of this century. the treaty of lisbon has made a major step forward in this respect, particularly on the basis of the principle already mentioned by the rapporteur, mr duff, which makes it clear that the european citizens are directly represented in the european parliament at the level of the union. yet despite these and other important innovations in the treaty of lisbon and despite the fact that everyday life shows us unequivocally how necessary a political europe is, the construction of a genuine european political area is still a long way off. the debate in our member states is too nationally oriented, the political parties are too much discussing only on a national level and the european elections themselves often appear to the citizens as a continuation of the internal political debate, which is also one of the reasons for the low participation. we believe that a reform of the european electoral law which strengthens the common principles can contribute to this europeanisation of the european political debate. of course, this is not the only condition, but it can contribute. the socialist and democratic group, therefore, while being aware of the many problems associated with this proposal, supported the proposal for a transnational list in committee. we have also supported the request for a return to committee, because we understand that a broad consensus is needed on this proposal, but we also believe that we must continue with determination on the road to reforming the european electoral system in order to strengthen the transnational character of these elections.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the aim of this report is to amend the european electoral law in the direction of the creation of a european federal state. the commission is also proposing to add a transnational electoral college, elected by proportional representation and governed by a european union electoral authority. we are strongly opposed to this choice, both because it does not respect the political forces rooted in the territories, and not at european level, and because of the enormous cost of its introduction. we would have two different types of meps, because it would be unthinkable that meps who have to travel to 27 and then 28 member states could be considered as the others, with what funds would they be able to follow their territory? another point we do not agree with is the establishment of an electoral register of the european union, since its management, from deletion to insertion, modification and control of hundreds of millions of voters, would involve an unnecessary burden on the union's budget. the creation of a single political area at community level would limit the sovereignty of the member states. we believe in a europe of the peoples, which respects the territorial realities, giving them representation and strength, and does not impose itself as a bureaucratic and bossy 'superstate'.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the people are the basis of democracy. "people" means identity, unity in history, tradition and ideals, but it also means unity, the will to have a single government. in this context, a unitary electoral system is clearly an instrument for building a people, a european demos. this european demos is not yet fully present, as is shown by the fact that there has been a large drop in participation in the last european elections, and therefore little sensitivity, and as is shown by the fact that national debates have been mainly on national problems and not on european problems. we must therefore implement what the treaty of lisbon proposes. the treaty of lisbon does not impose an obligation on the european parliament to submit, to draw up a uniform electoral law, it merely indicates a power, but it is a power of extraordinary importance and therefore we must not abandon the project of drawing up this reform of the 1976 act. we shall be returning to committee this document from mr duff, whom i thank once again as chairman of the committee on constitutional affairs. the committee on constitutional affairs approved his text almost unanimously, and today it is somewhat reluctant to see it returned. but precisely because we must not be complacent, i believe that what is at stake here is to reformulate a more workable text, one which can have a greater consensus. but whatever happens, the postponement must not be a cover-up. the need for a european vision is not only due to the fact that elections are possible in a transnational body, but also to the fact that the people would directly elect the members of the commission or at least the president of the commission. i would like to conclude with this question, thanking mr duff again.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, this amendment to the act concerning the election of members of the european parliament gives us the opportunity to state two principles, namely: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. however, it is wrong to think that the transnational list alone will arouse the interest of the citizens, half of whom are already deserting the ballot boxes in the european elections. innovative criteria of quality and proximity to society are needed. as the italy of values, in the committee, we proposed a ceiling on the mandates of the members, for a replacement of the elected and a dynamic of renewal. an amendment which was rejected, even for reasons which i think are almost laughable, because of a certain self-preservation of the caste of members. we are committed to other changes for the next plenary session: the first concerns the regional dimension of elected representatives and constituencies, of the colleges, to ensure a strong link with the territory of origin, and the second, through both the joint amendment by the socialist and democratic group - and i thank mr gualtieri - and a separate text for a 'clean parliament', as society has called for. a "clean parliament" that introduces the ineligibility for those sentenced to final sentences and who have therefore obtained all the guarantees of a fair trial for very serious crimes, such as terrorism, corruption, organized crime, incitement to racial hatred and so on. it is a shame that today those who have been tainted by such crimes can sit in these benches. we need more courage, ladies and gentlemen, and only with standards that are at the forefront of europe will the european parliament gain the credibility it deserves.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the right to european citizenship must be guaranteed by the proper implementation of the treaty of lisbon, which is primarily entrusted to the representatives of the citizens of the union elected in the territory of the member states, with the aim of establishing a genuine right to european citizenship as an essential prerogative for every citizen who recognizes the values of europe. the postponement of the vote on the report which was to amend the provisions on the election of representatives to the european parliament does not detract from the excellent work done by the rapporteur and the committee. it is nevertheless a matter of mature reflection, because if the provision of a transnational list serves the function of guaranteeing a unitary representativeness, there is no doubt that today more than ever the need to guarantee the recruitment of the political leadership class is really an expression of the individual territories. the united states of europe is moving above all from the common application of the values of solidarity and integration to the benefit of the whole community, in particular the outermost and island communities, which are more exposed than ever to the growing pressure of irregular immigration. i am convinced that the rapporteur and the committee will work hard to introduce those amendments which are consistent with the idea of embracing the sentimental vision of a europe really united also by the single electoral constituency, but modelled on the link between elected representation and territory. because one thing is certain, the citizen today really wants to be recognised in europe. the european union must recognize the size and needs of the territory, because that is the starting point for an organisational model that really meets the needs of the citizen.

in writing. − at a time of great concern, when commissioner andor tells us that by 2060 europe's pensioners will be twice as many as the working population, the european commission has strategically proclaimed 2012 as the european year for active ageing. the consequences of population ageing are reflected in social policies and public finances, but they also require improvements in the lives of older people, who must be able to live healthy and active lives. that is why 2012 should be seen as an opportunity to build a europe that is not afraid to age! it is important to rediscover the role of the elderly in society: they are an irreplaceable asset to the whole community that we cannot give up. a professor at the university of padua in my hometown - i agree with him - used to say that every time an elder leaves us, an entire archive disappears with him. in order to improve the integration of older people into active society and to encourage solidarity between generations so that old age is a good old age as such, the european year aims to raise public awareness, promote debate and the exchange of experience between the various countries of the union and facilitate the development of specific policies.
in writing. − today, europeans are living longer and happier lives: the ageing population is also one of the major challenges facing the european union. the european union will soon face a considerable increase in the proportion of older people and a sharp decline in the population under 50 years of age, with consequent pressure on public budgets, pension and health systems and social welfare systems for the elderly. we support the commission's decision to establish the european year of active ageing for 2012: this should encourage the efforts of member states, local and regional authorities, social partners and civil society to promote active ageing and to mobilise the potential of the population aged 50 and over. the european year should therefore be the right context in which to raise awareness, identify and implement good practices and, above all, encourage policy makers and stakeholders to promote active ageing at all levels. finally, we believe that to promote active ageing, solidarity and cooperation between generations must be increased and that the objectives to be achieved must be vitality, dignity and solidarity between the different age groups.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on the european year of older people was voted on today at the strasbourg plenary session. the increase in life expectancy associated with ageing is certainly a remarkable social achievement and a success of our time. european citizens are living longer and healthier lives than before. however, this success presents many challenges for european society, first and foremost from an employment and social security point of view. the general objective of the european year of ageing is to encourage the efforts made by member states to promote active ageing. active ageing involves the creation of better working opportunities and conditions in order to enable older workers to maintain their role in the labour market and to combat social exclusion by strengthening active participation in society and encouraging healthy ageing.
in writing. − from 2012, the population aged over 60 will increase by two million per year. it is therefore necessary to build a framework for action to raise awareness of the contribution that older people can make to society and to strengthen dialogue between generations. the european commission has decided to launch this initiative with the aim of creating new employment opportunities and better working conditions for the growing number of older people in europe, helping them to play an active role in society. the challenge for all stakeholders is to improve the chances of ageing, by intervening in areas as diverse as employment, healthcare, social services, adult education, volunteering, housing, information services or transport. active ageing policies will provide greater opportunities for older people to continue to contribute to the good of society. with the adoption of today's document, each member state will also have to inform the commission of its work programme, detailing the national activities planned in the context of the european year.

in writing. president. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the resolution on the programme for the distribution of food to the most deprived in the european union. the european food aid programme for the indigent has been an essential instrument for providing aid to those in need since 1987. the programme is financed by the european agricultural guarantee fund (eagf) and involves voluntary participation by the member states. each year, on the basis of eurostat poverty data, the european commission sets a budget ceiling and compiles a list of products to be withdrawn from public stocks or purchased on the market, within the limits of the allocation. the proposed cut of 387 million for next year must not affect the 13 million people at risk of poverty who are currently receiving aid through the many charities and food banks in the eu. we must work together to find a system to ensure that this form of assistance is secure and constant for the future too, in the context of the reforms under way both in the social and agricultural sectors.
in writing. − the right to food is a fundamental human right and is realized when everyone, at any time, has physical and economic access to adequate, health-safe and nutritious food to meet their nutritional needs. in the eu 43 million citizens are at risk of poverty and, due to the economic and financial crisis, the number could increase. we support the initiative of the commission and the united nations to take a common stand against food insecurity and malnutrition in the world. we believe that the programme to support the most deprived in society should be maintained and that the commission should identify a legal basis for the existing food programme or for a new programme to help the poor. consideration should also be given to increasing the supply of products for the programme by allowing the purchase of products withdrawn from the market through non-intervention instruments such as export refunds or private storage. finally, we believe that the commission should ensure that, as part of the adjustment of the structural funds, individual vocational qualifications and diplomas are increasingly promoted, so that the poorest can participate in the social welfare system through their work.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i value its aim to find a synergy between the various dimensions of mine action, with a special focus on humanitarian and development aspects. this report condemns the fact that, since the elimination of the eu’s dedicated budget line in 2007, the eu has not had an instrument able to respond coherently to mine action priorities. it is essential to restore a more dedicated approach by establishing a budget line managed by one lead directorate. the commission, moreover, should take into account the specific needs of individual countries and acknowledges that in some areas of the world the existence of landmines has become a structural issue. i would like to underline that efforts should be concentrated on sustaining the development of greater local capacity, meant as training for local personnel on a structured and professional basis, and use of military units, specifically trained for humanitarian demining in post conflict situations.

in writing. - the removal of anti-personnel landmines and other unexploded and abandoned ordnance is an act of humanity, given the suffering caused by these evil devices. the report envisages greater involvement of the countries receiving financial assistance. i shall vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - in some countries the presence of mines is a structural problem which still causes a large number of victims, mainly civilians. therefore, mine action should be a mandatory element of the national strategies of countries where anti-personnel mines and/or stockpiles of such mines are known to be predominantly present. despite advances in technology and detection techniques, fast, reliable and cost-effective solutions are still a matter of chance. we therefore believe that it is necessary to promote the universalisation and implementation of the anti-personnel mine ban treaty and the convention on cluster munitions, and to invite all states which have not yet done so to accede to them. we believe that the countries concerned should also be involved more closely and reminded of their responsibilities. synergies between the different dimensions of mine action, with particular regard to the humanitarian and development aspects, should be identified. we believe that funding is needed for research into the techniques and technologies of detection and census to ensure greater assistance to victims, hoping to achieve a world finally free from the danger they pose to life, resources and economic development.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today the report on progress in the fight against landmines was voted at the strasbourg plenary session. the report by mr van orden seeks to clarify the current situation regarding the production, use and casualties of antipersonnel mines and the efforts made to assist the states signatories to the ottawa treaty. it also examines the consistency of the actions undertaken and highlights the steps needed to improve the community approach to mine action by focusing community efforts on the most important aspects at a time of scarce resources. the committee also calls for the reintroduction of the budget line for mine action, which was abolished in 2007.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because, despite the progress made in the fight against landmines over the last ten years, efforts must be stepped up if this threat is to be eliminated once and for all. to date, 156 countries, including 25 in the eu, have signed and ratified the anti-personnel mine ban treaty, and there is much pressure to ensure that those who have not yet done so can also adopt it. another aspect on which much remains to be done is the destruction of stockpiles of such weapons, especially with regard to the arsenals of china and russia, which today boast stocks of 100 and 24.5 million anti-personnel mines respectively.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report as it deals with the issue of mine action, specifying how this term includes the investigation, removal of anti-personnel mines and explosive devices. the presence of mines is not only a humanitarian problem but also an economic one, since the land on which they are laid is uninhabitable. the report focuses on prevention and education, mainly aimed at children, and on how to avoid and reduce the risks posed by mine explosion. it is precisely the minors who, because of their young age, are less aware of the risks they run by playing or moving around in mined areas. it is not possible that every year thousands of innocent children are killed or maimed by unexploded bombs or mines scattered on the battlefields.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr van orden on the sad problem of anti-personnel mines. the report provides detailed data on the production, use and casualties of antipersonnel mines today and highlights the good work done in recent years in the fight against landmines. the call for the union to concentrate its efforts on the most important issues is particularly important, in my view, given the time of crisis and the scarcity of resources available.

the next item is the report by mr antonio masip hidalgo, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on the audit policy: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the new regulation to include the following areas:
member of the commission. - madam president, i remember very well what i said at my hearing before the european parliament in january 2010. on that occasion, mrs flašíková, i made a commitment, in accordance with the g20 road map and the commitment of the heads of state and government of the european union, that no sector, no product, no financial market would be left out of intelligent regulation and effective supervision. since then, mrs flašíková, i have been working with all my teams, on a forced march, to prepare legislative texts to lay down rules or to give rules, to ensure transparency, accountability. i was going to say put morality back where it had disappeared, in the financial markets, so that these markets that we need work well in the service of the real economy. do not doubt, madam member, that for all the other sectors, beyond the audit we are talking about today, we do this work. we have already done some of this with you and you have many texts on your legislative table which are already under discussion and which will arrive by the end of the year. we are talking today about one of these sectors, about some of its actors, the external auditors, who, as we know, have not all played their part and have not all been able to sound the alarm in time in the financial crisis, which is not over. we have taken time to reflect, because in this field as in others i want us to work together, in a serious way, without improvisation. we have consulted and listened a great deal on this complex subject, and the european parliament has taken part in this consultation. i am very pleased - i say this in return - that parliament, thanks to the very high quality report by mr antonio masip hidalgo, very much shares my own idea of resolute action at european level to overcome the failures of the past. i thank you, mr masip hidalgo, for your personal commitment. i also welcome the work of several of your colleagues: mrs kay swinburne of the econ committee, who has just spoken, and other members who have contributed to this reflection, mr gauzès, mr bodu, mr lópez-istúriz and mrs berès. this report - and i say this quite frankly - is a very good basis for the proposals we are going to put forward in november. there are certainly differences of opinion on certain points and i am counting heavily - as mrs swinburne said earlier - on the determination and contribution of the two committees juri and econ to work together and rapidly in the coming months to develop the new regulatory tools we need. i will not respond to all the recommendations in mr masip hidalgo's report. i would simply like to mention three aspects of our proposals by telegram: the independence of the profession, the opening up of the audit market and the creation of a large, more integrated european market with strengthened supervision. first, the independence. our first concern, and yours, is the quality and credibility of the audit. we need to restore confidence in the accounts of the companies. this means that auditors must be independent of the entities they audit. but all too often we find that many companies keep the same audit firm for long periods, even decades, even a century - it has already happened. the result is less confidence in the accounts of the companies concerned, which is detrimental to the profession and to the audited companies. i do not therefore rule out proposing in november the mandatory rotation of the audit firm, a well-managed rotation, after a well-chosen period of time. another factor in the over-familiarity between auditors and auditors is the provision by auditors of too many services that are classified as ancillary or 'non-audit' services. for most networks, these services generate more revenue than the audit itself. in such circumstances, are we really sure that it is possible to judge objectively and to audit the company independently, when we are also advising it on its development strategy? mrs regner, you made that point very clearly earlier. i am therefore determined to limit, or even prohibit in some cases, non-audit services to audited clients. i believe in uniform rules for all of europe in this area. i wonder if we should not go so far as to propose pure audit firms, which would not be able to provide any other services than audit. this would also have the advantage of opening up these 'non-audit' markets to small and mediumsized enterprises, which otherwise have no chance against the dominance of the large firms, as we see today. we are still considering the practical feasibility of this option - i need a few weeks to work on it - and its proportionality in the light of the challenges of this proposal. secondly, the audit market must be more open. just a generation ago, this market was divided among eight major accounting firms. today it is concentrated and is even more concentrated as the audited companies are larger mr tavares, you have made that very clear. four firms control about 80% of the market for listed companies. this situation is even more concentrated in some countries, where the term "big four" has been replaced by "big three" or "big two". in germany, only two firms hold 90% of the mandates for the main stock index, the dax 30. in spain, it is even possible to speak of a "big one", since a single firm certifies the accounts of the largest banks and owns 58% of the largest listed companies. i have no ideology on this subject, nor on any other. i want to be determined and pragmatic. i am not in any way opposed to the big four, but i cannot accept that the market for auditing large companies is so dominated by only four large networks, when there are at least as many firms in europe that would like to enter this market. we want more players, more competition, more dynamism, especially in this market segment. there are several possible ways of stimulating this market, and we are working on them. one is the joint commission formula. i am pleased to note that your report, mr president, agrees with our analysis and that, if it is well balanced, the joint commission could provide a boost to the market. we are analysing the possible extension of this formula to europe. i am also thinking of compulsory, regular, transparent and fairer competition. in this context, i also want to see a ban on restrictive contractual clauses in favour of the 'big four'. i think that this current practice is unacceptable in a european market where competition must be free, fair and genuine. finally, with my colleague, the commissioner responsible for competition, joaquín almunia, we are following with interest the approaches of the national competition authorities and we will also be looking at what more can be done at european level to encourage the emergence of new international audit firms. the third and final area is the creation of a large european market and the strengthening of supervision, as mr paška has mentioned. paradoxically, this market, which is so concentrated in a few hands, is nevertheless very fragmented at the level of each of our countries. european integration is a solution to this. common european rules would promote the free movement of professionals and improve the quality of auditing and its supervision by the supervisory authorities. in order to make the audit market more european, i intend to advocate the idea of a european passport for auditors. we shall be inspired, in particular, by some of the solutions which have been found in the field of vocational qualifications. i do not think it is acceptable that an auditor should have to take exams in every country in which he wishes to work. i will also propose the automatic recognition of firms already approved in other states and the award of a european quality label which would demonstrate the ability of all firms concerned to audit larger companies. finally, there is another lever to help harmonize the rules applicable to auditing in the european union and to ensure professional mobility: this is - as you said, mrs flašíková - the introduction of international auditing standards, the isas (international standards on auditing). we are looking at how best to do this, and i agree with the parliament's report that it is necessary to provide for measures adapted to small and mediumsized enterprises. this is a daily concern of my colleague, antonio tajani. the last three very important points concern the supervision of audit firms and the transparency of their work. firstly, we want the audit authorities to cooperate more closely. i am glad that you share our view that this cooperation should take place within esma (european securities and markets authority esma). the times are not propitious for the creation of new structures at european level. let us use the existing ones, let us make sure they work well, and then the national supervisors - the auditors - will also be able to benefit from the experience of esma. secondly, i also want to strengthen the independence of the supervisory authorities at national level. they must be completely independent of the auditors and their professional organisations. thirdly, and finally - as you very well say in your report, mr masip hidalgo - we will propose that audit reports be more detailed, contain more information. during the audit, the auditor acquires a thorough knowledge of the company being audited, its activities, its organisation and its risks. he has privileged access to a lot of information. unfortunately, they are not always presented in a structured way in his report. this also applies to regulators, managers, audit committees and shareholders. this is also something that can be changed and improved, as mr masip hidalgo has suggested. i am very grateful to parliament for its interest and commitment in this matter. i wanted to bring you updated paragraph 13 of my reflections myself, a few weeks before the commission, informed and encouraged by your report, will present its legislative proposals.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow, tuesday 13 september, at 11.30 a.m. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.

should not be considered as mutually exclusive measures. cooperation is a key requirement in improving fisheries management in the black sea. the commission is ready to join forces and work with the european parliament and all stakeholders.

of safety and environmental protection in offshore oil and gas operations. the european parliament has broadly supported the commission's objectives. the precise and well-researched report of parliament which we are discussing tonight confirms the complexity of offshore issues. i am particularly pleased to see that there are many similarities between your conclusions and those of the commission. i can assure you that the commission fully shares your concerns about the need to avoid destabilising the offshore sector through inappropriate regulation. we are therefore building on existing best practice in europe and are in contact with stakeholders to ensure that our future proposals are based on concrete and realistic elements. offshore oil and gas production has been and will be an important source of energy for europe, and is a major industrial structure whose safety standards are widely recognised as an example of excellence. but to remain at the highest level of global security, we must continue to make progress. experience shows that one should never rest on one's laurels. unfortunately, the recent oil spill in a north sea pipeline has again confirmed the need for action. there is no simple recipe for improving the safety of offshore operations. we believe that the responsibility for offshore oil and gas operations should remain with the industry and national administrations. however, our analysis also confirms that the european union has an important role to play in various sectors. we must ensure that best practice is extended to the whole of the european union, we must increase transparency in the industry and promote the sharing of experience. we also need to improve our contingency plans in the event of failure to prevent. we see the role that the european union can play in providing guidance and motivation in the ongoing work on such improvements. a lot of work has already been done since the five-point plan on offshore security. the commission is currently finalising this proposal on offshore safety, accompanied by the impact assessment, which is expected to be adopted around october. these proposals must be forward-looking and provide a comprehensive solution to the shortcomings and complexity of the present system and, above all, provide instruments for its continuous improvement. these efforts must be shared by all stakeholders and the commission warmly welcomes the positive response of the industry to some of its calls for progress. neither security nor oil spills know borders. this is why the commission is entrepreneurs, of both sexes, are by definition business-oriented and committed to the success of their business. in the eu, despite women making up a significant share of the member states' labour force, there are still more female entrepreneurs than male entrepreneurs. at present, each member state of the union has adopted different approaches to supporting and promoting women in decision-making and on company boards. the different support systems that have developed over time in the member states are adapted to the cultural and individual needs of the country of origin. in response to this situation, the commission is running a voluntary group of female ambassadors in the member states who provide valuable technical support to women entrepreneurs. i share the rapporteur's view that there should be more support for this initiative and the sharing of best practices. the valuable contribution that working women can make to both the community and the economy of the european union is undeniable. many of them are able to juggle, not without difficulty, family commitments and their own career aspirations. i therefore encourage all initiatives in the member states to support and encourage projects for women entrepreneurs.

vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i should like to begin by thanking the members of the european parliament, and in particular mrs bauer, for the preparation of this report. equal economic independence for women and men is a priority of our 2010-2015 gender equality strategy. we will only achieve the 75% employment target for women and men if we have national policies specifically aimed at increasing female employment rates and reducing gender gaps, particularly among women over 50. the commission notes how women approaching retirement age are in a special situation, as they may be helping their adult children to raise their families or looking after their elderly parents. a better reconciliation of work and private life is fundamental if we are to see an increase in the number of women in the labour force and an extension of their pension rights. the commission recognises the considerable role that paternity leave and leave for caring for a dependent relative, alongside other available instruments, play in pursuing these objectives. it has therefore commissioned studies to assess the costs and benefits of these two types of leave. the results are expected by the end of the year. on the basis of these two studies, the commission will decide whether to reserve the right to apply these measures in the future. the report rightly points out that women over 75 are more at risk of poverty than men in the same age group. the poverty of women may be the result of insufficient pension cover, but it is also often the result of the shortness of their working lives. it is therefore essential that women's actual career paths should be as long as those of men. one way of achieving this is to set the same retirement age for women and men. measures should be taken within the pension scheme to compensate for interruptions in professional activity. the current legislation guarantees the acquisition of pension rights during the period of maternity leave. our white paper on pensions is still being drawn up and the commission will consider ways of improving pension provision for women. next year we will have to discuss with the member states the adequacy of the pension system and we will publish a report on this together with the report on ageing. this report will focus on the situation of retired women who are victims of poverty and social exclusion. we will continue to work closely with stakeholders in the coming months to draft the white paper and look forward to your active involvement in the best evidence and input to support the measures we are considering. the european union is facing a significant ageing of its population due to low fertility rates, increasing life experience and the impending retirement of the baby-boom generation. the european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations will be an important opportunity to break the narrative of the ageing population as a social and economic burden and to show the wealth that women and men in this age group have to offer.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, madam commissioner, the successful implementation of directive 2008/52 shows that mediation is a viable alternative to the traditional conflict-based approach between the parties, allowing for an amicable settlement of disputes and thus lightening the workload of the courts. this is confirmed by the various initiatives taken by some member states which, by financial incentives or legal provisions, facilitate the use of mediation wherever possible. in this context, i would like to draw attention to a number of aspects which, in my view, merit further reflection and study, first of all the question of costs: the example of the member states which have tackled this problem by encouraging the use of mediation economically is to be followed. i also believe that other possibilities need to be explored, including the use of awareness campaigns to promote the use and knowledge of alternative litigation compositions, especially by businesses. to achieve this objective, the cooperation of the legal system operators is also and above all necessary, and they must understand the added value of mediation as an element that is ancillary to their activity and not competitive. finally, in view of the commission's forthcoming communication on the implementation of the directive, and in particular the forthcoming legislative proposal on alternative dispute resolution, i would like to emphasise the complementarity of mediation with other reforms of union law, above all the approach to collective redress and contract law. mediation can be an excellent preliminary alternative to forms of collective redress and can make an important contribution to the future instrument on contract law by significantly reducing the use of litigation.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the rapporteur for her work. as the european parliament's mediator in cases of international child abduction, i particularly appreciated paragraph 14 of the motion for a resolution, which stresses that the mediation procedure makes the parties more open to considering each other's position and to working together to resolve the issues at issue, and this often has the advantage of preserving the relationship that the parties had before the dispute, which is particularly important in family matters involving children. mediation, wherever practicable, not only avoids lengthy court cases but also leads to an agreement agreed by the parties and i personally hope that such a practice can be extended as far as possible, including for family mediation. in europe, commissioner reding reminds us, there is a growing trend towards mixed marriages: each year, there are over 350 000 crossborder marriages and 170 000 divorces in the union, which is 20% of all divorces in the european union. after a marriage breaks up, sometimes the children become the object of contention. often the foster parent keeps the children without the consent of the other, or the noncustodial parent removes the child or refuses to return the child after a regular visit. in recent years, unfortunately, there has been a dramatic increase in cases of international parental child abduction: in many cases, however, the mediation procedure has allowed these children to have contact with both parents again, as an agreement between the parties reached through a mediation procedure can avoid unnecessary suffering of the child and allows the parents to deal with all family matters without incurring a long, costly and heartbreaking legal action.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the amendment to the frontex regulation which we are voting on today is aimed at strengthening the european agency, giving it greater operational capacity and strengthening respect for the fundamental rights of refugees and asylum seekers, but above all the prohibition of refusal. the establishment of a fundamental rights officer on the frontex management board and the obligation of solidarity between member states go in this direction. the reform of frontex must enable us to deal with the real migratory urgencies in europe. just today, the financial times reminds us that of the 104 000 migrants who arrived illegally in the eu in 2010, about 85% came through greece, not italy or malta, and that is how it will unfortunately be in 2012. only if frontex fully respects the human rights of migrants and avoids the death toll in the mediterranean, which has become a graveyard where the lives and hopes of people fleeing poverty, oppression and despair are extinguished, can we say that we are on the right track. this must be the mission of frontex and the european parliament will have to monitor progress in this direction.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, one of the prerogatives of the european union's common area of freedom, security and justice is that it has eliminated internal frontiers in the schengen area. this has, however, made the external borders of the eu member states a matter of common concern and has made even more urgent the need for their integrated management through a coordinated approach. to this end, the adoption and application of common rules, increased cooperation between member states, better coordination of efforts and greater sharing of resources are essential. the fundamental aspect is that cooperation must be based on solidarity between member states, especially towards those border states which, because of their geographical or demographic situation, have to cope with large migratory flows, such as italy. we therefore welcome the adoption of this report because, after lengthy negotiations, we have been able to achieve excellent results and improvements in the functioning of the frontex agency, by providing more resources and instruments to make its work more effective.

in writing. − the report on state-supported export credits highlights an important fact: targeted and deliberate export credits issued by the state can provide a significant support to its economic development by facilitating the acquisition of new trade opportunities, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises. in order to ensure full transparency and maximum efficiency in the allocation of export credits, the report provides that each member state will have to submit an annual report to the european parliament and the commission on the operation of its export credit agency, the support credits granted and the evaluation criteria, assets, liabilities, remuneration paid and the recovery of funds, risks and premium costs. on the basis of the information received, the commission will present to the european parliament its analysis of the activities of each member state's export agency, giving meps the opportunity to introduce the necessary corrections to improve the efficiency of export credits. the amendments proposed in the report will promote transparency in the allocation of export credits and involve more directly the electorate's representatives meps in matters of importance to economic development.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in a global context in which many raw materials are in short supply and europe is one of the largest importers, in a market often dominated by monopolies from third countries, it is essential to ensure a secure and competitive supply for european industry. i believe that a european raw materials strategy can pursue important objectives such as secure and competitively priced supplies for europe, a more sustainable use of existing resources and economic opportunity for european businesses. a raw materials strategy can also be an economic opportunity for europe, provided it does not place an additional burden on businesses over existing environmental legislation. in my view, an effective strategy must be based on an integrated approach that makes the most of existing european legislation governing resource efficiency in different areas. for this reason i do not support an overly prescriptive approach in terms of raw material management, recycling, recovery and reuse objectives, which imposes binding principles and further affects producer responsibility. finally, this strategy should be an integral part of a policy aimed at promoting research and innovation as a stimulus to the competitiveness of european smes.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the ford report on the safety of offshore activities in the hydrocarbon sector because it is one of the first european parliament's statements of position on the european commission's communication following the disaster in the gulf of mexico (april 2010). although the existing legislative framework provides a strong basis for ensuring human and environmental safety, the report considers that there is still a wide margin for developing an approach that ensures an adequate level of environmental protection throughout europe, so as to achieve the highest possible level of safety and environmental protection standards in all offshore oil and gas activity areas. i find the focus on responsibility in the event of an environmental disaster particularly interesting: the polluter pays principle places responsibility on industry, although the state is also called upon to monitor to ensure general safety and coordination of activities in the event of a disaster. in addition to industry and the state, the report refers to an 'independent third party' which, in this case, could coincide with emsa (european maritime safety agency), whose already important role in the event of an accident would be greatly strengthened.

in writing. − the 2010 environmental disaster in the gulf of mexico in the us led to a reassessment of the existing safety regulations for offshore oil and gas production in the eu as well. the available data are conclusive over 90% of oil and 60% of gas in the eu is extracted from offshore activities. energy consumption continues to rise rapidly, while traditional sources of energy are being depleted, requiring deeper and riskier drilling and more advanced technologies. how can oil and gas activities be regulated without harming the environment or the economy? first, there is a need for uniform, general eu standards to control these activities. oil and gas projects submitted shall be assessed individually, taking into account their different environmental and technical conditions. the basic principles must be clear no project may be licensed without an effective crisis response plan and the necessary resources. the industry concerned should continue to be liable for the damage caused. secondly, cross-border authorities must be established to monitor compliance with agreed standards, respond to incidents and conduct audits. such a joint body is already working successfully in the nordic countries; it is also needed in other regions, including the baltic sea. the european maritime safety agency could monitor the activities and standards of these bodies in the eu and its maritime borders.

acting president of the council. - mr. speaker, the house! at today's sitting of the european parliament, i have the honour to present to you the position adopted by the council on 25 july on the draft budget for 2012. for the second time, the budget is being adopted under the lisbon treaty procedure and i hope that we will use the lessons we learned during the 2011 budget debate. the development of a satisfactory agreement on the 2012 budget will require an open and constructive dialogue between our two institutions. i hope in particular that we will be able to avoid any reference to matters which are not directly related to the annual budget. mr. speaker, the house of lords! i was particularly pleased to note that the first round of trilateral budgetary talks on 11 july was conducted in an atmosphere of fruitful cooperation. i hope that this positive atmosphere will continue to prevail and help us to adopt a realistic and balanced budget for 2012. i should now like to outline the four main elements which the council has followed in its analysis of the draft budget presented by the commission. this is a philosophy that was developed during the discussion of the draft budget by the finance ministers and it reflects the way in which certain expenditure has been assessed and approached by the european commission. i hope that this will help you to understand the council's position better than just the figures for the expenditure in the various headings. first, the growth of the european union budget must reflect the situation in member states which are experiencing a period of weak economic growth and which are facing severe budgetary constraints. particular attention should be paid to controlling administrative expenditure so that our actions are in line with member states' efforts in this respect at national level. secondly, the european union budget should give priority to programmes and actions that help to overcome the current crisis, promote competitiveness and convergence, bring real eu added value, create employment opportunities and accelerate economic growth. thirdly, the increase in commitment and payment appropriations must be realistic. we should take account above all of current and future budgetary execution indicators as well as of absorption capacity, in order to avoid any overestimation which would only put unnecessary pressure on national budgets and increase outstanding commitments. fourthly, the budget should respect the current ceilings of the multiannual financial framework. the budget should also be flexible with appropriate margins to respond to unforeseen situations or to take account of new political priorities during the financial year. in this context, i am pleased to inform you that the council's position on the 2012 draft budget provides for an increase of 2,9% in commitment appropriations and 2,02% in payment appropriations compared to the 2011 budget. i am convinced that such a budget will strike the right balance between fiscal consolidation on the one hand and support for those european union programmes and projects which can most effectively contribute to the recovery of the union's economy on the other. it is also sufficient to meet the financial commitments arising from current and planned programmes and actions. i therefore believe that we are in a strong position to explain and justify such a budget to our citizens who have been affected by the economic and financial crisis, and in particular by the far-reaching fiscal consolidation efforts in the member states. the council agreed to targeted reductions in a number of specific budget lines across all headings. these reductions were based on a detailed analysis of the budget execution in previous years, but also took into account the most recent budget forecasts. i think these reductions are entirely justified. in addition, the information available in the commission's mission statements was used to assess the actual capacity of the commission and the member states to implement programmes and actions in time and to use the relevant funds during the financial year. particular attention was paid to administrative expenditure and the level of employment in the institutions. this includes administrative expenditure relating to operational programmes and executive agencies, as well as appropriations paid from the budget of the european union to decentralised agencies. the council considers that, in line with the direction of action taken at national level, the efficiency of the administration should be improved. the additional measures and staff plans, both for the european union institutions and for decentralised agencies, were approved only for new entities and entities with new tasks. the council's position, which is based on a clear methodology and an objective approach, is therefore a balanced, fair and just solution. finally, i would like to stress the point i raised at the very beginning of my speech, namely the need to strike the right balance between taking account of the difficult economic situation in which the member states find themselves and ensuring sufficient budgetary resources to support in particular those programmes and activities which can generate economic growth. i am convinced that the 2012 budget, at the level proposed by the council, will enable the european union to meet its obligations and will also send a signal to european taxpayers that we are acting responsibly and in the interests of those we represent. i would also like to add that when the council adopted this draft budget it also made a commitment, a declaration, that if in the course of the 2012 financial year there were no appropriations in any of the headings and no transfers could be made, then additional appropriations would be guaranteed by the member states on the initiative of the european commission.
member of the commission. − mr president, our budgetary trialogue in july was the first opportunity to react to the council’s position. developments in the summer confirmed that these are very difficult times. it is even more important, therefore, to strike a balance between budgetary self-restraint and necessary investment. the european budget should be seen as supplementing national efforts to reinforce investment in growth and jobs. that has determined the structure of the draft budget proposed by the commission. to avoid falling into a deflationary vicious circle, we must use all the instruments we have at our disposal. the european budget is one of them. so our budget proposals target increases in the area of competitiveness and cohesion as well as the phasing-in of agricultural payments – which, of course, is obligatory. the other budget headings came in below inflation, however, with clear self-restraint in administration. the council has decided to cut payments by eur 3.7 billion and adjust the increase of the payment level to the 2011 inflation rate forecast. at the present time, i cannot agree that this is the right way to strike a balance between smart investment and self-restraint in this time of austerity, especially when it comes to the eur 1 billion cut in the area of competitiveness, which is conducive to growth and jobs. i cannot reassure the two arms of the budgetary authority that what is in the cohesion budget after the council reading is enough, as our proposal was eur 18 billion below the forecast from the member states. the same member states are now cutting the figures that they were proposing, and on which our draft proposal was based. i must point out that we have outstanding commitments. we are proposing to raise the co-financing rate of the structural funds to 95% in order to help six member states that need to be helped at the present time. therefore, the inflation rate cannot be seen as the only parameter that needs to be taken into account when framing the budget. i will deal only briefly with the other aspects of the council proposals. with regard to the heading ‘europe as a global player’, we acknowledge that the neighbourhood proposals have been taken into account, but at the expense of pre-accession assistance and development aid. having seen the humanitarian consequences of the drought in the horn of africa, i am not in favour of cutting development aid to the poorest parts of the world. under heading 3a we have cuts in the european return fund, frontex and the external borders fund, although we clearly need much more budgetary funding to underpin immigration policy. the further cuts to the administration budget fail to acknowledge or assist the commission’s efforts to freeze its administrative budget. this will not help us to persuade our administration to exercise self restraint. i acknowledge the very focused, positive approach of parliament’s committee on budgets. our role now is to provide updated information in the expectation of compromise over the 2012 budget. we promise to provide updated information and monitor trends in budgetary payments so as to provide realistic data as a basis of conciliation. this would make a valuable contribution to the achievement of a timely, reasonable budget in response to all the challenges with which we are currently confronted.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the reading by the council last july, the institutions involved in the budgetary procedure, the commission, the council and parliament, expressed their position. the council and the commission with their numbers, parliament with its priorities. these are apparently very different positions, often distant, i am thinking above all of payments, research funding, but there are also points of contact and it is on these points of proximity that we will have to work a lot to arrive at a common position. parliament has a very difficult task, which is to look also to the future, to be proactive and this is the most difficult aspect of elected institutions: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this year, therefore, the budget will have to be a delicate balancing point between opposing forces: we're not just going to hold onto the present, but keep looking to the future and start building it now. this parliament will be making a strong demand for funding for the 2020 strategy, starting with quality employment, but there are also new skills, some of which are delicate; i am thinking of the new powers that the treaty of lisbon gives us, the european financial instruments and markets authority, and then there is the level of payments, which will have to be adjusted from the start, from the moment the budget is adopted, and then there are the undeniable emergencies, i am thinking of the migratory pressures in north africa. what we will continue to do consistently and transparently with respect to the documents on priorities which we have already voted on is therefore to continue to research and to build concrete instruments which will enable us to implement our policies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as rapporteur for the european globalisation adjustment fund, i feel it is my duty to express my concern about the council's preliminary approach to the european commission's proposal to extend the coverage of this fund until 2013 because of the economic crisis. i regard as irresponsible the obstructionist attitude of some delegations in the council, including the dutch delegation, which are seeking to create a blocking minority by opposing this important derogation and at the same time, as is the case today, are benefiting from egf funds worth several million euros, citing precisely the same causes of the economic crisis. a substantial recovery in european labour market conditions is not expected before 2013 and this assessment leads us to make this extension necessary. it would therefore be a grave mistake to undermine this fund, which public opinion sees as one of the few instruments of concrete solidarity of the union precisely because of the economic crisis.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the gas and energy market is one of the instruments of economic growth and employment, which is essential to restore the union's competitiveness and to help it overcome the crisis quickly. it is therefore necessary to prevent abuses and avoid market manipulation, the control and sanctioning of which is entrusted to national competence, together with the prohibition of insider trading. the recent introduction of acer allows market transactions to be monitored, and national and european registers for operators in the sector allow transactions in wholesale energy products to be recorded, thus promoting transparency. today's vote, the result of close cooperation between the polish presidency, the commission and parliament, has laid the foundations for a more transparent market to protect consumers.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is the task of public authorities to legislate in the interests of citizens in order to achieve many objectives: ensuring a fair and competitive market, protecting health, providing safety, stimulating innovation and protecting the environment. it is the responsibility of the member states to transpose european union legislation in a timely and correct manner, for the benefit of the citizens, but unfortunately there are still a large number of infringements, particularly in the area of recognition of professional qualifications, services and public procurement, and therefore many petitions have been lodged denouncing non-compliance with community rules. the eu-pilot project, which has been in operation since 2008, has therefore been useful in that it has reduced the time taken to examine infringements and, for those countries that have made themselves available to collaborate and participate in this project, has avoided the need for infringement procedures and financial penalties.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we welcome the adoption of this report, which is intended to implement one of the fundamental objectives of the lisbon treaty, namely to create a new institutional framework for the transparency of the european institutions. in order to build an open, efficient and independent european administration, it is essential to guarantee a certain right of access for european citizens to documents of the community institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. we consider transparency to be an essential element of participatory democracy, complementary to the representative democracy on which the functioning of the union is based, since it allows citizens to take part in the decision-making process and to exercise public control, thus ensuring the legitimacy of the democratic political system. we cannot remain indifferent to our citizens' calls for greater democracy, for greater transparency and openness of institutions and political actors and for a more determined and precise fight against corruption!
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there is no doubt that the measure we have supported and approved today represents a decisive step forward in terms of the accessibility of the institutions' documents, a further reason for ensuring transparency in the institutions' documents, but also a reason for striking a fair balance between the right to access to documents and the right to privacy, which must in any case be guaranteed in respect of facts and situations that have nothing to do with the need for proper participation in the decisionmaking process of the institutions. the use of community funds can be better guaranteed by means of a process of knowledge which is more significant than in the past, the refusal must always be justified, a step forward in the training of staff and accessibility to documents which also represents a moment of justice for the european citizen.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union has always defended and encouraged multilateralism, especially within the wto, which is the guarantor of economic governance and the regulated liberalization of the world market. i hope that the difficulties encountered this year, the differences arising from the contents of the package to be presented next december, will be resolved, or at least that there will be consensus on specific issues contained in it. there are important issues such as services, the protection of intellectual property and, in particular, the increased protection of geographical indications, trade facilitation and non-tariff barriers. i hope, however, that the negotiations on the doha agenda will not be concluded hastily, thus sacrificing all those requests which have not found a common ground over the years. we need a stronger and more dynamic multilateralism than we have today.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is almost ten years since the doha negotiations began, we will be celebrating their tenth anniversary in two months' time, and they have still not led to any conclusion. the world has changed dramatically. countries that were considered developing in the meantime have become emerging countries, and today those countries are even emerging to the point where they can present themselves as the saviours of the european union or some of its states. the rules of world trade must be rewritten, and trade remains a tremendous source of potential for the advantages of growth and for a better distribution of wealth in the world and for the rebalancing of the north and south of the world. all this has remained unchanged in the multilateral framework, but we also need the possibility of a new reciprocity between countries and we also need to initiate and contribute to a new process of democratization of the world trade organization which, as it stands, cannot work well.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on doha: not only is there no agreement, but it is now obsolete, and it is a failure. we call on europe to take a strong stand - as our parliament did in the last legislature - and for structural changes to the wto. the economic crisis, which is worldwide, cannot wait any longer for a doha agreement which has been a pain for us for 10 years and which we know will never be accepted by many countries. we therefore ask the parliament, the commission and the council to be more firm in their demand for a follow-up to what parliament established in the last legislature, a new functioning of the wto, structural reform, a real step forward to enable the internationalisation of smes and the relaunch of the economy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the treaty of lisbon introduced a number of new features, among which i think the protocol on the role of national parliaments deserves greater attention. the protocol calls on national parliaments to play an active role in defending the principle of subsidiarity during the legislative process. i voted in favour of this report, but i would like to stress that very little has been done so far. the application of this protocol would give our citizens an answer, even if only partial, to their need for democratic legitimacy, and would put an end to the feeling of distance which accompanies the european institutions. i believe that such a need felt so strongly by our citizens deserves more attention, and i therefore hope that further measures will be taken as soon as possible.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the single market, free movement, the treaty of lisbon - these are all things that have come into play without any change in our way of legislating, the european way and the national way. the commitments made on these occasions must be followed up, and in particular a genuine simplification of the legislative system must be initiated, a simplification which must lead to a different dialogue between europe and the individual states. i would start with our own documents - and i take advantage of that to suggest a sort of clarity test on our documents - when we make a white paper, a green paper, everything must be more understandable and i would go so far as to say that the real, perhaps strategic, proposal for our europe to really start this virtuous phase of initiating legislation is to allocate a specific delegation to a european commissioner who is specifically concerned with clarifying legislation and the relations between the states and europe itself.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has confirmed the right to petition the european parliament as a fundamental element of european citizenship. it is therefore a key tool for citizens to bring to parliament their concerns about the impact of different eu policies and legislation on their daily lives. however, an analysis of the various statistics shows that most petitions were declared inadmissible because the signatories continue to confuse national competences with those of the european union. this shows how much more effort is needed to better inform citizens about the meaning of the right to petition. we also want to stress once again the need for a european 'one-stop shop' for citizens to advise them when they are looking for solutions to what they consider to be violations of their rights. we believe that this is an extremely important objective to be achieved in a very short time.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i cannot but agree with the text of this report. mr meyer rightly stressed the need for a european single window. the construction of these offices remains the most important objective yet to be achieved. however, it is clear from the statistics in the reports that there is a major problem of misinformation at european level, not only in relation to citizens' right to petition, but also in relation to so-called informal mechanisms. for example, solvit has been shown to work well, quickly and effectively, but this has not changed the fact that our citizens use this service only marginally. i wonder if it would not be more appropriate to organise a european-wide media campaign on these issues instead of simply improving the parliament's website, an important communication tool, but which does not yet reach all citizens.
