in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the lichtenberger report, which assesses the european commission's control of the application of eu law and the consequent power/duty to initiate an infringement procedure against a member state which has failed to comply with the treaty. the text therefore calls on the commission to propose a code of procedure to ensure greater respect for the rights of european citizens. at the same time, it is desirable to increase cooperation between the community institutions and national parliaments, especially in the implementation of community legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i am convinced that transparency is the best way to prevent corruption, fraud, conflicts of interest and mismanagement. for this reason, the eu must provide a model of institutional transparency and modern democracy for the member states as well as for third countries. it is important to bear in mind that with the lisbon treaty transparency became a legally binding fundamental right of the citizen, and that the need for transparency is not limited to legislative procedures, but also covers the non-legislative work of eu bodies, offices and agencies. the first step is for the eu institutions to make as many categories of document as possible publicly accessible by default on their internet sites, including budgets and lists of public procurement contracts awarded over the last three years.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mrs sargentini's report, which provides an annual review of the application of the regulation on public access to documents of the community institutions. this gives community citizens a fuller picture of the work of parliament, the commission and the council, and enables them to understand better the reality of the institutions.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this proposal for an amendment to parliament's rules of procedure is intended to ensure that parliament itself evaluates the commission correctly, by means of more effective monitoring procedures. i fully agree with the proposal itself, which states that the correct assessment by the commission is vital to improving the governance standards of the eu itself, and i believe that maximum transparency and mutual supervision between the institutions are essential to this end. my vote is therefore in favour.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the text adopted today aims to change the current procedure for hearing commissioners-designate. in particular, the report proposes that for each commissioner-designate there should be two joint questions from the conference of committee chairmen, the first on general competence, european commitment and personal independence and the second on portfolio management and cooperation with parliament. the committee responsible should be asked to put forward three additional questions. in the case of joint committees, each committee would be entitled to put forward two questions. after the hearing, the chair and the coordinators should meet to evaluate the individual commissioners-designate. after these closed-door meetings, the coordinators should express their opinion on the commissioners-designate.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, economic cooperation, including trade, is one of the instruments through which foreign policy is conducted. the european union, for its part, has as its original founding rationale sectoral trade first and the wider single market second. this is a fundamental reason for the absence of a unified, far-reaching, strong and authoritative foreign policy, which would also allow the definition of strategic positions in economic cooperation with other states and geopolitical areas. this situation allows each member country to act autonomously and without coordination, both on its own and within the various international organisations to which it belongs. in order to make the doha negotiations a useful outcome, and to renew the usefulness of the world trade organisation as a forum for solving the problems of equitable development and cohesion among all the associated countries, action must be taken to promote the integration of other countries into long-term policies, by exploiting their competitive advantages on the one hand and strengthening their effective capacity to determine their own development on the other. i believe that the report we have adopted supports this view, albeit modestly.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this text because i believe it shows the utmost commitment of all the institutions to supporting a multilateral trading system in which the world trade organisation is the guarantor of a trading system governed by appropriate measures. the organisation plays a key role in ensuring that globalisation is better managed, that the benefits of globalisation are more equitably distributed and that economic growth is more balanced. a fair and proper conclusion to the doha negotiations would therefore be an important signal of political confidence in the future of a fair world trading system based on shared rules.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the eighth wto ministerial conference will be held in geneva next december. what can we expect from this new negotiation? it will be difficult to wait for a new effort by the developed countries to make further concessions in terms of preferential tariffs. the eu's competitiveness margins are very tight and therefore require some flexibility in the use of export refunds, especially in certain sectors such as cereals, meat, dairy products and wine. our farmers are competing in a market distorted by subsidies, with low world prices, with very strict european quality standards. the doha negotiations will focus, among other things, on the attempt to achieve food security - a subject which is well known to us in the committee on agriculture and on which i would like to stress the need for coherent action and the urgency of the subject. i welcome this new attempt at agreement, but i look forward to seeing tangible results from these negotiations. i hope that in the course of these new negotiations the difficulties faced by our farmers will be taken into account. i would like to conclude by quoting the director-general of the wto, pascal lamy: the more economically developed countries now expect the major emerging economies to compete on equal terms.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, a programme to reduce the administrative burden resulting from european union legislation has been in operation since 2005 with the aim of reducing this expenditure by 25% by 2012, thus generating an increase of 1.4% of gross domestic product. my support for mr karim's report is in the direction of speeding up this process of reducing burdens and simplifying administration without, however, compromising the quality standards that must necessarily be part of the legislative process. the work of the institutions must be simplified and our work must be made clear to the european citizens, who must have easy access to eu databases and legislative acts. greater use of white papers and exclusive use of regulations in legislative proposals are just some of the simple tools that could ensure smaller volumes of legislation without compromising the quality of the legislation.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on better regulation, subsidiarity and proportionality and smart regulation because one of the main objectives of the europe 2020 strategy is precisely to make european legislation more effective and accessible in all european countries. the text therefore calls for the national parliaments of the member states to cooperate and to be involved in the development and application of the new european legislation, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, and also for consultation with the community institutions. better regulation means achieving the objectives set, facilitating the economy by helping businesses and speeding up the european market by making it more competitive.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today in the plenary we voted on the report entitled 'better regulation, subsidiarity and proportionality and smart regulation'. the report by mr sajjad karim further elaborates the presidency's conclusions on the lisbon strategy, with the aim of putting the emphasis on competitiveness and reducing administrative burdens through smart legislation at the service of the citizen. the report stresses in particular public consultations, impact assessments, comitology and simplification of existing legislation. the main recommendations of the report include: member states should be required to justify decisions to introduce requirements in their national legislation that go beyond the standards set in the eu legislative acts they are about to transpose. the european parliament, which has so far received over 300 documents from national parliaments, should give an opinion on the effective functioning of the systems set up within the parliament itself in order to identify any shortcomings and propose improvements.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this text because it stresses the importance of competitiveness and the reduction of administrative burdens through intelligent legislation, capable of bringing benefits to citizens and insisting in particular on public consultations, impact assessments, comitology and the simplification of existing legislation.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr meyer's report, which has made a good point of the work of the peti committee over the past year. by highlighting the data on petitions received by parliament's services, the number, origin and legislative areas concerned by citizens' requests, and by assessing the degree and quality of interinstitutional relations between parliament, the commission and the council, as well as with the european ombudsman, the report provides a true picture of the state of the art in the use of this important tool, such as the petition to the european parliament, available to citizens.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because it is extremely comprehensive in providing an overview of the activities of the committee on petitions in 2010. the report provides a precise and complete picture of the work of the committee, illustrating a series of statistics on the number of petitions received, archived or examined relating to the countries concerned or the subjects dealt with, which constitute an important quantitative tool for evaluating the work of the committee.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have expressed my approval of mr meyer's text on the activities of the committee on petitions in 2010. although slightly down on 2009, the peti committee collected petitions from european citizens who exercised their right to petition on topics of primary importance such as justice, the environment, the internal market, fundamental rights.

the agenda includes the statement by the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the situation in libya.
on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in a communiqué of 5 october last, commissioners füle and malmström welcomed the good results of the dialogue with tripoli as part of a cooperation agenda which included the management of migration flows, border management, pan-african policy and international protection of refugees and asylum seekers. this ambitious agenda has been interrupted for reasons we know, by nato military intervention and regime change in tripoli. i think the first objective is to resume as soon as possible cooperation with libya on these big issues - border management, migration flows, energy supply and the fight against terrorism - but another point that is equally important is support for the new libyan leadership in organising free elections as the first act of a long process that can lead, i hope, one day to building a genuinely democratic and stable state. building a democracy is much harder than winning a war, especially if there is no memory of a previous democracy in the country. i wanted to know what concrete programmes could be put in place in the short term to intervene in civil society and especially in the fields of culture and education, which are the fundamental elements for building a true democracy in the minds and hearts of citizens.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, although there are still pockets of resistance among the supporters of the old libyan regime and although, as long as gaddafi is in power, the national transitional council is still afraid of possible rear-end blows, it is right and proper to focus attention on the post-war challenges. the role of the european union in the process of reconstruction and stabilisation in libya is of considerable importance, beyond the immediate priorities. i am thinking of food, medicine, a plan for security, public order, border control and the very sensitive issue of the withdrawal of weapons. after the wartime phase of the crisis which has seen the european union disintegrated, it is fair to say that now is the time to strengthen europe's role with the necessary determination. we have not only a humanitarian task, although it is important - i am thinking of the many migrants in libya - we cannot fail to be present at the table which is redrawing the new geopolitical picture in the region, which today also marks a new protagonist, turkey, as we see in these hours with the triumphant visit of erdogan to several arab countries, just as we cannot delegate the effective management of the post-war phase to the group of countries which participated in the nato mission. already in the libyan theatre there are signs of a not so creeping competition between some member states that will not be good. in fact, in the race to a new libya, it is not difficult to see the economic and energy interests, but the project for the democratic construction of libya is not as clear, and this is where we need to work very hard. the european union's role is therefore important, not least because the road ahead will not be easy or short, and above all, we must be aware that the democratic outcome is by no means certain.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to draw your attention to a passage in the resolution we are voting on tomorrow in the house concerning libya, which takes note of president jalil's speech in tripoli announcing that libya wants to be a moderate muslim country with a constitution reflecting this state of affairs. i believe that this is a crucial aspect, not only for the future of libya, but also for the future of the whole scenario of the countries of the mediterranean area. tunisia and egypt will also have a new constitution. i ask you and i ask us as a parliament what we are doing to bring ourselves as interlocutors at this delicate stage when new constitutional charters will decide the way in which populations of millions of people live together, and i say this because the constitutional issue is extremely slippery and extremely complex. god is in the u.s. constitution and also in the sudanese constitution, but the result is not the same. god is not in the french constitution and he is not in the chinese constitution, but the result is not the same here either. it is not enough to announce or not to announce values or disvalues, we must understand how we build our future together. i therefore propose that there should be a mission of the european parliament, as a committee on constitutional affairs, and a mission of the european commission which does not want to tell the libyans how to write their own constitution, but simply repeats to the libyans the convictions, what we believe in and which is the basis of our constitutions and our understanding of democracy.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, after 42 years of dictatorship and six months of conflict, libya is at a turning point in its history which can open the way to a future of democracy, peace and development. this future is in the hands of the libyans and no one can think of imposing pre-packaged choices and solutions on them, but at the same time it is clear that the european union has a great responsibility, a decisive role to play in supporting the process of stabilisation and democratic transition in the country. after being marginalised by the divisions among its members in the initial phase of the conflict - a conflict whose wise management must be given to nato - the eu has progressively demonstrated a capacity for action which we appreciate and which has brought concrete results, with the opening of the office in benghazi, with the missions in tripoli, which we would like to see more coordinated, of the external action service and echo. this activism must now be part of a strong and credible political strategy, capable of defining a solid and effective multilateral framework, and of ensuring a real unity of purpose in the international community, avoiding duplication, avoiding competition and guaranteeing real support for the libyan transition. a transition that will inevitably be long and complex, which will have to aim at national reconciliation while avoiding the creation of new rifts of division within the country and at the same time will have to ensure progress and democracy, ensure the involvement of civil society and the renewal of the ruling classes. a transition in which the return to normalcy and the restoration of public order require urgently dealing with complex issues such as border control, the reconstruction of the judicial system and the security sector, the control of the proliferation of arms, but which at the same time will have to be based on a solid and credible democratic and constituent road map. all of this requires dialogue, commitment, leadership skills, and also intensive planning and resource identification. it is therefore an important test for the eu, for the european external action service, for its comprehensive approach, and the european parliament is ready to do its part and to provide its support for this commitment.
in writing. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent years many companies have been encouraged to invest in libya. the serious instability and political and institutional crisis in several north african countries, particularly egypt, libya and tunisia, have forced many european companies to leave libya, leaving behind loans, equipment, etc. council regulation (eu) no 204/2011 of 2 march 2011 concerning restrictive measures in view of the situation in libya provides that the funds may be used only for humanitarian purposes and not for the settlement of claims or losses suffered by companies/companies operating in libya. as a result, many european companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, are having difficulty recovering claims arising from the supply of goods and services in libya. if europe is to provide support for the libyan people and help to rebuild the country, it must also prevent european companies from suffering serious and irreversible damage as a result of the loss of liquidity resulting from any failure to collect debts and thus ensure their survival.
madam president, i am happy to see that the whole parliament has a clear and strong position on the tragedy that is unfolding in syria. the s&d group has just tabled a joint motion for a resolution which reflects the deep concern of europe, the arab world and the rest of the planet over the continued brutal crackdown on peaceful protesters perpetrated by the al-assad regime. the figure of 2 600 has been quoted as the number of people whose lives have been destroyed by the brutality of the regime, but many more have been injured, tortured or detained. demonstrations and protests in syria are demanding the ousting of al-assad and his family and an end to the rule of the baa’th party. the same demand comes from the eu and the most important international actors. the protesters insist on the peaceful nature of their political movement but, in order to justify the atrocities against them, the syrian regime claims it is confronting religious extremists. this message is false and misleading. all indicators and information show that no extremists are leading the democratic protests in syria. we must reject the invitation of the al-assad regime to listen to them and to the other arab tyrannies on the spectre of mujahidism and similar threats. our support for the syrian democratic forces should continue and our revulsion towards the current regime’s course of action must continue to be total. just one final word about sanctions. sanctions by the international community should be maintained, but we should be very careful to keep in place smart sanctions: sanctions against individuals, against prominent members of the government and the al-assad circle of power. that approach works. they should be different from the sanctions of the past that strengthened authoritarian regimes instead of weakening them. i associate myself with the call by several colleagues for a ban on european companies which invest in energy and other sectors in syria.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr minister, mr nicolai, mr commissioner, i think there are three things we can be sure of: the first is the deep friendship with the palestinian people, a people who suffer, suffer every day, and you have to go to the occupied territories to see the daily suffering of the palestinians, and it is a people to whom the international community owes something. the second certainty is the bond that binds us to israel as europeans, a bond that is stronger than any other country probably outside the union, because israel is an indispensable part of europe's cultural and moral identity, it is part of our family. the third unfortunate fact is that europe is always divided or always very conservative in its positions, limits which are also apparent in this vote at the united nations, which will probably be another humiliating occasion after the absence of european policy as such in the libyan crisis, and yet it is up to us, mr minister, mr commissioner. the european citizens are finally demanding a qualitative leap forward, a position of the whole of europe, and i hope that, if possible, a position in favour of the declaration of independence will be adopted, as many israelis are also demanding against their government and as they are calling on the palestinians for a basic sense of justice. support for independence would be in line first of all with the reality of a palestine that exists, that exists in spite of everything, and that no one can erase from the maps, and whose identity is paradoxically being strengthened day by day in the national feeling due to the occupation. secondly, it would also strengthen israel's security and identity itself, security and identity which are better guaranteed by the existence of two divided states with certain borders, rather than by the prospect - and this should be asked of the israeli leaders in twenty years' time - of a single state shared by palestinians and israelis. finally, this declaration of independence would be a breakthrough in the stagnant waters of european diplomacy, in the negotiations which are going nowhere, it would be a breakthrough which, if we give up, condemns us to being, after the financial crisis, a periphery in international diplomacy as well.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, everyone is convinced of the desirability and necessity of creating two states living together in peace. the only difference of opinion is how to achieve these objectives. the intention of the palestinian authority to apply unilaterally to the united nations for recognition as a state is an initiative which in my view could damage the peace process and provoke a chain reaction in the middle east. the intention to isolate israel diplomatically and to make it look like an accomplished fact is evident, at a time when the peace agreements with egypt are being threatened by extremist positions and relations with turkey are in crisis. the attack on the israeli embassy in cairo is the latest in this chain. the palestinian unilateral initiative is contrary to the principle shared by both sides, according to which the only solution to the conflict is bilateral negotiations between both sides. unilateral recognition could therefore create further instability and remove the possibility of building a democratic palestinian state that lives in peace with israel. i therefore believe that we should return to the basic principles of the oslo agreements, based on mutual recognition, peaceful coexistence, security and political rights.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, if arab dictators shoot at the crowds, there is an immediate reaction from the west, no-fly zones, un intervention, and so on. if the israeli air force is bombing gaza, there is silence, because it is natural that israel can bomb the palestinian people. yet the unresolved arab-palestinian conflict is the main cause of conflict between the arab world and the west and is giving strength to extremists. today, the arab revolutions have brought a new wave of democracy to north africa and the middle east, which cannot but affect the relationship between palestinians and israelis, and the very existence of israel is somehow linked to the understanding of this cause: either israel accepts the existence of a palestinian state, or israel will not be able to live under the same conditions in that region. in this context, i think it would be very hypocritical for europe not to show the palestinians the same solidarity that it is showing to those in the arab world, and in other places too, who are fighting for freedom and rights today, because i believe that the right of peoples to have their own territory, to self-determination, to be able to have their own state, is an inviolable right and i believe that europe must support the palestinian resolution at the un.
author of the book. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i have studied the anti-corruption package presented by the commission in june with great attention and i must say that i am very impressed by the contents of this package: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a good starting point and all the european institutions, especially the european parliament, must work to ensure that concrete and quantifiable results are achieved in a short time. corruption is today the main area of penetration of organised crime into the legal economy and the public sector; through corruption, criminal systems are created, dangerous connections between businessmen, politicians, public officials. the estimated damage from corruption in europe is estimated at about 120 billion; i would say that this is an underestimate, because in my country alone, in italy alone, this practice costs 60 billion euros a year, which is practically the amount of money that would save my country from defaulting at the moment. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. what measures does the commission propose to improve the fight against corruption in the private sector? mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr president of the council and mr commissioner, i too would like to welcome, as have other members, the anti-corruption package which the european commission adopted on 6 june. corruption is a transnational phenomenon and measures at european level are needed to combat it. the vast majority of our european citizens, according to eurobarometer estimates, believe that europe must do more. how can you blame them? in many member states there is a lack of political will to fight corruption, and there are still european countries which have not signed the united nations convention against corruption. when we consider the devastating impact of corruption on democratic processes, citizens' rights and trust in the rule of law, it is clear that the national measures taken by member states to combat corruption to date are insufficient to contain the growing phenomenon. it is the european union which must give a united and strong response, especially now, in the midst of an unprecedented economic crisis, which is weighing on people's lives, on the health of social security and welfare systems, on the ability of institutions to guarantee essential services. corruption causes a loss of €120 billion per year, equivalent to 1% of the eu's gdp, and robs the union and its member states of resources that could be used to provide basic services: education, childhood, employment, transport; it's a clean drain on the people's livelihood. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. in particular, we cannot talk about fighting corruption if we are not able to adopt at least minimum standards for the definition of the crime of corruption, of which there is no trace in the package just launched. the same applies to the definition of uniform parameters to measure the extent of the phenomenon in the member states, which is essential to prepare an effective response. we are in favour, for example, of relaunching the eu's network of contact points against corruption, as i proposed in the resolution we are voting on tomorrow.

member of the commission. − mr president, i am delighted to have this opportunity to address all of you before the final vote tomorrow morning on the green paper own-initiative report ‘towards a common strategic framework for eu research and innovation funding’, now known as the horizon 2020 programme. i congratulate the rapporteur, ms matias, for this excellent and enriching report and for delivering it in good time, allowing the commission to consider your proposals in depth in the context of drafting the horizon 2020 package. i would also like to thank the itre shadow rapporteurs, as well as the members of the six committees that delivered their opinions to itre. the parliament has been showing an immense interest in the operation of the future eu research and innovation programme, which is very significant as the horizon 2020 proposals will be transmitted to you for your consideration. horizon 2020 will come into effect for the next financial framework commencing in 2014. within the commission’s proposal for this new budget, the multiannual financial framework adopted on 29 june, we set out a total budget of eur 80 billion for horizon 2020 at constant 2011 prices. this is a budget designed to stimulate growth and jobs. the overall financial envelope is ambitious but realistic. prioritising investment in these areas now is the recipe to ensuring growth and jobs in the future. with this proposal the commission is clearly showing its strong commitment to delivering on the ambitions of europe 2020 and innovation union. the aim of horizon 2020 is to make eu research and innovation funding more efficient, easier to access for participants and have a greater impact. the overwhelming response to the consultation launched by the green paper earlier this year has given us a very practical input as to how this can be achieved. more than 1 300 responses to the online questionnaire were received and stakeholders also submitted some 750 consolidated position papers. i would like to thank ms matias, as well as the other meps who participated actively in the event on 10 june 2011 to wrap up the green paper consultation process. this was an excellent way to show all stakeholders that the eu institutions are working together to achieve the same policy goals. i think that the main issues addressed in your report are in line with those raised during the consultation process. we are clearly in broad agreement concerning the main issues that should be considered in our future funding programme. i would like to highlight some of your suggestions for horizon 2020 that are particularly interesting to the commission. i am of course very satisfied with the strong support you show for the concept of the common strategic framework and its objective of bringing research and innovation closer together and providing support across the full innovation cycle, from lab to market. excellence will remain the main criterion for allocating research and innovation funding. at the same time it is necessary to build stairways of excellence for those member states and regions that are under-represented in the current framework programme. this will mainly be a task for the structural funds. i am determined that our researchers should spend more time at their work and less time on administration. simplification will be a major element of the horizon 2020 package. one issue where we strongly agree is the need for a measure of continuity as regards the main successful instruments in the current programmes. this concerns, in particular, collaborative research, the european research council and the marie curie actions. i am also pleased that we both support an approach that places eu funding close to societal challenges and therefore close to the eu’s ambitious policy objectives in areas such as climate change, health, energy and security. finally, i would like to highlight that the matias report takes on board several ideas already foreseen in the carvalho report on simplification, the merkies report on innovation union, and the audy report on the fp7 interim evaluation. from the commission’s point of view, a line of continuity and coherence has been maintained and this has been of great help to us as we prepare the legislative proposals for horizon 2020.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the commission, the council, the shadow rapporteurs and the opinion rapporteurs of five other committees, which, in addition to the committee on transport and tourism responsible for the subject, have worked on this own-initiative report. it is the first own-initiative report since the lisbon treaty introduced tourism policies as a matter of union competence in article 195. tourism is of course a subject in which there is strong competition between countries and often within each country between regions and territories. so what is the point of trying to work together on a european tourism policy? i think it makes a lot of sense, because we are facing a different world from that of 20 years ago, a multipolar world in which new countries are emerging, giving europe a huge amount of new tourist potential which we must intercept, reinforcing the primacy which europe today holds as the world's leading tourist destination. it makes sense because tourism is one of the sectors that has best withstood the global crisis, so we need to invest heavily to support the competitiveness of our tourism businesses and to support the visibility of our tourism destinations. with this report we aim to develop the 21 actions that the european commission and vice-president tajani identified in their communication of june 2010 and to identify within these 21 actions the priorities to be addressed immediately with a certain timetable. first, the subject of measures to support the competitiveness and access to credit of tourism enterprises; the issue of vocational training and qualification, with the need to invest heavily in new professionals with a more managerial outlook in order to attract these new tourist flows; the key theme of innovation and ict to improve the visibility and presence of our businesses and destinations on the web market. we must find new ways of overcoming a rigid seasonality which is constricting the tourist season and limiting the growth potential of our businesses. we need to keep investing in the stocks that have done well so far, i think calypso among them. we need to work on environmental sustainability and accessibility of accommodation facilities and destinations, so that many millions of possible and potential tourists with disabilities can also be full-fledged tourists. we must give greater value to cultural itineraries, as has been done in recent years with the council of europe, and introduce new ones. we must invest in international events, because international events can be an attractive element for tourists from outside europe. we must invest in quality, by strengthening quality as a central element of the european tourism proposal. we must not hide the fact that there is a problem with the financing of tourism policies. until now, there was a lack of competence and therefore no substantial budget lines to develop these projects, and there were also many resources, somewhat hidden, within the structural funds. so we must, on the one hand, make these existing resources more visible and, on the other hand, work closely with the commission to have specific funding lines to be able to develop the 21 actions and all the ambitious projects we have. this is the horizon we have outlined with this report, which should not remain a stone thrown into the pond, but is the first step in a work on which i believe the european parliament can still do a lot.

in many countries during the summer of this year and the situation has even improved, especially with our work targeting the younger generation, as tourism is one of the sectors in the business world that provides the most employment for young people. i am glad to be able to share the report when it proposes new initiatives and concrete actions of great interest, which i will certainly take into account in implementing the 21 actions of the action plan, which aim precisely at developing a coherent union policy for high-quality, modern, competitive and at the same time sustainable tourism. tourism enterprises, in particular small and mediumsized enterprises, and their digital transition. we intend to improve the supply-demand relationship in the tourism labour market by mapping qualifications and professional skills. we want to ensure a constant quality of the european tourist product and intensify efforts to promote europe as a set of sustainable and high-quality destinations and, as the rapporteur mentioned in his speech, in the context of social tourism we must ensure the future implementation of the calypso preparatory action by creating an internet-based supply and demand platform as a tool to facilitate transnational tourist exchanges. i am convinced that, with increased attention from stakeholders and the involvement of one member state, transnational tourism exchanges and web projects co-financed by calipso will achieve very positive results. as regards sustainability, it is closely linked to competitiveness in this important sector, because the quality of tourist destinations is strongly influenced by the natural and cultural environment and their integration into the local community. our efforts are therefore also aimed at ensuring sustainable development for tourism. in this connection, i intend to propose a european charter for responsible tourism, which will establish at european level the commitment of public administrations, tourist companies and all those interested in promoting tourism activities in europe which meet a set of sustainable and socially, economically, environmentally and culturally responsible principles. i was in madrid last week to conclude the first ethical tourism day and in my speech i emphasized the commitment to combat the exploitation of women and children, but also to protect the environment, and therefore to use tourism as a tool in our strategy to combat climate change. i also intend to increase the visibility of europe and its tourist destinations. we are ready to take part in the summit in krakow on 6 october, which will focus on joint transnational promotion with third countries, and i would like to stress that the european commission has been the protagonist of an initiative, a pilot project, to increase tourist arrivals in europe with latin american countries during the low season. we have signed an agreement with chile, argentina and brazil, to which some of the countries of the union have acceded: first of all spain, france, italy, portugal, poland, but also romania, which - just the other day when i was in bucharest - decided to take of the joint undertaking and the future of the european tourism sector will of course depend to a large extent on the ability to obtain adequate political and financial support for european tourism policy within a current financial framework as well as beyond 2014. i want to reassure those who may have concerns about competence; i am not going to use the legal basis of the treaty, i am not going to violate the principle of subsidiarity, and the european commission - i believe i am once again in agreement with parliament - does not intend to occupy the space and competence of the regions or the competence of the national states in the field of tourism. we are simply trying to increase tourist arrivals within the european union. as i had the opportunity to reply to mr fincantieri during included in the activities to support competitiveness, and i am also counting on parliament's support once again, once the discussions reach the level of the two co-legislators. i thank you once again for your attention and i can assure parliament once again of my commitment to ensuring that tourism can, at this delicate stage, be a key factor in growth and above all a means of protecting the environment and creating new jobs, especially for younger workers.

in writing. i thank mr fidanza for his fruitful work. tourism has enormous potential for achieving some of the european union's important objectives, such as sustainable development, economic growth, employment and socioeconomic cohesion. in recent years, employment growth in tourism has been considerably higher than in other sectors. in fact, the tourism sector in the european union generates more than 4% of gdp, with some 2 million businesses employing around 4% of the total workforce, around 8 million jobs. the need to support the sector is therefore clear, including by improving training and the recognition of professional qualifications. at european level, the union needs to implement an integrated strategy with clear and high-level objectives, with effective and targeted measures that promote innovation and improve the quality of tourism services, for example by ensuring increasing accessibility for people with reduced mobility. i agree with the creation of a european quality label and with the idea of diversifying tourism through cultural, historical and religious promotion, and i stress the importance of tourism promotion through the promotion of european personalities who have spread european culture beyond the continent.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in september, the hunting season opens in many european countries and millions of wild animals are being shot in the name of an anachronistic and no longer justifiable activity. despite the protection provided by european legislation, in some countries, such as italy, some local authorities allow hunting by derogation: it's a hunt for protected birds like the finch or the piper just to appease the hunters' lobby and secure their votes. the veneto and lombardy regions have recently approved the hunting by derogation again, showing contempt and indifference also towards the european court of justice and its very recent judgments condemning it. europe needs tougher rules, to protect wildlife we must say enough to this barbaric medieval practice. we must immediately stop these illegal regulations in these regions.

in writing. citizens of the european union have the right to a high level of road safety. the statistics provide an encouraging figure: in recent years, safety on european roads has increased, with the number of road deaths in the union falling by 36% between 2001 and 2009. the third european action programme 2001-2010 has made a decisive contribution to this, introducing progress in road safety and helping to save precious lives. a recent commission communication sets out the new strategic objectives and, in particular, the ambitious aim of halving the total number of road fatalities in the european union by 2020. while i share and welcome the commission's objectives, i believe that maximum coordination at local, regional, national and european level in the preparation and implementation of the measures to be implemented should not be overlooked. however, given the current structures existing at eu level, it seems unlikely that such an integrated approach can be developed consistently. i therefore share the rapporteur's proposal to establish a european road safety coordinator, who, with the support of the commission itself, would play a valuable role as an intermediary for cooperation between the different levels of intervention.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i must really thank all those who have contributed in these weeks and months to the production of this document which we are voting on today in this house. we have worked very well, i must say, and there has been a very constructive debate. the motion for a resolution which we are voting on today is therefore the fruit of a very joint effort, the fruit of the contribution of all the political forces and of the whole of parliament. i think there's a very strong common sensitivity to this issue, partly because, we have to remember, we live in an era that is really characterized by an exponential increase in disasters. the numbers, if you look at them in their raw form, they speak volumes. the number of disasters in the world has increased fivefold. in 1975, there were 78 catastrophic events, and today we have almost 400 per year. in the last 20 years, these disasters have unfortunately claimed 90 000 lives and affected more than 29 million people, while the economic losses amount to 211 billion euro. it is clear that we are facing phenomena of this magnitude which call for a stronger response, a more effective response and a very strong commitment on our part. we all have in our eyes the images of the earthquake in haiti, the floods in pakistan, what happened in japan. europe itself sees on its territory every year flash floods, fires, let us remember the ash cloud following the eruption of the icelandic volcano. it is not necessary to go any further to say how important the work we are doing here in parliament is, following two fundamental principles which are our polar stars: the principle of solidarity which is reinforced by the solidarity clause of the lisbon treaty and the principle of subsidiarity. we're moving along these lines. the european union's intervention has always been generous and effective in the past - i believe that commissioner georgieva's unsuccessful work is proof of this - but today we need to make a qualitative leap. we are prepared to make a qualitative leap from ad hoc to a response where the response is enhanced by the early identification of the means available in the member states to the european civil protection mechanism. it is also important to emphasize for this leap in quality and to move from information sharing and emergency response to the role of planning and monitoring and coordination that we want the fundamental role of services like gms, and i take this opportunity to also say the concern that there is for what is happening with respect to the budget for these new technologies that are fundamental. we have inserted the importance of communication to the citizens, because this too has been taught by the japanese experience, it is never enough and never sufficient. and we are waiting for the commission, which we ask to submit as soon as possible, to present the proposal on civil protection in legislative form.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner georgieva, we are pleased and i would like to thank first of all rapporteur gardini and the other shadow rapporteurs for their fruitful cooperation on a very topical and extremely important matter such as this. we are pleased, i said, with the balanced and rational approach with which the dossier has been dealt with, which perfectly reflects the principle of subsidiarity and the idea of a solidarity clause which should inspire the actions of the member states in response to disasters and in the role of civil protection. in particular, i believe that it is necessary to develop a predictable and planned system within the framework of the european union's civil protection mechanism, in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity and therefore without this entailing the creation of a supranational body, which would risk duplicating costs and competences without guaranteeing efficient operation. i particularly appreciate the attention paid to extremely vulnerable areas such as islands, which is well expressed in the body of the whole report, as well as the emphasis on the link between preparedness, prevention and response to disasters which forms an inseparable triad. finally, i think it deserves attention, and i am pleased that other colleagues have also shown the same sensitivity in dealing with the subject of major regional risks, and in particular the many references to actions and strategies aimed at fighting fires.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too join in thanking mrs gardini for her excellent work. it is clear, and we all know it, that in the event of natural disasters, and also human disasters, the best thing to do is to prevent them, but that is not always possible. and yet, when they do, we must be prepared to intervene in the best possible way and as quickly as possible. the lisbon treaty therefore allows the european union to also act in the field of civil protection and it is therefore appropriate, in the event of a disaster, to be able to set up emergency management centres that are operational 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. we must avoid overlapping and duplication of efforts at both political and operational level, and it is therefore important, in the spirit of european solidarity, to stress the need for all member states to contribute to the implementation of this project. there must be no barriers when we are in need, but we must be able to intervene quickly and as efficiently as possible. and then, if you can also reduce costs in times of crisis, of course it doesn't hurt.

member of the commission. − madam president, thank you very much for the excellent comments and suggestions for the legislative proposal. i shall try to group my answers, starting with what this proposal would do in bringing together a true european capacity. madam striffler brought up this question first. we also had a question from madam grossetête on how this relates to the barnier report. what we are proposing is to integrate the capabilities of member states and in this sense it is more lexis than substance: where the barnier report was leading us on to and where we are going to be. in the barnier report, from which we have adopted a total of 12 proposals, the idea is to integrate the capabilities of member states but there the approach was more top-down, whereas what we are coming with is bottom-up. i can say with confidence that we have support from member states for this proposal, especially from member states where the national requirements are such that the delegation is not even at the level of federal or central government but goes down to regional authorities. so we will have an integrated capacity, we can call it a force, of member states’ assets. i want to stress that we are not waiting for the legislative proposal to advance. we have already made significant advancements in integrating the capabilities of member states. when i took office, we had less than 40 modules registered at european level. i can report today that we have 124 modules registered at european level, plus eight coordination teams. the advancements we have taken are in response to the needs. just for information, in 2010 alone we activated our civil protection mechanism 28 times. for reference: in previous years it would be two, three, four or five times and this year we already have activated it 11 times and the probability is that there may be more activations. let me take a second point that was brought up by many meps – mr arsenis, mr czarnecki and madam de brún and, i am sure, others – on the importance of preparedness and prevention. we know that a euro invested in prevention brings four to seven euros in return. yet, moving ahead with prevention has proven to be difficult in europe and elsewhere in the world. we recognise how critically important prevention is. i have just come back from washington where, we in the commission took the lead, together with the world bank and the government of japan, in making this question of preparedness and of prevention a high global priority and we will continue with structured measures focusing on actions taken in prevention in order to boost this work. we will come back with additional legislative proposals in this area as we advance in our operational thinking. of course, forests are a big part in our prevention measures. they matter in floods, they matter in being ready for forest fires, they matter in the ecological system for cities and rural areas. so, mr arsenis, you will see forests becoming a big part of our preparedness and prevention work. but preparedness is also training together, and this is where the commission has already advanced our role. just last friday i was in poland taking part in a five country preparedness exercise, carpatex, and i can tell you that bringing our community of civil protection together is paramount in saving lives, and reducing property, and we in the commission are dedicated to do more of it. i was asked by mr leinen and mr seeber how we coordinate with the high representative and i can give you a very positive report that on the basis of activations and practice in dealing with crises we have advanced significantly the institutional arrangements and we have much more clarity in who does what, when and where. clearly, inside europe the high representative has no role. two-thirds of activations of the civil protection last year were inside europe and there it is a matter of internal eu action. outside europe, we act as a first responder bringing civil protection humanitarian aid, whereas the high representative has a role in political and defence coordination. of course, in complex crises the high representative takes the lead and there we bring our skills and capabilities – this is best practice in our member states, where civil protection is coordinated. member states have their own civil protection coordination centres and politics and defence are coordinated. sometimes civil protection steps in and sometimes they have no role depending on the type of crisis. those of you who watched president obama of the united states responding to the floods recently, will have seen that he did it from the civil protection centre of the united states, but when you watch him, in the case of bin laden, he was in the situation room of the united states, in the white house. so, we do have separate roles, we do of course have to coordinate in complex emergencies and depending on the emergencies we define exactly how this coordination takes place. what obstacles do we face from member states? the critical issue we face is to assure member states that we are mindful of their legislative conditions, in other words, that we respect how civil protection is organised in each and every one of our member states, and recognise that in national disasters where there is no role for the european union and the country can cope on its own, of course we will not interfere in this response. member states in current fiscal conditions and the budgetary environment want to be sure that we will be mindful of cost efficiency. i can give you my word that i am very fiscally prudent and that, yes, we will make sure that every euro of our taxpayers’ money is spent in the best possible and most effective manner. in other words, at community level when it makes sense and at the country level when it is more appropriate. i was also asked about how we deal with post-disasters. it is a very critical question to link relief to rehabilitation and development and to make sure that development assistance, including technical capabilities from the european union, is made available to countries affected by disasters. we have taken some measures in that respect to improve the post-disaster risk assessment that is carried out and then make sure that the european contribution is in this context of internationally coordinated efforts in developing countries. i do agree that this is an area where more work needs to be done, and we have made it a priority with commissioner piebalgs for our cooperation. i very much agree with ms de brún that we must respect the principles of neutrality, impartiality and independence when we provide humanitarian assistance, including civil protection in-kind assistance in developing countries, especially in areas that are affected not only by disasters, but also by conflicts. this must always be respected and i am grateful to baroness ashton for very much supporting this principle of neutrality and independence in humanitarian work. speakers including ms dăncilă – i apologise if i mispronounced the name – made a point on the solidarity fund. we work together with commissioner hahn to make a proposal for redefining the solidarity fund so that it can act immediately through a pre-funding arrangement in case a country is affected by disasters. last year i faced a very uncomfortable situation when floods affected moldova and romania. in moldova we can provide humanitarian assistance overnight, in romania we cannot. i am therefore a very strong proponent of making sure that solidarity is expressed right at the time when people need it when a disaster hits. on the question of gmes, this is a pilot project that is very much on the priority list of the working programme for the commission. the pilot project is now completed but the commission intends to support gmes financially to the extent possible in the next multi-year financial framework and of course we count on parliament to support our proposal so that it can be done. last but not least on the forest fire-fighting reserve, this is a pilot project that unfortunately came to an end. we cannot extend it, but we are going to include it in the legislative proposal. talking about where we have difficulty with member states, some of our member states are really not in favour of it so we would need your support in parliament. it is the right thing to do, we have seen it in the years we have applied it, but we still have some work to do to convince member states that this funding arrangement has to be continued once the legislative proposal is being done. i apologise for taking so long, but there were very many good questions and i did not want to skip any of them.

member of the commission. − on the currency issue, it is true that the currency of china is undervalued and it is not good that a currency does not reflect the strength of an economy, so they should adapt. but on the other hand, there are always two sides to every coin. you should realise that two thirds of what we import from china we re-export, to the extent that if the renminbi were to suddenly rise, a surge would also certainly harm our economy. so, let us try to look at it from both sides.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we welcome the adoption of this report because it has the great merit of combining european programmes relating to research, competitiveness and technological innovation with the structural and cohesion funds for the same areas. this is a necessary step forward in the reorganisation of existing instruments and programmes, which aims to define a new long-term strategic policy. strengthening convergence, consolidation and the union's overall competitiveness, based on a cooperative model, are elements of the response to economic recovery and a development model based on sustainable growth and increased employment creation. proposing a common framework despite the obvious differences in the european context is a unique opportunity to strengthen the european research area and to define a clear convergence strategy. this will enable us to restore the right balance in terms of access and participation.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i fully supported mrs matias' report because it combines the many factors which will have to promote and implement future innovative processes. scientific research must play the strategic role of finding cures and solutions to the problems of european citizens, and innovation must translate these results into the operational reality closest to us. this is particularly true of agriculture. as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on agriculture and rural development, i wanted to stress the role that research in the agricultural sector should play, aimed not only at obtaining results in the laboratory but also and above all at transferring its effects to the field, to the benefit of farmers and all agricultural stakeholders. we still need to invest in human resources as distribution, training and consultancy services are essential elements to promote knowledge-based growth in agricultural and agri-food enterprises.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report is an important step forward. research and innovation are essential for development and economic growth. it is therefore a matter of priority to propose a common framework for the reorganisation of existing instruments and programmes. europe, despite being the richest macro-region in the world, has not invested adequately in research, development and innovation. it is enough to say that the united states and japan have invested considerably more in this area. and so we must run, we must break down the inequalities that remain between the different european countries. only in this way will it be possible to avoid the more advanced countries in terms of science and technology continuing to benefit to a greater extent from existing programmes at european level. i therefore stress the need to reorganise existing instruments and programmes and to create new ones, so as to make possible a strategy of sustainable and inclusive growth, bearing in mind the objectives of stability, economic convergence and employment.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the preparation of the common strategic framework for the financing of research and innovation is one of the greatest opportunities for development and the european economy. it is a question of acting on the lever that can really trigger a moment of growth and also of new skilled employment, such as that of researchers and young people who are devoted to the new opportunities of innovation and technology and related professions. one observation that emerges from this work is that we must increasingly emphasize in europe research and innovation that leads to practical application, that leads to the creation of new businesses, that leads to new patents and that does not remain pure basic research, pure knowledge, important, yes, but not such as to really trigger the spring of development. the second point is the relationship with local authorities, regions and territories, which are also an important tool for planning in the territory and for the meeting between research, universities, centres of excellence and businesses.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome mrs cavada's report and i believe that it deals with a very important and very topical subject: the question of the future of the european union. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the budget. in times of crisis, unfortunately, there is always a tendency to sacrifice a little bit of everything in the spending on culture, education and social affairs, and above all there is a tendency to adopt a conservative attitude, which is certainly not to be supported. this report gives substance to a concern expressed by a large group of representatives of parents of pupils in european schools who also addressed the committee on petitions, precisely because they had the feeling that the budgetary manoeuvre would not include provisions to accompany the new programme for european schools. the report certainly has a clever plan to try to respond positively to the concerns of the people concerned and at the same time to give a solid base to the policy of the european institutions. the european school and the european schools are a frontier which this parliament and the european institutions have set for all of us. this policy, on the other hand, risks closing the horizon of european training for all.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european schools were set up with the aim of ensuring access to education in their mother tongue for the children of staff of the european institutions who are called upon to work and live abroad in a cultural context different from that of their country of origin. the first european school was set up in luxembourg in 1953 on the initiative of a group of civil servants. over the years, in view of the positive aspects of this form of education, as many as 14 european schools have been set up in the various member states. while recognising that the european school system is a necessity rather than a luxury, it is clear that more than 50 years after the creation of the first european school, this system may be outdated and must be adapted and adapted to new economic and social needs. i therefore voted in favour of mr cavada's text, which calls for the european union to be more involved in supporting and coordinating the action of the member states in developing and improving the european school system. and we know that investing in education means investing in the future of our young europeans.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report clearly shows the difficulty many european regions have in managing the structural funds made available to the union through cohesion policies. we often find ourselves in a maze in which, if the regions manage to manage these funds, it is often the national governments who then have difficulty in activating the cofinancing funds. so sometimes it's the dog biting its tail: we are therefore unable - as has recently been the case in our own country, italy - to spend the funds which we consider to be essential for growth and european cohesion. i therefore voted in favour of this report, but i believe that we must speed up the adoption of the new economic programming cycle for 2014-2020 in order to allow individual european states and regions to equip themselves in time. the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. this could be a way forward, so i voted in favour, but i think that further steps must be taken to ensure that european funds are actually spent in the interests of the citizens.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, if i have supported this report, i think it is a very good report. what mr theurer has done is a reconnaissance exercise which will certainly also serve the imminent legislative effort which the regi committee is undertaking with regard to the new regulation on the funds. the problems highlighted are many and varied, just as the absorption capacity of individual states is different, as the rapporteur points out, because each one shows different performances with regard to the volume of expenditure and therefore its efficiency and effectiveness. i believe that of the nine problems highlighted in this report, the two which require more attention are, firstly, the problem of programming time, as mr antoniozzi has also pointed out, and secondly, the problem of controls. controls that indicate that member states are focusing more on procedures than on objectives. we should instead be pushing ourselves towards the objectives in order to achieve effective and efficient performance, and to do this i reiterate my proposal, which i try to point out to this institution at every useful opportunity, which is the one concerning the possibility of replacing contributions with tax levies. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the face of the dramatic increase in natural disasters both inside and outside the european union, we are increasingly called upon to intervene and ensure a rapid and effective response, as provided for by the new legal basis introduced by the treaty of lisbon. however, we should be able to concentrate on a preventive identification of the means available in the member states and made available by the european civil protection mechanism on a voluntary basis; this would be a major step forward from the current ad hoc response to disasters, in the sense of advance planning through the development of baseline scenarios, the assessment of member states' resources and effective emergency planning. we therefore support a further simplification of the european civil protection mechanism, which has so far proved too bureaucratic, and we support the creation of a single emergency response centre, operating 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, which, in conjunction with the member states, will decide on the means to be deployed in the event of a disaster, in order to ensure immediate and effective assistance to the victims.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, every year we have a few thousand people who die as a result of natural disasters and tens of billions of euros are lost. now, these numbers are dramatic numbers, and not all disasters are inevitable. the report by mr gardini is timely in this respect, because it essentially identifies the two main points of the new european strategy for civil protection. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter, and whether it is not in the interests of the community to take a decision on the matter. we must move from the emergency, which is requested by a state in the event of a disaster and its subsequent intervention, almost as a concession by another country, to a real strategy. i hope that the opinion voted today will be useful to the citizens of europe.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent decades the exponential increase in the number of natural disasters has caused the death of tens of thousands of people in various parts of the world. last year, in the committee on development, i followed the report on the european union's disaster response capacity, which showed how much more could be done to ensure a coordinated european union response to the increase in earthquakes, floods and tsunamis. the european union's response to the earthquake in haiti, for example, has clearly demonstrated the complexity of existing instruments and procedures. although the member states and the community institutions acted promptly in terms of sending humanitarian aid, the management of the crisis raised a number of problems in terms of efficiency, coordination and transparency. for this reason, i voted in favour of the text by mrs elisabetta gardini, who calls for greater efficiency in all phases of disaster management, greater coordination between the parties involved and simplification to avoid unnecessary duplication and loss of time which would impede the provision of rapid and effective aid.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, three small points: we need more europe here too. i think it is inevitable that on some subjects there is indeed an attitude in which not only is more europe desired, but more europe is built. more europe means, for example, that we should really start thinking about a common road police force, with identical rules in the field of safety. more europe means having a european training policy, not simply delegating this to the individual states, but building, for example, a real training policy for schools, for young people, even for the categories that are a little more at risk. more europe means having common tools in cars to improve safety, alcohol and sleeping protection - i believe that this is a timely strategy to build with car companies and european car manufacturing. i think that if all this falls within the framework of the conviction of a common policy, i really think that perhaps conditions will improve.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report deals with the subject of global food security: it means that this issue is not just about hunger in the world or in the poorest countries, but that the issue of food supply affects all communities, even those in the most developed countries. i draw some essential lines of coherence between european policies and this objective of global food security, because we are an institution that preaches very well, but is often not consistent in its choices. i just want to outline three other innovative titles that i think we should develop more. first of all: the food supply is now threatened by price volatility, because of food speculation that must be contained or prevented, derivatives, etc. secondly: the issue of land grabbing, land grabbing, which must be the subject, i think, of some form of treaty or negotiation, because it is not only the democracy but also the survival of many peoples at risk. thirdly: the consistency between energy supply and energy policies. we cannot, in order to produce new energy, prevent the production of food for the peoples of the world.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted strongly in favour of this report by mr zimmer, first of all for a purely political reason, because i think it is necessary to put this great question of food security back at the centre of the initiatives of the whole european union. it is not just and solely about helping developing countries to deal more effectively with this issue, but the food crisis - with demand for agricultural products expected to increase by over 70% by 2050 - is a major issue which, if not tackled in time and with determination, will become one of the main threats, if not the most important threat, to stability, peace and even democracy, as we have seen. i therefore believe that it is essential that the whole of the european union, together with the member states, should make all the necessary efforts, starting with adequate economic investment, as indicated in the report, in this direction to tackle this great issue seriously.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thanks to the wto and the many multilateral and bilateral initiatives, world trade has experienced a real expansion in recent years. however, if in 2000, when the lisbon strategy was adopted, the european union still accounted for 25% of world production, it is estimated that its share in 2020 will not exceed 18%. at the same time, developing and emerging countries have increasingly integrated themselves into international trade and have become the real new engines of the world economy. this was particularly evident during the crisis of 2008-2009, when it was primarily emerging countries that played a stabilising role in a time of widespread financial crisis. the european union cannot ignore the fact that population growth is following a reversal of trend in the union. the population of the developing countries continues to increase rapidly, and this will also have an impact on their economic situation. we therefore urge the commission to make a more careful analysis and to prepare forecasts which take account of the current realities of the world economy and the present situation in the european union, as well as the likely future changes.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the estimates in mr caspary's report on the forecasts for gdp growth in the european union and for exports are really discouraging. we cannot continue to plan our trade strategy on the assumption that the status quo will continue in the current international trade environment. the overall europe strategy has been a failure and i think the european commission should look into the causes behind it: we need critical and detailed analysis, but above all a global vision of how to tackle the economic challenges of the future. the trade policy must be coordinated with the other economic policies of the european union, but above all it must be accompanied by a parallel policy capable of countering the phenomenon of demographic decline.
