in writing. - mr president, i voted in favour of the cavada report on the european schools system because they have been an excellent education and training system since the first european school opened in luxembourg. they are the only means of enabling the children of european officials to receive education in their own language and to learn about the other languages and cultures of the union in a multilingual and multicultural environment. however, the system needs to be reformed to make it more compatible with national systems and at the same time the member states must make a greater effort to meet their commitments in terms of financial support and the identification of native-language teachers, which many member states are partially failing to do, with the result that the financial support of the commission and some member states is being burdened. i think it is important that these schools take on pupils with special educational needs and improve their skills in the education of disabled pupils in order to ensure their full integration.
in writing. the european school, established in luxembourg in 1953, is a unique training experience, offering students with different mother tongues the opportunity to study on a single course. the european schools, which had over 22,000 pupils in 2010, allow children whose parents work abroad to study in their mother tongue, following a structured educational path, so as to ensure their proper reintegration, at any time, into a school in their country of origin. the project, which is a clear investment in the future of europe's young people, should therefore be evaluated, even if the economic crisis means that cuts are inevitable. i therefore support the idea of adequate funding so that teaching can continue to be entrusted to native-language teachers, despite the costs. i also call on the member states to work not only to preserve this system but also to develop this model of teaching, unique and exceptional in europe, which opens up exciting prospects for the creation of a european system of education. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i strongly believe that education plays a vital role in the process of growth of each individual. i fully share the desire to move towards an integrated school system which uses the 'european schools' as a vehicle for the transmission of an education geared to promoting greater student mobility between member states and greater multilingualism and multiculturalism. i would also like to stress the need to ensure that all children have the same conditions of education, and to avoid the idea that the european schools are an elite system that is not easily accessible. to this end, it is important that member states agree on the organisation of the education system and the content of teaching, while protecting the cultural and linguistic identities of the various students.

in writing. the european schools were set up to ensure that the children of staff of the european institutions who are called upon to work and live abroad in a different cultural context have access to education in their mother tongue, so that they can return to a school in their home country at any time. they are therefore a necessity, not a luxury. more than 50 years after the creation of the first european school, it is clear that the concept on which they are based must be developed and adapted to new economic and social needs. however, this concept must remain an inspirational model for national education systems, so as to enhance european citizenship and promote the development of mobility. although the financial crisis imposes some budget cuts, it is essential to look at the situation more as an investment in the future of europe's young people than as a cost.

in writing. - mr president, i support mrs gardini's report and the call on the commission to improve the european response to disasters. the increasing pace of climate change and the depletion of natural resources are increasingly affecting different countries and regions of the world, and the european union is certainly not exempt from the many risks that arise from this. fortunately, the european union has the main tools to respond to disasters, although these are still limited to systematic scenarios and protocols of action that make it rigid to deploy them in other contexts. i hope that concrete consideration will be given to the possibility of creating a european emergency response centre, a nerve centre for the timely and effective coordination of assistance, and also the creation of a european civil protection force to bring together the resources and capabilities of all the member states.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because it underlines the vital need to reinforce the coordination of the response to disasters affecting the european union, both within and outside its borders. unfortunately in the past years there has been a dramatic increase in the number and severity of these natural and man-made disasters affecting the union and its citizens, as well as other countries and regions around the world. this text highlights the need to rationalise and simplify the functioning of current european disaster response and reassert that disaster preparation, prevention and response cannot be dissociated from each other. i also would like to stress that preventing disasters is often more cost-effective than combating them. for this reason it is fundamental to complement the policy for enhancing the eu’s emergency reaction capacity by stepping up the eu’s and member states’ risk prediction and prevention policies. in order to do so the commission should prepare a comprehensive and innovative eu strategy on disaster risk reduction.
in writing. - the times we live in are characterised by an exponential increase in catastrophes: last year europe faced a series of very serious disasters, including flash floods and rare wildfires. over the past 20 years, disasters in europe have affected more than 29 million citizens and caused economic losses of €211 billion. in the context of the dramatic increase in natural disasters, i share the rapporteur's call for greater efficiency in all phases of the european disaster management cycle, including prevention, preparedness, response and recovery, while optimising economic resources. the lisbon treaty itself introduces a new legal basis for civil protection to ensure a rapid response to disasters occurring in the eu or beyond its borders. i also hope that the european civil protection mechanism will be simplified, which i think is too bureaucratic. i welcome the creation of a 24-hour emergency response centre which, in conjunction with the member states, will decide on the means to be deployed in the event of a disaster, in order to ensure immediate and effective assistance to the victims.

in writing. − water is an invaluable resource given its scarcity and the need for careful management. the management of freshwater requires special attention: if we also consider climate change, it is a fundamental challenge for the whole world. on the other hand, it should not be forgotten that in recent decades no other natural phenomenon has been as damaging as flood disasters, despite the fact that the costs of managing and preventing them have been far from negligible. a balanced investment is needed to improve water collection and storage methods, to increase the effective and sustainable use of water resources and to reduce both the effects of flooding and the adverse effects of drought. that is why i voted in favour of this report, although i believe that further work is needed to achieve the objective of limiting climate change.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thought i could support mr deva's text, which deals specifically with the problems of global warming and the consequent need to invest in dam infrastructure for developing countries. the floods that have also affected various parts of the world in recent years are a testimony to the fact that the problem of flooding is contingent and requires specific responses from both a preventive and an infrastructure point of view. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment and the environment from the adverse effects of certain substances and preparations is a very good one.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as members of a community so developed and full of initiatives, i think it is appropriate to support increased financing for the construction of infrastructure, in this case dams, in developing countries. the solidarity and humanitarian aid we can give to these realities, sometimes so distant from our own, is fundamental for these countries. i believe that it is a moral and civic duty for the european union to provide aid that can prevent disasters and, above all, that can provide drinking water and irrigation in areas where the situation is highly dramatic.
in writing. − no other natural hazard has caused more damage or loss of life than the floods of the last century, despite billions of dollars invested in flood management. the development of decentralised water infrastructure is a prerequisite for ensuring water security in africa and for achieving the millennium development goals. some improvements in storage methods are needed to ensure sufficient water supply during periods of drought and to retain excess water during floods. the current average storage capacity per capita in africa is about 200 cubic metres per year, far below that of developing countries in other regions. the text voted today stresses the need for a comprehensive flood strategy in those regions where the presence of unstable glacial lakes poses a serious threat of flooding.
in writing. the report will be voted on by a majority of the members of the committee on budgets. there is no doubt that dams bring about immediate changes in the ecosystem and sometimes damage to existing homes and structures, but we must consider that they also bring about economic and social well-being linked to the possible uses, in addition to the production of clean energy. the rapporteur is able to consider dams to be harmful because they produce co2. perhaps the official documents of parliament should stop regarding co2, which we also ingest by drinking carbonated drinks, as the worst poison on the planet. i think we would emit a lot more co2 producing electricity using fossil fuel than we would with a hydroelectric system.
in writing. − since the middle of the last century there has been a steady increase in the frequency of severe flooding and this will become an even more serious problem in the coming decades. according to a united nations estimate, by 2050 as many as two billion people will have to live with the threat of severe flooding. and if flooding is becoming a serious problem for western countries too, it must be stressed that, unfortunately, once again developing countries, lacking in early warning systems and reliable construction, are the most vulnerable to the effects of flooding. these countries, moreover, base a large part of their economy on agriculture and if agricultural areas are not safely protected from the effects of flooding, the damage caused may result in, in addition to crop losses, a serious slowdown in the already fragile economic chain. the european union must therefore continue along the path it has started, by working to increase the construction of dams in these countries and to improve the protection of buildings against flooding by developing flood storage areas and adequate diversion systems. for these reasons i have expressed my support for mr deva's report.
in writing. - mr president, i voted in favour of mrs zimmer's report because the problem of food security, especially in developing countries, is a challenge for all industrialized countries and in particular for the eu, in order to achieve the millennium goals. despite the commitment made, progress in this area is still insufficient and fao's estimates of the number of hungry people in the world - over 900 billion - are impressive. the eu, like the member states, should give the fight against poverty the highest priority so that its eradication can be achieved and made a sustainable goal. the eu must make its efforts to promote respect for human rights in relation to food, water and energy more effective, giving them the appropriate weight in the eu's energy policy strategy, sustainable development strategy and future development cooperation.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because it asks for immediate steps in order to make the right of food security a reality. food insecurity is challenging the achievement of the millennium development goals, especially in sub-saharan africa and the least developed countries. as we all know, the growing threat of food speculation, climate change, global land acquisitions, loss of biodiversity and pressures on water have contributed to further affect the state of food security in the world. for this reason all the european institutions as well as the member states must put the eradication of poverty, hunger and malnutrition as the first item on their agendas. it is imperative to stress that emergency mechanisms could have negative effects, especially on local economies, and must not be thought of as a long-term solution. a sustainable development policy could only be based on a cooperation approach.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important to support developing countries in implementing food and nutrition security policies, which are essential for the extension of human rights in these countries. i would like to stress in particular how the alleviation of the problems of poverty in the world must be the result of a wide-ranging cooperation which is essential for the promotion of common peace and security. in this connection, i believe that each member state must contribute to assisting the developing countries through new and more substantial investments in agriculture, and in reducing the debt of these countries, removing barriers to international trade and promoting youth employment policies. ensuring the availability of food, its accessibility and adequate caloric intake must be a priority for all countries as a fundamental right of every individual.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, food security is essential to balanced development at all levels. its relationship to the sustainability of primary sector production is expressed in several ways. both in environmental terms, through the use of eco-friendly techniques and products and through the non-speculative exploitation and management of the immense natural genetic heritage that exists, especially in developing countries. both in economic terms, by exploiting the competitive advantages between the different areas and countries, which would also allow developing countries to be part of a fair and global growth, and on the other hand by promoting the relationship with the territories, favouring zero-kilometre products where the costs and energy pollution linked to transport and the quality and tradition of the products can be better appreciated. in social terms, the processes of progressive urbanization and demographic growth, especially in developing countries, must be balanced with the needs of presence in the territories. finally, in political terms, because the primary and food sectors represent the most concrete daily foundations of coexistence between people, including in relations with the institutions. the report approved supports this view.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i supported mrs zimmer's report because i believe that growth in agriculture is an effective lever in the process of poverty reduction and job creation. if we add to this the synergy of factors which encourage agricultural production, guaranteeing those countries a guaranteed food supply, then the step taken will have been a very important one. the eu's role in this difficult process is to create and dialogue in order to launch an education and training project that can create professionalism, investment opportunities and enable young people to pursue agronomic studies that can produce better and in a specialised and sustainable way, thus curbing rural exodus and reducing poverty. i believe that the creation of partnerships between local agricultural organizations at the various stages of implementing an agricultural policy in developing countries would strengthen the process of agricultural development. in this context, the european union should work to strengthen local associative structures in order to ensure that the interests of local communities are protected.
in writing. − food insecurity is a challenge to the achievement of the millennium development goals, particularly in sub-saharan africa and the least developed countries. according to fao estimates, 925 million people suffered from hunger in 2010; this is down from 1 023 million in 2009, but still higher than the number of undernourished people in 2008 (around 815 million). new challenges, including the growing threat of food speculation, climate change, global land acquisitions, biofuels, biodiversity loss, land degradation and pressures on water resources have contributed to further undermining the food security situation in the world. in this context, the current problems of hunger and malnutrition have led to a review of the approach to food security not only at eu level but also at global level. the report adopted today calls on the european union and its member states to affirm their commitment to combating poverty and hunger in the world in the framework of international organisations such as the world bank, the international monetary fund and the wto.
in writing. - the rapporteur's arguments, which we agree with, that 'financial speculation' on food markets is the cause of price rises or sudden price falls, lead to proposals which we strongly oppose. the rapporteur calls for the elimination of incentives for european farmers and for the elimination of all agricultural export subsidies, always putting the interests of third countries ahead of those of the eu countries.
in writing. - congratulations to mr zimmer, who has succeeded in harmoniously balancing the proposals of the committee on development with almost all the suggestions contained in the opinion of our committee on agriculture. i am particularly pleased that the point which was particularly close to my heart, namely energy self-sufficiency, has been taken up in its entirety in paragraph 22. i think it is important to stress that part of the aid for the pvs must contribute to the construction of renewable energy plants and to good water management, all in the context of aid for the acquisition of know-how with the aim of the country's independence from external influences. self-sufficiency, whether in energy or food production, must be integrated into the policy of developing countries aiming to improve their food security, especially through the implementation of food strategies aimed at alleviating poverty and eventually making aid itself superfluous. i would like to conclude by making a point. as shadow rapporteur for the opinion in the committee on agriculture, i voted against paragraph 63. this is because, in the opinion we expressed in the committee on development, we have already specifically stressed the need to phase out export subsidies (see paragraph 29), but we cannot accept that, in a full review of the cap, the committee should with an additional paragraph require the permanent elimination of incentives.
in writing. - mr president, the challenge of the europe 2020 strategy is to boost the growth of our economies in a smart, sustainable and inclusive way through the opening up of trade and investment. but to achieve these objectives and to move rapidly towards a productive future, it is first necessary to combat unfair trading practices with the appropriate instruments and to guarantee to us consumers and our businesses free access to the market, to services and investments, to raw materials and to public procurement, and also to protect intellectual property rights. it is right that the european union should continue to negotiate in the wto so that both 'offensive' interests, i.e. those aimed at free access to the world market, and 'defensive' interests, linked to the consequences of liberalisation, are properly taken into account in the conclusion of bilateral agreements.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the union needs a coherent long-term trade strategy in order to take account of the major emerging countries. such a strategy should be based on a thorough analysis of the current trends in world trade, the union’s internal and external development as well as the diversity of european enterprises. it is important to stress that micro-enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises represent 99 % of all enterprises in the eu and have great potential to create new jobs and innovation. for that reason internal and external policies should better address their specific needs to enhance their competitiveness. with regard to external policy, the parliament must support the commission in its goal to promote sustainable development, free and fair trade, international labour standards and decent work. we should not forget that trade policy must promote development, permit better regional cooperation, encourage investment and improve economic governance, reminding all stakeholders that other regions of the globe have shown how trade can contribute to welfare.
in writing. - i support the new trade policy. increasing european gdp, tackling demographic change and increasing exports are essential to reduce the eu's dependence on trade. i stress the need for balanced trade agreements between the eu and its trading partners, to the mutual benefit of all. it is also important to protect (through international standardisation) consumers, the environment, health and safety standards for products and intellectual property rights. cooperation between customs and external border surveillance authorities is therefore essential, but it must also develop a reciprocal exchange of goods and technology between the eu and developing countries. the importance of relations with the united states for the development of efficient, low-carbon technologies and for dialogue on legislative and regulatory issues was emphasised. finally, i believe that in an economy based on low labour costs, innovation and the identification of competitive advantages are crucial for the eu. foreign direct investment is vital for the european economy, given the importance of innovation for strong and sustainable growth, through the creation of european project bonds (project bonds).
in writing. - we cannot define the guidelines for the new european trade policy without taking account of the considerable changes which have taken place over the last decade on the international economic scene. just think of the great expansion of countries like china and india, which in 2000 contributed only 10% to the world economy, whereas by some estimates, by 2020 they could reach 25%. in order to promote the competitiveness of european industries, i believe that the time has come to develop a long-term external trade strategy capable of meeting the many challenges of this new scenario. only by strengthening dialogue with our strategic partners, reducing trade barriers and a new european investment policy can we promote smart growth and safeguard, even in this time of crisis, the more than 36 million jobs that depend, directly or indirectly, on the eu's ability to trade with the rest of the world. finally, i would remind you that our task is also to protect eu production from the distortions of international trade caused by globalisation. i therefore hope that appropriate trade defence instruments will be put in place to respond effectively to the legitimate concerns of european smes.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i am in full support of the content of the report we have just voted on, because it is essential that a new trade strategy be put in place that looks to the future, especially at a critical time like the one we are living through. we live in a globalised world, in a global market, and the european union's strategy cannot ignore this assumption. free trade, protection for small and mediumsized enterprises, progress in dialogue with other countries such as china, russia, the usa and japan, and the key role of the wto in international trade must be the cornerstones of a constantly evolving strategy that adapts to change, but at the same time is able to manage it and not just be a spectator.
in writing. − the commission's communication on 'trade, growth and world affairs' comes at a time when the eu has acquired new competences as a result of the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. the document, however, does not present a forward-looking trade and investment strategy, but rather an introduction to the policy to be pursued in the coming months rather than a far-reaching trade strategy for the european union in the face of a rapidly changing world economy and a major rebalancing of economic balances. the text adopted today calls on the commission to analyse and prepare forecasts which take account of the current realities of the world economy and the present situation in the european union, as well as likely future changes. this analysis should form the basis for the elaboration of a long-term strategy adapted to the needs of the european union and its citizens.
in writing. - this report contains several references and several objectives which the european commission should have achieved but did not. it also contains very interesting analytical data on european and world trade, showing that the emerging countries' shares of world exports have increased in a few years. the eu's share of the eu's gdp fell from 37% in 1999 to 29% in just ten years. the vote will be against it because, instead of providing for rules to protect the interests of our companies and thus of europe, it contains repeated references to liberalisation as a system to generate productivity, without taking account of the enormous imbalances that exist and limiting to the minimum the references to the social and economic dumping carried out by asian countries. the text includes unacceptable praise for the current policy of the european commission, which is proliferating free trade agreements with countries whose products will create incalculable damage to our companies.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, unfortunately our delegation was not able to vote in favour of this report. the liberalization of trade with third countries, in addition to diminishing europe's role in the international economic context, favours the growth of the latter, without protecting in particular the interests of our own and those of other member states which still believe in the defence of a local production system and not, instead, in unregulated relocation. i also believe that this report, which is part of a subject which deeply divides europe, requires further political analysis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr caspary's text, which represents the european parliament's assessment of the new eu trade policy strategy presented by the european commission in november 2010. the rapporteur, in addition to calling for the commission to take action on international trade in a more long-term manner, stresses the need to integrate trade policy more closely with other eu policies, first and foremost industrial policy: the competitiveness of european industry and the economy are at the core of the trade strategy for the period up to 2020, with actions that should aim at strengthening trade with the eu's major trading partners; to curb the proliferation of tariffs or other forms of customs barriers; ensuring access to raw materials (including through greater opening to third country markets); to avoid unfair practices that are counterproductive to the interests of european businesses.

president of the eurogroup. - mr president, i am very concerned about what is happening in greece, because i often find, when reading my letter, that many greek citizens do not understand what we are doing and that many of your fellow citizens feel that the european union, the eurogroup, are punishing the greek citizens. i would like our greek friends to understand that the consolidation of greek public finances is essential. i want your fellow citizens to understand that you cannot fight debt with debt. i would like the greeks to understand that they cannot go on like this and that we too should understand that we have a duty towards greece, apart from the historical duty of gratitude, a duty of actuality which requires us to be in solidarity with the hellenic republic, provided that the greek authorities agree to bear the burden that weighs on them. as far as economic governance is concerned, i repeat that we must agree on the content. i would like the euro area or the european union as such to adopt within a few months a programme of economic governance which will see the various dimensions of economic governance and governance being put in place step by step. when we prepared for the introduction of the single currency, and in the framework of the maastricht treaty, we proceeded in stages. we had three stages to introduce the euro because we were investing in a field that we did not know. economic governance is another area where we do not know all the ins and outs, and so i would like us to draw up a step-by-step programme which is understandable to the citizens, which is designed in such a way that governments, national parliaments, community bodies, including the european parliament and our public opinion understand the pace at which we are moving.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the whole package of six measures and therefore understand this because it is a fundamental step towards real european governance. we do this to take responsibility and to control budgets even where national governments, the governments of the member states, have failed. and this is the moment when the credibility of our institutions, of the european institutions, is at stake. europe has a duty to respond to the demands of its citizens, to ensure that stability, that government, to create the conditions for growth without which there would be no future for our citizens and especially for the new generations.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too have given my support to this and to the other dossiers forming the six-pack because i am convinced that in a time of extraordinary crisis the response of the european parliament as a whole and of the european institutions must be strong, decisive and above all ready both on the issues of economic governance and on the issues of strong cohesion within the european institutions and on a prior review of the policies for the coordination of the budgets of the member states. that is where action is needed, we are waiting for all the member states to put in place the concrete measures that have been called for in this regard for an extraordinary plan that can boost competition, real employment, with an eye to the poor and the marginalized and social inclusion. these are the issues we will have to focus on in the coming months.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are living through a decisive moment for the future of the euro and, with it, for the whole of european construction. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we all want the accounts of the various states to be in order, we all want to reduce the debt. however, it is clear that without a smart investment policy that can give the economy a boost, there will be no chance of growth. the only clear result of this approach is that the heaviest costs will, as always, be borne by the weaker classes. that is why we, together with the socialist and democratic group, voted against this report. in fact, it is moving in one direction, namely rigidity without growth, a direction which has so far proved to be wrong.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we too voted in favour of the six-pack. i strongly believe in a path that promotes stronger common economic governance. we are now at a decisive juncture, and it is therefore a juncture fraught with difficulties, which cannot but make us aware of the many opportunities that europe has lost. i would remind you that on 16 june the president of the european council, mr van rompuy, came here to stress the need to talk about a euro-country rather than a euro-zone. in june the problems seemed to be more about vocabulary and terminology than substance. i would also like to recall that president barroso - whom i greatly appreciated today for the determination and persistence with which he conducted his report - assured us in 2008 that there was no rational reason to fear a recession. we are living in a time when a new european and europeanist pride is leading, also through the acts adopted by this parliament, to a great sense of responsibility. and stronger economic governance is also a policy that takes responsibility for driving growth and development by not delegating economic scenarios to market speculation.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the current crisis has shown that the stability and growth pact is not working as it should. six member states, three of which are in the euro area, are facing budgetary problems and are at risk of defaulting on their debt. this is a situation that must be brought to an end urgently. it is important, however, that this be done in a sustainable and forward-looking way. that is why i voted in favour of mr goulard's report, which i share in its sanctioning approach, particularly in cases of manipulation of financial data, fraudulent statistics or misleading information by a member state. at the same time, however, future efforts will have to be directed towards the heart of the problem, namely the inadequacy of the european union's economic integration. the sanctions will have a substantial deterrent effect if the link between the various economic policies is not strengthened by increased surveillance missions by the commission and, in the medium term, by means of eurobonds.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, by approving the six-pack, the european parliament has finally given the green light to a concrete strategy to combat the crisis. the keywords are stability, rigor, budget transparency and debt reduction. but as juncker said yesterday and barroso said today, we must also invest in development and employment and think about young people who expect a lot from us. and today barroso has presented us with the next steps of a truly bold strategy. among the important points is the presentation of a series of proposals on eurobonds and above all a tax on financial transactions, a revenue of eur 56 billion a year because it is right that the banks, perhaps above all the banks, bear the costs of the crisis and not just companies and citizens.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to congratulate mrs sylvie goulard on having tackled and completed a dossier of this difficulty, which is also a fundamental step towards european governance. and this is something that parliament is doing in a concrete way by carrying forward the statements that we have heard in this house today, but which are often not put into practice. this is the concrete invitation, i repeat, that we are also making to president barroso. because when you make a statement of principle, everyone agrees. when the commission's programme was voted on here, we agreed with it, but it is a question of putting it into practice. this measure is an implementation towards that programme.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the experience of recent years has shown that we need a strengthened framework for economic governance, as well as a broader and stronger framework for surveillance, making it credible and effective, and introducing sanctions which will only be effective deterrents if they are effectively applied. finally, i believe that europe cannot respond to the economic and financial emergency solely through austerity plans. it is important to settle accounts, but this is not enough. more and better can be done, especially in terms of equity, development and employment, and it is for these reasons that i felt i had to abstain on the haglund report.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report has shown us what new and important powers the treaty of lisbon has given the european parliament. the commission's proposals for better economic governance are of decisive importance for our economic growth and specifically for the growth of the euro area. the improvements made by the european parliament in creating a sound and coherent regulatory framework are obvious. i share the general approach of this report and have therefore voted in favour of it. we have new responsibilities ahead of us, the package of measures must be further improved and strengthened. i think we need to pay more attention to preventing unsustainable fiscal and macroeconomic policies, but above all give parliament a relevant role in the monitoring process by providing for regular and systematic debates and public hearings in parliament itself.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate mr haglund here, too, on the work he has done, and i voted in favour of him, as i did for the whole package. the report defines sanctions for macroeconomic imbalances, but it must be said that these are sanctions which should be imposed only and exclusively if the member state shows that it is not willing to adopt the necessary corrective policies, because if the financial situation does not improve there cannot be, mr de angelis, any chance of development, or there would be a chance of growth which would be small and would lead to nothing. for this reason i believe that the package which has been approved today will be the basis for achieving the growth which all the member states must objectively aim for. if we stop here we will certainly not have achieved the objectives we set ourselves, but with this step we can certainly achieve that other objective.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i voted for the ferreira report, as i voted for the whole package. i would like to take this opportunity to thank mrs ferreira, the rapporteur, for her cooperation throughout the year and to congratulate her on the result of the vote. i am convinced that the ferreira report and the macroeconomic surveillance that goes with it represent a real innovation. in the area of the stability and growth pact, we have done nothing but to reinforce what was already there. we have not introduced any new criteria, and if there is a part of this house which says that we will do this to stifle growth, then i have to ask the reverse: have those who have not complied with the stability and growth pact in recent years experienced growth? and did those who observed it least have the greatest growth? i think that the analysis of the results in the member states these days shows that the opposite is true. but what is in the ferreira report is a real innovation. it should help us in the future to recognize early on -- and i think this is fundamental -- that in some countries something is wrong. if we had known this early on, we would have been spared greece, ireland, portugal, spain and perhaps italy, and we might have seen years ago that something is not going the way we think it is. i would just like to see the commission use this instrument effectively, and achieve its objective, which is to work for the good of the union and the people who live in it.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is important that the stability and growth pact, the comprehensive framework for economic governance, supports and is compatible with the union's strategies for growth and employment, with the aim of increasing competitiveness and social stability. it is therefore necessary to provide for penalties to punish fraud, to pay fines into a central fund for the permanent crisis mechanism and to regulate financial markets more closely. finally, i believe that the austerity measures under discussion today risk undermining social equity policies. this is not the case with the ferreira report, which i voted for and which introduces considerable elements of social balance. it is the rest of the package that is wrong because it is all about austerity and austerity and it does not promote growth. europe will have a future only if we can combine strict accounting with the objectives of development, growth and employment.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the world crisis has led to instability and the inability of small and micro-enterprises to survive, which are a feature of much of the european business fabric. the measures adopted today with the adoption of the six-pack will help to prevent macroeconomic imbalances, but small and micro enterprises must be given immediate support. that is why, with colleagues from various political groups, we have tabled a motion for a resolution calling on europe to introduce a measure providing for a tax exemption for micro-enterprises for three years of up to eur 30 000 in annual profits and a bonus corresponding to the social security contribution for micro-enterprises that employ a young person on a permanent basis. we shall thus be able to prevent the exit from the market of many of the factors which guarantee employment and development and we shall be able to reduce unemployment, which has reached excessive levels to the detriment of social stability. we also remind the council of the need to initiate the trilogue with parliament on the regulation on designations of origin.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the regulation we have voted on to prevent macroeconomic imbalances between the 27 countries is certainly an innovation compared with the previous situation. it lays down rules and controls and, in particular, introduces the concept of symmetry whereby the commission must assess not only deficits but also surpluses. in practice, contrary to what is usually assumed, that there are some bad countries, such as greece or italy, countries like germany and the netherlands are being put under control because they have too little domestic consumption. the regulation also incorporates a federalist perspective and thus insists on the concept of equity, which in our view represents one of the positive elements of the future of europe and the member states. equity and solidarity will be the preconditions for european growth.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have greatly appreciated the work that mr ferreira has done with this report. in fact, on the package of six legislative proposals on economic governance, my group and i voted in favour of only this one. we have done so because, among other things, a clause has been inserted to protect social rights from the point of view of collective bargaining and there is also a strengthening of parliament's role in the adoption of delegated acts. so while it cannot change the overall balance of the six-pack, this report certainly does make a step forward in having, among other things, a monitoring system which takes account of fundamental rights. and so, in this context, while we are convinced that a vision based on a policy of austerity alone does not produce positive results, this report is certainly a positive note in the face of this trend.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we also voted in favour of the goulard report because it introduces mechanisms to prevent macroeconomic imbalances, finally made up of rules and guarantees, rules and guarantees which have been lacking until now and whose lack has been felt so much during this phase of the crisis. there is a new phase of accountability, control and also surveillance of budgets in the euro area, with mechanisms that are semi-automatic - and this is one of the major criticisms that have been put forward - but with sanctions that are finally imposed on any macroeconomic imbalances that may occur. it is a decisive step which, if i may use an analogy, will be completed by the following steps which, by a coincidence which is also fortuitous but important, president barroso has announced today: the introduction of the tobin tax, the taxation of financial transactions, means that the moments of crisis and difficulty are not paid for by households alone, that the prevention of crises is not always and only paid for by the producers of material goods, but also by those who operate in the financial market.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the feio report revises the stability and growth pact and thus finally establishes - i would like to remind you of this now that we have reached the conclusion after one year since the proposal was tabled - a control which imposes a 5% reduction on those states whose debt-to-gdp ratio is above 60%. it does this by introducing and clarifying the debt criterion and the procedures with respect to the pace to be followed. in this overall economic context, the commission will have to take account of a number of characteristics before it assesses and makes its recommendations to the member state. it introduces the basic principle that by reducing debt, there is less interest to pay and therefore the possibility of having more spending power in terms of investment and growth, which is the real objective we have to focus on in the coming months.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the regular availability of up-to-date and reliable budgetary data is the key to regulating public expenditure and enabling rapid corrective action in times of crisis. i therefore share the need to allow the commission to monitor, with the help of a tax authority, the compliance of the budgetary rules of the individual member states. in this context, i would like to stress that, under the treaty, the establishment of a medium-term financial framework does not affect the right of newly elected governments to amend the programme choices previously adopted. it is therefore necessary that this directive be applied faithfully and that the commission constantly monitor its application. in order to avoid that the intervention has a practical effect which is not cosmetic but useful in achieving the main objective of the directive: uniform respect for budgetary discipline as required by the treaty.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, more than a year ago, when the first problems of the greek economy and then of other countries began to emerge, i was interviewed by the european channel. and one of the things that i raised was actually the attention on statistics that has allowed some countries to rig the accounts. the ford report which we voted for and supported today introduces criteria for the transparency and independence of the national statistical institutes, with penalties for those who commit fraud and forgery. it is a fundamental report, as it aims to avoid a lack of transparency in the processing of statistical data and to make them uniform. this will enable the european government and the governments of all countries to proceed in a uniform manner, and thus to have uniform criteria not only of knowledge but also of action.

in writing. − the recent financial crisis has highlighted the need to review and strengthen the existing instruments for the multilateral coordination and surveillance of the economic policies of the various member states. that is the ambitious aim of the economic governance package voted on here today. the stability and growth pact is based on the objective of sound public finances as a means of strengthening the conditions for price stability, strong and sustainable growth and employment. we can therefore benefit from stricter forms of supervision which ensure that member states act in a consistent manner and in line with the union's financial coordination framework. this new strategy must focus on developing and strengthening the single market, promoting international trade relations and competitiveness, and preventing and correcting excessive budgetary imbalances. the council and the commission must make their positions and decisions public at the appropriate stages of the coordination procedures. we also believe that it is of the utmost importance that the strengthening of economic governance goes hand in hand with the strengthening of the democratic legitimacy of european governance. in this respect, the role of the european parliament must be strengthened throughout the monitoring process.
in writing. - having carefully analysed the legal basis used and the objections raised by the commission, i think it appropriate to vote in favour of the report by mrs wortmann-kool on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1466/97 on the strengthening of the surveillance of budgetary positions and the surveillance and coordination of economic policies. it is clear that the stability pact needs to be reformed on the basis of the experience of the last few years. i agree in particular that in the event of a serious recession, not only economic but also social, a temporary deviation from the budgetary policy as defined by the regulation should be allowed.
in writing. - i have decided to abstain on this and the other reports on the implementation of the new european economic governance. these measures may be useful, but they are late and they show the failure of the community's economic policy since the introduction of the euro. the maastricht treaty and the subsequent stability and growth pact already provided for certain criteria to prevent dangerous situations, and we have seen how they have failed miserably: greece in 1999 did not meet any criteria and only two years later was already in the euro; in addition, portugal, another country in enormous difficulties today, was the first to receive warnings in 2002 about its deficit situation. all these rules in the past were useless: we shall now see whether these new initiatives will be of any use in at least trying to save the salvageable.
in writing. - the monitoring of the budgetary policies of the member states is strengthened and the power of scrutiny and initiative is transferred from the council to the commission, two of the most important points in the wortmann kool report which i fully share. it is important that the commission assesses the annual stability programmes of the member states, provides an opinion and can issue a formal warning indicating the steps to be taken by the member state at risk of default. i also agree with the compromise solution on the failure to take measures to put an end to the violation of the rules of the preventive part of the psc which takes place through a 'two-stage voting procedure'. i also support the possibility for the european parliament to call a state which is the subject of recommendations by the council to report to the econ committee of the parliament. i take this opportunity to compliment the rapporteur.

in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report under discussion today is of particular importance because it concerns the adoption of the package of legislative proposals on economic governance aimed at defining a solid framework for the coming decades, ensuring compatibility between fiscal discipline and economic growth in the european union. the comprehensive economic governance framework should support and be compatible with the eu's strategies for growth and jobs and with the objective of increasing the competitiveness of member states and social stability in all regions of the union. the experience gained during the first decade of the functioning of economic and monetary union highlights the need for an improved economic governance framework which, in my view, should be based on two main elements: a stronger national ownership of commonly agreed rules and policies and a stronger system of european surveillance of national economic policies. i also welcome the provision for sanctions to punish fraud or failure to act on agreed recommendations without any reasonable justification. finally, i believe that improving the framework for economic governance cannot be achieved without greater regulation and supervision of financial markets.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to help clear up a misunderstanding. the principle of subsidiarity not only defends the prerogatives of the states, but also makes it clear that if a state is not able to provide, the higher level intervenes in subsidiary terms. the possibility of the european commission intervening is therefore well founded, as the polish presidency has understood, as has the european commission. we must therefore do nothing but mobilize our efforts to meet the needs of 18 million people, who are obviously not being met by the government of some countries. we must do this and we must also be careful in doing so, that is, do we want to move on to the social chapter? that's great. but beware, we would lose the virtue of the agricultural chain, which has been able to manage the surplus mechanism well and we would perhaps also lose the possibility of clarifying when social matters should be a matter for national or community competence.
the resolution on the rio+20 summit puts the spotlight on the crucial principle of equity. equity on an international global scale which ensures the right of developing countries to their development; intergenerational equity that does not make those who come after us pay the price of our decisions; this is a fairness that becomes a genuine solidarity and a vehicle for new sustainable development. we must reject the old conception of three independent pillars - economic, social and environmental - and instead recognise the interdependent nature of these elements because they are indivisible. setting the conditions for truly sustainable development requires not only that we develop new standards, such as the project beyond gross domestic product, but also that we ensure the active involvement of all parties at all levels of governance. it is by focusing on the indivisibility of equity, solidarity and global governance that we can shake off the screen of false freedoms and return to models of society centered on the person and the common good. rio+20 is therefore a call for high ethics, and in this context the proposals put forward by the european parliament are of value, both from the financial and from the purely technological point of view: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union's external relations. the assessment of the impact that biofuel production may have on food supply and biodiversity, with a focus on the overall assessment of the technological impact on the environment and societies. our proposals are intended to prepare the ground for an international conference which will really mark a political turning point in the planning of the development of the planet.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the un conference on sustainable development is the continuation of previous world summits and also takes up the contents of the un millennium summit held in 2000 and, in this case, the millennium development goals. i believe that the sustainable economy represents an opportunity for european businesses to grow, provided they set themselves realistic and achievable targets, avoiding unjustified increases in production costs that would expose them to competition from countries not subject to the same constraints. it is essential that the european union can put in place an effective international strategy to ensure that european environmental legislation, which is currently among the strictest in the world, is also adopted by third countries through comparable and binding commitments. this is a priority objective in order to ensure that european companies have a level playing field which enables them to remain in the market and to be globally competitive. to this end, we believe that the main lever on which a stronger strategic approach should be insisted is the strengthening of international partnerships for the promotion and diffusion of sustainable and low-impact technologies in emerging and developing countries. it is essential that, if a comprehensive agreement is not reached, europe cannot and must not engage unilaterally, or else the business system will fail. a weapon of pressure against third countries which do not want to commit themselves to an environmentally friendly future is the imposition of customs duties at the frontiers, proportionate to the assessment of the economic advantage they derive from their failure to commit themselves.

author of the book. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, finland and the netherlands opposed the council for a very simple reason: bulgaria and romania are currently unable to ensure effective border controls and are the scene of rampant corruption involving the political class and organised crime. this is not the view of populist parties and movements, but of europol in its 2010 report on organised crime. there is no populist propaganda, but a serious security problem. if bulgaria were to join the schengen area at this time, the police and security agencies predict that bulgarian borders, especially those on the sea, would become easy targets for turkish and eastern european crime, and bulgaria and romania would become the crossroads of human and drug trafficking. it is natural that some member states have many reservations about the real ability of bulgaria and romania to ensure effective border controls against organised crime and corruption, and it is therefore quite natural that they have opposed their entry into schengen. allowing this now means opening the way to transnational crime and opening a door on europe's borders, precisely where there is a very strong migratory pressure from turkey. the reasons for opposing this are many and europe cannot ignore them. i therefore ask what the commission and the council intend to do about this sensitive matter, which in my view has been dealt with sufficiently so far and without taking into account the dangers that the accession of bulgaria and romania would entail, according to the competent bodies, in terms of international security and crime. in my view, the commission and the council should postpone the accession of these two countries to schengen and give the go-ahead only when there is reasonable assurance that the accession of bulgaria and romania will not have repercussions on the security of european citizens.
in writing. the opposition to the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen airspace is due to one of the main aims of european policy: the precautionary principle. it is more than foreseeable that some member states, already receiving large immigration flows, will be put under even greater strain by the entry into the schengen area of two countries which do not seem to have achieved a sufficient level of control of the external borders. this is particularly true of the border between bulgaria and turkey. the free movement of citizens can only be allowed if it is certain that this does not determine: increase in micro-crime and illegal immigration, decrease in security and risks to public order. the figures on the fight against organised crime in these two countries are certainly not comforting for those who are concerned about a serious and effective european policy against the mafias.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, first i would like to thank the honourable members for their replies to my introductory remarks. also, i have to thank the european parliament for a very constructive approach towards this mechanism and also towards the cooperation between the commission and the national parliaments. i am deeply convinced that the good work of the subsidiarity control mechanism and its efficient application is in the interests of all of us. this is not about blocking european integration but about making it more transparent to the citizens and also more democratic, because the issues are, in this manner, being brought closer to the hearts of citizens and to their concerns. i also very much welcome the positive tone and constructive approach of the speakers and the roles of the national parliaments in this debate, because their role is also essential when it comes to the building of an inclusive europe that resonates in the capitals of our member states and is closely linked to the concerns of the citizens. the commission is fostering an active political dialogue with the national parliaments. this has been very fruitful, as has been demonstrated by the numbers of opinions and reasoned opinions. we would, of course, very much encourage this tendency to continue in the future. on the question relating to the committee of regions, of course we cooperate with the committee of regions very closely. the committee can play an active role in the mechanism and, most importantly, ensures that there is a voice for local and regional authorities at european level. more specifically, the committee of the regions’ subsidiarity monitoring network provides a very good access point for regional and local authorities, and can enable the commission, in some situations, to reinforce the analysis of regional aspects in its impact assessments. it can also help the commission to strengthen the analysis of subsidiarity and proportionality in the future. in conformity with the protocol on cooperation between the commission and the committee of regions, the commission regularly provides the committee of the regions with comments on its opinions. as regards the subsidiarity control mechanism and regional bodies, we have to respect the treaty. the treaty is very clear in this respect, because it states that it is for each national parliament or each chamber of a national parliament to consult its appropriate regional parliaments with legislative powers. we have to respect the treaty in that respect. the first and last questions were on how the mechanism works in practice. i have to say that the national parliaments have been quite efficient and effective in their responses to the legislative proposals from the commission. it does not look as if they have a particular problem with respecting the eight-week deadline, and we are absolutely punctual when it comes to the legislative deadlines. at the same time as the legislative proposal is sent to the european parliament and to the council, it is also sent to the national parliaments. we have seen that within eight weeks the national parliaments are ready and able to send us their opinions. what we are trying to do now in the commission is to be more efficient in terms of responses. the commission has installed a new it system which is making it easier to record all the responses, and it is trying to improve the quality of its responses to the national parliaments and to work in more detail on the opinions we receive from the national parliaments. as has already been said, two years after the lisbon treaty entered into force, the subsidiarity monitoring mechanism is working very well. i am sure that it will be a very important tool for involving the national parliaments more closely in the process of european cooperation.
the agenda includes the report by mr david casa, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the future of vat (2001/2082 (ini)) (a7-0318/2011).
member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank the european parliament, and in particular mr casa, for his positive and constructive report on the green paper on the future of vat. when this commission began its mandate, we felt that the time had come to have a fresh look at the european vat system, which has now been in place for over 40 years. it is indeed high time to develop a new and modern vat system – fully compatible with the single market and with newly emerging business models – which should continue to ensure and even improve its role as a revenue raiser in the long term. the green paper on the future of vat presented in december 2010 constituted the first step in this process. the overwhelming reactions from stakeholders confirmed that there was a need for such a debate. more than 1 700 written contributions were submitted. they generally confirm that the current vat system is too complex and burdensome, primarily because of the existing divergences across the eu. this is quoted as a major obstacle to maximising the benefits of our internal market, in particular for smaller businesses. one conclusion that can already be drawn is that our initiative has created considerable expectations. indeed fundamental changes to all major aspects of the vat system are advocated by business stakeholders as well as the general public. the next step in this process of reforming vat will be a communication to be presented before the end of 2011, identifying a comprehensive strategy for a stable and long-term vat regime. clearly, it will not be possible to tackle all aspects of vat at once. the communication will set out the ultimate objectives to pursue and make a distinction between those areas in which progress can be made in the short term and those areas which will still require more substantial work and in which results can only be expected in the longer term.in the forthcoming debate of the college on its work programme for 2012, i will propose new initiatives directly linked with one of our main priorities, namely consolidation and sustainable growth. in this framework, concrete proposals will follow the new vat strategy. they will cover issues such as a rapid reaction mechanism, vat governance with the business community and a reduction in the administrative burden for businesses. the opinion of parliament expressed in this report often reflects the view of the stakeholders. it is also ambitious. for the commission, this is positive and encouraging. i can already assure this house that its opinion will be given full consideration.
