in writing. − insurance guarantee schemes (igs) are a useful tool for reducing the risks faced by policyholders in the event of the insolvency of an insurance company. in my view, the next few years will see an expansion of crossborder activities and, as consumers will increasingly find themselves buying insurance services from companies in markets without or with divergent sgi, the question of the uniformity of consumer protection will inevitably arise. the european parliament has repeatedly expressed its support for the assessment of the desirability of a european approach in this area, which i fully share, especially in view of the wide variety of systems currently in existence in the various member states of the union. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that, in view of the serious implications of the insolvency of a national insurance undertaking on the general level of market confidence, the supervisory authorities of the member states should subject them to specific european-wide stress tests in order to verify the real capacity to cope with the insolvency of one or more insurers and to make recommendations on any shortcomings found in the models applied by insurance undertakings.
in writing. the econ report supports the introduction of a homogeneous system of insurance guarantee schemes within a legally binding framework. the introduction of this system is particularly necessary at the present time, when banking and insurance finance are in crisis and the detrimental effects of the crisis are also felt by the final consumers, who in the event of the failure of insurance companies are now without uniform protection at community level. the measure would help to restore consumer confidence in the insurance financial environment and would also close some regulatory loopholes in consumer protection. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on insurance guarantee schemes, the so-called igs, which are fundamental instruments for consumer protection, for reducing the risks for policyholders in the event of the insolvency of an insurance company. however, this is a very complex area both in terms of the wide variety of insurance systems in the member states and the implications of the future application of the solvency ii directive. this directive introduces a range of supervisory measures to be implemented before the insurance company is declared bankrupt. in this respect, i support the rapporteur's position that there are four main and strategic areas of consumer protection, irrespective of the country of origin, in the event of bankruptcy, fraud or the use of unorthodox sales techniques, and of taxpayer protection in the event of the insolvency of an igs. these are sectors where a european dimension of the igs is needed, through a harmonization directive based on an equal level of consumer protection irrespective of the insurer's geographical location.
in writing. − developing an effective insurance guarantee schemes (isps) policy and implementing it in a methodologically correct manner is a delicate and complex task, especially in the absence of a mechanism to compensate for losses suffered by consumers in the insurance market. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the directive. the commission's proposal is a complex one because the generally accepted parameters are not necessarily good for all member states. the commission's work in this respect is therefore to be commended, because the rigorousness of the method has been matched by the necessary flexibility. providing for a subsidiary role for the national gaos to provide more guarantees for consumers is a sign of sensitivity and high professionalism. the directive on uniform crossborder standardisation for sga is very broad and consistent and puts the commission in the position of guaranteeing the consistency of the common insurance guarantee system. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i believe that particular attention should be paid to transparency in the exchange of information: in the event of insolvency by the insurer, having a single, cohesive contact point for all financial guarantees will ensure that the directive really benefits consumers.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr skinner's text because i believe that european legislation on igs is necessary but at the same time to be carefully considered and evaluated because of the possible recessive effects on the market. if it is true that, on the one hand, the protection of the customer who takes out a policy to cover the risk of the insurance company being insolvent must be our priority, it is also true that igs must ensure, in a period of economic crisis, a broad outlet to national and, above all, european markets. i believe that the text of this resolution is in that direction and seeks to combine these two aspects with a vision that does not prejudice the protection already guaranteed by some member states. consumer protection against the risks of insolvency of insurance companies must be ensured by measures which are both effective in preventing risks to customers and also allow insurance companies a margin of manoeuvre to operate in the free market.
in writing. − insurance guarantee schemes (igs) are considered a valuable tool for reducing the risks faced by policyholders in the event of an insurance company's insolvency. the european parliament has repeatedly expressed its support for the assessment of the desirability of a european approach. the problem is complex, not only in view of the wide variety of schemes currently in existence in the various eu member states, but also in view of the interactions between igss and the other issues currently under consideration at eu level, in particular the imminent introduction of the solvency ii directive. our objectives are: consumer protection in the event of the insolvency of an insurer; consumer protection irrespective of the country of origin of the insurer; consumer protection in the event of fraud or the use of unorthodox selling techniques (mis-selling); protection of the taxpayer in the event of the insolvency of an igs. we believe that these four strategic objectives can only be satisfactorily achieved through a minimum harmonisation directive which ensures a level of consumer protection irrespective of the geographical location of the insurer with which the policy is subscribed and limits the exposure of taxpayers to claims by policyholders on the markets.
in writing. - the consumer is almost always the most affected by the effects of the economic crisis. the insurance industry is a case in point. i therefore agree with mr skinner's report on the proposed surveillance measures.
in writing. - the insurance market, too, has shown the need for greater consumer protection and guarantees, particularly in the event of the bankruptcy of an insurance company, particularly in the light of the recent financial crisis. igs, or insurance guarantee schemes, are designed to provide protection against possible risks. this report proposes greater harmonisation of igs at european level, in order to cover the risks that may arise in the event of non-compliance by companies with cross-border activities. the adoption of the principle of the country of origin for applying surveillance measures is right, but a key role must also be played by eiopa, the european authority set up specifically to monitor the european insurance system. this report puts consumers at the very centre of its concerns, with numerous references to greater protection and guarantee for them: i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i am voting in favour of mr skinner's report, to which i have also contributed a number of amendments in the econ committee. i believe that, alongside what is already happening in this respect for banks and investment companies, it is also appropriate to set up insurance guarantee schemes at european level in the insurance sector. however, i believe that, given the specific nature of the sector, if the principle behind it can be the same, the measures must be adapted and calibrated to the sector in question. for example, 'rcauto' policies which already have a mandatory cover pool and are restricted to life insurance products should be excluded from the scope of application given the need for greater protection of these products as long-term and often pension products. i also believe that it is essential to link the creation of the insurance guarantee funds with the prudential framework provided for by solvency2, which has yet to be fully implemented. i hope that the commission will take these suggestions into account when it presents its legislative proposal in the future.
in writing. − insurance guarantee schemes are a valuable tool for reducing the risks faced by policyholders in the event of the insolvency of an insurance company. the european parliament has repeatedly expressed its support for the assessment of the desirability of a common approach and, in adopting today's proposal, it welcomes the proposals made by the commission in the white paper on guarantee schemes in the insurance sector. the lack of harmonised european consumer protection rules in favour of 'host country' rules offers benefits but leads to a duplication of costs for pan-european insurance companies, which are forced to participate in different national schemes. in order to ensure consumer confidence both in the insurance sector and in the single market for financial services, it is necessary to ensure a uniform level of consumer protection for all types of insurance products. in this document parliament stressed that the new european legislation should not lead to a reduction in the protection afforded to consumers. european citizens must be able to rely on the coverage of a guarantee system for all types of insurance products and on the ability of that system to guarantee 100% compensation within a given period of time, uniform in all member states.
in writing. − madam president, as also outlined in the 2010 green paper on the future of the vat, the time has come to critically examine this instrument in order to strengthen its coherence with the single market and its capacity to increase revenue by improving its economic efficiency, robustness and resistance to fraudulent attacks. a simpler and more harmonised vat system would also reduce the operational costs for taxpayers and tax administrations, avoid market distortions, particularly in the transport sector, and help achieve the objective of the better regulation agenda of reducing administrative burdens by 25%.
in writing. the report on the future of vat contains positive insights and suggestions which should be carefully considered and evaluated in order to reorganise the tax structure of the member states and the relationship between the market and national bureaucracies. i welcome, for example, the fact that, alongside the simplification and harmonization of vat, there is talk of simplifying and reducing the administrative and bureaucratic burden on businesses in relation to their tax obligations arising from vat. simplifying vat will help both businesses and governments to reduce red tape and administrative burdens. the proposal to create a vat exemption threshold for smes extended to the whole of the community, also with a view to reducing administrative burdens and costs, and the encouragement of the use of electronic means by national administrations to facilitate cross-border transactions and bureaucratic procedures arising from vat, were also positive. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr casa's report, which i consider to be balanced as a whole and because i share its basic values, namely simplification, transparency and harmonisation, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity. in the 17 years since its introduction, vat has undergone considerable changes by the member states, creating a disjointed and excessively burdensome system, but also becoming the largest tax revenue available to the states. however, the financial crisis, which affects the whole of the euro area, also requires a review of the taxation system, moving towards standard and neutral accounting. this would firstly create greater efficiency and simplification, and at the same time ensure the necessary reduction in the administrative burden on smes. the commission's proposal for a directive on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes is a good one.
in writing. the process initiated by the publication of the green paper on the future of vat can only be supported. the need for restructuring the system cannot allow for any further delay, since the mechanism introduced on a transitional basis has shown a number of limitations, in particular with regard to the risk of fraud. the commission's proposal is to make the new vat system, together with the taxation of financial transitions, an important resource of the european budget. in the meantime, the call to the commission is to act quickly and to pursue the road taken, encouraging the member states to prepare all the necessary preconditions to avoid duplication and overlapping and to allow greater bureaucratic fluidity and a reduction in administrative costs. in times of difficulty it is important to devote considerable energy to counteracting the dispersion of resources caused by evasion and fraud. the committee therefore welcomes the report by mr casa and hopes that the commission will take due account in its proposal of the call for the adoption of mechanisms to make checks on crossborder fraud less haphazard, making the best use of mechanisms already tested in individual states or using all the instrumental resources made available by technological development.
in writing. - i welcome the report by mr david casa which, together with the european commission's green paper, aims to stimulate debate with the interested parties, firstly on the current vat system, and secondly to find possible solutions to strengthen its coherence with the single market and its ability to increase revenue while also reducing compliance costs. i regret that the report does not contain a reference to the need to promote reduced and harmonised rates in the tourism sector and to the sensitive issue of the special vat scheme for travel agencies, a debate which has been stalled in the council since 2002.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr casa's text because i believe it is the most correct administrative and procedural approach to a subject of european interest from both an economic and a commercial point of view. the application models contained in the resolution deal in particular with specific issues also related to consumer protection and the risk of fraud. in particular, a new model for the collection of vat, using a specific bank account, allows for greater traceability and security to avoid illegal or fraudulent transactions in this area. i think that we need a more efficient and organized procedure for collecting vat, which will lead to the implementation of the system and a drastic reduction in bureaucratic procedures, on the one hand, and to greater security for consumers and the commercial sector in general, on the other.
in writing. - value added tax is an important source of revenue for the national budgets of the member states, although the regulations adopted at european level and implemented at member state level have many shortcomings which compromise their efficiency and compatibility with the requirements of a genuine single market. as regards the treatment of crossborder supplies, we share the assessment of the commission, of some member states and of many professionals and stakeholders that the country of origin principle, which the member states have committed themselves to respect, and which has been supported in the past by both the commission and us, is not feasible, mainly because of the lack of political support among the member states themselves. we therefore support the commission's initiative to recognise the status quo and to move to the principle of destination. a vat system based on the place of establishment of the purchaser, both for goods and services, seems to be a promising solution, but it needs to be accompanied by the introduction by member states of efficient one-stop shops to avoid the multiplication of vat registrations, the increase in compliance costs and the negative liquidity impact for internationally active companies.
in writing. - it is essential that the report on the future of vat be adopted. the objective of a common vat system must be achieved in the shortest possible time.
in writing. - i congratulate mr casa on his excellent work. the text that has been adopted is the european parliament's response to the commission's green paper on the future of vat, published in december 2010, and is a contribution to the preparation of the future european strategy on the future of vat, expected later this year. the main objective of this report is to strike a balance between maintaining vat revenue at the levels necessary to provide an important source of revenue, while ensuring that it does not stifle business activity. this could be achieved mainly by fighting fraud (which currently costs the eu €100 billion in lost revenue) and by reducing the glut of different exemptions and tariffs. in addition, the intelligent design of new vat regimes at european level would make life easier for honest entrepreneurs and help non-profit organisations in the supply of goods and services. in this context, i ask the commission and the member states to consider introducing a vat exemption threshold for smes at european level, in order to reduce red tape and costs and to facilitate access to the internal market.
in writing. - vat is an important source of revenue for the national budgets of the member states. its system, which is based on european legislation and is implemented at member state level, is, however, lacking in many aspects which undermine its efficiency and compatibility with the requirements of a genuine single market. the report adopted today supports the commission's intention to move to a 'broad-based' vat system. it is therefore necessary to solve, in addition to the problem of the deduction of input vat in relation to domestic production as a system as opposed to outsourcing, also the problem of the so-called hidden vat in supply chains. a vat system based on the place of establishment of the purchaser, both for goods and services, could be a solution.
in writing. - a review of the vat system, more than 40 years after its introduction, is essential, as the structure of trade in favour of increased crossborder transit has demonstrated the system's limitations and the great opportunities for fraud that can result from it. for my part, i hope that the legislative proposal will aim at further simplifying the system in order to reduce the administrative burden on businesses (largely due to vat formalities); the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the situation of the small and mediumsized enterprises in the community. the number of enterprises in the community is estimated at 4 335 448 (99.9%). the reinforcement of simplification measures is therefore essential through the use of harmonised vat return templates; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules. for intra-community transactions, the commission has stated that it is prepared to abandon the objective of taxation in the country of origin for a final taxation in the country of destination. such a mechanism would have the benefit of preventing certain types of fraud. but the proposal is not welcomed by small retailers, who see the system of vat fractional payments (one of the main benefits of the current system) being abolished, concentrating the financial risk on the traders who should pay the full vat to the retailer.

in writing. - madam president, considering that the european union is one of the world's leading arms producers and exporters, it is essential to create a unified system for the trade in firearms and their parts, components and ammunition. it is not simply a regulation designed to reduce the time taken to process applications for authorization, especially for civilian weapons, but the obvious need to draw up a traceability line, through export authorizations and import and transit measures, aimed at tackling the illegal trade in arms. i congratulate the rapporteur on the content of the text aimed at protecting the security of the union and the arms industry, and i hope that all those countries which have not yet signed or ratified the un firearms protocol will reflect on and adopt the measures contained in the protocol and decide to fight together against transnational organised crime and to strengthen cooperation between national authorities.

in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr iacolino's report, which has the merit of dealing with a sensitive and controversial subject such as the implementation of article 10 of the united nations protocol on firearms and the provision of export authorizations and import and transit measures for firearms, their parts and components and ammunition. article 10 of the protocol must be adopted by all the member states in order to give a concrete and unanimous response to the illegal trafficking in arms, which is undoubtedly one of the main reasons for opposing this resolution. on the other hand, we must not risk, in the more than positive intention of fighting crime, hindering or making difficult the legal trade in arms. in this sense, mr iacolino's text reflects the needs of a commercial sector which is important for the economy of the individual member states and also for the european union. i believe that the fact that we have managed to combine both aspects of a thorny issue has been a remarkable achievement in the approach to the implementation of article 10 of the protocol.
in writing. the stockholm programme considers the trafficking of arms as one of the threats to the internal security of the european union. the general objective of harmonising and simplifying procedures is of course complemented by the objective of effectively combating the illicit trafficking in firearms by promoting and strengthening cooperation between states, an objective which has been made even more relevant with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon on 1 december 2009. we believe that export authorization should be granted only after import authorization by the third country and a notification of 'no objection' by the transit country, thus introducing an innovative procedure tacit consent in the event that the transit country does not raise objections within a certain time. we consider it essential that certain simplified procedures be provided for certain types of exports and certain categories of users. the member states will then have to commit themselves to providing appropriate powers to the competent authorities and to define the sanctions for infringements of this regulation. we also stress the importance of the application in all member states of article 10 of the un protocol to harmonize procedures and finally create a common system for the trade in firearms.

in writing. - i congratulate mr iacolino on his excellent work. the agreement on the export of firearms for civilian use is the european parliament's response to the norwegian tragedy. the tragic events in norway confirm the need to create a clear regulatory framework for exports and imports of arms for civilian use in the eu, which is a sector of industrial excellence in europe and which also involves many sportsmen and enthusiasts. the text contains very important elements such as the correspondence for each export to a third country of an equal import measure so that we can combat arms trafficking more effectively. the text also makes it possible to reconcile the need for simplified and streamlined procedures for operators in the sector, hunters and sport shooters, with the security profiles and controls imposed by exports of firearms.

in writing. the arms sector is an industry in europe with a turnover of almost eur 694 million in exports and over eur 220 million in imports. i share the rapporteur's view on this because i believe that the adoption of the regulation would make it possible to apply article 10 of the un protocol in all member states, establishing a unified system for the trade in firearms, harmonising and simplifying procedures, to the benefit of european companies specialising in the field, and combating the illicit trafficking of arms. the right balance is also struck between security needs and bureaucratic simplification in favour of the companies.
in writing. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am voting in favour of the implementation of the un protocol on the trafficking of arms, which italy has already ratified. i would also like to congratulate the rapporteur on the completeness of the text, which, in addition to promoting greater controls on the illicit trade in arms, provides for the simplification of the trade in arms in favour of certain categories such as hunters and sport shooters.
in writing. − the european union, through regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, granted exceptional duty-free access to the european market for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. these measures provide for preferential access for the western balkan countries to the eu market with the main objective of giving a new impetus to their economies. in its november 2009 resolution, the european parliament called on the commission to make every effort to mitigate the effects of the economic crisis in the western balkans. at that meeting the european parliament expressed its support for measures to promote the economic development of these countries so that this in turn could lead to political stability. the end of trade preferences in december 2010 effectively deprived the beneficiaries of an objective economic advantage in trade with the eu. this could not only seriously undermine the economic recovery of the western balkans, and thus frustrate all efforts made so far, but could also have a negative impact on the internal reform and transition processes. therefore, i am more than in favour of extending the validity of the trade preferences regulation until december 2015.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. on the one hand, the provisions contained in it may appear controversial, since they are intended to promote a preferential regime for goods from the balkan countries. given our opposition to the rapprochement and accession of these states to the eu, the establishment of a preferential regime for balkan goods might seem problematic. however, the document in question acknowledges the possible damage that such an entry might cause to the eu market and therefore proposes to adopt defensive countermeasures to prevent our market from being damaged in any way, even contemplating the partial suspension of the preferential regime in the event that actual problems arise. since the document takes account of the needs of our market by placing them on a priority channel, i have chosen to vote in favour.
in writing. − by regulation (ec) no 2007/2000, subsequently codified, with numerous amendments, by regulation (ec) no 1215/2009, the european union granted exceptional and unlimited duty-free access to the community market for almost all products from the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. in particular, the aim was to boost the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market, implementing economic development and fostering political stability in the whole area. the trade preferences granted expired on 31 december 2010 and since then the beneficiaries have been deprived of an objective economic advantage useful to support the difficult transition and internal reform process that the entire balkan area is undertaking. i therefore voted in favour of this report because i think it is appropriate to extend the granting of trade preferences until at least 2015. this can avoid any negative economic impact caused by the economic crisis that could undermine the reform processes undertaken in these countries.
in writing. - i am in favour of amending regulation (ec) no 1215/2009. it is absolutely essential, in this time of crisis, to support the economies of the developing countries. by granting the western balkan countries (temporary) privileged access to the eu market, the effects of the economic crisis in the region can be mitigated and thus the processes of political stabilisation can be promoted and accelerated. by amending regulation (ec) no 1215/2009, the granting of trade preferences for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from such an advantage is extended until 2015. i would like to emphasize that the balkans are a region of high priority in our foreign policy. the geographical proximity, the interdependence in terms of security, migration flows and trade are all factors which help to define the importance of south-east europe for us. it is also essential to understand that these countries will have a major impact on the political and economic stability of the eu itself in the future. it is therefore imperative that the economic development of the balkan regions be facilitated by this proposal, which will allow the extension of trade preferences to them, and thus bring political stability to the whole region.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the weight and importance of small and mediumsized enterprises in the european economy is universally known and it is therefore right that they should be at the centre of the union's action. access to credit is often cited as one of the major problems for smes, and we have spoken extensively about this today. however, with the entry into force of the basel iii regulations, this could prove even more difficult and costly. basel iii, although well-intentioned, does impose higher capital requirements on banks, and this necessarily implies a tightening of credit provision and an increase in financing costs, which is likely to hit smes particularly hard. given that loans to smes are the least risky, could specific measures be taken to solve this problem? and most importantly: to be competitive, you have to innovate, but can you innovate without resources?
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that in these last two years, which have been so difficult for the european economy, our small and mediumsized enterprises, despite having felt the crisis, particularly in terms of employment, have coped very well and continue to be the backbone of the european economy. of the various data i've been able to read, one of them seems interesting to me: smes living and working in member states that are innovation leaders are recovering much faster than those living in countries considered to be modest innovators. this means that the path it has chosen to take europe through strategy 2020, together with the role it wants to give to innovation, is the right one. but we need to make sure that it delivers tangible results in much shorter time than was expected before 2009. we must also ensure that the member states respect their commitments, apply the directives and make life easier for our smes. the commissioner's speech, which highlighted important figures that we know are linked to the reality of smes in the european union, was interesting to me: the idea of giving micro-enterprises a breathing space. they'll be a revelation to everyone.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, if we could hear the voice of a small businessman in this house today, we would hear a story even more disturbing than the data we have been given, especially as regards the four structural problems facing this sector, which is a crucial sector that is part of europe's identity, namely: we have heard about the obstacles to simply paying vat in the various countries, innovation and access to the structural funds, which some of our countries do not use as they should, and access to credit. it is unacceptable, mr commissioner, that europe should recapitalize banks without imposing strict conditions on them to facilitate access to credit for a crucial sector of the european economy, such as small and mediumsized enterprises, which are not rewarded but blackmailed, if not strangled, by credit institutions.
in writing. small and medium-sized enterprises account for 99% of all european enterprises and employ more than 90 million people. these are the data from which to start a constructive discussion, especially in the light of the recent economic crisis, which has led to the loss of some 3.25 million jobs in the sector. it is also true that the structural weaknesses of our enterprises are deep-rooted: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. just to quote a fact: the average cost of opening a business in the us is only 694 euros, while the average in europe is 2,285, with a licensing time of 2 to 3 months. simplification is needed! on a daily basis, european companies have to deal with too much red tape and administrative burdens, and this does not help them in their daily challenges with china and other emerging economies. that is why i hope that, for a more competitive europe, more favourable conditions for entrepreneurship will be created, which will promote the growth of smes by helping them to overcome the problems that hinder their development and encourage an innovative and entrepreneurial mind-set among young people.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent days i have heard from many quarters that china is the possible saviour of the euro and of europe itself. reactions ranged from fatalistic to enthusiastic. however, i do want to ask you a simple question: why should china help europe? this aid would certainly not be an end in itself but it could be the last and final death blow from the asian country to the west. i am surprised and sorry, because this chinese strategy is well planned and planned out, while europe seems to me to have no idea or line of action. i'm from prato, the city with the highest concentration of chinese in italy. maybe they came to us to help, but now they control most of the city and the economy and society of prato have been slowly and deliberately destroyed.
the debate is closed.
the agenda includes the report by traian ungureanu, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on promoting the mobility of workers within the european union (2010/2273 ((ini)) (a7-0258/2011).
member of the commission. − madam president, let me start by thanking the rapporteur, mr traian ungureanu, for his report on promoting worker mobility within the european union. the commission shares this house’s opinion of the positive impact of geographical mobility on europe’s economies. over the last 40-plus years, geographical mobility and the fundamental principle of freedom of movement for workers have contributed to european integration and the building of the single market. in addition, geographical mobility contributes to both employment and economic growth. this is particularly relevant at a time when high levels of unemployment coexist with labour shortages across sectors and regions. citizens must be encouraged and better informed if they are to undertake a cross-border career move with confidence. it calls, inter alia, for better knowledge of the job market situation. people need to know where the jobs are. anticipating and matching labour market and skills needs are a top priority for the eu. that priority has been followed up by practical action and the development of new tools like the job vacancy monitor for example. these tools will also be helpful for the eures network of european employment services. eures provides high-quality information, advice and recruitment services for workers and employers. it is a powerful resource available to the eu for promoting geographical mobility. eures will be reformed next year to step up its matching and placement capacity and to develop mobility and employment in europe, as the commission announced in its communication ‘an agenda for new skills and jobs’. the commission will support targeted mobility schemes at eu level through eures. one such scheme is your first eures job. a preparatory version is currently under trial. despite the eu’s very extensive legislation in the area of free movement of workers, more effective channels of communication between mobile workers and state services are needed to give workers full access to information on their rights and obligations. to that end, i can inform you that, in response to your report, the commission is assessing the advisability of adding an enforcement dimension to existing eu rules on equal treatment of mobile workers and what the best options for that would be. the commission has also given fresh impetus to member state enforcement of the directive on freedom of movement for citizens (directive 2004/38/ec) in response to concerns voiced on the topic. this rigorous policy of enforcement has produced substantial results: the majority of the member states have amended their legislation – or announced their intention of amending it according to a clear calendar – to ensure full transposition of the free movement directive. the commission is also committed to continuous monitoring of the accession treaties’ provisions with respect to the member states which have opted temporarily to restrict free movement of workers. in response to a request from bulgaria and romania on 20 june under the 2005 act of accession, before the end of this year the commission will present a new report on the way in which the transitional arrangements on the free movement of workers from those countries have functioned. the report will analyse the post-enlargement migration flows, the main characteristics of the intra-eu mobile persons, and the economic and labour market impact. while any decisions to maintain restrictions on bulgarian and romanian workers in the third phase, from 1 january 2012, lie with the member states, they will have to be notified to the commission by the end of the year and be justified by serious labour market disturbances. the commission welcomes this own-initiative report and agrees with the house that reaffirming a fundamental treaty principle and promoting geographical mobility is vital. mobility is among the best ways of reducing skill mismatches and boosting our economies, particularly in the current context of high unemployment and very uneven economic growth. it therefore represents a key element of the europe 2020 strategy to which all member states have signed up.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 25 october 2011 at 12.30 p.m. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by małgorzata handzlik, on behalf of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, on the peer review process provided for in the services directive (2011/2085 (ini)) (a7-0324/2011).
member of the commission. − madam president, the report on the mutual evaluation process of the services directive provides new evidence of the main role played by the european parliament on this important issue, a central role both during the negotiation of the directive and the transposition period. this report is, for me, an essential contribution to the full implementation and the good quality of the services directive in all member states. i would like to thank the rapporteur, ms małgorzata handzlik, for the relevance of her analysis and the strong messages delivered by this report. i would also like to thank the shadow rapporteurs, especially ms evelyne gebhardt, who did impressive work in her report on the implementation of the services directive adopted in february, and of course throughout negotiations on the directive, as well as the chair, mr harbour. your report highlights the importance of fully implementing and operating all aspects of the services directive, whether they are legal or practical aspects. i welcome this. we do not only need an adaptation of the national legislation, we must also ensure that the one-stop shops are fully operational. the report points it out clearly. the report also introduces a strong signal with respect to the next steps in developing the internal market for services. the services directive has already brought a tangible success, but the internal market for services is not complete. there is still untapped potential. that is why we must move forward and your report contributes to this goal. i welcome your support for the actions proposed by the commission in its communication of january 2011 on the results of the mutual evaluation process. the results show that we must take more into account the needs and practical problems of users of the internal market, our citizens and our businesses. which tools should we use to achieve this goal? together with the member states the commission has launched a review of the consistency of eu rules on the ground. the community instruments often operate simultaneously and their implementation may lead to practical difficulties. thus an architect based in belgium who works for clients in the netherlands may be subject, depending on the situation, to the services directive, the directive on professional qualifications, the directive on electronic commerce and many other instruments. in cooperation with national administrators, we are currently conducting a performance test or consistency test on these rules. these tests are performed on the basis of case studies in three key sectors: construction, tourism and business services. i am determined to keep parliament and notably the committee on the internal market and consumer protection closely informed of progress in the coming months. on the basis of the outcome of the benchmark, the commission will propose concrete actions in 2012 in order to ensure a better functioning of the internal market. in addition, we will look closely at the specific barriers identified during the peer review. thus the requirements limiting the choice of legal form or requirements relating to the ownership of capital can be an impediment to the growth of service activities, domestically and cross-border. such restrictions often apply in sectors with high added value, which are an important source of growth and skilled jobs – lawyers, engineers, tax advisers, architects and so on and so forth. they can prevent the development of innovative business models without even being necessary for the protection of consumers or workers. the commission will assess the impact on the ground of these requirements and decide by 2012, if possible, whether specific initiatives should be launched. we will also carry out a study of the economic effects of the implementation of the services directive based on the result of the work achieved by the member states. your report shows the importance that parliament attaches to the achievements of such a study. i would like to present the results of the study to you personally early in 2012. finally, concerning the mutual evaluation of the working method, we know that it is an essential tool in the context of the services directive; the scope is very broad and involves profound changes in national legislation. this is without any doubt a tool of the future, but i agree with you that a case-by-case analysis is required before applying this methodology to other legislative tools. we must be pragmatic. i count on the continuous support of parliament to maintain the dynamics created by the implementation of the services directive.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 25 october 2011 at 12.30 p.m. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by diana wallis, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on alternative methods of dispute settlement in civil, commercial and family matters (a7-0343/2011).
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i very much appreciate the fact that in mrs wallis' report on alternative dispute settlement methods she calls for a general agenda for justice for growth across all sectors, going beyond consumer-producer disputes to include civil transactions and in particular family disputes. i believe that family mediation and a strong european position in this field are of great importance, given the growing number of conflicts in the european union, usually as a result of separation and divorce, and the corresponding increase in disputes between spouses, often of different nationalities, which then have a heavy impact on children. experience in many countries shows that the institution of the family mediator, as a neutral person to whom one can freely turn, helps partners to find mutually acceptable agreements in written agreements to be submitted to the court for approval. this objective must therefore be pursued with determination within the community, while respecting subsidiarity, also in the light of the 2005 european union regulation on parental responsibility, also to strengthen cross-border protection, with particular reference to child abduction and the role of the european parliament's mediator. i therefore hope that the commission will also take this into account in its legislative proposal in its address to the member states.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, the commission welcomes the support on alternative dispute resolution (adr) for consumers and businesses and we also welcome your suggestions concerning the commission’s legislative proposal on adr for consumer disputes. the krakow declaration, which the single market forum adopted earlier this month, repeated this call. adr is also one of the 12 proposals in the single market act. my colleague commissioner dalli will be putting forward two legislative proposals which are scheduled for adoption by the commission on 23 november: one for a framework directive on adr for business-to-consumer (b2c) disputes; and one for a regulation on online dispute resolution. the directive will ensure that consumers and traders can access adr schemes for any dispute between them, and the regulation will establish an eu platform for disputes related to cross-border online transactions between consumers and traders. these proposals will be the first bricks for the construction of an effective out-of-court redress system. the commission is also aware, as your report states, that we have to deal with business-to-business (b2b) dispute resolution, particularly for smes. during the commission consultation on b2c disputes, stakeholders were very clear: they expressed a preference for a different type of instrument to apply to b2b disputes, catering for them more specifically. therefore the commission is at present examining different types of adr, including arbitration work, in particular in the cross-border context of b2b disputes. we are at a very early stage of information gathering and we will examine all possible problems which could hinder businesses, in particular smes. however, we would welcome all proposals on this while we are working on it. if the outcome of the work is positive, as i believe it will be, i will ultimately come forward with a proposal. concerning the mediation directive, it is a viable option of ‘first resort’, particularly – as has been mentioned – in family law cases where the parties cannot settle their conflict themselves and going to court may unnecessarily escalate their dispute. mediation may lead to fast and cheap results. the mediation directive has applied everywhere except in denmark since 21 may 2011. this directive can be applied to civil and commercial matters, including family matters and disputes between businesses and consumers. the only exclusion is where parties are not free to decide on their rights and obligations under the applicable law. the commission welcomes parliament’s support for the key provisions in the mediation directive, which should also apply to other adr schemes. independence, impartiality, confidentiality, the effects on prescription and the enforceability of agreements are to be regarded as common standards for all kinds of adr. specifically concerning the mediation directive, following the opening of pre-infringement proceedings in july 2011 against nine member states which were late in transposing the directive, today 20 member states have notified the commission of national measures for implementing it. i am continuing to follow carefully the situation in the other member states.

the agenda includes the report by barbara matera, on behalf of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, on the situation of single mothers (2011/2049(ini)) (a7-0317/2011).
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to begin by thanking the shadow rapporteurs and all the other rapporteurs who have contributed to the content of the report with new ideas to support this vulnerable group of women who, not by choice, are left to face the growth of their children and the need to pursue their own careers. this category of women at high risk of poverty needs the support of the european institutions through concrete forms of support. i am honoured to have been entrusted with the responsibility of drawing up this report on the situation of single mothers in europe: this is the first own-initiative report by the european parliament to identify measures to support single-parent families. i organized a public hearing in the european parliament several months ago to invite experts from associations working in support of single mothers and to have a first exchange of views on the priority areas in which to act and support this category. in the last few months i have met with associations which have supported single mothers in several member states such as ireland, portugal, the united kingdom and belgium, and in brussels i had the opportunity to visit personally an association where single mothers live and during this visit i had the opportunity to exchange information and ideas with the head of the structure and to understand more closely the difficulties these women face on a daily basis. in addition, during my visit to warsaw with the femm delegation, i was able to learn more about the benefits and measures to support single mothers in poland. single mothers are an underrepresented demographic: geographically across europe there are different perceptions and policies towards single mothers. in the southern mediterranean countries, such as italy, portugal, spain and greece, it is generally accepted that the extended family will contribute to the upbringing of single-parent children on a voluntary and unpaid basis. in the north and in northern states such as france, sweden, germany, denmark, government welfare systems are in place to help single mothers with benefits and social assistance policies. in the member states of eastern europe, on the other hand, there is a mixture of policies, some linked to strong family values of the communist regimes, others characterized by a mixture of policies from the north and south of europe. at present, 5% of the female population in europe are single mothers. in some member states, such as estonia and latvia, this figure is as high as 9%. single mothers are often stigmatized as young and irresponsible, when in fact 85 percent of them are between the ages of 25 and 64. in addition, the negative effects of the financial and economic crisis that hit the european union have had a severe impact on this category of women. already burdened by the gender pay gap, these mothers are hampered by the need to take on debt and have to care for their children. the health status of single mothers is statistically more unstable than that of married women. these mothers are under more stress because they have to perform tasks that normally fall to both parents. often they cannot afford proper medical care and do not have time for rest. statistically, single mothers across europe are less educated than their married counterparts, and so their entry into the world of work is also difficult and hindered. the report is full of new initiatives and, above all, new objectives which the european union must set itself, because this is a subject which must be at the centre of the union's priorities, certainly considering that the number of these women is growing throughout europe.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the rapporteur for her complex, interesting and rich report. we know that in europe, as has been said, more than 5% of the female population are now single mothers, and i also remember that 85% of single parents are women. so there is a focus on the female side of the single parent situation which is now increasingly being taken up by welfare, employment and social security policies. of course, this is a population which, as the report says, is very diverse in age, legal status and economic status. for example, in northern europe, young single mothers with very high scores predominate, especially in some scandinavian countries and the united kingdom, while in the south, single mothers with children predominate after separation, divorce or widowhood. the conditions are therefore also very different and, while in northern europe some services and welfare systems are probably more advanced, partly because family networks are smaller, in the south we are faced with a new phenomenon that is emerging, including single mothers and young people, with a welfare system that has not yet been sufficiently targeted and thought out. so there are different response rates. i therefore believe that the first thing to be done is - as the report also states - to compare welfare systems and best practices, to see what kind of mix of services for employability, training and welfare can be created which prevents poverty and exclusion from the labour market and which allows a much more complex reconciliation for this type of women.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i wish to thank ms matera for her very useful and timely contribution, because the topic she has chosen is of the utmost importance. we must be aware that the structure of households in europe is constantly changing, and that single parents (some are fathers, but the vast majority are mothers) now account for a growing percentage of households with children, and their numbers are on the rise. recent oecd analyses indicate remarkable similarities in all the member states. by 2030 there will be between 22% and 29% more single parents than there are now, so what we are currently seeing is only the beginning of a very large-scale trend. this, of course, calls for action. the first action is in our europe 2020 strategy. we aim to reduce the number of people living at risk of poverty or social exclusion by 20 million. this is exactly the number of children at risk of poverty in the european union today, and the figure rises to over 30% for children living with single parents. this is why we want to make a recommendation to the european platform against poverty and social exclusion on combating child poverty in 2012. it will propose principles and indicators in key areas such as support for families and access to essential services including child care, housing and education. affordable childcare is very important for single mothers and single fathers, who have to be able to enter the labour market if they do not want to be trapped by poverty and social exclusion. we also need to know more about the phenomenon, which is why we are collecting data to identify trends and compare welfare provisions. such data are already partly available in the oecd family database (which is co-financed by the european commission), and the new family support calculator is a tool that allows users to compare the income situation of various types of families. the european alliance for families is a very important eu platform for sharing good practice on family policies and fostering cooperation and mutual learning in this field. there is also our european institute for gender equality, which analyses the data and develops methods and tools for gender mainstreaming and also facilitates mutual learning and the exchange of best practice. ms matera, you said that it is the first time that we have spoken in plenary on this subject; i am very sure it is not the last.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday, 25 october 2011, at 12.30 p.m. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by sonia alfano, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on organised crime in the european union (2010/2309 (ini)) (a7-0333/2011)
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am very pleased with the work done with the political groups, in particular with the shadow rapporteurs, mr iacolino for the ppe, mr crocetta for the s&d, mr albrecht for the greens, mr kirkhope for the ecr and mr de jong for the gue, who have made a decisive contribution to reaching an advanced and ambitious final text. organised crime and the mafia are one of the main threats to the security and freedoms of eu citizens. for the first time in european political history, an official document explicitly refers to the mafia and the need for specific, transnational forms of opposition. it is essential to focus on organised crime and the mafia because, as the europol reports show, we are witnessing organised criminal metastases, which are taking root in the member states and have heavily infiltrated the economy, finance, politics and public administrations. the european parliament, in this report, proposes a concrete policy of opposition, a serious coordinated intervention, a therapy finally adapted to the gravity of the situation; it's a therapy that comes from listening to and analyzing the people who are fighting organized crime on a daily basis. i would like to take this opportunity to thank the judges and police officers, the scholars and witnesses in the courts who contributed their valuable experience to the final solutions proposed and who, every day, in a spirit of service and self-sacrifice, represent the member states in an unequal fight against criminal organizations. criminal organizations are motivated by profit: the report also stresses the need to ensure that the european union is able to take action to combat organised crime. we therefore look with great interest to the proposal for a directive which the european commission will present in the coming months on a european corpus juris on the detection, freezing, seizure and confiscation of criminal assets. i am therefore very pleased to have commissioner reding here, to whom i express the clear political will of the european parliament: we call for european rules allowing for so-called extended confiscation and for preventive and effective measures such as confiscation without conviction. we are calling for rules to allow the seizure of assets held in trust and, above all, we are calling for rules on the use of confiscated assets for social purposes, to close the circle of this cultural operation and the full involvement of civil society, without which the mere fight against organised crime would be a futile effort. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to vote on the report. harmonisation of the rules on organised crime; rules for greater protection of victims; the extension of the crime of mafia association to all member states; improving coordination and cooperation between europol, eurojust and olaf, and with national authorities; improving judicial cooperation and fully implementing the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions; transparency and prevention rules to prevent public funds from ending up in the hands of organised crime; rules against financial crime and money laundering; the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of penalties for the use of the death penalty in the european union. we are convinced of one thing, commissioner: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we will use all the means at our disposal to ensure that we get down to business, in line with the existing treaties which, in full respect of the democratic nature of the european union, give the national and european parliamentary assemblies the fundamental role of guiding and evaluating policies on freedom, security and justice in the interests of citizens. we therefore expect the commission to take note of the importance and political significance of the european parliament's position right away. one last thing, though perhaps the most important: i would like to dedicate this work, this first step which the european parliament is about to take, to all the innocent victims of organised crime and the mafia. their memory, the memory of those who paid with their lives for their choice not to give in to the stench of moral compromise, must be our guide and require us to send strong and unmistakable signals, such as the one i hope we will send to the citizens of europe tomorrow.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, madam commissioner, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs alfano, on having given a strong impetus to an important measure which, as you said earlier, clearly shows a consistent contribution from all the other political groups: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union. with this measure, and especially with the proposals which the commission will certainly want to put forward, there will no longer be the present barriers at the frontiers of the member states to attack the assets of the mafia and, above all, to give concrete enforceability to the orders issued by the judicial authorities of the member states. hard prison, severe prison for those who have been stained by such abnormal crimes; remote hearings of witnesses and judicial assistants; confiscation for social purposes; judicial cooperation based on trust; the report makes possible a new kind of legislation, one which is increasingly being developed to protect honest citizens, to protect honest businessmen and to respond to the pride of those who have not bowed to the mafia and have had to pay, in some circumstances by dying, for this pride and this pride.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too congratulate the rapporteur, mrs alfano, on this important report, which is becoming a fundamental reference point for parliament's action in a field which constitutes a new and strengthened competence under the lisbon treaty and which, with regard to the subject of the fight against organised crime and the mafia in the european union, with the provision of a special committee, the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office and the harmonisation of the legislation of the member states, is a fundamental point. i also appreciate that some of the proposals i made as rapporteur for the opinion of the femm committee have been incorporated, for example, to promote the role of associations of victims' families and the creation of a european forum, and to call for a holistic approach to the issue of trafficking in human beings, and in particular children, and illegal adoptions, also in the light of the recent european directive. i would like to emphasize a little more than what has been said in the text that women and children are the majority of the victims, direct or indirect, especially of criminal activities against the person, and that there must therefore be a specific and targeted effort to support and protect women victims of crime and violence, even when they are witnesses or dissociated, especially within mafia and criminal families, also enhancing their role when they are involved in the culture of legality. i would also like to mention the many women who are increasingly involved in the fight against crime, in the judiciary, in the legal profession, in law enforcement, but also among teachers, who are really trying to change the culture of our young people in this area.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, although it is too early to make a final judgment, it is difficult to escape the impression that this semester is producing weak coordination and inadequate democratic legitimacy, and the two are linked because, without full democratic legitimacy, the semester risks being more a bureaucratic exercise than a substantive coordination. this limitation certainly refers to the crucial point of the union's powers, the prerogatives of parliament, which should be the very heart of an otherwise useless or harmful reform of the treaties. but this limit also highlights a problem of actual political will to use all the instruments offered by the treaty immediately, to strengthen coordination and to give a greater role to the european parliament. there is also a problem of content. the council's recommendations reveal a clear limit to the economic policy which inspired them: the reduction of the deficit and the development of the internal market are necessary but not sufficient conditions for countering the crisis and, without a large investment plan, they risk triggering a vicious circle that can lead to our collapse. it is therefore good that the political line of the six-month period should be the subject of a genuine political debate, which can only take place in the dialectic between the european parliament and the european council.
member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank everybody for their contribution to this debate. the most fundamental change introduced by the european semester is the fact that european-level coordination of fiscal and economic policies now happens before national decisions are finalised. until this year, national policies and budgets had been assessed at eu level only after national decisions. this is a major change and, as has been mentioned by many members today, it implies an increased democratic responsibility for eu institutions. this calls for more participation of the eu institutions in national debates. we need to find a way to do this. the commission has so far preferred to avoid challenging national policies in public debate. the european semester and the ‘six-pack’ will be instrumental in delivering stability, growth and jobs in europe in the coming years. they will help us avoid the emergence of the kind of fiscal and market economic imbalances that resulted in the current crisis. but you are right: the european semester is not a crisis management tool. it will deliver results in terms of stability and growth within a few years, which is why two weeks ago we presented the stability and growth roadmap, elements of which have been addressed by the european council and will feature in the euro summit tomorrow. in the short term we need to agree on a substantial recovery path for greece, coordinated recapitalisation of banks and maximising the firepower of our financial backstops. in the longer term we need to agree on measures for growth and strengthening of economic governance. with the european semester we are already making good progress on the last element: building a true economic union. as a final note, let me just underline my conviction that the introduction of the european semester represents a very important step forward. this house has already made an important contribution to making the european semester more acting president of the council. - madam president! - what are you doing? i would like to thank all the speakers who have expressed their views on the european semester. the dominant element that was reflected in your statements was the democratic element of this whole process and who should really decide in this whole process. i often have the pleasure of attending meetings in the national parliament, my own, in poland. what i'm hearing is exactly the same thing, just from a slightly different angle. national parliaments are constantly claiming to be the ultimate decision-makers in their countries, believing that they know best what is good for their citizens. the european semester is for that purpose. on the one hand, for the first time, as the commissioner has pointed out, the european parliament is involved in the whole decisionmaking process. on the other hand, it is the national parliament that knows what the european institutions think about the economy of the country and the implementation of the priorities set by the european union. it knows the position taken by the government when preparing the draft budget and the national reform programmes and it alone, with its own autonomy, decides how and to what extent it will be implemented, because it is the national parliament that makes the final decision on the shape of the national budget, which is the most important instrument for the implementation of macroeconomic policy in a country. so i find it hard to accept that the whole process is devoid of the democratic element and transparency, because the institution that has the most influence on the whole process is involved in it at this very moment. it is difficult to say whether this whole process, the whole european semester, is a great success or not, because the process is not yet over. we do not know how national parliaments will translate into national budgets the european union's recommendations on the country's macroeconomic policy priorities. the european semester was designed to involve national parliaments in the process, to show national parliaments and other institutions, especially national ones, because they are the ones who make the final decisions, about the threats that may be lurking in their country or that already exist at this moment. the aim is to redress the macroeconomic imbalances that have arisen between member states. when, as the commissioner said, the control of the whole process was secondary, after the adoption of the budget, after the adoption of most of the implementing laws, the european commission and the council could only point out that the member states had taken the wrong path, that the actions in question would exacerbate the disadvantages of the economic situation of the country concerned. now the process has been reversed, and the final decision has been left to the most democratic institution in the process, the national parliament, which has the best contact with its own citizens and with what should be done. so i think that the structure of the european semester is at least correct, and it is difficult to say that it lacks democratic rules. but if it is used by the main addressee, the national parliaments, we will only be able to assess it in a few months.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the die is cast. i would like to begin my speech by saying what caesar said when he crossed the rubicon with his legion, the tenth invicta, and thus open the debate on the discharge of the council. this quote marks, then as now, a decisive moment, a real watershed in the history of this legislature and of this parliament. it is through the power of control over all the community institutions and the budgetary power that the european parliament expresses and at the same time makes its political priorities known, and to deprive it of these powers would be to empty the very meaning of the democratic principle and the right of representation. the question we are discussing today is therefore not one of claiming a privilege; the council has not, as it would like, shown a desire to extort money and to seize political power at the expense of others. it is rather the affirmation of the legitimate, intangible, inviolable role of the european parliament, its duty to ensure the constant monitoring of the expenditure of the european institutions and its right to be recognised as the discharge authority. parliament is not a self-referential authority but an authority, an institution representing the people of europe. this role, as the legal service has repeated, involves a twofold articulation: on the one hand, a first accounting phase, the closure of accounts, which culminates (in accordance with the provisions of article 319 of the treaty) in the granting of discharge to the commission, is carried out, and on the other hand, the political value of the discharge is developed, that is, the opinion expressed by parliament on the management of the accounts of all the institutions, without exception. we reluctantly acknowledge that we have been pushed aside too many times. the council has too often been uncooperative, often reluctant to exchange documents and unwilling to recognise us as the 'legitimate discharge authority'. it is for these reasons that we are today expressing a strongly negative opinion of the council's expenditure and voting against discharge. it is precisely this last phase that we must confront today, with respect for the diversity of views and with the sole aim of affirming the integration of europe, which, in a word, finally becomes the europe of the peoples. that is why we believe - and we firmly believe - that europe, precisely because of its millennial civilization, precisely because it is a community of destiny, represents the hope and the reference point for a world without a soul, emptied of mercantilism and shaped by an absurd conception of the world and of life, which would like to deprive its role of fundamental principles and values, such as those of belonging and of being rooted. today's vote is also all of that: the lisbon treaty has given us a high degree of efficiency and a difficult task to accomplish in compliance with the principles of transparency and democracy, which are the foundations of europe's system of protection of its citizens. it is in accordance with these principles that we do not believe we can today call the council's work satisfactory and, being certain that it is acting for a just cause, for the common good, we have no reason to fear a possible confrontation before the court of justice, nor do we fear the intergovernmental institution after our vote. i therefore ask the house to vote against the council's discharge.
