mr president, i voted in favour of mrs wallis's text. while not prejudicing the usual channels of access to justice, i am convinced that alternative dispute resolution (adr) is a quick and cost-effective alternative to litigation. in addition to being an effective tool for small and medium-sized enterprises, adr can have a significant development, including online, for the resolution of minor disputes. it is therefore necessary to promote, through joint action with the member states, the creation of a harmonised legal framework which, by strengthening citizens' confidence in the internal market, can help to stimulate the european economy.
mr president, i voted in favour of the report by mr tatarella, which calls for a three-year delay in the entry into force of phase iiib for the introduction on the market of more efficient tractors for the reduction of co2 and polluting gases. in the case of tractors, the parameters set out in directive 2005/13 were revised for several reasons: the sudden drop in sales due to the current economic crisis and the lack of technical solutions to limit co2 emissions. the amendment to the directive should be transposed swiftly so that it can be implemented as quickly as possible. i hope that the european commission will heed the european parliament's call to examine in advance whether the available technologies will be able to meet the requirements of the phase iv foreseen for 2014.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report on the provisions for tractors placed on the market under a flexibility scheme, which we voted in favour of, was inspired by a measured and realistic approach which was achieved, on the one hand, by avoiding the setting of unlikely and impossible requirements and, on the other, by providing for a so-called flexibility scheme which, by providing for time-frames and corresponding quantitative limits on permitted emissions, provides for the placing on the market of a predetermined annual quota of tractors with certain characteristics and thus makes it possible to dilute over time the adaptation to the standards laid down, without prejudice to the production and industrial sectors concerned. the work carried out by mr tatarella was important and he was able to strike a careful balance between the needs dictated by the great challenges facing the european union at this time and those of environmental protection and the current context of economic crisis.
mr president, although it is important to reduce the emissions of gaseous pollutants and pollutants produced by the internal combustion engines of non-road mobile machinery, we cannot turn a blind eye to the current crisis situation facing manufacturers. since 2008, the non-road mobile machinery sector has been hit hard by the financial and economic crisis. further extension of the flexibility scheme for the transition from stage iiia to stage iiib was an obligation. the increase in the flexibility scheme from 20% to 37.5% of the number of engines used on ground-based machinery is, in my view, an unsatisfactory result for the european industry in this sector. however, in view of the situation and the continuing delays on the part of our parliament, the producers were demanding a rapid response. i would therefore like to make it clear that it is for this reason alone that i have decided to support the report with my vote.
mr president, in order to ensure the full integration of disabled people into society, it is necessary that the member states, in line with the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, invest in accessibility, both in terms of transport and modern and advanced infrastructure, for mobility that guarantees the full and effective inclusion and participation of disabled people on an equal basis of dignity. in the context of a new union disability strategy, with particular reference to the tourism sector, it is important to ensure accessibility for disabled people not only to means of transport but also to accommodation, catering and all tourist services in general. it is also important to remember the importance of providing information in formats accessible to people with sensory disabilities, an aspect that must be increasingly central in regulating the rights of passengers and tourists. this is all the more relevant in the light of the approximately 80 million potential disabled tourists in the union, with the resulting induction, who must be enabled to travel and be considered tourists in their own right. for these reasons i voted in favour of the kósa report.
mr president, in order to assess the report adopted today, we must start by projecting two basic figures: the fact that the number of people with disabilities is likely to double by 2050, and the fact that we don't have enough data at the moment to process the severity of the problem. the challenge we face with this disability strategy 2010 is to ensure that people with disabilities not only enjoy human rights like everyone else, but that those rights can actually be exercised. it is therefore essential to give disabled people a higher status by encouraging them to train, by allowing them freedom of movement and access to the world of work: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of the unemployed, and this will also help to combat one of the major problems that accompany this category in their misfortune, namely poverty.
mr president, there are still many obstacles to the full social inclusion of the 80 million disabled. i hope that the member states and the commission will take up the challenge and draw up legislation to facilitate its integration. member states have not yet signed the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. despite the economic crisis, i hope that national governments will demonstrate their capacity to protect them by putting in place policies consistent with the european disability strategy and europe 2020. i appreciate and share the report by mr kósa, who, drawing on his own experience, has been able to give, with an open heart, concrete indications to enable disabled people to have non-discriminatory access to social protection, health care and education.
mr president, the statistics are well known, but perhaps it is worth recalling: 80 million people in the european union with disabilities, over 15% of the population: one in four europeans has a disabled person in his or her family. people with disabilities are three to four times more likely to be unemployed than the rest of the population. people with disabilities are 50% less likely to achieve a university level of education than people with normal abilities. one in two disabled people have never participated in recreational activities or sports and one third of all disabled people have never travelled abroad, or even participated in day trips, because of the inaccessibility of facilities and services. europe must really do more to break down the differences which unfortunately lead to the existence of 'a' and 'b' citizens. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work.
mr president, i not only congratulate mr kosa but i thank him for the work he has done and for this excellent report. each of us carries with us a world of our own, made up of personal experiences and different lifestyles. each person is unique and special, and that's why they're different. in this sense, diversity must be understood as a resource, in terms of growth and enrichment for the whole of society, a heritage of culture and skills. accepting any disability is not a good deed, but a recognition of the person's true nature. unfortunately, the barriers that still exist today are not just architectural but mostly mental. we must remove all the barriers that society still poses in order to finally move from the culture of disability to that of normality. while the state intervenes with specific laws, society is not always ready to accept them fully and to maintain them spontaneously. the european parliament's message in this report is: disabled people are a resource of society and must be an active part of it as much as the rest of us.
mr president, public procurement can play a decisive role in the economic budget of the european union: public expenditure on works, goods and services represents around 17% of the union's gross domestic product and almost a fifth of this expenditure - around €420 billion - falls under the european union's public procurement directives. i therefore congratulate mrs rühle on drawing what i believe to be the red lines of the forthcoming reform of the procurement directive: i am referring in particular to the lowest price criterion, which cannot continue to be decisive during the award phase and must be replaced by the most economically advantageous tender in terms of economic, social and environmental benefits. i also fully agree with the urgency of simplifying the rules so that procurement procedures are streamlined, less cumbersome and more closely aligned with the needs of small and mediumsized enterprises and small contracting authorities.
mr president, i too fully agree with the general approach taken by mrs rühle in her report and that is why i voted in favour. i am convinced that the measures adopted will ensure legal certainty on the one hand and clearer rules and more flexible procedures for public procurement on the other. i support the view of the honourable member that the procurement directives themselves are the biggest obstacle to making public procurement serve general social objectives: the criterion of the lowest price cannot have the same value as the most economically advantageous price. the most economically advantageous tender should become the rule. only then will the criteria for the preparation of the tender be feasible.
mr president, i voted in favour of the green paper on the modernisation of public procurement for two main reasons. firstly, the identification of the most economically advantageous tender which takes account of the costs of the entire life cycle of works, services and supplies and therefore not only of the lowest price, the implementation of a common and widespread feeling in all countries and in all contracting authorities, which will allow for an increase in quality, while at the same time paying greater attention to the environmental and social sustainability of products and services. secondly, simplification, which will be achieved through greater flexibility, which will allow for more streamlined procedures and more competition for small and mediumsized enterprises in the award of contracts. i would add, in particular, that in this respect e-procurement, which currently represents less than 5% of the union's public procurement coverage, should be encouraged and that the publication of calls for tender, broken down by lots, will allow participation in contracts to be more transparent.
mr president, there is no doubt that this text, the one on the modernisation of public procurement, can be an important element in the renewed efficiency and sustainability of the economic system. there is no doubt that an objective criterion for measuring the efficiency and effectiveness of public procurement is to have procedures that are streamlined, agile and simplified. the transition to the most economically advantageous tender for the selection of the contractor is important and the use of online procedures and so-called electronic procurement is appropriate, while simplified access for small and mediumsized enterprises can certainly be a moment of enhancement for this very important sector. in the committee on international trade we had foreseen and defined the exclusion of companies and firms convicted of mafia offences by a judgment which has been upheld, irrespective of the member state whose judicial authority has decided in this respect. we hope that this measure will be accepted in the revision of the subsequent directive.
mr president, with today's vote we have laid the foundations for the future revision of the procurement directive. simpler bureaucratic procedures and criteria for participation in public tenders are a key tool for speeding up the implementation process and for giving full effect to contracts between public administrations and private parties. increased use of information and communication technologies would save both time and cost for businesses and public administrations, with increased transparency and accessibility. i would like to stress that the lowest price criterion does not always have to be the main means of awarding contracts: perhaps it is necessary to replace it with the most cost-effective offer to achieve economic, social and environmental benefits.
mr president, the present world economic crisis, even more serious than that of 1929, has caused unsustainable imbalances in the international economies in recent years. trade disparities between countries, financial markets lacking common rules, instability in banking systems, are all potential threats to financial and economic stability. this resolution, which i support, stresses the urgent need for total reform with new rules and for global economic coordination. the economy needs a system of global governance, open markets, high economic and social standards, a more responsible monetary policy and stricter supervisory policies, and international decision-making bodies and economic bodies must be the main actors at the heart of this new approach. europe in particular needs a clear and transparent framework to reduce the instability exacerbated by globalisation and to ensure far-reaching reforms to promote growth and reduce the debt of individual states. this is the commitment which this resolution stresses to all countries.
mr president, 5% of women are single mothers and they represent 85% of single-parent families: this is a very worrying figure, not least because it is a worryingly growing phenomenon and because it represents a segment of society at high risk of poverty. as single mothers with dependent children, these women are often forced to make forced choices, work part-time, drop out of school, be underpaid, live in poverty and suffer unacceptable discrimination. let us not forget that there are also many women, single mothers, with disabled children to care for. i am therefore grateful to the rapporteur for her sensitivity and for the excellent work she has done.
mr president, by adopting this report, the european parliament is once again showing its support for women who are left to raise a child alone. all too often, these mothers are forgotten by the institutions and hastily labeled as a minority of irresponsible young people, forced to pay a heavy price for their mistakes. the truth is very different, and - as my colleague angelilli has also pointed out recently - single mothers now represent 5% of all european women. and it's also crucial to dispel once and for all the myth of their middle age: 85% are aged between 25 and 64. to continue to ignore this reality only aggravates their situation. i welcome the adoption of paragraph 29, which aims to promote the reconciliation of family and working life, by promoting flexible working hours and creating nursery schools, but i hope that these are not just promises but concrete commitments which will soon be fulfilled.
mr president, i voted in favour of the report by mrs matera, which analyses the situation of single mothers, who today represent, as has already been said, more than 5% of the population of the european union. the european union has a moral obligation to protect them and the text adopted today supports policies which can provide practical help for these women, such as facilitating access to health care, flexible working arrangements which allow a balance between private and professional life, priority access to affordable housing and special unemployment benefits. only by adopting these measures can the needs of a growing number of people in all the advanced and industrialized countries be met.
mr president, the report, which is based on a principle which we all share, namely that single mothers are at a disadvantage compared with a normal family situation, does not provide any measures to prevent fraud. let me get this straight: if a woman in a cohabiting couple declares herself to be a single mother, she in fact gains advantages over another woman who is legally married or who declares herself to be cohabiting. in italy, but i believe also in other countries of the union, it is not compulsory to register the existence of a cohabitation in a couple, even if the couple lives as a normal family. it is therefore clear that rules favourable to mothers who declare themselves to be single could facilitate the choice of couples not to register the existence of cohabitation, thus hindering the creation of stable families. for these reasons, we abstain on the report.
mr president, today europe is taking an important step towards becoming aware that organized crime is a european problem that has been underestimated for too long and reduced to local situations or individual member states. i fully support the report's approach and hope that a legislative proposal will soon be put forward to establish a european anti-mafia committee capable of analysing the phenomenon of organised crime in a professional manner and combating it through the institutions. culture, education, development and employment in europe are the cornerstones on which criminal organisations can build their recruitment networks. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against crime and to ensure that the fight against crime is not confined to the criminal justice system.
mr president, it is important that europe is on the front line against all forms of organised crime and all mafias. i really want to thank the rapporteur for the excellent work she has done. i would like to mention a few of the highlights of this report: stricter rules to prevent access to public funds and criminal or mafia-like organisations; new laws to exclude from procurement enterprises linked to organised crime; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's new rules on the protection of personal data and the protection of personal data against fraud and other irregularities. our efforts must continue if we are to achieve a european area of freedom and justice. we owe it to our citizens, we also owe it to the many victims of organised crime and their families.
mr president, europe is one of the main donors of development funds and we must maintain this characteristic despite the crisis, because any country in difficulty would not have the strength to rise up without the help of the international community. but this aid must follow a strategic development plan, especially in view of the expiry of the millennium development goals in 2015, promoting democratic ownership of development support policies and aid to development projects and measures, through a constant commitment from all development actors, but also providing for accountability to them. it is important to stress that aid is a temporary measure, a source of inclusive and sustainable growth, but with clear and quantifiable objectives, aimed at empowering the beneficiary countries.

in writing. − access to justice is a fundamental right: our task must be to develop simpler and clearer procedures to meet the needs of european citizens and businesses. the judicial process and alternative dispute resolution methods are intended to restore legal peace between the parties to the dispute, to adequately protect a substantive subjective right and to resolve conflicts between the parties. an alternative dispute resolution, which allows the parties to avoid the traditional arbitration procedures, can certainly be a quick and inexpensive alternative, an amicable settlement mechanism that helps consumers and traders to resolve a dispute through a third party (mediator, arbitrator). we have experience in many countries where public authorities - ombudsmen and regulators - play an important role in facilitating conflict resolution, thus helping to build public trust and legal certainty. we therefore believe that legislative measures should be taken to encourage the knowledge and application of alternative dispute resolution systems in civil, commercial and family matters, especially in crossborder disputes, since judicial proceedings in this case are more complex, more expensive and usually much longer.
in writing. − the lack of a uniform development of alternative dispute resolution systems across the union is a major obstacle to their use. i fully agree with the rapporteur that we need a system covering all the territories of the european union.
in writing. − in accordance with the principle that access to justice is a fundamental right, i consider that the promotion and awareness of a body such as adr (alternative dispute resolution) by eu citizens is a key priority in order to ensure adequate safeguards for disputes between the parties concerned, as well as to ensure citizens' confidence in the internal market by stimulating its economy. in order to facilitate the application of the adr and to encourage natural and legal persons to use it more often, i am voting in favour of the proposal presented in committee.
in writing. - the house voted today on the report by mrs wallis on alternative methods of settling disputes in civil, commercial and family matters. the report responds to the consultation process launched by the european commission on the possibility of introducing a common legislative instrument on alternative dispute resolution (adr) as amicable settlement mechanisms that help consumers and traders to resolve a dispute through a third party (mediator, arbitrator). in particular, the adopted text sets out some basic requirements for adr procedures, such as the impartiality of any third party and the need to safeguard the heterogeneous nature of the procedures. finally, it emphasises the importance of alternative dispute resolution as a preventive tool for the resolution of multiple disputes and as a means of avoiding legal action through collective actions.

in writing. - mr president, directive 2000/25/ec lays down the conditions for the entry into service of tractors in relation to harmful exhaust emissions and sets increasingly ambitious targets through successive phases limiting exhaust emissions. the report concerns the application to narrow-track tractors, i.e. those used in orchards and vineyards, of specific stages within which emission limits are to be set. the size and manoeuvrability of these tractors are dictated by the arrangement of the crops, and an increase in their size or a reduction in their manoeuvrability would, in my view, risk depriving the most advanced and productive sector of european agriculture of its main mechanisation tool. i therefore agree with the contents of this report where it recognises the technical impossibility of installing engines complying in particular with stages iiib and iv of directive 2000/25/ec in narrow-track tractors, as this would result in an alteration of the operational functionality of the engines. i also welcome the rapporteur's request that the industry in this sector be given more time to adapt to the standards of new engines. finally, i hope that the directive under discussion will be adopted quickly in order to clarify for the industry concerned the mandatory requirements for their machines.
in writing. − the exhaust emission limits for agricultural and forestry tractors were amended in 2005. at the time of introduction of this amendment, the requirements were also applied in full to engines of agricultural tractors, without any specific impact assessment on the technical feasibility of such transposition. however, there were obvious difficulties in applying the measure to tractors generically called 'narrow gauge tractors' used for automated operations on land with particular characteristics, such as orchards and vineyards. the technical impossibility of installing compliant engines while preserving the operational functionality and manoeuvrability of tractors, if not corrected, would put some of the most developed and productive agricultural sectors in difficulty, further aggravating the effects of the ongoing economic crisis. in full compliance with the european policy of combating emissions reductions, which must be developed, the current peculiar economic situation in general and the sector in particular fully justifies the decision to postpone the application of the rules for three years, allowing the parallel development of the essential design and technology necessary for the application, including on low-floor machines, of after-treatment systems capable of ensuring compliance with emission limits without compromising operational requirements.
in writing. − in 2005, emission limits were applied to engines for agricultural tractors without any specific impact assessment on the technical feasibility of such transposition. that is why it is right that the commission has granted a three-year extension. my vote is in favour of the tatarella report.
in writing. − the proposal for directive 2000/25/ec on the emission limits for agricultural tractors with compression-ignition engines of between 18 kw and 560 kw provides for a pathway of gradual emission reduction in several stages by setting lower and lower limit values for the various stages. the next dates already planned are 1 january 2011 (phase iiib) and 1 january 2014 (phase iv) and will involve the installation in the engine compartment of after-treatment systems which are very bulky in relation to the size of the engine itself, making it impossible to ensure operation in terms of size and manoeuvrability for agricultural tractors classified in categories t2, c2 and t4.1 (generally referred to as 'narrow-gauge tractors'). the limited possibility of installing such systems does not guarantee the engine performance requirements as demonstrated by the various studies carried out or commissioned by the commission, with the result that compliance with the requirements of stages iiib and iv is exempted or that compliance with the requirements for narrow-track tractors is postponed for at least five years.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because it sets new limits for the emissions of carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxide, hydrocarbons and particulate matter from narrow gauge agricultural and forestry tractors. this is a natural choice in view of the increasingly significant reduction in the pollutant emissions of this particular category of vehicles. in addition, in response to the needs of the major producers who are asking for more time to develop systems to achieve these objectives, i consider the commission's proposal to postpone the introduction of the last two, more restrictive, emission ceilings by three years to be balanced.
in writing. the commission has proposed a 50% derogation for vehicles produced in the eu over the last five years, due to the technological backlog which makes it impossible to comply with the mechanical changes required to move to the new phase, except at disproportionate cost, and as a consequence of the economic crisis affecting the tractor market, which has seen an annual decline of 20% since 2008. we have spoken in favour of the derogation and the rapporteur also agreed, because the impact on emissions is absolutely negligible. unfortunately, the european unions have expressed themselves in the opposite way purely on the basis of principle, without giving the slightest thought to the risk that, if this derogation were not approved, our factories would be closed and jobs would be lost. the agreement at first reading, following the trilogues, provides for a 40% derogation for tractors. it should be noted that the new cap provides for funding for farmers who reduce emissions from their farms. i hope that with this possibility many farmers will choose to buy the new low-emission agricultural machinery. even if we are not satisfied, we will vote in favour of the directive because of the extremely tight deadlines which, if not respected, would make it useless.
in writing. − while we share the ambitious exhaust emission targets set out in directive 2000/25/ec on the putting into service of tractors in relation to harmful exhaust emissions, we must not underestimate the incredible economic crisis affecting the european union. at this particular historical moment, an increase in the size or a reduction in the manoeuvrability of tractors, in application of the said directive, would deprive european agriculture of its main instrument of mechanization. for these reasons i voted in favour of mr tatarella's text, which, in addition to setting a three-year deferral on the terms of application, calls for a further technical review of the possibility of installing engines complying with stage iv on narrow gauge tractors.
in writing. - i fully agree with the objectives set by the directive. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's internal market is not affected by the introduction of new technologies. this is a subject on which improvisation is not possible. the reference to limits on emissions of air pollutants, for example, shows how important it is to organise and go in the direction we have set ourselves when we have defined our policies on human health and the environment. at the same time, the approximation of legislation between member states should lead to better harmonisation of emission parameters and type-approval procedures. i therefore also welcomed the acceptance of the priorities identified in the amendment on the oem, especially the reference to economic estimates, as i believe they are essential to optimise market flexibility. the choice not to place an excessive burden on small and mediumsized enterprises, so as not to give excessive advantages to large producers, is essential in the long term in the pursuit of our general interests.
in writing. − today's vote will make it easier for european industries to adapt engines to the new exhaust emission limits imposed by the entry into force of phase iiib of directive 97/68/ec. at a particularly critical time for the industry, emissions legislation - and phase iii b in particular - is forcing manufacturers of non-road mobile machinery to redesign some or all of their products to accommodate the new engines. we had to deal with an emergency situation in order to give planning certainty to the approximately 1500 manufacturers of these machines, which are very different from each other, and which have to meet specific technical requirements in order to comply with european legislation on the subject. greater flexibility will therefore not only allow producers to transition more smoothly to the strict phase iiib limits, avoiding excessive burdens, but will also give them the possibility of diluting the necessary investment in research and development over a longer period of time, without sacrificing any of the environmental objectives of the basic directive.
in writing. - the increase in the flexibility scheme from 20% to 37.5% in the non-road mobile machinery sector is certainly a first step, and a necessary one, for a rapid response to manufacturers. i think it was important, at a time of global crisis such as the present one, which has also affected the non-road mobile machinery sector in particular, to be able to have quick response times with regard to the extension of the flexibility scheme from stage iii a to stage iii b. a complex aspect, combining the needs of a lower environmental impact and lower carbon dioxide emissions with a real understanding of the needs of producers, must be managed in the direction of concrete cooperation, including legislative, between the member states. i voted in favour of the report because, despite the difficulties arising from the demands for greater flexibility and the need for a response which does not frustrate efforts in this direction, i consider it to be a good compromise overall.
in writing. - mrs pietikäinen's report has rightly put a brake on the commission's proposal to extend the flexibility scheme too far. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road, rail and inland waterway. my vote is in favour.

in writing. − parliament has on several occasions drawn attention to the situation of people with disabilities, recognising and protecting their rights. in line with the recent europe 2020 strategy, one of the most important objectives is to increase the employment rate among the approximately 80 million people with disabilities living in the union. at present, against an ambitious target of 75%, their employment rate is low across the eu at 30-40%. by 2050, according to eurostat, the number of people in dependent employment will double. between 2010 and 2050, the working population will decline by some 50 million people, while the number of people over 65 with disabilities will increase by 77%. in future, therefore, employment protection and safety at work will play an increasingly important role in the definition of national policies and strategies for persons with disabilities within the member states. the principle of freedom of movement is a fundamental right of the citizen. i agree with the rapporteur that the introduction of a unified european mobility card, which would allow for the mutual recognition of assistance provided to disabled people, could make an important contribution to the protection of their rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr kósa's report because it touches on a number of aspects in which i too have decided to take a personal interest, in order to promote the protection of the rights of disabled people, all the more so after having seen and experienced their needs. in general, i agree with the rapporteur's approach, which proposes the adoption of a number of concrete measures aimed at creating a sustainable society, based on an approach rooted in the defence of human rights. at the same time, however, i believe in the need for precise dates and deadlines to enable the national implementation of the conventions adopted by the united nations (the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and its additional protocols) and the european union (the european disability strategy and the europe 2020 strategy). in particular, among the various key elements addressed by the report, i would like to highlight the achievements in the following areas: the production of vehicles compatible with the needs of persons with reduced mobility; the production of electronic interfaces that allow better communication for disabled people; support for families aimed at the inclusion in the education system of children and young people with disabilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe in the joint effort of the member states of the european union to ensure the integration of people with physical and communication disabilities into society. the social exclusion of disabled people, together with the lower employment rates for them, in my view causes serious damage to civil and human rights which should be guaranteed to all citizens without distinction. in this connection, it is necessary, on the one hand, to remove the barriers which lead to the exclusion of such individuals and, on the other hand, to adopt measures which can facilitate their integration into the labour market. protecting their rights is an important step towards better implementation of the european disability strategy, as well as towards the employment target of the europe 2020 strategy. the mobility and integration of these people is an important tool in the fight against poverty, which many of them face because of the lack of work. i am confident that all member states will be sensitive to the need to put an end to discrimination against disabled people and to promote their full integration into society.
in writing. - the number of disabled people in the european union is about 80 million, or 16% of the total population. these figures should therefore make us reflect on the importance of a policy in their favour, which covers the employment and, consequently, social aspects of all aspects of their lives. the report by mr kósa, which i have supported, has the merit of putting the problem of the employment needs of disabled people at the centre of the debate, with particular reference to the europe 2020 strategy. considering that the employment rate of the disabled is only 45% and that, at a time of crisis such as the one we are experiencing, unemployment for the disabled is about twice that of non-disabled people, it is clear that there is a need to initiate employment policy processes aimed at increasing the employment of people with different disabilities. it is from employment that investment in people with disabilities must be made in order to improve their processes of social cohesion and integration into the personal relational structure. we must not talk about equal opportunities, as mr kósa points out in his text, but about specific measures to promote the integration of disabled people into the workforce in the first place.
in writing. − with this report we intend to encourage the adoption of a whole range of specific measures aimed at promoting the creation of a sustainable society, based on an approach based on respect for fundamental human rights. we therefore call on all member states not only to sign and ratify the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and its additional protocols, but to develop national disability policies and strategies, in line with the european commission's european disability strategy (eds) and the europe 2020 strategy. we agree with the rapporteur that it is important to show that the mobility of people with disabilities, including access to communications as a means of spreading ideas and expressing oneself, and social integration are not two separate elements, nor two factors that complement each other, but are the two cornerstones of an approach based on respect for human rights, capable of improving equal opportunities for people with disabilities in all member states of the european union.
in writing. − in europe, the need for personalised measures for people with disabilities, including measures for different levels and characteristics of disability, remains clear. i fully agree with the rapporteur's approach to such an important subject and therefore i am voting in favour. i would like to stress that inclusion in the world of work and economic autonomy are extremely important factors for the social integration of disabled people.
in writing. - in this situation of general difficulty, certain sections of the population, which are already suffering more than others, cannot be abandoned, but must be given more help. unfortunately, disabled people still have many difficulties in accessing the labour market, which is the basis for a full and independent life. it is also necessary to promote their mobility as much as possible: the simple example of the european label is quite significant. it seems to me that this is not a very difficult task to accomplish, but the european union should be able to take the lead in putting an end to this problem once and for all. finally, i find the explicit reference to sign language as an official language of the union very important: we hope that europe will send a strong signal to the member states to adapt in this direction. the report under consideration touches on these and many other important aspects, and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. − the integration of people with disabilities and the recognition of their rights are crucial to the creation of a sustainable society based on an approach based on respect for human rights; member states should therefore not only ratify the un conventions on the rights of persons with disabilities but also develop national disability policies and strategies to ensure equal opportunities, leveraging factors such as increased employment rates, education and training systems and the unhindered movement of people. i am pleased with the motion for a resolution on a subject of primary importance in the field of human rights, and i feel it is necessary and my duty to vote in favour of moving towards an approach based on respect for human rights and thus capable of improving equal opportunities for people with disabilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr kósa, who highlighted the physical and social obstacles which unfortunately still exist in many member states and which limit the lives of 80 million disabled people living in europe. however, to date, the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities has not yet been ratified by all eu countries: the appeal is still lacking in 11 out of 27 member states and, even where it has been ratified, implementation is weak precisely on accessibility to space and buildings. in line with the europe 2020 strategy, one of the most important objectives is to increase the employment rate and this will require the elimination of all barriers preventing disabled people from accessing the world of work, as well as the development of national policies in line with the european commission's european disability strategy, which also provide for easy access to public and private transport. employment and social inclusion must also be more present in strategies and more envisaged in european funding. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that a european mobility card is needed, which would allow for mutual recognition of assistance provided to disabled people and guarantee that everyone can travel in an appropriate manner by any means of transport.
in writing. - mr president, an open and regulated public procurement policy is a decisive factor in making all procurement procedures more transparent, non-discriminatory and competitive, also to avoid falling into patronage and corruption. i agree with the rapporteur, mrs rühle, that the award of contracts should no longer be based solely on the criterion of the most economically advantageous tender. today, with a view to achieving many of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, priority must also be given to quality and innovation, which are also criteria offered by smes. the latter now obtain a lower percentage of public contracts than other larger companies, this because the procedures for access to contracts are too complicated and onerous. i therefore support the need for clearer rules, for greater simplification of european rules and for better access to flexible instruments not only for smes but also for ngos providing social services.
in writing. - this year marks the 40th anniversary of european procurement law: in 1971, the first directive 71/305/eec on public works contracts came into force. this, in my view, provides an opportunity to assess the successes and failures of european policy in this area. as regards the achievements, i believe that european public procurement law has made a decisive contribution to making the award procedure more transparent and to combating corruption; on the other hand, transaction and external consultancy costs have increased, due to the preponderance of unilateral legal issues. this is particularly problematic in times of economic crisis and budget cuts. i would also point out that access to public procurement for small and mediumsized enterprises is hampered by a number of difficulties, mainly bureaucratic. i therefore welcome a review of european law on public procurement. i would like to take this opportunity to draw the commission's attention to the need to consider introducing measures to reduce transaction costs for small and mediumsized enterprises and, in addition, to provide for greater simplification and flexibility of public procurement rules.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs rühle on the modernisation of public procurement, because i think it is appropriate to revise the subject in order to make it more relevant. initially, strict rules were needed to ensure uniform rules in the member states, based on the criteria of transparency and free competition. now that these principles have become established in the union, i share the view that it is appropriate to review the rules in order to make them more flexible and modern. the public procurement sector plays an important role in the europe 2020 strategy, which is why we need to ensure that this discipline ensures the efficient use of public funds. in particular, through appropriate use of this financial instrument, energy efficiency, innovation and environmental protection can be supported. i welcome the call for the prevention and fight against corruption to be implemented through more transparent and controlled selection procedures, in cooperation with the states. i also share the desire to make it easier for smes to enter the public procurement market, thereby also allowing small and mediumsized firms to participate in this important economic sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which parliament has drawn up in response to the european commission's green paper. public procurement can be a real engine for the european market, for the promotion of jobs and for the development of skills and innovation. i believe it is essential to continue with greater vigour the fight against the phenomenon of corruption and favouritism in public administration. the existing legislation must also be improved by simplifying the rules, in particular by using information and communication technologies and appropriate standards. this would lead to a wider participation with a corresponding reduction in costs: the optimal efficiency of public spending. i agree that the dominant criterion should not be the 'lowest price' but rather the 'most economically advantageous offer'. this would undoubtedly stimulate innovation and efforts to achieve the highest quality and value. in addition, improving access for smes to public procurement is also of central importance, as they must be allowed to participate on fairer terms, given the obstacles they face due to their small size.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report by the honourable member is intended to provide an analysis of european public procurement policy. i think that the report contains some very important points, such as flexibility in procedures and more transparency in the rules of implementation. the report calls on the commission to pursue the path of simplification. one aspect which i find very important is the incentive to encourage tenders which stimulate innovation. that's why i'm voting yes.
in writing. − in a time of worldwide budgetary constraints, public procurement policy must ensure a more efficient use of national money to boost the economy. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information it receives from the member states. that is why i agree with the rapporteur in his choice of criteria for selecting the winners. criteria for selecting the most advantageous tender in terms of both economic and social benefits, in relation to the whole production cycle of the good or service to be guaranteed, such as for contracts in the food sector. the new provisions laid down in the green paper on public procurement must also guarantee passive consumers, such as patients in hospitals or nursing homes, access to the best quality/price health food and not simply to the cheapest products available. finally, i hope that, with the introduction of these new measures, the procurement instrument can increasingly be a driver of innovation and an incentive for businesses to propose solutions from which the whole of europe can benefit.
in writing. the subject of mr rühle's report is significant and sensitive for the business and public administration world. this year marks the 40th anniversary of european procurement law, as the text emphasizes, in particular with directive 71/305/eec. the process of modernising public procurement, including the computerization of the system, is complex and requires attention to the aspects of the protection of companies, particularly smes, the competition system and a degree of transparency of transactions to ensure a procedure that also has a legal impact. i am convinced that reconciling the different aspects of a delicate sector such as public procurement is a mechanism that requires careful attention to all the parties involved in order to guarantee their rights and obligations. we cannot, in fact, draw up a plan for the modernisation of public procurement simply because we are dazzled by the effectiveness of the words 'sustainability' and 'computerization'.
in writing. − modernising public procurement means increasing transparency and equal treatment and thus fighting corruption. i agree with the rapporteur on the objectives and the means of achieving them, and i also agree with the objections to the commission's proposal: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the public procurement directives are revised. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - public procurement, especially in a period of general economic stagnation, can certainly be a steering wheel for recovery. this report proposes a further definition of the rules and procedures for tendering and a simplification of them. a large part of the budget is devoted to small and mediumsized enterprises, for which the most simplified legislation is needed; the commission proposes in particular to facilitate the award of large contracts in batches, so as to enable smes to participate massively in a greater number of calls. i would also like to point out the need for more and more public contracts to be concluded electronically: this model involves a significant reduction in burdens and costs, as well as a significant saving in time. i think that in the final analysis this report is very well done and is going in the right direction and that is why i wanted to express my positive opinion.
in writing. - the 40 years of european contract law (on 26 july 1971 the first work contract directive 71/305/eec came into force) have allowed the legislator to gain experience which has led to great successes on the one hand and failures on the other, such as a lack of legal certainty which has led to contradictions and confusion. i therefore believe that it is essential to revise european public procurement law in order to simplify and make it more flexible, ensuring aspects such as transparency, non-discrimination and the security of competition. i therefore welcome the following motion for a resolution and i shall vote in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because the european rules on public procurement must be simplified to allow small and mediumsized enterprises to access tenders more easily. in addition, contracts should not necessarily be awarded to the most economically viable tender, but also to the most innovative or environmentally friendly one. finally, to simplify the procedures for awarding contracts, it is necessary to create a genuine electronic passport certifying that the tenderer complies with the relevant community rules.
in writing. - mr president, i congratulate the rapporteur on making such a complex report and subject accessible to all. i welcome the following document, as it calls on the commission to follow the path of simplification and protection of the different legal practices of the various member states of the union, and to reject the introduction of new rules for contracts awarded at european level. the report also devotes a great deal of attention to the protection of smes in relation to their ability to access european contracts. finally, i would like to emphasize that the simplification of legislative procedures not only offers numerous advantages to local administrations but also helps to eliminate economic burdens. i therefore call on the commission to pursue this line of legislative clarification.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text presented by mr rühle on the modernisation of public procurement, also in the light of the forthcoming debate on the proposal for a revision of the so-called 'procurement directives'. while i am very much in favour of a general simplification of procurement rules and procedures, which would undoubtedly help to speed up the signing of contracts, i believe that more controls should be made on self-certification: while this is a means of simplifying the participation of undertakings in tenders, it is also necessary to establish a database of administrative acts and measures as proof of the requirements declared in order to combat the submission of false certificates or statements.
in writing. − the union is an area of freedom and security, where free movement means freedom to move to another member state to find work or to respond to a job offer. however, statistics show that only a small number of citizens avail themselves of this right and only 2.3% of european citizens reside in a member state other than their member state of origin. in the context of the economic crisis, the current rate of mobility is not sufficient to enhance the efficiency of the labour market: the commission has already taken a number of measures to encourage the mobility of workers. the most recent studies have shown that the exercise of the right of free movement of workers does not have adverse effects on labour markets, and therefore member states should facilitate the exercise of this right by adapting national legislation in order to remove potential direct or indirect obstacles, in particular those related to discriminatory behaviour on grounds of nationality. achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and supporting the economy in the current crisis situation requires joint and concrete action by member states to strengthen mutual trust to support workers and markets.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that, although the right to live and work in another eu country is one of the fundamental freedoms enshrined in the treaties, the specific initiatives taken to support mobility are still not sufficient to achieve it fully. but be careful . mobility must be seen positively and as an opportunity. considers the exercise of the right of free movement of workers to be essential to boost the union's economic performance and to achieve the employment objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy; the european commitment to this end must therefore be further reaffirmed. it is necessary to support full harmonisation between national and european legislation to ensure that potential direct and indirect obstacles to mobility are removed, and the need for greater convergence with other existing policies and strategies to facilitate the movement of workers from one state to another.
in writing. - at this particular historical moment, marked by a global force which requires us to rethink the labour market model, i find mr ungureanu's proposal relevant and determined to resolve crucial issues on the role of labour mobility in the eu. i therefore voted in favour. the promotion of labour mobility must be carried out on two fronts: on the one hand, by working to break down the bureaucratic barriers which restrict a proper approach to the free market; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the report contains a number of proposals, including one on the recognition of diplomas and qualifications acquired abroad in one's own country. the reduction of a step in the bureaucratic process which often represents an obstacle to labour mobility and hence to a process of economic and social growth is an achievement which must be supported by similar initiatives in the future and in the european political and institutional context.
in writing. − the issue of labour migration within the eu has long been perceived as a potential problem due to imbalances at national level in terms of labour supply. however, labour migration has had a beneficial effect on the eu as a whole, often by rebalancing labour supply and demand. the concept of 'free movement of workers' was inserted in the treaties to ensure the completion of the single market and the strengthening of a genuine european identity, while allowing member states the right to maintain temporary obstacles for transitional periods in relation to the opening up of the labour market to new member states. the free movement of workers is a right of citizens. the exercise of this right does not have adverse effects on labour markets. the member states, together with the relevant local and regional authorities, therefore play a key role. they should cooperate to ensure that potential direct or indirect obstacles are removed, in particular those relating to discriminatory behaviour based on nationality, refusal to grant rights to family members, social security systems and other obstacles which may prevent or discourage the free movement of workers seeking work.
in writing. - the report on the promotion of worker mobility within the european union will have my vote in favour. the free movement of workers is one of the greatest achievements of the european union. i agree with the rapporteur that this right must not have a negative effect on the labour market.
in writing. the question of the mobility of workers within the european union is of particular relevance. the report stresses that little has been done to encourage this practice, which, in the rapporteur's view, is generally beneficial to everyone. i would like to disagree with this point because it is not at all true that complete freedom of movement has only positive aspects. in a period of great general expansion, flows of workers may fill in production gaps, but this is only now a thing of the past. the present is a time of enormous difficulties for all, and greater mobility cannot solve the problems, but rather exacerbates them. the mass arrival of foreign workers in areas in difficulty can, for example, create a number of problems, perhaps even leading to racism and xenophobia. it is history that teaches us this: if there is widespread prosperity, there can also be mobility, but if there is not, it is desirable that everyone stays in their own country. at the moment, in my view, the conditions for complete european mobility are not in place, and that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. − given that the right to live and work in another eu country is one of the fundamental freedoms of the union, there are still too few citizens who make use of this right despite numerous initiatives to promote and support workers' mobility. however, it should be considered that the mobility of workers contributes positively to the achievement of the employment objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy and, in addition, in times of economic crisis, the occupational and geographical mobility of workers can contribute to reducing unemployment. despite the eu's legal acts and programmes to promote the free movement of workers, i believe that there are still obstacles to the full implementation of this freedom, and i am voting in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is essential that there should be no discrimination on the labour market against citizens from other eu countries, including those from countries that joined the union only in 2004. any restrictions must be removed by the end of this year, as they are counterproductive and contrary to the community values of free movement, non-discrimination, solidarity and equal rights. in this sense, the european commission should start infringement proceedings against governments which do not comply with these rules as soon as possible.
in writing. the report considers that the low mobility of workers between member states constitutes a constraint on the functioning of the internal market and therefore presents and promotes a comprehensive framework of migrant workers' rights with a view to the practical implementation of the principle of free movement. we are opposed to the report because its implementation would entail considerable costs for the member states' budgets in terms of training, learning, language support, health and education for migrant workers and their families. in addition, it is believed that workers from countries where the cost of living is lower may create situations of unfair competition with workers from countries where there is a different standard of living. for example, a bricklayer company moving from romania to italy to work will settle for 35%-40% less than local companies, creating a distortion of the market. the free and full movement of workers between member states will only be possible when the cost of living and working is uniform throughout the union.
in writing. - mr president, the transposition of the services directive has been the most complex and lengthiest process ever implemented at european level, both in terms of its complexity and its scope: the services sector accounts for more than 40% of community gdp. the main provision of this directive concerns the establishment of single points of sale throughout the community, but its implementation is still far from being complete and efficient. i therefore stress the importance of the implementation of fully operational one-stop shops in the territory and share the wish that information be available everywhere, including in english. i also agree that it would be appropriate to complete a quantitative study of the impact of the directive on both economic growth and employment before proceeding with the revision of the directive. i hope that any revision of the services directive will be aimed primarily at removing the regulatory and administrative obstacles which still exist and which, in my view, are responsible for the slowdown in the free movement of services within the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it highlights the main aspects to be taken into account in the current transposition of the services directive into national legislation. the overall potential of the common market in services has not yet been fully exploited and the correct implementation of this directive is undoubtedly the essential condition for the completion of the internal market. however, it is also necessary to ensure a consistent implementation of the various legislative acts of central importance to the activities of services, such as the new regulation on european standardisation for which i am the rapporteur, which will deal, among other things, with the application of standards to the services sector. i would like to make it clear, however, that the timely transposition of the directive must not prejudice the possibility of safeguarding national characteristics, particularly those relating to the entrepreneurial activity of smes. in my view, the commission should assess whether the services directive could have a negative impact on smes in certain sectors - i am thinking for example of smes in the italian seaside industry - and propose measures to mitigate this impact and ensure that the specific characteristics of certain occupational categories are taken into account in the application of the directive.
in writing. − increasing and improving the services sector, which today accounts for two thirds of gdp and employment in the eu, is a commitment to be pursued, as intra-eu trade in the sector accounts for only one fifth of the total. the report by mr handzlik, for which i voted in favour, stresses the importance of implementing the peer review process provided for in the services directive adopted in 2006. the priority underlying the improvement of the mutual evaluation process is the full transposition of the services directive for all member states and a proper approach to relations between states in the subject matter of the report. once this obstacle has been overcome, it is appropriate to focus on the implementation of the mutual evaluation process based on the principles of cooperation and dialogue. it is clear, however, that this process must make its objectives clear and tangible if it is to be considered a virtuous evaluation tool that will promote and increase trade in the sector within the european union.
in writing. − report on the mutual evaluation process under the services directive the functioning of the single market in services is a fundamental prerequisite for generating growth, employment and innovation in europe and for maintaining europe's competitive role in the world. i agree with the rapporteur that mutual evaluation should be extended to other areas, but in a balanced way and in line with the experience of recent years.
in writing. − agreeing on the importance of the services directive adopted in 2006 as an essential tool for the establishment of a fully functioning single market for services, and considering the usefulness and relevance of peer review in view of the results, i agree with the idea of proposing to extend the use of the services directive to other sectors and i vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. mr president, i would like to express my strong opposition to this report, not so much because of the specific subject dealt with in the text, namely the instrument of mutual evaluation on which, despite the delays and inconsistencies in the process, it is possible to draw some positive elements, but because of the commission's attitude to such a complex issue. unfortunately, the report deals with only a marginal and unimportant aspect of the services directive, failing to address the serious problems it is creating, such as the lack of consumer protection, the lack of autonomy left to local authorities and the questioning of those small productive activities on which the economy of entire families has been based for generations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr handzlik's text on the transposition of the services directive, which is without doubt the most difficult and complex transposition process ever undertaken in europe. the main aspect of the directive concerns the creation of one-stop shops throughout the community, but the objective is still far from being achieved, especially if the obstacles still remaining in the various national systems are not overcome.
in writing. − i voted for this report because effective global economic governance would make it possible to minimise the negative effects of globalisation, such as rising inequality and the destruction of the environment. in particular, i support the idea of reconsidering the use of ‘special drawing rights’ (sdrs) as a possible replacement for the dollar as the world’s reserve currency. this measure could be a starting point in helping to stabilise the global financial system. the international monetary fund should explore further allocation, as well as broader use, of sdrs, in particular for the purpose of enhancing the multilateral exchange rate system. this text also calls on the commission to design a comprehensive mechanism, largely based on and strongly interlinked with world trade organization regulations, to prevent the use of trade as a foreign-policy tool in a way contrary to internationally recognised democratic values as reflected in the charter of the united nations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and i would like to commend the excellent work done by the rapporteur, mr hökmark. the current economic crisis has prompted major economic powers, including the european union, to rethink the governance model of the global economy, necessitating a common approach to monetary policy, international trade, sustainable public finances and flexible currencies based on economic fundamentals. only a multilateral governance of the world economy and trade can prevent further economic crises and minimize their negative impacts. i am convinced that the eu must play a leading role in this context, supporting the process of reform of global economic governance, intervening in a unified way in international economic affairs, including through stronger external representation. i believe that the union, acting in a coordinated manner, can, on the one hand, relaunch international economic and commercial cooperation, including the bric countries (brazil, russia, india and china) and, on the other hand, make a decisive contribution to the reform of the imf and the world bank, extending their institutional coordination action at world level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the hökmark report on global economic governance because it deals in a comprehensive way with all the areas of the international economic, financial, fiscal and monetary policy sphere of the current situation. global imbalances are a major threat to stability. the report provides excellent guidance in terms of improvement actions that would be useful to take to improve the functioning of the international monetary fund, the g20 and the world trade organisation in the face of current and future challenges. europe needs action to strengthen economic governance and the single market in order to be a valuable partner in dialogue with other global players. it is emphasised that in a global economic environment of open markets in constant exchange, it is all the more necessary to achieve high shared social and environmental standards, and the european union can act as a global forerunner in this regard. i therefore believe that this is an important contribution to the work that parliament is doing on the economic strengthening of europe in the global context, following the adoption of the so-called '6-pack' on european governance relating to the internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it very important to review and improve the mechanisms of governance at global level through a strategy of multilateral cooperation, especially in view of the serious instability that is characterising our economic system today. global imbalances seriously jeopardise the financial and economic stability of all countries already severely affected by the recent economic and financial crises. in this connection, i believe it is essential to adopt a common approach at community level with regard to monetary policy, international trade and public finances. sustainable development and fair trade make a significant contribution to strong and balanced growth, as called for in the lisbon treaty. improving governance mechanisms is instrumental in achieving these objectives and aims to avoid imbalances in which different economies are unable to produce wealth. europe must therefore, in my view, adopt a coherent approach based on standard setting and information exchange aimed at creating better governance mechanisms for the benefit of the whole community.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr hökmark's report because i believe that the proposals contained in the text are in the direction of further strengthening the european union in the world economic and financial institutions. the eu accounts for 50% of world gdp and therefore the role of european economic institutions in the international context needs to be strengthened. the period of crisis we are living through and the exposure to the attacks of speculation which have afflicted and continue to afflict world markets in a context of a global economy, require us to make choices aimed at strengthening the role of world economic institutions. the report's proposals are aimed at greater coordination between actors in political and economic institutions such as the imf and the g20 in order to make decisions on monetary policy, monetary agreements and tax administration more effective. a reform of global economic governance is a proposal consistent with the eu's cooperative role and the needs of the current historical moment.
in writing. − global economic imbalances pose a potential threat to the financial and macroeconomic stability of the major european economies. the current economic and financial crisis has shown that capital flows resulting from global imbalances require a more responsible monetary policy and strong financial regulation and supervision. we therefore support this report because it recognises the need for policy makers around the world to continue to work on solutions for reforming global financial governance, in order to help rebalance the world economy and avoid another crisis. the reform of global governance will need to ensure that markets are integrated into an organic institutional framework that allows them to function properly; the creation of a favourable environment for long-term investment must be the main objective. the european union is called upon to play a leading role in global economic reform to make international institutions more legitimate, transparent and accountable. we believe that the european union can speak with one voice and we therefore ask for its seat in the imf and the world bank.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of mr hokmark's report. the world needs policymakers to put in place solutions for global financial governance reform quickly to help rebalance the world economy and avoid another crisis. the reform must start with markets that are integrated into an organic institutional framework.
in writing. - it is undeniable that a global economy requires global economic governance and this report draws some important lines. first, there is a need for greater international cooperation and the so-called 'emerging powers' must also take up their responsibilities: it is unthinkable that there are rules that apply only to europe, while elsewhere it is the "far west". i am referring, for example, to unanimous respect for the working conditions of individuals, because we can no longer tolerate that in different countries these standards are constantly trampled upon. i would also like to point out a very important aspect of this report, namely the call for a global financial transaction tax: it is only in this case, that is to say, when applied universally, that this tax could make sense. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the report is therefore a good starting point and that is why i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. − despite the development of the world economy in recent decades, which has led to an increase in wealth, lifting millions of people out of poverty, the number of people living in poverty is still intolerably high. this is the result of social and economic inequalities between countries, which create an environment of unsustainable imbalances in the development of the world economy. in this context, effective global economic governance is needed to minimise the negative impacts and to correct the adverse effects of globalisation.
in writing. - the resolution by mr hökmark on global economic governance was voted in the house today. parliament approved its contribution to the reform of global economic governance in the run-up to the g20. the resolution calls for a reorganization of the imf, more effective regulation of global finance and strict controls on possible subterfuge, and stresses the need to correct the existing imbalances in the world economy in order to avoid further turbulence, something the g20 has so far found difficult to do. it also called for greater democratic participation in the decisions of the imf and the world bank and for parliamentary involvement in their decision-making processes. it also calls on all these financial institutions to coordinate their work more closely.
