in writing. − the global economic crisis, originating in the financial sector, has led to high levels of indebtedness in key policy actors such as the united states, japan and the european union. the weaknesses in the economic system have exposed the shortcomings of the lack of coordinated financial regulation and supervision, thus aggravating the sovereign debt crisis. at this point, as i have already said in the hokmark report, which i voted in favour of, the international monetary and financial system must be reformed, with the creation of common rules on global economic governance to give back to the operators and investors in the sector the guarantees and certainties that are no longer there.
in writing. in europe, 5% of the female population are now so-called 'single mothers'. the economic and financial crisis has affected the entire european population, but women have been particularly affected. moreover, recent studies have shown that the impact has been even more severe for the vast majority of single mothers at the beginning of their careers. the problem of single mothers cannot be ignored: the high unemployment rate in these countries has a significant impact on the education and care of dependent children. in fact, with limited resources, children have less chance of succeeding in their school careers and, consequently, of being competitive in the labour market. i therefore share the rapporteur's concerns and her determination to tackle the issue. the inequalities faced by single mothers in europe should be tackled through concrete actions such as promoting and investing in research in the field, including by using the recently established european institute for gender equality. as soon as the results of the research are available, i believe that a dialogue should be initiated between the member states in order to share best practices in implementing european policies to solve the problems encountered.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that more attention should be paid to the situation of single mothers by investing in and promoting research in this field. at present, 5% of the female population are single mothers, who are now a neglected but increasingly significant demographic category in all advanced and industrialized countries, often living in vulnerable conditions, with all the consequences this can have on their children. unfortunately, these women in particular also have statistically more difficult access to education than other mothers and are therefore subject to higher unemployment, lower wages and low-quality jobs. i therefore support the need to respond appropriately to the new reality that has emerged by engaging in a dialogue with other member states to share and learn best practices in implementing policies aimed at reducing the risk of economic insecurity that single mothers face in the labour market. it is therefore desirable to introduce new provisions to improve the employment rate of the latter.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 5% of the european population are in the position, by necessity or choice, of being single mothers. the report highlights the socioeconomic difficulties of mothers (and children) and calls on the commission to work with member states which do not have such resources to provide support for this category. that's why i'm voting yes.
in writing. - we support this report because we share the intention to encourage member states to tackle the issue of single mothers by investing in and promoting research in this area. to this end, member states could enhance their cooperation with the recently established european institute for gender equality in vilnius. once the results of the research carried out are available, member states should engage in a permanent dialogue to share and learn best practices in policy implementation and best solutions. we believe that some examples could be useful and transferable to all member states. national policies should be promoted which provide indirect support, such as food purchases, or which can provide tax credits for single parents, as is the case in austria, belgium, the netherlands and the united kingdom. single mothers and their children should also be able to benefit from health care benefits to compensate for the absence of one of the parents. the creation of a european-wide incentive for those member states which provide free health care to mothers and children living on incomes below the national average would be a step in the right direction.
in writing. - a difficult situation, that of single mothers in europe, which we must address immediately through a series of actions which the member states must undertake in the most coordinated way possible. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - given the heterogeneity of the phenomenon of single mothers, and therefore the many disparate issues that affect each mother differently, it is extremely difficult to identify a pressure group that can support the interests of the whole category of single mothers. more importantly, the precarious ability of single mothers to provide education or care for their children is also highlighted, given the high unemployment rate among single mothers. the possibility of relying on limited resources alone does not guarantee a stable livelihood to the mother. it is for these important reasons that, in addition to congratulating the rapporteur, i am voting in favour of the report, stressing the importance of encouraging the member states to tackle the issue of single mothers through investment and research in this field.

have done. trust, support and progress are the three objectives of effective implementation, management and reporting of the eu budgetary funds. the economic and legal basis of the financial regulation is now finding new strength, with the prospect of financial changes that want to innovate europe by promoting and improving infrastructure investments, guarantees and financial methodologies. we must make the best use of the resources we have. we must invest in the sectors most suited to fostering growth and advancing europe, a europe that is more integrated, more competitive, with sufficient resources to pursue common policies and to play a leading role on the international scene. the first commitment today must be to encourage public investment, private investors and the governments of the individual member states to take more courageous action from the economic and financial point of view and, in this spirit of mutual cooperation, to face any opposition arising from democratic confrontation. in this sense, the issuance of new financial instruments is a key element of the regulation, which supports the financial market and system of the union and the member states. in an economic context of serious crisis, characterized by a globalised and bipolar system which is increasingly seeing the political and economic binary of the united states and china assert itself, europe must equip itself with new financial instruments if it is not to be marginalized and penalized. the goal is this: we are also working on a new strategy for the european union, which is to be implemented in the next few years. only then can progress and a positive future be guaranteed. i therefore believe that, in order to achieve the objectives of economic and financial growth, it is essential to make it clear that we must closely monitor the effective promotion of european society. the increase in spending power and therefore the power to create wealth, if not wisely directed towards concrete ends, does not have the desired effect and produces only waste. the contraction of national budgets must therefore be met by financing from banks or guarantee institutions, in order to encourage investment in situations where, without union support, there would have been no capital increase, nor the acquisition or creation of new resources to be used in the advancement of the european production process. all this - i stress - is not to benefit banks or wealthy individuals, but to increase a spill-over effect which can thus affect all social strata. similarly, european support for potential losses from sub-optional investments is certainly perceived as a great example of support and guarantee for the citizens of the union, since we know that otherwise some large projects, for example the supply of energy resources, without public initial capital, would make no sense. the key role of project bonds is undeniable, and they are now gaining new strength with the joint decision of the epp group and the commission to start a phase of promoting private investment in infrastructure and in the energy, transport, information and communication sectors. through investment in infrastructure we can support and help the european market and the financial system of the union. without a system of solidarity based on mutual trust and the incorporation of past experience, the market cannot fully fulfil its economic function. a people who ignore their past will never know anything of their present. this principle is necessary if we are to learn from the difficulties of the past financial management and to ask ourselves what mistakes were made, what did not work, how we can do justice to the european market and the economic system that unites us and that makes us, despite the difficulties, a beacon and a support for the countries we represent today. the more you can look to the past, the more you can push into the future. we improve the research, technological and innovation sectors by supporting competitiveness and innovation projects, which are particularly efficient in providing financial guarantees, which are not provided in almost all member states, by supporting research and innovation projects where ad hoc financial systems allow loans to be granted to individual beneficiaries. as far as the reform of europe is concerned, it is in the present economic constraints that we can see a structural solution to the crisis we are facing. as long as europe's action is not more efficient and decisive, as long as the spaces between capital and investment are multiple and confusing, as long as private individuals can rely on a system, we cannot rely on a system that gives them guarantees and confidence, first years of implementation of the multiannual financial framework, are to be dealt with.

in writing. - i am in favour of the revision of the council directive on the common system of taxation. the now unsustainable levels of sovereign debt of eu states require a common approach at european level to mitigate the effects of the current financial crisis. in recent years we have seen a decline in the average tax rate applicable to eu companies (from 44% to 23.2%), coupled with the introduction of eu rules to combat double taxation for eu companies. this is leading to an inevitable race-to-the-bottom of tax rates, to long-term non-taxation, and even to double non-taxation. i would also stress the problems that arise when multinational companies make profits through subsidiaries located outside the eu (tax havens), which attract capital by providing for zero or limited taxation. the state is losing out to multinational companies which no longer take on a proportionate share of the financing of public needs. i therefore support the introduction of a minimum tax rate of 25% applicable in the inbound state and the introduction of measures to combat double non-taxation. this directive will inevitably reduce the sovereign debt of member states and mitigate the economic disparities caused by the different tax regimes of eu and non-eu countries.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by briefly introducing the oral question we have put to the commission. it is more than a political act, it is an act of recognition that we intend to make to the european commission because it is showing great interest in the protection and promotion of the rights of children. on 15 february, commissioner reding therefore presented a communication on the european union programme for the rights of the child, a package of 11 concrete actions that the commission intends to implement in the coming years on the justice side in order to establish child-friendly justice in all 27 member states. i'll list some of the measures. first of all, the proposal for a directive on the rights of victims, which is already under discussion in the libe committee, and one of its objectives is to protect child victims in criminal proceedings. another important point concerns the protection of roma children, as well as the activation in all free states of telephone helplines for missing children and early warning mechanisms for missing children, as well as a commitment to open a kind of information desk within the european parliament and european union website dedicated to children. the following are some of the indications included in the package: it is important to take account of the extraordinary efforts which the commission and individual commissioners are making to protect the rights of children, both inside and outside the european union. i now come to the proposal for a directive on the fight against the sexual exploitation of children and child pornography, for which i am rapporteur, and i would first like to thank the shadow rapporteurs, mr sippel, mr lambert, mr wikström, mr triantaphyllides and mr kirkhope, who have helped me along a path which has not always been easy. i would like to thank commissioner malmström, who was very keen to see this directive, the council, the hungarian and polish presidencies, which followed this legislative process very closely, and all the non-governmental organisations, starting with unicef, ecpat, save the children, all the main ngos that have followed us and helped us to draw up this directive. i remember . the second criminal law measure following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, after the trafficking in human beings directive, and the first legislative measure to address a specific area of criminal law, namely the protection of children against sexual exploitation, abuse and child pornography. the directive in question, among other things, takes all the indications of a resolution that was adopted by the european parliament in 2009 and takes the lanzarote convention as a reference point. some qualifying points: the definition of offences. the text defines the offences of sexual abuse, sexual exploitation, child pornography and sexual exploitation of minors. we have introduced a specific definition of child pornography, referring to the lanzarote convention. it also introduces uniform and effective criminal sanctions throughout the european union and specifies aggravating circumstances, in particular when a child is in a vulnerable situation, is otherwise able or perhaps the offence was committed by a family member or by a person who has in any case abused his position of trust and authority. then, the ban. anyone who has committed a crime and has a conviction will be banned from even volunteering with children. we have provided for the seizure and confiscation of property and proceeds of crime under this directive. much has also been done in the area of assistance to victims, to prevent the so-called double victimization, the crime of sex tourism, the crime of grooming, that is, the online harassment of minors and, lastly, as regards the online child pornography material, it is planned to remove all these illegal contents. i conclude by saying that, of course, this is never about censorship of freedom of expression and freedom of opinion: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the content of the internet is not subject to censorship.

member of the commission. − madam president, i should like to say thank you very much to all who took part for a most interesting and very important debate. i would like to highlight a few things, because much has been said. baroness ludford asked me about the countries that have not acceded to the hotline number 116000. in the revised universal service directive it says that the member states should have made every effort to accede to this by 25 may of this year, and still 11 countries have not done so. it also says that the member states shall inform citizens that it exists and facilitate the operation of services in order to comply with this. it is up to the member states to choose how they promote the hotline. in order to raise awareness, allow exchanges of best practices and identify practical tools, the commission is organising best practices meetings and high-level meetings with stakeholders and will continue to do so every year until all countries have made sure that it is operational. i also had a question from ms nedelcheva on the convention of the rights of the child. it is more complicated than it might seem to adhere to this, because the european union can – as the members well know – only act within the limits of the competence conferred on it by the treaties. moreover, in accordance with the articles in the actual convention of the rights of the child, the instrument is open only to state parties. for these reasons the commission does not, therefore, envisage acceding to the convention. however, the eu agenda for the rights of the child reaffirms the importance of the convention and will do everything to make sure that all eu legislation and proposals are in line with that convention. i would also like to highlight something that might be a misunderstanding; i do not wish to open the debate again but want to assure you that nobody has promoted, proposed or envisaged introducing blocking instead of deletion; that has never been an issue. what we should do – and this is very clear in the commission proposal, and i am very happy to have the huge support in this house – is ensure that member states delete at source. this is the only way to combat child pornography on line. we shall delete at source. however, we all know that with the majority of these horrible sites – and i do not know if you have seen them (there are toddlers on these sites) – there are a lot of people making huge amounts of money every time someone sees those babies being abused, and every time someone looks at it they are abused again, again and again. the majority of these sites are not hosted in the european union: that is why the commission proposes that the member states should block access to the content until it can be removed at source. in this proposal it says that member states may now do so. of course, we must also cooperate with the countries which host the majority of these sites, and we are engaged in very active negotiations, talks and collaboration with, for instance, the united states on this – they are moving forward – and also with russia and other states. having said this, i think you, ms angelilli, with the massive support and praise you have got in this plenary from the left to the right, can be very proud of what you have achieved. we can all be proud: the council, the commission, parliament and yourself, because with this we are providing good tools to prevent, to protect and to prosecute people who commit these offences. we are also sending the very important political signal that sexual abuse of children like this is not acceptable, and this is a clear message from the whole of the european union. thank you very much for a very important debate and very important work. in writing. the sexual abuse and exploitation of children, including child pornography, constitute serious violations of fundamental rights, and in particular of the 'right of children to protection and care necessary for their well-being', as enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the directive we are about to adopt is the first measure to be taken in a specific area of criminal law: the protection of children against sexual exploitation, abuse and child pornography. after years of active struggle against the phenomenon of paedophilia, i can only welcome this new directive which acts on three fronts: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european police office. in addition, innovative measures are introduced to combat all forms of abuse: introduction of the grooming offence , definition of the sex tourism offence within the union; rules of injunction to avoid the risk of repeated offences; confiscation and seizure of property arising from child pornography offences. finally, i believe that it is a major step forward in the fight against abuse to give member states the power to take the necessary measures to ensure that websites containing or disseminating child pornography are immediately deleted.

in writing. − i voted for this report in view of the importance of the directive on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children and child pornography. this document aims to establish minimum rules concerning the definition of criminal offences and sanctions in the area of sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children, child pornography and solicitation of children for sexual purposes. as the european parliament report underlines, this directive should be fully complementary with the directive on preventing and combating trafficking in human beings, and protecting victims. in addition to that, this report asks for reinforced protection for victims and prevention measures, both at eu level and at member states level. the text stresses also that member states must ensure the prompt removal of web-pages containing or disseminating child pornography hosted in their territory and endeavour to obtain the removal of such pages hosted outside of their territory, measures that i consider to be of primary importance.

in writing. - the sexual abuse and exploitation of children are particularly serious crimes, which can cause lasting physical, psychological and social harm. we believe that it is essential to adopt an approach that addresses the root causes of the problem, with the aim of eliminating crime, the nature of which is changing rapidly, especially due to the progress of technology and its applications. in the past, manifestations of child pornography were limited to physical media, correspondence or photographs. today images can be sent around the world via the internet, quickly and free of charge. the criminal nature of these acts calls for strong and determined action. we have long discussed the issue of blocking and deleting content from websites. a careful balance needs to be struck between freedom of expression and the protection of minors. member states have a duty to work with internet service providers to ensure that minors are protected from illegal activity through the establishment of a monitoring system. member states must first obtain the deletion of internet pages containing or disseminating child pornography or, if deletion is not possible, provide for the blocking of access to such web pages.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, before i begin briefly with my report, i should like to thank the shadow rapporteurs who have worked with me on the revision of the railway recast and, in particular, i should like to thank mr kuhn, mr tremosa i balcells, mr zīle, mr krahmer and mr wils. i would also like to thank the chairman of the committee on transport, brian simpson, the group coordinators and all the other members for the extensive discussion we have had on a particularly complicated report, but one which i believe is important for the implementation of the railway system. this is the revision of the first railway package, which has not been properly applied since it came into force, so much so that 13 infringement procedures are currently under way against different states in relation to the application of the first railway package. the aim of the railway reform is to achieve a single european railway market. it is an ambitious objective because the railway system is the most backward of all transport systems, that is to say, the one which has not been able to catch up with other means of transport. it is enough to recall that, as far as rail freight is concerned, we are stuck at an average of 6-7% of freight transport in our european countries, while only 11-12% of passengers travel by rail. it is clear that we must harmonize the rules, that we must strengthen and add new systems and new elements to ensure that railways, especially on cross-border routes, which are the most difficult for european integration, develop properly. the single european market is therefore necessary, as it has been for the air transport sector. the single market will enable citizens to travel by train throughout europe at better fares and with a service on a par with other modes of transport. to date, few trains can travel across the border. the aim now is to enable them to compete throughout europe, which, as i said, is not the case today. the first railway package was therefore intended to guarantee the objective of this reform and all the measures that will follow for the unification of the railway system. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. one of the important points we have discussed at length and which i believe is also the most important result of the railway reform is the envisaged creation of a national regulator, a network of national regulators with clear powers, a national regulator such as the one for energy, which is strong, has resources and which perhaps - this is the hope of many - will then enable us to arrive at a single european regulator in the future. we have tried to give precise rules for the transparency and separation of the accounts of the infrastructure manager and the service manager, prohibiting cross-transfers between the network and the service manager as is the case for example in the case of many holding companies. we have tried to maintain the separation of accounts, which has been in force since 1991, according to which public funds for infrastructure must be used only to improve infrastructure and not to finance the activities of transport companies, also because these subsidies prevent fair competition for all operators in the service. i would have liked to see more ambition in the railway package as rapporteur, i would have also liked to see a complete separation between infrastructure and service operator. however, we have obtained a commitment from the commission that this will be done by 31 december 2012. other important forecasts concern the ease of access to infrastructure, which is essential to ensure that all new operators can use the network services, and we have also obtained a commitment not only to full unbundling but also to the submission by the commission by 31 december 2012 of a proposal for the liberalisation of the national market. we have also envisaged benefits for all those operators who will make important technological innovations to reduce the environmental impact and we have also envisaged that improvements can be made in this area by providing for the possibility of strategic plans that go from 5 years to 7 years. we have also wanted to ensure that the rules on labour law and safety at the workplace are respected and that the right to strike is preserved.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to ask the honourable member who - i think quite rightly - insists on rail transport being used primarily instead of rubber, how he views the attitude of those people in italy who, even by violent means, oppose the rapid rail link between france and italy, even contesting the underground passage.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i thank mr serracchiani for the work he has done this year with the colleagues who have followed him. i must say that we have tried to influence the efficiency of the railway market. the text proposes that we create a single european railway area. the expectations were high, but after a year of work, i think i can see that it has been considerably scaled down. the analysis of the situation has shown that the market is far from being single and integrated and, above all, the issue of the liberalization of national and regional passenger transport markets is not yet recognized by this parliament. we are talking about 60% of the railway market, which is not, in fact, free at the moment. i am personally astonished at the lukewarm approach to a matter which concerns one of the four fundamental freedoms of the european union. given the contingent situation in which we must concentrate on growth, i wonder how it is possible to give up the removal of administrative barriers which impede the competitive development of competition and the european market. the same fate was assigned to the reflection on the relationship between infrastructure managers and railway companies. in this connection i have tabled an amendment to annex i to include passenger stations in the infrastructure in order to have equal and fair access for all those who exercise the role of passenger services. this is important, otherwise we would start with the wrong division.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, these remarks reflect a large variety of the details of this complex matter. i think that this railway recast legislation is worthy of support. it has some important elements, such as clear and efficient rules on infrastructure, financing and charging, the strengthening of national regulators – so the regulatory dimension will be strengthened and will be very important in our future deliberations – and better access to rail-related services. so these are elements which clearly show improvements in this railway recast package. of course, a lot of things will remain for the future. it is far from the end of the story – it is one step. i must ensure that our main aim is to create an attractive railway area and in order for this to happen, railways need punctuality, reliability and speed to compete with roads, and they must operate in europe as a whole. these are the basic points. then we can also create more jobs in the railway sector if railways offer better services for people and businesses. so we will work on the next package and let us follow our ambitions.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, as the previous speakers have pointed out, this proposal for a directive has involved a very complex task: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. among these compromise texts is also article 7 which the commissioner mentioned, in which parliament calls on the commission to make a proposal on the separation and liberalisation of the national market by 31 december 2012. there is no proposal that is premature in any way, but there is a clear call for an equally clear and precise direction to be given, a direction which, if it had been there from the beginning, would probably have helped in the gestation of this long railway project. meanwhile, my assistant also had a baby, so it was indeed an extremely long and complicated pregnancy, but i'm sure we understand how important it is to increase the rail system. we have said that we need a competitive railway system, so we must set ourselves rules, perhaps few but clear, which are respected by all. we know that there is a problem of free competition on the railway market, and we know this particularly in the case of freight. the railway industry has the ambition of making the european single market. so the call is strong for this commission to come up with a clear proposal by next year and, since next year is so close, we propose to start working so that this parliament can also fulfil its role as legislator, also because the text which has just been dismissed by the council is a text which is extremely negative also on the proposals. we hope therefore that this parliament will give us a clear and full mandate to be able to make a full negotiation which will really open up the european single market to all the expectations to which - i hear the cry of pain from mr cancian - we must respond.
member of the commission. - madam president, good evening to each and every one of you, ladies and gentlemen. i thank you for giving me the floor to raise an extremely important subject at a time when we are talking about citizens and the market, the large market, and the human dimension of this large market which we want to strengthen. the recognition of professional qualifications is of particular interest to citizens: 28% of them now plan to work in another country during their career. between 2007 and 2010, the automatic recognition of professional qualifications enabled more than 100,000 europeans to realise this personal project. we think the potential of this device is even greater. it now covers some 6.4 million professionals, including 5.7 million healthcare professionals, 160,000 veterinary surgeons and over 435,000 architects. such figures, ladies and gentlemen, show what the circulation of such skills throughout the internal market can mean. that is why we must, and we want to, make this recognition easier, simpler, quicker. this recognition of qualifications is an additional source of confidence and god knows what confidence is needed at the moment for citizens and for businesses in the european project. i would like to say, after these general remarks, how pleased i am that the own-initiative report you have just presented, mrs mcclarkin, is a real convergence with many of the ideas put forward by the commission in the green paper published in june. this confirms once again the high-quality cooperation between our two institutions, which i am very keen to see. and i was able to verify this quality and frankness in our relations at the public conference which the commission organized on 7 november in brussels, where many of you were present, in particular president malcolm harbour, but also emilie turunen, bernadette vergnaud, constance le grip, who were pleased to speak in the panels. i would like to thank in particular you, mrs mcclarkin and mr harbour, and to commend the work of all the other members who, in the imco, envi and emploi committees, have contributed to the reflection you have presented in a very constructive way. i would like to confirm that this report, which you have just presented, is a very important contribution to me as we are in the very last stretch of preparing the legislative proposal which the commission will present on 20 december. our positions are not always the same, but beyond these few nuances there are no major differences of opinion. i would like to emphasize four important points. first, the business card. the first objective of this modernisation of the directive is to promote mobility by simplifying and making more efficient the procedures for the recognition of qualifications. that is why we are thinking - as i have already said - of creating this european professional card, which must be easy, pragmatic and practical. this is not a traditional smart card which could be very expensive and in any case difficult to make at a reasonable cost. the card we are proposing is an electronic certificate based on the exchange of information between the competent authorities. this optional card for professionals but mandatory for the competent authorities could reduce the time taken to process an application for recognition from a few months to a few weeks. and naturally, it will involve the home member states much more and, as you said earlier, rely on the internal market information system imi, which must help to reduce costs for all the actors concerned. secondly, the number of regulated professions. i am aware - you have also mentioned this a moment ago, mrs mcclarkin - of the debate on the number of regulated professions which some consider to be too large. i would like to put this delicate point in context. of the 800 regulated occupational categories, 43% are health professionals, 9% teachers and social workers. i do not think it is unreasonable, if i can give you my objective opinion, that, in such sensitive sectors, there should be regulation of the professions involved in these sectors. so i think we must first see exactly what is regulated and why. i do not exclude the possibility that a stronger obligation of transparency towards the member states may be envisaged as a first step. it is up to these member states to make this effort of critical analysis on the number and type of regulated professions. i was at the competitiveness council the other day, and one of the ministers around the table, the portuguese minister, explained that by national will, some 15 regulations which were considered unnecessary had been abolished. however, without waiting for this work to be encouraged in the member states, we will propose solutions such as partial access which could reduce the difficulties faced by some professionals in their mobility. thirdly, the preservation of automatic recognition. automatic recognition is currently a mobility-friendly regime. it is an achievement that we want to preserve. i am very glad that parliament supports this position. i will nevertheless propose to modernise this system and go even further by extending it to other professions, in particular through common training frameworks, which could usefully replace the old concept of common platforms. we need to modernize, yes, but without questioning this automatic recognition. for example, you have just mentioned, mrs mcclarkin, the question of language requirements for health professionals, which must be considered with a certain degree of caution. the problem is not so much the directive itself. i believe that this directive imposes an obligation on professionals to have knowledge of the language of the host country, which is obviously necessary for the proper exercise of their profession. the problem, we believe, is the implementation of this obligation for health professionals in the member states. two points on this. first, as regards salaried professionals, i would stress the role of employers who must check the language skills of their employees; secondly, i find that the best solution we have in this respect is to disconnect the verification of language skills from the recognition of professional qualifications. the fourth and final point is the one-stop shop. for businesses, for the selfemployed, the services directive has been a great step forward. i also want to say that every week, in my visits to the member states and in my relations with the national administrations, i try to check that the services directive has been properly transposed and, above all, that it has been properly implemented, since its potential is not yet fully exploited. a great deal of progress has been made with this 'services' directive, with the establishment of one-stop shops to obtain information, to complete administrative formalities by electronic means. the same benefits must be extended to wage-earners, to health-care professionals. we should therefore set up an online information centre, as you yourself have suggested, based on these one-stop shops and allowing these professionals to carry out the recognition procedure online. these are the four points i wanted to make, and i thank you very much, mrs mcclarkin, for the quality of this report, which will be very useful to me and my services in the next few days, before the legislative proposal we will be presenting on 20 december.
the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the mobility of european workers is one of the pillars of the full realisation of the internal market and a lever for development and the economy. in europe, there is an estimated shortage of about one million healthcare professionals. this requires a system of recognition of qualifications which is fast and effective, and the professional card could facilitate this process. in the health sector, however, mobility must be combined with patient safety and security. this is the direction taken by the report which was voted almost unanimously in the committee on the environment, on which i was rapporteur. mobility and patient protection must be considered as two sides of the same coin. the rapid alert mechanism extended to the health professions is therefore not only acceptable but also necessary.
on behalf of the efd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the recognition of professional qualifications is an important step at european level, since it is a prerequisite for a professional who is legally practising in one member state to be considered sufficiently qualified and competent to practise, even temporarily, in any other member state. there are professions which require continuing training, and it is important that this is accessible and verifiable at all levels and throughout europe. the report pays particular attention to the health sector, which involves doctors, nurses, pharmacists and other professionals who also need to know the language in order to avoid misunderstandings with the patient. the clause which we consider to be fundamental is that each member state may make access to a given profession legally conditional upon possession of a specific professional qualification. the professional card proposed by commissioner barnier could make it easier to check in advance whether one is qualified to use one's qualifications in any other member state.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, europe is a continent rich in fresh water but in danger of becoming poor in drinking water. this is a paradox due to the increasing number of cases of pollution of the aquifers. in italy, for example, in veneto, my region, in the last fifty years, underground mining and landfills have been authorized, which have led to serious pollution of the groundwater, soil and drinking water wells. in may this year, the regional agency for environmental protection in the veneto region found mercury poisoning in more than 100 wells in several municipalities in the province of treviso. the most important and necessary soil directive, adopted by the european parliament at first reading in 2007 but still blocked in the council, which provides for the obligation to survey and remediate contaminated sites and thus solve the problem of groundwater pollution, must therefore be unblocked immediately.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, 18 months ago i committed myself to open a wide consultation on this very important subject of online gambling. we are returning to this subject today and i would like to return to it for my part, indicating my firm intention to translate its main conclusions into action, beyond and after this consultation. we have received more than 250 responses which, together with the five expert workshops we have organised and the intense debate which you, ladies and gentlemen, have had on mr creutzmann's own-initiative report, clearly demonstrate this dynamic in favour of concrete action at european level on a basic regulatory framework which respects - i say this to president malcolm harbour - what he himself has called - and which i would like to take up for my own account - active subsidiarity. i would like to thank mr creutzmann for his commitment and mrs schaldemose, mrs rühle, mr abad, mr de jong and mr fox for their contributions to this report. this report shows a great deal of convergence of views among you on the diagnosis. first, in the online environment, no member state can ensure consumer and citizen protection on its own. i say this in reference to what my colleague and friend john dalli said earlier on the consumer issue in general. secondly, consumers and all citizens must be able to rely on an equal and effective minimum level of protection, and in particular for young people and minors, which was mentioned earlier by mrs roithová, regardless of the gaming platform they are playing on. thirdly, while each member state remains free to determine the level of openness of its market, in accordance with the principle of coherence, it is clear that we are gradually moving towards this controlled openness - mr abad described it very clearly - of many markets. fourthly, in the absence of legal offers in europe, europeans are playing and will continue to play on illegal third country sites, which are unprotected and open to all kinds of fraud and money laundering. fifthly, we must ensure that, to avoid the consequences of what i have just said, we offer attractive conditions to online gambling operators if we are to protect players and prevent fraud. sixthly, we must act because this sector is expanding. it generated a turnover of eur 8,5 billion in 2010 and could reach eur 13 billion in 2015. even though this represents only 14% of the gambling market in the european union, europe still accounts for 45% of the global online gambling market. we must support this sector in its expansion while ensuring that it is properly supervised. what could be, what should be our roadmap to answer all of your questions and all of these challenges? ladies and gentlemen, let me be clear. harmonisation is not on the agenda, but joint action on some key issues can be envisaged and perhaps at the end of our road, a framework - i repeat - of a common regulatory base. i would like to mention six key areas where we are going to act. first, there is the dialogue between national regulators. we know that there is a lack of cooperation between national regulators which is probably the result of a lack of mutual trust. apart from a few bilateral agreements and a recent attempt to create a common platform, there is no culture of cooperation between national regulators. on the contrary, i have observed that there was - i repeat - often a lack of confidence. but without a new degree, an additional degree of mutual trust, no progress can be made at european level in strengthening controls and protecting players, especially young people. the priority should therefore be to get european regulators to work together. the second key issue is a minimum requirement for protection. we must guarantee a high level of protection for every european citizen - and i repeat, first of all for young people - to move forward in this direction. we will have to bring together the online gambling professionals who today self-regulate and the regulators who, i remind you apply different requirements. there is therefore a general call - and you have relayed this in your report, mr creutzmann - for greater clarity and legal certainty. the third key issue is the fight against fraud. there is a very broad consensus in this consultation and in what you yourself say in favour of extending the scope of the anti-money laundering directive, which currently only covers casinos, to the whole of the online gambling sector. this would be a significant step forward in the regulation of the sector at european level. the fourth key topic is addiction. it has been mentioned earlier by mrs irigoyen pérez or mrs sehnalová. we cannot seriously talk about consumer protection without recognizing the need for more studies, research on the scientific data that are linked to gambling and addiction. we must mobilise our research capacity on a subject which is sometimes considered marginal, but which i do not consider to be marginal. integrity of sport is the fifth key issue. here again, mr creutzmann, ladies and gentlemen, i have noted your interest in the issue of sports fraud and i share your desire to contribute to effective solutions, including the idea of a definition of sports fraud at european level, or even a criminal indictment, an idea which i find interesting but difficult. we can't just go off the rails. it requires a lot of legal and technical work and we are working on it with my colleagues who are directly concerned, in particular commissioner reding, mrs vassiliou and of course mr dalli for consumers. i am also convinced that progress will have to be made towards better cooperation between sports organisations - mr abad mentioned this - with operators and regulators, in order to prevent match-fixing. the sixth area of work is the question of the conformity of national schemes with the treaties. i would like to reply to mr takkula on this point, since he himself has quoted the court of justice, which is extremely clear about restrictions which can be justified in the public interest. i think, mr takkula, that in order to make progress in this area, we must clarify what distinguishes a legal gambling offer from an illegal one; the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the principle of equal treatment to all workers in the same sector. the commission will take its responsibilities on this and other points. how, mr creutzmann, are we going to work on the basis of these key issues, on the basis of your requests, your proposals and this report? my personal inclination is, first of all, to promote cooperation between regulators, and i intend in the very next few weeks to convene and organize myself a meeting of all the national regulators to create this climate of confidence, which does not really exist, and to lay the foundations for this cooperation. if, as one might expect, the cooperation of regulators makes progress on the key issues we have mentioned, but above all highlights the need for complementary action, then we will work on a second stage, which could, as mr paška has asked, be based on regulatory initiatives and create minimum standards. naturally, i want to be very clear on this. i am a member of a college, i have to work with all my colleagues and therefore make them share this conviction. we are going to proceed with the first step which i mentioned very quickly: the joint work of the regulators. i should like to take this first observation and this first work as a starting point and share with my colleagues the conviction i have just expressed that we must go further, particularly in the development of minimum regulatory initiatives. so we have to follow the steps one by one. that is why, having mentioned the main challenges we face, i will now work in the light of your report, mr creutzmann, and i intend to propose to you, after the college has deliberated and decided, a plan of concrete actions which i will submit to the college of the european commission in the middle of 2012. i am very grateful to mr creutzmann and to the members for this report which will inform, guide and support the commission in its future work. we have a collective responsibility to help member states regulate online gambling, protect consumers, especially young people, develop legal offers and fight fraud effectively and together. you can be assured of my determination on all these matters.
in writing. according to recent data, the online gambling sector continues to grow. these games now account for 10% of the european gambling market, and their market share is continuously growing, with a turnover of over eur 10 billion. the continuing growth in supply and the number of players is increasingly highlighting the fragmentation of the european market in this sector. in some member states, there is an absolute prohibition or a reservation of authorization, while in others the market is completely liberalized. moreover, given the cross-border nature of the internet, member states alone are not in a position to regulate all aspects of online gambling. i therefore believe it is essential to ensure that national regulatory bodies cooperate closely. i also agree with the rapporteur that such cooperation should be institutionalised, including through the internal market information system, in order to share information efficiently and quickly. on the front of combating the growth of the black market on the internet, i believe that national regulatory bodies must have the necessary powers to punish any infringements and prosecute unauthorised operators.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the council has made an urgent request to parliament to express its opinion - i repeat, only opinion - on the matter for which i have been appointed rapporteur at the november 2011 meeting of the committee on fisheries. as rapporteur, and on behalf of the whole committee on fisheries, i oppose the council's request for urgency and i think it is necessary to explain why we have taken this decision. this council proposal concerns access for vessels flying the flag of venezuela to the exclusive economic zone off the coast of the french department of guiana. the proposal is similar to an international agreement on which, under the lisbon treaty, parliament has the right to speak as a co-legislator under the ordinary legislative procedure and is not required to give its opinion. the proposal presents no difficulties in substance and, if approved by the council, will create obligations for the parties concerned in international law similar to those of a fisheries agreement in due form. but the crux of our decision lies elsewhere. the european commission put forward this proposal to parliament on the basis of a specific legal basis, namely articles 43 and 218 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and parliament, in view of the content and spirit of the proposal, which gave it, among other things, a power of approval, fully accepted it. it was then that the council, in its subsequent referral to parliament, amended the legal basis in question, setting aside articles 43 and 218 and opting for articles 43 (3) and 218 (6), thus reducing the expression of parliament to a simple opinion. the coordinators of our committee on fisheries have rejected this amendment by the council and have referred the matter to the legal affairs committee of the european parliament before taking any final position. the commission has confirmed the validity of the legal basis initially adopted by the european commission and, in particular, has warned our committee on fisheries of the unpleasant precedent which could be set by the implementation of such a combination of articles 43 (3) and 218 (6) of the treaty. in response to the council's insistence that the opinion be obtained as soon as possible, rather than approval, the chairman of the committee on fisheries, mrs fraga estévez, in a letter to mr buzek, recalled both the position of the committee on fisheries and that of the legal affairs committee and suggested that mr buzek send the council a proposal containing the original legal basis in order to resolve the dispute. president buzek sent a letter to that effect to the president of the council on 26 october 2011 and has not received a reply to date. i therefore think it is appropriate to await the council's reply and it is nevertheless essential to reiterate that we are not prepared to abandon the fundamental rights of parliament which we have a duty to defend.

the polish presidency, took place in krakow. this convention brought together over 400 participants from 38 european countries, including ministers and state secretaries, other policymakers, civil society representatives, journalists, people experiencing poverty and independent experts. i was very pleased that members of the european parliament, including mr daerden himself, today’s rapporteur, attended the convention. i represented the commission there, and i think the first meeting of this convention was successful, useful and forward-looking. the convention took stock of the implementation of the poverty platform and it discussed how the different policy areas – employment, education, health, just to mention a few – could contribute to tackling poverty and social exclusion. this multidimensional approach, which was welcomed by all participants, should be further strengthened in the future in line with the european platform; employment, education, and health, together with housing, are the key parameters in the european framework of roma integration strategies, which is a major anti-poverty effort that requires european-level coordination but also support. mr daerden, in your report you underlined the multidimensional aspects of poverty, ranging from extreme poverty and homelessness to in-work poverty, but also the gender and age dimensions, and the specific questions of people with disabilities and ethnic minorities. the european platform against poverty and social exclusion alone will not be able to solve all the issues raised in the report, but it provides, in my view, a good framework for actions, and each and everyone should accept their share of responsibility in tackling the rising problem of poverty. among the actions to be implemented and solutions, you mentioned that there is a need for a better monitoring system allowing rapid and accurate analysis. i agree with you. we have already started to develop such a system with the involvement of eurostat and the indicators subgroup of the social protection committee. you also called for regular and critical monitoring of the member states’ poverty-reduction targets. 2011, and i am sure we can do more in this area. we need to promote the implementation of the three pillars of active inclusion: namely, active labour-market policies, minimum income and access to member of the commission. − the reference year for eligible agricultural areas is 2014 in order to take account of the reality at the time of the decision or from the time when this decision will apply. on the other hand, 2011 is the reference year for farmers who are entitled to apply for these aids precisely in order to avoid speculation in 2012 or 2013 and farmers who did not exist as farmers registering with certain areas for the sole purpose of obtaining entitlement to subsidies. during this period we are giving the possibility to integrate young farmers who would be setting up in 2012 and 2013 and we are also giving the possibility to the member states to take account of specific situations as was done in the 2003 reform. there are thus two references: 2011 for the farmer who has rights and 2014 for the area which will allow him to apply for rights from the member states in order to avoid speculation and the possibility to take into account the margins of manoeuvre during this period. i know that there are situations in ireland, particularly in northern ireland, for example, where landowners are also farmers. they farm part of their land and rent the rest. these are specific situations which will have to be dealt with in order to avoid speculation on either side. i am well aware that these are specific situations to be dealt with in discussions in the decision-making process.

member of the commission. - the proposal, as presented, recognises the role of tree plantations on the environment since the crop rotation measure is not proposed. but this measure of keeping 7 per cent at the level of the ecological use of the areas can easily be applied to tree plantations, because the areas, the spaces between the rows of trees or the edges of the plantations can very well be kept under grass. this is a system that works well in the production of fruit trees, for example, which is part of the technology and also has a positive impact by keeping this grass in certain bands. so if in an olive grove, there are areas at least every two or three rows that are kept grassed, this can have a beneficial effect on production and in any case, it will not affect production and it is not necessary to cut down trees and, in addition, the 7% can be covered. so seven percent on a plantation, where all the third or fourth rows are still weed, will be enough. this will be the only greening measure planned for such a farm, since tree plantations are recognized as having a positive impact on co2 reduction.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, online gambling is a growing market with a turnover of over 10 billion euros. at present, the regulation of the gambling market is a matter for the individual member states, but the most sensitive issue is the proliferation on the internet of an unregulated black market of considerable size, the main players of which are located in asia. the principle of subsidiarity for the benefit of the member states remains a cornerstone, but coordination at european level is necessary to combat external threats. these dangers concern not only consumer protection but also the very revenues of member states which rely heavily on taxation of so-called legal gambling. another significant point is the difficulty of identifying the identity and age of players via the internet. the commission and the member states must act without delay to protect european consumers from unscrupulous operators and the risk of addictive gambling.

in writing. − differences between national insolvency laws often create competitive advantages or disadvantages and difficulties for companies with crossborder activities, which could hamper the successful outcome of restructuring operations of insolvent companies. the conditions under which insolvency proceedings may be opened should therefore be harmonised at european level. the legal affairs committee has rightly identified four points for future legislative initiatives. in addition to harmonisation, where possible, a revision of the insolvency procedure regulation is desirable where still needed and where practice has shown the possibility of improvement. the third point is that cooperation between trustees and general administrative cooperation should be strengthened in cases where companies are part of a group of companies which has become insolvent. finally, it is suggested that a european insolvency register be set up. the recommendations are intended to provide the commission with guidelines for reform of the matter to eliminate disparities between national legislation.
in writing. - mr president, we have a challenge, and that is to tackle demographic change in a concrete way, through targeted policies and a virtuous allocation of financial resources. unfortunately, we are witnessing an ageing european population: the population growth rate is among the lowest in the world, while the birth rate is below the replacement threshold, at 2.1 children per woman on average. demographic change will have a decisive impact on the political, social and economic situation, particularly as a result of the crisis, the age of retirement and the large migratory flows to europe's borders. in addition, cities will face high population density, while in some 20 regions the population decline is estimated to exceed 10%. there is no time to lose, we need targeted policies, efforts and concrete and visible progress in a short time, for example by acting on women's and youth employment and the integration of people with disabilities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because demographic change is creating new possibilities for some regions in the world and, instead of being viewed purely as a threat, it should also be seen as an opportunity. the support provided by the cohesion policy instruments should be carefully examined and exploited in an appropriate manner. the impact of demographic change varies substantially from region to region, depending on whether it is rapid or slow and whether the region concerned is a region of net immigration or of shrinking population. for this reason, this text calls on the member states and regions to consider the divergent development levels of the regions and take into account demographic indicators when allocating and distributing eu structural funds and defining impact indicators. furthermore, demographic developments in the regions should be made comparable, and exchanges of best practices between member states, regions and local communities should be encouraged.

in writing. − demographic change as highlighted in the fifth cohesion report represents one of the central challenges for the future of the european socioeconomic system, a challenge that invests in a broad territorial context and has a profound impact on the management of services and infrastructure. without detracting from the commitment of the individual member states, this challenge - which can become an opportunity - directly affects the european institutions and, in particular, regional development policies, characterized by differentiated strategies and adapted to meet the needs and requirements of areas with a positive population balance and those with a declining population, respectively, as well as the different needs of urban and rural areas. in response to these challenges, the european funds (both the erdf and the esf) represent a potential to be fully exploited to ensure the rebalancing of needs and, to this end, the prospect of using specific demographic indicators in the allocation of european funds as well as in the redistribution of funding at the level of individual member states is positively assessed. the vote in favour calls for policies which will link the effects of demographic change with the fight against old and new poverty.

in writing. - according to eurostat, no eu country has a positive replacement rate. only a few, including britain, france and ireland, have a population balance with a progressive upward trend. indeed, the european countries with a negative demographic balance - germany, italy and spain - have reached what some call the point of no return. according to some demographers, the latter are in a "low fertility trap". the reasons for low birth rates lie in the fact that childlessness and one-child families are becoming the norm, with the resulting cultural institutionalization of 'zero growth'. in the developed world, delaying childbearing is one of the main causes of low fertility, while greater access to contraceptives has allowed the adult population to exercise greater control over the timing of births. an increasing number of men and women are seeking to establish themselves in the world of work, postponing the conception of children. the possible dramatic repercussions of demographic change are already known and are many. i would like to mention one of them, which is affecting our national systems, namely the ageing of the population. the result is that an increasing number of older people are dependent on an ever-shrinking workforce.
in writing. − in the current climate of crisis and financial emergency in the eu, it is important to regulate and standardise certain aspects of member states' legislation on short selling and credit default swaps. we must give markets and investors a coherent framework and thus ensure effective and prompt supervision against the speculative phenomena that have fuelled the economic crisis. the proposal which is now being voted on contains restrictions on the sale and purchase of financial products and derivatives on markets which, as they stand, are instruments in the hands of speculators intent on damaging sovereign debt securities and profiting from the downward spiral in prices. the possibility of restrictions on short selling on a temporary basis should also be provided for, as provided for in the text, and in particular cases cooperation between the different national authorities responsible for market surveillance should be encouraged through the coordination of the european securities and markets authority.

in writing. − to end the current fragmentation situation in which some member states have adopted divergent measures, it is important to address in a harmonised way the potential risks arising from short selling and credit default swaps. in the event of a significant increase in the price of a financial instrument on a trading venue, which is clearly disproportionate to previous values, competent authorities should be able to temporarily prohibit the sale of that instrument on that venue. the rules suggested by the committee on economic and monetary affairs are designed to address the risks identified, increase market liquidity and allow investors to act when they believe a security is overvalued, so that short selling leads to a more efficient system of securities price formation, but taking into account differences between member states and the potential economic impact of the rules, and without unduly reducing the benefits of short selling for the quality and efficiency of markets.

in writing. − despite being one of the richest regions in the world, the european union has over 80 million people at risk of poverty, including 20 million children, or 8% of the working population. this situation is incompatible with the european values of justice and solidarity enshrined in the treaties. the european platform against poverty and social exclusion is one of the seven flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy and aims to propose to the member states a work plan to achieve the main objective of reducing by 2020 the number of people in precarious situations by 20 million. in recent years, poverty and social exclusion have increased despite the union's efforts, while the consequences of the recent economic and financial crisis have further aggravated the problem, putting pressure on the most vulnerable sections of the population. in my view, since poverty is a multifactor phenomenon, it requires an integrated response that actively involves various levels of public authorities, both at european and local level. although the fight against poverty and social exclusion is essentially a matter for national governments, the union can and must play an important role in raising awareness of the problem, coordinating and financing action to combat poverty.
in writing. - the european platform against social exclusion contains proposals which i do not share, as they envisage a commitment by the european union and the member states to support categories which do not represent the social emergency at this time of crisis. we are talking, as so often happens, about policies in favour of the roma and their social inclusion, when we are talking about an ethnic group which simply shows no desire to integrate into the social fabric of our societies. we are talking about guaranteeing quality accommodation for certain categories of migrants, forgetting that the national and community authorities should first of all take care of the many disadvantaged groups in our countries, the disadvantaged groups who are suffering the disastrous effects of the current economic crisis, such as the elderly, young couples, and so on. these are the people who really should be helped by making every possible financial effort, before throwing away hundreds of millions of euros as has been done in recent years to pursue ghostly goals, such as the inclusion of the roma. my vote is against the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the daerden report, which stresses a very worrying aspect of the current economic crisis. in recent years, there has been an increase in the number of eu citizens in economic difficulties: there are over 80 million people at risk of poverty, of whom 20 million are children. despite the concrete european commitment, poverty and social exclusion are increasing considerably, obviously affecting the weakest sections of society. that is why i voted in favour of this report. while recognizing that the fight against poverty is essentially a matter for the states, there is no doubt that the union must play an active and more decisive role in raising awareness, coordinating and financing, since poverty reduction is a driver for growth. in the context of the eu 2020 strategy, which aims to reduce the number of economically vulnerable eu citizens by 20 million, integrated responses involving all institutions, from europe to individual countries and territories, are needed, promoting innovation, optimising european funds and improving the efficiency of social protection. to ensure sustainable growth, the most vulnerable must be placed at the heart of the european project.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i strongly believe in the need to tackle such a social scourge in a coherent way. eradicating poverty and preventing the social exclusion it causes is part of the tasks of each member state, which must protect the human rights of its citizens. parliament and the commission should therefore strengthen the political commitment made in the lisbon strategy, thus making a decisive impact in terms of poverty reduction. poverty is a problem which affects many aspects of an individual's social, economic and political life and i believe that an integrated approach can be an appropriate response to ensure that the needs of individuals are respected. in order to ensure non-discriminatory access to rights, services and resources, it is necessary to adopt certain measures to monitor member states in relation to the achievement of the targets set, to encourage the adoption of the open method of coordination, to create jobs and to provide for a minimum wage.
in writing. − the european platform against poverty and social exclusion, which is part of the wider objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, must be characterised by taking into account the peculiarity of a phenomenon which is itself complex, articulated and multifaceted and which, with the onset of the economic crisis, has assumed even more dramatic and worrying dimensions. the gradual expansion of the sectors affected or threatened by the consequences of the financial crisis into poverty or 'severe deprivation' requires a strengthening and differentiation of assistance. on the other hand, it is concerned about the distortive effects which, in this area too, may result from the unfortunate decision not to exclude investment by investment from the stability pact. the platform albeit in a context of scarcity of financial resources is a positive sign, in line with the need to develop, within the european framework, specific socioeconomic interventions capable, outside the mere logic of emergency or temporary support, of marking a structural reversal of the trend of the phenomenon. in particular, the importance of the desirable possibility of launching a global initiative for the introduction of a guaranteed minimum wage, an instrument which, if appropriate and conducive to economic development, will reduce and prevent poverty and social exclusion, is underlined.
in writing. − to achieve the ambitious target of reducing poverty and social exclusion for 20 million people by 2020, the european union must do more to raise awareness, coordinate and finance. i believe that european funds must be used more effectively and more effectively to combat the increase in discrimination and social exclusion which are often the direct cause and consequence of poverty. the fight against poverty cannot be separated from the fight against unemployment. however, i would like to stress that having a job is often not enough to ensure that people get out of poverty and that further action is therefore needed to combat the phenomenon of the working poor and to ensure access to quality and lasting employment. unfortunately, the european union today has over 80 million people at risk of poverty, which corresponds to 8% of the working population. we must confront this dramatically worsening situation by remembering that poverty is a shared responsibility and a challenge for society as a whole and should not be stigmatised or seen as a failure of individuals who are in economic difficulty or social exclusion.
