member of the commission. − mr president, that was really one of the most heated debates i have heard on development cooperation and that is why i will pick only a couple of issues that i think should be highlighted. in terms of financial volumes, 0.7% of gni is really a very small amount of money. and for new member states, it is only 0.33%. second, development aid is clearly a form of investment: investment in our security. to take just one example, the eu’s operation atalanta to combat piracy has cost, i am afraid, more than all the development aid that we have provided. the root causes of piracy are not to be found at sea, but on land. this is just one example. if people are dying from poverty, with no access to food, they will go out to rob others. so it is very clear where there is investment in people. we should also learn courage from our african friends. 200 soldiers, mostly from burundi but also from uganda, have died this year fighting and protecting the somali civilian population. 200 of them died, 800 are injured. what they say is that when there were difficult times in burundi, they got help. it is about solidarity. and if there is solidarity inside the european union, we should also have solidarity with the poorest nations in the world. to answer mr kelly’s question on ngos, we are rich because of our civil society. i know that there are a lot of issues such as whether ngos should be more streamlined, but i think ngos are an asset to our society. even if their activities are not always fully efficient, they are doing what they do from the heart and i do not think we should try to limit them. at the same time, the eu basically provides support through states where we can. where we cannot, ngos are the most effective mechanism to provide support for people on the ground. on differentiation, the agenda for change is very clear. there will only be support to the countries most in need. by developing the fight against poverty, we can increase our support to them. my last point is on john bufton’s comment: it is wrong. we are accountable for each euro. yes, the court of auditors and parliament’s budgetary control committee look at how we spend – and how we document – each and every euro. there is what we call an ‘error rate’, but for these operations we put all the preconditions in place to monitor each euro spent and ensure that it is spent according to the needs, and to the benefit, of the poorest people.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, we should be proud of our assistance and positive example. the european union has brought other donors to this table where we share what we have. we should be proud that other countries – emerging economies – are joining the team of those who are supporting countries in need, and supporting people in need. this is especially true today. two weeks before busan, we should concentrate on effectiveness – on effectiveness in the investment sense. yes, this is investment. countries like poland understand that foreign support can be investment, enabling countries to become stable and independent. this is how we in the council see our official development assistance. we would like to support those who can achieve stability later on. certainly it is extremely important to share, and discuss, values and rules with the new donors. busan, and our joint position for busan, will be the space where we can discuss the rules with new donors. one of the most important rules, especially for us in the european union and in the council, is the issue of transparency. given that we are spending public money, first of all we should be transparent on our side. on the other hand, we expect this transparency also on the recipient side. we discussed this in the council yesterday. when we think about budget support, we discuss the responsibilities on their side, and what kind of conditionality we should apply when placing so much trust in a country to support the budget directly at sectoral level. we also understand that if we do not invest in development we will be forced to provide humanitarian assistance. we see this situation in the horn of africa. we see that the lack of resilience in local communities leads to famine – a situation which should not be happening at this time. unfortunately, it is happening precisely because there is not enough development, and we cannot provide effective support to these communities and these countries. finally, in response to mr berman’s comment, yes, we should support entrepreneurship. this is exactly where the key to development lies: in finding a way to empower local partners and local communities, with our support, to set off on the path to development. to sum up, i would like to say again that we should be proud of what we have done, and we should share with others the values and the standards we try to uphold. finally, when it comes to innovative financial instruments, we need them both for ourselves, to support our economies, but also to support those who are in need, especially when we are talking about our neighbourhood in africa. this is really also about our security. without development in these regions, we will also be in trouble. this is why we should try to build solidarity with the new donors to provide reasonable assistance to these countries.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the text on the work of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, which, thanks to the quality of its work, has established itself as a key player in cooperation between the north and the south of the world. as a member of that assembly, i myself participated in the meetings held in brussels and in the work carried out in tenerife in april 2010 and in kinshasa, congo, in december of that year. it was precisely through these visits that i was able to see firsthand, as i did in 2009 in angola, the sad conditions experienced by certain peoples on a daily basis and, at the same time, to assess the efforts made by the acp to improve things. in conclusion, i would therefore like to stress at a particular historical and political moment, especially for the countries of north africa and the middle east, how the role played by the acp has been of fundamental importance, especially in the context of the supervision of the negotiations for economic partnership agreements, favouring the transparency of these processes and the development of disadvantaged local realities.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the proposal which aims to strengthen the sense of belonging of citizens to the european union on the basis of common elements of history and heritage, as well as awareness of diversity, and to intensify intercultural dialogue. i think it is extremely positive that initiatives such as the recognition of european heritage are being encouraged, which aim to bring citizens closer to the idea of belonging to a europe that unites us. the concept of europe often remains vague and the national one still tends to prevail. the european cultural heritage label has a special character: the commission considers that the exemption from the obligation to provide information on the historical value of a monument is justified by the fact that the information provided by the member states is not sufficient to demonstrate the historical importance of a monument, indicates that this site has an important role for european culture and explicitly emphasises the intangible value of the monument as a bearer of a historical and cultural message. it differs from other distinctions in this field that refer to the extraordinary historical, cultural or artistic value of the object by its materiality. of course, this does not mean that the historical substance of a monument is irrelevant, it is precisely this that makes it authentic through the physical tradition to convey in a convincing way the immaterial importance of the place, in short a symbol in relation to values and ideas such as democracy, freedom and diversity.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i personally find it interesting to have a european heritage label. at a time when, because of the continuing economic crisis, a certain euroscepticism is taking hold in many member states, i believe that an initiative of this kind can strengthen the sense of belonging of european citizens to the union. the characteristic element of the european brand is not the beauty of a site, but the symbolic value that it has represented or represents for the integration of european citizens on the path towards a better intercultural dialogue.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i supported the rapporteur's position because i believe it is useful to simplify and facilitate a process which will allow the real and genuine promotion of the territory in all the member states, a potential moment of tourist attraction, a valorization of sites of particular importance, in short a certain identification of the fundamental values of the community in which we live. the strict selection of projects for educational activities which are mainly aimed at young people is fine. the european heritage label certainly points the way forward, both in terms of the rediscovery and rehabilitation of sites, but at the same time in terms of the concrete and authentic enhancement of sites of civilisation and of the concrete testimonies to which our memory must always refer.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, europe and its history speak through the great achievements which have marked the civilization of our countries. much of europe's history is told through the streets, monuments and convents that made the path of the european peoples civilised in dark times. i share the approach of this measure which should of course perhaps be extended to countries waiting to join europe - i am referring to the countries of the western balkans - because i think it is appropriate to involve them in this project of identifying a european brand. i think their involvement would send a positive signal to them. i am glad that this measure has been adopted today by a large majority, and this gives me further confidence that the council will not put any further obstacles in the way of its rapid adoption.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the objective of promoting a european identity and of improving knowledge of our common history, especially among young people, is of fundamental importance, particularly at a political historical juncture such as the present one. in order to achieve this, i voted in favour of mrs paliadeli's report, in which i fully agree with the criteria for the identification of sites, which i believe should be transnational and should take place every two years, thus improving the quality of the process. finally, i fully agree with the role of this parliament, which will be duly involved in the process of selecting the sites selected. the european parliament has also long supported the development of this brand, first in its 2007 resolution on tourism and then in its 2008 resolution on a european agenda for culture in a globalised world.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i have supported the proposal for a directive on the implementation of a free and single european railway area. i am convinced that only the opening up of markets can improve the quality of the supply of rail transport for passengers and goods in europe. i am particularly pleased that article 32 has been adopted, because rail transport also causes noise. this is mainly due to the quality of the rolling stock, particularly in freight transport, where some completely outdated wagons are used. the resistance of the population to this noise is growing, and this is also likely to threaten the shift of goods transport, especially from road to rail. we must therefore take urgent action to reduce noise pollution. noise has to cost money, and i think the approach of article 32 is going in that direction. i hope that now with the council a rapid agreement can be reached on this point too.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report has been passed by a very large majority in this parliament. i voted for it, but i would have liked to have voted for something different, something more courageous. i think that parliament has not taken advantage of the opportunity to go further. it is true that the single railway area can and must mean a much better relationship with consumers than we have had so far. but why stop at the single national regulator and not move towards a single european regulator? why stop at the question of unbundling, i.e. the clear separation of ownership and management of services? the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we shall only be able to change the fate of the goods route, to improve the lives of people, to improve the lives of the free movement of goods when this single european area is useful. after all, staying off the tracks is better for your health than economic policy, because maybe if you stand too close to a track, the train will run over you.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the revision of the first railway package is of the utmost importance in order to create a truly european railway area, which is more competitive, modern and efficient. we certainly expected a more ambitious final text in the face of a not very courageous position on the part of the commission. we are bringing home a more effective national regulator, which must fully fulfil its market control function, and greater clarity on financial management. we are therefore calling for a new directive on the separation of the infrastructure manager from the railway operator and on the opening up of the market. i believe that the liberalisation of the railway market, and in particular the opening up of national markets to non-national carriers, is a necessary condition for the modernisation of the european railway system, which will ensure that our citizens can move as comfortably as possible and without distorting competition between national markets. i can only stress the negative impact of the rejection of the amendment which sought to introduce a distinction between light maintenance and ordinary maintenance as opposed to heavy maintenance. a maintenance centre should not be obliged to provide heavy maintenance to all railway operators, because responsibility is at stake here, the principle of safety, which has also proved to be a very sensitive issue for european rail transport in recent incidents. i hope that in the next negotiations with the council a more ambitious position can be reached.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too voted in favour of this document because i accepted the thesis that 'a general test on liberalization is better than nothing' as the headline of finanza e mercati, a well-known italian business daily. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is already beginning to take account of the guidelines introduced and launched with the 2011 white paper on transport, but it is not able to go all the way, it is not able to express its courage to the maximum. as other colleagues have also pointed out, the rail transport sector has not grown since 2001, to the benefit of road transport, which is now showing a worrying level of saturation. i believe that with this decision today we are taking a step forward, especially in the introduction of new instruments for the regulation and financing of the transport system, but there is still a long way to go and unfortunately we will have to wait until the end of 2012 for decisions on real liberalization.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the railway sector has always been a special context in which the competitive logic promoted by the single market and the european union has been slow to take hold. the deficit in services offered to citizens in this sector is linked to this delay. i believe that more transparent and easier market access conditions, together with explicit rules on conflict of interest and discriminatory practices in the railway sector, are the appropriate measures to encourage more competition. i fully agree with the legislative proposal on the obligation to separate completely the infrastructure managers from the transport service companies, i.e. the railway companies. i would ask the commission to submit concrete proposals within the time limits set. i believe that the measures contained in the report will make it easier to provide rail services and improve the quality of services for passengers and freight users. the report by my colleague gives concrete answers to the call for greater liberalization and competition in the railway sector and i have given my full support to it.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is essential to halt the decline of rail transport by reforming it, paying particular attention to the right of european citizens to mobility. it is essential that passenger trains are able to transport disabled people in a dignified manner and at a reasonable price. it is therefore appropriate to establish minimum quality rules for railway wagons, to ensure that timetables and coincidences are respected, and to allow free competition between operators in order to maintain moderate ticket prices. we must insist that the major european infrastructure for high-speed freight and passenger transport be built. given the positive outcome on the cost allocation for the construction of the third crossing rotterdam corridor and the tav turin-lyon corridor and their inclusion in the ten major works recognised as necessary by the european union, work must begin as soon as possible. as regards the obligation to separate infrastructure managers from incumbent railway undertakings, which traditionally own the infrastructure, it is appropriate to provide for compensation for the costs incurred.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the scope of the liberalized market remains unchanged from that provided for by the existing legislation and covers all rail transport services, with the sole exception of passenger services with a national scope. the demand we have made with all our strength was that the scope of liberalization should be extended to this market segment as soon as possible. the amendments proposed to this effect commit the commission to present, by 2012, specific legislation on the obligation of complete separation between infrastructure managers and transport undertakings, together with a proposal to extend the scope of liberalisation to rail passenger services operated at national level. in a liberalised market, which is the natural endpoint of the liberalisation process initiated by the european legislator, there is no doubt that the complete separation of the infrastructure manager from the railway undertakings is a basic prerequisite for the optimal functioning of the competitive mechanisms. i also hope that the delays will be liberalized, so that the delays which accumulate in some countries such as mine, once liberalized, will spread and be shared among all the european countries and perhaps some, like italy, will gain in punctuality.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the resolution on the forthcoming un international conference in durban because i believe that the challenge of climate change due to global warming requires, now more than ever, a very strong commitment on the part of europe. the climate disruption caused by global warming is backed by overwhelming scientific evidence, and the resulting environmental, human and economic damage is now in plain sight. reality forces us to make quick and courageous choices. europe must maintain a leading role in the fight against global warming, with a commitment to help other countries in terms of technologies and resources. we must also recover these resources by introducing a tobin tax on international financial transactions. durban must lead to a legally binding international agreement with concrete results for the fight against global warming and above all it must produce a clear timetable with precise deadlines and commitments for all countries of the world. all countries must finally put their own particular interests ahead of the collective interests because either we commit ourselves, or we all pay a very high price. these are challenging, very important and compulsory choices, because there is no plan b yet.
mr president, the resolution voted this morning calls on the european union to come to the negotiating table with a commitment to reduce emissions by more than 20% by 2020, regardless of the outcome of the international negotiations. as is well known, there is no prospect of reaching a global agreement in durban. the european commission has said that the earliest possible date for a comprehensive agreement could be 2015 and that a transition period would be in place until then. i believe that the international context does not allow us to go beyond the objectives already set. the european union already has a commitment after 2012, namely to reduce emissions by 20%, as provided for in the climate and energy package. the european union further confirms its willingness to sign a second commitment period only as part of a transition to a comprehensive climate treaty that requires agreement by all countries on a timetable and roadmap. commissioner hedegaard herself said that it would be a strategic mistake for the european union to sign a second kyoto commitment without the participation of other economies. moreover, it is known that some major economies have already declared that they will not sign a kyoto 2.
mr president, in december 2009 i attended cop15 in copenhagen as an official member of the european parliament delegation. it is with regret that i say that the work done and the commitments made in copenhagen and formalised in cancún will not be enough to achieve the objective of limiting the increase in the average annual temperature of our planet to two degrees celsius. some large emitters, such as japan and russia, seem to be evading their commitments, while others do not seem to be giving the problem of climate change the right priority. today, while i am voting in favour, i am aware that only with the strong and unwavering will of the heads of state and government of the world can we create the conditions for a comprehensive international agreement.

in writing. - mr president, i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the european heritage label because it strengthens the sense of belonging of european citizens to the union. the brand certainly adds value to the sites to which it is assigned. the latter will have to have a symbolic value for the integration and history of the european union and will be identified on voluntary application in relation to the activities and the educational dimension they offer, especially for young people. the identification of sites that are emblematic of europe's common history and heritage will strengthen european identity, including through cooperation instruments that will foster intercultural dialogue, the exchange of ideas, projects and good practices, and a relationship of solidarity for the benefit of the whole of europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the european heritage label. when we speak of culture at european level, we are referring to the individual cultural experiences of the various member states, while we rarely refer to the common heritage, that is to say the european heritage, which goes beyond the boundaries of individual national 'stories'. the european brand, in this respect, is a key initiative that bears witness to europe's common roots, regardless of the sites of the past. the european label will therefore strengthen the cohesion, visibility and credibility of the whole of europe by defining clear and rigorous selection criteria and will be awarded every two years after approval by an authoritative and independent committee. the metric of judgment will not be the beauty of the site, although it is the subject of evaluation, but its intrinsic and symbolic value, mainly concerning european integration. the european union's brand is therefore essential for the development of a cultural europe and not just a more economic and political one.

in writing. - the report by mr paliadeli was voted on today in plenary. following the decision taken today, 16 november, a european heritage label will be available from 2013 on a voluntary basis to sites that are symbols of european history and integration. from 2013, each member state may propose up to two candidate sites every two years. the label will guarantee the quality of the selected sites, which may be natural, submerged, archaeological, industrial or urban monuments or sites, cultural landscapes, places of memory, cultural goods and objects or intangible heritage associated with a place. the label may also be awarded to contemporary heritage sites which are of relevance to the history and common heritage of europe, as well as for architectural or aesthetic merits. member states will be responsible for the management, protection and promotion of the sites. the commission will be responsible for the communication and sponsorship of the brand, including the creation of a dedicated website for the project and the promotion of networking activities for the branded sites.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because i consider it a highly significant gesture to give the possibility of awarding, from 2013 onwards and on a voluntary basis, a european heritage label to places that are symbols of the history and integration of the old continent. the label will guarantee the quality of the sites selected, which may be natural, submerged, archaeological, industrial or urban monuments or sites, cultural landscapes or places of memory. this decision is another arrow in our bow to safeguard, promote and protect the wealth of europe, the importance of which is often underestimated.
in writing. − the first railway package adopted in 2001 was an attempt, unfortunately unsuccessful, to halt the decline of rail transport. the whole system has failed to catch up with other modes of transport, such as road transport, and the data confirms this. between 1996 and 2008, rail freight transport decreased by around 2-10,8%, while road freight transport increased from 42,1% to 45,9%. the causes are varied. transnational rail services face many technical, legal and political obstacles unlike road services. the commission has also taken the view that the aid should be limited to the minimum necessary to ensure that the aid is compatible with the common market. the railway system needs strong support, also in the light of the co2 reduction pursued by europe, which retains considerable growth potential while, on the contrary, road transport shows increasing signs of oversaturation. the report therefore has the merit of promoting the creation of an integrated and global european railway area. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i too want to join, not out of practice but out of conviction, in thanking my colleagues for the work they have done, a complex work but one whose result, i think, we can all be pleased with, especially as regards the development of a new concrete action plan. in this respect i have welcomed and supported the proposal for the reform of the comprehensive and integrated european railway area, because it lays the foundations for overcoming the limits imposed by the interests defined at national level in the sector and aims at last at the construction of a truly european railway area in which passengers and goods can cross borders without complications. the report sends a very clear message to our governments: coordinated action is necessary to ensure effective and rigorous enforcement of safety standards. compliance with new safety requirements should therefore play a more important role when operators apply for a licence and the commission should therefore collect more data. i sincerely hope that this impetus will enable the railway market to make our economy more efficient and more competitive in terms of resources.
in writing. − the first railway package adopted in 2001 sought to reform the european regulatory framework and aimed to ensure the integration of the sector, improving its attractiveness compared to other modes of transport. unfortunately, after ten years, we can sadly see that this first reform has not been able to bring about any significant improvement in the situation of the railways. rail transport has not been able to catch up with other modes of transport, in particular road transport. one of the main reasons is the discrepancies in national rules and the incorrect implementation of the first railway package by many member states, many of which ended up neglecting rail financing while providing maximum support to road infrastructure. the current system has revealed its shortcomings. the rules therefore need to be strengthened and harmonised and new elements need to be added to make railways a more attractive mode of transport for passengers and goods. we therefore support this report because, with its revisions, it sets itself the ambitious goal of achieving a comprehensive and integrated european railway area, a genuine european railway area in which passengers and goods can cross borders without problems.
in writing. the distance between the railway sector and the other transport sectors must be bridged urgently. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the 2001 railway package is no longer sufficient.
in writing. − rail transport has not yet fully developed its potential at european level. there is still too much fragmentation and lack of competition, which results in a disadvantage for all citizens who would like to use this safe, economical and environmentally friendly means of transport. the increasing interconnections in european mobility require greater harmonisation between the different regulations, with the ultimate aim of benefiting the users of the service, i.e. passengers, through reduced fares and the guarantee of easier travel within the different countries of the european union. the report sets out these and other shared priorities, and that is why i have decided to vote in favour.

this regulation we can do something, and that is what we are trying to do now. to make our framework even stronger, i plan to introduce two specific elements in the future european maritime and fisheries fund. first, conditionality. no subsidy can be granted to operators involved in illegal fishing. this will be a rule: absolute conditionality. second, financial correction. subsidies granted to such operators will be withdrawn. we need these clear rules to fill the existing gaps. i also subscribe to ms lövin’s views that illegal fishing activities by their very nature are in fact criminal activities. countries need to cooperate with each other in investigations, proceedings, and ultimately prosecutions if we want to actively combat these ‘pirate’ actions. as a final point, the eu as the biggest player in this market has a moral obligation to take the lead in this fight. i am looking forward to continue working with parliament and all stakeholders in order to best shape our role. use taxpayers’ money in the best way in order to have concrete results.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is so widespread at international level that it is impossible to estimate precisely how many tonnes of fish are caught illegally every day. as already acknowledged by the fao in 2001 with the adoption of an action plan against illegal fishing, the fight against this phenomenon is a priority for the international community. this phenomenon causes serious environmental, economic and social damage and, as the united nations report on drugs and crime also shows, is often carried out by real criminal organizations that commit crimes such as tax evasion, customs fraud, money laundering, bribery and bribery. the european union, with its regulations on unreported and uncontrolled fishing and on community control regimes, has provided itself with effective instruments to combat this phenomenon by defining obligations and opportunities for both member states and third countries. it is therefore important that joint action be taken at world level by all states, not just the european ones. to achieve this, the european union must first of all behave in an exemplary manner, taking all necessary measures, including against the member states themselves, to combat these illegal actions. i think it is useful to continue and even improve the various surveillance programmes in the developing countries. it is necessary to implement all the measures clearly identified in mrs lövin's report, which i commend, and which lead to closer cooperation, both at the legislative and operational level, in the various regional fisheries organisations. mr president, i conclude by saying that it is essential that the european union takes the necessary initiatives at multilateral and global level because, as is clear to everyone, this is a problem that the european union cannot solve alone.

in writing. the rome statute marked a major step forward in the field of international human rights protection. it is a fundamental turning point. for the first time it is possible to prosecute individuals found guilty of certain international crimes. until then, the main supranational judicial body had been the un international court of justice in the hague, which was set up specifically to ensure the "peaceful settlement of international disputes", and thus interstate ones. the parties involved were therefore the states, and the concept of international individual responsibility was not yet clearly defined. under the rome statute, the icc has jurisdiction in relation to war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide cases, for which individuals are held and possibly found responsible. with the establishment of the international criminal court, the international community seems to be moving towards greater responsibility, by gradually abandoning a culture of impunity. the fact that an international body can, by applying the principle of aut dedere aut iudicare, systematically and automatically replace national courts in criminal jurisdiction, the quintessential expression of national sovereignty, is therefore a revolutionary fact.

in writing. − i voted for this resolution because our parliament must take a clear position against the use of cluster munitions. with this text we call on the council and the commission to include the ban on cluster munitions as a standard clause in agreements with third countries. cluster munitions represent serious risks to civilians and, in post-conflict settings, the use of these munitions has caused many tragic injuries to, and deaths of, civilians. as we unfortunately know, unexploded sub-munitions left behind are often found by children and other unsuspecting innocents. for this reason, member states should not endorse the draft text of protocol vi on cluster munitions to the convention on the use of certain conventional weapons. this draft protocol would only ban pre-1980 cluster munitions and threatens to undermine the clear and robust international humanitarian law standard established by the convention on cluster munitions (ccm), ratified by 22 eu member states, which comprehensively bans cluster munitions.

in writing. - cluster munitions are a large and growing problem. if such weapons can be further spread in terms of their use and who uses them, they will represent an even greater humanitarian and development challenge than landmines were in the 1990s. cluster munitions are designed to explode on impact with the ground. however, the failure rates are related not only to technical factors but also to the ground conditions and the height from which they are launched. it follows that if the submunitions do not work as intended, they will be deposited in the ground, becoming particularly dangerous, since they can explode at the slightest touch or movement. in fact, unexploded ordnance acts like land mines. the essential question has long been whether the production and use of cluster munitions constitutes a violation of international law. i am glad that the resolution voted this morning by the european parliament provides an answer to the question: i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter.

in writing. − the own-initiative report is on a topic of importance for the conservation of biodiversity and the health of marine fauna; i am not going to go into the details of the commission's proposals, but i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to put forward a proposal for a regulation on the common fisheries policy. moreover, the phenomenon is increasingly linked to other activities which are dangerous to peace and to the stability of civil coexistence among men. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be given the opportunity to present their opinions on the draft directive on the protection of the marine environment. i therefore welcome this report, as well as others on the same subject and with the same approach, because the eu must contribute to the efforts of the international community to combat iuu fishing by calling on itself and the member states to do everything possible to eradicate a criminal phenomenon, a criminal one that puts the survival of the marine ecosystem at risk and indirectly threatens international security.
in writing. - illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is a huge damage to the whole system: several surveys show alarming figures, with no less than 15% of the world's catches reportedly coming from illegal activities. this fact makes it clear that, even from an economic point of view, this reality has become unsustainable. regular fishing also contributes to the respect and maintenance of appropriate criteria for marine environmental sustainability. it is easy to see how illegal fishing is difficult to trace back to the maritime borders of a single state, but often involves much larger areas, and therefore increasingly joint action and cooperation is needed. i also believe that the establishment of a 'european coast guard', as indicated in the report, could increase the common monitoring and inspection capacity and effectively combat current and future threats at sea, such as illegal fishing, but also terrorism, piracy, trafficking and marine pollution. the report under discussion touches on all these and many other important aspects, and that is why i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. the report by mr lövin, which proposes to strengthen inspections, close markets to illegal fishing and impose sanctions on states which do not comply with the rules in force, was voted on today at the strasbourg plenary session. i believe that international action is necessary, because two thirds of the world's waters are outside any jurisdiction and the fleets of fishing vessels are mobile and often do not comply with regulations. the eu, as the world's largest fishing power, should take responsibility for mobilising the international community to this end. it is estimated that about 15% of the world's fisheries, between 11 and 26 million tonnes a year, are illegal. therefore, as the resolution states, it is impossible to defend marine resources without combating illegal fishing. the new measures should include mandatory registration of fishing vessels above 10 gt, the development of document retrieval systems, the mandatory use of electronic vessel monitoring systems (vms), the exchange of information on vessel activities, import controls and an agreement on the closure of illegally caught fish markets.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this measure because illegal international fishing is undermining efforts to conserve and manage fisheries resources in all the world's seas. this not only has serious consequences for food security and environmental protection, but also leads to the loss of economic and social opportunities in the short and long term. illegal fishing can lead to the collapse of a fishing zone, seriously undermining efforts to restore depleted fish stocks. the current international instruments to combat this phenomenon have so far been ineffective due to a lack of political will, priorities, capacity and resources to ratify them. the european union has a very important specific responsibility in this respect, as it is the largest market for fishery products in the world and one of the major powers in this sector.
in writing. − illegal fishing undermines efforts to conserve and manage fish stocks in all catch zones. this may make it impossible for national and regional fisheries management organisations to achieve management objectives. this situation leads to the loss of economic and social opportunities in the short and long term, as well as negative impacts on food security and environmental protection. the european union has, with its new legislation, equipped itself with the tools to combat illegal fishing. the union must first set an example in order to persuade other states to take action. the existing regional fisheries management organisations have significant differences in their approach to illegal fishing and the legal measures, including sanctions, applied to combat it. the global nature of fishing means that most of the measures to combat fishing must be implemented between regional organisations. finally, the european union could support existing global initiatives and propose new ones at the same time.
in writing. - 26 million tonnes a year, an exorbitant figure! the volume of illegal fishing has reached record levels, equivalent to 15% of catches, and is now the largest market in the world for fish products. it is therefore clear that the european union, through appropriate diplomatic action, must introduce the necessary measures to improve transparency and to curb the proliferation of illegal fishing. for these reasons i voted in favour of mrs lövin's text.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the situation is getting worse and it is time to act with the timeliness and efficiency that have been lacking so far. it would be useless and counterproductive to rely on the thaumaturgical effect of the announcement of a reform of the treaties. the adventurous path of an intergovernmental treaty would have devastating consequences for the markets. the reform of the treaties is too long; the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. the truth is that the problem facing the eu today is a political problem and not an institutional one. the current treaty can strengthen economic convergence, fiscal discipline, safeguard the stability of the euro area and boost growth. the two new proposals for regulations submitted by the commission demonstrate this, and with that legal basis, article 136, it is possible to go even further, also with regard to the role of the court of justice of the european union. the flexibility clause would allow the eurozone to increase its powers and article 122 (2) is an appropriate basis for that extraordinary eurobond debt redemption fund devised by the german council of economic experts. in short, there is a feeling that the reform of the treaties is being sought in order to avoid codecision, to have less europe and no more. there is no excuse for this, we must act now and lay the foundations for the full implementation, with the consent of the citizens, of a fiscal union based on stability, growth, solidarity and democracy, which is the basis for that reform of the treaties, which is too important an objective to be compromised by a clumsy and untimely reform, which would be legally useless, economically insignificant and politically harmful today.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, we are indeed entering a critical period of ten days to complete a comprehensive and effective response to the crisis by the european union. european citizens are calling for decisive action from leaders in order to protect sustainable growth and employment and in order to counter the contagion that is currently going on in the financial markets, which is threatening our jobs and growth. this means that countries under market pressure need to continue to put their fiscal house in order and reform their economies to generate growth and jobs. this work is going on, not only in the ‘programme countries’, but more recently, for instance in belgium and italy with new governments, new budgets and/or other new perspectives. in parallel we must reinforce our economic governance and strengthen massively our financial firewalls to counter the speculation in the markets. to be credible and effective these efforts must be based on the community method. that is the commission’s position on how to tackle the crisis. we need to work on all relevant fronts. yes, the decisions of the eurozone summit of october need to be fully implemented. that is a necessary, even if not sufficient, condition of overcoming the crisis. as to the treaty-change debate, let us be clear on that. a treaty change cannot offer an immediate contribution to the solution of the current crisis. but it is true that reinforcing fiscal prudence and economic surveillance, in the euro area in particular, may help to prevent any future fiscal crisis. thus it matters to the confidence in the construct of the euro, which has been questioned in recent weeks. in the meantime, the commission has taken the initiative and we have proposed new legislation that will strengthen economic governance significantly. we have done that within the scope of the current treaty. the two regulations which i introduced today, based on article 136, will ensure closer monitoring of fiscal and economic policies. they add another building block onto the economic and fiscal union and especially onto tighter fiscal surveillance based on the ‘six-pack’ legislation which you have recently approved. i sensed yesterday in the euro group and today in the ecofin meeting of finance ministers that there is strong support for these proposals – and even going beyond these proposals – among the ministers. i trust that is also the case here in the european parliament. concerning our financial firewalls, the euro group yesterday took important decisions on the leveraging of the efsf and thus reinforcing the financial firewalls. these have already been welcomed by several market participants, including the institute of international finance. in the very short term – or rather immediate term – this work must continue and we must consider further means to reinforce this leveraging effect, for instance through increasing resources available from the imf for the european union. in the longer – or rather already medium term – the green paper on stability bonds lays out credible options which to a different extent, depending on the option considered, could bring us closer to a fiscal union, could protect us better against speculative attacks, and would also reassure markets to have confidence in the credibility of the euro. let me underline again – as i said in the committee on economic and monetary affairs a few days ago and i have said several times before other compositions of the parliament – the necessary condition for considering any serious move towards eurobonds or stability bonds is a further and very substantial reinforcement of economic governance to ensure fiscal discipline and economic stability, in fact to build a real fiscal union or an ever-closer economic union. the european council will at this critical juncture need to take bold and determined action to reverse the current negative dynamics in the financial markets. it calls for immediate decisions both to ensure fiscal consolidation and growth-boosting reforms in the member states. it calls for further reinforcement of our financial firewalls and for a road map on how to further reinforce economic governance and in parallel to put in place new stability instruments and thus to create a true economic union. our citizens expect us to do whatever is needed in order to protect jobs and growth and we can best do it by deeper economic integration in europe.

european central bank. − mr president, thanks to all the honourable members of the european parliament for their statements and their contributions. let me say at the very beginning that i look forward to sharing views and to exchanging opportunities to look together at the present situation and to reflect together at this very difficult contingency. i think many of your statements really come under one heading: how do we reconstruct confidence in the euro in the euro area? this process will have three pillars: the first one is what i called the setting of an anchor in the long term. this redesign of the fiscal rules, of the fiscal compact – meaning by this word an agreement of new fiscal rules – is necessary to create trust for all countries who are members of the euro area. this design has not been completed. i think the next few days will be very important in telling us whether we will make any progress on this path. this is very important because, as i said, this gives the long-term trust which is necessary for the other two pillars. by the way, for the second pillar, which is the design of a financing mechanism within the euro area, we have the efsf. it is a design in which we have to put our confidence that it will work, but some steps are still needed, as we all know. the third pillar is the national economic policy response and frankly we are seeing much improvement on that front. as i said before, i do believe that countries are nowadays on track. we see a good future but we have to be aware that in the end what matters is the delivery of the proposed reforms. reforms – i do not want to be misunderstood – do not have to be focused only on the budget and budgetary issues; they also have to be structural reforms, reforms that enhance competitiveness and growth. so these are the three pillars upon which confidence can be reconstructed. i have been asked: what is the role of the ecb in all this? some of you said the ecb should do more; some of you said the ecb should do less. let me start by saying the ecb can act within the treaty so the ecb should not be asked to do things that are not within the treaty. the ecb is the lender of last resort for solvent banks. the ecb has created an enormous amount of liquidity and we see that this liquidity is now being redeposited with the ecb deposit facility, which means that it is not so much the amount of liquidity that matters, but it is the fact that this liquidity is not actually circulating through the banking channel, through the financial system, through the credit channel. in our view, the most important thing now for the ecb is to repair the credit channel in a way that enables this liquidity to actually finance the real economy – especially the small and medium-sized enterprises which are now in difficult conditions because they are the ones who mostly need the banks’ credit. the large corporations are on average, generally speaking, able to access capital markets on their own, so they are less dependent on the banks. that is why we have to make sure that a credit channel will start to work again. we have observed serious credit tightening in the most recent period which, combined with a weakening of the business cycle, does not bode at all well for the months to come. i think this is one of the first things. also, some of you mentioned the smp, the securities market programme, should be more active, less active. let me say – and i did say this a moment ago – that the rationale for having the smp active is that you want to make sure that you repair the monetary policy transmission channels. it is not to create liquidity, it is not to subsidise governments; it is to repair the monetary policy transmission channels. that was the rationale with which it started and that is still the rationale with which we employ it. by itself it is a non-standard measure and therefore by itself it is going to be temporary, it is going to be limited. let me be clear about what i mean by limited. it is not eternal and it is not infinite. we have to understand that the ecb can act within the treaty. it would be a mistake to have the ecb acting outside the treaty; it would not be legal and it would also be a mistake because it would, especially in some parts of europe, undermine the credibility of the ecb, which nowadays is the strongest signature in the euro area. i take the words on communication with great pleasure. it is true always, but especially in this situation of extreme difficulty, that it does not really make any sense to have a cacophony of voices anticipating monetary policy decisions, reflecting individual views and not the collegial decision-making process. i could not agree more. i will certainly take this message to the rest of the governing council, but, as i said, these are opportunities and occasions that are cherished very much and i will continue cherishing them. i am very much looking forward to my next meeting with the european parliament, which is going to be in a few days with the committee on economic and monetary affairs. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the activation of the stability instrument once again highlights the crucial need for ever greater flexibility in the budget of the european union. at the same time, despite the modest increase in the commitment appropriations of certain budget lines and the numerous reductions in the appropriations of other budget lines, the ceilings for subheading 1a and heading 4 do not suffice to finance certain priorities set by parliament and the council. in the framework of the general budget of the union for the financial year 2012, the flexibility instrument is therefore used to provide the sum of eur 30,75 million in commitment appropriations in subheading 1a and eur 208,67 million in commitment appropriations in heading 4. the activation of the flexibility instrument for the financing of the eu 2020 strategy will therefore commit a total amount of eur 239,42 million. we are satisfied with these figures and that is why we have voted.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, after 15 hours of constructive negotiations, the 2012 budget is closed with a level of payment appropriations approved of eur 129.08 billion, corresponding to the amount adopted by the council in its position of last july. the commitment appropriations amount to eur 147.23 billion, almost eur 1 billion more than the council's position. during the negotiations, when it became clear that there would be no room for manoeuvre on payment appropriations, given that the delegations of the member states had explained the difficulties in paying national budgets, the european parliament's approach was based on the level of commitments, with particular reference to competitiveness and external relations. that is why i support this 2012 budget which, given the period of economic and financial difficulties, has nevertheless found a broad solution in the competitiveness chapter, for example by looking at innovation and investments useful for a future european recovery. i would like to conclude by recalling that for the first time since the new procedure was introduced under the lisbon treaty, an agreement was reached within the conciliation deadline.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report which the ecb has presented to us today contains some very interesting data: in 2010 the ecb recorded a gross profit of eur 1 334 million; the decrease compared to the previous year is due, on the one hand, to the reduction in net interest income due to lower interest rates on both the main refinancing operations of the eurosystem and on official reserves denominated in us dollars and, on the other hand, to the fact that no gold sales were made in 2010. the governing council decided to transfer an amount of eur 1 163 million to the reserve fund by 31 december 2010, thus reaching its current maximum allowable limit. the ecb thus closed the year with a net profit of eur 171 million, which the governing council decided to distribute in full to the national central banks of the euro area countries. the reserve fund is intended to cover exchange rate, interest rate, credit and gold price risks, and its size and the need to maintain it are reviewed annually. the ecb's ordinary income consists of income generated by the investment of its official reserves and the portfolio held against its own funds, as well as from the interest accruing on the 8% share of the total value of euro banknotes in circulation allocated to the ecb and from the net interest accruing on the portfolios created for monetary policy purposes under the covered bond purchase programme and the securities market programme.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the mid-term review provided for in the regulations establishing the financial instruments has had the effect of bringing to light a substantial difference of opinion between the european parliament, the commission and the council on the procedures for approving multiannual cooperation programmes with developing countries. the distance between the two sides of the house made it necessary to convene a conciliation committee with a trilogue, which led to the formulation of the four compromise proposals. in the case of the instrument with industrialised countries, the amendment was designed to extend the geographical scope of ici programmes to emerging countries which are still beneficiaries of the traditional cooperation instrument. the most delicate aspect of the negotiations concerned parliament's request to include in the text of the regulations the specific financial allocations for each country or region, in monetary or percentage terms. for the council and the commission, these allocations can only be indicative and should not affect the allocation of funds by region and country by the council and the commission in accordance with the procedures in force.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the overriding objective of european union cooperation is the eradication of poverty in partner countries and regions in the context of sustainable development, including the pursuit of the millennium development goals, and the promotion of democracy, good governance and respect for human rights and the rule of law. its action plan for the development cooperation financing instrument includes support for acp countries which are party to the sugar protocol, geographical assistance programmes for south africa and forty-seven countries in latin america, asia and the middle east, and thematic programmes. in the multilateral field, the millennium declaration is the main reference point and its aim remains the halving of absolute poverty, that is, of those people living on less than a dollar a day by 2015. the european framework is an essential reference for development cooperation in each member state. one third of italy's official development aid is managed by the european commission in brussels, hence a strong vote in favour of this measure.

in writing. − we voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 on the structural funds to introduce a general definition of reimbursable aid. the regulation does not define whether aid is reimbursable or non-reimbursable, and article 44 contains only provisions relating to 'financial engineering instruments'. however, member states continued to use forms of reimbursable aid, building on the positive experience of the previous programming period. the definition of 'reimbursable aid' includes reimbursable grants (which are fully or partially reimbursable without interest) and credit lines managed by the managing authority through intermediary bodies (public financial institutions). in view of the increasing application in the field of financial engineering instruments referred to in article 44 and given that the commission has only limited information on such instruments so far, it was considered appropriate to amend the regulation to ensure that member states and the commission can properly monitor these forms of repayable aid and inform the commission thereof.

in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur and her colleague on having dealt with a subject which is necessary to deal with the difficult situation europe is facing in this report, for which i voted in favour. the continuing economic and financial crisis, which has a worrying impact on the macroeconomic stability and the budget of the member states, requires rapid action by providing additional financial resources for those member states in particular difficulty in order to ensure that the programmes continue to be implemented. the method chosen is to 'increase' by 10 percentage points the co-financing rates applicable to the priority axes of the programmes, thus increasing payments to the beneficiary countries. the proposed measures will be transitional and in force until the member state's withdrawal from the financial support mechanism, but a retroactive application of the regulation is necessary. i also share the rapporteur's view on the procedure for a transparent allocation of the surcharge: to this end, a comprehensive accounting of the use of transitionally increased payments is useful, without however increasing the administrative burden.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. we have all now realised that the peripheral debt crisis has turned into a new economic crisis in the euro area, with a very negative impact on the macroeconomic stability and the budget of the member states. the european commission's proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 (the general regulation) providing additional financial resources in other eu member states experiencing particular difficulties in managing their public debt and deficits, therefore aims to ensure fiscal stability by moving along slightly deviated but still right-oriented paths. the eurozone now needs a strong political message. i hope that the next eu summit meeting on 9 december will demonstrate the common will of all member states to cooperate in adopting very specific measures to overcome the crisis.
in writing. - it is impossible not to agree to support a measure which represents a real and substantial breath of fresh air for those member states which are experiencing the greatest economic and financial difficulties. similarly, we cannot but support a measure which is an attempt to maximise the use of european funding, avoiding the risk of it being left unspent because of the lack of financial availability in the member states, and the consequent further deterioration and weakening of economic and social conditions. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the introduction of a new system of financial stability in the euro area. however, this does not prevent us from stressing how much it is proof of the failure of the stability pact and the six-pack as desired and approved by the right-wing majority in the commission and in parliament. in particular, this 'quota' intervention is limited to mitigating the 'structural' effects of the vicious circle triggered, in particular, by the failure to exclude investment appropriations from the rigidity of the criteria of the stability pact, also due to the failure to introduce a golden rule on investment. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive.
in writing. - my vote on the hübner report is in favour. the cuts in national resources available to finance public investment have clearly become a constraint on the implementation of cohesion policy and the implementation of the structural funds in some countries. it is therefore necessary to provide member states with additional resources to optimise the management of public debt.
in writing. − on 1 december we voted on the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 to introduce an exceptional provision for certain member states in serious economic and financial difficulties. it is part of the package of extraordinary measures adopted by the european commission in august 2011, which became necessary in the light of the economic and financial crisis, which is putting increasing pressure on national financial resources, at a time when member states are making budgetary cuts. this creates a liquidity problem resulting from budgetary constraints, which jeopardises the implementation of cohesion policy programmes and the impact of such investments on the real economy. the purpose of this measure is to amend article 77 of the regulation in order to enable the commission, at the request of the member states concerned and after the council has decided to grant assistance under the support mechanisms, to increase by 10% the reimbursement of expenditure declared for the period in question, thus increasing the cofinancing rates applicable to the priority axes. this will not impose any additional financial burden on the general budget as the total financial allocations of the funds to the countries and programmes concerned for the overall period will remain unchanged.
in writing. the economic crisis we are facing, which is affecting the budgets of the member states every day, is being fought by the member states themselves through different forms of financing. financial stability, the main objective of every state, is in the balance and any proposal to guarantee it must be considered. i voted in favour of mrs hübner's text because it amends council regulation (ec) no 1260/1999 in such a way as to solve a dilemma faced by many of the member states which use the system of reimbursable grants, alongside structural fund contributions, as forms of direct aid. in the absence of a precise definition of reimbursable subsidies, it was not possible to establish the extent to which member states could refer to this form of aid without additional interest. the new text states that the structural funds may co-finance repayable aid.
in writing. - i support the amendment of decision 2002/546/ec as regards the extension of the period of application until 31 december 2013 because, due to the crisis, removing from a country such as spain the possibility of not paying a tax such as the aiem on products manufactured in the canary islands may further aggravate an already precarious situation. with this extension, the country will have an expiry date which will coincide with that of the guidelines on regional aid for the period 2007-2013. of course, the temporary and extraordinary measure must remain so.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs hübner's report because i believe it is important to give the outermost regions of the union equal opportunities to trade with the internal regions and therefore it is necessary to lower the level of excise duties for trade in specific products placed on the market by the outermost regions. this is a way of stimulating trade in these products while keeping the price in line with the demands of european markets. taking into account the special conditions and characteristics and the particular constraints of the outermost regions of the european union, the council will adopt specific measures to define the conditions for the application of these policies.
in writing. - in recent weeks, risk premia in italy have reached historic levels on the financial markets. despite recent tensions that may indicate otherwise, the euro has been a success since 2008: without the single currency the global financial crisis would have been far worse for all european countries, and furthermore, the northern european countries would not have recovered from it as quickly as they have since 2009, through their export-based model. there is a thought that even the academic world agrees on: without the euro, the single market and the free movement of people - the union's greatest achievements - would probably implode. i therefore believe that the euro has not failed in its function in the face of the effects of the severe economic and financial crisis but rather that there has been a problem of economic governance of the euro area. economic theory teaches that the feasibility of a single currency depends on the ability to minimise large economic imbalances, where they exist. it is precisely at these times of tension for the european project, of which our currency is a symbol, that the current failures in the euro area must be regarded as a valuable experience to avoid repeating the same mistakes.

in writing. - the financial crisis is bringing the euro area close to breaking up. country by country, bailout by bailout, the debt crisis threatens to generate a domino effect throughout europe. the euro has not failed as an integration mechanism for strengthening the single market. however, something definitely did not go as planned: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council. there is a lack of internal discipline in the euro area, particularly with regard to compliance with the stability and growth pact, since there have been dozens of violations by many countries since 1999 and no sanctions have ever been applied. for this reason, the euro area has become vulnerable to speculative attacks targeting the sovereign debt of the least efficient and competitive countries. we believe that the european monetary union has a duty to keep inflation under control and to safeguard the purchasing power of the currency. if the euro is to remain a viable project, a clear framework is needed, one that can help countries with liquidity problems, but at the same time be able to encourage fiscal responsibility and a lasting convergence of competitiveness levels between member countries.

in writing. - school dropout is a social issue that must be tackled. more than six million young people in the union leave school before completing secondary education. the average drop-out rate in the european union is 14%. it is also a phenomenon that affects roma children and children with different disabilities, for the latter the rate of drop-out is much higher than their peers and only 40% of them enter secondary school. member states must adopt inclusive integration policies and take more effective action to reduce school dropout, which is one of the main causes of poverty and unemployment. i strongly support mrs honeyball's report, because immediate and concrete action by the union is needed to achieve the target of bringing the school drop-out rate below 10% by 2020.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the inclusion of the kaliningrad region and other polish administrative districts in the eligible border area. since 2004, following the enlargement of the eu to ten countries including poland, the kaliningrad region has become a de facto russian enclave within the territory of the european union, which has led to a profound change in the living conditions of local citizens. the initiatives taken so far have not been able to reduce to any significant extent the marginalization of the inhabitants of the region concerned and of the region itself, and there was therefore an objective need to remedy this situation. i therefore support the amendment of the regulation on local border traffic, which would avoid the region being fragmented into several districts and would allow the inhabitants of the area to benefit from the facilities for local border traffic. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal, considering it appropriate to facilitate the movement of people and cultural, social and economic exchanges in that region.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the triantaphyllides report. with the adoption of regulation (ec) no 1931/2006, the european union introduced a general derogation for local traffic at land borders for border residents, considering a local border area to be an area within 30 km. member states can thus admit border residents into the union with only a local border traffic pass, without the need to present additional documents such as a visa. poland and the russian federation have proposed an amendment to the regulation in view of the particular situation of the kaliningrad district. this region, with a population of about one million and surrounded by the eu except for the baltic sea, is artificially fragmented into three districts: one subject to the border traffic agreement with poland, one with lithuania and one not subject to any agreement. such a change would allow all inhabitants to benefit from the facilities for local border traffic and would ensure the elimination of artificial and arbitrary barriers between the residents of the region.
in writing. − local border areas are a very important tool developed by the european union to ensure that no artificial and arbitrary barriers are erected between residents of regions divided by national borders. we agree with the rapporteur that member states should conclude bilateral agreements with neighbouring third countries in order to promote regular contacts between people living on both sides of the external borders of the european union. the 2004 enlargement created an artificial barrier to the long-standing cultural, social and economic links between the inhabitants of the whole region, so we support the request for amendment of the regulation as formulated in the commission proposal. this is an important opportunity for us to reaffirm our strong commitment to the principle of free movement and to support firmly and consistently the right of people to move freely. we therefore call on poland to take concrete action to facilitate movement and to avoid unnecessary delays or other ordinary complications which in fact hinder the free movement of citizens in the kaliningrad region.
in writing. - this report is a very useful tool to clearly reaffirm the european parliament's unconditional commitment to freedom of movement. in this context, as mr triantaphyllides rightly points out, the amendment of the regulation should be designed to ensure that the whole of the kaliningrad district is considered as a single border area.
