in writing. - mr president, a global eu response to hiv/aids is needed as it is a virus and a disease affecting 2.2 million people in the eu and neighbouring countries. according to the latest available data, about 26 000 people are infected each year in europe and neighbouring countries, and it is estimated that more than 30% of those infected in the eu are unaware of their infection. the union must respond effectively and appropriately to the evolution and spread of the virus in order to combat it and to provide assistance to those already infected. the commission and the council should swiftly implement the communication 'the fight against hiv/aids in the european union and neighbouring countries 2009-2013' and implement a specific action plan to combat new infections, supported above all by numerous information and awareness campaigns, to make everyone understand the seriousness of the phenomenon.
in writing. - today is world aids day. this is a very important meeting to raise awareness of this complex disease and the worrying increase in the number of people affected. since 1981, aids has killed over 25 million people, making it one of the most destructive epidemics in recorded history. it is therefore essential that europe adopts a common strategy to combat aids/hiv, focusing primarily on prevention and on comprehensive and effective information. i think, however, that the approach adopted in parliament's resolution is not exhaustive and does not properly highlight the vulnerability of women to this disease. in europe, the number of women affected by the disease is steadily increasing: in fact, as many as 35% of new diagnoses are in women. it is also shown by various studies that women are twice as likely to be infected in unprotected sex as men, due to both cultural limitations and greater biological vulnerability. i therefore believe that the resolution should have highlighted the initiatives that could be taken to alleviate this situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i believe that a complete and early diagnosis of hiv is of fundamental importance in the fight against its spread. in fact, timely treatment can reduce the infectivity of patients and the rate of hiv transmission by up to 96%. prevention and information remain the cornerstones of appropriate and effective healthcare for the protection of the patient. i would also like to read this resolution in the light of the specific context of the defence of the right to health of the immigrant population, which must be guaranteed the best possible level of care and treatment. consider that, according to the 2011 unaids report, 68% of the world's hiv-infected population resides in sub-saharan africa, an area from which considerable migration flows to europe originate. in addition, the migration process often puts migrants at a disadvantage and exposes them to a higher risk of contracting infectious diseases such as hiv/aids. it is therefore important to work towards ensuring universal and equitable access to prevention, testing, treatment and care for people living with hiv, as well as treatment for co-infections such as tuberculosis and hepatitis b and c, among others.
in writing. − hiv infection is still a widespread phenomenon in our society, and many people who are infected are often unaware that they have it. it is therefore necessary to take all the necessary measures both in the treatment and, above all, in the prevention, taking into account also the fact that aids is a predictable disease. in this sense, i support the idea of making hiv/aids prevention programmes an integral part of sexual and reproductive health care and of facilitating women's access to preventive treatment, since they often face difficulties due to the limited financial resources available or their position of responsibility in caring for their children. i therefore welcome the measures suggested by the rapporteurs to the community institutions, such as the commission and the council, and to the member states, to improve and make more efficient the fight against hiv/aids in the european union and in neighbouring countries. that is why i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. - the problem of hiv virus transmission is still dramatically relevant 30 years after its discovery. the resolution presented today certainly contains positive aspects, such as the call for strengthening the tools for detecting and preventing the virus, the need to improve the care of those affected and the call for investing in research so that this syndrome can finally be defeated. it is also important to have a proper information and awareness campaign to combat the prejudices still present in our societies. however, i could not vote in favour of this resolution because it contains a message which i do not think is acceptable: i refer to article 22, which states that abortion is a legitimate means of preventing infection. i therefore abstained because, while i share the general support for the fight against aids, i cannot allow any compromise in favour of the practice of abortion.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, one of the greatest health problems of our time is undoubtedly that of hiv and aids. although the information is now very widespread, statistics show that every three hours there is a new infection, and that is why i think it is absolutely necessary for the eu to continue its fight against this tragedy which continually affects millions of people in the world. we are not just talking about poor and underdeveloped areas, such as those in africa, but the whole world, europe. i think that it is necessary and necessary to persevere in order to reach a common response, without letting our guard down.

the european union must guarantee its citizens and residents effective freedom of movement between the 27 member states in safe conditions. this is not guaranteed today to those people - mainly women, but not only - who, despite having obtained protection measures in their own country, often with great difficulty as a result of persecution, stalking, repeated threats - even death - by a person they know - often a relative, as commissioner reding also said, or an ex-husband or boyfriend, or any other person they know - are no longer protected when they move to another member state. with this directive, parliament and the council, in collaboration with the commission, have sought to fill this legislative gap. i would like to remind you that we have applied the codecision procedure for the first time, on the initiative of the spanish presidency, together with 12 other member states, including italy, and with the strong support of the polish presidency, which i thank. this is the first legal instrument for the effective prevention and protection of victims actual or potential of crimes against the person, including moral crimes within the community, which can be adopted by national authorities, both civil and criminal, with measures equal to or equivalent to those of the issuing state. as shadow rapporteur for the s&d group's femm committee, i would like to highlight the excellent cooperation that has been established with the two rapporteurs and the valuable contribution of ezio perillo from parliament's legislative office, today at the luxembourg court. i would also like to express my satisfaction with the qualifying points of our proposal: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the protection of the rights of the child is not restricted to the protection of the physical and mental integrity, dignity and personal freedom and sexual integrity of the child, the right to information, the guarantees of information also for the person making the threat about the consequences of the breach of the ope, the obligation of the member states to compile comparable statistics. i naturally expect parliament to express its views on the victims package, which has already been announced by commissioner reding, in order to make this central role of protecting victims truly transversal.
madam president, the adoption of this directive marks the end of a long, positive legislative journey that started with the european council in december 2009, a journey that saw 12 member states, including italy, at the forefront of a european approach to the protection and protection of victims, including first and foremost victims of gender-based violence women including domestic violence and stalking, as well as other categories of very vulnerable victims, including minors and people with disabilities. the european protection order is a mutual recognition instrument in the field of judicial cooperation in criminal matters and a system for removing and punishing offenders by prohibiting access to the protected person's place of residence and by imposing restrictions on contact with or approach to the victim. i believe that this is a concrete step towards the creation of a european area of freedom and justice, a step forward in terms of cooperation between the member states for the concrete affirmation of the fundamental rights of european men and women. it is measures like this that strengthen the confidence of our citizens in the authority of the european institutions and, for this very reason, i conclude by congratulating all those who have worked on this important dossier, first of all mrs jiménez-becerril barrio and mr romero lópez. i also thank commissioner reding for her proverbial sensitivity on these issues and, above all, for her practical commitment to the defence of the victims.
mr president, the report we are discussing is in fact proposing a total equality of rights between migrant workers and european citizens, who are the real pillars of our economies and social systems. in some cases, the measures contained in this report would even open up a preferential lane for workers from third countries who are staying in a member state, such as tax benefits and ad hoc forms of assistance to move around the labour market. i believe in all sincerity that - especially at a time of economic and social crisis such as this - the european and national institutions should first and foremost support our citizens. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the data on poverty in europe paint a dramatic picture: more than 60 million citizens are at risk of poverty, with 15 percent of the population having to make do with incomes below 60 percent of the national average. one in eight people live in households where no one is working, and one in five children is at risk of poverty. in the face of this, euro-boonism is thinking about how to accommodate workers from third countries, but in reality we do not even know how to guarantee decent living standards to our own workers.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, although all the member states of the european union must respect the right of citizens to a fair trial, national procedures for information during criminal proceedings vary considerably from one country to another. some states provide that defendants are only given oral information on their procedural rights, others provide information - especially if technical - only in writing or at the request of the accused. if we consider that more than eight million criminal proceedings are initiated in the european union every year, it is easy to see the inadequacy of an information system that is still so varied and heterogeneous. i therefore share the content and objectives of this directive. i refer in particular to the general rule that the accused must be informed of his procedural rights before the proceedings are opened, with particular reference to the right to be assisted by a lawyer and to have official translations if they are in another language. as regards the post-opening phase, i agree with the two specific rights chosen: the right of the accused to full information on the charges against him and his right of access to the public prosecution file. these are two essential conditions for assessing and combating the lawfulness of arrest or detention and for providing the best line of defence. i therefore congratulate the commissioner, the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs on the work done in the informal trilogues which led to the adoption of measures which will allow the spread and harmonious development of fundamental rights, such as the right to a defence and the right to a fair trial.

the rapporteur. mr president, the council has again made an urgent request on the matter for which i was appointed rapporteur for parliament to express its opinion at the december 2011 meeting of the committee on fisheries. as rapporteur and on behalf of our committee on fisheries, i oppose the council's request for urgency, as i did for the same request on 15 november 2011, and i also think it is necessary to briefly summarise the matter. this council proposal concerns access for vessels flying the flag of venezuela to the exclusive economic zone off the coast of the french department of guiana. as the title suggests, the proposal is similar to an international agreement on which, under the lisbon treaty, parliament has the right to express its opinion as a co-legislator under the ordinary legislative procedure. the question is not difficult in substance: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the essential point is, however, something else. the european commission has submitted the proposal to parliament on the basis of a specific legal basis, articles 43.2 and 218.6a of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the parliament, in view of the content and spirit of the proposal, which gave it the power of approval, accepted it in full. however, in its subsequent referral to parliament, the council unilaterally amended the legal basis in question, setting aside articles 43.2 and 218.6a and opting for articles 43.3 and 218.6b, thus reducing the expression of parliament to a simple opinion. i would remind you that the coordinators of our committee rejected this amendment by the council and referred the matter to the legal affairs committee of the european parliament before adopting any final position. the commission has confirmed the validity of the legal basis initially adopted by the european commission and, in particular, has alerted our committee on fisheries to the unpleasant precedent which could be set by the implementation of such a combination of articles 43 (3) and 218 (6b) of the treaty. in response to the council's insistence that only the opinion be obtained and not the approval as soon as possible, the chair of the committee on fisheries, fraga estévez, in a letter to president buzek dated 5 october 2011, recalled both the position of the committee on fisheries and that of the committee on legal affairs and suggested to president buzek that, in order to resolve any dispute, the council be invited to refer to parliament again a proposal containing the original legal basis by restoring to our assembly its full right as co-legislator. on 26 october 2011, president buzek sent a letter to the council to that effect which, in its reply, simply states and i repeat, simply this: the council's amendment of the legal basis initially adopted by the european commission was not a light-hearted choice and was the result of careful reflection. that is not a satisfactory answer. the european parliament is therefore obliged to vote, in the committee on fisheries on 20 december, on the draft report which restores the appropriate legal basis. it is therefore essential that parliament should reject this proposal.

madam president, i wholeheartedly support the initiative to strengthen the area of rights of the defence in criminal proceedings within the european union, which is why my country has actively cooperated within the council to secure the rapid adoption of the instrument. the aim of the directive is to lay down rules on the right of suspects and accused persons to be informed of their rights and of the charges against them in criminal proceedings. the framework of the directive should apply to anyone who is informed by the competent authorities of a member state that he is under investigation or charged until the proceedings are concluded. the general right of all suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings is to be informed, orally or in writing, of the relevant procedural rights as soon as possible after the commencement of the proceedings. the commission has also proposed that the council and the european parliament should be given the opportunity to discuss the proposal with the council and the european parliament.

in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs matera's report because i believe that the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund is a timely and necessary response to the increasingly serious problem of unemployment and the reintegration of people who have lost their jobs into the labour market. the economic crisis which has unfortunately been accompanying the world and european economies for the last three years has hit a highly productive and skilled area such as trentino-alto adige. in particular, italy's application for 643 redundancies, of which 528 were eligible for assistance from the egf, fulfilled the eligibility conditions laid down in the egf regulation. i am convinced that the management of this fund, not only in terms of assistance but also in terms of training and reintegration into the labour market, is the best way forward to deal with the effects of the severe crisis which is still continuing today.
in writing. − despite the economic crisis, i believe it is necessary for the european union to continue to finance those sectors and those companies, which are seeking aid, which fall within the parameters for the transposition of loans. finally, it is time for a globalisation adjustment fund to help small italian businesses in trentino alto adige. i hope that my vote in favour will also mean that the fund, which is almost eur 4 million, will be allocated. this would save the jobs of more than 500 workers and therefore of as many families. which is why i think everyone should vote for it.
in writing. - having regard to the fact that the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows and having regard to the importance of mobilising the egf in favour of italy in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, i shall vote in favour of the following proposal for a decision.
in writing. − with this vote italy will receive €3.9 million in eu aid for construction workers made redundant as a result of the international crisis. the funds will now be used to help find new jobs for the 528 workers made redundant by 323 construction companies in the trentino-alto adige/südtirol region.
in writing. − the globalisation adjustment fund instrument is often activated to deal with redundancies, redundancies and difficult working situations. the reintegration of individual workers who have been made redundant into the labour market must be supported. the global economic crisis has not spared even one of italy's most prosperous regions, trentino alto adige. the construction sector in italy, as in other eu countries, has suffered the most serious consequences: the sector experienced in 2011 the worst season since the italian economic boom of the 1960s. in order to support the reintegration of workers and to revive the construction sector, i voted in favour of the parliamentary initiative.
in writing. − the european union is a composite, multilingual and multicultural society, built around the four fundamental freedoms, including freedom of movement, which the union guarantees its citizens. in view of this, it is important that anyone suspected or accused of a crime within the union is informed immediately of his or her rights and of any charges against him or her in a language that he or she understands. at present, european citizens are not guaranteed full information. i therefore voted in favour of the directive on the right to information in criminal proceedings, because i believe it is essential to guarantee this right to anyone accused or suspected of a crime throughout the proceedings, investigations and any appeals.
in writing. - mr president, the reluctance of the member states to harmonize certain aspects of their respective systems of procedural law does not benefit either the member states themselves or, above all, the citizens of europe. the commission's 'step by step' approach is proving successful. however, i believe that the european parliament should raise its voice to the council in order to try to speed up the adoption of the other directives in this area. to have to talk in 2011 about rules on the right of suspects or accused persons to be informed of their rights and the charge in criminal proceedings within the member states of the european union seems to me to be something anachronistic, to say the least.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the sippel report, which aims to establish common minimum standards for the right to information in criminal proceedings in the european union: defendants and the accused have the right to be informed of their rights and this information must be explained in accessible, simple language and in a language that the defendant understands! specific information should also be provided in writing in the event of deprivation of liberty by the competent authorities of the member states during criminal proceedings. finally, i agree with the inclusion in the report, alongside the general right to be informed about procedural rights, of two specific rights: the right to information on the charge and the right of access to the file, unless there is a serious risk to the life of another person or the possibility of serious harm to the internal security of the member state. this directive will improve the rights of suspects and accused persons by ensuring that they receive timely information on their rights.
in writing. - i am pleased to support this report on the right to information in criminal proceedings. if we are to guarantee common minimum standards in the present criminal proceedings and thus equality before the law and justice in every european court, then i believe that this act is of paramount importance. finally, this report achieves a minimum standard of information in criminal proceedings and through this new principle we can aim to ensure the protection of the fundamental rights of all citizens of the european union, which are then the basis of our law. i fully agree with the rapporteur on the importance of continuing to work closely together in order to harmonise the basic aspects of our legal procedures. i would like to congratulate you on your excellent work.
in writing. − the implementation of the principle of mutual recognition of decisions in criminal matters requires that member states have mutual trust in their criminal justice systems. to ensure this, defendants should be fully informed of the proceedings concerning them. i agree with the report, especially in the part where it stresses the importance of ensuring that, when providing information in accordance with the directive, the respondent or accused person is provided, if necessary, with translation and interpretation in a language he or she understands, in accordance with the rules laid down in directive 2010/64/eu.
in writing. - my vote in favour of this report is motivated by the rapid change in a condition which may be a limit for suspects and accused persons who are in other countries of the union. the fact that there can be common rules to simplify the understanding of citizens' rights in criminal matters can only be of benefit and increase the chances that those who are accused also have a greater guarantee of being informed and can actually exercise their right to a defence.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the need to establish common minimum standards for the right to information in criminal proceedings throughout the european union would ensure better recognition of fundamental rights for eu citizens and would also help to overcome the difficulties encountered in implementing the principle of mutual recognition in criminal matters due to a lack of trust between authorities. the following proposal aims at greater collaboration in addition to legislative standardisation through a phased approach as provided for in the roadmap adopted on 30 november 2009. i am voting in favour of the proposal for a directive in order to ensure that the right to information is effectively granted.
in writing. - the report by mr sippel on the right to information in criminal proceedings was voted on in plenary today. the multiple branches of the right to information are a fundamental element for the effective protection of the rights of citizens directly or potentially involved. the european union is working towards more detailed and uniform procedural rules in this area. the right to information in criminal proceedings is intended to ensure that the accused or the defendant is aware of the charges against him or her or of the investigations being carried out against him or her, that he or she has the right to interpretation and to communicate with his or her family members, and also provides for the introduction of sound guarantees in the application of security or preventive measures so that the right of defence, exercised through the legal prosecutor, can be exercised to the best of his or her ability by virtue of the principle of culpability. it was also equally clear that the regulation of the european arrest warrant must be further developed with regard to the rights of the persons involved and the limits of the judicial authority. the european parliament considers that intergovernmental and interinstitutional cooperation is necessary in order to ensure that the provisions on the right to information in criminal proceedings, in order to better protect the suspected offender, can be extended and clarified where there are deficiencies or contradictions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr sippel on the right to information in criminal proceedings. i think it is right that under the new legislation, those who are being investigated for a crime within the european union will have to be informed of their rights in a language they understand: this measure aims to ensure that all eu countries provide anyone arrested or subject to a european arrest warrant with a communication on their fundamental rights in the course of criminal proceedings. the establishment of common minimum standards in criminal proceedings is a guarantee for a better recognition of the fundamental rights of european citizens and also helps to overcome those limitations and difficulties which may arise between different judicial authorities in implementing the principle of mutual recognition in criminal matters.

in writing. - i voted in favour because the european protection order is going to fill a major legislative gap for the protection of victims who decide to settle in a member state other than their own. at present all member states have a legislative apparatus with measures to protect life, physical, mental or sexual integrity and the protection of victims who have suffered various forms of abuse. i also believe that in the broader context of the stockholm programme, the adoption of this important european directive can have a threefold objective: (1) to prevent a new offence being committed against the victim in the member state where the victim intends to settle; (2) to claim in the member state to which the victim is travelling a level of protection and protection which is equivalent to or higher than that of the member state which granted the measures; (3) to prevent the victim from being subjected to any form of discrimination which might further aggravate his already vulnerable situation.

in writing. - i voted in favour because i believe that the european protection order is a key step towards a european area of justice. the text approved today will allow victims of crime who have been granted protection under the law of one member state to apply for the same protection in another member state. these laws, already approved by national governments, are designed to protect victims of gender-based violence, harassment, kidnapping, stalking or attempted murder. measures to protect victims of crime already exist in all member states, but they cease to have effect if the victim moves to another country. the european protection order will therefore enable a person who is protected in one member state of the union to obtain protection in all member states.

in writing. - the report by mr klaus heiner lehn was voted on today in plenary. micro-entities are currently still subject to the same rules as larger enterprises. the complex financial reporting rules applied to them are not proportionate to their specific accounting needs and create unnecessary financial burdens. in 2009, the commission therefore put forward a legislative proposal to exempt such enterprises from budgetary obligations. the european commission estimates the potential savings of the proposal at eur 6.3 billion. after difficult and lengthy negotiations in the council, a compromise was reached which, while maintaining certain accounting obligations, allows exemption from budgetary obligations for undertakings which meet the following criteria: (a) a total budget of not more than eur 350 000; (b) a net turnover of not more than eur 700 000; (c) a number of employees not exceeding 10.

in writing. - the international market crisis and the budgetary crisis in some member states mean that action is urgently needed to ensure that the member states in difficulty comply with their commitments, in line with the principle of solidarity which guides the european union. the financial management provisions we voted for do not provide for additional commitment appropriations, but advance the 2013 appropriations to the 2011-2012 period. the measure is necessary because of the urgency of the moment. the vote will allow the member states to temporarily raise the maximum rate of union co-financing for co-financed community programmes such as the structural and cohesion funds, the eafrd and the european fisheries fund.
in writing. - i have expressed my support for mr de castro's text. as a result of the financial crisis, some member states have faced budgetary constraints that could prevent them from meeting their commitments under the joint co-financed programmes (structural and cohesion funds, eafrd and european fisheries fund). to remedy this situation, the commission has proposed to temporarily raise the maximum rate of union co-financing for programmes under way in member states receiving support from the european financial stabilisation mechanism (currently affecting greece, ireland and portugal) and the balance of payments support mechanism for non-euro area countries (currently affecting latvia and romania). this temporary increase in union co-financing, provided at the request of the member state concerned, would reduce the amount of corresponding national funds needed in the financial years 2011 and 2012, thus contributing to the mobilisation of the funds programmed for the rural economy and to an overall economic recovery in those member states.
in writing. - non-tariff barriers, first discussed in the 1979 wto multilateral trade negotiations, are all trade restrictions that restrict imports. i believe that open and above all fair trade is the best way to ensure and maintain a level playing field for european businesses operating internationally. bilateral and multilateral negotiations offer the commission the opportunity to strengthen regulatory cooperation with the eu's main trading partners. in my view, the commission should act proactively and in a targeted manner to reduce the restrictive impact that non-tariff barriers have on the ability of european companies to access foreign markets. this should be a top priority of the union's new trade policy under the europe 2020 strategy. moreover, as regards free trade agreements between the european union and third countries, it is essential to ensure that they provide sufficient reciprocity in market access and mutual benefits for both parties. the ultimate objective should be to limit litigation and the costs associated with it for european businesses, without compromising the quality of the resulting regulatory environment.
in writing. - in my view, europe is not doing enough to protect its industry and services from external competitors, who are protecting themselves with internal safeguards that are much stronger and more effective than ours. in any case, it is acceptable that in the course of trade negotiations with the most important partners and in the production of community legislation on international trade, we should try to take account of the need for europe to balance the terms of trade and the quality and quantity of non-tariff measures between ourselves and our trading partners. i agree with the need to include the issue of non-tariff barriers in all free trade agreements, the possibility of setting up automatic warning mechanisms to detect new unjustified non-tariff barriers, and the focus on the sensitive issue of raw material supply. i therefore voted in favour of the sturdy report.
in writing. - i welcome the report presented, which i voted in favour of, as it deals with a very sensitive subject, that of non-tariff barriers, in the light of the financial crisis europe is experiencing. non-tariff barriers, identified by european companies, exporters, analysts and the commission as a growing barrier to free access to the markets of partner countries, are trade restrictions, excluding duties, which restrict imports. they can be of two main types: measures that directly affect prices such as export subsidies or duty drawback, or measures that indirectly affect prices such as import licences. they are therefore instruments with a potentially legitimate nature, but often used politically incorrectly. the commission needs to act proactively in reducing the impact of these barriers on the ability of european businesses to access foreign markets. in this context, europe must address the problem in a holistic way, by reviewing trade measures, removing unlawful barriers and paying particular attention to current and future free trade agreements, ensuring sufficient reciprocity in market access and providing for bilateral safeguard mechanisms including appropriate corrective measures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that globalisation is only good to the extent that we control its direction. my generation, on this continent, has access to a wealth of goods and services that would have been unthinkable in other eras or in other parts of the world. at the same time, opening up international trade has made it possible to move the economy more and better, with positive consequences for the majority of citizens. this does not mean that compensatory measures should not be considered for those who, despite themselves, fail us because of the greater degree of exposure to the international market, and, again for the sake of fairness, obstacles cannot be left which perpetuate the existence of pockets of inefficiency to the exclusive advantage of the few who benefit from them. i look forward to seeing the commission's proposal on this subject, so that we can further increase the well-being of european citizens.

in writing. - the liberalization of trade and investment can only bring advantages, and that is why i am voting in favour. the opportunities offered by an open market are much greater and benefit those countries which have eliminated customs duties and non-tariff barriers, which prevent european companies from trading freely with foreign markets, which would undoubtedly lead to a considerable advantage, increasing demand for goods and also the common wealth. at a time like this, the world economy needs to support each other and work together to ensure that the recovery can be as fast as possible.

in writing. - the report by mr sturdy on the reduction and elimination of unjustified tariff and regulatory barriers to trade and investment by the eu's strategic partners was voted on today in strasbourg. it was considered appropriate for the european union, which has exclusive competence in trade and investment matters, to address the issue of non-tariff barriers, in the framework of the europe 2020 strategy, combining a diplomatic approach to be pursued in close cooperation with the european external action service (eeas) and a strengthened regulatory dialogue with the eu's trading partners, with a view to placing non-tariff barriers at the heart of international negotiations. it was also hoped that the wto and the commission would also jointly work to assert the benefits of trade liberalisation so that the european union could fully enjoy the opportunities provided by an open market, while offsetting the possible negative externalities of widespread liberalisation, by mutual agreements with trading partners on certain transitional exceptions.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the new legislation seeks to avoid the confusion that consumers experience when buying fruit products. fruit juice can only be defined as such if it contains 100% fruit, without any type of addition, including sugar or otherwise. fruit nectar, on the other hand, may be sweetened by adding sugar or honey up to a maximum of 20% by weight of the product, and in any case the quantity must be indicated on the label. where a product is made from more than one fruit species, it must be indicated in the list of ingredients, unless it is chosen to indicate all the ingredients individually. in order to avoid confusion, a transitional period of four and a half years is envisaged during which the indication 'without added sugar' may continue to appear on the label of fruit juice. i have often pointed out to the commission, referring to the previous speech by my green colleague, that fruit juices are marketed in a clearly misleading way, for example, by displaying the image of a fruit on the entire package, while the small print on the back of the packaging reveals that the fruit is only a minority part of the product. the last case, reported to the commission, concerns a well-known brand from the same country mentioned by the green member, which offers the consumer a package with the image of a waterfall of blueberries and the words '100% fruit smoothie'. the label on the back states in small print that the product contains only 8 percent cranberry juice and 40 percent apple juice. i would also point out that, since 85% of orange juice is produced with extra ec fruit, it would have been appropriate to require the indication of origin on the label in order to provide correct information to consumers, but unfortunately this has not been possible either. we shall vote in favour of the report, despite some criticisms, partly because the lengthy negotiations have led to a text which has been widely accepted.
in writing. the consumer associations tell us that most of the people interviewed do not really know the difference between a 'fruit juice' and a 'fruit netting', between a 'juice without added sugars' and a 'natural fruit juice'. we believe that greater clarity is needed for a free and informed choice. for example, a mixture containing 90% apple and 10% strawberry juice will have to be called 'apple and strawberry juice', whereas it can currently be labelled 'strawberry juice'. a generic name such as 'mixed juice' may be used if there are three or more sources of fruit. that is the spirit of the resolution we have voted today: the commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of consumer information. the ppe group to which i belong balances the needs of producers equally: until now, european producers have been treated differently from their counterparts importing fruit juices from third countries (the usa and china, for example) into the eu, sometimes without the same strict controls as european producers. today we have ensured that this discrimination will cease by imposing the same obligations on importers from third countries, thereby reassuring consumers of the quality of the products they will freely choose to buy.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, now that the legislation for reinforced economic governance, the ‘six-pack’, has entered into force – which it did yesterday – we must hasten its implementation. on the fiscal side this is already a work in rapid and serious progress. on the macro side we need to move on as well. i therefore welcome your draft resolution on the envisaged design of the scoreboard for the surveillance of macroeconomic imbalances as well as your oral question, which in fact consists of nine questions, to which i shall try to respond in my remaining two minutes and seven seconds. following your resolution tomorrow, and as the commission received the views of the council and the european systemic risk board respectively in november, we can now finalise the design of the scoreboard without any further delay, and in full compliance with democratic principles. the final scoreboard will become part of the alert mechanism report, which is currently scheduled for adoption by mid-january. it will be discussed in ecofin and the euro group in january/february. taking due account of these discussions, the commission will launch in-depth reviews of the member states for which they are needed. these in-depth reviews will analyse macroeconomic imbalances and provide the basis for any recommendations to be addressed to member states. let me underline the key difference between fiscal and macroeconomic surveillance, and between the excessive deficit procedure and the excessive imbalance procedure: both are preventive, but macroeconomic surveillance is even more preventive than fiscal surveillance, and as such is necessary for economic stability and fiscal sustainability. this we have seen, for instance, in the cases of ireland or spain, both of which had sound public finances prior to the crisis. once the crisis hit with its full force, however, their serious macroeconomic imbalances led to a very serious fiscal crisis which then turned into a recession in the real economy and led to high unemployment, with very serious social and human consequences. moreover, while fiscal surveillance is highly numerical and quantifiable, macroeconomic surveillance requires a thorough economic reading and is much more qualitative. this means that, when we propose countries for an in-depth study, it will not imply that they face an imminent crisis. instead, it means that for these countries there is a risk of imbalances which, if confirmed, would clearly need to be addressed effectively. in other words, it serves as an essential early-warning system and a strong call for pre-emptive action to correct the build-up of those imbalances. this brings me to the further aspects of your oral question, especially the regulation’s equal application to all member states. the assessment of member states’ current account balances is an essential element of the economic analysis of the alert mechanism report. the commission stands fully by its declaration to the european parliament on 28 september stating that ‘macroeconomic surveillance covers countries with current account deficits and surpluses with appropriate differentiation as regards the urgency of policy responses and the type of corrective actions required’. to conclude, let me also recall that all 27 member states will be subject to surveillance. thus all member states will benefit from its findings, both on their own account and jointly for the common good of the european union. i am certain that the united kingdom will also want to participate in this work; we for our part want to – and indeed will – involve each and every member state of the european union. the regulation applies to all and we continue to work for the benefit of each and every member state and the whole european union, even though that sometimes seems to be forgotten in the midst of the most heated debates of the day.
i am speaking on behalf of the ppe group. the commission has already made a number of proposals. we have been fighting here for a long time about economic governance, about the six-pack. the package of laws came into force yesterday. this is a package of measures to detect economic misdevelopments in member states at an early stage. in the area of macroeconomic surveillance, the scoreboard has always been at the heart of the political debate here in parliament. parliament ultimately decided to lay down only basic guidelines in the legislative text and to entrust the commission with the task of drawing up the scoreboard. the commission has now completed this work. the parameters proposed can be a good way to achieve the desired goal. we have already discussed the symmetrical approach of the six-pack in our political debate here in parliament. but such a symmetrical approach also assumes the incorrect view that the european union is a closed and bilateral market. if one exports too much, does that automatically mean that another exports too little? i don't think it is. is the problem of those member states currently experiencing difficult economic times really due to the fact that other member states are more successful in the internal market or in the world? this would also mean that it is not a problem if member states do not do their economic policy homework. that approach would not get us very far. the scoreboard will evolve. it takes time, new indicators will be introduced in the next few years and the limits will probably change with economic developments. that is why parliament has also provided for us to have a task of monitoring and assessing this development. we are also doing that with this question to you, commissioner. the commission's proposal is useful and useful to us in the european people's party as a starting point. i am convinced that it can go its way and that it can lead to success. that is why we will agree to it.
