mr president, phosphates in household detergents end up in europe's water systems, rivers, streams and lakes. phosphorus accelerates the reproduction of various life forms, so algae and other fast-growing plant species proliferate at an unprecedented rate when phosphorus is increased in an aquatic environment. this overgrowth of algae deprives other living organisms of oxygen and can also produce toxins by destroying fish and plant species, thus reducing the quality of the water itself. i therefore voted in favour of the text voted on today because, in order to clean up europe's water resources, it is desirable to reduce the amount of phosphorus that is discharged into the waters of our continent.
mr president, the text presented by mr lisek analyses the possible measures to be taken to reduce the cost of defence, which, in a period of financial crisis, is a heavy burden on the community budget. the main proposals concern better coordination of defence system planning, pooling and sharing of defence capabilities, and support for research and technological development. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's view that the economic and financial crisis which has hit us can be an opportunity for the integration of the european union's defence policies, providing the impetus for the elaboration and finally implementation of those ambitious reforms which have been stalled for years. for these reasons i voted in favour.
mr president, despite the serious financial crisis we are in, there are sectors of the economy which are never, if ever, affected by the cuts imposed by the austerity measures adopted by the member states. for example, the so-called 'blood and tears' financial maneuver of the italian government is proving to be blood and tears only for the usual well-known, namely workers and pensioners. the military spending, on the other hand, does not seem to be affected, since the purchase of 131 jsf fighter-bombers has been confirmed, a purchase which the italian government is committing to until 2026, for a total expenditure of about 15 billion euros, that is, about half of this "blood and tears" manoeuvre we are undergoing. for this and other reasons i voted against the lisek report which, despite some good ideas for cutting expenditure, calls the cuts in the defence sector worrying. ladies and gentlemen, there are other cuts that should worry us more at a time like this! i'll close with a rhetorical question: "is it not possible that all these weapons purchased today will be used tomorrow on our citizens in revolt who will ask us to account for our poor choices?"
mr president, there is no doubt that the strengthening of bilateral relations between the european union and a world power like russia will make these meetings - which will be fruitful in terms of trade - necessary, especially if russia, as we hope, finally joins the world trade organisation. this would be a way of widening relations and at the same time giving a second chance to the many entrepreneurs who operate in the territory of the member states. another useful step could be the liberalisation of short-stay visas to facilitate internal movement, while an important step was the elections - defined by the high representative of the european union as technically well prepared and administered - but the wind of freedom that continues to blow in russia must be supported and assisted to guarantee fundamental rights, freedom of expression and above all those high freedoms that are closely related to a system of law that we trust will soon also mark russia.
mr president, the revision of the european neighbourhood policy is certainly a strength in relations with the southern part of this important area, which borders on southern europe. it is a significant aspect which does not exhaust the activities of the european union, but which at the moment gives the mediterranean a central role: the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment is a very important one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done in drawing up this report. this is the objective which not only concerns the southern dimension but which is now known for its centrality.
mr president, the arab spring and its aftermath have necessitated a review of the european neighbourhood policy. it is clear that, as things stand, relations with these countries must be more focused on cooperation in order to ensure that democracy and security on both sides of the mediterranean are given priority. in this respect, i believe that intercultural and interreligious dialogue is essential to strengthening mutual respect and tolerance with the neighbouring partner countries, while at the same time promoting the fight against terrorism and extremism. for these reasons, mr president, i naturally voted in favour.
mr president, i can only welcome today's report on the review of the european neighbourhood policy, and in particular the proposal to strengthen the union's southern partnership, which is essential for the democratic consolidation of the region after the historic events of last spring. the funds for the countries of the southern mediterranean were allocated before the crisis and appear inadequate in relation to the actual needs and the modernisation of the societies of these countries; i believe that the support for the civil society instrument should be increased; i reiterate to the european commission the parliament's proposal for the creation of the erasmus and leonardo programmes with a euro-mediterranean character, in order to promote mobility and the exchange of good practice among young people.
in writing. − the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa) provides support for the period 2007-2013 to countries in the process of joining the eu. this assistance is provided in the context of the european partnerships with potential candidates and the accession partnerships of the actual candidate countries covering the western balkan countries and iceland. iceland and montenegro have been candidates for accession to the union since 2010. as the ipa is a flexible instrument, it is possible to modulate support to these beneficiary countries according to the needs arising from the commission's assessments and documents. they 're two different realities: iceland, for example, has a gdp per capita higher than the european average, while montenegro's administrative and financial management, due to its different national history, presents different needs and problems also in the field of financial transparency. the rules for the allocation of ipa-cbc and enpi funding should therefore be adapted to the new findings on the two candidate countries.
in writing. - i am in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the introduction of assistance for the pre-accession of new member states to the union. i think that it is necessary to impose basic conditions so that countries wishing to join the community as it already exists can adjust to the level of those already members, in order to avoid that there is too great a difference from the outset, which could lead to problems and more complicated cooperation between them.
in writing. − the amendment responds to concerns expressed by eu member states involved in crossborder cooperation (cbc) programmes regarding participation in calls for proposals. in agreement with the member states that participation in calls for proposals is limited to applicants from countries participating in the relevant cbc programme, i am voting in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the accession negotiations.
in writing. the text presented by mr albertini concerns the proposal to amend the regulation establishing a preaccession assistance instrument for those countries which have the prospect of becoming members of the european union. the aim is to provide assistance according to the needs of the countries involved in the current exercise, based on the commission's annual strategy reports for the countries concerned. i therefore voted in favour of this instrument of pre-accession assistance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the rodriguez report. in europe, fruit juices and similar products represent an important industrial sector. however, using orange juice as a reference model, 82% of the juice consumed in the eu comes directly from brazil and the usa, and less than 20% is produced in europe. the european processing industry, unlike other countries, is complementary to that of the marketing of fresh products and consequently generates a massive import of these products, causing high environmental costs in terms of co2. it is necessary to support the european sector, which has a significant added value in terms of employment, and to improve the quality of products, including more sustainable production processes that can also affect producers in third countries. i also agree with the importance of using statements on packaging such as: 'no added sugar' as there is considerable confusion about these types of products. i think that the commission should be able to take the necessary steps to ensure that the consumer is informed of the products he is buying.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the proposal in the light of the amendments made to it during the trilogue. it is more in line with the newly adopted regulation on food information to consumers to have the word 'without added sugar' on the packaging for a transitional period of four and a half years.
in writing. − in the last two decades, fruit juice consumption in europe has almost doubled, thanks in part to european campaigns to raise awareness of good nutrition. the directive finally adopted today will mean that fruit juice can only be defined as fruit juice if it contains 100% fruit without any additives, with an indication of the origin of the raw material used. europe is also called upon to ensure greater transparency for consumers, including the indication of the origin of the raw material used. this is a key figure when you consider that 82% of the orange juice consumed in the union comes from brazil and the usa. from now on, therefore, we will no longer run the risk of finding on our tables juices made with mixtures of unknown fruits, not indicated on the product. i hope that this new element in the codex alimentarius of european legislation will help the new directive to enhance the quality of european products by encouraging more informed purchases by consumers.
in writing. − the protection of consumers requires the provision of the highest possible level of information, in the most transparent and clear way. it is logical that the rules should apply equally to products manufactured in the european union and to those imported. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of this report on the labelling of fruit juices, as it certainly serves to clarify matters. consumers must be informed as much as possible about what they eat and drink every day: in the past, there were often indications concerning the ingredients used in the preparation of these drinks which did not always correspond to the actual content of the product. from now on, however, you should be sure that the label is "real", that is, it accurately states the content of fruit juices or nectars. i am always in favour of rules which help to combat misleading and deceptive claims to consumers and, at least in this area, we have managed to achieve a rather satisfactory result.
in writing. - the amendment of the directive on the consumption and production of fruit juices in europe is a sensitive and highly debated subject of interest to many consumers. the text i voted for aims to make the product better than it is today by providing better information to protect the consumer. the buyer must be able to know exactly what kind of product he is buying, what kind of quality and, beyond the discussion of the preservation of the fruit used, the amount of saccharin or sugar and the diversification between fruit concentrate-derived products or not. i think the most important factor is the possibility of having a better final product which consumers can choose in a clear and informed way.
in writing. − given that the fruit juice and similar products sector is a major industry in the european union, it should be noted that more than three quarters of what is consumed in the eu comes mainly from brazil and the united states, meaning that a small part of the eu's consumption is produced in its territory. this is why we need to support the european industry by bringing the directive into line with international law and by establishing the same rules for all products marketed in the eu: the aim is to contribute to the free movement of these products, but also to clarify the rules on their labelling, product classification, authorized ingredients and the admissibility of certain practices. in order to support the proposal for a directive, i am voting in favour of all the amendments to the directive.
in writing. - we voted today in plenary on mr rodriguez's report, which refers to the need to adopt the proposal for a parliament and council directive amending directive 2001/112/ec on fruit juices and other similar products intended for human consumption. the rapporteur stressed the importance of supporting the european fruit juice sector by bringing the directive into line with international law and the codex alimentarius, in order to contribute to the free movement of these products and also to clarify the rules on their labelling, categorisation, authorised ingredients and the admissibility of certain practices. the directive should improve the dual designation which distinguishes squeezed fruit juices from concentrates; in practice, it is difficult for the consumer to distinguish between the different categories. clarification of this point is important for the sugar content of these products, which is a sensitive issue for groups of consumers with specific needs. the rapporteur is in favour of harmless practices such as adding tangerine to orange juice, which can enhance the flavour and colour of the fruit, to promote the marketing of the products. these measures must be reinforced by information campaigns that enable the consumer to know what he is buying.
in writing. - the european parliament, by adopting this report, is calling for the introduction of a new set of consumer-friendly rules on the labelling of fruit juices and nectars. the new rules aim to prevent potentially misleading names for mixed juices and miscellaneous terms such as 'without added sugar'. the priority is to provide consumers with accurate information so that they know what they are buying. the final document highlights the key role played by this assembly in banning the addition of sugar in products sold as fruit juices and in clarifying the presence of sugars or sweeteners in similar drinks.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr perello rodriguez, which seeks to improve the quality rules and production standards for fruit juices, a product which european consumers buy every day. the report ensures greater product transparency for the consumer by indicating the origin of the raw material contained in fruit juices. the report is a benefit not only to consumers, who can benefit from more accurate information, but also to european farmers, as it increases the value of european products on the market. i believe that consumers have a right to know what they are buying and to make healthier choices. the report requires a distinction to be made between fresh fruit juices and juices made from concentrated fruit juices, or between juice and nectar, depending on the concentration of fruit and sugar contained in the juice. the consumer is thus freed from the confusion that accompanied it and is now able to make informed purchases.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to reduce the amount of phosphates used mainly in household washing machine detergents. phosphates are damaging the already delicate and precarious balance of our ecosystem. these substances end up in water systems, rivers, lakes and streams, causing an acceleration of the reproduction of life forms such as algae, a process that leads to eutrophication by depriving other life forms of oxygen. this produces toxins, which are responsible for the death of several fish species. however, phosphates cannot be banned altogether, as many are man-made; however, their use can be reduced by using less of them in household detergents and automatic dishwashers, for example. i also share the intention to encourage the use of alternative detergents with minimal amounts of phosphates, which already occupy a large and growing share of the eu market, through harmonised legislation which will be an incentive, with a view to a future agreement, for third countries to reduce the level of phosphorus in water.
in writing. − the adoption of the new regulation on the use of phosphates in household detergents and dishwashing detergents will bring about the same standards for the marketing of these products throughout europe. i hope that greater harmonization in this area will help to overcome the fragmentation of the internal market which has hitherto required detergent manufacturers to comply with divergent national regulations. that is why i believe that with today's vote europe has taken another step towards the free movement of these products, while at the same time ensuring better protection of the environment.
in writing. - i fully support the proposal to reduce the phosphorus content of detergents used in household washing machines. the commission has rightly chosen to present a proposal for a regulation rather than a directive, because this instrument makes it possible to harmonize better the different regulations in the member states. my vote is in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr newton dunn on the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household laundry detergents because it reduces the maximum levels of these substances in detergents. the general aim is to ensure greater consumer safety and environmental protection because these substances can be and often are harmful. pollution of groundwater and various domestic accidents are evidence of this. i therefore believe that each member state must adapt to the new standards as soon as possible, reducing the presence of phosphates as required by the amendment of the regulation in question.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the different national legislation in the european union on phosphates in detergents is creating a disorganized harmonisation at european level on this matter, which is fragmenting the internal market for detergents, where different member states have different policies and legislation. the aim of the commission's proposal for a regulation is to reduce the use of phosphorus in detergents, limiting pollution of water systems, rivers, streams and lakes, and to create harmonised regulations at european level for the member states. with the ultimate aim of purifying europe's water resources and promoting an agreement with third countries on the reduction of the phosphate content of detergents, and agreeing with all the amendments, i am voting in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the report by mr newton dunn on the use of phosphates in household detergents was voted on today in the plenary. reducing the percentage of phosphoric acid in household use is a decisive step in the process of monitoring and monitoring the development of methodologies to combat toxic and polluting processes. the access of the phosphorus component to the seas leads to the over-proliferation of certain plant components which destroy and reduce a multitude of marine animal and plant species. combating the excessive use of phosphorus in household detergents, fertilisers and appliances means effectively and efficiently combating the degenerative cycle that the use of products with low environmental respect brings to the environment and to the health of the population. these objectives can be achieved by promoting alternative formulations that reduce phosphorus-rich washing and by harmonizing the different national regulations on this matter. the need also emerged to draw up agreements with third countries so that europe would commit itself, by a predetermined date, to reducing the use of phosphorous substances and to advancing the process of market adaptation towards new regulatory rules which are more properly respectful of the european environment.
in writing. − protecting europe's waters also involves small everyday gestures. by adopting this important report on the reduction of phosphorus in household washing machine detergents, we are making a valuable contribution to the reduction of pollution in europe's water systems. phosphorus from household detergents used to combat water hardness is a major contributor to this type of ecological imbalance. the commission has already taken a number of measures to reduce the phosphorus content of domestic products, which will help to protect our waters and facilitate trade agreements with third countries in the context of regional initiatives to clean up water resources, such as the baltic sea action plan and the danube region strategy. the protection of europe's water resources is a priority and a responsibility towards future generations.
in writing. - i fully supported the report by mr newton dunn on the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household laundry detergents, because i believe that the report, despite its highly technical content, deals with a subject which is part of everyone's daily life. substances in detergents for washing machines, although necessary to ensure minimum standards of hygiene and health safety, can be harmful to the environment if present in excessive quantities, in particular they are responsible for the 'eutrophication of water'. eutrophication promotes the growth of algae and other plant species, which proliferate to the point of depriving other organisms of oxygen and releasing toxins that are highly harmful to our waters. the baltic sea alone receives 16,000 tons of phosphates a year, and the cost of removing the algae that periodically accumulates is quite high. i think we need to find a solution, by looking for substitutes for phosphates, which are equally effective but not harmful to the environment.
in writing. − the european union's priorities include the protection of the environment and the promotion of sustainable policies. in this case, today's vote is aimed at reducing the phosphorus content used in household washing machine detergents. phosphates often end up in water systems, rivers, streams, lakes, causing an overgrowth of algae and other plant species. this causes an overgrowth of algae that deprives other living organisms of oxygen and can also produce toxins, destroying fish species as well as other species and reducing the quality of the water itself. to avoid this environmental damage, the phosphorus content of detergents must be reduced. at the same time, we must think of small and mediumsized enterprises producing detergents for automatic dishwashers which do not yet have the know-how to produce detergents without phosphates, in order to avoid job losses.
in writing. − i voted against the extension of the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement for several reasons. the first is that we are facing a clear violation of international law. morocco is selling the natural resource of an occupied territory. according to the basics of international law, it would be able to do so only if the agreement were in accordance with the benefits and wishes of the local saharawi people. the moroccan government has failed to show any such benefits or wishes. in addition to that, of all the eu’s ongoing bilateral agreements, the deal with morocco is the worst. the rapporteur of the recommendation, along with an independent evaluation produced by the commission, plus the opinions of the development and budget committees and the assessment of authoritative un experts concur that the agreement is a waste of taxpayers’ money, it is ecologically and environmentally unsustainable and it has no significant macroeconomic effect on either the eu or morocco. for all these reasons i strongly believe that extending this agreement undermines the eu’s credibility as a defender of international law and as an impartial and equal institution.
in writing. - i am against the extension of the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement. the european commission's assessment of the previous agreement, which is being extended for a further year, is one of the worst ever for a fisheries agreement. the facts have shown that the agreement is ineffective in terms of costs and benefits to the moroccan economy and maritime infrastructure. only a small part of the funds made available has been used to support the fisheries sector in morocco and the agreement is proving costly and unable to achieve its objective of helping the economic and social development of the north african country. my vote in the plenary is therefore against, consistent with the negative assessment of the agreement in question.
in writing. - i am against the extension of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement with morocco for one year, as this protocol presents a number of problems both in terms of its economic usefulness and its ecological implications. the question of western sahara is also not to be overlooked. the agreement raises serious concerns about the ecological issue. we know that of the 11 demersal stocks fished in moroccan waters, 5 are overexploited, which raises concerns about the fishing carried out by european vessels. the question is whether the agreement on fishing for surplus stocks can be respected, given that they are running out. last but not least, there is the widespread problem of discards, shark catches and the likely capture of marine mammals by trawlers. the fisheries off the coast of western sahara are a controversial subject. we know that western sahara is a 'non-self-governing territory' as provided for in article 73 of the united nations charter. morocco has never been recognized as an official administering power by the un. the exploitation of this territory should, in my view, only be carried out if it is in the interests of the local population, and i do not think that the agreement, as currently drawn up, allows for this.
in writing. - my vote is in favour of the haglund report. the disappointing results of the four years of the fisheries agreement make it imperative to rethink the conditions set in 2006. i agree with the possibility of not extending the current agreement.
in writing. − the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement renews an initial fisheries agreement reached in 2006 and valid until february 2011. the agreement provides for the possibility of a fleet of european vessels, including an italian vessel, fishing off the moroccan coast. i think it is in the interests of the eu, of maritime traffic, of fish trade and the importance of relations with non-european countries that i should vote in favour of this partnership agreement.
in writing. - i am against the conclusion of the agreement with morocco because it will not benefit moroccan fishermen or european taxpayers. it will not benefit moroccan fishermen because it will not create new jobs and will increase the disproportion that already exists between the local fleet and fishing potential. it will not benefit european taxpayers because they will spend €13.5 million to subsidize morocco's fisheries policy, without guarantees that the funds will be used profitably. moreover, for every euro invested, european taxpayers will recover only 65 cents, less than half of what they recover on average under similar agreements.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the fishing industry, which is the main source of income for the eu. the difficulties in renewing the agreement stem from the fact that, while it does not exclude the possibility of fishing in western sahara, it does not clearly involve the saharawi people in its benefits. in this context, the council approved on 21 february a negotiating mandate for the commission to proceed with a provisional annual renewal of the agreement, pending more precise information on the involvement of local populations in the benefits of the agreement. the renewal is on 13 july 2011 and we are called this morning to give our opinion on this agreement. i have personally supported the conclusion of the provisional protocol (for a period of 12 months) pending clarification of the distribution of the benefits of the agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the appointment of benoit coeuré as a member of the european central bank. with his appointment, the ecb's board of governors once again has one representative from each member state. i think that at a delicate moment like the present one it is important that each member state, especially one as important as france, has its own representative who can contribute with his experience and knowledge to the daily work of the institute. at the same time, however, this national representativeness must not lead to the loss or risk of undermining the independence which has characterised the ecb's work in recent years and which has been fundamental in managing the crisis, resisting strong pressure from the member states. i would also like to thank mr lorenzo bini smaghi for the excellent work he has done during his tenure at the ecb.
in writing. - the considerations already made on the protocol already in force between morocco and the eu are, i believe, fundamental in view of a future protocol. given the financial contribution to the fisheries sector, it is essential that the cost-benefit ratio be changed, that more attention be paid to the economic and ecological consequences of overexploitation of depleted stocks. i hope that all the considerations already highlighted in the external report and those raised by parliament will be taken into account, on the assumption that bilateral agreements must be mutually beneficial and that the european union must not endorse any exploitation in the waters of western sahara or any other action which does not respect the rights of the population.
in writing. - in the context of the current economic crisis, we need to put military spending to work in the context of a continental rationalization. avoid costly national duplication in the field of defence, cooperate in scientific research for military purposes, create a european system for the coordination of military actions and international commitments in the field of counter-terrorism and conflict prevention: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i therefore vote in favour of the lisek report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr lisek. in recent years, as a result of the continuing economic crisis, member states have reduced their defence budgets, which has resulted in a shift in their responsibilities for peacekeeping. member states spend around €200 billion a year on defence, which is about one third of the us defence budget. the non-organized and uncoordinated management of these funds has led to a disproportionate dependence of europe on the us, resulting in persistent gaps in capacity, overcapacity and duplication, with the result that the union has neither the resources nor the influence to be considered a credible guarantor of peace. the european union's defence policies must be progressively integrated through coordination of defence planning, through capacity sharing, particularly in areas such as logistics, strategic and tactical, medical assistance, education and training. finally, a european union white paper on defence is desirable in order to develop a european security strategy, defining more clearly the objectives, interests and needs of the union in relation to the means available.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr lisek's report because i believe that the defence sector has suffered a setback which should not be underestimated, especially in view of the importance of the sector. from this point of view, the report proposes a european defence structure capable of optimising costs by exploiting the instruments of interstate and community coordination. such a structure, with the appropriate institutional bodies, should also serve to make economic operations (cost cuts or new structural models) concerning the defence sector more transparent and clear. i am convinced that this sector, which is strategic for the future of the eu, deserves due attention, both in terms of economic and financing policies and in terms of the appropriate measures to promote communication between the member states in order to improve efficiency and productivity.
in writing. − pooling and sharing defence capabilities is no longer an option but a necessity. all defence efforts undertaken by the european union in response to the financial crisis should be channelled to the european defence agency (eda). that is why the agency must be restructured. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - from the statistics that have been presented we can see that due to the severe crisis of recent years there have also been several cuts in the defence budgets, an area very important for the protection of our integrity. my vote in favour of this report is based on the idea that there can be no cutbacks in a sector such as the one mentioned above, which is essential for the security of any country. in order to avoid being caught off guard and unprepared for situations which may lead to conflict, it is always better to be protected and prepared.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, as a result of the economic and financial crisis, the fiscal consolidation in the european union and the reductions in defence budgets in most member states could lead to substantial programme cuts, reductions or delays for almost all member states, which is likely to continue to have a negative impact on the european defence industry and scientific progress in this field; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. in view of the importance of the facts and in agreement with all the amendments tabled, i shall vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - i fully support the conclusions of mr lisek's report. the defence sector is undoubtedly one of the most affected by the austerity policies resulting from the economic crisis. at this rate, europe risks not being able to meet its international responsibilities and to see some of its traditional strategic weaknesses, such as the duplication of military capabilities and the inability to conduct operations without american support, become more acute. to prevent such a scenario from occurring and to avoid draining funds from other important spending lines, the only effective solution, as highlighted in the report, is to proceed with increased cooperation within the union, while respecting national prerogatives; cooperation covering all areas of defence, but in particular the liberalisation of contracts, technological research, coordination of planning and the sharing of certain capabilities. greater cooperation would also allow european countries to increase their strategic autonomy and political influence within the atlantic alliance.
in writing. - one of the items cut most heavily from the state budget during the international economic and debt crisis is certainly defence. the trend towards cutting military spending, however, limits the european union's ability to effectively assume its responsibilities in peacekeeping. in this context, there is a need for greater coordination between the member states, as uncoordinated budget cuts could lead to the total disappearance of certain european military capabilities. member states should seek to exchange information, where appropriate, and improve transparency of current and future cuts in defence spending. the vote in favour underlines the need for common support for technological development in this field and the priority given to building a european defence industrial and technological base.
in writing. - i welcome this resolution on russia: i believe that it is essential to continue the partnership in the energy field and in the political field, especially in the light of the current world situation. the european union is also committed to the principle of mutual recognition of diplomas, certificates and other evidence of formal qualifications. the recent elections have shown that some of the habits of the past have not completely disappeared. paradoxically, this situation is damaging the majority party united russia first: the election victory was still a foregone conclusion, perhaps with lower percentages. we hear about the russian spring, often from the very people who once praised soviet ideology, the consequences of which russia today still pays, with strong traces in its structure and within society. perhaps it is convenient for them to distort reality: there is no real alternative in russia at the moment to lead the country and keep it among the world's leading players. i condemn repression and all forms of violence, the right to speak and to demonstrate are inalienable values, among the foundations of the europe we all represent. i wonder why the reaction to russia's events is not the same as the recent american events related to the occupy movement street protests.
in writing. the resolution adopted by parliament on the eu-russia summit anticipates a summit of historic importance as it will coincide with russia's accession to the world trade organisation. my position on this is absolutely positive, this new opening will favour both russia's internal development and the resulting bilateral relations with the eu. the more favourable climate in relations, with the enlargement of markets, the opening up of transport, the liberalisation of short-stay visas and specific agreements on local traffic between the eu-russia border areas, will certainly be positive and beneficial for all and will, above all, strengthen the foreign and security policy.
in writing. parliament rightly calls for an immediate investigation into all reports of fraud and intimidation during the elections in russia on 4 december and expresses its support for the demonstrations of the past few days, which it considers to be an expression of the popular will. the conduct of the elections has shown that russia does not comply with the electoral standards set by the organisation for economic cooperation and development (osce). i am deeply concerned about the preliminary findings of the osce inquiry, which report a number of allegations of procedural violations such as fraud, lack of impartiality in the media, harassment of independent observers and lack of separation between state and party. the registration process for the election round effectively excluded numerous opposition parties and compromised freedom of association, political competition and pluralism from the very beginning of the election campaign. i therefore ask the president of the european council, the president of the european commission and the high representative for the eu's foreign policy to raise this issue at the next eu-russia summit on 15 december.
in writing. the second eu-russia summit of the year will take place in brussels tomorrow, 15 december. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. in principle, negotiations for a new bilateral agreement could also be relaunched, particularly as regards trade rules. the other important outcome expected is the adoption of the so-called 'common steps' towards a possible future short-term visa liberalisation. this is essentially a series of measures which take up the terms of the branding charts and action plans approved for the balkan and eastern european countries. i think we should welcome the conclusion of the negotiations on the common steps: the prospect of visa liberalisation in the future, by facilitating contacts between the peoples, should indeed contribute to the modernisation of the country.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i believe that the review of the european neighbourhood policy creates an opportunity for the eu to meet its objectives and to acknowledge the mistakes of eu and member states’ policy with regard, in particular, to the complacent approach towards the former tyrannies of the southern neighbourhood. it is fundamental to stress that the enp is based on shared values such as democracy, the rule of law, the fight against corruption and good governance. we must consider that it is in the highest interest of the eu to be ambitious in economic cooperation to support the defence of human rights. i also agree on the necessity to improve the role of the european parliament and to insist on the need to systematically include civil-society organisations at all stages of the review process.
in writing. - the report on neighbourhood policy stresses in many places the desirability of facilitating immigration from neighbouring countries to member countries. the rapporteur believes that the conditions for the passage of legal immigrants to europe should be improved, immigration itself facilitated by concluding partnerships on mobility, taking due account of the demographic, social and employment situation of both the country of origin and the country of destination. in addition, the issue of immigration should be seen as an opportunity, not so much from the point of view of possible security implications, and it would therefore be necessary to facilitate visa liberalization in order to move towards a free movement regime, in any case working towards facilitating the issuing of visas as much as possible. i do not agree with the basic principle that immigration should be seen as an opportunity, regardless of the consequences for the security and social and economic environment of our countries, and i am opposed to the basic policy suggested in the report, which is to facilitate the issuing of visas and the procedures for entry into europe for immigrants from neighbouring countries. i therefore vote against the report.
in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteurs who have jointly produced this important work to which i have given my positive vote. the european union must focus its efforts on its neighbourhood policy through a careful and constant dialogue aimed at promoting universal values such as the rule of law, democracy, good governance and human dignity, in accordance with the principles of conditionality and specificity, as not all processes are equal and require differential treatment depending on the country. in particular, for the countries south of the mediterranean, europe must accompany this transition by representing, on the political scene, a credible partner, guarantor of democracy and peace, through support for civil society. it is therefore necessary to involve in this process above all young people and women, who represent an important potential for the development of these societies. the democratic changes must be strongly supported by promoting cooperation and integration between the countries of this region in order to remove existing obstacles such as those to the free movement of people and goods. europe must and will be an example to the thousands of young people who are waiting for concrete answers.
in writing. - this report deals in an excellent way with all the major issues of democracy and the rule of law in the field of immigration, especially as regards the fight against poverty. in this connection, i would ask everyone to realize that the strengthening of the european union's relations with its neighbours in the mediterranean and eastern europe is now more essential than ever. this new approach is consistent with the reforms undertaken by our partners and at the same time provides an opportunity to share our democratic values embodied in the rule of law and good governance. i would like to stress, however, that the values we transmit and the changes themselves must be aimed at fully meeting the specific needs of individuals who have had the courage to reject oppressive situations, without however being invasive. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. the revision of the european neighbourhood policy is necessary in the face of the changes brought about by the so-called 'arab spring' in the north african countries, which are still engaged in a long process of economic, political and social reconstruction. i believe that the european neighbourhood policy must be redesigned, looking at the developments and changes that the neighbouring countries are experiencing and facing over the months. in this sense, i think it is appropriate to adopt a more regionalist approach to this policy, which takes account of the differences and specificities of individual cases. in this context, the european union is called upon to play a key and substantial role in stimulating the emergence of new forms of democracy in neighbouring countries. the european neighbourhood policy therefore has a wide scope and addresses all those areas of interest which actively contribute to the process of democratic construction. protection of children's rights, freedom of expression and information, economic and commercial rights, are some of the aspects which will need to be monitored and encouraged more and more in the neighbouring countries, which are facing important and decisive challenges of change.
in writing. − in the full interest of the eu's neighbourhood policy objectives, tangible and credible incentives must be provided to neighbourhood countries to commit themselves to the common goal of bringing about a full-fledged democracy. the rapporteur rightly stresses the importance of monitoring bodies and also the need to encourage partnership from below, from society.
in writing. - i cannot but vote in favour of a point like this. the neighbourhood policy is one of the strengths on which we must work, but above all we must cooperate, because if we cannot support each other, it will be difficult to carry out concrete projects that can develop and consolidate the relationships created over time and sometimes built with great effort.
in writing. − considering that the union for the mediterranean was established with the ambitious aim of acting as a permanent instrument in strengthening relations with the countries of the southern neighbourhood, it is necessary to highlight the existing differences which can be an obstacle to relations. in this context, relations with these countries must be reoriented towards cooperation, which gives priority to democracy and prosperity on both sides of the mediterranean, and not just security and immigration control. in the light of the following considerations, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - there are many points in common with the report presented by mr siwiec and mr david: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to support them. i do not share a few of its conclusions on immigration. the proposal to liberalize visas quickly, for example, seems to me to be a proposal that will cause discomfort to indigenous peoples and migrants, at least until the economic and social systems of europe and neighbouring countries are similar. the same applies to the idea of decoupling migration flows from security, a key link in preventing social tensions in areas of economic poverty.
in writing. - we voted today in plenary on the own-initiative report which highlights the role of cohesion policy in reducing economic, social and territorial disparities, creating new jobs, increasing growth, building infrastructure, ensuring the cohesive development of the eu through its specific objectives and instruments, and thus meeting the economic and social needs of european citizens. cohesion policy was among the first to adopt its regional dimension, representing its added value and helping to ensure its effectiveness and sustainability. the way each member state exploits the opportunities offered by membership of the european single market depends on its maturity and level of development, which vary from country to country. it follows that it is the responsibility of each member state to indicate the most effective measures to enable its economy to function within the global system. the report proposes new directions for the future architecture of the policy, to strengthen its performance, to ensure strong sustainable growth and increased global competitiveness.
in writing. − the new neighbourhood policy instrument aims to strengthen bilateral relations with partner countries and bring tangible benefits on such fronts as democracy, human rights, the rule of law, bilateral, regional and crossborder cooperation programmes. the new guidelines for future eu cooperation concern the countries of the eastern neighbourhood, but also nine countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean. the new guidelines have several key elements, ranging from the principle of 'more money to the most virtuous' in the field of reforms to the democratization process. another priority is to reduce the complexity and time-consuming nature of the intervention planning process by simplifying the requirements for implementing eu projects. another need will be to focus european support on key objectives and to strengthen member states' cooperation with partner countries along the union's external borders.
in writing. − the report on the european neighbourhood policy emphasises the relations between the eu and neighbouring countries, recalls the importance of building a partnership with civil societies in these countries in order to promote the democratisation process and stresses the need to create free trade areas. the text unfortunately recalls that the eu should improve the management and maximise the mutual benefits of development migration by encouraging legal labour immigration and facilitating visa procedures. at a time of crisis such as the one we are living in, when community workers are in danger of losing their jobs, such proposals are out of place. for these reasons, i am voting against.
in writing. − the review of the european neighbourhood policy should as a matter of priority lead to a strengthening of eu support to the countries of the southern shore of the mediterranean, especially in the current crisis context, both in terms of resources allocated and in terms of how they are used. i share the aim of giving greater importance to democratic reforms and the rule of law, but i note that an approach based on mere differentiation on the basis of merit or 'performance' is not without risks of marginalisation for the less virtuous countries, which pose greater problems from the point of view of security and stability. the reorientation of funds towards the areas of political and governance reforms, if not accompanied by an increase in overall resources, could paradoxically also lead to a reduction in aid in the very socioeconomic sectors that triggered the uprisings in the south. the union's action in the neighbourhood must continue to be guided by uniform principles and criteria, and must be the expression of a single policy, without foreshadowing privileged paths for some neighbours to the detriment of others.
in writing. − terrorism is a serious threat to international stability and to the security of european society. the first decade of the 21st century has been marked by the fight against terrorism. the sense of security of the european population has decreased significantly following terrorist attacks on european soil, such as those in madrid in 2004 and london in 2005. the fight against terrorism therefore requires a coordinated international response and a global approach based on intelligence, police, judicial, political and, exceptionally, military instruments. the eu's counter-terrorism policy must therefore be in line with its foreign policy and internal security strategy. nevertheless, especially at a time when the neighbouring arab countries are moving closer to democracy, the union has a duty to serve as a moral compass, and not just towards its own citizens. the union's counter-terrorism policy must also always be designed to act in full respect of the human rights and fundamental freedoms of all citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it clearly underlines that the union’s external actions to combat international terrorism should be aimed at prevention. the text also highlights the need to promote dialogue, tolerance and understanding among different cultures, civilisations and religions. tracking and prosecution of terrorist activities must be part of a systematic approach based not on emergency but on a coherent, necessity-founded strategy. at european level i believe that one of the biggest problems is the absence of proper evaluation of eu counter-terrorism action. this evaluation should be carried out by an international multilateral body involved in crime and criminal law. the commission must fully assess the set of counter-terrorism policies and focus on future challenges, including the reform of europol and eurojust in the light of the new potentialities offered by the lisbon treaty.
in writing. the report on counter-terrorism policy comes to the plenary after a passage in the commission which did not allow for the inclusion of important and crucial amendments which were aimed at giving the text a stronger imprint and more in line with the real needs of the fight against terrorism in europe. the need to update and increase the databases with appropriate technological means, and the need to protect the victims of terrorism with appropriate national and community policies, has not been included. the eu's priorities in this area have not been to raise awareness among european citizens of the emergence of terrorism in our society. it has not been accepted to recognise the well-known fact that uncontrolled immigration and youth unemployment, especially within certain immigrant communities, are a prime recruiting ground for terrorist activities and transnational terrorist organisations. i therefore vote against the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this formulation of the eu's counter-terrorism strategy. the threat of terrorist attacks in the european union remains serious and the links between terrorism and organised crime are growing. terrorist acts seriously jeopardise human rights, threaten democracy and aim to destabilise legitimately constituted governments, thereby weakening pluralistic civil societies. i therefore stress the need for the eu, its member states and its partner countries to base their strategy for combating terrorism on promoting dialogue, tolerance and understanding between different cultures, civilizations and religions. we must therefore expand existing strategic counter-terrorism partnerships with countries outside europe and create new ones. the prevention, investigation and prosecution of terrorist activities are crucial policies at eu level and must be part of a systematic approach based on a coherent strategy. it is important that these strategies are effective in terms of objectives and costs, avoiding duplication of measures and improper use by the institutions, agencies and bodies concerned.
in writing. the commission's communication is too narrow in its scope. the rapporteur is right to say that national policies to combat terrorism or national measures transposing policies agreed at european or international level must also be taken into account. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - in the light of the last 10 years of the fight against terrorism following the attacks of 11 september, i think it is important to reiterate with all of you the cornerstones of the fight against terrorism. i also believe that the eu must have a common anti-terrorism policy which is effective in preventing and protecting citizens, prosecuting terrorism-related offences and responding to such acts. a policy with firm positions that requires broad consensus, as expressed in the resolution by mrs in't velt, which i supported, and which is in defence of the state and in defence of fundamental rights.
in writing. − following the horrific attacks of 11 september 2001, the first decade of the 21st century has been characterised by the 'war on terrorism', whereas in recent years the european union has been increasingly targeted and victimized by terrorism and faces a constant threat. however, the absence of a clear and universally accepted definition of terrorism hinders discussions about terrorism and how to combat it. although i cannot agree with all the amendments tabled, i would like to vote in favour of the idea of giving the eu counter-terrorism policies a boost to achieve their objectives.
in writing. − counter-terrorism measures must correspond to the threat level and must be regulated to prevent risks, so it is important that the european commission documents as counter-terrorism policies of the various states and national are compensated and coordinated. an amendment which is fundamental to us, and which states that surveillance is a fundamental element in preventing illegal acts, was not adopted. equally important are the collection of personal data, the evaluation of best detection and identification technologies, the exchange of data and the risk assessment. it is amazing how much the eu is committed to helping the united states to solve the problem of the guantanamo prison, which, as a third country, is not really subject to any kind of control on our part. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. elements such as cyberterrorism, irregular immigration and phenomena related to the risk of recruitment from disadvantaged classes were not considered. for these reasons, the vote was against.
in writing. - in the first decade of the third millennium, the european union has been the constant target and victim of international terrorism of a political and religious nature, as witness the attacks in madrid in 2004 and london in 2005. the 2011 europol report indicates that the threat of terrorist attacks in the european union remains serious and that the links between terrorism and organised crime appear to be growing. we must not let our guard down, but we must study and analyse the new frontiers of terrorism, such as cyberterrorism, new structures, means and funding. the main objective of european policies in the fight against terrorism must be to protect and strengthen the fabric of democratic societies by strengthening civil liberties and democratic control. today's vote means more security for citizens and more prevention against terrorist acts.

in writing. the cashman report on public access to european institutions' documents takes account of a fundamental value, enshrined in the treaty, which is that of transparency. the provisions for the implementation of this right are contained in regulation 1049/2001, which is intended to be amended by this legislative procedure. in its proposal the commission expresses an 'open' position, which i believe the rapporteur wants to extend far beyond the objective of transparency, putting at risk the protection of personal and sensitive data. mr cashman also defines 'document' as all data and content which is in any way connected with the policies, measures and decisions of all the eu institutions, including preparatory, confidential and informal documents, i.e. any piece of information. the "space to think" is thus minimized. i believe that the value of transparency and democratic participation of citizens in the life of the institutions is fundamental, but it should be reconciled with other fundamental values, such as the protection of personal and sensitive data and concern official documents and not just the procedure for the adoption of decisions.

the agenda includes the report by mr mathieu grosch, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, on the roadmap to a single european transport area towards a competitive and sustainable transport policy (2011/2096 ((ini)) (a7-0425/2011)
mr president, tomorrow we will vote and adopt this strategic direction for the future of transport, but we already have some legislative acts on the table. i congratulate the rapporteur on the fact that in just three months he has succeeded in converging an important document which will keep us in touch for the foreseeable future. i would like to recall the following essential points: the creation of a genuine single market in all transport sectors, because administrative and technical barriers discourage competition by preventing the cost of transport services from falling. the reference is clearly to the railway sector, whose situation is unacceptable 25 years after the adoption of the single act. the list of barriers to this sector is a luxury we cannot afford at a time when the market is the way out and the means of reviving our economy. i am thinking in particular of the opening up of national passenger transport markets, the creation of a european regulator, the implementation of rtms technology throughout the tnt network. the infrastructure was mentioned, the cross-border infrastructure in particular, and of course the last mile link between the nodes and the axes. the financing of infrastructure is unthinkable because the funds entered in the budget will only enable us to achieve what is planned: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the dossier we have, called the projet bond, deals with these guarantees, but we want to go beyond road safety, because we have to consider all aspects of the problem: driver, medium, infrastructure and their interaction. the single sky, finally, the technological pillar cesar, which must be completed, but at the same time we must work on a single governance. the commissioner has assured us that there will be ambitious proposals next year, and we are really looking forward to them.
in writing. the white paper on transport aims to improve the quality of transport in europe. mobility plays a key role in the internal market as it is a prerequisite for economic development and growth. the challenge is to develop sustainable transport, but we must also aim to build an efficient intermodal transport network. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the transport system is truly competitive in all transport sectors, and the road transport sector, which in some member states is one of the pillars of the production and economic system, is facing a number of particular difficulties. in this connection, i am in favour of the creation of an authority with responsibility for road transport, which will be able to promote the harmonization of the member states in areas such as environmental sustainability, safety, vocational training and certification, accompanying the process of liberalization and solving the challenges of the sector, in a way similar to what has been considered to be done in rail transport.
author of the book. - mr president, i am honoured to have been the initiator of this debate in the house. it seems to me that european prisons suffer from at least two problems. the first is that there is a great difficulty in getting the instruments of european democracy into these institutions. the human rights of prisoners are violated, and the dignity of the person is violated, both in relation to the prisoners and to those who work there, such as the prison guards. prisons are overcrowded, a symbol of the lack of investment: people are crowded and the door is closed. knowledge of prison regulations is scarce, whereas they should be distributed and transparently known to all. the principle of re-education which prisons should assume is being abdicated, even by no longer facilitating work for prisoners within the prison. there is little transparency, little openness to citizens, schools, ngos! the cuts threaten essential services and staff training and we have a general lack of interest from the media and politics. i'll move on to the second point. personally, following the initiative launched by marco pannella in italy, i have visited two prisons every august for three years - the symbolically most holiday-filled day - and have been struck by the lack of a european dimension in prisons. there is no exchange of best practice, and there are few opportunities for comparison between staff and operators from the various european countries. i therefore welcome the publication of this green paper, which will help to clarify a number of points: how to improve mutual trust and, of course, prison conditions; how to link the conditions of detention with the european precautionary order, the european arrest warrant, the conditions of minors, the power of inspection, the rights of family visits and all the activities of cultural mediators, which is necessary. the council is here today and many answers depend on it. it is a test of civilization, of european identity. prisons will always be prisons. i do not think that the solution lies in emptying them, they must cease to be those dark corners of european rights and responsibilities.
author of the book. - mr president, there is no doubt that one of the indicators of the degree of civilization in a society is the conditions of prisoners. overcrowding is a constant feature of many member states, also because of the considerable presence of nationals from third countries: the number of prisoners is particularly significant, some 650,000. there is a right, as well as a duty, to serve the sentence on the part of the prisoner, provided, of course, that the dignity and decency of the person are guaranteed. we believe that there should be a uniform and homogeneous treatment and we believe that cooperation and trust between member states can only exist if there is a uniform treatment of prisoners. it's not like that! there are some particularly complex situations in the member states which will need to be investigated further. of course, these are questions of awaiting trial and pretrial detention, which are not always used with caution and prudence in many member states. there is also the question of reintegration into employment, rehabilitation and social redemption, because these are people who must be given a chance. there is the problem of hard prison for those who have been guilty of serious crimes - first and foremost mafia, organised crime and terrorism. in these cases, of course, the attention threshold must always remain very high. mutual recognition in judicial matters between member states can be useful. we would like the commission and the council to show more courage by identifying this priority in the list of measures to be implemented - why not - with more means and more resources to expand and modernise prison facilities - there is a specific provision in the stockholm programme. at the same time, member states must also provide for alternative measures to facilitate the reintegration of prisoners: dignity and decency must always be offered to the person.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank the committee on international trade and its rapporteur, mr cutaş, for this interim report. first, the object of this consent procedure is an amendment to the partnership and cooperation agreement with uzbekistan concerning trade in textiles. its only objective is to ensure that textile exports from the eu to uzbekistan would get most-favoured-nation treatment. so let us keep clearly in mind that we are talking about an agreement that gives legal certainty to the eu and does not grant any benefits to uzbekistan itself. the commission is well aware of the problem of child labour in the cotton sector in uzbekistan and fully shares parliament’s concerns in this respect. we have already been monitoring for quite some time uzbekistan’s compliance with its obligations in the field of child labour under the conventions of the international labour organisation (ilo) and the relevant united nations conventions. the eu regularly relays concerns about forced child labour in the country in its political dialogue with uzbekistan. the country has taken some steps to address the problem, notably by ratifying two ilo conventions concerning child labour and by setting up a national legislative framework against forced labour and child labour. however, what matters is not only the ratification but the actual implementation of these conventions. in this respect, it is a fact that the use of child labour in the cotton sector in uzbekistan is still an issue of concern. therefore the commission will, in close cooperation with the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, continue to monitor the situation and actively scale up its efforts to urge the uzbek government to take the necessary steps to fully implement the ilo conventions. we undertook a mission to uzbekistan in november 2011. the eu team enjoyed the full cooperation of the uzbek authorities and discussions with international organisations confirmed some positive changes in certain regions during this year’s harvest. the uzbek authorities showed new openness to discuss the issue and there have been some positive signs about cooperation with the ilo. the uzbek side emphasised that the problem can only be handled by means of a gradual approach, notably by restructuring and diversifying the agricultural sector so as to reduce dependency on the cotton sector. we fully agree with parliament – and this has been our message to the uzbek authorities – that the best way to have a clear and accurate picture of the situation would be to allow the ilo to undertake a mission to the country. the commission is open to make the necessary arrangements with parliament to jointly monitor the situation in cooperation with the relevant international institutions and to regularly assess the situation with a view to resuming this consent procedure as soon as reasonably possible. while we fully understand the justified human rights concerns, we are of the view that an agreement that serves only the eu deserves to receive the consent of the european parliament in a timely manner.
