the agenda for the joint debate includes:- the commission statement on the recent council decisions and the commission's review of the egf regulation, and- the report by barbara matera, on behalf of the committee on budgets, on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, in accordance with point 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (application egf/2009/019 fr/renault from france) (com (2011) 0420 c7-0193/2011 2011/2158 bud)) (a7-0396/2011)
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, almost 23 million people are unemployed in europe today and more than 113 million are at risk of poverty and exclusion. in this context, the european union plays a crucial role in financing areas of social investment which are difficult to support by the member states, whose finances are being put to the test by the economic crisis which is weighing heavily on us all. every year, instruments such as the european social fund, the globalisation adjustment fund, the progress programme - to name just a few - provide support to millions of european citizens, improving their skills, broadening their employment prospects, promoting self-employment and labour mobility. the european globalisation adjustment fund is a new fund, the main objective of which is to provide support for workers made redundant as a result of changes in world trade flows by co-financing active labour market policies. in the light of the rapid escalation of the economic and financial crisis in 2008, the european commission proposed a temporary derogation from the igf regulation due to expire at the end of this year, in order to broaden the scope of the igf to provide support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic crisis and by increasing the igf co-financing rate from 50 to 65% for member states. i have seen from my own experience as the igf standing rapporteur for the committee on budgets that the adoption of this amendment has allowed the fund to be used more extensively. in fact, in the 28 months of the igf's existence, before the entry into force of this derogation, only 15 applications for funding were submitted and involved, i say "only" 18 000 redundant workers. but it was just after the approval of this derogation that the applications quadrupled. member states also indicated that without the temporary derogation it would have been impossible to support 45,000 workers made redundant by their companies due to the economic and financial crisis. moreover, with the increased co-financing rate to 65%, the burden of financing borne by the member states has enabled them to support their workers and their businesses in a timely manner. ladies and gentlemen, the european commission's economic forecasts foresee that a substantial recovery in labour market conditions at european level is not expected before 2013. these assessments, together with the difficulties facing member states' budgets as a result of fiscal consolidation efforts, therefore force us to consider the current extension of the deadline for this month to be effective from 1 january 2012 to be necessary. unfortunately, however, the examination of this proposal by the council on 2 december resulted in several delegations - the netherlands, germany, sweden, denmark, the united kingdom, latvia, the czech republic and slovakia - opposing the commission's proposal and blocking the extension of this derogation. i would like to conclude, mr president, by saying that this act of the council is truly irresponsible. the fund is seen by public opinion as an important solidarity instrument for the financial support of our citizens and of workers made redundant. we cannot allow the council to block the extension of the extension and i hope that all members will symbolically support the report which will be in favour of the 3,500 redundant workers at renault.
the rapporteur. - madam president, first of all i am pleased with the warmth with which the debate in the house today was approached by my colleagues, because this fund deserved it, but above all its objective and its argument deserved it: we are talking about solidarity with the european citizens! we are now at the end of 2011 and i want to conclude with a final speech in the chamber with good wishes for the coming year. my first wish is that the next danish presidency of the council will put on its political agenda the importance of supporting the economic crisis derogation for this fund until 2013. the second wish is that the european commission may continue to support the extension of the scope of this fund, so as to include the agricultural sector, which will certainly suffer as a result of the economic crisis which is expected to continue in the coming years, by also supporting the agricultural sector. finally, i would like to appeal to my colleagues - and i regret that some of them have already left - to support this report today, which will result in a disbursement of some eur 24 million to renault and consequently to the french member state. this is a great sign of the solidarity, unity and cohesion of the european parliament, because i am convinced - and i think you are absolutely convinced too - that this parliament cannot and must not be the forum for the release of all the inaccuracies, choices and reforms that are taking place within the member states. i therefore trust in the sense of responsibility of all colleagues: i do not want to and cannot believe that some people will abstain or vote against the renault case simply because they want and must follow the priority of the electoral calendar of their own member state! i do not think so, i am sure they will be responsible and will enable us to give new vigour and credibility to this fund which would be seriously undermined if our colleagues did not vote unanimously in favour of the disbursement of these funds.
member of the commission. − madam president, i should like to thank the members for their comments. i have three short remarks: the first on the crisis derogation. fortunately the misunderstanding was clarified. yes, the commission wanted an extension until the end of 2013, but this was voted down by a blocking minority, including some states which benefited from the scheme. there were good reasons for extending the scheme due to the developments in the labour market, with a sudden recent acceleration of applications – two thirds of all the applications came in 2010 and 2011. i can agree with ms ţicǎu that countries in eastern europe undergoing the so-called transformation from the old system to the new system know how painful this might be without globalisation, as our countries can neither be termed developed or under-developed parts of the world; this was rather a mis-developed part of the world, with a lot of industrial stock on the ground but completely useless in terms of a market economy. my second remark concerns renault. thank you, mr gauzès, for explaining the action from the local point of view. i can only say that i know a special unit has been set up by renault to deal with the issue. our prerogative is to monitor and contact, but i can assure all of you that, from the legal point of view, this case fulfilled all the criteria of the european globalisation fund application. what matters is the future: as the globalisation fund is on the table in the proposal for 2014-2020, this means that we fully understand the added value of the fund in terms of making the reactions of the member states more durable and of improved quality in terms of active labour market policy. what is clear from the mid-term review is that exactly 42% of the workers covered by the scheme under this crisis derogation were able very quickly to find places on the job market. so this is working and is probably very conducive to the reintegration of redundant workers into the labour market. i agree fully with those who ask for a much quicker response by the globalisation fund. this is as slow as the solidarity fund, which is also part of the proposal. what was very controversial – and here the remarks of mr daerden and ms cornelissen are relevant – is whether to extend it to farming. this was done in a very clear context, and the context, as i can reveal, was going into the mercosur trade liberalisation talks with insecurity in the rural areas around the impact of trade liberalisation on the farming community. for my colleagues, and especially the one responsible for this major deal on trade liberalisation, this was a kind of insurance cover for entering into the trade liberalisation agreements with countries with more competitive pricing for agricultural products. this was the context of the decision to risk the extension of the globalisation fund to farming. but this is not at the cost of industrial workers, because we have our estimates in the pipeline, and i think the numbers proposed could be adequate as insurance for both areas: industry and farming. but i can agree with mr alvaro and the others that this is keine wunderwaffe: this is one of the tools in the toolbox for dealing with a crisis: valuable, therefore extended and should be defended, because this is also a tangible and visible sign in several corners of the european union that the european institutions are useful, credible and could help.

the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the internal market. over 500 projects funded, more than 3,000 partners involved - most of them small and medium-sized enterprises - not to mention the added value that the programme itself has brought to the renewable energy and energy efficiency sectors. like my colleagues, i am concerned about the future of the programme, which has played a central role in raising awareness, exchanging good practice and implementing the european union's energy policies. i therefore ask the european commission what it intends to do to continue the programme, because to stop it would be to frustrate the many hopes; i would like to ask you, finally, what is the heading of the multiannual plan which will provide the necessary funding.
member of the commission. − madam president, you do not need to convince me or the commission about the usefulness of a programme that is performing so well. this usefulness and cost-effectiveness can be seen in a programme with a not-so-big budget of eur 743 million that still has a huge leverage effect and impact on energy efficiency and renewable energy in the european union. as regards the involvement of small and medium-size companies, only part of the 3 000 partners – that is 1 500 partners – can be classified as small and medium-sized companies. the position of parliament was not only visible as regards the awards; parliament was able to increase the budget for this programme for 2011 by eur 10 million and for 2012 by eur 7.5 million. this is a commitment which is expressed in budgetary lines as well. the programme will not disappear. the commitment cannot disappear because this is so conducive to the goals of the 2020 strategy, and energy efficiency is among the seven priority areas of the strategy for the future of europe. we also have to respond to the need for mainstreaming programmes. mainstreaming is clearly indicated in all the evaluations of various programmes of the european union. given the constraints of not being able to spend more money, we need in future to look at better spending. this is about the mainstreaming of programmes, not the disappearance of a programme that is performing so well. what is the future of this programme? it will be placed under a consistent framework which links research development and market update within the growing envelope for horizon 2020 – growing from eur 50 billion to eur 80 billion. the energy component is classified as secure, clean and efficient energy. we cannot give up on the issue of energy security on the continent, on which we will be so dependent in the coming years. energy security is an important aspect of horizon 2020. it is clearly the place for an energy component which is classified as clean and efficient energy; it is the place for intelligent energy and for a dedicated element of this energy component. so it is going to be a very visible commitment, in monetary terms as well. of course this is not the only place to find money for intelligent, renewable and efficient energy. as you probably know, this is high in the hierarchy of the goals of the structural funds, which attract a much larger amount of money in so-called interim regions, namely the regions with a per capita gdp of less than 90% of the european union average. there is a very limited range of goals, and energy efficiency is the number one area of the structural funds to which funding is to be committed in this type of region of europe. so we are looking at the position of intelligent energy in the multiannual framework. this could be more than eur 1 billion instead of eur 700 million, for example; i cannot give exact figures today, but i know that this is a growing envelope. therefore, visibility and financial commitment is to be guaranteed in the multiannual framework for 2014-2020. the role of the european parliament is very clear in shaping the future by shaping the rules of the game in this component of the multiannual framework.

in writing. the report on the european maritime safety agency was voted on today in plenary. the european maritime safety agency (emsa) was set up in response to the oil spill caused by the sinking of the oil tanker erika. the agency started its activities in march 2003. the emsa's founding regulation has been amended three times. the commission's latest proposal should aim to introduce lasting changes, although more time will be needed for negotiations. the report argues that emsa's increased tasks will need to be realistically reflected in its budget and staffing so that it can cope with the new tasks proposed by the commission: contribute to traffic monitoring systems with a view to achieving a european maritime area without barriers; assist the commission and the member states in preventing pollution from oil spills by increasing the role of the existing cleanseanet; assisting neighbouring countries in reducing pollution risks.
in writing. − the european maritime safety agency was set up in response to the oil spill caused by the sinking of the oil tanker erika and started its activities in march 2003. the emsa's founding regulation has been amended three times. the latter proposal should aim to introduce lasting changes, although more time will be needed for negotiations. the parliament's resolution of 7 october 2010 states that emsa's mandate 'should be extended from ships to offshore installations' and calls for 'the possible conferral of new functions of this kind to be reflected in emsa's budget and staff'. the additional tasks of emsa must be realistically reflected in the agency's budget and staff. otherwise, its essential function of promoting maritime safety could be jeopardised.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the text tabled by mr fleckenstein amending the regulation establishing emsa, the european maritime safety agency. by clarifying the agency's tasks more specifically than in the past, the changes introduced are aimed at achieving greater efficiency and lower costs: the various tasks of emsa will therefore include assistance in preventing pollution from offshore oil and gas installations, combating piracy and illegal maritime traffic, and strengthening traffic monitoring systems to achieve a european maritime area without barriers.
in writing. - the situation in syria is not, unfortunately, the simplest. the discussions in this area are becoming more and more heated because of the continuing criticism. since last spring, we have been experiencing a period of hard clashes and demonstrations all over the syrian territory, in order to obtain something that we, all of us, are exporters and custodians of, democracy. in these parts of the world, sometimes the word democracy, people power, seems like a utopia, something so far away and so unattainable that it's considered a threat. those in power cannot conceive of cooperation, equality and peaceful dialogue between the parties for the sake of building a better state and for their own seat, for their own prestige, they are willing to risk the destruction of their own people. the current situation is still dramatic, and there is a need for greater respect and an immediate solution.
in writing. - we have voted today a compromise resolution by various political groups strongly condemning the repression of civilians by the damascus government. i personally follow developments in syria with concern, particularly as i consider it necessary to give serious thought to the prospects for a way out of the crisis before even looking for solutions that could have potentially even more destabilising long-term consequences. while it is absolutely essential and necessary to ensure respect for freedom of expression and above all the safety of citizens, it is equally important to consider the perspective of the international community and in particular to ensure that, if there is a change at the top of the institutional hierarchy, this does not happen by replacing officials who would disturb the already fragile political balance of the region.
in writing. − in the light of the continuing deterioration of the situation in syria, eu efforts to increase pressure on the assad regime continue. the eu has been saying since last august that assad has lost all legitimacy and must step aside. the list of persons subject to restrictive measures was extended last november, in parallel with a suspension of european investment bank loans to syria. sanctions in the oil and investment sectors were adopted in september and strengthened on 1 december. measures have also been added concerning telephone and internet interception equipment. the possibility of creating a humanitarian corridor in syria has also been recently discussed. in conclusion, and in the light of all that has been said, i believe that strengthening the eu-turkey dialogue on the prospects for the syrian crisis could be the best solution, given the key role played by ankara.
in writing. - i voted against this report. certainly, many of the points it contains are more than agreeable. i refer in particular to the paragraphs calling for the liberalization of the railways, which would particularly benefit the italian railway market. however, the report's unquestioning support for the ten-t project is problematic. this project, which concerns the construction of trans-european rail, motorway and river networks, is showing increasingly critical aspects. this is a "pharaonic" project whose feasibility is in doubt, both from the financial and the design point of view, as evidenced by the slow and ambiguous progress made so far. as the lega nord has always maintained, our territory does not need grandiose, unrealizable works, but rather greater attention to its concrete and immediate needs. at the moment, the whole management of the ten-t project seems superficial and poorly planned, and that is why i cannot express a favourable opinion on this.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a common transport area is an important achievement for the european union and its citizens. i believe that the creation of such a space is essential in order to increase the economic efficiency of the sector and the protection of the environment, but also to ensure better social and employment conditions for the citizens of our community. transport is of fundamental importance to citizens as it ensures their freedom of movement within the union. they also constitute a pillar for the development of the union, for social cohesion between the various member states and help to make the eu a strategic centre for research and innovation. the creation of a single european area is therefore a factor of connection with regional, environmental, social, economic and employment policy. i therefore hope that the transport regulations will be harmonized so that each country can make long-term investments in the sector, so as to allow the economy to recover, especially in the light of the economic and financial crisis which has hit us hard.
in writing. − the citizens of the european union would greatly benefit from the creation of a single european transport area that would remove all barriers between transport modes and national systems and be free from distortions of competition and social dumping. mr grosch's report goes in that direction and i therefore vote in favour of it.
in writing. - i abstain because, although the objectives are shared, the report does not address issues which in the long term could jeopardise the construction of railway sections which are considered important. as far as italy is concerned, the main problem is that the state railways are showing a lack of interest, probably because they still have a near monopoly on the railway networks. the commission has proposed to strengthen the authority of private coordinators and the european commission in order to oblige disadvantaged local authorities such as rfi to agree to the needs of ten-t projects and their coordinators. such a choice would constitute an interference with the national sovereignty of the member states. the extremely positive part of the text is the choice of the definitive liberalisation of the railway networks which would put an end to the de facto monopoly held by the state railways in our country. as the operator of the rfi railway network and the treni italia operator owned by ferrovie dello stato, they have a de facto monopoly on the national railway networks to the detriment of other operators and therefore of free competition.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr grosch's own-initiative report, which regulates a crucial area of our activities, which is inevitable and necessary for the functioning of our society. i support and share the objectives that have been set to achieve competitive and efficient transport by 2050 with two steps through intermediate stages in 2020 and 2030, ending the barriers that exist between one member state and another. i support the text of the report, which appears to be homogeneous and unitary, particularly comprehensive, covering the different transport areas (road, rail, air, water) and ensuring sustainability in each of these areas and a coherent and efficient overall network. i am pleased that the various aspects of transport, from the impact on the internal market to innovation, have been addressed, without neglecting road safety. the key point i particularly appreciated in the report was the eco-sustainability aspect, the emphasis on using transport which is more environmentally friendly and energy-efficient.
in writing. - i expressed my support for the text presented by mr grosch which, taking as its starting point the white paper presented by the european commission, sets ten objectives to make the european transport system safer, more competitive and more efficient by 2050, passing through intermediate objectives to be achieved by 2020 and 2030.
in writing. − i support this text because the european parliament has the duty to take action on the treatment of detainees in europe. the european court of human rights has repeatedly condemned eu member states with regard to detention conditions, duration of pre-trial detention and administration of justice. for this reason we ask the eu and the member states to take urgent measures to ensure that the fundamental rights of prisoners are respected. it is of fundamental importance to implement minimum standards of detention in all member states. appropriate resources should be granted by the member states to the restructuration of prisons, to ensure respect for the fundamental rights of prisoners and to prepare detainees for their release and social integration. i also agree with the necessity to point out that pre-trial detention remains an exceptional measure to be used under strict conditions and for a limited period of time, in compliance with the fundamental principle of presumption of innocence and of the right not to be deprived of liberty.
in writing. - the european model of civil and democratic coexistence cannot be without conditions of detention which fully respect the rights of individuals. it is therefore right to urge member states to take urgent measures to ensure that the fundamental rights of prisoners, in particular the rights of vulnerable persons, are respected and protected. i also agree that common minimum standards of detention should be applied in all member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the interim report on the partnership and cooperation agreement with uzbekistan. parliament has every reason to make any changes to the agreement subject to compliance with minimum standards on child labour, given the situation in the former soviet republic where hundreds of thousands of school-age children are being taken away from school to be sent to the cotton fields where they have to participate in the cotton harvest for many months. we must insist that the european union give the green light to the agreement only on condition that uzbekistan accepts monitoring missions from the international labour organisation. the agreement itself would be beneficial to the economic interests of our companies, which would have access to raw materials on favourable terms; however, it is not acceptable that children are exploited in the intensive cotton harvesting and only when uzbekistan is willing to remedy this serious situation can we give our consent to the agreement.
in writing. - it is absolutely out of the question, given the current human rights situation, that the european parliament would give its approval without changes being made to uzbekistan's policies. i fully agree with the rapporteur and therefore i shall vote in favour.
in writing. - i share and support the balanced report by mr cutaş. the strengthening of euro-uzbek relations is an important link in our partnership with asian countries. the european textile industry, which is skilled in the processing of raw materials, can only benefit from free trade with the third exporter, the fifth largest producer of cotton in the world. but closer cooperation, especially in the textile sector, must be based on respect for human rights and for the rights of the child. as the eu presidency acknowledged last june, during the cotton harvest season the uzbek government employs between 200,000 and 2 million children as labour, closing schools and firing teachers who refuse to send pupils to the plantations. this is a matter of grave concern.
in writing. as i said in yesterday's debate, i have confirmed my vote in favour of mr cutaș's report. i would ask the commission to take this important vote seriously and to put all the pressure on the uzbek government to end child labour in the cotton fields. europe cannot make agreements with countries that commit such acts. cotton is a very important raw material for the textile industry in my padania: we must demand that it be collected in a way that respects human rights. children belong in school, not in the fields.
in writing. - we have voted in favour of the amending protocol to a partnership and cooperation agreement with uzbekistan on textiles. the agreement will benefit eu exporters by creating legal certainty for them. the value of european textile exports to uzbekistan is in fact eur 16.4 million. uzbekistan is the world's fifth largest producer of cotton and the third largest exporter of cotton, but within the country, the achievement of human rights is unfortunately still a utopia: it is often the same government - which controls the cotton and textile industries - that uses children as a source of cheap labour. the european union will therefore have to implement a coherent policy towards uzbekistan, which still raises concerns about the human rights situation. valid instruments for change exist, but they must be implemented.
in writing. − i voted for this report because, considering that eu assistance funds are too limited to allow the eu to have an impact in all policy areas in central asia, i agree with the view that the cornerstones of the eu new approach in the region must be human security and regional cooperation. these issues are among the main sources of instability in central asia and can be targeted by eu efforts. in addition to that, i believe an enhanced cooperation between the eu and the five countries of central asia is of mutual strategic interest in order to deepen political and economic relations. furthermore i would like to stress the importance of the implementation of the central asian nuclear weapons free zone by the five central asian republics. the treaty, with its binding commitment to nuclear disarmament by countries that previously hosted nuclear weapons on their territory and that have neighbours with nuclear weapons, is a significant contribution to the efforts to achieve a world free from nuclear weapons and a powerful example of non-proliferation cooperation.
in writing. - with the end of the cold war, central asia has gained increasing weight on the international chessboard: the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. the success of our strategy is therefore a key factor in maintaining stable and fruitful relations with the countries of the region. unfortunately, the conclusions of mrs kiil-nielsen's report seem to suggest that europe is not moving in the right direction. progress has been made, but it is still not enough for those who want to establish a lasting partnership: the economic support we provide to those countries is limited; the level of corruption in political regimes is high and widespread; inadequate respect for fundamental rights, with systematic cases of torture, repression of political opposition and child labour. finally, as the report points out, dangerous movements linked to islamic fundamentalism are spreading in the region, and for these reasons i am opposed to the report.
in writing. the european council welcomed the commission's proposal to establish a european union-wide network of information centres for the protection of the environment. the rapporteur recalls that since 2007 the eu has intensified its relations with the countries of central asia, which have a strategic role for europe, by establishing regular bilateral dialogues on human rights and national water policies. the eu is unable to reconcile its different objectives in effective programmes to be adapted to local realities and to the events, often tragic and potentially having repercussions in europe itself, experienced by central asia. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. in the new approach, the eu will have to play a mediating role in order to ensure respect for fundamental rights by asian governments and to achieve real regional cooperation between the countries of central asia. the establishment of an ad hoc eu-central asia parliamentary forum will also be important for monitoring these objectives.
in writing. the european union considers central asia to be strategically important from a political and economic point of view. since 2007, diplomatic relations have intensified, as evidenced by bilateral dialogues on human rights and national water policies. the central asian states, however, have serious shortcomings in democracy, human rights, the rule of law and fundamental freedoms. despite undeniable progress, the limits of the european strategy for central asia are now clear. the european union, moreover, is unable to reconcile its different objectives, values and interests in effective programmes adapted to local realities. the vote calls for a series of initiatives to step up european engagement, focusing on the objectives and actions most likely to help meet the most pressing challenges: human rights and the rule of law, water, energy and regional security.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text presented by mr kiil-nielsen which examines the results (and future prospects for implementation) of the strategy pursued by the european union in central asia. the report, while highlighting increased multilateral cooperation and the positive improvements brought about by european aid, renews the call for greater commitment to promoting respect for human rights and economic development in the countries concerned, and calls for an enhanced eu presence in these areas.
in writing. − in the field of health and safety at work, there is a substantial body of legislation which allows the implementation of the european treaties and the charter of fundamental rights in the field of health at work and which guarantees respect for the fundamental right to health of citizens. however, the community strategy 2007-2012 stresses that this is not enough, but that legislation needs to be developed to adapt it to new risks such as psychosocial risks. in my view, the implementation of workplace health promotion policies and practices produces beneficial results in all areas, whether economic, social or personal. i believe that the verification of the correct implementation of legislation on health and safety at the workplace gives a crucial role to labour inspections for the prevention and control of risks. inspections, in my view, also play a positive role in improving information and experience within the company. member states should therefore strengthen the staff and resources of their labour inspection services. in this context, it is essential to identify the categories of workers at risk in order to provide appropriate responses so that they can effectively benefit from the respect of their fundamental right to health.
in writing. the report focuses its attention in some parts on the situation of ethnic minorities, immigrants as particularly vulnerable categories. the text proposes the introduction of targeted incentives that member states should put in place to improve the conditions of these categories of people in the labour market. in addition, the report repeatedly refers to the need to increase the employment of immigrants, recalling that this objective is also included in the eu 2020 strategy. i do not agree with these parts of the report, which focus on categories of people no more vulnerable than the millions of european citizens who, in the current crisis, are in great difficulty both from the employment and social and economic point of view. the member states should now concentrate all their efforts on these people more than ever before, before thinking of other vulnerable social groups. i therefore vote against the report.
in writing. − i am in favour of the community strategy on health and safety at work. we believe that technological developments and changing socioeconomic conditions also change workplaces and work practices. rapid political, administrative and technical responses are therefore essential to ensure a high level of health and safety at work. the impact of the crisis on the economy and the severity of the recession in many member states should not be used as an excuse for a lack of scrupulous application of legislation on health and safety at work. it is therefore important that the european union and the member states develop a european occupational risk surveillance programme based on health indicators, definitions and epidemiological tools common to the 27 countries. i also stress the need for an integrated approach to surveillance which takes account both of the career path of active workers and of the health status of retired employees. it is important to support the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to achieve an employment rate of 75% by 2020, by promoting the employment of women, young people, older workers, low-skilled workers and regular immigrants.
in writing. − the current community legislation on health and safety at work is based on the 1989 framework directive 391 and the directives on risks or specific sectors. however, the community strategy 2007-2012 notes that the regulatory framework is not sufficient. legislation needs to be updated to take account of new risks such as psychosocial risks. the resolution also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the safety and health of workers is not compromised by the use of the workplace. member states are invited to strengthen the staff and resources of labour inspection services and to achieve the target of one inspector for every 10 000 workers, as recommended by the labour inspection organisation.
in writing. − implementing workplace health promotion policies and practices generates benefits in four areas: economic, social, personal and corporate image benefits. the verification of the correct implementation of legislation on health and safety at the workplace gives a crucial role to labour inspections for the prevention and control of risks. inspections also play a positive role in improving information and experience within the enterprise. member states should therefore strengthen the staff and resources of their services and achieve the target of one inspector per 10 000 workers, as recommended by the labour inspection organisation. the text of the report would be acceptable, but the clauses which identify migrants and ethnic minorities as vulnerable categories to be given targeted treatment are unacceptable.
in writing. − europe is facing a period of great change in the field of occupational health and safety. while strategies need to focus on three key areas - stress, burnout and musculoskeletal disorders - national strategies should also devote greater efforts and resources to prevention. one of the objectives of this vote is to provide specific statistical means for evaluating prevention, not only in terms of accidents but also in terms of diseases and the percentage of workers exposed to chemical, physical or biological agents and to dangerous situations from the point of view of work organization. it is also necessary to advance european harmonisation by including all workers in prevention policies.
in writing. - i have expressed my support for the text presented by mr delli, considering the importance of protecting the safety and health of european citizens at work. investing in preventive policies would not only reduce social security expenditure but also improve the quality of work, while ensuring greater efficiency and competitiveness.
